title: Clustering Ensemble Realisations into Weather Scenarios with Uncertainty Estimates
abs: This project aims to develop TEMPEST (Tropical Ensemble Model Post-processing with Explainable Scenario Typology), an innovative framework for transforming complex ensemble weather forecasts into interpretable, actionable scenarios specifically designed for tropical meteorology. Current ensemble forecasting systems present two critical challenges: (1) information overload for operational meteorologists and general public who must interpret numerous ensemble members under time constraints, and (2) limited ensemble sizes that insufficiently characterize the full range of weather possibilities, particularly for extreme events. These challenges are especially acute for tropical weather forecasting in Singapore and Southeast Asia, where complex local patterns and high-impact phenomena require both accuracy and interpretability. The project will develop methods which start with processing operational ensemble forecasts from global and regional NWP (e.g., ECMWF-EPS, SINGV-EPS) currently available in Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS), but will be applicable for ensemble products from next-generation NWP model SINGV_NG. The project will have special focus on tropical phenomena including Sumatra squalls, extreme precipitation, and monsoon surges. TEMPEST will deliver a comprehensive framework enabling more effective decision-making for weather-sensitive operations across Singapore’s government agencies and private sectors, while advancing the state-of-the-art in tropical weather forecasting and postprocessing.
kw: post-processing, ensemble augmentation, deep learning, pattern recognition, large language models (LLMs)

title: Novel Data Assimilation Methods for Tropical Weather Prediction
abs: Data assimilation (DA) is a fundamental component of numerical weather prediction and a prototypical inverse problem, where the objective is to estimate the true system state by optimally combining sparse, noisy observations with prior model forecasts. The inherently ill-posed nature of DA, stemming from data sparsity and model uncertainty, often necessitates strong physical priors and expert tuning. Contemporary challenges include computational complexity, nonlinear dynamics, and processing large-scale heterogeneous data. This project investigates AI-based data assimilation to enhance key algorithmic components in the Joint Effort for Data assimilation Integration (JEDI) system. We focus specifically on optimizing the assimilation scheme logic in OOPS via learnable structures. We aim to propose interpretable AI models to bridge the gap between traditional DA theory and modern machine learning. The proposed methodology involves: (1) Developing interpretable AI architectures aligned with the algorithmic principles of classical DA methods, with the aim of improving transparency, physical consistency, and theoretical grounding in AI assimilation. (2) Systematically exploring modular integration strategies, where traditional DA components are progressively enhanced or substituted with learning-based alternatives while preserving domain knowledge and structural coherence. (3) Advancing deployment potential by developing lightweight AI components and exploring the integration strategies with the JEDI framework. These efforts will be evaluated against existing DA algorithms in terms of estimation accuracy, computational performance, and robustness, focusing especially on tropical, urban-scale weather prediction. The proposed research is strategically aligned with CCRS’s operational priorities and JCSDA’s roadmap for integrating AI into the JEDI framework, aiming to ensure long-term compatibility and practical deployment.
kw: Data Assimilation; Artificial Intelligence

title: Innovative carbon sequestration by mineral carbonation of industrial wastes into artificial aggregates for land reclamation and backfilling applications.
abs: Thermochemical treatment of freshwater sludge (FS) and sewage sludge (SS) by sintering is an innovative sludge management strategy. It harnesses the heating value of the organics and recovers the inorganics to produce lightweight aggregate (LWA) as alternative construction and gardening materials. However, concerns about greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO2), undermines the environmental sustainability of the sludge-to-LWA technology. Leveraging the flue gas from Zerowaste Asia (ZA) ’s upcoming pilot sludge-to-LWA facility, this project aims to conduct a pilot demonstration of a decarbonization technology that utilize industrial wastes for mineral carbonation. Besides flue gas, this project will also evaluate the effectiveness of the decarbonization technology in capturing CO2 from the biogas exhaust produced by PUB’s water reclamation plant (WRP). Different local wastes, including thermal process residues like incineration bottom ash (IBA) from waste-to-energy (WtE) facilities, ash from coal and biomass combustion, sewage sludge incineration ash (SSIA) from incineration of SS, ladle slag from steel making, and waste concrete washing slurry from concrete batching plant, will be comprehensively evaluated for their alkalinity potential and carbon sequestration capacity. These waste materials will undergo a series of pre-treatments such as size reduction and impurities removal to enhance their reactivity, followed by water application to form a slurry. The resulting slurry will be fed into a carbonation reactor configured in the form of spray dryer and/or gas scrubber system. The slurry will be atomized into fine droplets in the spray dryer and upon contact with flue gas and/or biogas exhaust, CO2 will react with the slurry and precipitate into stable calcium or magnesium carbonates. While in the gas scrubber system, the slurry will be directly in contact with the incoming flue gas and/or biogas exhaust to precipitate stable calcium or magnesium carbonates. Additives may be introduced during the process to regulate pH and optimize conditions for metal ion dissolution and carbonate precipitation. The resulting carbonate will be pelletized by adding binder in a cold bonding process to form pellets for land reclamation and backfilling applications. Mass balances and process conditions will be optimized for commercial scalability. Finally, a net CO2 and other GHG balance and feasibility studies, Techno-economic Assessment (TEA), Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), and Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) will be conducted to further determine the feasibility and scalability of the decarbonization technology for commercial applications.
kw: Decarbonization; mineral carbonization; industrial waste; waste-to-resource; carbon capture; and carbon utilization

title: Indoor Environments and Attention Span: A Naturalistic, Non-Intrusive Approach
abs: The proposed research project aims to objectively assess the impact of indoor environmental conditions on students' attention spans in naturally ventilated classrooms in Singapore. Conducted over a year, this longitudinal observational study will utilize non-intrusive tools, such as infrared thermal imaging and video analysis, to monitor thermal comfort and students' attention. The project seeks to validate two hypotheses: first, that infrared thermal imaging can accurately predict students' thermal comfort, and second, that a significant relationship exists between indoor environmental conditions and attention spans. By employing machine learning-driven video analysis, the study will gather empirical data that could inform educational strategies and policies globally, offering a scalable solution for similar educational settings worldwide, particularly against the backdrop of anticipated climate change impacts. The research is guided by theories from environmental engineering and cognitive science, focusing on cognitive processes like attention. Data collection will be conducted through microclimate sensors, video, and thermal imaging cameras. Data analysis will employ multiple regression analyses to determine how variables such as temperature, humidity, and wind speed affect attention, while controlling for confounding factors. The feasibility of the study is supported by the use of established technologies like computer vision and thermal imaging, which have proven effective in other fields. The project's importance lies in its potential to fill existing knowledge gaps by providing robust, long-term data on the effects of environmental conditions on cognitive performance, influencing classroom design and educational policies in tropical and subtropical regions.

title: AI Foundation Models for Regional Weather Prediction in the Maritime Continent
abs: Artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models (FMs) offer significant potential for enhancing regional weather predictions through accelerated forecasting and improved accuracy. However, global-scale AI models require substantial adaptation for regional contexts, particularly within computationally constrained operational environments. This project addresses these challenges for the Maritime Continent (MC) and Singapore by systematically evaluating existing AI FMs to identify optimal architectures suited for regional applications. We propose developing lightweight, domain-specific FM frameworks tailored for tropical weather systems, integrating multi-modal local observations to achieve kilometre-scale spatial and hourly temporal resolutions. Furthermore, we aim to innovate advanced architectural implementations to operationalize high-spatiotemporal-resolution AI-driven weather forecasting, facilitating robust, efficient, and region-specific predictive capabilities.
kw: Weather prediction; Foundation model; Pre-training; Fine-tuning; Artificial intelligence

title: Predicting Convective Hazards in the Maritime Continent
abs: Predicting convective hazards (e.g., intense precipitation, strong winds, lightning) in the Maritime Continent is challenging due to the complex, localized, and rapidly evolving nature of tropical convection. This project aims to enhance both understanding and forecasting these hazards by integrating multi-source observational data, numerical weather prediction (NWP) model outputs, and nowcasting models, with a strong focus on machine learning-based post-processing and forecast interpretability. Key challenges in accurately predicting tropical convective hazards using existing models include: (1) NWP models, including km-scale regional NWP models, initialized hours in advance, face the challenge of predicting detailed features of tropical convection and lack the resolution to explicitly resolve the small-scale processes driving hazards like lightning and strong winds; (2) Existing radar-based nowcasting models, while satisfactory for precipitation nowcasts (up to 1 hour), degrade in performance for longer lead times and extreme events and cannot directly predict other convective hazards such as strong wind and lightning due to hazard-specific characteristics. To address these challenges, the project introduces key innovations: (1) detection and probabilistic nowcast of tropical Convective Initiation (CI) as augmented observation to guide nowcast models and mitigate NWP latency limitations, (2) NWP-informed machine learning models to improve forecast skill at extended lead times, and (3) multi-task learning to optimize predictions across multiple hazards while addressing observation gaps. Additionally, forecast interpretability is enhanced through attention mechanisms, uncertainty quantification, and scenario-based simulation analysis incorporating physics. The project prioritizes high-impact regions and lead times for each hazard to ensure that the forecasts are actionable: lightning (Singapore region, up to 1 hour), intense precipitation (Maritime Continent, up to 8 hours), and strong winds (radar region, up to 8 hours). The expected outcome is skillful probabilistic forecasts of tropical convective hazards to support operational decision making for aviation, maritime and public safety, and deeper understanding of convective hazard development.
kw: Convective Hazards, Tropical Convective Initiation, NWP-Informed Machine Learning, Post-Processing

title: Understanding the effects of multi-scale atmospheric processes in the prediction of tropical weather systems
abs: Accurate weather forecasting is essential for disaster preparedness and mitigation in Southeast Asia, a region highly susceptible to extreme weather such as typhoons, intense convective storms and heat stress. Traditional high-resolution regional models are often constrained by side boundary inconsistencies, limiting forecast accuracy and lead time. To address this challenge, this project aims to develop an atmospheric model for Singapore-centered Southeast Asia, leveraging on a next-generation atmosphere model (such as the Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) or LFRic) as the core framework. This research will focus on developing scale-adaptive physical parameterization schemes tailored for unstructured and non-uniform mesh frameworks, enabling seamless transitions between spatial resolutions from 9 to 1 km. Key advancements will include improvements in cumulus convection parameterization, cloud microphysics, planetary boundary layer, and land package, ensuring accurate representation of small-scale processes in high-resolution domains. Additionally, multi-platform observations (e.g., satellite, radar, and in-situ data) and large-eddy simulations will be integrated to develop process-based diagnostic techniques, aiming for providing the robust validation dataset to refine high-resolution modeling of key physical processes. The project will also emphasize computational efficiency, by optimizing the model’s dynamical core emulation and dynamical-physical coupling using a novel hybrid AI/ML dynamical core to reduce the computational cost of supporting regional-scale grid and long forecast lead times. A state-of-the-art variable-resolution weather forecasting model will be developed and evaluated over Southeast Asia, focusing on its ability to capture mesoscale structures of extreme weather events. The results will provide valuable insights into improving regional weather prediction capabilities and advancing next-generation numerical weather prediction models.
kw: MPAS-A; Variable Resolution Model Development; Fine Tuning

title: Blending Weather Forecasts from Multiple Models
abs: Different weather prediction model products, such as NWP and nowcasting, cover across different forecast periods and vary significantly in update frequency, geographic coverage, and spatio-temporal resolution. To enhance predictive skill and ensure a seamless transition between models, this project aims to develop an advanced blending framework that integrates forecasts from multiple models while preserving critical information that might otherwise be lost through averaging. Two key types of blending will be explored in this project: 1) Spatial and Multivariate Blending of NWPs: This involves integrating high-resolution regional NWP models (such as SINGV-DA/EPS) with global models (such as ECMWF and data-driven WP) to ensure spatially coherent NWP predictions to support downstream applications; and 2) Temporal Blending of Nowcast and NWP: This aims to bridge the gap between radar-driven nowcasts (0–3 hours) and NWP forecasts (from 3 to >12 hours) by ensuring a smooth temporal transition, leading to a unified and enhanced prediction. While most existing studies concentrate on a narrow range of models, such as regional NWP and extrapolation-based nowcasts, this project proposes a comprehensive, hierarchical framework that leverages the strengths of a diverse range of weather prediction models. Specifically, we first propose benchmarking the performance of existing blending solutions across different resolutions, with a focus on the tropical region (i.e. around Singapore) and adaptation to various models. The goal is to establish baseline methods and identify key challenges. Next, we introduce a framework comprising three key components: 1) NWP blending for longer forecast lead time, 2) nowcast blending at short lead time, and 3) optimized blending of NWP and nowcast, building on the first two. Given the substantial differences in spatio-temporal accuracy and resolution among prediction models, each component is designed to tackle specific challenges while collectively forming a robust, end-to-end blending solution.
kw: Spatio-temporal blending, data-driven adaptive weight, generative AI, multivariate coherence

title: Exploring Sodium Storage Mechanisms in Sphalerite SnP-Based High-Entropy Compounds
abs: The proposed research aims to enhance the performances of sodium-ion batteries (NIBs) by focusing on high-entropy compound anodes derived from sphalerite SnP based materials. These anodes exhibit metallic conductivities and high Na-storage capacities enabled by dual Na-active elements. The high-entropy compounds offer complementary constituent elements, allowing for deliberate adjustments to fine-tune structure and regulate reaction mechanisms, thereby obtaining favourable physicochemical properties and electrochemical intermediates for Na-storage. By leveraging on the synergistic effects of multiple cations and advantages of high conformational entropy, remarkable electrochemical Na-storage performances can be obtained. Our work will focus on optimising microstructure, physiochemical properties, formation of electrochemical intermediates and improving Na-storage mechanisms. The research approaches include optimizing the constituent elements through isomorphic substitution, high conformational entropy incorporation strategies, and other specific synthesis strategies to control specific morphologies. By careful examination of electrochemical behaviours, we aim to elucidate the correlation between composition, structure, physicochemical properties, Na-storage mechanism and performance. Ultimately, our goal is to produce cost-effective high-entropy anodes with outstanding electrochemical properties, avoiding an over-reliance on any single element, leveraging the inherent advantages of high-entropy strategies. The research will offer valuable insights into the preparation of superior high-conformational entropy anode materials for NIBs, thereby contributing to the advancement of energy storage technologies.
kw: High-Entropy Materials, Sodium Ion Batteries; Electrochemical Energy Storage

title: HeartIMPACT: An ultrasensitive and multiplexed IMmunoassay Platform for Advanced Cardiovascular Triage
abs: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) symptoms are often vague in the early stages. It can lead to unnecessary referrals to cardiologists or emergency departments (ED), which exacerbates ED overcrowding or it can result in delayed diagnosis with dire consequences of cardiovascular events. We aim to develop an ultrasensitive and multiplexed digital immunoassay platform that enables risk stratification of CVD patients using a panel of three cardiac biomarkers, covering diverse CVD pathophysiology. This is aimed for use by primary care providers (GPs and community care) and also for acute and accurate in-hospital point-of-care diagnosis. This point-of-care testing (POCT) platform aligns with the Healthier SG initiative, enabling efficient triaging of CVD in primary care and looking beyond in overseas in rural healthcare institutions. Our technology is a one-step, isothermal (37°C) digital immunoassay that delivers ultra high sensitivity and precision for digital testing at the point of care.
kw: Point of Care;Immunoassay;Cardiovascular disease;Heart Failure;Myocardial Infarction;Myocarditis

title: Development and Validation of an AI-enabled, Non-contact, Self-testing Tonometry Device
abs: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness, projected to affect over 100 million people by 2040. Effective management requires frequent intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring, yet the gold standard, Goldmann Applanation Tonometry (GAT), is limited by its reliance on specialized equipment, prescription anesthetic eye drops and trained personnel. From our current CIA-INV project, we have developed a novel handheld device (STOP tonometer) uses a trained neural network to measure IOP through the eyelid, eliminating the need for topical anesthesia or direct ocular contact. However, the current STOP AI algorithm, has been trained on a small dataset (14 normal, 14 high IOP patients). This requires further optimization to enhance accuracy and generalizability. We will expand data collection, allocating 80% for training, 10% for validation, and 10% for testing. Additionally, we will implement a pretraining and in-context learning strategy using waveform datasets from related ophthalmic devices to improve model adaptability without parameter fine-tuning. Through this follow-up study, we aim to achieve a correlation of at least 0.9 between our device and standard tonometry (GAT, Tonopen), with ≥85% of measurements within ±5 mmHg of reference values. Furthermore, our target is ≥90% sensitivity and specificity in distinguishing high and low IOP patients.
kw: medical technology; artificial intelligence; digital health; data science and data analytics

title: Artificial Intelligence-incorporated hand phone application for detection of Skin Cancers
abs: There is a rising incidence of skin cancers in Singapore and in the world, with a significant economic burden and a need for timely diagnosis to reduce mortality and morbidity. With the CMTi-NHIC/19009 grant, we performed a quantitative study of color (C) and asymmetry (A) features for automatic melanoma detection and this study had been published and presented in Annu Int Conf IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc. in Nov 2021. We have developed an adaptable, attachable, affordable dermoscope during this grant period as well. With the ongoing NHIC-I2I-2303013 grant, we have developed the algorithm for Border (B) and Dermoscopic structures (D), completing the ABCD rule. We have also developed an additional deep learning component for melanoma identification. The deep learning component and ABCD AI algorithm have been incorporated into a handphone application, SkAI Pro. This application, along with our inhouse dermoscope, allows physicians to take a dermoscopic picture with their handphone and dermoscope, have the image analyzed instantly, and provide early access for patients. We are currently amid a prospective study, with plans for an overseas study site in Australia. In addition, we have developed SkAI Lite, which is a smart phone application, utilizing AI to aid in earlier detection of skin cancers. SkAI Lite is targeted at public and family physicians, allowing instant analysis with a photo taken by the phone. We would like to expand the use of our AI model with this grant application, to cover the non-melanoma skin cancers (BCC and SCC) as well as the acral melanomas which are not covered in the earlier grants. We have proven that the concept of utilizing AI to aid with skin cancer diagnosis is effective and would like to expand the idea to cover the other skin cancers which are more common in Asians.
kw: Artificial Intelligence, skin cancers, Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Melanoma

title: 3D Printed Biphasic Osteochondral Plug for Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis
abs: Background: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is prevalent globally, affecting 9.6% of men and 18% of women aged more than 60 years, leading to significant economic burdens, including a $82 billion cost in the USA and a surgical market of $5.9 billion for moderate knee OA. The gold standard treatment, microfracture, fails to regenerate hyaline cartilage, while Osteochondral Autograft Transfer (OAT) and Osteochondral Allograft (OCA) involve risks of donor site morbidity and infection. Knee arthroplasty is invasive, with a limited lifespan (15-20 years) and has significant potential complications, necessitating less invasive cartilage regeneration options for younger patients and those with prior treatment failures. Proposed Solution: We have developed a 3D-printed biphasic osteochondral plug (OCP) that exhibits promising hyaline cartilage regeneration in an in vivo porcine study. In this study, 75% of OCP pigs showed over 90% closure with hyaline cartilage compared to 50% in microfracture pigs. Histological analysis revealed up to 99% hyaline cartilage, with no signs of chronic inflammation. Study Design: We will conduct a prospective, First-in-Human, non-randomized, open-label trial involving 15 patients aged 21 to 75 with cartilage defects (up to 1cm²). A comparable control group will undergo microfracture. MRI imaging at 12 months will evaluate cartilage repair, along with assessment of patient-reported outcomes and adverse events. Specific Aims: The primary aim is to evaluate the safety of the OCP. Secondary aims include assessing functional outcomes and determining cartilage regeneration compared to microfracture through imaging. Significance: If funded, this study will provide crucial safety and efficacy data for the OCP, facilitating progress to larger clinical trials and ultimately leading to FDA Class III regulatory clearance and global commercialization strategies.
kw: 3D printed; osteochondral plug; knee; osteoarthritis

title: Reconceptualizing Golgipathies in Neurodevelopment
abs: Currently, Golgipathies are believed to arise from abnormalities in membrane trafficking. Our proposed research seeks to reconceptualize Golgipathies in neurodevelopment by establishing the role of Golgi-dependent microtubule assembly in both Drosophila and human neural stem cells during brain development. Aim 1. Investigate Golgi-dependent reactivation of neural stem cells in Drosophila. Our recent finding stands out as the first to unveil the novel function of the Golgi protein Arf1 in microtubule nucleation in Drosophila neural stem cells. We will systematically identify and investigate the key regulators governing this process. Aim 2. Investigate the function of Golgi proteins in human neural stem cells. We hypothesize that the Golgi apparatus serves as a microtubule-organizing center in human outer radial glial cells, contributing to brain development. We will investigate the localization and function of Golgi protein ARF1 in human neural stem cells. In addition, we will establish a new link between Golgi dysfunction in human neural stem cells and Autism. Our research is expected to reconceptualize Golgipathies and related neurodevelopmental disorders such as Autism. It may open a new avenue for the treatment of neurodevelopmental disorders.
kw: The Golgi apparatus; neurodevelopmental disorders, microtubule-organizing center (MTOC); neural stem cells; outer radial glial cells; Arf1

title: Representing the complexity of Singapore’s urban environment and understanding its effects on our weather, including extremes
abs: Urban environments significantly alter the local meteorology and climate with real-life impacts on weather extremes, human comfort, energy demand, etc. Traditional mesoscale models struggle to accurately represent the complexities of urban surfaces at sub-km scales due to their coarse resolutions and simplified parameterizations. This results in deficiencies in simulating key urban processes such as urban heat island effect, urban boundary layer turbulence, localized wind flows, rainfall extremes or air pollution dispersion. Next-generation models, such as the MPAS (Model for Prediction Across Scales) and the UK Met Office's LFRic model, present a unique opportunity to enhance urban modeling. MPAS is a numerical Earth system model developed by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) for global and regional simulations of the atmosphere, ocean, and climate. Similarly, LFRic is designed to replace the current Unified Model (UM) for weather and climate prediction. These models feature stretched-grid capabilities, enabling high-resolution simulations in specific urban areas without incurring excessive computational costs. However, existing urban parameterizations in MPAS and LFRic are insufficient for capturing the complex dynamics of the urban roughness sublayer, requiring explicit representation of sub-km urban features. Additionally, traditional physics-based approaches alone may not fully capture the non-linear interactions within urban environments, necessitating the integration of AI/ML techniques to enhance parameterizations of the urban atmosphere. Addressing these challenges is crucial for improving weather and climate predictions at high resolution in densely populated regions. By advancing urban modeling in next-generation modelling systems, we can enhance forecast accuracy, integrate real-world observations, and enable better decision-making for effective disaster risk reduction, urban climate adaptation, and resilience planning. This project includes three work packages which focus on the (i) development of a next-generation urban-scale weather and climate prediction model, (ii) implementation of AI/ML-based parameterizations (e.g. for urban roughness sublayer fluxes), and (iii) generation of urban observations (e.g., from LiDAR, remote sensing, radiosonde, AWS sensors) to evaluate the model predictions and in turn improve the modeling of local-scale urban processes.
kw: Core urban modelling, artificial intelligence, urban meteorological measurements

title: Pegasus - An integrated Robotic Fit-out Station
abs: This research aims to address the challenges within Prefabricated Pre-finished Volumetric Construction (PPVC) fit-out phases, particularly the high dependence on manual labor for interior finishing operations. The primary objective is to develop an integrated robotic system, referred to as PEGASUS, which offers modularity, adaptability, versatility, and compatibility with diverse PPVC components. It should function efficiently in various sheltered factory environments and handle both 3D and 2D modules. The system is designed to perform tasks such as tiling, finishing trades, and quality control inspections. The implementation of the PEGASUS prototype is anticipated to enhance productivity significantly, with a projected 40% improvement in both private and public sector PPVC residential projects. Additionally, the system is expected to reduce fitting-out

title: Development and Integration of 3D Concrete Printing and Robotics Systems for Designing, Monitoring, and Reinforcement of Volumetric Construction
abs: The construction industry increasingly recognized the potential of 3D Concrete Printing (3DCP), given its ability to redefine construction processes in terms of efficiency, cost, and labor demands. However, challenges persist, particularly in material selection, equipment capabilities, and the absence of standardized operating procedures and testing protocols. The PI’s team’s research proposal aims to address these critical areas that hinder the application of 3DCP. We proposed an integrated dual-bridge 3DCP system combined with mobile robotics to streamline construction and post-processing. Simultaneously, recognizing the drawbacks of existing reinforcement methodologies for 3DCP structures, the PI’s team intend to develop printing system capable of in-process reinforcement by developing a BIM-enabled collaborative robot system that harmonizes Building Information Modelling (BIM), Computer Vision, and advanced Robot Control. This system integrates innovations like automated rebar insertion, steel cable reinforcing, and the capability to print concrete enhanced with coarse aggregate and steel fibers. Beyond these improvements, the PI’s team intend to develop an advanced digital software package that encompasses generative design tools, and comprehensive structural analysis utilities while enabling seamless translation of 3D designs into robot-readable codes. Furthermore, we proposed to develop specialized QA/QC standards for 3DCP and evaluate traditional concrete design methodologies for potential incorporation or adaptation. Given the existing knowledge of the PI’s team, this research is feasible, although challenges might arise, requiring iterative adjustments. Given the proposed advancement, a substantial shift in 3DCP technology can be achieved, offering sustainable, efficient, and cost-effective solutions that can potentially revolutionize the construction industry.

title: Logic and Memory Devices beyond CMOS Based on Spin and Electric Polarization
abs: Tradional computing system is based on CMOS which utilizes the electrostatic field to control the charge carriers concentration of semiconductors. The scaling of CMOS is approaching the physical limit. To make significant improvements in the energy efficiency and speed of integrated circuits, non-traditional computing paradigm - beyond-CMOS is required. Instead of utilization of charge, new state variables such as electron spin and electric dipole are emerging as the leading state variables for logic, which is non-volatile and therefore suitable for in-memory computing or neuromorphic computing. Magnetization switching by electric current induced spin transfer torque (STT) and spin orbit torque (SOT) has been developed for non-volatile memory.The traditionally proposed spin logic devices based on STT, SOT, dipole nanomagnets, spin wave, or domain walls unfortunately still suffer from the energy inefficiency, scaling, low speed and incompatibility of input and output. Very recently, Intel proposed scalable and energy efficient beyond-CMOS spintronic logic device: magnetoelectric spin orbit (MESO) device.3 It is voltage-driven magnetization switching by a magneto-electric effect, which requires a ferroelectric/ferromagnetic heterostructure with a strong coupling between its spin and electric polarization. The detection of the resulting spin state is possible by an inverse Rashba Edelstein effect that converts spin polarized current into a potential difference in a material with a large spin-orbit torque. This device allows energy efficiency improvent by about 30 times and logic density by more than 5 compared to advanced CMOS devices. However, However, there are still a few challenging problems for practical implementation of MESO device. 1) Heterostructure designing for lateral mirror symmetry breaking to enable direct 180-degree switching of the magnetization (axial vector) by the electric field or electric polarization (polar vector); 2) materials with large SOT efficiency for large voltage output. In this project, we propose a siminar MESO device which utilizes FM/multiferroic coupling induced exchange bias and further switch the magnetization by SOT. Although ferroelectric with electric polarization switching has been commercialized for non-volatile memory none reports electric polarization based logic device. It is recently found that head-to-head and tail-to-tail domain walls in ferroelectric are conductive which are electron and hole dominated, respectively. It is possible to utilize the 2D charged domain walls to construct the logic similar to the silicon based CMOS.
