title:
Understanding the effects of air-sea-land interactions on the
weather of the Maritime Continent
inst: TCOMS - Technology Centre for Offshore & Marine Singapore
abs: Earth’s climate system comprises three major components i.e., the atmosphere, land, and the ocean. Interactions between these three components are the key drivers of weather and climate. As such, exchange of fluxes between the atmosphere, land, and ocean is better captured in a coupled modelling system compared to standalone models. The Maritime Continent (MC) region experiences strong atmosphere-land-ocean coupled processes across multiple timescales (diurnal, intra-seasonal, and seasonal) and plays a pivotal role in the Earth's climate system from atmospheric and oceanic perspectives. Owing to its unique position between the Indo-Pacific warm pool region and Walker circulation, the MC region is of extremely high importance in understanding regional and global weather and climate. To better represent atmosphere-land-ocean coupled dynamics and flux exchanges over the MC region, we propose to develop a fully coupled modelling system by integrating a next-generation atmospheric model (MPAS or LFRic), a land surface model (Noah-MP or JULES), and an ocean model (NEMO) through a model coupling interface OASIS3-MCT. We aim to improve the representation of dynamic flux exchanges among the atmosphere, land, and ocean models. The development of a fully coupled atmosphere-land-ocean system would provide a more realistic representation of feedback mechanisms within these model components. This coupled system has significant potential in advancing numerical weather prediction (NWP) and improving forecasts of extreme weather events in the Maritime Continent (MC).
kw: Air-sea interaction, flux exchange, flux coupler, OASIS3-MCT, MPAS, LFRic, NEMO, MJO, SST.

title: AI-Driven Texture Design – From New Ingredients to Meat Alternatives (AIDTex)
inst: SIFBI - Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation
abs: Singapore's commitment to food security necessitates exploring new sustainable protein sources like regional protein crops, microbial biomass, cultivated animal cells and insects. However, transforming these ingredients into whole-cut meat alternatives with consumer-preferred textures remains a challenge. Optimizing the texturization process for these new ingredients relies on time-consuming trial-and-error approaches, slowing their commercialization. This project proposes the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate the transformation of these new protein sources into whole-cut meat alternatives with desirable fibrous textures. We hypothesize that a product's fibrous structure and texture can be predicted by the key physicochemical/functional properties of its ingredients and the extrusion process settings used. To validate the hypothesis, we propose to build and test a predictive AI model using these principles. First, the project will characterise the key physicochemical/functional properties of various alternative protein sources and blends. These ingredients will then be extruded to create whole-cut meat alternatives and the texture attributes of these extrudates will be analysed. The generated data will be used to develop a Gaussian Process Regression AI model capable of predicting the texture of extrudates from the ingredients’ key physicochemical/functional properties and extrusion process settings. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization will then be employed to improve the model's accuracy. This optimization aims to replicate consumer-preferred meat textures, such as cooked chicken breast, using sensory data from previous projects as a reference. Finally, the project will use the trained model to identify promising new protein sources from existing in-house ingredient databases for developing whole-cut meat alternatives with textures like meat. This project's AI-driven approach has the potential to accelerate the development and commercialization of new, sustainable protein alternatives. By overcoming the texturization bottleneck, the project will contribute to Singapore’s ’30 by 30’ vision and promote the adoption of a wider range of protein sources for alternative meat products.
kw: alternative proteins;meat alternatives;food security;artificial intelligence;ai;machine learning

title: Next-generation production of cultivated chicken adipocytes with nutritional and flavour parity through functional genomics
abs: Adipocytes play a crucial role in influencing cultivated meat’s (CM) taste, aroma, and nutritional composition. However, commercial manufacturing of adipocytes is hindered by scalability challenges due to low growth efficiency of cell lines, raising concerns about the viability of CM production. Another critical obstacle stems from poor differentiation capacity, where these adipocytes fail to attain sufficient maturation in vitro, resulting in suboptimal sensory and nutritional properties. A primary impediment lies in the limited understanding of the distinct genetic makeup and signalling networks governing in vitro growth and adipogenesis in livestock species. The team aims to develop a scalable production platform for generating cultivated chicken adipocytes that match the nutrition and flavour of conventional adipocytes, which so far have been underwhelming for the industry. This will be achieved by enhancing both proliferative and differentiation capacities through functional genomics (Fig. 1). Firstly, the team will perform genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screens and Flow-FISH to identify functional genes pivotal in driving chicken adipocyte proliferation and differentiation. By targeting all 18,023 protein-coding genes in the GRCg7b reference genome from broiler chicken, we hypothesize that the generation of large-scale data will unravel genetic determinants underlying these biological mechanisms. Subsequently, to elucidate the impact of this platform in strengthening nutritional, sensory and functional attributes of cultivated adipocytes, total lipid content, quantification of fatty acids, and volatile organic compounds will be assessed via GC-MS analysis. These readouts will provide a quantitative comparison against conventional counterparts regarding nutritional and flavour profiles, and upon optimization to parity, can greatly enhance consumer acceptance. Finally, the litmus test entails validating the functionality of the engineered cultivated adipocyte by its integration into hybrid cultivated chicken product, while assessing critical parameters of cooking behaviour, including appearance, texture, cooking loss, and fluid holding properties. Overall, this proposal will strengthen knowledge base essential for the production of cultivated chicken adipocytes with nutritional and flavour parity and establish functional production platform.
kw: Functional genomics; Nutrition; Future Foods

title: Pixelated Programmable Photonics: A Platform for Accelerating Artificial Intelligence Beyond Electronics
abs: This research proposal aims to develop scalable, efficient photonic accelerators capable of achieving petascale compute throughput and femtojoule energy efficiency, thus addressing a critical gap in current AI computing technologies. The project focuses on overcoming the scalability limitations of existing photonic computing systems by conceptualizing a photonic slab as a cohesive, programmable, and trainable entity. The methodology revolves around the pioneering development of (1) a pixelated non-volatile programmable photonic platform using emerging photonic materials, formulation of (2) an in-situ training method for photonic accelerators through investigating backpropagation in photonic systems, and the ambitious demonstration of (3) AI inference at petascale compute throughput and femtojoule energy consumption through advanced photonic integration. The feasibility of this ambitious project is underscored by the advancements in material sciences and physical computing system, the availability of sophisticated fabrication resources, as well as some proof-of-concept demonstrations of this kind of photonic computing systems at a small scale. This proposal outlines a comprehensive approach to developing next-generation photonic accelerators, promising to revolutionize AI computing, and find impact on other applications such as data communication, and microwave photonic processing.
kw: Photonic Computing; Artificial Intelligence; Integrated Photonics

title: Focal Therapy or Radical Therapy: A Phase II Trial validating the role of Molecular Profiling in Treatment Stratification for Early Prostate Cancer
abs: Focal therapy (FT) is a novel strategy for localized prostate cancer where ablative treatment is targeted to clinically significant cancer (csPCa) lesion(s) only, minimizing urinary, sexual and bowel side effects. In our phase II clinical trial of limited volume csPCa undergoing FT, 70% of men were recurrence-free 3 years post-treatment. Detailed molecular profiling of each cancer lesion showed that a higher genomic classifier score (GC >0.5) and luminal-proliferative (PSC-LP) molecular subtype were associated with cancer recurrence. We thus propose a clinical trial examining treatment stratification of patients suitable for FT using our defined molecular profiles. In FLAME-PC (Focal therapy or radical therapy: a Lesion-based Marker Evaluation in Prostate Cancer), all patients suitable for FT by clinical trial criteria will undergo pre-treatment molecular profiling of their cancer lesions. Patients with favorable molecular profiles (GC ≤0.5 or non-PSC-LP subtype) will receive FT, while those with unfavorable molecular profiles (GC >0.5 and PSC-LP subtype) will be recommended standard curative radical treatment (prostate removal or irradiation). Our primary objective is to prospectively validate the use of molecular profiling in patient selection for FT. We hypothesize that 1-year cancer recurrence rates in the FLAME-PC cohort will be significantly better than that of our historical clinical trial cohort. Our secondary objective is to elucidate the mechanisms of recurrence after FT. We hypothesize that recurrent cancer lesions are related to the original pre-FT lesions. These insights will further inform patient selection as well as therapeutic strategies for FT failures. Last, we will explore whether detailed radiological features are able to predict molecular characteristics. FLAME-PC is the first ever prospective study to use molecular profiling to assign primary treatment for prostate cancer. This will let us better personalize cancer care, leading to achieving oncological cure with minimal treatment-related morbidity.
kw: Prostate Cancer; Focal Therapy; radical therapy

title: Evaluating an eHealth and Healthcare Professional Support Program to Promote Physical Activity During Pregnancy: A Hospital-Based Model for Holistic Prenatal Care
abs: This proposal focuses on maternal care, emphasizing upstream investment in health promotion and preventive health. Our goal is to shift current clinical practice paradigms and become the first hospital to implement the "Guidelines on Physical Activity and Exercise in Pregnancy" within a healthcare system. We will launch a programme to increase adherence to these national guidelines in Singapore, an Asian society where women have low awareness of recommended guidelines, and lack professional support from healthcare staff. A survey of pregnant Singaporean women found that while 99.0% acknowledged the benefits of exercise during pregnancy, only 31.6% engaged in physical activity, and just 12.0% met the recommended levels. Similarly, a survey of obstetricians and gynaecologists (O&Gs) revealed that only 3.2% discussed exercise with their pregnant patients, and 88.7% did not recommend exercise for sedentary patients. In response, Singapore launched the "Guidelines on Physical Activity and Exercise in Pregnancy" in 2020, providing a structured framework for healthcare professionals. The eHealth Integrated Maternal Physical Activity Programme in Prenatal Care Trial (e-IMPACT) will be a pioneering randomized controlled trial (RCT) aimed at enhancing maternal health through physical activity and exercise in Asia. This innovative programme will leverage telehealth and digital health interventions, providing significant benefits such as reduced resource demands, improved cost-efficiency, and increased accessibility for participants. Conducted at KKH, this study will leverage the healthcare team's expertise to provide insights into the facilitators and barriers of integrating this new model of care in public healthcare institutions. We hypothesize that the proportion of pregnant women meeting the guidelines will be higher in the intervention group compared to the control group. The long-term goal is to implement the full-scale e-IMPACT program in community healthcare, aligning with Healthier SG's vision for a healthier future generation in Singapore.
kw: Healthier SG's vision; Physical Activity ;Preventive healthcare ; Pregnancy; eHealth

title: PREVENT-RISC: Predictive Evaluation and Early Intervention for Risk Reduction of Suicides in Emergency Care
abs: Background: Suicide remains a global public health crisis, exerting profound emotional, social, and economic impacts on individuals, families, and communities. Despite significant efforts, traditional clinical assessments often fall short in accurately identifying individuals at high risk of suicide, particularly in high-pressure settings like Emergency Departments (ED). The integration of electronic health records (EHR) with machine learning (ML) models offers a novel and promising approach to improving suicide risk prediction, enabling earlier and more targeted interventions. Objectives: This study aims to (i) develop advanced suicide risk prediction models tailored to the ED population at the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) in Singapore, (ii) benchmark the performance of these predictive models against traditional clinical assessments, and (iii) implement actionable, individualized risk assessments to inform and enhance clinical decision-making and interventions. Methods: Leveraging longitudinal EHR data from IMH and other National Healthcare Group institutions, the study will adapt a predictive model inspired by the John Peter Smith (JPS) Health Network. Using both structured data (e.g., demographics, medical history, clinical assessment scales) and unstructured inputs (e.g., clinical notes), ML algorithms will estimate the near-term risk (within 30 days) of intentional self-harm (ISH) or suicide. The model will be validated through retrospective data analysis and integrated into clinical workflows, with input from stakeholders to ensure feasibility and optimization. Expected Outcomes: The ML model is expected to outperform traditional assessment methods in predictive accuracy, facilitating the early identification of high-risk individuals. Its integration into clinical practice aims to enhance resource allocation, reduce suicide-related morbidity and mortality, and contribute to the formulation of evidence-based national healthcare policies. Significance: By addressing critical gaps in suicide prevention strategies, this research has the potential to revolutionize mental health care in Singapore, fostering a data-driven, proactive approach to saving lives.
kw: Suicidality; Suicide Prevention; Emergency Services; Predictive Modelling; Articificial Intelligence

title: Early Nursing Turnover Intention Considered by Incoming Nursing Graduates (ENTICING): A scale development and cross-sectional study
abs: Background Nursing shortages remain a global healthcare challenge. Despite increased enrollment in nursing programs in Singapore, many graduates do not join the workforce. While studies often examine turnover intention among practicing nurses, research on early turnover intention in nursing graduates is limited. Current tools to measure turnover intention are overly simplistic, treating it as a unidimensional issue despite its complexity. Aims The overall aim of the study is to explore Early Nursing Turnover Intention Considered by Incoming Nursing Graduates (ENTICING) with the following specific aims: 1. Develop and determine the psychometric properties of a multidimensional ENTICING scale. 2. Examine early turnover intention among incoming nursing graduates and its association with actual turnover behavior. Methods This study employs a two-phase design: Phase 1 will involve the development and testing of the psychometric properties of the ENTICING scale through 1) item generation from a comprehensive literature review and an exploratory study; 2) content validation using Delphi’s method; 3) pilot testing to refine items and ensure clarity; and 4) psychometric properties evaluation. Phase 2 will involve a cross-sectional survey to examine incoming graduates’ turnover intention using the newly developed ENTICING scale, followed by a six-month monitoring of their actual turnover behavior to explore the relationship. Significance The development of a validated multidimensional ENTICING scale will help identify key factors affecting early turnover intentions. This will enable stakeholders who are planning for retention efforts to develop retention strategies to entice the new nursing graduates to join the nursing workforce. The ENTICING scale could be applied by the researchers to evaluate the effectiveness of the retention strategies. The ENTICING project has the potential to enhance nursing workforce sustainability in Singapore as well as contribute to broader global efforts to address nursing shortages and high nursing turnover.
kw: nursing workforce, nursing retention, multidimensional scale, sustainability in nursing

title: Optimising precision surgical resection and neurostimulation using personalized mapping of structural and functional connectivity
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Functional and diffusion MRI reveal the functional anatomy and structural basis of brain function, particularly in epilepsy and brain tumor surgeries where damage to eloquent areas can result in lasting neurological deficits. Damage to the posterior hippocampus, inferior longitudinal fasciculus, and inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus has been linked to naming difficulties, with certain tract subdivisions being critically important. This study will map functional and structural networks subserving memory and language. Neuropsychology tests assessing word finding, fluency, memory encoding, and attention will be administered before surgery and at 3 and 12 months after anterior temporal lobe resections for medication-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy. Preoperative and postoperative T1 MRIs will be co-registered to create a resection mask, which will then be mapped onto native diffusion MRI, functional MRI and a standard template (MNI). Using healthy control tract reconstructions, we will identify voxel-level areas of disconnect in patients with neuropsychological decline. Overlapping tracts will be reconstructed on preoperative diffusion MRI, and the resection mask will help assess the extent of tract damage and its relationship to cognitive decline. We will also delineate fine-grained memory representations in cortical and mesial temporal structures using fmri data-driven machine learning approaches to identify key regions in the mesial temporal lobe and lateral neocortex essential for memory formation. We hypothesize that precise identification of critical functional and structural connectivity will allow a greater resection extent, improving seizure outcomes without additional deficits. We aim to integrate this knowledge into a semi-automated computer-assisted surgical planning software (EpiNav) for intraoperative guidance. By creating resection masks that preserve essential cortical and subcortical structures, we aim to increase seizure freedom rates and reduce cognitive deficits.
kw: Neuroimaging, Diffusion tensor imaging, functional MRI, connectivity, brain mapping

title: Understanding the role of RAD21 in treatment response and resistance in breast cancer
abs: Background: Numerous studies indicate RAD21, a key protein in the cohesin complex, influences tumorigenesis, and resistance to treatment. The RAD21 pathway is frequently altered in ~30% of breast tumours (TCGA) with ithe gene more commonly upregulated in Asian patients with breast cancer. Hypothesis: Treatment resistance and poor clinical outcomes in breast cancer is associated with aberration in the RAD21 pathway Aims: 1. Understanding the association between RAD21 expression and treatment outcomes in Asian patients with breast cancer stratified by intrinsic subtypes 2. Investigate molecular mechanisms behind therapy resistance using preclinical models. 3. Identify and validate novel and combination treatment strategies for RAD21-overexpressing or amplified breast cancers. Methods: Asian patients with breast cancer from TTSH hospital undergoing selected standard of care treatment will be stratified based on their RAD21 expression and correlate with clinical outcomes and treatment responses. The cohort will be stratified by intrinsic subtypes, including Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-positive, and Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), to identify subtype-specific associations. Where available, paired pre treatment and post treatment samples will be analysed using spatial transcriptomics to further understand mechanisms of resistance/ response. Subsequently, using isogenic cell lines of relevance, we will interrogate the RAD21 pathway including associated genes of relevance to ascertain relevant mechanisms of resistance . Finally, we will conduct a drug library screen to identify inhibitors/ combination strategies targeting this pathway. Leads will be validated using relevant patient -derived preclinical models (ie: xenograft and/or organoids) currently available in the lab as well as isogenic cell lines. Conclusion: Ultimately, our research findings will aim to discover and confirm innovative therapeutic approaches that may improve the effectiveness of current treatment approaches to breast cancer, leading to tailored cancer care. The results may greatly influence clinical choices and enhance outcomes for patients with this devastating disease. .
kw: RAD21; resistance mechianism; biomarker; breast cancer; therapeutics

title: Enrichment of Next Generation Tumour Reactive Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocytes (TILs) in Solid Cancers for Adoptive Cellular Therapy (ACT)
abs: This study aims to develop novel protocols for enhancing the expansion and enrichment of tumour-reactive tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) to improve the efficacy of adoptive cellular therapy (ACT) in solid cancers. The central hypothesis is that combining cytokines from the IL-2 family (e.g. IL-7, IL-15, IL-21) with selective enrichment of tumour-reactive TIL subpopulations (e.g., PD-1+, CD103+, CD39+) will enhance TIL efficacy, while reducing reliance on high-dose IL-2, thereby lowering toxicity and improving patient safety. The study has three specific aims: 1) Cytokine optimisation to determine whether combinations of IL-7, IL-15, and IL-21 can improve TIL expansion, activation, and tumour killing compared to high-dose IL-2, while also assessing the reduction in IL-2 toxicity; 2) Subpopulation enrichment using flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing to isolate TILs with the highest tumour-reactivity based on specific surface markers, followed by their expansion with the cytokine combinations established in Aim 1; 3) Efficacy testing of enriched TILs in both immunogenic and non-immunogenic cancer explants, comparing their proliferation, activation, and tumour killing to that of standard anti-PD-1 therapy. Feasibility is ensured by leveraging established methods in TIL isolation, cytokine optimisation, and patient-derived tumour explants. This research could revolutionise TIL therapy by expanding its applicability to not just immunogenic cancer, but also non-immunogenic cancers in the future, which currently have poor immunotherapy responses. By improving TIL expansion protocols and reducing IL-2 toxicity, this study aims to make ACT a safer, more effective treatment for a wider range of solid cancers, offering a promising strategy for next-generation cancer immunotherapies. The results could significantly advance the clinical implementation of TIL therapies, making them a viable option for more patients and contributing to the future of cancer immunotherapy.
kw: Cancer immunology; tumour infiltrating lymphocytes; TIL therapy; cellular therapy

title: A Clinical-Biomarker Classification of Early Neurocognitive Syndrome in the Community: Framework for Novel Diagnostics and Therapeutics
abs:
While Singaporeans have a life expectancy of around 85 years, their healthspan or healthy life expectancy is lower at 74 years. Cognitive diseases contribute significantly to the mismatch between life expectancy and healthspan. The earlier stages of cognitive diseases collectively termed Early Neurocognitive Syndrome (ENS) is prevalent with estimates of about 400-500 thousand residents aged 50 and above having ENS. ENS progresses at a rate of 5-12% annually to dementia which contributes significantly to reduced healthspan. A major challenge in the ENS management is the lack of a structured and comprehensive classification framework that can guide investigations and management strategies.

In this proposal, we will develop a novel classification framework for ENS that incorporates cognitive-behavioural information and blood-based biomarker information. The framework will be developed based on local prevalence of biomarkers and the actual risk of progression from ENS to dementia. We will also develop a AI based point-based score to risk-stratify patients with ENS for their risk of progression to dementia. We will investigate rates of progression to dementia, changes in quality of life and patterns of healthcare resource utilization for the various subgroups in the novel classification framework. A total of 870 subjects with ENS from the LKCMedicine BIOCIS cohort, Institute of Mental Health, Duke-NUS CARE cohort, National Neuroscience Institute and NUHS will be studied over a 4-year
kw: Early neurocognitive syndrome; classification framework; AI-driven point-based risk stratification; ageing; healthspan

title: Implementation of Digital dEtection of Cognitive Impairment and DEmentia in the community (I-DECIDE)
abs: Dementia is a growing public health concern, with cases projected to rise sharply in the Asia Pacific region by 2050. Delaying dementia onset by five years could halve its prevalence. While no disease-modifying treatments are currently available, early detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and dementia is crucial for initiating lifestyle interventions and preparing for emerging therapies. However, barriers such as cost, technical limitations, and staffing constraints hinder large-scale cognitive screening in primary care settings. This study examines the feasibility and effectiveness of the digitized Quick Dementia Rating System (QDRS) for early detection of MCI and dementia in community settings. The QDRS, a self-administered, digital tool with excellent sensitivity and strong correlations with established cognitive assessments, offers a user-friendly, accessible, and low-resource option for identifying cognitive decline among middle-aged and older adults in Singapore. Integrated into community-based programs in Active Ageing Centres (AACs) and health fairs, the QDRS will be evaluated using a hybrid effectiveness-implementation framework and the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) framework. The study has two specific aims: (1) to evaluate the QDRS’s effectiveness in detecting MCI and dementia and its association with biomarkers and brain imaging findings, such as cerebrovascular disease and Alzheimer’s pathology, and (2) to assess the feasibility and acceptability of the QDRS as a community-based early detection tool. Aligned with Singapore’s Healthier SG vision, this project addresses barriers to early detection and supports the development of scalable and sustainable screening pathways. Findings will inform healthcare policies, enhance community health programs, and contribute to dementia prevention efforts, improving cognitive health outcomes and quality of life for older adults.
kw: Dementia, Alzheimer's Disease, Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), Early detection, Digital health tools, Community-based screening

title: Unlocking Pre- and Postnatal Time Capsules in Deciduous Teeth: Advancing Next-Generation Forecasting of Adolescent Neurodevelopmental Trajectories
abs: Since the COVID pandemic, mental disorders have surged, becoming leading contributors to the global disease burden and undermining long-term societal and economic prosperity. In many countries including Singapore, neurodevelopmental and mental health outcomes (NMHOs) have alarmingly deteriorated among children/adolescents. Emerging evidence indicate that pre-/post-natal exposures to neurotoxins/micro-nutrients (EM), stressors (HM) and inflammation (IM) tremendously impact NMHOs. Yet, pinpointing the precise timing and impact of both harmful and protective exposures and their interactions remain challenging. This project introduces a transformative approach using dental biomarkers from deciduous teeth, which form incrementally (like tree rings) from the second trimester in utero until 36 months after birth, archiving time-specific exposures continuously. Nested within the GUSTO (Growing Up in Singapore Towards healthy Outcomes) birth cohort, our team had collected 2,793 baby teeth from 367 participants over the past decade and developed three state-of-the-art methodological platforms to conduct (1) Elemental/Metal (EM) quantification using synchrotron-based X-ray fluorescent microscopy; (2) Histo-morphological (HM) analysis employing non-linear/linear optical microscopy; and (3) Inflammatory Marker (IM) profiling via immunocytochemical assays. By integrating these dental biomarkers with comprehensive biopsychosocial and multi-omic GUSTO data (including MRI and polygenic scores), our study aims to deliver two key outcomes (KOs). KO-1 includes novel time-specific risk factors/predictors and pathogenic pathways pertinent to NMHOs, including neurodevelopmental deficits, ADHD, autism, and children/adolescent depression. KO-2 comprises AI-driven Biopsychosocial-Environmental Prediction Models (BEPMs) to forecast NMHOs, at the personal, clinical, and community levels, for early detection/intervention of youth with high-risk of NMHOs. In summary, this project leverages innovative strategies and technologies to develop new knowledge and build comprehensive multi-level time-specific cost-based BEPMs to facilitate healthcare policy formulation and improvement of NMHOs in Singapore and beyond.
kw: tooth, deciduous; prenatal exposure delay effects; growth and development; biomarkers; neurodevelopmental disorders

title: Evaluating the cost-effectiveness of antimicrobial stewardship interventions in Singapore hospitals
abs: In Singapore, hospitals antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) programmes use different interventions to promote appropriate antibiotic use. However, decision-makers today do not have evidence on which AMS interventions are cost-effective and should be given priority. Our goal is to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of different AMS interventions in three Singapore major hospitals, considering both the health system perspective and societal perspective. We will develop decision analytic models to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of AMS intervention, and combinations of different interventions, in each hospital. Data from hospitals' medical records, AMS database, previously completed AMS research and quality improvement work, published literature, and expert opinion will be used as model input parameters. Transmission dynamics and Bayesian regression methods will be used to estimate the costs and outcomes related to impact on antibiotic spread and resistance trajectories. Since we may encounter incomplete information for some parameters, it is important to formally address the uncertainty in our research. Hence, we will conduct value of information analyses to identify parameters that contribute most to decision uncertainty, to set an evidence-based agenda for future AMS research. Identifying cost-effective AMS interventions will help us achieve our goal of improving the efficiency of the healthcare system. Continued adoption of cost-effective AMS interventions will be recommended, while disinvestment of interventions that are not cost-effective will be considered. Resources saved can then be redirected to meet other healthcare needs.
kw: antimicrobial resistance; antimicrobial stewardship programme; cost-effectiveness; health services research; economic analyses

title: Abdominal adipose tissue phenotype-based risk stratification for metabolic syndrome in children
inst: IHDP - Institute for Human Development and Potential
abs: Obesity, particularly abdominal obesity, is a significant public health concern due to its strong association with metabolic syndrome and cardiometabolic diseases. Recent advances in deep learning models, have enabled accurate segmentation and quantification of abdominal superficial (SSAT) and deep subcutaneous adipose tissue (DSAT), intraperitoneal (IPAT) and retroperitoneal adipose tissue (RPAT). These depots have distinct structural and functional characteristics and show differential associations with metabolic risk. Our earlier research identified a metabolically unfavorable abdominal adipose tissue (AAT) phenotype in women (SPRESTO study), characterized by a higher proportion of IPAT and a lower proportion of DSAT. This phenotype was significantly associated with an increased prevalence of metabolic syndrome, liver fat, higher risk of developing gestational diabetes, and alterations in the plasma lipidome. However, there is a notable gap in the literature regarding AAT phenotyping in children. We aim to identify and characterize metabolically distinct AAT distribution phenotypes in children and evaluate their sex-specific manifestations. By leveraging previously identified AAT phenotypes in SPRESTO women, we will assess the manifestation and relationship of these phenotypes with cardiometabolic health in children from the GUSTO study. We will perform longitudinal tracking of adipose tissue remodeling from childhood to adolescence using unsupervised modeling techniques. Additionally, we will examine lipidomic and metabolomic signatures of the identified phenotypes to understand the biochemical pathways contributing to metabolic risk. We will also validate the use of digital photography-based body volume index assessment for metabolic risk stratification. With the increasing prevalence of childhood obesity in Singapore, understanding AAT phenotypes and their associated cardiometabolic risks in childhood is imperative for early identification and intervention. The body volume index can serve as a practical and scalable tool for screening large populations. Our proposal could significantly improve population health outcomes by facilitating targeted management strategies and enhancing public health policies on obesity and metabolic disorders.
kw: Deep subcutaneous adipose tissue; Intraperitoneal adipose tissue; Abdominal adipose tissue distribution; Metabolic syndrome; Body volume index; Metabolomics

title: Breast cancer Risk prediction Incorporating metabolic Dysfunction, obesity and Guidance on lifestylE modification (BRIDGE)
abs: This study focuses on breast cancer (BC) in Singapore, where incidence is rising faster than in Western countries. Obesity and metabolic dysfunction, both modifiable risk factors, are linked to BC risk. However, there is limited research in Singapore on preventing BC through managing these factors. To address this gap, the study proposes analyses using large Singapore-based cohort studies with high-quality exposure data and cancer registries. The research has three key aims: 1. Understanding BC Risk Factors: Using nested case-control studies within the Singapore Population Health Studies (SPHS) and the Singapore Chinese Health Study (SCHS), the researchers will estimate the contribution of obesity and metabolic dysfunction to BC incidence. They will also assess variations in risk by BC subtype, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status. Additionally, they will evaluate the impact of other modifiable lifestyle factors on BC risk. 2. Improving BC Risk Prediction: The study will explore pre-diagnostic blood-based metabolic biomarkers and incorporate obesity-related measures into new BC risk models. These models will be tested against traditional models to determine if they improve detection rates without increasing screening visits. 3. Enhancing Prognostic Tools: The researchers will investigate how overweight/obesity at diagnosis affects BC outcomes, considering factors such as treatment and tumour characteristics. They will also analyze the role of visceral fat composition in BC prognosis. The study's findings will inform the design of risk-based BC screening trials and preventive lifestyle intervention programs for women at high-risk of BC in Singapore.
kw: Health Promotion, Preventative Health, Cancer, Obesity, Diabetes, Metabolic Health

title: Assessing the effectiveness and implementation of a collaborative shared care model for breast cancer survivors with multimorbidity
abs: Background: Breast cancer survivors with multimorbidity face complex care needs due to the combined burden of cancer and chronic conditions. Fragmented care, poor medication adherence, and long-term treatment side effects often hinder effective multimorbidity management, increasing the risk of poor health outcomes and premature cardiovascular mortality. The current oncologist-led model in Singapore focuses on cancer surveillance but lacks a structured approach to chronic disease management. We propose a shared care model integrating oncologists, family physicians, and community pharmacists to improve care coordination, medication adherence, and self-efficacy, ultimately optimizing multimorbidity management. Aims & hypotheses: We aim to assess the effectiveness of a shared care model for breast cancer survivors with multimorbidity. We hypothesize that shared care will improve multimorbidity management as compared to usual care through reducing unmet needs and symptom burden, improving medication adherence and self-efficacy, and strengthening care coordination. Concurrently, we aim to assess ways to improve the implementation of the model in Singapore. Approach: To assess effectiveness, we will conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) recruiting 140 breast cancer survivors with multimorbidity from the National Cancer Centre Singapore. Data on multimorbidity management will be extracted from electronic health records at 12th month, and participants will complete patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) at baseline, 6th, and 12th month. Guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, we will assess implementation through stakeholder interviews and process evaluation. Study feasibility: We have piloted an acceptable and feasible shared care model in Singapore and demonstrated that an RCT design is feasible with a reasonable recruitment rate, high retention, fidelity, and PROM completion rates. Importance: Establishing the shared care model as an effective and sustainable alternative to specialist-led care can reduce reliance on specialized manpower and inform broader implementation strategies, empowering cancer survivors to lead healthier lives while lowering mortality risk.
kw: shared care model; breast cancer; cancer survivorship; supportive care; multimorbidity; health services research

title: A Novel Multi-Antigen Targeting Cellular Therapy Approach for AML
abs: Acute leukemia is the most common cancer in children. While overall cure rates have improved over the years, prognosis remains poor for patients with relapsed/ refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells have emerged as a new curative option for patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). By contrast, the clinical results of CAR-T cells for AML have been disappointing. The overall objective of this project is to develop effective CAR-T cell therapy for AML. We hypothesize that CAR-T cells targeting multiple antigens can exert major anti-tumor activity in AML. We aim to develop CAR-T cells directed against myeloid antigens that can be combined with anti-CD7 CAR-T cells. Our clinical data has shown that anti-CD7 CAR-T cells are highly effective in T-ALL. CD7 is also expressed in up to 30% of AML cases. Therefore, anti-CD7 CAR-T cells hold potential as anti-AML agents, particularly when combined with CAR-T cells directed against myeloid antigens, such as CD33 and CD123. Because CD7 is also expressed by CAR-T cells, any CAR-T cell therapy targeting CD7 must be designed to avert CAR-T cell self-killing or fratricide. Our aim is to design and develop fratricide resistant anti-CD33 and anti-CD123 CAR-T cells. The functional capacity of CAR-T cells directed against CD7, CD33 and CD123 will be assessed. The results of this study will inform the design of pre-clinical testing of anti-CD33 and anti-CD123 CAR-T cells in xenograft mouse models of AML. The research proposed relies on unique technologies developed in our laboratory, long-standing expertise in CAR-T cell development, an active cell manufacturing facility, and a track record of translating CAR-T cell therapies to the clinic. Given our recent success with anti-CD7 CAR-T cells, this project represents an important next step that could potentially advance cures for patients with AML.
kw: Acute Myeloid Leukemia, CAR-T cell therapy, cellular therapy, CD7, CD33, CD123, cancer

title: Implementation Effectiveness of an AI-enabled mhealth application EMPOWER and INteGrated priMary care Ecosystem (EMPOWERING-ME) to improve outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus patients - a hybrid type 2 cluster randomised controlled trial
abs: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus among Singaporean adults is projected to reach 13.3% by 2030. Effective management requires an interdisciplinary and patient-centred approach integrating pharmacological and non-pharmacological cares. General practitioners (GPs), who manage about 80% of primary care and 55% of chronic disease care, face challenges such as limited resources, absence of robust IT systems, and a lack of data-sharing frameworks. While digital health solutions are promising in enhancing care delivery, their integration into GP practices remains challenging and underexplored. EMPOWERING-ME addresses these challenges with three key components: (1) interdisciplinary care and social prescriptions through collaboration between GPs and SingHealth Healthier Singapore (HSG) team; (2) the EMPOWER+ mHealth application, paired with wearable trackers, to leverage patient-generated health data (PGHD) and deliver AI-driven educational and behavioural nudges; and (3) a robust data-sharing framework among key stakeholders to integrate PGHD into care workflows for personalised interventions. EMPOWERING-ME will be co-designed, piloted, and implemented in 24 GP practices across SingHealth regions. Using a hybrid type 2 effectiveness-implementation cluster randomised controlled trial design, we will evaluate the intervention’s implementation, clinical effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness over six months. Primary outcomes include improvements in glycaemic control (measured by glycated haemoglobin), with secondary outcomes examining diabetes-related quality of life, emotional distress, self-efficacy, and sustained health behaviour changes six months post-intervention, and cost-effectiveness. We will also examine the intervention’s scalability and sustainability within GP practices. Supported by key GP leaders and aligned with HSG ‘s strategic priorities, EMPOWERING-ME has the potential to redefine chronic disease management in Singapore by improving care coordination in primary care and empowering patients through personlised data-driven care. Its findings will inform national policies on digital health implementation and data sharing, offering a scalable model for enhancing chronic disease management in primary care, promoting population health management, and contributing to the digital transformation.
kw: primary care; cluster randomised controlled trial; hybrid trial; interdisciplinary and person-centred care; type 2 diabetes mellitus; digital health

title: Implementation of a Patient & Caregiver Coaching Intervention for Patients with Advanced Cancer Undergoing Major Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial with Hybrid Type 1 Implementation Design
abs: Current generalist palliative care (PC) model in surgical oncology faces two major challenges. First, patients with advanced cancer lack receptiveness and are unprepared for surgeon-delivered PC. Furthermore, caregivers who often play critical roles in decision-making are not well-attuned to the patient’s’ PC needs. This results in surgical care that is not aligned with the patients’ goals and preferences, decreasing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and increasing healthcare utilization. Coaching informed by the serious illness care program’s pedagogy has been shown to enhance decision-making and future planning PC aspects. At present, caregivers are not routinely involved, and few interventions exist to improve patient-caregiver communication. To address limitations in generalist PC delivery, we propose a patient-centred, caregiver-supported coaching program - Coaching in surgical ONCology to improve Readiness and Decisions (CONCORD), before and after major surgery. A trained care coach will deliver coaching sessions focusing on decision-making and future planning aspects, while facilitating patient-caregiver communication. This is opposed to usual care where only surgeons are trained to deliver PC, including the conduct of serious illness conversations (SIC) and advance care planning (ACP), and patients and their caregivers are not coached on PC interventions and benefits. We conduct a 2-arm randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of CONCORD over usual care on quality of SIC, decisional conflict, HRQoL, goal-concordant care, ACP rates, healthcare utilization and costs in patients with advanced cancer and their caregivers. We hypothesize that CONCORD is effective over usual care in patient and caregiver-centric outcomes. We also evaluate implementational processes in a hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation design using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance framework. If proven effective, CONCORD can transform surgical care delivery by integrating PC-trained surgeons with well-prepared patients and caregivers. It is also scalable and can be adopted to improve quality care for other seriously ill patients.
kw: Palliative care, advanced cancer, surgery, coaching

title: Sepsis Optimal Recognition Toolkit in children (SORT): An early recognition tool for children in Asia
abs: Paediatric sepsis accounts for more than 3 million deaths worldwide annually, while survivors are at risk of neurodevelopmental disorders and poor health-related quality of life. Early recognition of sepsis is vital to expedite initial resuscitation, reduce mortality and lower healthcare costs. Current gaps include the lack of (i) a local data-driven early recognition tool, (ii) benchmarking of recognition tools against an internationally accepted and high-performing paediatric sepsis definition, and (iii) collaborative paediatric sepsis research in Asia. Therefore, we seek to improve the early recognition of children with sepsis in Asia, through the derivation and validation of Sepsis Optimal Recognition Toolkit in children (SORT). Specifically, we aim to derive SORT among children (1-month – 18-years-old) with suspected infection presenting to KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH), and National University Hospital (NUH) using patient demographics, vital signs and co-morbidities, as well as point-of-care-tests. We hypothesize that SORT will perform with a sensitivity of 90% and a c-statistic of at least 0.85 in predicting for sepsis (defined by a Phoenix Sepsis Score of 2 or greater). We also aim to validate SORT among children with suspected infection in participating Pediatric Acute and Critical Care Medicine in Asia Network (PACCMAN) sites with varying resource availability. We hypothesize that SORT will perform with a sensitivity of 90% and a c-statistic of at least 0.80 in predicting for sepsis (defined by a Phoenix Sepsis Score of 2 or greater). Finally, we aim to study the feasibility and acceptability of implementing SORT in clinical practice at KKH. We hypothesize that SORT can be successfully incorporated into clinical care. This study answers the call of the Singapore National Action Plan for Sepsis (SNAPS) to improve clinical recognition of sepsis, and provides a platform for paediatric sepsis data to be systematically collected at national and regional levels.
kw: sepsis; child; early recognition; risk stratification; Phoenix

title: The Effectiveness of Multidisciplinary Protocolised Interventions to Reduce non-adherencE rates (EMPIRE) in patients with chronic macula diseases receiving intravitreal injections: A randomised controlled trial
abs: Overall Aim: Data on the effectiveness of interventions to improve adherence to intravitreal therapy (IVT) in patients with chronic macula diseases are limited. We aim to assess whether a personalised multi-disciplinary protocolised intervention (MPI), implemented based on patients’ quality of life (QoL) domain scores using computerised adaptive testing (CAT), enhances adherence; clinical parameters; macular-specific CAT QoL domain scores; and is cost-effective with the potential for implementation. Methods: This prospective, randomised control trial will recruit 200 patients with neovascular age-related macula degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macula edema (DME) treated with IVT from a single, tertiary eye centre. The MPI comprises medical consultations to optimize the treatment regime with referrals to: (a) nurse-directed patient education program; (b) low vision optometrist; (c) occupational therapy services; and (d) a medical social worker, based on suboptimal MacCAT (nAMD) and RetCAT (DME) scores. Standard care includes a medical consultation, where the clinicians, masked to the CAT scores, will make treatment decisions and referrals based on their own discretion. Adherence rates will be calculated every 6 months, with the main time point at 18 months (primary outcome measure). CAT scores, visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, and disease free intervals determined by retinal imaging, will be assessed at baseline and every follow-up visit. A cost-effectiveness analysis and qualitative interviewing will assess appropriateness, acceptability and feasibility of the MPI implementation. Expected Outcomes: MPI will improve adherence rates, and clinical and QoL outcomes as measured by disease-specific CAT scores, compared to standard care and will be an appropriate, acceptable and feasible intervention, and is cost-effective. Potential Impact: Our proposed MPI introduces a novel approach to address the unique needs of each patient to promote adherence, will guide clinicians on appropriate and effective interventions in response to QoL scores, and represents a significant step towards patient-centered care.
kw: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Healthy and Meaningful Longevity, Implementation Science, Precision Medicine

title: Developing an AI deep learning-based paThology solution for predictive biomArker predictioN for oncoloGy clinical trials allocation (DATANG)
abs: The growing cancer patient demographic far exceeds the limited availability of clinical trials, with delays in trial matching and patient recruitment contributing to a >90% trial failure rate and an annual loss of >USD 9 billion. Immune profiling, including immunohistochemistry and multiplex immunohistochemistry, is essential for efficient trial recruitment and biomarker discovery to identify patient subsets who may benefit from trials. However, its widespread adoption is hindered by high costs, technical complexity, limited tissue availability, and labour-intensive processes. Given our track record in spatial biology and developing artificial intelligence (AI) solutions to advance drug development in clinical trial (on-going Phase 1b), it demonstrates our ability to integrate cutting-edge technology and positions us uniquely to innovate effective solutions. The current trend of combining immunotherapy with antibody-drug conjugates increases the need for biomarker testing, both individually and in combination, to guide therapeutic decision. With challenges such as limited tissue availability, high cost, and manpower constraints, AI presents a promising solution. The study objective is to accelerate the process of patient triage during clinical trial recruitment by developing an AI solution that integrates our AI pathology concept known as H&E 2.0, to screen multiple clinically relevant and actionable predictive biomarkers for clinical trials. It will be a robust and scalable AI-driven pipeline using H&E 2.0 that improves cost-effectiveness and efficiency of patient triage and outcome prediction. The hypothesis is that H&E 2.0 can detect biomarkers at a single-cell level directly from H&E-stained whole slide images, which are routinely acquired in large volumes at low cost in the clinic. This approach complements existing pathology workflow and reduces unnecessary tests, costs, workload, and turnaround time while maintaining accuracy and accelerating clinical trial recruitment. Biomarker-specific AI solution as companion diagnostic assay will be developed with industrial partners for regulatory clearance.
kw: AI, clinical trial, oncology, pathology

title: From Prototype to Full Deployment: A Comprehensive Deep Learning Pipeline for Whole-Spine MRI
abs: Back pain is widespread, affecting up to 80% of adults in Singapore and significantly impacting quality of life. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the spine is commonly performed to detect and grade stenosis, identify spinal cord compression, and assess for other conditions including disc disease, fractures and spondylolisthesis. With an estimated 120,000 spine MRI examinations performed annually in Singapore, timely and accurate interpretation is essential yet challenging. Over the past award period, we successfully developed and deployed a prototype deep learning (DL) model for lumbar spine MRI and signed a technology development agreement with an industry partner to advance this solution. We have also made considerable progress in cervical spine DL model development. These achievements provide a strong foundation for the next phase of research, which this grant renewal will support. The goal is to further develop and fully deploy our DL pipeline for comprehensive whole-spine MRI interpretation. By expanding the DL models to cover the entire spine, this project aims to streamline reporting workflows, improve diagnostic accuracy, and enable earlier clinical interventions. The renewed funding will support full-scale deployment of a whole-spine solution, incorporating an optimised user interface and experience (UI/UX), structured reporting capabilities, and tools for longitudinal follow-up. Through these advancements, we aim to create a clinically viable tool that enhances patient care while reducing healthcare costs. Overall Aims: Aim 1: Further develop and deploy DL models for stenosis assessment and spinal cord compression in the cervical and thoracic spine, building on the lumbar spine prototype and technology partnership. The UI/UX will be optimized to include structured reporting and tools for longitudinal follow-up. Aim 2: Expand DL capabilities beyond stenosis assessment to include detection and grading of fractures, spondylolisthesis, intervertebral disc disease, endplate changes, and facet joint arthropathy, integrating these features into a unified pipeline for clinical deployment.
kw: Spine; MRI; Deep learning; Artificial intelligence; Back pain; Radiology

title: Social return on investment (SROI) for universal youth mental health screening: a discrete-choice experiment
abs: A large proportion of youths in Singapore experience symptoms of anxiety and depression yet remain untreated, resulting in large health and human capital losses with potentially life-long consequences. A universal youth mental health screening programme (including referral and evidence-based treatment) has been proposed as a solution to address this growing public health challenge. The objective of this study is to conduct a forecast social return on investment (SROI) analysis of expanding mental health screening for anxiety and depression targeting youths aged 12–17 (secondary school) in efforts to identify the societal value that Singaporeans place on such a programme. This will be achieved using a discrete choice experiment (DCE) administered to a nationally representative sample through a low-cost web panel. Social value will be quantified by modality of screening (school-based vs healthcare provider-based screening) and as a function of potential changes in youth mental health symptoms and other relevant indicators identified by key stakeholders. Using these findings, along with implementation cost estimates for each modality, we will calculate the SROI for school-based and healthcare provider-based (GPs, polyclinics, paediatricians) screening programmes under both more and less optimistic scenarios. We hypothesize that both screening approaches will show a positive social return on investment, but that, all else equal, Singaporeans will prefer healthcare provider-based screening. These results will assist the Ministry of Health as they consider whether to use public funds to expand youth mental health screening in Singapore.
kw: health economics; discrete choice experiments; mental health

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Peripheral Blood Film Analysis
abs: Background: Peripheral blood film (PBF) analysis is a cornerstone of hematological diagnostics, yet it remains labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Existing AI solutions lack explainability, limiting their adoption due to end-user distrust and difficulty in detecting rare but clinically significant cells. This study aims to enhance Blade, an AI-driven digital analysis platform, by integrating Explainable AI (XAI) to improve the accuracy and transparency of PBF interpretation. Specific Aims Develop an XAI-enabled deep learning model to classify both mature and immature white blood cells, providing interpretable predictions that enhance end-user confidence. Extend Blade’s capability to red blood cell morphology and lymphoproliferative disorders Validate the AI model’s diagnostic accuracy and real-world feasibility Methodology & Approach: A dataset of 100,000 red blood cells and 100,000 lymphoproliferative cells obtained from 500 digitalized PBF slides will be annotated by laboratory medical technologists and hematologists, ensuring high-quality ground truth labels, and combined with an existing annotated dataset of 282,997 blood cells that was used to train the first model of Blade. The new model will be trained using a dual-model architecture—integrating YOLO for classification and Random Forest with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for interpretability. The AI’s accuracy will be assessed using AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score, while its explainability will be evaluated through user acceptance studies. A blinded clinical validation with laboratory staff and hematologists will determine improvements in diagnostic confidence and efficiency. Feasibility & Importance: The study leverages existing collaborations between NHG, NTU, and ASUS Intelligent Cloud Services (AICS), ensuring technical and clinical feasibility. The proposed solution has the potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy, improve workflow efficiency, and reduce laboratory burden, leading to faster and more reliable hematology diagnostics. If successful, this research could transform AI adoption in laboratory medicine, establishing Singapore as a leader in explainable medical AI.
kw: Artificial Intelligence; Deep Learning; Haematology; Peripheral Blood Film; Clinical Decision Support

title: Iterative Co-Design for Sustainable and Scalable Implementation of an AI-Driven Modular Platform
abs: Visual impairment (VI) affects approximately 600 million people worldwide, including 20% of elderly individuals in Singapore, a number projected to reach 350,000 by 2030. While half of these cases result from uncorrected refractive errors that can be corrected with spectacles, the remaining cases stem from major eye diseases such as cataract, diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma, which require timely medical intervention. Early detection through vision screening is essential to prevent vision loss and improve quality of life. However, current screening models are less efficient making them inadequate to meet future demands. To address this, we propose AVIRI 2.0, an AI-driven vision screening platform that integrates multiple diagnostic models through a router algorithm. This system intelligently directs retinal images to relevant disease-specific AI models, such as those for DR, AMD, and glaucoma, thereby reducing computational demand, improving diagnostic accuracy, and optimizing workflow. Unlike conventional AI-based approaches that require multiple models to run simultaneously, this platform enhances real-time processing while maintaining high diagnostic performance. To ensure successful real-world deployment, this study will adopt a structured co-design and iterative refinement process, engaging stakeholders, including general practitioners, optometrists, community health organizers, and patients. This implementation approach will be guided by the EPIS (Exploration, Preparation, Implementation, Sustainment) and CFIR (Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research) frameworks, which will help systematically map existing workflows, identify barriers, and refine implementation strategies based on real-world feedback. AVIRI 2.0 will be evaluated in two key settings: periodic polyclinic-based screening and mobile vision screening at community health events. By integrating AI with real-world implementation science, this study seeks to establish an efficient, sustainable, and scalable efficient AI-assisted vision screening model. The insights gained from AVIRI 2.0 will contribute to Singapore’s Smart Nation initiative by leveraging technology to enhance healthcare accessibility, efficiency, and preventive eye care.
kw: Vision, Screening, Artificial Intelligence, Preventive health, Implementation, Co-design, AI-driven, Multi-disciplinary

title: Characterising PIK3CA mutation variants for individualised treatment of PIK3CA mutant colorectal cancer
abs: PIK3CA mutations occur in up to 20% of colorectal cancer. Given PIK3CA's critical role in cellular proliferation and invasion, patients whose cancers possess a mutation in this gene have a worse overall prognosis. The top three commonest sites of mutation in the PIK3CA gene are the E545K, H1047R, as well as the R88Q missense mutations. Presently, mutations of this gene are considered without a deeper understanding of the unique impact of each mutation variant of PIK3CA. The aim of this proposal is to characterise the effect of each PIK3CA mutation variant. We hypothesise that different mutation variants confer a unique cellular phenotype to the cancer cell, and that the molecular mechanisms underpinning these effects can be targeted to deliver personalised therapy for cancer patients with a PIK3CA mutation. We aim to generate the above three PIK3CA mutation variants in colorectal cell lines using prime editing. Having generated these mutation variants, we will proceed to test for differences in downstream mediators of PIK3CA such as AKT and mTOR. We would also perform experiments into cellular phenotype by investigating cellular invasion, migration, proliferation, and apoptosis. The PI has completed doctoral training at the University of Oxford and is the recipient of an NMRC Transition Award. He runs a small group who will use the funds provided in this grant to generate pilot results to apply for larger grant funding. Findings from this research is highly important as PIK3CA mutations are ubiquitous in a range of cancer including colorectal, and breast cancer. Understanding unique molecular perturbations in the PIK3CA gene moves away from treating all mutations equally, and instead focuses on how unique mutation variants change cellular processes which affect oncologic phenotype. This paves the way for personalised treatment in patients who have a PIK3CA mutation.
kw: colorectal cancer; mutant variants, PIK3CA, personalised treatment

title: Evaluation of the relationship between inflammatory cytokines and loss of myogenic potential in sarcopenia
abs: Sarcopenia, the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength, affects nearly one in three older adults in Singapore. Despite its high prevalence and association with poor outcomes, sarcopenia remains underdiagnosed and poorly stratified. A major limitation lies in current clinical criteria, such as AWGS 2019, which do not reflect the biological complexity of disease. Without molecular insight, therapeutic progress remains stalled. Recent data from our group offer a new direction. Using what is likely the world’s only sarcopenia-phenotyped human biorepository with matched muscle and serum samples, we identified four distinct molecular subtypes (G1–G4) marked by progressive inflammation and loss of myogenic programs. These findings, validated across bulk RNA-seq, snRNA-seq, histology, and epigenomics, point to inflammation as a central, potentially modifiable driver of muscle degeneration. However, the mechanistic link between systemic inflammation and impaired regeneration remains untested. This disconnect reveals an urgent need to shift from observation to mechanism: How do circulating cytokines alter muscle-intrinsic signaling to impair regeneration in sarcopenia? Addressing this question is critical, not only to clarify disease biology, but to guide future therapeutic strategies that move beyond general anti-inflammatory approaches. We hypothesize that systemic inflammation drives muscle-intrinsic inflammatory signaling that suppresses myogenic regeneration in sarcopenia. This proposal directly tests that hypothesis by using patient-derived muscle and serum samples to define how inflammation alters regenerative biology. We will address this through two aims: Aim 1: Identify serum cytokines associated with transcriptionally defined subtypes of sarcopenia. Aim 2: Define how inflammatory cytokines impair muscle regeneration.
kw: sarcopenia; inflammation; regenerative medicine; ageing; mechanism; treatment

title: Environments of Adolescents on Sleep and socio-Emotional development (EASE)
inst: IHDP - Institute for Human Development and Potential
abs: Background: Adolescents of today face unprecedented challenges that can impact their development, mental and overall wellbeing, such as social media influences and academic pressure. Social and emotional learning (SEL) equips them with essential skills to navigate the complexities of their lives. By enhancing their emotional intelligence and interpersonal skills, SEL fosters resilience and prepares them to cope with challenges effectively, leading to healthier relationships and better overall well-being. Supportive and conducive environments are important for optimal SEL. Adolescence also coincides with a period where there are significant changes in sleep patterns such as delayed sleep-wake phase. Physical environment, academic stress and wellbeing of the family unit are associated with sleep in youths and sleep problems are known to negatively impact executive function, resilience, mood and emotion regulation of youths. Objectives: Aim 1 will be to establish the relationship between various environmental factors around adolescents: learning, material and socio-familial environments, and study the link between these environments and SEL. Aims 2 and 3 evaluate respectively, the mediating and moderating role of sleep between the various environments and SEL of adolescents. Aim 4 uses dynamic network analysis to study the temporal change in the network structure of the established relationships among the factors from early to mid-adolescence. Methods: This project will be nested within the GUSTO cohort study where the children are currently between 13 to 14 (n=874). This project will include two work packages that covers early adolescence (age 10 to 14 years) and middle adolescence (age 15 to 17 years): (1) Work Package 1 (age 10 to 14 years) will use existing data already collected in GUSTO (2) Work Package 2 (age 15 to 17 years) will involve new data collection on environments, sleep and SEL outcomes. This study will adopt a mixed-methods approach, incorporating both quantitative and qualitative data collection. Briefly, we will have objective measures using accelerometer (sleep and light), subjective measures of their environment (e.g. noise perception, neighbourhood perception) and the adolescents’ self-reports of their sleep and social-emotional development. Laboratory task(s) will be conducted to measure executive function. We will also perform environmental data modelling using postal code (residential and school) and public data. We will use Network Analysis to establish the relationships and pathways of the exposure (environment), mediator/moderator (sleep) and outcomes (SEL and SEL outcomes). Thereafter, we will use Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and mediation analysis to formally test the relationships and quantify the effect size. Dynamic Network Analysis will be used to study the change in network structure between early and mid-adolescence. title: Structured Atomic Materials for Symmetry-Fusion Topological Photonics
abs: Atomic materials with rich macroscopic topological phases are revolutionizing quantum information, medical imaging, energy technologies, and material science. However, the practical application of most atomic materials faces constraints, operating at small-size (< 10 mm) and low temperature (< 250 K). Overcoming these long-existing challenges is pivotal for advancing paradigm-shift atomic-material-integrated topological photonics, as the real-world impact of on-chip photonics requires the integration of wafer-size (~8-inch, 200 mm) atomic materials with photonic structures, operating at room-temperature (300 K). Addressing those challenges requires not only breakthroughs in engineering but also in-depth and interdisciplinary science explorations in multiphysical systems (electronics, photonics and polaritonics) across drastically varying scales from the atomic, to wavelength and wafer scales. We aim to establish a new paradigm of structured atomic materials (SAMs), fusing hierarchical symmetries, quasi-particle behaviors, and photonic meta-structures in both energy and size scales to realize configurable symmetry-fused topological photonic devices. This paradigm will be explored at multiple levels to build novel SAMs, operate emerging topological phases, and realize innovative topological photonic devices with a wafer-size ( >8-inch, about 200 mm) at a room temperature (300 K). This will be achieved by developing multiscale multiphysics theory and integrating and configurating both atomic material and photonic structural symmetries. The fusion of fundamental principles from physics, optics, materials science, and engineering can bring these visionary concepts to life — a testament to the power of interdisciplinary research in shaping the future of photonics. These specific goals become accessible, though still challenging, thanks to our team's world-leading and complementary technical expertise. We anticipate that our efforts will reshape the landscape of future technologies, ranging from electronics to photonics and energy transmission to quantum computing. Achieving our aims will yield proof-of-principle demonstrations for groundbreaking SAMs and their resultant configurable topological photonic devices, laying the foundation for future advancements in science and technology. Our objectives embody a meticulously designed program poised to establish an internationally competitive initiative in SAMs within the local context of Singapore.
kw: Structured Atomic Materials; Symmetry-Fusion; Topological Photonics

title: Bedtime-advance intervention to improve adolescent sleep, attention, & wellbeing
abs: Background: Healthy sleep is important for learning and wellbeing. Adolescents should be sleeping for about 8 hours at night in synch with their circadian rhythm of melatonin. However, Singaporean adolescents get only about 6.5 h of sleep on school nights, and they go to bed late and wake up early relative to their melatonin rhythm. This is a major concern because short sleep and circadian misalignment are associated with impaired cognitive performance, daytime sleepiness, and lower mood and motivation. title: PERFORM: PERsonalized learning digital platFORM for assessing and training cognitive abilities
abs: Training can improve performance on numerous cognitive tasks, including those that involve executive function to coordinate multiple sensory inputs and motor outputs. These high-level cognitive functions decline with age, with noticeable decrements even in middle adulthood, yet they are important for managing daily life and learning new skills. In this project, we propose to develop a tablet-based platform for training executive function in a multitasking context, evaluating learning through lab-based assessments of behavior and neurophysiological measures. Specifically, we will modify our existing platform based on the NASA-developed Multi-Attribute Task Battery (MATB), aiming for effective at-home use with an adaptive training procedure designed to increase gains and transfer to a lab-based setting. We will then recruit a large community sample (n=150, ages 40-60) to participate in a 10-week training programme with an active control arm. Participants will train for three days per week at home and also come to the lab for three evaluation sessions (weeks 0, 5, and 10). They will return for follow-ups to check retention (weeks 26 and 42). During the in-lab sessions, we will record EEG and gaze patterns while the participants perform the MATB tasks. Participants will also segment a replay of their actions into events and complete a cognitive task battery to test for transfer effects. We expect to observe gradual increases in performance, modulations to fronto-parietal attentional control networks, and alterations in gaze patterns and reported event boundaries with training. We will test whether these changes or other markers are predictors of training success, potentially identifying future intermediate training targets.
kw: training; cognition; multitasking; remote learning; EEG; event segmentation

title:
Printed logic from mixed ionic-electronic halides for sustainable hybrid
electronics
abs: Printed logic components such as thin film transistors and memories are key for enabling concepts such as ubiquitous electronics, wearables and the internet of everything. These printed devices serve as integral components within hybrid electronic systems, enabling the deployment of highly distributed sensors, communication and authentication devices that can be embedded in physical spaces to monitor human activities, manage healthcare, and monitor resources. Hybrid electronics integrate conventional CMOS-based electronic components with non-traditional printed technologies for enhanced functionalities and novel applications. Since heavy processing would remain CMOS-based, the opportunity for materials, green processing, and disruptive devices lies in the sensing and communication modules. While additive electronic printing is increasingly recognized as a more sustainable manufacturing process due to their reduced resource usage, much of the research has focussed on the passive dielectric components and interconnects. The choice for the printable active semiconducting materials is still unclear. Halide perovskites are strong candidates for printed logic due to their low-temperature processability, long-range carrier transport length and high absorption coefficients. In addition to modulatable structural and optoelectronic properties, they possess a unique advantage- ionicity. Since they are mixed ionic-electronic conductors, they are imbued with interesting phenomena such as chemical inductance, low-energy stimuli-responsiveness and electronic memory to enable novel reconfigurable devices. While Pb-based perovskites are widely studied, lead-free halide perovskites share the advantages listed above. They offer a tantalizing blend of tunable optoelectronic properties and ease of fabrication, making them ideal for a wide range of applications in printed electronics. In parallel to targeting performance enhancement, cost-effective manufacturing and sustainable lifecycle management also need to be pursued. The true cost (both economic and environmental) and sustainable lifecycle management can only be considered by adopting a green approach through the electronic product’s entire life cycle (both manufacturing and end-of-life management). In this proposal, we aim to realize green hybrid ionic-electronic devices based on lead-free halide perovskites fabricated via additive manufacturing. The choice of materials and fabrication will be informed by a full life cycle approach, considering the environmental footprint of fabrication as well as end of life management. Recycling of high impact materials will also be evaluated. Our specific aims include (A) developing novel eco-friendly lead-free perovskite inks, (B) constructing proof of concept logic devices using additive manufacturing and (C) develop sustainable electronics via a thorough life cycle and recyclability analysis. The first work package aims to develop non-toxic and stable lead-free perovskite
