title: Optotwistronics: Enabling Ultrahigh-efficiency Nanoscale Nonlinear Light Sources
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Nonlinear light sources harvest the nonlinearity of materials, such as second-harmonic generation (SHG) and spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) process, and are of fundamental significance in advancing modern quantum technologies. To achieve high quantum efficiency, traditional nonlinear optical crystals with stringent phase matching conditions are exploited with centimeter bulk size, rendering them fundamentally unscalable and substantially impeding the widespread integrated photonics and quantum technologies. In this project, we aim to harness the recent scientific breakthrough of optotwistronics with emerging van der Waals (vdW) materials for ultrahigh-efficiency nanoscale nonlinear and quantum light sources. It aims to overcome the challenge of the intrinsic short light-matter length of nonlinear vdW solids via a systematic development of synergetic efforts. The workscope comprises: 1) vdW twistronics including the establishment of a data library of nonlinear vdW solids, twisted phase matching, and inverse design for highly efficient twistronic vdW solids; 2) moiré twistronics including the moiré patterned vdW solids with significantly enhanced vacuum fluctuations; 3) synthetic twistronics via multiphysics hybridization of nanophotonic resonance with vdW solids; 4) twistronic engineering by scalable fabrication. Our objective is to demonstrate nanoscale quantum light sources with a quantum efficiency, i.e., SHG efficiency of 3.2x10^-7 W^-1 and SPDC efficiency of 1x10^8 GHz W^-1 m^-1 respectively (~10^4x higher than layered niobium oxide chloride (NbOCl2)). Through this project, our team will overcome the technology bottleneck of quantum efficiency and achieve a breakthrough in realizing ultra-compact on-chip quantum light sources and modulators, that address demands from next-generation quantum photonics technologies.
kw: Optotwistronics; quantum efficiency; nanoscale nonlinear light source; twisting and stacking; moiré engineering; quantum entanglement

title: DEBUT: Discovering Novel Biomarkers and Unveiling Therapeutic Vulnerabilities in Drug-tolerant Persister (DTP) cells
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Drug resistance is a significant challenge in precision medicine, particularly acquired resistance, which limits systemic treatment efficacy. Drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells contribute to minimal residual disease (MRD), leading to disease relapse and cancer-related mortality. Targeting DTPs is thus vital for preventing tumour relapse. Equally important is the ability to detect and monitor DTPs early during therapy. Progress in these areas is hindered by the lack of reliable biomarkers for identifying DTP cells. In our preliminary work, we used a dual-colour fluorescent timer (FT) reporter system to monitor persister cell kinetics in real time. This led to the identification of the novel surface biomarker, distinguishing slow-cycling DTPs from primary resistant cells, a significant advancement in DTP research. This discovery offers a precise tool for studying resistance trajectories and presents promising opportunities to identify new biomarkers and therapeutic targets for targeting DTPs and DTP-derived resistant states. Our research objectives: 1. Deciphering DTP Biology: Investigating the biology, biomarkers, and therapeutic vulnerabilities of distinct DTP and DTP-derived resistance states. 2. Bridging Bench to Bedside: Studying DTP dynamics and clinical progression using Patient-Derived Xenografts (PDXs), syngeneic mouse models, and validating findings in clinical specimens. 3. Establishing a Translation Pathway: Conducting targeted surfacesomic analysis of DTP and DTP-derived resistant cells to identify surface targets, assess heterogeneity, and perform a chemical phenotypic screen for differential drug responses. Building on the novel surface marker as a starting point, our goal is to identify and validate novel biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and lead molecules across persister states. Leveraging IMCB's expertise in molecular and cell biology, preclinical mouse models, state-of-the-art surfaceomics, EDDC's HiTAD proprietary platform, and high-content phenotypic screening, alongside NCCS's clinical trials and tissue repositories, we aim to translate our understanding of DTP mechanisms into valuable assets (biomarkers, targets, lead molecules). This integration aims to revolutionize precision oncology and improve patient outcomes.
kw: Epigenetics; drug resistance; cancer cell plasticity; biomarker discovery

title: Electro-Biocatalytic Conversion of CO2 into Valuable Aromatics
abs: CO2 will become an abundant feedstock in the future due to the planned activities in CO2 capture for preventing catastrophic climate change. Rapid advances are also being made to reduce the cost of renewable energy. Based on these two predictions, electrolysis of CO2 into valuable chemicals using renewable energy has become a popular topic, attracting sizable investments. This proposed project aims to combine such electro-catalysis with bio-catalysis to derive specialty chemicals (aromatics) from CO2. The PIs of this project have individually developed key foundational technologies in the past 5-10 years, making the proposed process to be possible. Dr. Wang Lei (Team PI) has developed cascade electro-reactors to produce ethylene glycol (EG, a C2 molecule) from CO2 at high rate. Dr. Zhou Kang (Lead PI) has developed an Escherichia coli strain that could convert EG into L-phenylalanine with promising yield (0.15 g/g). Dr. Li Zhi (Team PI) has constructed new pathways to produce many specialty aromatics from L-phenylalanine. In this four-year project, they will solve key technical challenges that will theoretically prevent up-scaling of their processes and provide a lab-scale fully integrated model device that could make 5-10 specialty aromatics on demand from CO2. Specifically, in Work Package 1 (WP1), reaction mechanisms will be studied to facilitate rational design of more durable catalysts that could also result in higher EG selectivity and productivity in the CO2 electrolysis sub-process. WP2 will introduce new-to-nature EG assimilation pathways into E. coli and engineer its metabolism for higher L-phenylalanine titer and yield. WP3 will capitalize on the new pathways Dr. Li’s group has developed and focused on further improving the catalytic activities of the involved enzymes. It will use a microfluidics-based enzyme screening technology that was developed in a completed CRP project. In WP4, all the sub-processes will be integrated to deliver the project. This project will provide a new model for future chemical manufacturing industry and the developed technologies could be ready for translational research funding towards larger scale applications.
kw: CO2 utilization, Electro-catalysis, Bio-catalysis

title: Novel Chemoenzymatic Strategies for Rare Sugar Synthesis
abs: Rare sugars display unique structural features and chemical properties that set them apart from common sugars such as glucose. Rare sugars, including rare monosaccharides and oligosaccharides, serve as essential building blocks in the synthesis of a wide range of high-value products such as small-molecule drugs, pesticides, food additives, and vaccines. Despite the growing recognition of their economic importance, the practical utility and potential of rare sugars are hindered by challenges in sourcing. The scarcity and heterogeneity of the starting materials render the isolation of rare sugars from natural sources labour-intensive and economically unviable. Current synthetic methodologies for rare sugars are also technically demanding and environmentally unsustainable, underscoring the need for ground-breaking and sustainable approaches. Addressing these challenges, this research proposal contains three objectives aimed at transforming the field of sugar synthesis through the development of innovative chemoenzymatic approaches to synthesize rare mono- and oligosaccharides. While our primary aim with this research endeavour is to advance the scientific frontiers of sugar synthesis, the anticipated outcomes will yield patentable technologies and products with substantial commercial potential. An important application involves synthesizing biomedically significant antigenic oligosaccharides, which poses challenges with current methods, to facilitate the development of novel vaccines. Through the implementation of these transformative technologies, our ultimate goal is to seize valuable opportunities in the commercial sectors of drug and vaccine manufacturing, while driving the transition towards more cost-effective synthetic routes and environmentally sustainable practices.
kw: Rare sugar; biocatalyst; microbial fermentation; catalysis; enzyme engineering; vaccine

title: Hot-electron Integrated Nano-devices: A Versatile Electromagnetic Synthesizing Technology from THz to EUV (Hot INVEST)
abs: Electromagnetic waves play a pivotal role in our modern society, serving diverse applications from telecommunication and nanofabrication to medical diagnosis and treatment. Solid-state device technologies such as transistors and lasers are widely used in system designs, as they provide large-scale integration capability. In contrast, the application of high-performance bulky vacuum and plasma device technologies is limited to high-end defence and satellite systems. Here we aim to develop new device technologies to use the immense potentials of hot electrons in vacuum and plasma to generate electromagnetic signals from terahertz to extreme-ultraviolet with unprecedented performance, all within a compact and integrated device form factor. These innovations are projected to surpass the constraints of solid-state technologies, while enabling implementation and integration on traditional wafer platforms. Hot electrons in nanogaps can trigger intriguing phenomena that can be technologically and scientifically very promising: 1) High-power picosecond electrical switching can occur in a nanogap due to transition from insulating to nano-scale plasma (Nanoplasma) conducting state. The process is driven by field-emitted hot electrons. This device technology can enable generation of terahertz signals at high-power levels ( >100 mW), bridging the terahertz gap, addressing a longstanding technological challenge. Our new hardware platform enables ultrahigh bandwidth telecommunication and broadband spectroscopy. We have the following aims in this thrust: Aim 1.1) Measuring the actual switching time of Nanoplasma switches. Our credible preliminary work [Nature 579, 534–539 (2020)] shows switching time of 5 ps, which was the limit of the experimental setup. The actual switching time of Nanoplasma devices remains unknown up to date. Aim 1.2) Bridging the terahertz gap: Realization of high-power room-temperature integrated terahertz sources using Nanoplasma switch technology. Aim 1.3) Identifying the physical mechanism behind Nanoplasma formation and development of a particle-in-cell model for circuit-level simulation of Nanoplasma switch as a new integrated electronic component. 2) Hot electrons can activate spontaneous, stimulated, and plasmon-mediate emission, leading to generation of intense optical waves. The output spectrum can be tailored by design, ranging from infrared to ultraviolet. Formation of Nanoplasma in a nanocavity whose fundamental mode strongly couples with one of the dominant atomic/molecular excitation energy levels, resembles a two-level quantum system, and can enable intense lasing. Here we focus on application of such novel optical sources for deep-ultraviolet generation, which is a technological gap, and has numerous applications in information technologies, such as sensing and non-light-of-sight (NLOS) communication, as well as environmental technologies in water purification and sterilization. title: Precision Health Research, Singapore (PRECISE) - NPM Phase III
abs: PRECISE is the central entity set up to coordinate Singapore s nationwide effort in implementing Phase II of Singapore s three-phase National Precision Medicine (NPM) programme. Phase I (2017 2020) focused on developing an Asian reference genome database called SG10K_Health, which comprises whole genome sequences of 10,000 Singaporeans representing multi-ancestry Asian populations. The SG10K_Health dataset is a national resource of Asian genetic normality supporting clinical and biomedical research. The dataset also provided initial estimates of genetic disease burden in Singaporeans, focusing on clinically relevant genes. Phase III (2025 2031) will focus on healthcare transformation and precision population health through partnerships with healthcare clusters in Singapore. Phase III aims to address three core areas: identifying genetic factors in Asian-relevant diseases for novel treatments; gathering research data to support scaling precision medicine from pilots to national implementation; and leveraging innovative data linkages to enhance Asian-centric datasets for artificial intelligence applications and international collaboration. PRECISE is a programme of CRIS.
kw: precision medicine, precision health, genomics

title: Validation and Pilot Implementation of a Novel Symptom Appraisal Tool for Early Diagnosis of Patients with Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases in the General Population and Primary Care
abs: Early diagnosis of autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARDs) remains a global unmet need. Evaluating individuals with persistent musculoskeletal (MSK) symptoms who are at risk of ARDs using questionnaires is deemed the best approach to address this. We therefore developed the Symptom Testing for Autoimmune RheumaTic diseases (START) questionnaire. Study aims Aim 1: To refine START to improve its performance among patients referred from primary care with suspected ARDs, then translate it into Chinese. Hypothesis 1: Refined English and Chinese versions of START would address barriers to symptom awareness (e.g. language, suboptimal understanding of symptoms) and would be well accepted for self-administration by patients with suspected ARDs referred from primary care to rheumatology clinics* Aim 2: To assess the sensitivity and specificity of START among patients with suspected ARDs referred from primary care to rheumatology clinics* Hypothesis 2: START will demonstrate sensitivity of ≥ 80% and specificity of ≥ 60% in identifying patients with ARDs among patients referred from primary care to rheumatology clinics* Aim 3: To identify facilitators and barriers to implementing START and obtain preliminary data on effectiveness in patients with suspected ARDs who complete START at Community Health Posts (CHPs) or Primary Care Clinics (PCCs). Hypothesis 3: Pilot data would show that START shortens time to diagnosis for ARDs Methods Aim 1: cognitive debriefing to refine START before translation into Chinese. Aim 2: sensitivity and specificity of START would be assessed in patients referred from primary care to a Rheumatology clinic. Aim 3: in depth interviews after pilot implementation of START in CHPs and PCCs to identify facilitators and barriers to implementation This project is of global importance because it addresses global unmet needs for (1) early diagnosis of ARDs, using a novel questionnaire which addresses limitations of existing questionnaires and (2) approaches to optimize implementation of such questionnaires.
kw: Rheumatic Diseases; Population Health; Primary Health Care; Arthritis, Rheumatoid; Spondyloarthritis; Help-seeking Behaviour

title: DEFIN3E (DiabEtic Foot IN Engaging, Educating, Empowering) Community Care
abs: The DEFIN3E (Diabetic Foot in Engaging, Educating, Empowering) Community Care project aims to transform diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) management in Singapore's Woodlands community through an AI-enabled health program. This innovative approach seeks to integrate community resources and cutting-edge technology to improve clinical outcomes and overall patient quality of life. Aim: To enhance clinical outcomes for DFU patients by utilizing an AI-driven community health program to engage, educate, and empower them. Hypotheses: 1. The use of a diabetes AI Health Coach will improve patient activation scores. 2. AI-enabled wound healing reports will prompt quicker medical consultations during critical episodes. 3. The AI-enabled community program will effectively improve DFU management at the population health level. Methodology & Approach: The project employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative data from AI interactions and qualitative feedback from patients and healthcare providers. Key components include: Technology Deployment: Implementation of the Pingoo.AI health coach to deliver personalized, real-time educational content. Clinical Integration: Use of AI-generated wound reports integrated with patient electronic medical records to alert clinicians to deterioration. Human Interaction: Complementary engagement by Care Corner’s health coaches to reinforce AI-driven insights through direct patient interactions. Feasibility: The study is grounded in prior successes of the DEFINITE Care program, which has shown significant improvements in DFU management outcomes. The integration of AI with proven clinical workflows ensures both the feasibility and scalability of the intervention. This approach leverages existing infrastructure and protocols, minimizing startup costs and maximizing the utilization of available resources. Significance to Science and Medicine: This project addresses critical gaps in DFU care continuity post-discharge, which is often a high-risk period for complications. By providing continuous, AI-enhanced care in the community setting, the project aims to reduce hospital readmissions, improve care outcomes, and maintain cost-effectiveness. The outcomes have the potential to inform future policies and practices not only within Singapore but globally, setting a new standard for chronic disease management in community settings.
kw: diabetic foot ulcer; population health; community care; artificial intelligence; wound imaging; health coaching

title: Digitization of Rehabilitation's Evaluation and Activity Monitoring using Thermography (D.R.E.A.M.T.): An exploratory clinical study
abs: The aim of this project is to develop a sentinel thermography camera-based monitoring system to continuously track and analyze patients' physical activities in rehabilitation wards. Current healthcare systems lack accurate data and effective feedback mechanisms, making it challenging to motivate patients to improve their physical activity levels and mitigate sedentary behavior. Without precise monitoring, bed exercises prescribed by therapists largely depend on the patient's own motivation, resulting in suboptimal compliance and progress. By integrating clinical and functional data, this system will provide real-time feedback and personalized goal-setting to enhance patient engagement and autonomy, leading to improved health outcomes. Phase 1 involves collecting and manually labeling of 3,000 sample activities, with 200 samples for each of 15 different physical activities. This data will train advanced AI algorithms to accurately recognize and categorize patient activities. Phase 2 will focus on validating these AI-generated labels against 1,000 random samples verified by clinicians. This phase will also involve developing a comprehensive dashboard to visualize patient progress and activity trends. The final phase will pilot the system in a rehabilitation ward, evaluating its effectiveness in enhancing patient outcomes and optimizing nursing workload and resource allocation. This project addresses the critical need for precise, continuous monitoring to improve patient care and operational efficiency in rehabilitation settings.
kw: thermography camera, rehabilitation, physical activities, nursing acuity

title: Implementing PROMs in routine clinical care (IPROMs)
abs: Background and Aims Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) allow clinicians to understand what matter most to patients. PROMs provide the patients’ perspectives of their health, and are one of the key outcomes in value-based care (VBC). Despite their importance, implementation of PROMs in routine clinical care worldwide remains an unmet need and has been challenging due to significant barriers affecting implementation. This proposal aims to facilitate this unmet need through three specific aims: (1) To understand the barriers, facilitators, and strategies to implement PROMs in patients and clinicians, mapped to the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Changes (ERIC). (2) To map the readiness of the departments in Singapore General Hospital (SGH) in implementing PROMs using the PROMs healthcare system implementation framework. (3) To develop a repository of locally validated PROMs in the diseases listed under MOH Value Driven Care (VDC) conditions via a scoping review. Methods Aim 1 involves qualitative studies with 30 patients and 40 stakeholders (clinicians, nurses, allied health professionals, administrators) while Aim 2 involves a survey with champions for PROMs in 48 departments in SGH. Aim 3 involves a scoping review of locally validated PROMs in Ministry of Health VDC conditions. Importance to Population Health The list of barriers and facilitators will allow us to develop strategies to facilitate PROMs implementation in clinical care. This implementation would be tested and refined though the pilot study, and (1) could allow us to be able to use PROMs as a potential important outcome in facilitating shared decision making and VBC. (2) would provide a sound basis for further implementation science research to investigate the use of PROMs in evaluating and improving chronic disease management in Singapore.
kw: Implementation science, patient-reported outcome measures, value-based care, shared decision making, chronic disease management

title: A model-based economic evaluation of a screening and stepped care intervention for the treatment of common mental health conditions among employees
abs: Due to the high cost to employers resulting from untreated mental health conditions, a workplace-based screening and stepped care model is a potentially cost-effective solution to address this growing public health challenge. The goal of this study is to estimate the net costs and cost-effectiveness of a screening and stepped care intervention for the treatment of common mental health conditions among employees, where Step 1 includes access to a low-cost digital solution. The analysis will be conducted using a Markov model, nested within a decision tree, that takes into account transitions between different health states. The modelling will be based on the health system and broader employer perspective where the latter includes potential savings to employers from reduced rates of absenteeism and increased productivity resulting from effective treatment. We hypothesize that the screening and stepped-care intervention will be cost-effective from the health system perspective when compared to established thresholds and cost-saving from the broader employer perspective. Findings will contribute to MOH’s stated goal of developing care pathways to prevent and treat mental health conditions in the workplace and can be used to educate employers about the net cost implications of subsidizing these interventions.
kw: economic evaluation; cost-effectiveness; mental health

title: Promoting early relational health with PlayReadVIP to prevent socioeconomic disparities in child development
abs: Singapore experiences income-related disparities in educational achievement that begin during infancy and have lifelong implications for health, well-being and productivity. This proposal seeks to determine the role of a theoretically- and empirically-supported parenting model (Video Interaction Project, now known as PlayReadVIP) in preventing the onset of these disparities. PlayReadVIP promotes early relational health by supporting responsive parenting through shared reading and play, and has proven scalability and impact cross-culturally. Drawing on the Ecological Validity Framework, we will formally adapt PlayReadVIP and test its effectiveness and implementation in a rigorous, randomised hybrid trial. The aims of the study include (1) To formally tailor the content and delivery of an evidence-based intervention for early relational health, PlayReadVIP, through cultural adaptation to diverse populations in Singapore; (2) To conduct a randomised Type I effectiveness-implementation hybrid trial of PlayReadVIP that begins prior to the hospital discharge of a newborn infant i) to compare early relational health, family functioning, and neurobiological indicators between intervention and control groups, ii) to examine for potential moderation of household income on improved early relational health, iii) to test for mediation of early relational health on changes in brain development measured through electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS); and (3) To identify barriers and facilitators to the implementation of PlayReadVIP. We will enrol 450 Singaporean families who require financial subsidies during their antenatal care and are representative of those from lower income households. The longitudinal impact of building early relational health on both neurobiological (i.e., EEG and fNIRS) and functional (i.e., language, executive function, school readiness) outcomes will be examined. We hypothesize that the positive parenting practices of PlayReadVIP will improve cognitive stimulation and brain development indicators of children. Findings will inform implementation on a population level to address equity and support human potential.
kw: Socioeconomic disparities; child development; early relational health; cognitive stimulation; positive parenting; preventive intervention

title: Multimodal speech parameters for mental health
abs: Mental illnesses frequently manifest through behavioral changes, making alterations in speech a significant indicator. However, the multi-dimensional nature of language representation presents challenges, impeding computational techniques for modeling and analyzing speech in mental health contexts. This proposal aims to develop multi-modal AI models for the early detection of mental health issues by leveraging speech as a key modality. The research will focus on four main themes: Identification of Important NLP Features: We will analyze various independent datasets to identify natural language processing (NLP) features that are consistently important for predicting mental health issues. This will ensure the development of robust and reliable models. Linguistic Analysis in Contextual Settings: By examining speech within its contextual settings, we aim to extract novel features and gain deeper insights from linguistic and conversational analysis. This approach will enrich our understanding of how speech clues precede the onset of mental health issues. Complementary Data Modalities and Modeling Strategies: We will investigate which data modalities or modeling strategies work synergistically with text to create more accurate and comprehensive AI models. This multi-modal approach is expected to enhance the explainability and overall performance of the models. Development of Acceptable Assistive AI Technology: We will focus on constructing AI models as assistive devices that are likely to be accepted by health practitioners and patients. Emphasizing usability, reliability, and practical benefits, we aim to address the concerns of stakeholders, particularly in primary and non-specialist care sectors. The anticipated impact of this research includes the identification of key NLP features, a richer understanding of speech as an early indicator of mental health issues, and the development of synergistic multi-modal AI models. Furthermore, by focusing on stakeholder acceptance, we aim to bring these assistive technologies closer to practical deployment, ultimately improving early detection and intervention in mental health care.
kw: Artificial Intelligence; Detection; Linguistics; Mental Health; Speech

title: From Exposome to Health Outcomes: A Population-Based Approach to Understanding and Mitigating Early Menopause in Singapore's Diverse Communities
inst: IHDP - Institute for Human Development and Potential
abs: This study investigates the complex interplay between exposome factors and menopausal health in Asian women, addressing critical gaps in understanding environmental influences on reproductive aging. We hypothesize that exposure to multiple environmental toxicants, unfavorable socioeconomic conditions, and lifestyle factors accelerates biological aging, leading to earlier menopause onset and increased health risks. This acceleration is mediated through alterations in epigenetic patterns, metabolomic profiles, and gut microbiome composition. Our prospective cohort study will recruit 400 women aged 40-60 years across Singapore, integrating new recruits with existing cohorts. Employing cutting-edge multi-omics technologies and comprehensive exposome characterization, we aim to: • Build multidimensional exposome profiles affecting women across pre-, peri-, and post-menopausal stages. • Investigate how environmental factors influence early menopause onset, symptom severity, and overall life quality. • Elucidate biological mechanisms accelerating ovarian aging due to environmental exposures. • Explore transgenerational impacts by examining the relationship between maternal exposome and daughters' age at menarche. The study will utilize advanced statistical and machine learning techniques, including mixed-effects models, exposome-wide association studies, and causal inference methods, to analyze complex, high-dimensional data. Preliminary data suggest a trend towards earlier menopause onset associated with higher prenatal air pollution exposure and identify specific PFAS compounds as potentially important factors influencing menopausal timing. This research addresses current gaps by focusing on cumulative and interactive effects of multiple exposures, integrating diverse exposome proportions, highlighting the gut microbiome's role in reproductive health, and investigating transgenerational effects. It is particularly relevant for Asian populations facing unique environmental challenges from rapid industrialization and urbanization. The study's outcomes have significant potential for healthcare policy and practice implementation, including developing evidence-based guidelines for exposome-related risks in women's reproductive health, informing environmental regulations, and creating personalized interventions. We anticipate reductions in cardiovascular disease risk, osteoporotic fractures, and menopause-associated mental health symptoms, while also providing insights into intergenerational reproductive health impacts.
kw: Early menopause; Exposome-menopause interactions; PFAS exposure; Accelerated ovarian aging; Menopausal transition biomarkers; Exposome-wide association study (ExWAS); Environmental endocrine disruptors

title: Population level estimation for chronic kidney disease and end stage renal disease; costs and drivers for effective screening
abs: Singapore is lagging in actively addressing the upcoming epidemic of chronic kidney disease (CKD), despite multiple global calls and urgent warnings for preventative action by expert panels. As the country with the highest prevalence of diabetes-induced CKD globally, screening is currently the only tool available to avert this epidemic. However, many questions remain unanswered about who, how, and when to screen. The overarching aim of this study, using an existing national individual/agent-based model, is thus: (1) to estimate the future prevalence of CKD under different diabetes and hypertension scenarios, which will allow us (2) to establish the effectiveness of population health interventions, including sodium restriction, and (3) to investigate the cost-effectiveness of different screening regimens in identifying individuals suffering from stage 1 CKD onwards who remain undetected. Additionally, new technologies (4) such as home test kits will be explored, as well as survey data collected on (5) general population blood pressure and kidney health perceptions and behaviours, CKD patient experiences and treatment adherence, and healthcare professional treatment behaviours. The identified challenges, barriers, motivators, and solutions will assist in model parameterisation and describe the CKD landscape in Singapore.
kw: Screening; CKD; ESRD; Microsimulation modelling; cost-effectiveness

title: Developing and Testing a Patient Decision Aid for Treatment Resistant Depression
abs: Major depressive disorder is the single largest contributor to global disability. Many with the condition will improve with antidepressant medications. This is not the case for those with treatment resistant depression (TRD). As many as 19,000 Singaporean adults are treatment resistant, meaning they fail to respond to two or more antidepressants. TRD is particularly debilitating. Compared to MDD, those with TRD are at increased risk for high healthcare utilization and costs, unemployment, substance abuse, and suicide. There are now several effective treatment options available to manage TRD in Singapore. In addition to pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy, public and private clinics currently offer repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation, electroconvulsive therapy, intranasal esketamine, and intravenous ketamine. The decision of which treatment to choose is difficult. Not only are outcomes highly variable, so too are onset of response, short- and long-term side effects, delivery mechanism, treatment
kw: decision-aid; treatment resistant depression; mental health

title: Effectiveness of An Integrated Palliative Surgical Oncology and Rehabilitation Care Model in Patients with Advanced Cancer Undergoing Major Surgery: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
abs: Advanced cancer represents a debilitating condition that negatively impacts function and quality of life. In Singapore, up to 60% of patients suffer from advanced cancer at diagnosis and are recipients of resource-intensive and costly life-prolonging treatments including surgery. Given the life-limiting nature of advanced cancer, these patients have high palliative care (PC) needs. Functional decline is also common following surgery and multi-modality cancer treatments. Yet, there has been limited efforts to address PC or functional needs among surgical patients, leading to poor health related quality of life (HRQoL) and high healthcare utilization. To address longitudinal PC and functional needs, we propose an integrated palliative surgical oncology and rehabilitation (PSO+R) care model involving PC-trained surgical oncology teams, rehabilitation professionals, supported by specialist palliative care (SPC) physicians who will provide PC and cancer rehabilitation throughout the advanced cancer journey. This is opposed to usual care where surgeons are untrained in PC, and patients do not receive PC or rehabilitation. In PSO care, surgical oncology teams will screen and manage basic PC needs, escalating complex cases to SPC. In PSO+R care, patients will receive PSO care with concurrent cancer rehabilitation during the various treatment phases. We conduct a 3-arm cluster randomized controlled trial to evaluate the incremental effectiveness of PSO+R over PSO only over usual care on HRQoL, function, PC delivery, healthcare utilization and costs. We hypothesize that the PSO+R care is incrementally effective over PSO only over usual care in these patient-centric outcomes and is cost-effective. We also qualitatively evaluate the proposed care model using ecological frameworks. If proven effective, PSO+R care can improve well-being while enhancing economic efficiency of health care provision for patients near end of life. It is also potentially scalable to other surgical communities and may be adopted to improve quality care for other seriously ill populations.
kw: Advance cancer, palliative care, rehabilitation, surgery, care coach

title: Implementation-Effectiveness Hybrid Study of a Collaborative Model of Care between Orthopaedics and Allied Healthcare Professionals (CONNACT Plus) in knee osteoarthritis in Singapore
abs: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of pain and poor function, particularly in elderly. The Collaborative Model of Care between Orthopaedic and Allied Healthcare Professionals (CONNACT) started in 2017 as an innovative, multidisciplinary, biopsychosocial, community-based intervention with 12-weeks personalized group-based psychoeducation and exercise therapy to transform the model of care for OA. Following an effectiveness-implementation hybrid randomized control trial (RCT) in 2019 assessing CONNACT, the modified CONNACT Plus incorporated the use of health coaches was introduced in 2021 for upscaling to a cluster-wide program. The aim of the proposal is to evaluate this scaled-up version of CONNACT Plus where we hypothesize that CONNACT Plus is a clinically and cost-effective intervention. Our effectiveness-implementation hybrid study will study 2 core components employing a mixed-method approach following the Practical, Robust, Implementation and Sustainability Model (PRISM) framework. The first component (implementation-related) aims to assess the delivery of the CONNACT Plus program, specifically the contextual factors, reach and fidelity influencing its implementation, with an emphasis on scalability and sustainability. It will compromise of (1) Semi-structured interviews with key participants for the qualitative component and (2) Analysing program process data (recruitment, treatment logs, observation checklist) for the quantitative component. The second component (effectiveness-related) aims to evaluate the clinical effectiveness and cost effectiveness of CONNACT Plus by comparing health outcomes and costs incurred by program participants and those receiving usual care at 12 months. Additionally, we aim to identify the characteristics of responders vs non-responders. This will be done through (1) Prospective non-randomized study design embedded in an existing cohort study for the quantitative component and (2) Semi-structured interviews with participants for the qualitative component. Findings will inform sustainable upscaling of CONNACT Plus through precision population health, underpinned by implementation science principles to optimize rehabilitation and deliver value-based care.
kw: osteoarthritis knee; model of care; implementation science; precision population heath

title: Prospective Validation of a Real Time Neurological Deterioration Risk Score for Management of Spontaneous Intracranial Haemorrhage
abs: The long-term goal of this study is to provide an AI decision metric for the stratification of haemorrhagic stroke patients with spontaneous intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) to guide management of ICH patients. Based on current clinical practice, patients diagnosed with spontaneous ICH are admitted directly to HD/ICU from the emergency department. However, up to 90% of these patients remain clinically and neurologically stable and could potentially be triaged to general ward (GW) for their care management. Nonetheless, currently available local data offers little guidance on factors predicting risk of neurological deterioration. Several prognostic models have been developed for studying spontaneous ICH. However, these models are limited to clinical score development, with no evidence on their performance in real-time prediction of neurological deterioration (ND) during hospitalization. Additionally, the impact of implementing a real-time ND risk score for the management of spontaneous ICH has not been evaluated. Therefore, this study aims to validate and evaluate an AI-based decision metric for early prediction of ND in patients with spontaneous ICH, which can be integrated into the Epic EMR system to guide real-time patient management. The specific aims are: Specific Aim 1: To externally validate a risk score for real-time prediction of early neurological deterioration in a cohort of haemorrhagic stroke patients. Specific Aim 2: To prospectively validate the model's performance against clinician judgment and patient outcomes specifically on deterioration and mortality. Specific Aim 3: To develop an AI decision metric integrated within the electronic medical record system to facilitate spontaneous ICH triage, setting the stage for future randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
kw: Neurological Deterioration, spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage, Machine Learning, Augmented Intelligence, Predictive Modeling

title: A Precision Medicine–based Approach to Advancing Population Kidney Health in Singapore
abs: A Precision Medicine–based Approach to Advancing Population Kidney Health in Singapore Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health problem globally and in Singapore, resulting in substantial and rising health and economic burden. Heterogeneity in CKD risk has resulted in worse health outcomes in specific sub-groups, such as ethnic minorities. In Singapore, Malay individuals have a three-fold higher prevalence rate of kidney failure, compared to Chinese. A better understanding of the predictors of CKD development and progression will allow for targeted policies and strategies aimed at prevention, early detection, better risk stratification and optimised treatment of CKD. We propose that a more individualised, targeted, precision medicine-based approach to prevention, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of CKD will be better suited than a one-size-fit-all approach strategy and has the potential to advance population-level kidney health. In this study, we will analyse a comprehensive fused research dataset from a large representative multi-ethnic Asian longitudinal cohort (PRECISE-SG100K), which consists of detailed phenotype, genotype, lifestyle (including activities and nutrition) and electronic health linkage data. We aim to determine prevalence of CKD among adults in various sub-population, examine association of CKD with genetic, clinical, and socio-behavioural predictors, the relative contribution of key predictors driving differences in CKD risks across different sub-population, and develop and validate an integrated risk assessment for the development of CKD in a representative multi-ethnic Asian population-based cohort in Singapore. These findings will form the basis for future targeted, interventional clinical trials for health promotion and disease prevention, using personalised and precision medicine approaches, as well as population-based, cost-effective public health actions. These will, in turn, prevent complications and adverse patient outcomes of CKD, improve population kidney health and ensure a more sustainable healthcare system.
kw: precision medicine; population health; chronic kidney disease; kidney failure; personalised treatment; targeted screening

title: Be Right! Back: An Artificial Intelligence enabled mobile application for patients with Low Back Pain
abs: Background: Low back pain (LBP) is a complex condition and its causes are multifactorial, of which the physical, lifestyle, cognitive and emotional factors are potentially modifiable. Due to the complexity of LBP, Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be used to accurately measure and analyze large amounts of data from different sources to aid in the assessment and management of LBP. Objective: Development of an AI model that accurately assesses and measures 4 core components that comprise the Physical factor of LBP. The 4 core components are functional activity (measured using the 5 times sit-to-stand task – 5xSTS), trunk range of motion (ROM), gait pattern and pain levels during movement. Methods: The project aims to recruit 120 LBP patients receiving care at SGH Physiotherapy. For the first (primary) study (n=103), we will compare the measurements (5xSTS, trunk ROM, gait pattern and pain levels during movement) taken by the AI model against that of a trained assessor/physiotherapist. For the second study (n=17), following integration of the AI model with our industry partner’s platform, a pilot study will be conducted to assess the feasibility and usability of a minimum viable product. Planned Analysis: For the first study, the Bland-Altman plot will be used to compare the measurements taken by the AI model against that of a trained assessor/physiotherapist. If our hypothesis is correct, the results should show narrow limits of agreement between the 2 methods of measurement. Descriptive statistics will be used for the second study. We anticipate that there will be positive feedback and satisfaction from use of the minimum viable product. Discussion: Successful development of our solution will allow accurate remote tracking of the progress made by LBP patients. This will support/assist physiotherapists in clinical decision-making, hence allowing for more effective management of LBP.
kw: Digital Health; Musculoskeletal; Pain; Low Back Pain; Artificial Intelligence

title: Development of novel heating blanket to prevent unintentional perioperative hypothermia
abs: Hypothermia following surgery is a common unintentional consequence of Anaesthesia.Unintentional Perioperative-Hypothermia (UPH) has been found to be associated with higher risk of postoperative complications like wound-infections, blood-loss, longer hospital-stays and mortality. Therefore, many organizations have recommended measures like patient warming-systems to prevent UPH.Globally,Patient warming-systems have a market-size of over $1 billion and an expected growth of 8.5% .Of these patient warming-systems, Forced-air warming-systems (FAWS) are most commonly used in the operating-room to prevent UPH. A FAWS consists of warm air blowers connected with a large hose into a plastic inflatable blanket.The warm air blower not only adds to capital expenditure costs but also restricts mobility of the covered patient , adds to hospital energy consumption and has limited utility in certain healthcare environments like with MRI, ambulances.There have also been concerns that the forced airflow in the FAWS disrupt operating room laminar air flow, which may lead to wound-infections.To address these issues , our team of experienced clinicians and material scientists propose to develop a blanket incorporating a novel non-toxic material which is able to generate heat (using an exothermic chemical reaction) when applied to skin prior to induction of anaesthesia.We hypothesise that this novel material incorporated blanket will prevent hypothermia bimodally (by producing heat and preventing heat loss) . It can be expected that our novel and disruptive solution will lower healthcare costs by, reducing length of stay attributable to wound-infections, reducing medical-waste, and negating the need to purchase equipment like forced-air warmers. With this grant support we will test candidate materials for effectiveness in the laboratory and test their biological safety in animal models.The pilot data obtained will be used to apply for future national funding to further develop the solution.
kw: Hypothermia;medical device,surgery,anaesthesia,blanket;forced air warmer

title: Design to Fit: A Novel 3D-Printed Prosthetic Solution for Diabetics
abs: This proposal aims to develop and validate a novel 3D-printed diabetic transtibial prosthetic socket to enhance comfort, fit, and functionality for diabetic amputees, addressing current clinical and technical challenges. Aim 1: Develop and validate a minimal viable product (MVP) for a 3D-printed diabetic transtibial prosthetic socket, ensuring clinical effectiveness and user satisfaction. Aim 2: Evaluate user satisfaction and clinical outcomes through a clinical trial comparing the quality of life (QoL), clinical consistency, and user satisfaction of 3D-printed sockets against traditional production techniques. Aim 3: Optimize and scale digital manufacturing processes in collaboration with Hewlett Packard (HP) to refine the prosthetic socket design, assess scalability, and explore commercialization opportunities. Aim 4: Standardize transtibial socket production in Singapore using a remote-digital method to ensure equitable access to superior prosthetic design and quality while minimizing cost variations. Background & Clinical Need: The demand for prosthetics and orthotics (P&O) services in Singapore is rising due to an aging population and high rates of diabetes-related amputations. Traditional socket manufacturing is labor-intensive and depends heavily on individual practitioner skill, leading to variable outcomes. Hypotheses: 1. A 3D-printed prosthetic socket will significantly reduce production time and costs. 2. Diabetic patients fitted with 3D-printed transtibial sockets will report higher satisfaction and better clinical outcomes. 3. Collaboration with HP will refine and scale 3D-printed prosthetic sockets, improving market penetration and viability. Methodology: • Phase 1: Develop and validate prototypes against international safety standards using HP's 3D printing technology. • Phase 2: Conduct a clinical trial comparing traditional and 3D-printed sockets. • Phase 3: Optimize manufacturing with HP and conduct a feasibility study. • Phase 4: Implement a digital production pipeline in Singapore. Feasibility: Supported by TTSH and HP's collaboration, preliminary data, and Singapore's digital health infrastructure. Importance: This research aims to revolutionize prosthetic care for diabetic amputees, enhancing patient outcomes and setting new standards in prosthetic design.
kw: Innovation, Design, Prosthetics, Orthotics, 3D printing, Rehabilitation, amputation

title: STAG2 Mutant-induced KRAS Upregulation in Normal Colon Tissue - Characterising a Novel Mechanism of Colorectal Oncogenesis
abs: Somatic mutations in normal tissue have recently been discovered, yet the role of such mutations in relation to cancer initiation remains to be discovered. Based on my preliminary data using scRNAseq, I observed that co-cultured STAG2 mutant cells induce an upregulation in the KRAS pathway in neighbouring wildtype cells. Upregulation of this KRAS pathway is well-described in the oncogenesis of colorectal cancer. Here, I hypothesise that STAG2 mutant cells induce an upregulation of KRAS dependent oncogenesis, leading to colorectal cancer initation. My aims are 1. to validate the observation of my preliminary studies that STAG2 mutant organoids result in KRAS activation in neighbouring wild-type organoids, and 2. to determine the mechanism of KRAS activation by STAG2 mutant cells. To achieve Aim 1, I will use multiple approaches to validate in vitro the results derived from my already performed scRNAseq experiment. This includes performing quantitative PCR (qPCR) of KRAS pathway genes, western blot of KRAS pathway genes, as well as KRAS activity assays in the neighbouring wildtype cells. To achieve Aim 2, I will study the culture media of STAG2 mutant cells for ligands or proteins that may be absorbed by the neighbouring wild-type cells employing KRAS activity assay, ELISA, Western blot, and CellChat analysis. All experiments will be performed using patient-derived human colonic organoids, for which I have already demonstrated by ability to generate. Understanding the molecular biology behind pathways that lead to cancer has been fundamental in our development of therapeutic agents. Characterising the role of somatic mutations in normal tissue can reveal new oncogenic mechanisms and pathways, potentially resulting in new approaches to detect and screen for malignancy. This will contribute to the goal of reducing the incidence of colorectal cancer, and the morbidity and mortality associated with the disease.
kw: oncogenesis, colorectal cancer, somatic mutations, organoids

title: The role of diabesity and ageing-related mitochondrial dysfunction endophenotypes in the paradigm of physical frailty
inst: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital Pte Ltd
abs: Background Diabesity may be a driver and response to ageing-related mitochondrial dysfunction. There is a lack of understanding on association between diabesity and physical frailty and its underlying pathophysiological mechanism. Aims: Primary:To examine association between diabesity and frailty Secondary:To examine (1) association between diabesity and ageing-related mitochondrial dysfunction endophenotypes; (2) association between ageing-related mitochondrial dysfunction endophenotypes and frailty; and (3) mediating role of ageing-related mitochondrial dysfunction endophenotypes in the association between diabesity and frailty Hypotheses: (1) Diabesity is associated with frailty; (2) Diabesity is associated with ageing-associated mitochondrial dysfunction; (3) Ageing-associated mitochondrial dysfunction is associated with physical frailty; (4) Ageing-associated mitochondrial dysfunction mediates association between diabesity and frailty Methods We will conduct cross-sectional study to recruit 400 patients aged ≥50 years. Exposure is diabesity (diabetes and obesity) vs. no diabesity (no obesity nor diabetes). Outcome is physical frailty assessed by short physical performance battery(SPPB). Mediator is ageing-related mitochondrial dysfunction which will be quantified using multiplex immunoassay. Logistic regression will be performed to examine association between (1)diabesity and frailty; (2)mitochondrial dysfunction markers and frailty; and (3)mitochondrial dysfunction markers and diabesity. Linear regression will be performed to examine association between diabesity and mitochondrial dysfunction markers, and between diabesity and SPPB score. Linear regression will be performed to examine association between diabesity and mitochondrial dysfunction markers, and between diabesity and SPPB score. Clinical significance With triple tsunamis of diabetes, obesity and ageing, physical frailty in people with diabesity will pose an important public health issue. There is a strong impetus to better understand pathogenesis of physical frailty in people with concurrent T2D and obesity so that healthcare professionals will be better informed in development of management strategies tailored at older patients with diabesity at risk of frailty. The findings will also allow us to identify potential intervention points for future study and potential therapeutic points.
kw: diabesity; mitochondrial dysfunction; frailty

title: Evaluation of the Healthy Early Life Moments in Singapore (HELMS) Program during Preconception
abs: Singapore's total fertility rate is critically low at 0.97 despite comprehensive pro-natalist policies. Concurrently, over 30% of pregnant women in Singapore are overweight or obese (ow/ob), contributing to subfertility and non-communicable diseases. Addressing maternal ow/ob with effective preconception interventions remains a significant clinical gap. The overall goal of this study is to evaluate the preconception phase of the Healthy Early Life Moments in Singapore (HELMS) intervention by integrating participant experiences with clinical outcomes. HELMS is an integrated mobile health (mHealth) lifestyle intervention supplemented with in-person or teleconsultation visits. The HELMS program will recruit 500 women (aged 21-40 years, BMI 25-40 kg/m²) attempting to conceive. Participants will complete a validated 6P metabolic assessment and intervention tool, receive real-time feedback and recommendation, and asked to set and review their 6P goals every 3-months. Participants will also receive weekly mHealth nudges, and engage with the 4S education module (Screening, Size, Supplements, and Sex). We hypothesize that participants who are satisfied with the HELMS intervention, and achieve the 6P goals, will be able to achieve improved clinical outcomes, including nutritional behaviours and successful pregnancy. Satisfaction will be measured using a validated evaluation questionnaire at the end of the preconception phase, with an 80% satisfaction score cut-off for high satisfaction. Achievement of 6P goals, defined as a 10% or greater improvement, will be assessed at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. In-depth interviews will explore participant experiences, including barriers and facilitators to intervention adoption and goal achievement. This study will also explore the association between intervention satisfaction, overall goal achievement, and clinical outcomes. A robust evaluation of HELMS that integrates both participant experiences and clinical outcomes will inform the development of scalable lifestyle intervention programs, enhancing metabolic and reproductive health outcomes for women attempting to conceive, and shape future maternal-child public health strategies.
kw: preconception, metabolic health, implementation science, evaluation, mobile health

title: Guarding Against Coronary Artery Disease and its Hidden Risk Factors in the Singaporean Population without Standard Modifiable Risk Factors (SG-GUARD Study): A Prospective, Cross-sectional Study
abs: Coronary artery disease (CAD) has been attributed to the presence of standard modifiable risk factors (SMuRFs), namely hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, and smoking. Yet, our preliminary data have shown that CAD is found in one out of two “healthy” persons without SMuRFs, coined as ‘SMuRF-less CAD’. Our studies forewarn that people with untreated SMuRF-less CAD who experience an acute myocardial infarction (AMI or heart attack), are 50% more likely to die at 30 days compared to those with SMuRFs. This SMuRF-less AMI phenomenon affects 1 in 10 AMI patients in Singapore. The overarching study aim is to address the need for upstream detection of high-risk coronary plaques and the hidden risk factors in these seemingly “low-risk” adults. We propose a prospective cross-sectional study of 210 asymptomatic community-dwelling participants aged between 30-55 years, to evaluate for the presence of high-risk coronary plaques, using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Our study group is well-positioned to undertake this project based on our experience with similar community-based studies using CCTA. Aim #1: To screen for the presence of high-risk coronary plaques on CCTA among community-dwelling asymptomatic participants without hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia and smoking (SMuRF-less). We hypothesize that the prevalence is about 40% in the SMuRF-less cohort. Aim #2: To study the association between other known risk factors of CAD and the occurrence of high-risk coronary plaques in our population. These include lipoprotein (a), apolipoprotein B/A1 ratio, biomarkers of chronic kidney disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and Cardiovascular Event Risk Test score. We hypothesize the presence of the candidate risk factors are associated with the presence of high-risk plaque. Aim #3: To examine the associations of targeted proteomic and lipidomic biomarker measurements with high-risk plaques. We hypothesize that specific proteome and lipidome profiles are associated with the presence of high-risk plaque.
kw: Coronary artery disease; modifiable risk factors; coronary computed tomography angiography

title: Developing and validating an AI-Based Assessment Tool to predict the motor progression of Parkinson’s disease
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the most common hypokinetic neurodegenerative disorder, leading to gradual motor decline. This impacts patients, families, and healthcare systems significantly. There is currently no risk scoring model used for predicting outcomes in PD. We aim to develop and validate an AI-based risk scoring model to predict motor decline in early PD patients within 3 years post-diagnosis. The study will use data from the Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH) cohort and the Singapore General Hospital (SGH) cohort. The proposal has 3 specific aims: 1) To identify the predictors including clinical assessments, blood markers, significantly associated with motor progression in PD. We hypothesize that specific clinical variables significantly related to motor progression will be shortlisted by the Shapley variable importance cloud (Shapley VIC) technique. 2) To develop and validate a risk scoring model based on the predictors identified in SA1 to estimate the risk of motor progression of PD in the existing TTSH PD cohort. We hypothesize that the AI-Based prediction model based on Automatic Clinical Score Generator will outperform a conventional logistic regression model. The data from the TTSH PD cohort will be randomly split into training and test dataset. Model accuracy will be evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). 3) To further validate the risk scoring model in the SGH PD cohort. The performance of the model is expected to demonstrate good accuracy in the external validation. The AI-Based Prediction model could contribute valuable insights into clinical risk stratification, empowering clinicians to enhance patient care. By effectively identifying patients at a higher risk of motor progression, timely interventions can be provided to prolong patient autonomy and reduce the burden on the healthcare system. Consequently, the optimization of medical resource allocation will improve cost-effectiveness and ultimately benefit the broader healthcare ecosystem.
kw: Parkinson’s disease; Motor progression; Prediction model; Machine learning

title: Advancing Precision Medicine in Ocular Surface Diseases: Developing and Implementation of a Point-of-Care Diagnostic Device
abs: Ocular surface diseases (OSDs) present a significant health challenge, posing a risk of blindness from potential complications. Despite their impact across age groups, the molecular processes driving inflammation and scarring in OSDs remain poorly understood, resulting in a lack of targeted therapies. Current immunosuppressive treatments are sub-optimal and have adverse effects, highlighting the need for precise interventions. Disease detection and monitoring rely on imprecise clinical techniques, necessitating more sensitive measures for clinical practice and research.Principal Investigator Dr Ong's expertise in severe OSDs positions this proposal at the forefront. His internationally recognised work on severity scoring systems for OSDs and ocular mucous membrane pemphigoid phenotype underscores the translational potential of this proposal. Aim 1: Optimise and validate a point-of-care microfluidics multiplex sensing device for detecting proteins in tear fluid. This includes evaluating the device’s ability to quantify protein concentrations, assessing its sensitivity to various biologically relevant concentrations, and validating its reproducibility and temporal stability using clinical samples. Aim 2: Identify and characterise molecular changes in immunological signalling pathways in patients with ocular Stevens-Johnson Syndrome through comprehensive gene and protein expression studies. Correlating these biomarkers with clinical phenotypes will enhance the diagnostic utility of the point-of-care device. Exploratory Aim: Pilot the device in routine clinics and collect feedback from users. This project addresses unmet needs in OSDs, promising advancements in clinical practice and research. The innovative point-of-care device, validated for efficiency, has the potential to transform OSD diagnosis, monitoring, and precision medicine. Insights into biomarkers will improve disease detection, monitoring, prognostication, and therapy evaluation, reshaping OSD management. Discoveries will guide future studies, exploring therapeutic targets and potential clinical trials. Leveraging Dr Ong's expertise and international collaborations, this proposal aligns with the vision of establishing an OSD Centre of Excellence in Singapore, contributing significantly to patient care and scientific advancement in OSDs.
kw: Ocular surface disease; Molecular pathways; Precision medicine; Diagnostic; Biomarkers; Microfluidics

title: Environmental Standards and Engineering Behaviours of Reused Incineration Ashes from Municipal Solid Waste and Sewage Sludge
abs: Singapore’s only active landfill, Semakau Landfill, is projected to reach full capacity by 2035, highlighting the urgent need for alternative strategies for waste reuse. This study focuses on two major types of waste: incineration bottom ash (IBA) and non-incinerable waste (NIW) - such as wastewater sludge. In Phase 1, a comprehensive field trial at Tanah Merah Coast Road (TMCR) and conceptual site modelling assessed the environmental standards for using IBA in construction. The study investigated leaching characteristics of the treated IBA and its reuse in concrete, vulnerability of local groundwater and soil, and climate change conditions. The Reference Values (RVs) were derived based on conservative modelling assumptions with the intent of allowing widespread adoption of IBA use in Singapore. Phase 2 will review and calibrate the modelling assumptions used in Phase 1 based on 1) more realistic considerations; 2) insights from leaching data of local soil across the proposed test sites; 3) replacement ratios of sand by IBA as subbase material; and 4) endpoint criteria based on the new local soil and groundwater standards to finalise the RVs for road-based and non-structural concrete (NSC) construction applications using treated and untreated IBA. Laboratory tests will assess the environmental and engineering properties, and 15 potential waste reuse sites in Singapore will be studied to map out the local baseline environmental conditions. IBA-embedded concrete's interactions and leaching behaviour at low mixing ratios and various grain sizes, and feasibility of using IBA in structural concrete and coastal protection applications will also be studied. NIW is the second largest group of waste residues disposed at Semakau Landfill (SL). R&D initiatives have been undertaken to treat NIW for construction applications, more notably the development of light weight aggregates (LWA) made from sewage sludge incineration ash (SSIA) by Zerowaste Asia. As NIW and SSIA possess different physical properties and contaminants compared to IBA, the RVs for IBA could not be directly applied. Therefore, the second part of Phase 2 project will study the properties and contaminants of SSIA and develop preliminary RVs for the LWA derived from SSIA (SSIA-LWA). Additional types of NIW may be included into the study using earlier established conceptual site model (CSM), if needs arise and there are sufficient resources. Risk assessments, both regarding Environment (ERA) and Health (HRA), will be used to evaluate the impacts from IBA and SSIALWA. Studies like Material Flow Analysis (MFA), Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA), and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) will estimate future availability, cost, demand, and reuse limits, informing local waste management policies and strategies.
kw: Environmental standards; engineering behaviours; incineration bottom ash; sewage sludge incineration ash; light weight aggregate; concrete

title: Economised Scaffolds and Coatings for Customised Organoleptic Cultivated Meat Products (ECO-Meats)
inst: SIFBI - Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation
abs: The objective of our current grant proposal is to comprehensively address the problem statement presented by the SFS2.0 call, which is to develop customisable scaffolds to lower costs by reducing growth factor requirements while allowing for more complex cultivated meat (CM) products with better organoleptic properties. We will build on the approach of incorporating growth factors in the scaffolds to reduce cost, the rationale for this being the smaller quantities of growth factors required for the proliferation and differentiation of CM cells, when released in a sustained manner from scaffolds. We will leverage on an additional advantage- by coupling this sustained release of growth factors to the adhesion of cells on the scaffolds, there will be a higher local availability of the growth factor, and signalling pathways can be activated that further promote cell proliferation. The knowledge base that we will build upon to develop CM scaffolds for growth factor reduction includes non-animal derived cell-adhesive factors (CAFs) with integrin-binding moiety (RGD), platform technologies of fibre scaffolds, macroporous plant-based scaffolds and extrusion processing, and growth factors (GF) sustained release. The technologies above will be combined- the CAFs will be incorporated into the scaffolds by coating or encapsulation, and growth factor binding to the CAF microparticles will be adopted as a strategy for sustained release. Specific challenges to be addressed would be the adaptation of the scaffolds for coating and the optimisation of the growth factor release kinetics with respect to cell proliferation and cost reduction. To demonstrate the applicability of our cost reduction strategy, we will work towards the production and formulation of meat prototypes with desired organoleptic properties such as appearance and texture.
kw: scaffolds; coatings; growth factor reduction; organoleptic; cultivated meat

title: A universal scaffolding process for cultivated meat: Intelligently engineering organoleptic properties via digitalization
abs: The high cost of cultivated meat (CM) is a key challenge. The cost-drivers of CM are mainly operational costs such as cell culture and differentiation media. One such strategy to reduce cost of differentiation media is through mechanotransduction, which employs mechanical stimuli to transduce a signal to stem cells and alter their differentiation, which could be enabled via scaffold material and design. However, in the state-of-the-art development for CM, scaffolds serve only as a platform to house the cells and do not facilitate cell differentiation and organization. Expensive differentiation media is still required. In departure from tradition, our lab introduced an innovative single-step process that integrates scaffold fabrication and stem cell seeding, effectively eliminating the cumbersome multi-stage process of the past. Due to the mechanotransduction process, it also does not require expensive differentiation media and the need to customise for different cell lines. Our laboratory has successfully proven the concept of this process. Despite the promise of this technique, optimization of these processes through experiments is time consuming and expensive. This process could be accelerated through digitalization of scaffold design by taking advantage of simulation and digital twinning. Here, we would like to propose a collaborative project with various parties (NTU; IHPC, A*STAR; SIT) to develop this technology holistically from simulation, materials development, processing to novel characterization of the properties of the final muscle bundles that are produced using this one-step platform.
kw: Cultivated Meat; Smart edible scaffold, cost-effective scaffold; 1-step simple, scalable process

title: Surveillance of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFASs), Polymer Additives and UV Filters in the Urban Water Cycle
abs: Extensive anthropogenic activities have inevitably introduced different kinds of pollutants to the urban water cycle. Among the pollutants, emerging organic contaminants (ECs), such as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), polymer additives and UV filters have received increasing attention during recent decades due to their ubiquity under urbanization and potential adverse effects to ecosystems and humans. Understanding the occurrence, source and fate of these ECs in the urban water cycle is crucial and urgent to address potential health concerns as well as develop treatment technologies to eliminate them. In this project, we propose to conduct a comprehensive surveillance of PFASs, polymer additives and UV filters in the urban water cycle of Singapore, by establishing sensitive and robust analytical detection protocols via integrated mass spectrometry techniques, investigating their occurrence and distribution trends in selected catchment-reservoirs, exploring their removal efficiency in water supply systems and understanding their mechanisms of transformation. The project will achieve an inclusive dataset of PFASs, polymer additives and UV filters in the urban water cycle of Singapore and further help improve the risk assessment of water quality and aquatic ecosystems. Its outcome will also help decision makers to better manage the impact of evolving ECs on the environment.
kw: PFAS; emerging contaminants; polymer additives; UV filters; surveillance; water

title: Novel Centrifugal Reverse Osmosis (CRO) for Low Energy Desalination
abs: The high energy consumption of seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination is due to the high transmembrane pressure (TMP) to overcome the osmotic pressure differential across the membrane. One approach to reduce the energy demand is using multiple RO stages in series, each successive one of which operates at a higher pressure, thereby avoiding pumping all the feed up to the maximum pressure required for the desired recovery. However, employing multiple RO stages in series requires interstage pumping that has limited this approach to just two or three stages. Another approach, the Closed-Circuit Reverse Osmosis (CCRO) desalination process, which continuously recycles the retentate while gradually increasing the pressure as the retentate becomes more concentrated. However, it is a semi-batch process that has challenges to be advanced to large-scale applications. This proposal advances a novel Centrifugal Reverse Osmosis (CRO) that achieves RO with a TMP only differentially above that required for local thermodynamic equilibrium between the retentate and permeate on opposite sides of the membrane, i.e., it approaches the thermodynamic restriction that defines the minimum pumping energy required for desalination. Whereas superficially this would appear to require an infinite number of stages in series, it is possible via a novel RO module design that employs rotation about an axis to create centrifugal pressure on the feed-retentate-side. Centrifugal force causes the feed-retentate-side pressure to increase differentially with increasing radial distance from the axis-of-rotation. A prototype of low-pressure lab-scale CRO system for brackish water application has been successfully demonstrated in NEWRI-SMTC. The mathematical model for CRO based on design at the thermodynamic limit has also been established. This proposal aims to explore the novel CRO technology for high-pressure seawater desalination and refining the idealized process to account for the irreversibilities not included in design at the thermodynamic limit.
kw: Desalination, low energy

title: Alginate to Oil (A2O): Non-photosynthetic Diatoms and Sustainable Approaches to Produce Carbon-Neutral Foods and Fuel
abs: The development of new technologies for the sustainable production of fuel and food is critical to the attenuation of global warming and feeding an expanding global population without increasing agricultural land. This is not only a global imperative, but also relevant to Singapore’s goals of food and energy security, and development of a knowledge-based economy. This project seeks to develop a new method to employ microalgae for the production of biomass and oil for food and biofuel applications. The key advantage of our approach lies in the exploitation of Nitzschia sing1 (N. sing1), a non-photosynthetic diatom (single-cell microalga) that has the unique ability to produce oil when grown on seawater containing alginate from brown seaweeds as the sole carbon source (Alginate to Oil, A2O. See Figure 1). N. sing1 was isolated from the coastal waters of Singapore [1] and constitutes a proprietary component of the technology. The sustainability of the A2O method is derived from low energy requirements and the use of a medium consisting of ocean seawater and alginate feedstock derived from the brown seaweed Sargassum. The method can be implemented both locally, where annual blooms in coastal waters produce over 1,000 metric tonnes of Sargassum, as well as internationally, where invasive Sargassum blooms are adversely impacting coastal ecosystems, economies and human health. Moreover, the non-photosynthetic diatoms are understudied. Thus, the exploration of their biodiversity combined with the development of knowledge and tools for their genetic manipulation will allow the team to pioneer and maintain a leadership position in the field. In summary, the project seeks to develop a new microbial fermentation method to produce carbon-neutral oils applicable to biofuel and food production. Successful execution of this project will promote Singapore’s food and energy security, foster new industries and create local jobs.
kw: Sustainability; carbon-neutral; feed, food, and fuel; non-photosynthetic diatom; fermentation; brown sea weed

title: EXTREME UV NANOPHOTONICS: QUANTUM CONTROL AND META-OPTICAL DESIGN OF EXTREME ULTRAVIOLET LIGHT SOURCES
abs: The field of nanofabrication has witnessed significant advancements in directing the propagation of light, driven by innovations such as photonic crystals and metamaterials, which have revolutionized various applications including as light detection and ranging (LIDAR), photovoltaics, and quantum technologies. However, the precise manipulation of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) photons, crucial for next-generation technologies like EUV lithography (EUVL), has remained challenging due to the mismatch between existing nanoscale structures and the wavelengths of EUV light. This disparity has hindered subwavelength control, prompting the exploration of novel materials such as van der Waals heterostructures and perovskite nanocrystals. Overcoming these challenges requires addressing fundamental hurdles, including the development of miniaturized free-electron sources for EUV light generation and the establishment of a theoretical framework for extreme EUV meta-optics. To tackle these issues, our project proposes to advance the theoretical understanding of nanoscale electromagnetism and quantum electrodynamical phenomena in EUV meta-optics while conducting experimental demonstrations of EUV emission from free-electron-driven nanomaterials. Of particular importance is the endeavor to develop chip-scale devices capable of generating 1mW of power at 13.5 nm of EUV light and showcase a proof-of-concept demonstration of nanopatterning, promising significant advancements in lithography and other nanotechnology applications. Preliminary work demonstrates feasibility since we have shown the generation of free electron-driven EUV radiation in a Si target, as well as the scaling up of the generated power with current. Furthermore, preliminary classical electrodynamic simulations, that hasn’t included the mesoscopic corrections, reveal the ability of multilayered nanoscale structures to enhance the intensity of free electron-driven EUV light sources by over 100 times.
