For in situ structure determination, we will first use the Arctis system to conduct cryo-focus-Ion-Beam milling of frozen virus-infected cells for cryoelectron-tomography imaging. We will then conduct subtomogram averaging to obtain their 3D cryoEM maps. We might observe some densities belonging to unknown host proteins associated with the virions. We will confirm the identity of these proteins by combining with results from TURBO-ID and super-resolution fluorescence microscopy. Our results will fill knowledge gaps about the mechanisms of virus infection, a pre-requisite for designing effective interventions against diseases. This grant allows us to build the infrastructure and the expertise in Singapore to conduct in situ structural research. This will also help the wider Singapore research community to branch into a new field.
kw: In situ cryoEM studies; Influenza virus; Dengue virus; cryoEM

title: The eMEASURE-RNA initiative: exploring the molecular basis of RNA editing, sensing and immune response – new approaches for immuno-oncology therapy
abs: This proposal aims to bring together an interdisciplinary, multi-institutional team in Singapore focused on RNA editing/modification and RNA-involved immune regulation. Through the eMEASURE-RNA initiative, the team, with diverse yet complementary expertise in ADAR biology, RNA biology, structural biology, immunology, and cancer biology, aims to uncover novel mechanisms underlying ADAR1-associated RNA recognition, editing, sensing, and their impact on immune responses, both intracellularly and extracellularly. This initiative goes beyond individual projects by adopting an integrated approach consisting of four distinct work packages. Interdisciplinary teams will collaboratively address these work packages, working together towards shared scientific goals. While the proposal primarily focuses on innovative fundamental research, it also establishes scientific foundations for the discovery of small molecules that can target ADAR1 and/or ADAR1-RNA recognition. These findings could potentially serve as starting points for the development of future anti-cancer immunotherapy drugs. Overall, the proposed program aims to establish Singapore as a global leader in RNA editing and RNA-associated immune regulation. It seeks to generate new knowledge, publish impactful research, and foster transformative collaborations. Through these endeavors, we aim to drive the development of novel treatment modalities that can overcome challenges in immunotherapy and pave the way for improved cancer treatment strategies.
kw: RNA editing, ADAR1, RNA sensing, Innate Immunity, iimuno-oncology

title: Optimising Antigen Targeting in Next Generation Regulatory T Cell Therapy
abs: Chronic immunosuppression causes adverse events in kidney transplant recipients, such as infections and malignancy, but is unable to eliminate the risk of graft loss from rejection. Early phase clinical trials demonstrated that autologous polyclonal regulatory T cell (apTreg) therapy can reduce immunosuppression without an increase in rejection. Newer Treg-based treatment strategies are exploring chimeric antigen receptors (CAR) Tregs directed against a specific HLA-type. However, these are limited by difficulties in cell manufacturing and can only be applied in specific cases of living donor transplantation where the donor is known far in advance. Moreover, the potential of Tregs for the treatment of autoimmune diseases remains unrealised. To overcome the challenges with current CAR Treg approaches, in this study we will explore Treg cell therapy programmed against specific tissue antigens to achieve the required specificity and potency. To achieve this, we will investigate three specific aims: 1. To identify potential target antigens for the next generation of Treg therapy using a coordinated single cell multi-omics analysis of peripheral blood and kidney biopsy tissue in Treg-treated kidney transplant recipients 2. To generate a platform to test Tregs against these antigens by engineering Tregs to express CARs and T cell receptor fusion constructs (TRuCs) with a universal adaptor for customisable antigen targeting 3. To compare the functional characteristics of Tregs programmed to target different antigens against autologous polyclonal Tregs and non-universal adaptor CAR Tregs The results will help optimise antigen targeting in Treg cell therapy with the ultimate goal of developing the next generation of Treg therapies to improve the outcomes of patients requiring transplantation or suffering from autoimmune diseases and replace current standard of care immunosuppressive regimens.
kw: Cell- and Tissue-Based Therapy; T-Lymphocytes, Regulatory; Kidney Transplantation; Glomerulonephritis; Antigen-Antibody Reactions

title: Implementation of Decade of Healthy Aging Action Plan to Screen and Prevent Decline in Intrinsic Capacity in Elders (SPICE) Through Multisectoral Collaboration
abs: Intrinsic capacity (IC) was introduced by the WHO and is defined “as the composite of all physical and mental capabilities that an individual can draw upon during his/her life”. The IC framework comprises of 5 domains which includes mobility, cognition, psychological, vitality and sensory (vision and hearing).” Decline in IC have been associated with participation restriction, social isolation, decline in activities of daily living, dementia and acceleration of progression to frailty. Large scale implementation of The INSPIRE integrated care for older people (ICOPE)-CARE program in the Occitania region for community dwelling older adults through ICOPE monitor have proven to be feasible where 90.3% of community dwelling older adults had decline in at least one IC and 9.3% required further evaluation. They have shown that screening for IC decline can be performed by caregivers and community partners which can then serve as a trigger for comprehensive assessment of underlying cause and intervention. The United Nations Decade of Healthy Aging recommends multistakeholder collaboration to improve the health of older adults. Multistakeholder engagement is important to enhance acceptability of intervention, bring in diverse opinions, improve reach especially to those at risk, improve sustainability and scalability. We aim to i) collaborate with the ICOPE-CARE program team to test the feasibility of implementing the ICOPE monitor digital platform in Boon Lay ii) overcome siloes, and uncoordinated work of screening and intervention through multistakeholder and community engagement. The Rapid Geriatric Assessment digital app will be used to screen for frailty where robust and pre-frail older adults will undergo IC assessment. Implementation science framework tools will be used to assess provider, recipient and other factors which may play a role in enabling and hindering implementation. For sustainability and scalability, peer leaders will be trained to conduct frailty and IC screening with Regional Health System conducting downstream assessments.
kw: intrinsic capacity; frailty; dementia; exercise; nutrition

title: IMPlementation stRategiEs for Scalability and Sustainability - Multidomain INterventions in a structured care pathway to Detect and Delay cognitive decline in community-dwelling older adults (IMPRESS-MIND2S)
abs: In response to the pressing challenge posed by the ageing population, there is an imperative to develop effective, scalable, and sustainable interventions for detecting and delaying cognitive decline and frailty. While multi-domain interventions have demonstrated effectiveness, their implementation at scale locally is relatively scarce. Guided by the Implementation Research Logic Model, we introduce a care model integrating a multi-domain intervention with implementation strategies, which will undergo further co-validation and pilot-testing in collaboration with key stakeholders - patients, caregivers, and partners from the Ministry’s Ageing Planning Office and Agency for Integrated Care. The multi-domain intervention encompasses targeted dementia risk factor control, guided physical activities, cognitive intervention, and social support; while implementation strategies include capability and needs-driven intervention adaptation, capability building through training and providing educational resources, establishing interrelationships and trust across collaborating organisations, engaging relevant stakeholders through co-design, and incorporating timely reminders and gamification. The primary objective is to evaluate this model in delaying cognitive decline among those with no or mild cognitive impairment, reducing caregiver burden, and improving quality of life, via a hybrid implementation-effectiveness cluster-randomised controlled trial. Secondary objectives include studying older adults with mild dementia and exploring the impact of this care model on delaying frailty status across all three groups. We hypothesise that intervention clusters, compared to control clusters, will demonstrate positive effectiveness and implementation outcomes, including a lower rate of decline in i) cognitive functioning and ii) frailty levels, improved iii) quality of life and iv) caregiver burden, v) higher compliance rates with intervention activities, vi) at least 80% feasibility, fidelity, enrolment rates, as well as vii) cost-effectiveness for scaling up. These findings are critical to identifying effective and scalable strategies to detect and delay the onset of cognitive decline and frailty, ultimately contributing to the well-being of the older population and their caregivers in Singapore.
kw: implementation strategy; cluster randomised controlled trial; practical adaptation; hybrid trial; cognitive decline; multi-domain intervention

title:
EaRly impAct theraPy with ceftazidime-avibactam via rapID diagnostics versus standard of care antibiotics and diagnostics in patients with bloodstream infection, hospital-acquired pneumonia or ventilator-associated pneumonia due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa or carbapenem non-susceptible Enterobacterales
(“RAPID”)
abs: Background Antimicrobial resistance is prioritised as a top 10 global public health threats facing humanity and has been declared a public health emergency by the WHO and United Nations. A key strategy in combating antimicrobial resistance is improving microbiological diagnostics, through prompt administration of targeted antibiotic treatment, and reduction of unnecessary empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic consumption. Conventional laboratory methods typically take two to five days for bacterial pathogen isolation, identification, and antibiotic susceptibility testing. Novel technology has emerged in recent decades to reduce or bypass laboratory steps required to identify antibiotic resistance in bacterial pathogens. Rapid diagnostics may speed up aetiologic diagnosis of infections and detect associated antimicrobial resistance within hours. Method: We will conduct an open-label, multinational, randomised, superiority trial. For the main cohort, hospitalised patients with bloodstream infections, hospital-acquired pneumonia or ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa or carbapenemase producing Enterobacterales will be randomised to control and intervention arms. Patients randomised to the intervention arm, will have the BioFire Blood Culture Identification 2 Panel (BCID2) used for positive blood cultures and/or the BioFire FilmArray Pneumonia plus Panel for respiratory tract specimens if having hospital-acquired pneumonia or VAP. Antibiotic guidelines will be provided to clinicians to aid interpretation of test results and treatment prescription. Ceftazidime-avibactam will be available for targeted use in patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa or carbapenemase producing Enterobacterales. Patients randomised to the control arm, will have samples analysed by clinical microbiology laboratories using standard of care diagnostics. Antibiotics will be available to these patients as per usual institutional practice. Patients with other MDR Gram-negative bacilli bloodstream infections, hospital-acquired pneumonia and VAP will also be enrolled and analysed as a secondary population, such that the trial results can be used to inform the utility of the interventions in this broader group of patients.
kw: antimicrobial resistance; rapid diagnostics; gram negative; hospital-acquired bloodstream infection; hospital-acquired pneumonia; ventilator-associated pneumonia; rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing

title: A Phase I Trial to Evaluate Allogeneic NKG2DL-targeting Chimeric Antigen Receptor-grafted GammaDelta T Cells (CTM-N2D) in Subjects with Advanced Solid Tumours or Haematological Malignancies (the ANGELICA Trial)
abs: Current CAR-T cell technologies for cancer pose several limitations. Firstly, to manufacture CAR-T cells, patients’ blood cells are collected through invasive leukapheresis. Secondly, some patients e.g., paediatric patients, are not eligible and are thus excluded. Lastly, patients going through multiple lines of chemotherapy compromises the number and quality of blood cells. Such poor starting material will make manufacturing quality CAR-T products difficult. CTM-N2D is an allogeneic CAR-T technology by CytoMed Therapeutics, proposed to overcome limitations of current CAR-T treatments. Together with built-in receptors of γδ T cells (e.g., γδ TCR, DNAM-1), grafting NKG2D ligand (NKG2DL)-targeting CAR onto γδ T cells produces CTM-N2D, which targets multiple ubiquitous stressed-induced cancer antigens including NKG2DLs (ULBP1-6 and MICA/B (8 types of antigens)), phosphoantigens, as well as PVR (CD155) and Nectin-2 (CD112). These antigens are a restricted set of conserved endogenous surface molecules induced by dysregulated mevalonate pathway, dysregulated proliferation and/or DNA-damage response, which are hallmarks of cancer. Hence, they are proven safe targets expressed in many tumour cell lines. Targeting such essential antigens may reduce the risk of cancer escape. Furthermore, production of CTM-N2D does not require the use of leukapheresis and lentiviral vectors. The manufacturing process involves simple blood withdrawal, mononuclear cell isolation, specific γδ T cell expansion and mRNA electroporation. The proposed project, ANGELICA, is a first-in-human trial intended to evaluate the safety, activity, and safe dose of CTM-N2D in subjects with advanced solid tumours or haematological malignancies. A dose of CTM-N2D will be given weekly for four consecutive weeks, and up to five maintenance doses. A conventional “3+3” cohort expansion study is designed to determine a safe dose of CTM-N2D based on the incidence of dose-limiting toxicity in three cohorts for three dose levels. A recommended phase 2 dose of CTM-N2D will be determined upon completion of this study.
kw: CAR-T; CTM-N2D; Advanced solid tumours; Haematological malignancies

title: ADL+ 2.0: Enhanced AI-assisted multidomain digital intervention for prevention of cognitive decline in community-dwelling older adults
abs: Singapore's rising dementia incidence with an ageing population presents an urgent need for effective interventions that delay or prevent cognitive decline. While multidomain intervention studies for dementia prevention show promise, there is a need for an effective personalised approach to address an individual’s multifactorial risks for dementia, and to achieve cost-effective, scalable and sustainable outcomes for wider implementation. Building on our positive proof-of-value results, we propose the ADL+ 2.0 programme. The overall goal is to delay or prevent cognitive decline in at-risk individuals without dementia aged 60 and above with subjective memory complaints and/or impaired cognitive capacity from the ICOPE screening tool. Through a population-level, technology-enabled, community-based preventative approach, ADL+ 2.0 provides remote assessment and multi-component intervention (cognitive training, dual-tasking exercises, and cognitive wellness) with smart scheduling and personalised intervention, and can be delivered in conjunction with the onsite 6 WELLS facilitated group-based activity, underpinned by the Self-Determination Theory to foster intrinsic motivation for lasting behavioural change. Our two-phase approach begins with Phase 1 test-bedding in a Type 2 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study. We will conduct a 3-arm cluster randomised controlled trial comparing remote and onsite, remote-only, and control groups to assess the impact on cognitive outcomes, social networks, quality-of-life and cost-effectiveness. We will identify barriers and facilitators for implementation, guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. In Phase 2 scale-up, ADL+ 2.0 will be further scaled across Singapore, including primary care, while assessing real-world implementation outcomes in a pragmatic trial. Together with our technology partner (NTU LILY/LKCMedicine), we will work closely with our community (NTUC Health, Fei Yue Community Services, Bishan East Sin Ming Constituency, National Library Board and Health Promotion Board) and evaluation partners (GERI/NUS) to provide evidence for and effectively implement a scalable, sustainable, and cost-effective community programme for the prevention of cognitive decline in Singapore.
kw: Cognition; Dementia; Multi-component intervention; Prevention; Implementation

title: The role of eating behavior in cardiometabolic health in Asian population
abs: Obesity, or excess adiposity, is a known risk factor for cardiometabolic diseases and other chronic diseases. Genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors influence fat deposition, including dietary habit and the underlying eating behaviour. Eating behaviour is a complex construct but can be characterized using established behavioural intervention frameworks. Eating behaviour in the multiethnic Asian population remains uncharacterized. I hypothesize that eating behaviour contribute to dietary habit and excess adiposity in the multiethnic Asian population. To test this hypothesis, I aim to i) collect a comprehensive eating behavioural phenotyping in 900 participants of the Health for Life in Singapore (HELIOS) Study using validated questionnaires, and ii) identify independent eating behavioural risk factors that promote excess adiposity in Asian population through epidemiological and metabolomic analyses. In Aim 1, I will administer multiple validated questionnaires on eating behaviour, such as emotional eating, appetite, taste preference and many more. I will invite a subset of 100 participants for reproducibility testing. In Aim 2, I will link the eating behavioural data with other behavioural sources collected in the HELIOS Study, including participants’ cognitive function and socio-demographic factors, along with dietary intake. I will then perform univariate and multivariable analyses to determine independent eating behavioural measures which contribute to adiposity. To biologically validate these epidemiological analyses, I will assess the associations of eating behavioural risk factors with representative metabolites in the HELIOS Study dataset of healthy (fruits, cruciferous vegetables) and unhealthy food groups (processed meats). These markers are established as part of the recently completed works. The shortlisted eating behavioural factors would guide the design of future intervention trial and help identifying the subgroup-at-risk for health policy formation at population levels. The knowledge would potentially equip our healthcare sectors with population-specific evidence for social prescribing.
kw: eating behavior; dietary habit; obesity; appetite; self-regulation; population health

title: Deep learning application for Cobb’s angle assessment in Singapore
abs: Aim: To implement and optimise an in-house preliminary deep learning (DL) model, trained for the automated quantification of scoliosis radiographs at the large volume screening centres at the Health Promotion Board (HPB) and central manpower base (CMPB), the screening point of National Service (NS) enlistment. Hypothesis: The DL model created using input from expert annotations from radiology and orthopaedics will be able to rapidly generate accurate scoliosis angles resulting in increased accuracy and reduced interpretation time, ultimately leading to cost savings at these high-volume sites. Methodology and Approach: 1. To implement the deep learning model into the current HPB workflow. 2. Validate the model for both accuracy and time savings in a prospective study at the HPB. 3. Based on (2), further retraining and possible optimisation of both the implementation workflow and model weights. 4. Final prospective validation of the model's accuracy and (potential) time savings.
kw: Deep learning, Radiology, Scoliosis, Population Health, Screening

title: Tackling issues facing the Singapore colorectal cancer screening programme
abs: Specific aims and hypotheses Aims: 1. Using a theory-driven approach to understand and intervene on factors associated with CRC screening uptake for average-risk individuals and compliance of FIT-positive individuals to recommended follow-up 2. Validate and demonstrate the efficacy of stool haemoglobin (Hb) levels in predicting colonoscopy outcomes using non-invasive Hb measurement Hypotheses: 1. Modifiable barriers and facilitators exist at each step of the national CRC screening process, including initial uptake and compliance after FIT-positive 2. Non-invasive Hb measurement can yield high diagnostic accuracy in predicting pathologic scope findings among FIT-positive patients undergoing colonoscopy Methods and approach Study 1 will use the extended health belief model (HBM) to identify barriers and facilitators to CRC screening uptake among average risk individuals (1a), and subsequently pilot a randomised behavioural intervention for increasing FIT screening among demographic groups with the highest proportion of screen-naive individuals (1b). Study 2 is a tailored educational intervention to convert non-compliant FIT-positive individuals to complete the first step of recommendations after a positive FIT, which is a follow-up consultation with a gastrointestinal specialist. Study 3 will validate associations between stool Hb values to the likelihood of detecting CRC and colonic adenomas using retrospective national data (3a). Subsequently, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV of FIT, and optimal quantitative cut-off values for the screen-eligible population will be determined using a prospective cohort (3b). Study 4 will evaluate instrument accuracy and reliability of the non-invasive Hb measurement tool (4a) and establish diagnostic accuracy of non-invasive Hb measurement in predicting colonoscopy outcomes in a prospective FIT-positive follow-up cohort. Importance to science and medicine This project will generate a more comprehensive understanding of the barriers, facilitators, and attitudes towards CRC screening for average-risk Singapore Residents. The project will also validate the efficacy of new, non-invasive tools to risk stratify individuals requiring follow-up colonoscopy.
kw: colorectal cancer; faecal immunochemical test; colonoscopy; screening uptake; risk stratification

title: Conversational Health AI for Mental Health
abs: In this research programme, we propose to develop Conversational Health AI (CHAI) framework and technologies that are capable of (a) understanding user’s mental health issues, as well as (b) improving user’s ability to cope with them, using Motivational Interviewing (MI) which is a principled counselling technique. This is a 3-year long research project. We will adopt a divide-and-conquer research strategy to divide MI techniques into different stages and formulate them as different conversational AI subtasks. We then design and optimize prompts that guide GPT-based Large Language Models (GPT-based LLM) to specialize in performing these subtasks under the coordination of a Conversational Meta Model (CMM). The work packages include: 1. Work Package 1: In this work package, we propose to develop the CMM module that automatically constructs a counselling plan based on MI which include multiple counselling sessions to cover the different subtasks. As the plan construction process is an exploration of subtasks to engage the counsellee (i.e., the environment) and exploitation of knowledge about the counsellee, we propose to incorporate reinforcement learning, a machine learning technique that rewards good choices of subtasks and penalizes poor ones. 2. Work Package 2 (GPT-based LLMs): To develop GPT-based LLMs, we perform prompt optimization include the prompts’ overall effectiveness in accomplishing each assigned subtask considering user attributes, mental health issues (if known), and the current user’s state of mind. For example, a Singlish-speaking user may add Singlish words and phrases to the conversations. By personalizing the language and tone used in the counselling session, CHAI is expected to enhance the user’s counselling experience. 3. Work Package 3 (User Evaluation Study): Two rounds of user evaluation study will be performed, one for measuring the performance of CHAI against human experts and another for measuring the performance of CHAI by human experts.
kw: Mental Health, Effective Use of Technology to Improve Health

title: Renal Medicine Strategic Research Programme – Singapore Prevention and Retardation of Kidney Disease Study (SPARKS)
abs: My current research focuses on developing a deeper understanding on the determinants of chronic kidney disease (CKD) development and progression through establishing a prospective CKD disease cohort with deep clinical and biochemical phenotyping. This cohort will allow us to study their socio-demographic, clinical, laboratory, health literacy and health behaviour data longitudinally. This would also allow us to understand the determinants of CKD development and progression, develop better risk prediction models, and develop more effective and personalized therapies to retard CKD progression for better cost-effective care. I am the project lead for one of the thrusts of the Renal Medicine Strategic Research Programme which focuses on novel target identification – specifically, signaling pathways in CKD. Through collaborative work with our colleagues across disciplines and institutions, this study aims to interrogate inflammatory pathways in the development and progression of CKD to assess the correlation between serum and urine biomarkers with the risk of CKD development and progression, as well as the incidence of cardiovascular disease in patients with CKD. This would allow identification of potential immune mediated pathways of inflammation and fibrosis that can be targeted to retard CKD progression.
kw: Chronic kidney disease (CKD), precision medicine

title: Developing a Genetic Treatment Strategy for GUCY2D-Related Autosomal Dominant Cone-Rod Dystrophy
abs: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a leading cause of blindness among the working-age population in developed countries, and until recently have been considered untreatable. Successful proof-of-concept has been demonstrated for gene therapy in IRDs, and there are many ongoing clinical trials in this area. Autosomal dominant (AD) cone-rod dystrophy (CORD) caused by mutations in GUCY2D is an attractive, and as-yet untapped IRD treatment target. GUCY2D-related AD CORD is an important and relevant IRD subtype in Singapore, Asia, and worldwide. However, current gene therapy techniques relying on gene replacement for recessive disease will not work in this case, as the disease mechanism is due to gain-of-function mutations. Instead, a different genetic treatment strategy is required to tackle dominant disease, such as gene editing. The overall aim of this proposed Doctor of Philosophy (DPhil) project at the Nuffield Laboratory of Ophthalmology, University of Oxford, is to develop and validate an effective genetic treatment strategy for GUCY2D-related AD CORD, with the eventual long-term goal of initiating a first-in-man clinical trial. Specifically, we aim to use clustered regularly interspaced palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 gene editing to target the two predominant pathogenic GUCY2D variants R838C and R838H, and demonstrate the feasibility of this approach in vitro on patient-derived immortalized cells lines and in vivo in a transgenic pig model. We also aim to utilize artificial intelligence techniques to design and engineer optimized CRISPR-Cas9 tools, to boost GUCY2D editing efficiency and minimize off-target effects. This proposed project addresses an important unmet clinical and scientific need, and has the potential to lead to an investigational new drug that could be the basis for a first-in-man clinical trial. The skills and expertise acquired from this project will allow the candidate to make impactful contributions to the continued development of precision medicine and genetic therapies in Singapore and the region.
kw: gene therapy; CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing; inherited retinal disease; retinal dystrophy; translational research; artificial intelligence (AI)-based engineering

title: Assessing the prevalence, metabolic aberrations, and mental health burden of Food Allergy in Singaporean Children - The Singapore Food Allergy Story (SFAS).
abs: Background: Patients with food allergies (FA) experience metabolic and growth derangements, food insecurity and significant adverse mental health outcomes due to food restrictions and lack of social, economic and psychological support in the community. The current burden of FA is unknown in Singapore, yet preliminary data suggests the rates of FA are rising rapidly in children. Aims: Conduct a cross-sectional prevalence study among children below 2 years of age visiting polyclinics for well-child visits to establish the current prevalence of FA; and To quantify and determine factors contributing to the metabolic and psychosocial impact of FA on children and their families in Singapore through a separate cohort of high-risk food allergic children. Methodology: We will survey 2000 children below 2 years of age visiting polyclinics across the 3 healthcare clusters in Singapore for well-child visits to capture the prevalence of convincing food allergy through validated questionnaires and skin prick testing. We will separately recruit a cohort of 400 children with milk, egg, peanut, shellfish and/or two or more food allergies from specialist allergy clinics across Singapore. Clinical questionnaires, growth assessments, dietary and mental health data in relation to food allergy, as well as plasma nutrients will be collected to assess the impact of FA on growth, metabolic phenotypes and mental health of FA patients and their families. Clinical significance: The study will comprehensively demonstrate the rising metabolic, nutritional and mental health burden of FA in Singaporean children. The findings will allow us to identify specific nutrient deficiencies, growth and metabolic abnormalities and aberrant feeding behaviours in food allergic children, and gaps in support infrastructure. This will form the basis for development of guidelines to optimize growth and metabolic outcomes, promote awareness in community and schools, and enhance socioeconomic and mental health support for food allergic patients in Singapore.
kw: Food; allergy; prevalence; metabolic; nutrition; mental health

title: Adolescents’ health risk behaviours in the Singapore context – perspectives, participatory action and predictors
abs: Health risk behaviours during adolescence can influence the risk of chronic noncommunicable diseases and morbidity later in life. There is a devoid of data on adolescents’ health risk behaviours in Asian populations, particularly emerging contemporary behaviours stemming from technological advances. The pathways to the development of these behaviours are also less understood. Involving youths in intervention development and implementation to better meet their needs and interests has shown to be efficacious, yet their involvement, perspectives and motivations for these behaviours have largely been unexplored. Adopting a Youth-led Participatory Action Research approach with community-based adolescents, this study (Project 1) aims to gain insights into adolescents’ perspectives of contemporary health risk behaviours that are of concern to them, understand their corresponding motivations and barriers and engage adolescents as co-researchers to develop relevant intervention strategies. Additionally, they will be engaged in the development of an age and culturally-appropriate risk behaviour assessment questionnaire for adolescents in a multi-cultural Asian setting. This questionnaire will be administered and validated in adolescents of an ongoing mother-offspring cohort (Project 2) and statistical analyses conducted to investigate the antecedents and predictors of adolescents’ health risk behaviours and their associations with mental and physical health outcomes. We hypothesize that some perceptions of health risk behaviours among adolescents differ from adults, thus influencing their motivations to engage in these behaviours. We posit that engaging adolescents to influence decisions about intervention design and services will lead to tailored and effective intervention strategies to mitigate current negative health risk behaviours. We propose that an in-depth examination of early life predictors that influence the development of health risk behaviours will inform targeted, relevant interventions that are central to a life course approach and may have a longer-lasting impact on an individual's propensity to engage in health risk behaviours during adolescence.
kw: Adolescents; Health risk behaviours; Participatory research; Predictors of Risk behaviours

title: Promoting Early Book Reading at Home: An Intervention with Enhanced eBooks
abs: Shared book reading has been found to have positive and lasting impact on many aspects of child development, such language skills, literacy, and socio-emotional well-being. In Singapore, the conduct of shared book reading at home has been found to be significantly related to Mother Tongue Language learning. Despite this, recent studies have found that many families rarely engage in this activity. In this mixed-method project, parents of 2–6-year-old bilingual children are interviewed, with the goal of uncovering parental attitudes towards Mother Tongue reading at home and identifying obstacles in conducting shared reading at home. The project also explores the potential efficacy of using enhanced eBooks to facilitate shared book reading both in the short and long term, through two interventions. In the first intervention, parent-child dyads engage in shared book reading utilizing an enhanced interactive eBook. Dyad neurological, cognitive, and behavioral engagement will be recorded. In the second intervention, children will be provided with enhanced eBooks on a specialized reading platform for a period of 10 weeks. Child reading frequency and language skills will be assessed. Parental and child perception to the enhanced eBooks will be explored with exit interviews. This study is a global pioneer in examining the unique challenges faced by bilingual parents in fostering ethnic language readers at home, and the first in Singapore to utilize multimedia features in digital books to tackle literacy issues that bilingual local parents face via examining the immediate and longitudinal efficacy of the new reading modality.
kw: Early Bilingualism; Mother Tongue Language Learning; Enhanced eBooks; Neuroimaging; Shared Book Reading

title: CSA-iTrust Master of Science in Security By Design Scholarship (CiMS) RIE2025
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: The CSA-iTrust Master of Science in Security by Design Scholarship (CiMS) Programme aims to grow and develop a pool of cybersecurity professionals in Singapore, by awarding scholarships to worthy candidates who are enrolled in the Masters of Science in Security by Design (MSSD) programme in the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
kw: Scholarship

title: Nano-needles for transgene-free, universal plant genetic engineering
abs: Singapore has set an ambitious food security goal and one way to achieve this is to strengthen our national capabilities in plant biotechnology such as genetic engineering. To do so, genetic cargo that confer desirable traits must be delivered into the nuclei of plant cells for stable gene expressions. However, it is challenging to develop a universal, efficient and transgene-free delivery technique that is minimally perturbative to transgenic plant regeneration. Delivery using Agrobacterium (with syringe infiltration), viruses, nanoparticles and biolistic particles suffer from limitations like low delivery efficiency, cargo load and throughput. Our technology which employs controlled mechanical puncture with nano-needles will serve as a universal and efficient tool for genetic engineering of any plant species (monocots and dicots) using leaves and pollens, without the constraints of biological agents like Agrobacterium and viruses. Furthermore, we have integrated our nano-needle technology into a clamp device for semi-automated, cost-effective and high throughput gene delivery. This proposal aims to (1) optimise nano-needles for delivering the CRISPR/cas9 plant gene editing cassettes for monocots (rice) and leafy vegetables (kailan), (2) screen for genetic constructs that will be usable in future to generate crop varieties with at least 20% faster growth, and (3) build an electronic nano-needle system to enhance platform use in controlled environment agricultural farms.
kw: Plant genetic engineering, delivery, nano-needles

title: TeethFiX-RPD - Automatic Teeth Anatomy Identification on 3D Intra-oral Scans via Multi-task Geometric Deep Learning Approach: Application in Removable Partial Denture Treatment.
abs: Most dental treatments involve examinations of patients’ oral cavities and teeth via impression taking and moulding which are unpleasant and laborious processes for both patients and dentists. In recent years, a patient’s three-dimensional scans of the oral cavity and teeth information can be accurately and efficiently digitized at the chairside with an intra-oral scanner (IOS). With the increasing availability of IOS data, recent computational studies have employed deep learning models to improve dental treatments by automatically segmenting and labelling teeth on the IOS data. However, existing models overlooked models’ generalizability, i.e., perform well on various dental dentitions found in young-elderly patients. They also require fully annotated IOS data which is time-consuming to collect. Moreover, there is no existing study on the automatic identification of teeth surfaces. These drawbacks hinder its application in routine clinical practice. To address these gaps, we aim to apply geometric deep learning models on the IOS data via multi-task learning architecture to two digital dentistry topics: (1) automatic teeth segmentation and labelling, and (2) automatic partition of the tooth surfaces to five anatomical sides, i.e., occlusal, buccal, lingual, mesial, and distal surfaces. Specifically, the proposed model should be generalizable, interpretable, and require minimal annotation of IOS data. To verify its clinical applicability, the proposed model will be incorporated into an in-house removable partial denture design software, and its improvements will be assessed quantitatively and qualitatively. Towards these goals, we have collected around 2800 IOS data of both normal and severe dentitions and developed tools to help dentists label the IOS data. This proposal will set a solid foundation for automating and improving many restorative and corrective dental treatments, e.g., aligner and denture fabrication, oral disease assessment, etc., which are clinically important and useful.
kw: teeth anatomy; digital dentistry; geometric deep learning; multi-task learning; teeth surface partition; teeth segmentation and labelling;

title: Bringing about Optimal weight loss Outcomes through dietary and weight management Support driven by generative artificial intelligence Technology (BOOST-AI): A pragmatic randomised controlled study in type 2 diabetes
abs: Background Weight management in type 2 diabetes prevents development of diabetes-related complications However, they are often intensive and costly, and health app-based programs can potentially be more cost-effective. Systematic reviews have found that apps combined with human-facilitated behavioural intervention are more effective. The emergence of large language models (LLM) and its ability to comprehend and generate human-like text may improve effectiveness while reducing dependence on clinician manpower requirement. Aims The first aim of our research program is to apply generative AI to develop the Boost-AI weight management program, which consists of an AI meal recommendation system and an AI weight management chatbot, that will be integrated with a virtual pet platform to support weight management in type 2 diabetes and pre-diabetes. The second aim is to conduct a pragmatic randomised controlled study to assess the effectiveness of the Boost-AI program in weight loss for people with type 2 diabetes compared to an existing diabetes self-care app in a primary care setting Methods A randomised control study will be conducted to compare the effectiveness of the Boost AI program compared to an existing diabetes self-care app with no generative AI functions. 119 participants aged 21 to 64 who are overweight/obese with type 2 diabetes will be recruited to each arm. Outcomes will be assessed over 6 months, and will include weight loss, clinical parameters (HbA1c, blood pressure), behaviors (diet, physical activity, self-care), self-efficacy, health related quality of life and resource utilization. A qualitative study will assess experience of the Boost-AI program. Conclusion This research program aims to apply generative AI to provide patient-centered care in type 2 diabetes, leading to improved lifestyle behaviors and weight loss. Findings from this study will guide future implementation in primary care settings.
kw: Artificial Intelligence; Weight Management; Diet; Type 2 diabetes; pre-diabetes: population health

title: Direct Admission from Primary Care to Hospital-at-Home: An Implementation Evaluation
abs: In response to the global challenges posed by an ageing population and the strain on hospital bed capacity, hospital-at-Home (HaH) programmes offer a potential solution by delivering hospital-level care to patients at home. As HaH programmes expand, efforts largely involve patient transfers from hospitals and emergency departments. Nearly 1 in 4 hospital admissions are initially referred from primary care settings, but direct admission of patients from primary care to HaH is underexplored. In this proposal, our main question is: how do we implement direct admission from primary care to HaH? To explore feasibility, barriers, and enablers to scaling, we will combine state-of-the-art implementation science frameworks with mixed methods approaches in a two-phase research proposal. The first phase quantifies the volume and characteristics of patients admitted to hospitals from four primary care settings (polyclinic, general practice clinics, home medical services, and nursing homes) that could be potentially admitted to HaH. Subsequently, a prospective controlled hybrid study compares patients directly admitted to HaH from primary care with matched controls from the Emergency Department, assessing clinical, cost, and implementation outcomes. Qualitative interviews will also be conducted to explore the acceptability and experiences of patients and caregivers. The second phase focuses on identifying implementation determinants and strategies. Qualitative interviews with primary care providers will first provide insights into potential barriers and facilitators associated with referring patients directly to HaH. These findings will be used to conduct policy labs that involve primary care leaders, healthcare cluster representatives, and policymakers to co-design implementation and policy strategies. The results of this study will be used to inform how to further scale and develop pathways to admit patients directly from primary care to HaH nationally as HaH programmes integrate into mainstream care, ultimately offering patients a seamless experience while reducing burden on hospital care.
kw: Hospital-at-Home; Primary care; ED avoidance; Health services research; Implementation science; Healthcare delivery

title: Dose-response Effect of Community Dance Programme on the Physical, Cognitive, Psychosocial Health of Pre-frail Older Adults: A Cluster Randomised Trial with Co-design Approach and Process Evaluation
abs: Frailty is a complex and common phenomenon among older adults which is characterised by depletion of reserves in multiple organ systems leading to physiologic vulnerability such as functional decline and increased risk of falls. Hence, it is important to prevent frailty and enable older adults to live healthily in the community. Dance is effective to improve muscular strength, endurance and balance. Furthermore, dance with music increases motivation and adherence to prescribed physical exercises. The overall aim of this study is to use data derived from our pilot study to design and conduct a definitive study to define the dose-response effect that a systematic dance programme may have on physical, cognitive and psycho-social health in our local ageing population. The primary objective is to develop and evaluate a Community Dance Programme, which is aimed at promoting physical strength, balance, cognition, and psychosocial well-being of pre-frail older adults. A cluster randomised trial with co-design approach and process evaluation will be applied. We will engage the stakeholders (older adults, Active Ageing Centres staff, and dance instructors) in the co-design process of tailored dance programme, taking into consideration of older adults’ age, physical conditions, and cultural preferences. Upon completion of the intervention, we will adopt focused ethnography to explore the perspectives and experiences of the stakeholders systematically and comprehensively. The Community Dance Programme focuses on preventive health, takes proactive steps to stay physically active, and leads to healthier lifestyles. Findings from this study will provide scientific evidence on the effective dose of dance programme which balances benefit on improving physical function against side effects of muscle ache and fatigue. This customized dance programme, if proven effective, can be optimized for our local community, which provides a platform to promote Healthier SG initiative to a wider population of older adults.
kw: Dance Intervention; Dose-response Effect; Frailty; Healthy Ageing; Older Adults; Physical Performance

title: Optimising and assessing electrical stimulation of the Optic nerve in comparison with visual stimulation for diagnostic and monitoring of ocular disease – the AESON Study
abs: Purpose: (i) To optimize stimulation of the optic nerve along the visual pathway; (ii) to get recordings of visual function from the visual cortex. To provide a baseline assessment of visual function in patients with optic nerve and/or retinal diseases (estimated 600 million people worldwide) as well as to compare visual function at follow up visits (to monitor disease progression or assess response to treatment). It will also be helpful in assessing optic nerve function when there is a media opacity. This technology also can be used for diagnostic and monitoring purposes in myopia (which will affect 4.7 billion people by 2050) to differentiate myopic maculopathy from glaucoma. The main hypothesis is that consistent evoked potentials can be achieved with electrical stimulation comparable to visual stimulation with the derived electrical current settings, potentially enhancing further research on stimulation of the optic nerve for therapeutic purposes. Methods: Preliminary in-silico and pilot clinical trials were conducted in Cambridge from 2022-2023 which found that transorbital stimulation with two electrodes (one stimulating and one returning) placed diagonally and periorbitally gave the most promising results. The study in Singapore will be in 2 phases. Phase 1: Recruitment of 100 patients (with optic nerve and/or retinal diseases) and 100 volunteers (with no eye diseases) who will perform the visual evoked potential (VEP), then the electrical evoked potential (EP) and the results will be analysed. Phase 2: 100 myopia patients will be recruited to undergo the VEP and EP tests with addition of multifocal pattern electroretinogram (PERG). Primary outcome measure is the measurement of amplitude of evoked potentials. Other outcome measures include the safety profile and side effects of electrical stimulation of the optic nerve using this novel electrical stimulation protocol.
kw: electrical stimulation optic nerve

title: AI-Optimized Oral Microbiome Metagenomics: A Gateway to Cardiometabolic Risk Prediction in Adolescents
abs: Despite tremendous advances in pathophysiological understanding of cardiometabolic diseases (CMD), their global burden remains high. Current preventive strategies, primarily targeting only proximal lifestyle factors in adulthood, have not effectively reduced CMD onset. Adopting a life-course approach, a Finnish study demonstrated the link between childhood oral health and elevated carotid intima media thickness (cIMT) in adults 27 years later. Our preliminary oral microbiome data in the GUSTO cohort also indicated a significant association between nitrate-reducing bacteria on the tongue at age 5 and both cIMT at age 6 and blood pressure at ages 7 and 8, indicating elevated CMD risk linked to oral microbiome even in childhood. Aligned with the goals of Healthier SG, a national initiative by the Ministry of Health (MOH), this multi-disciplinary project aims to yield two key outcomes (KOs) crucial for tackling CMD: KO-1, providing novel scientific insights pertinent to CMD etiologies and pathogenic pathways related to oral health/microbiome throughout childhood and adolescence, and KO-2, a three-tier AI-driven CMD-risk prediction model (ARPM) for specialists, general practitioners, and the public for secondary and primary prevention of CMD, incorporating oral health exposures alongside conventional risk factors. The strategic steps involve 1) employing the shotgun metagenomics platform to analyze oral microbiome/DNA samples collected at ages 2, 3, 5 and 14 years to elucidate mechanistic pathways between early childhood oral health (“exposure”) and adolescent cardio-metabolic health (“outcome”), 2) mapping the developmental stages of oral microbiome from childhood to adolescence (age 2~14 years), and 3) quantifying the additional value of oral biomarkers in the predictive accuracy of ARPM. Anticipated translational outcomes include inspiring novel lifestyle solutions tailored to youth (e.g. trendy pre/probiotic products, functional foods, and oral care products) and CMD risk calculator/apps for children/adolescents and/or clinicians to implement primary/secondary prevention of CMD and reduce CMD burden in Singapore and beyond.
kw: oral microbiome; oral health; early childhood; adolescent; cardio-metabolic health; risk prediction models; machine learning;

title: Spatial omics in deciphering crosstalk between microbiome and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment of early-stage colorectal cancer
abs: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide with more than 1.85 million cases and 850,000 deaths annually attributable to metastasis. Up to 25% of early-stage CRC (stage I/II) patients succumb to metastasis despite curative surgery. Tumor microenvironment (TME) governs CRC progression, invasion, overall survival, and treatment response. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) facilitate tumor growth and metastatic dissemination. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) support the epithelial cells and are key regulators in tumorigenesis. Bacteria co-localize within the TME with composition correlated to tumor type and treatment responses. Hypothesis: We hypothesize that CAFs and TAMs could mediate tumor-stromal cell interactions while modulated by intratumor microbiome (IM) and promote metastases via immune and inflammatory pathways. We aim to spatially characterize TME through proteomics profiling and single-cell imaging, targeting the CAFs (FAP marker), TAMs (CD163 marker) and CAFs/TAMs interactions with IM to identify pathogenic mechanisms in early-stage CRC. The goal is to understand the mechanisms underlying microbiota contributions to immune and inflammatory responses in TME and metastasis. Method: About 150 tumor sections with confirmed metastasis status of early-stage CRC will be profiled. Intratumor bacteria (Bac+) will be detected by 16S rRNA In Situ Hybridization (ISH) for bacterial localization. Morphology markers staining (FAP and CD163) will guide the selection for 4 regions: FAPhigh/CD163low/Bac+, FAPhigh/CD163low/Bac-, FAPlow/CD163high/Bac+ and FAPlow/CD163high/Bac- for proteomics profiling with spatial resolution, follow by spatial single-cell imaging to investigate cell-cell interactions under influences of microbiome. IM clusters will be profiled with shotgun metagenomics. Significance: Spatially resolved proteomics and single-cell analysis could identify tissue organization and dysregulated functions in the vicinity of pathogenic influences. The goal is to capture early events in TME for potential microbiome-associated metastasis initiation, enabling patient selection for tailored surveillance and further adjuvant chemotherapy to reduce disease burden and potentiate new therapeutic target for early-stage CRC.
kw: spatial proteomics; colorectal cancer; tumor microenvironment; intratumor microbiome; immune

title: Genetic and pharmacological targeting of Hippo Signaling effectors Yap/Taz for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis
abs: Human fibrotic diseases, where normal tissue is replaced by scar tissue ultimately leading to organ failure, are reported to be responsible for ~45% of all deaths worldwide. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is one of the most common fibrotic lung diseases. IPF is an interstitial lung disease that results from the excessive deposition of collagen, leading to progressive stiffening of the lung and the consequent loss of ability to mediate gas exchange. Due to the constitutive decline in vital capacity, median survival following diagnosis is estimated at only 2–3 years, with the severity of associated morbidities increasing continuously during the later stages of the disease. Aging is one of the strongest risk factors for IPF. As the population aging is particularly serious in Singapore: the population of 65 years or over is 12.4% in 2019 and is predicted to rise further to 33.3% in 2050, lung-associated diseases are going to pose an economic burden to our society and a serious challenge to our health care system. The molecular mechanisms of fibrosis in IPF patients are not fully understood and there is a lack of effective treatments. Towards this goal, we have uncovered that Yes-associated protein (Yap) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (Taz) play important roles in regulating macrophage and fibroblast-specific functions in the bleomycin-induced IPF model. Based on our recently published work and preliminary results presented here, we hypothesize that Yap/Taz-dependent functions of lung macrophages and lung fibroblast are critical contributors to the development of IPF and pharmacological targeting of Yap/Taz may provide a better option to treat IPF.
kw: Lung fibrosis, Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, Hippo Signaling, Macrophage reprogramming

title: An open-label, single arm, non-randomised investigator-initiated Phase 1B study to evaluate the preliminary clinical activity, safety and tolerability of ETC-159 in combination with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced or metastatic, platinum-resistant pMMR/MSS ovarian cancers.
abs: Ovarian cancer is a leading cause of death for women across the world. Patients who become resistant to platinum-based chemotherapy have very few treatment options. Single agent treatment with approved PD-1 inhibitors shows limited efficacy in mismatch-repair proficient (pMMR)/microsatellite stable (MSS) recurrent ovarian cancers. Small molecules that suppress Wnt secretion, such as the porcupine (PORCN) inhibitor ETC-159 were shown to effectively block hyperactivated Wnt signalling, which is associated with platinum and PARPi resistance in advanced ovarian cancers. Furthermore, ETC-159 stimulates immune-infiltration in the tumour and the tumour microenvironment (TME) and downregulates immunosuppressants. In a previous phase 1B trial, ETC-159, when dosed in combination with pembrolizumab (a PD-1 inhibitor), was shown to be tolerable with no unexpected safety signals in patients with various advanced or metastatic, or unresectable solid malignancies. Among these, in six heavily treated platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) patients, a disease control rate (DCR) (Stable Disease/Partial Response/Complete Response ≥ 12 weeks) of 67% was observed. The Objective Response Rate (ORR) was 33%, indicating an early signal of activity. The proposed investigator-initiated Phase 1B study aims to further explore this signal in an open label study of ETC-159 in combination with pembrolizumab in advanced pMMR/MSS PROC patients. Up to 16 eligible patients will be enrolled from two sites in Singapore. In addition to safety monitoring, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic assessments, radiological tumour response will be evaluated by RECIST v1.1. Tumour genomic profiling and gene/protein expression assays will also be performed. This study allows for data collection from an ethnically diverse patient population pool across various socioeconomic and educational backgrounds. Results from this study will provide further evidence to support use of ETC-159 in combination with pembrolizumab in PROC patients with limited treatment options and will significantly enhance the possibility of further advancing the clinical development of ETC-159 to Phase 2/3 studies.
kw: Ovarian Cancers; Pembrolizumab; pMMR/MSS

title: Eye gaze tracking for guidance of age-related macula degeneration therapy.
abs: Our technology is an Artificial Intelligence approach named Automated Vision Assessment and Impairment Detection through Gaze Analysis (AVIGA) technology to provide a non-invasive assessment of an individual's visual performance without the need for complex ophthalmic equipment. This device is intended for use for monitoring the disease progression or recurrence in wet Age-Related Macular degeneration (AMD). AVIGA is a gaze-based eye tracking device that is designed to be deployed in a home-based setting as an adjunctive tool for AMD monitoring. The AVIGA system is comprised of the: i) AVIGA eye tracker: the eye-tracking camera that detects eye motion events and computes the gaze coordinates in response to the visual stimulus. ii) AVIGA Software: the eye analysis software is loaded onto a desktop or laptop computer and connected to the internet to remotely upload and analyze data. During eye tracking, AVIGA collects the gaze data and processes it for correlation with the presented eye tracking and calculates a score. If the score deviates by a certain magnitude from the previous readings, possible abnormalities or progression of AMD are indicated. We propose a pragmatic randomized, controlled trial, non-inferiority study design to evaluate the safety and efficacy of AVIGA guided clinical workflow and the standard of care workflow. AVIGA’s visual stimulus method comprises of presenting a set of test patterns sequentially to the subject, collecting data on the subject's gaze in response to each displayed test pattern and assessing vision functionality of the subject based on the collected gaze data. AVIGA calculates a score based on the collected gaze measurements to determine potential anomalies or a degradation in visual field (VF) performance. Alerts shall be sent to the clinician and patients when there is such VF degradation for the clinicians to assess as per current clinical standard of care.
kw: age-related macula degeneration, anti-vascular endothelial growth factor, artificial intelligence, home monitoring.

title: A phase I Multicenter, Open-Label Study of an autologous CD19/CD20 Bispecific CAR T Cell Therapy in Adult Patients with Relapsed or Refractory B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
abs: While chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy are breakthrough therapies that can achieve response in patients with relapsed or refractory lymphoma, resistance with long term survivals in the range of 30-40% is common, due to downregulation or loss of CD19 expression, or related to poor T cell functionality and persistence. A further challenge is the risk of life-threatening toxicities related to T cell activation and release of high levels of cytokines (interleukin-6). To address these efficacy and safety concerns, we use a novel cell manufacturing platform to generate a bispecific CAR T-cell that simultaneously targets two pan B-cell antigens (CD19/CD20) and can enrich for naive and memory phenotypes while reducing cytokines associated with toxicity. We hypothesize that the CD19/CD20 bispecific CAR T-cell generated using our unique cell processing platform will have promising response rates with few adverse events. We propose to evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of the CD19/CD20 CAR T-cell in patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell lymphoma in a phase I dose-escalation using a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with 3+3 run in. Primary objectives include safety (high grade cytokine release syndrome or neurotoxicity) and determination of a maximum tolerated dose for phase 2 trials. Secondary objectives include evaluation of preliminary clinical efficacy of the CAR T-cell as measured by overall response rate, progression-free survival and overall survival. The trial is feasible as Singapore General Hospital has demonstrated expertise in clinical operations related to immune effector cell therapies with well benchmarked care pathways stipulated by FACT-JACIE accreditation. Our proposal to develop a safe and effective CAR T-cell therapy using innovative manufacturing approaches, in partnership with ACTRIS Singapore, is an important step towards improving the cost-effectiveness of CAR T-cell therapy for the benefit of patients and sustainable healthcare systems.
kw: lymphoma; chimeric antigen receptor; CD19; CD20; bispecific

title: Insights into the Pathobiology of Cerebral White Matter Disease in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Prevention Strategies with Pharmacological and Digital-Artificial Intelligence
abs: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an important disease stage along the cognitive continuum as interventions at the MCI stage could result in lower incidence and prevalence of dementia. Findings from our group have demonstrated a high burden of cerebral white matter disease among our subjects with MCI with 80% having some amount of white matter disease and 40% of these to be of moderate-severe white matter disease. The pathobiology underlying white matter disease in subjects with MCI is not clearly known. In this study we will classify 600 subjects with MCI having white matter disease based on their cardiovascular risk profile status. The contribution of endothelial dysfunction, blood brain barrier dysfunction, neuroinflammation and cerebrovascular amyloid to the onset and progression of white matter disease over 3 years will be studied. The contribution of these various pathologies to clinical outcomes including cognitive performance, behaviour and progression to dementia will also be evaluated. Cutting-edge neuroimaging techniques including diffusion-prepared arterial spin labelling, diffusion kurtosis imaging as well as ultra-sensitive blood biomarker detection systems will be used to identify early perfusion deficits and early blood biomarker changes in subjects with MCI. From an interventional perspective, two proof-of-concept studies will be carried out. The first will be to study the usefulness of empagliflozin, a novel SGLT2 inhibitor in reducing endothelial dysfunction and neuroinflammation in MCI patients with white matter disease. The second intervention would include an AI-driven multi-domain digital lifestyle intervention study. Machine learning algorithms will be used to integrate neuroimaging, blood-biomarker and neurocognitive data sources to tailor content and intensity of lifestyle interventions for subjects with white matter disease. The longitudinal neuroimaging biomarker study and the proof-of-concept intervention studies would result in new knowledge into the pathomechanisms of vascular MCI and potentially pave the way for novel interventions for MCI.
kw: mild cognitive impairment; clinical intervention; white matter disease; biomarkers; blood brain barrier

title: Antenatal Myo-inositol supplementation in pre-existing diabetes to promote healthy neonatal outcomes (AMulet study)
abs: In Singapore, 2-3% of pregnancies are complicated by pre-existing diabetes mellitus (DM), and with current standard of care typically involving insulin and metformin treatment alongside dietary adjustments, 40% still experience adverse fetal/neonatal outcomes. Myo-inositol is a naturally-occurring insulin-sensitising carbohydrate shown to reduce gestational glycaemia and suppress glucose-driven increases in birthweight and neonatal adiposity in non-DM pregnancies. Arguably, DM cases which display more extreme hyperglycaemia and have a higher risk of neonatal complications stand to benefit more from myo-inositol intervention. We hypothesise that, as adjuvant treatment in DM pregnancies, myo-inositol supplementation will promote the normalisation of fetal growth and birthweight, and a reduction in neonatal complications by optimising maternal adaptation to pregnancy and moderating placental metabolic function to tailor transplacental nutrient supply and delivery of bioactive factors for fetal developmental needs. We aim to conduct a pilot randomised controlled trial that would test for the first time the impact of antenatal myo-inositol supplementation in type 2 DM pregnancies on the regulation of fetal size and risk of neonatal complications. We also seek to establish the underlying mechanisms by which antenatal myo-inositol supplementation may alter fetal/neonatal risk by investigating longitudinal changes in maternal and fetal myo-inositol bioavailability; in metabolic, hormonal, chemoadipocytokine, lipidomic, and microbiome parameters; and in placental metabolism and function. Data will be integrated and used to identify the key mechanistic pathways by which myo-inositol supplementation may alter fetal/neonatal risks in pregnancies complicated by T2DM. This study will pave the way for more definitive trials to confirm the efficacy of myo-inositol supplementation as adjuvant therapy in promoting healthy offspring outcomes in this expanding high-risk obstetric population, ultimately lowering the healthcare and societal burden of pregnancies complicated by DM.
kw: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, pregnancy, myo-inositol, supplementation, fetal growth, neonatal health

title: Dissecting the role of immune-endothelial interactions and portal hypertension in driving patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) advanced fibrosis to decompensated cirrhosis
abs: We have previously demonstrated that clinically, patients with MASH cirrhosis have a unique phenotype, with portal hypertension driving the end stage disease. The current understanding of drivers of portal hypertension in MASH is still not well understood. We hypothesize that parenchymal inflammation in MASH drives LSEC dysfunction through abnormal immune-endothelial cell interactions. This leads to obliteration of increasingly larger portal and hepatic venules in the “congestive escalator”, driving portal hypertension in MASH. Progressive portal hypertension then causes parenchymal extinction lesions, which aggregate to form fibrous septa and liver cirrhosis. This study will be targeting a specific population of patients across the spectrum of MASH from advanced fibrosis (F3 fibrosis) to decompensated cirrhosis: F3 fibrosis → compensated cirrhosis (F4) with no clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) → compensated cirrhosis (F4) with CSPH → decompensated cirrhosis. We aim to (i) quantify the degree of LSEC dysfunction and parenchymal extinction lesions in progressive disease across the spectrum from advanced fibrosis to decompensated liver cirrhosis; (ii) characterize the spatial architecture and microenvironment of disease associated cell states involved in immune-endothelial interactions to determine culprit targets involved in LSEC dysfunction; and (iii) validate the findings from (ii) in a novel patient specific portal blood derived in-vitro LSEC assay.
kw: metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD); fatty liver; non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH); portal hypertension; cirrhosis

title: Risk Factors for Structural and Functional Losses Associated with Myopia-Associated Optic Neuropathy
abs: Progressive visual loss in myopic eyes may arise from myopic optic neuropathy (MON). It is challenging to diagnose MON at present, because conventional tools for accurately assessing optic nerve problems have technical limitations in myopic eyes. Limitations in our ability to accurately assess MON using conventional approaches have led to a lack of clarity on the detection and prevention of progressive loss of vision due to MON. It is also presently unknown if the treatment of non-glaucomatous MON should differ from glaucoma MON, which is currently managed through intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering. Our overall hypothesis is that improved structural imaging, which accounts for detailed myopic ocular anatomy as well as connective tissue changes, will help identify features of myopic deformation that are predictive of damage to retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). We also hypothesize that IOP-lowering may be beneficial for both glaucoma and non-glaucomatous MON. We will test our hypothesis with the following Specific Aims: 1) To determine longitudinal associations between neural canal anatomy and neurovascular tissues at the optic nerve head and macula in high myopia. We hypothesize that myopic morphological changes of the optic nerve head are associated with progressive thinning of peripapillary and macular neurovascular layers. 2) To strengthen focal structure-function correlations in high myopia eyes through evaluations of optic nerve head morphology and retinal topography. We hypothesize that artificial intelligence-assisted compensation of ocular anatomy improves the focal structure-function relationship in high myopia eyes 3) To longitudinally evaluate associations between intraocular pressure and features of glaucoma or non-glaucoma myopic optic neuropathy. We hypothesize that lower IOP is associated with reduced structural and functional damage to the myopic optic nerve Findings from this study will help to guide better risk stratification for eyes with MON and determine the therapeutic benefit of IOP-lowering for MON.
kw: myopia, glaucoma, optic neuropathy, imaging

title: T cell receptor mediated immune therapy in chronic hepatitis B and hepatocellularcarcinoma
abs: The clinical success of therapies with T cells engineered with a Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) or a T Cell Receptor (TCR) is limited in solid cancers. Strategies aiming to improve clinical efficacy are mostly focused on methods that increase the persistence and expansion capacity of engineered CAR/TCR-T cells. By characterizing the immune response in patients with HBV-related HCC treated with mRNA-TCR-engineered T cells, we found that a complete or partial response to the treatment was associated with the triggering of an inflammatory reaction and not proportional to the quantity of TCR-T cells infused. We therefore hypothesized that the efficacy of mRNA TCR-T cell therapy against HBV-related HCC is more associated with their ability to alter the HCC microenvironment than to directly lyse tumor cells. Localized inflammation within the tumor could allow the induction of endogenous T cells specific for existing tumor antigens or specific for novel neoantigens synthesized by tumor cells in the presence of restricted availability of specific AA (i.e., Tryptophan depletion). We therefore propose to: a) Define the characteristics of the HCC microenvironment and the quantity and function of mRNA HBV-specific TCR-engineered T cells that are associated with inflammatory events triggered by TCR-T cell therapy. b) Define the specificity and functional features (tolerant or exhausted) of endogenous T cells activated/expanded by mRNA TCR-engineered T cell therapy. If our hypothesis is correct, multiple infusions of T cells transiently expressing their introduced TCR through mRNA electroporation may induce pronounced inflammatory changes in the tumor microenvironment that boost induction of endogenous tumors-specific T cells. The characterization of these endogenous T cell responses, and their requirements for expansion and function (anti-PD-1 or IL-2), will elucidate the mechanism of action of mRNA TCR-T cell therapy and help to design adjuvant therapies to increase clinical efficacy against solid cancers.
kw: Liver Tumour, T cell immunotherapy, Hepatitis B, Inflammation

title: Elucidating the pathogenic mechanism and evaluate management strategies of ‘Pachychoroid disease spectrum’
abs: Pachychoroid is a new entity that encompass several potentially blinding disorders. Common to these diseases is the observation of choroidal congestion leading to retinal damage. The mechanism leading pachychoroid remains unclear. The overall aim of this project is to elucidate the pathogenic mechanism and evaluate management strategies of ‘Pachychoroid disease spectrum’ (PDS) through a combination of clinical studies and animal models. Specific Aim 1 will determine the progression pattern and risk factors for choroidal venous overload in pachychoroid. Hypothesis: End stage congestive choroidal failure culminates from chronic choroidal overload, which in turn leads to choriocapillaris ischemia and retinal pigment epithelial damage. Combination of predisposing, aggravating and perpetuating factors according to a ‘multi-hit’ theory is responsible for the clinical manifestations at an individual level. Methodology: 1) We will conduct an international multi-center, prospective, longitudinal cohort to evaluate the progression pattern of choroidal venous alterations and the association between choroidal vascular alterations and the development of retinal complications. 2) We will develop an experimental model of choroidal venous congestion and observe the progression of choroidal venous alterations. We will perform longitudinal imaging studies in a non-human primate model undergoing scleral buckling procedure and also in humans who receive this procedure for retinal detachment. Specific Aim 2 will evaluate the efficacy and safety of anti-VEGF therapy with or without high-density subthreshold micropulse laser(HSML) in eyes with macular exudation secondary to pachychoroid neovasculopathy. Hypothesis: Combination therapy is superior to anti-VEGF monotherapy as HSML targets choroidal congestion in addition to controlling neovascular exudation. Methodology: We will conduct a randomized controlled trial comparing the anatomic and functional efficacy and safety of intravitreal Faricimab monotherapy versus HSML combined with Faricimab in pachychoroid neovasculopathy. Our proposal will be crucial in developing scientific knowledge in this novel entity and importantly, development of therapies targeting the root cause in PDS.
kw: Pacychoriod ;Age-related macular degeneration; Precision medicine; Clinical trials; Animal Models; Imaging

title: An Oral Prebiotic Protected Full-API Nanodrug (FAND) for Precise Manipulation of Gut Microbiota to Amplify Immune Responses in Colorectal Cancer
abs: Colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks as the third most common cancer globally and is the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths. Current clinical intervention methods mainly include surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. However, their antineoplastic efficacy is limited by late-stage diagnosis, chemotherapy resistance, and serious side effects. Immune checkpoint blockers (ICBs) have changed the landscape of cancer therapy. Currently, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and probiotics are the most direct and conventional strategies to modulate the gut microbiota for disease therapy, where the first FMT product, Rebyota®, has been approved for marketing by the FDA. Nevertheless, the complex mechanisms, lack of clinical management standards, and serious health risks of FMT, as well as the poor anticancer performance, potential microbial imbalance, and suboptimal shelf life of probiotics still lie ahead. Although nanotechnology offers a promising strategy for gut microbiota regulation, its practical translation is still impeded. In this proposal, we aim to construct an oral prebiotic (inulin) protected full-API nanodrug (FAND) based on the antimicrobial metal ion (Ag+) and endogenous immunometabolic reprogramming enzyme (adenosine deaminase, ADA) with a desirable active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) content of 100 wt% through a simple two-step self-assembly approach. Our specific aims can be summarized as follows: Specific Aim 1: Optimization and characterization of the oral prebiotic protected AAg@In FANDs, analysis of their formation mechanisms, and investigation of the relationship between structure and properties. Specific Aim 2: Study of the efficient and safe drug delivery of the oral AAg@In FANDs with cascade-responsive release in CRC therapy. Specific Aim 3: Investigation of the precise regulation of gut microbiota, the enhanced antitumor immune response, and the improved therapeutic efficacy of the AAg@In FANDs and their further synergistic effect with anti-PD-1 in CRC treatment.
kw: full-API nanodrug; gut microbiota regulation; colorectal cancer; immunotherapy

title: Understanding iron-Fe3+ and Pirin dependent colorectal carcinogenesis
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Lifestyle risk factors, such as the over-consumption of red meat and iron overload, are associated with increased risk of colorectal carcinogenesis (CRC), yet the mechanistic basis of how metal-mediated signaling leads to oncogenesis remains enigmatic. Heterocyclic amines, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and alkylating agents, such as N-nitroso-compounds, and diazoacetate, present in red meat are potential carcinogens and have been suggested to be the causative agents linking red meat to increased CRC risk5-7. Mutations leading to hereditary hemochromatosis, which causes abnormally high iron uptake, are also linked to significantly higher rates of CRCs9-12. However, all these studies have not answered if or how high iron levels from red meat drive CRC development.
