title: Hybrid Low-cost Operational System for Remote Monitoring of Waves and Currents in Coastal Waters
abs: This proposal develops a Hybrid Low-cost Operational System for Remote Monitoring (HLOSRM) of waves and currents in coastal waters, and carry out its proof of concept (POC) with six components that can complement each other: a) Remote sensing with X-band radar This will serve as an all-weather, low-maintenance, nearshore monitoring system for surface waves over 3.2-sec wave period and surface currents, with POC at a site near the National Sailing Centre. b) Remote sensing with multi-satellite and UAV-based imagery We shall develop a standalone software to aid the long-term remote-sensing for surface waves based on multi-satellite optical and synthetic aperture radar imagery (very low temporal frequency with coarse grids ~ 10m, downscaling shall be attempted to reach higher resolutions) together with sporadic Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imagery (fine grids ~ 0.1m). c) Remote-sensing with UAV-LIDAR UAV-LIDAR approach can serve as a long-term nearshore monitoring system for directional waves from 0.1-20 periods. We shall also develop machine learning models to correlate the UAV-LIDAR data with the raw X-band radar data to attempt the range-extension of the radar measurements towards lower wave periods (with accuracy to be determined). d) Ground truth measurements with buoys and ADCPs In-situ measurements in high accuracy using buoy-mounted waves and current measuring system shall be carried out. The comparison with the remote sensing measurements can establish the accuracy achieved by the hybrid system. e) Smart analysis using advanced machine learning Probabilistic machine learning algorithms will be applied on the integrated remote-sensing information to improve the accuracy based on the ground truth measurements, as well as to identify explainable AI signatures in the data which can be due to sensor noises, ship wakes, wind-generated waves, etc. f) Finally, an on-line HLOSRM framework shall be established to facilitate exchange, analysis and interpretation of long-term wave and current information.
kw: Remote sensing, coastal waters, machine learning, wave and current monitoring

title: Cerebrovascular Health, Adult Learning, Resilience and Mechanisms: CHARM Study
abs: Work from our group has demonstrated that 72% of adult community dwellers have measurable small vessel cerebrovascular disease (SVD) in the form of white matter hyperintensities (WMH), visualised on brain MRI. WMH has been demonstrated to impair cognitive abilities, specifically related to processing speed and executive function. WMH also reduced the ability to acquire and retain new knowledge and skill sets, and thus may adversely affect mature adult learners. In addition to SVD, amyloid-β protein also begins to accumulate in the brains of middle-aged adults, resulting in a cascade of neurodegeneration. The extent to which SVD and amyloid-β (SVD-amyloid) impacts learning would be influenced by the baseline cognitive reserve as well as the inherent cognitive resilience (CR) of the adult learner to the detrimental effects of SVD-amyloid In this proposal, we will study how SVD-amyloid affects cognitive reserve and CR of middle-aged adult learners. Using a combination of cutting-edge neuroimaging techniques such as diffusion tensor imaging and blood-based biomarkers such as proteomic studies and micro-RNA discovery, we will develop novel biomarkers to predict CR against SVD-amyloid. Biomarkers for CR against SVD-amyloid can be used to risk stratify adult learners having poor cerebrovascular health in terms of their learning abilities, and introduce optimal learning methods to these vulnerable individuals in a timely manner, so that they can acquire and retain new knowledge and skills. We will also develop learning pedagogy for middle aged adults based on the principles of neuropsychological pedagogy and life-style interventions. The course components will include lectures, group-activities and homework. The study team brings together collaborative expertise from Nanyang Technological Institute, National Institute of Education, School of Social Sciences as well as National Neuroscience Institute. The team comprises experts in SVD, neuroimaging techniques, blood biomarker development, neuroplasticity as well as experts in pedagogy development for adult-learners. This study would be one of the first in the world to study cognitive reserve, neurological vulnerabilities, develop biomarkers for CR against SVD-amyloid and to develop pedagogy for adult learners incorporating neuropsychological principles and lifestyle interventions.
kw: small vessel cerebrovascular disease; cognitive resilience; cognitive reserve; adult learners; educational pedagogy

title: Potential of Interface Care models to deliver more appropriate care to patients with acute medical illness in Singapore and decrease utilisation of acute care bed-days.
abs: Accelerated population ageing has shifted demographics worldwide. Older patients with chronic multi-morbidity are the new normal. Singapore’s healthcare system needs to rapidly pivot to meet these changes, or service delivery will be increasingly mismatched to patient needs. This results in: (i) high rates of emergency department (ED) attendance; (ii) increased acute hospitalisation; (iii) poor patient experience; and (iv) long lengths of hospital stay. To address these urgent healthcare challenges, innovative care models have developed to work across the boundaries of traditional care interfaces. Two important models for internal medicine include Acute Medical Units (AMU) and Comprehensivist-Extensivist Care (CEC). Although their application is becoming increasingly widespread, their benefits have not been comprehensively studied. Three research gaps exist: (i) understanding which subgroup of patients benefits most from these care models; (ii) understanding how combinations of care models may work together optimally; and (iii) incomplete evidence for clinical and cost-effectiveness. For a subgroup of patients with acute medical illnesses, I hypothesise that AMU and CEC models are associated with three advantages compared to admission to the general medical unit (GW): (i) decreased utilisation of acute care bed-days; (ii) decreased ED reattendance; and (iii) better patient-reported outcomes. I plan to meet this urgent need for a “real-world” prospective multicentre matched-controlled study to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of the AMU and CEC models of care in Singapore. However, there is a need for preliminary data and an understanding of potential logistic issues to justify a full-scale multicentre study. To prepare, I will first conduct a pilot prospective matched controlled study and cost-effectiveness analysis at National University Hospital (NUH), comparing the outcomes of patients admitted to AMU and/or CEC compared with admission to GW. To optimise the care models, I explore the normative needs of patients with acute medical illness using a prospective tool.
kw: Acute Medical Unit; Comprehensivist Care; Extensivist Care; Simple Segmentation Tool; Health Services Outcomes Research; Cost Effectiveness

title: Singapore Knee Osteoarthritis Cohort Study (SKETCH)
abs: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the largest and fasting growing causes of pain, loss of mobility and poor QOL in the elderly. Beyond the knee, patients are at higher risk for other chronic conditions through physical inactivity. Many patients receive suboptimal non-surgical treatment contributing to rising and unsustainable knee replacement numbers. Understanding the biopsychosocial model and how social determinants of health (SDOH) impact outcomes can guides stratified treatment algorithms. There exists a paucity of research on prognostic psychosocial factors particularly in an Asian context. Primary aim: Identify psychosocial factors that prognosticate short and long-term clinical outcomes, physical activity, productivity, and healthcare utilization in knee OA. Secondary aims: 1. Explore the mediation and directional relationship between the psychosocial factors with clinical outcomes to support conceptual framework development 2. Develop and validate an AI-powered biopsychosocial predictive algorithm to predict patient clinical outcome and guide treatment 3. Understand the true cost (direct and indirect/productivity) of knee OA in the community Building from preliminary studies, the SKETCH study proposal is a multi-center, cross-cluster, community-primary-tertiary, prospective cohort study. The inclusion criteria are community ambulant patients with knee OA and exclusion criteria includes severe medical comorbidities and previous knee replacement. Outcome measures include (1) Baseline Characteristics (sociodemographic, arthritis status) (2) Psychosocial Variables (guided by the preliminary qualitative study) (3) Clinical (Function, QOL, Physical Activity, Physical Performance, EMG, Satisfaction) and (4) Cost (Productivity, Healthcare Utilization) at baseline, 4, 12 and 24 months. Regression analysis, mediation and structural equation modelling will support the development of an AI-power biopsychosocial predictive algorithm. In line with Singapore’s national strategic thrust towards HealthierSG and OneRehab framework, AI-powered “Psychosocial Phenotyping” will support “Precision Health” by identifying high-risk subpopulations to promote physical activity via targeted interventions anchored in primary care and the community to maximize function and avoid/delay surgery to deliver “Value-based Care”.
kw: Knee Osteoarthritis, Community, Primary Care, Psychosocial, Productivity, Health Utilization, Prevention

title: 360-degrees Video Virtual Reality for Nursing Job Shadowing to Improve Perceptions of Nursing as a Career
abs: Background With a continued expansion of Singapore’s healthcare infrastructure, more nurses and healthcare staff are needed to support public healthcare and elder care settings. The Ministry of Health is working with healthcare educational institutions to boost recruitment of healthcare students. However, compared to other healthcare courses, nursing faces greater recruitment challenges due to limited exposure and misconceptions about the nursing profession. Aim The study aims to develop and evaluate a virtual nurse shadowing using 3600 videos virtual reality (VR) to improve perceptions of nursing as a career choice among pre-tertiary students, and to translate the evidence-based intervention into the nursing schools’ recruitment activities. Methods The study will take place in three phases: Phase 1 will involve design and development of a virtual nurse shadowing using 3600 videos VR. The feasibility of the virtual nurse shadowing will be pilot tested using mixed methods study on pre-tertiary students. Phase 2 will be conducted using randomized controlled study to examine the effectiveness of a virtual nurse shadowing by comparing with conventional nurse shadowing on pre-tertiary students’ perception of nursing and recruitment in nursing course. Phase 3 will apply implementation science method to translate an evidence-based virtual nurse shadowing into the nursing schools’ recruitment activities, and to evaluate the implementation outcomes using mixed methods study. Significance The virtual nurse shadowing using 3600 videos VR will expose pre-tertiary students to the diverse roles of nurses working in hospital, community and home settings. Through the exposures, students can gain a holistic understanding of the role of the nursing profession. With adequate knowledge of the job scopes and career prospects of nurses, we hope to attract more school leavers into the nursing profession. The proposed study has significant national and international implications as the nursing workforce shortage is a global problem complicated by a worldwide aging trend.
kw: Nursing Manpower; Perception of Nursing; Career Choice; Nursing Recruitment; Virtual Reality; 360-degree Video

title: How Do We Scale Up Hospital-at-Home Successfully? A Prospective, Multi-method, Multi-phase Investigation.
abs: To address increasing demands for hospital beds, hospital-at-home (HaH) programmes present a scalable alternative to inpatient hospitalisation. HaH programmes deploy multi-disciplinary teams to deliver hospital-level services at home, supported by remote monitoring and telecommunication technologies. Although randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses have shown HaH programmes to be clinically and cost-effective, many current research strategies are still focused on programme evaluation of small pilots. How to implement and scale up these programmes from pilot to mainstream is not well explored. In this proposal, our main question is: how do we scale up hospital-at-home successfully? To explore barriers and enablers to scaling, we will combine state-of-the-art implementation science frameworks with mixed methods approaches in a three-phase research programme. Phase I will include a prospective cohort study of the HaH programme at the National University Health System (NUHS) as it scales, examining implementation outcomes and identifying contextual influences. Phase II will examine three areas identified in our previous work to be a major influence on scaling – technology, workforce and operations. Phase IIA will combine interviews, surveys and observations to evaluate the use of technology enablers (remote and hybrid consultations, and remote patient monitoring). In Phase IIB, we will carry out focus groups and discrete choice experiments to assess the motivation and choice preferences of care providers to form a sizable HaH clinical workforce and patient pool. Phase IIC will use operational research methodology to evaluate how to efficiently transport staff and goods to facilitate HaH implementation at scale. Finally, Phase III will use interviews and policy labs to explore regulatory and policy considerations in moving HaH to mainstream healthcare. The results of this study will be used to inform HaH programmes on a national scale and will contribute to the international literature on evidence-based practices for scaling up HaH programmes.
kw: hospital-at-home; health services research; implementation science; scale-up; healthcare delivery

title: Improving the Mental Health of Patients with Comorbid Chronic Diseases: A Randomized Controlled Evaluation of the Feasibility and Preliminary Effectiveness of a Single-Session Solution-Focused Consultation (SSC) in a Primary Care Setting
abs: The purpose of the proposed study is to test whether a single-session solution-focused consultation (SSC) can enhance the health and mental health of patients with comorbid chronic physical diseases and mental health problems, and increase their engagement with mental health services. The study will use a two-arm randomized controlled design to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the SSC in community settings that serves individuals with chronic physical diseases (e.g., non-profit organizations, such as Renal Health Services). We will recruit 50 patients, aged between 21 and 64 years old, with comorbid physical diseases and mental health problems and randomly assign them into an intervention (SSC) or comparison (treatment as usual) group with the aim of evaluating the feasibility and acceptability of the SSC (Specific Aim 1), the preliminary effectiveness of the SSC on self-reported health and mental health symptoms 2-weeks post-intervention (Specific Aim 2), and the effects of the SSC on patients’ initial uptake and engagement in formal mental health services (Specific Aim 3). Consistent with prior open trial studies conducted in the United States, we expect that the SSC will show good feasibility and acceptability in polyclinic patients with physical diseases and mental health problems (Hypothesis 1). We also predict that patients in the intervention group will experience greater improvements in their reported health status, mood, and anxiety symptoms 2-weeks post-intervention (Hypothesis 2), and will be more likely to endorse interest in obtaining more information on available mental health services in Singapore; and willing to have another counselling session with the interventionist. On follow-up, those in the intervention group will also be more likely that the comparison group to have attended or made an appointment with a formal mental health service since their initial session with our research team interventionist; and agree to engage with the interventionist at their next scheduled session (Hypothesis 3). By enhancing mental health support in community settings using a brief, highly scalable evidence-based intervention, the proposed study will address a critical challenge to mental health in Singapore, and globally, by contributing to the improvement of access to – and uptake of – mental health services in a key group of complex patients.
kw: Chronic Diseases; Mental Health; Psychosocial Intervention; Brief Intervention; Treatment Engagement; Solution-focused

title: Improving weight loss in healthy adults with overweight and obesity: An artificial intelligence-assisted dietary prediction and prevention system with continuous glucose monitoring
abs: Aim: To test the effectiveness of a novel dietary lapse prediction and prevention self-regulation app -eating behaviour trigger-response inhibition program (eTRIP)-, and the addition of CGM (eTRIP + CGM), on healthy eating and weight loss in people with overweight and obesity. Hypothesize: There will be a significantly higher improvement in healthy eating and weight loss in participants receiving eTRIP + CGM than eTRIP alone and a free commercial calorie counting app called FatSecret successively. Methodology and Approach: A three-arm randomized controlled trial will be conducted with 201 participants randomly assigned to the intervention group 1 (eTRIP+ CGM), intervention group 2 (eTRIP) or control group (FatSecret app) in a 1:1:1 ratio. Eating behaviours will be observed through an artificial intelligence powered image-based food log. Weight loss will be evaluated using body weight, waist circumference and percentage body fat. Participants will also complete a set of questionnaires (55 questions) on their sociodemographic profile, eating phenotypes, eating behaviour, consideration of future consequences, eating habits, depression, anxiety and physical activity. Participants in all three groups are required to return for anthropometric measurements and to complete the same questionnaires on weeks 10 and 24. Comparisons of baseline data, sociodemographic and clinical data will be made using an independent t-test and chi-square test. Intention-to-treat principle and generalized estimating equations model will be used to evaluate outcomes between baseline, week 10 and week 24 with adjustment for potential confounding factors. Feasibility and importance: Promoting healthy eating and weight loss in adults with overweight and obesity would prevent the onset of cardiometabolic diseases, thereby alleviating healthcare burden. With a smartphone penetration of 90.7% in Singapore, the use of a weight loss app provides a more efficient mode of healthcare service delivery for health promotion and disease prevention through empowering users with the skills and knowledge in healthcare ownership.
kw: artificial intelligence, smartphone app, obesity, weight loss, healthy eating, technology

title: Modelling cost-effective lung cancer screening strategies
abs: Despite multiple advances in both the research and treatment of lung cancer, its 5-year survival rates remain low at 14.4% for men and 26.5% for women, due to its late-stage symptomatic presentation and often metastasised status. Here we will explore the use of low dose computerised tomography across a range of screening scenarios on a projected lung cancer burden to 2050 through an individual based model of Singapore’s resident population. The model architecture will explore smoking, the most important risk factor, at an individual and household level, ascertaining active and passive smoker lineages and recording lifetime exposure to smoking. Cancer cases will develop and transition between stages according to rates from literature, and the efficacy of different screening strategies in identifying early-stage and more easily treatable cases explored. Smoking prevalence scenarios will additionally be added to observe the impact of potential cessation campaigns on the future burden of lung cancer and need for differing and adaptive screening programs. The proposal seeks to improve the quality of life for lung cancer sufferers in a minimal risk, cost-effective and sustainable manner for the healthcare system by exposing individuals to the least amount of radiation possible via screening yet maximising the capture rate to identify as many early-stage cancer sufferers as possible under a set of ICER thresholds.
kw: Lung cancer; Screening; Individual Based Modelling; Cost-effectiveness

title: Trends and cost models of general anaesthesia in children due to dental reasons: using Artificial Intelligence-based interpretable clinical score (GA-AI triage) to reduce the intervention
abs: Dental caries is prevalent in preschool children in Singapore. General anaesthesia (GA) is one of the pharmacological behavior management guidance techniques commonly used in treatment dental caries in young children who are pre-cooperative and/or with extensive dental treatment needs. Although GA is of minimal risks in general, dental caries is largely preventable and unnecessary GA exposure due to dental reasons could have been avoided. This study examines the trend and associated direct costs of GA due to dental reasons in Singapore. In addition, retrospective data on various caries risks factors and disease rate will be used to generate an artificial intelligence (AI) risk assessment model to guide clinician and parents in their treatment decisions and prevention strategies.
kw: general anaesthesia, dental caries, risk assessment

title: Assessing the Impact of an Oral Health Programme on Pneumonia among Older People living in Nursing Homes: A Stepped Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial
abs: The aim of this stepped wedge cluster randomized trial is to assess the effectiveness of a ‘real world’ oral health programme on reducing the incidence, hospitalizations, and cost of pneumonia among older Singaporeans living in nursing homes. Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbid-mortality in Singapore impacting individuals and the whole society. Poor oral health plays an important role in the development of pneumonia, among other risk factors. Most common oral diseases and conditions, such as poor oral hygiene, are largely preventable, and expensive to treat and therefore, a preventive approach to tackle oral diseases is the most cost-effective strategy to avoid oral diseases and their consequences as pneumonia. This proposal will advance knowledge about the effectiveness of a feasible oral health programme to be scaled up across the country targeting the most vulnerable elderly population.
kw: older people; oral health; pneumonia; hospitalization; community trials

title: Developing an integrated photonic platform for scalable quantum information processing
abs: Scaling today’s photonic quantum systems to implement practical quantum computation and simulation is a critical challenge. It requires a complexity (thousands to millions of components) that is infeasible using bulk optics. Integrated photonics is likely the only route to accomplish this task. However, existing classical photonic integrated circuits do not offer the full range of functionalities required for quantum information processing. The most critical ones include quantum light sources and detectors, and they are often the bottleneck constricting the computational power of current photonic chips. There is thus a pressing need for a new platform that surpasses the current limitations and offers a fully integrated solution for scalable quantum information processing. In this proposal, we aim to develop an integrated quantum photonic platform that allows scalable quantum light generation, detection, and control. Specifically, we choose lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) as the backbone and combine it with superconducting detectors. LNOI is a nonlinear optical material ideally suited for quantum photonics, allowing efficient photon-pair generation and electro-optic modulation. Superconducting nanowire detectors currently hold the best performance for single-photon detection. Their combination thus provides a viable solution for a fully integrated quantum processor. In this program, we will first (1) develop scalable fabrication processes to integrate single-photon sources and detectors on the LNOI platform. Leveraging the platform, we will then apply advanced protocols to address practical issues in operating the sources and detectors, including (2) generation of on-demand single photons from probabilistic sources, and (3) scalable readout of large detector arrays by optical means. This challenging yet high-impact proposal builds on my strong expertise in integrated photonics, superconducting electronics, and nanofabrication. Our research will produce an integrated quantum photonic platform for scalable quantum information and deliver practical resources for quantum communication, networks, and sensing. Our complements Singapore’s quantum ecosystem and strengthens its competitiveness in the second quantum revolution. Moreover, devices developed under this proposal, such as high-speed modulators and ultra-sensitive detectors, will have direct classical applications such as telecommunication, long-range light detection and ranging, microwave photonics, and infrared spectroscopy and sensing.
kw: Integrated photonics; quantum photonics; single-photon detector; superconducting nanowire; lithium niobate; nanofabrication

title: Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme - Centre of Excellence
abs: Climate change is an existential threat of our times. It has brought rising sea level and extreme weather patterns. Singapore, as a low-lying island state, is particularly vulnerable. One-third of the island lies less than five metres above sea level and these areas are highly vulnerable to sea level rise and extreme weather events such as intense rainfall and storm surges. The challenges Singapore faces in relation to climate change are indeed unique. Besides land scarcity and competing land use, we have very limited natural resources such as water and materials. This is complicated by our extremely high population density. No other place in the world experiences a confluence of challenges at this scale, and these challenges will be amplified by evolving climate change. Planning, design and construction of mitigation measures requires foresight and longterm planning. Given the high uncertainties in predicting the long-term impact of climate change, it is essential to provide adequate and timely mitigation measures that allow for future flexibility and climate resilience. As such, risk-based and resilience-based approaches must be developed to achieve robust and environment-friendly solutions. The environment-friendly solutions include integrating nature-based solutions with engineering systems, reducing carbon emissions in construction, and reducing ecological impact. To conceptualise and develop effective and resilient solutions, significant knowledge gaps still remain in our understanding of coastal science and the modelling of future extremes, including storm surges, waves and currents. Assessments of complex coastal processes impacted or transformed by varying climate change scenarios are also lacking. Advanced computational capabilities are therefore needed to enable fast and reliable process-based simulations of mesoscale meteorology, near-shore hydrodynamics, and inland flooding. Other important components required for successful coastal defense include the development of sustainable materials and construction methods, smart systems for operation and emergency response, and integrated planning and decision tools. To address knowledge gaps, it is imperative for Singapore to invest in fundamental and applied research that provides the necessary foresight for climate resilience, enables innovative solutions tailored to the nationa's geographic attributes and ensures our infrastructure and people are protected well into the future.
kw: Coastal Protection, Flood Management, Flood Resilience

title: In-Situ Investigation of Soft Porous Materials for Gas Adsorption and Separation
abs: To ensure a sustainable future, adsorption and separation using porous materials, especially soft porous materials (SPMs) such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs), has been recognized as a promising alternative. Innovative adsorbent materials that exhibit a large loading capacity, high selectivity, and minimal heat of adsorption are critical to realizing energy-efficient separation of small gas molecules. Significantly, SPMs meet these requirements through their peculiar "gate-opening" or "breathing" behavior induced by guest adsorption, designable crystalline frameworks, and desirable adsorption properties. The gate-opening and breathing effects cause stepwise changes in the amount adsorbed at a specific pressure for selective molecules, engendering larger working capacities and higher selectivity than the rigid adsorbents. The unique behaviors of SPMs are not observed in rigid frameworks but are desired features for the rapid pressure vacuum swing adsorption (PVSA) process. This proposal targets the investigation of dynamic structural changes in SPMs upon CO2 and hydrocarbon adsorption via in-situ analytical techniques. Specially, we focus on the dynamic in-situ X-ray diffraction studies to unveil the host-guest interactions and the essential nature of the structural transformations of SPMs for gas adsorption. The obtained results can be used to develop next-generation adsorbents for highly efficient CO2 capture and hydrocarbon separations.
kw: Soft Porous Materials; Metal-Organic Frameworks; Covalent Organic Frameworks; In-situ X-ray Diffraction; Gas Adsorption and Separation; Pore Engineering

title: Rational Design of Plant Nanotechnology: Towards Climate-Resilient and Smart Agriculture
abs: Agricultural production must increase by 70-100% of its current level to meet the food demand of an increasing global population by 2050. However, a shortage of arable land, a shrinking amount of resources, and climate change present an evolving threat to our food security. These challenges are coupled with notable knowledge gaps in our understanding of how plants respond and adapt to stresses, hampering efforts in plant biotechnology and crop health monitoring. Nanotechnology-enabled strategies have recently emerged as promising solutions to facilitate better understanding and healthcare of plants. However, progress in this field has been limited due to understudied nanomaterial-plant interactions, unknown nanomaterials’ impact on plant health, and lack of proper nanoscale design to control nanoparticle delivery. The overarching goal of this proposal is therefore to develop a comprehensive framework to understand nanomaterial-plant interactions, and leverage this understanding to study the mechanisms plants use to sense and respond to their environment for crop improvement. We will discover design principles to develop active, targeted, and biocompatible nanomaterials for use in agriculture and plant science. The output of this proposal will inform a principled, systematic and more sustainable design of nano-enabled agriculture, with the goal of improving agricultural output while minimizing resource use and environmental implications. Specifically, the proposed research program aims to advance the nascent field of plant nanotechnology by: (1) Developing species-independent nanosensors to monitor plant metabolites non-destructively for (a) revealing physiological insights into plant stress responses and (b) enabling communication of plant health status with growers, (2) Establishment of design principles for targeted delivery of nanosensors and nanoparticles as carriers of genetic materials, biomolecules, and agrochemicals, and (3) Understanding the impact of nanoparticle surface chemistry on plants’ transcriptional response to inform rational design of biocompatible nanoparticles. My academic background and interdisciplinary research training, at the intersection of nanotechnology, chemical engineering and plant science, provide a strong foundation to carry out the proposed multifaceted program. The research proposed here aligns with Singapore’s 30-by-30 vision, where advancement in agricultural technology solutions to increase farm productivity has been identified as one of the three major thrusts. My long-term vision is that findings and capabilities developed in this program can be leveraged to address other pressing challenges in food security and sustainability, such as to empower plant genetic engineering development and to inspire plant-based materials discovery. Hence, I would expect the research output of this program to pioneer new opportunities in plant science, precision agriculture, materials research and environmental sustainabili
