title: Novel PEEK-based implant material development for surgical treatment of metastatic spine disease and osteoporosis
abs: Specific aims We intend to develop a novel polymer composite with optimal radiological, mechanical, and bioactive properties for operative management of metastatic spine disease(MSD) and osteoporotic spine. Our novel polymer composite comprises polyether-ether-ketone(PEEK) and hydroxyapatite(HA) with magnesium silicate(Mg2O4Si) additive. Hypotheses We hypothesize that our material confers superior bioactivity due to its increased surface roughness and ability of magnesium & silicate ion release. Additionally, we hypothesize that our material would be radiolucent when subjected to CT/MRI. Furthermore, we hypothesize that our material would have better mechanical characteristics and optimal Young's modulus than current polymer-based implants, reducing risk of biomechanically-induced implant/construct failure. Methodology & approach We will manufacture novel composite materials with varying compositions with/without plasticizers. These materials would then be evaluated by mechanical, biological and radiologic assessments to select optimal compositions. Based on evaluation results, selected optimal compositions would be used to manufacture spine implants, namely pedicle-screws and cages. These implants would then be evaluated via mechanical, radiological and biological assessments to determine suitability and performance of the materials as implants. Feasibility of the study Our team comprises experienced clinicians and engineers with specific skillsets catered to this project such as material development, precision engineering, additive manufacturing and implant development. Additionally, our team is able to leverage institutional resources to increase the feasibility of our project. Importance of our project to science/medicine Our project would lead to development of novel implants with optimal bioactivity, compatibility with CT & MRI, improved radiotherapy compatibility and optimal Young’s modulus leading to reduced chances of implant/construct failure. This would allow for better postoperative monitoring, reduced unplanned readmissions and improved quality of life for patients with MSD & osteoporosis. Additionally, for MSD patients, our implants would facilitate early detection of tumour recurrence and allow for better local tumour control, with safer & more accurate radiotherapy.
kw: Spine implants; PEEK-based material; metastatic spine tumour surgery; osteoporosis; novel implant material;  implant development

title: Investigating the critical roles of gelsolin in Wnt/β-catenin-driven cancer progression and dissemination
abs: The Wnt signalling pathway, which is essential in the regulation of developmental and cellular processes, has been shown to be a key driver in several disease including cancers. The deregulation of canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling is key in contributing to cancer progression through several mechanisms by promoting epithelial mesenchymal transition, as well as invasion and metastasis. However, the link between Wnt/β-catenin pathway and cytoskeletal components, which could facilitate cellular motility remains largely unknown. Existing research has shown that there is upregulation of nuclear β-catenin (indicative of activated Wnt signaling) at the invasive front of colorectal tumours. Coincidentally, our group has identified that gelsolin, an actin regulatory protein, is upregulated at the invasive front of primary colorectal tumours and liver metastasis and promotes increased cellular motility and invasiveness. Gelsolin, an actin-regulatory protein, possess multiple functions including cell migration, signaling and transcriptional activity, and can contribute to tumour progression. Thus, we hypothesize that there may be an interplay between gelsolin and the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and this in turn, enhances invasiveness and aggressive behavior of tumours. Our preliminary findings showed that the overexpression of gelsolin enhanced Wnt/β-catenin signalling and Wnt/β-catenin-induced migration and mesenchymal-like morphology and gene expression. In addition, the enhanced Wnt/β-catenin signalling could be attributed to the increase in nuclear β-catenin localization. Since gelsolin is an actin regulatory protein, we postulate that its actin severing activity may be important in the regulation of gelsolin on Wnt/β-catenin signalling to promote tumour invasiveness and progression. Our study would uncover the novel roles of gelsolin in the regulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling and identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for intervention that could be useful in clinical settings such as in the treatment of colorectal cancers highly dependent on the Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
kw: Wnt/β-catenin, gelsolin, cytoskeleton, cancer, metastasis

title: Developing ‘Software as a Medical Device’ (SaMD) from 3D vitreous-retinal-choroidal imaging modalities, to enhance the clinical management of uveitis.
abs: Detailed understanding of the complex ocular changes associated with uveitis is limited. Our study aims to document vitreoretinal-choroidal changes in patients with posterior uveitis (PU), using three imaging-based quantitative parameters of intraocular tissue structure – Choroidal Vascularity Index (CVI), Vitreous Haze Index (VHI), and Retinal Vascularity Index (RVI). Our study proposes the development of a widely applicable clinical software, harnessing machine learning (ML) technology in order to reduce ocular morbidity from suboptimal management. We hypothesize that – 1) ML models can be developed to predict changes in CVI, VHI and RVI in response to treatment. 2) There exist significant differences in the CVI, VHI and RVI between eyes with PU and healthy controls. 3) These differences are associated with disease activity, prognosis and are predictive of response to different modalities of treatment. This is a cross-sectional and longitudinal study. 150 PU patients will be recruited prospectively and followed up over 6 months and 6500 records of PU patients will be retrospectively reviewed. 60 patients with autoimmune disease will also undergo baseline intraocular imaging and a dataset of 10,000 healthy controls will be recruited from the health for life in Singapore (HELIOS) database. CVI, VHI and RVI will be calculated from Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images and fundus photographs by automated algorithms. A convolutional neural network will be built with inputs from patient data, CVI, VHI & RVI. Due to the limited training data set for the ML model, we will use the generative adversarial network (GAN) model approach to generate synthetic data and apply few-shot learning-based algorithms. Considering the ageing population locally, efforts focused on reducing visual impairment will substantially improve the quality of life and years of healthy living.
kw: Machine learning; Artificial Intelligence; Software as Medical Device; Predictive Modelling; Intraocular Inflammation; Infectious Diseases

title: A phase II study of metronomic capecitabine, oxaliplatin and UGT1A1 genotype-directed irinotecan in metastatic pancreatic cancer patients.
abs: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most aggressive cancer in humans with a poor 5-year survival rate of less than 8%. Several deregulated biological pathways coupled with limited means of early detection and inherent resistance to multiple chemotherapeutic agents often result in metastatic PDAC patients having dismal response and survival outcomes. FOLFIRINOX and combination of nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine are approved first-line regimens and have demonstrated superior survival advantages over gemcitabine monotherapy. However, tolerability to these approved agents vary widely and often becomes a major limiting factor in terms of tumour response rates and survival benefits in PDAC patients with advanced, metastatic disease and poor performance status. Several modified versions of FOLFIRINOX have been designed to succumb to these treatment issues albeit with minimal success. We recently completed a phase Ib trial of OXIRI which demonstrated good tolerability and response rates in PDAC patients with locally advanced or metastatic disease. Immunotherapeutics have not shown much promise in treatment of PDAC due to the highly complex landscape of the tumour microenvironment as well as poorly understood interactions between various immune checkpoints. Thus, the current treatment status of pancreatic cancer is inadequate and necessitates the need for more effective regimens that are also less toxic, particularly in patients with metastatic disease with poor performance status. The aim of this Phase II study is to assess the efficacy and overall response rate of a low dose OXIRI regimen [LD-OXIRI; oxaliplatin (O), capecitabine (X) and Irinotecan (IRI)], a gemcitabine-free regimen, in patients with metastatic PDAC. We hypothesize that LD-OXIRI, comprising of 2 of 3 weekly doses of metronomic oxaliplatin and UGT1A1-guided dosing of irinotecan in combination with metronomic capecitabine administered twice daily on a continuous basis, will be a tolerable regimen in metastatic PDAC patients and would exhibit satisfactory improvements in response rate.
kw: Pancreatic cancer; irinotecan; oxaliplatin; capecitabine; UGT1A1; pharmacokinetics

title: Influences of an Auto-Reactive Milieu on the Immune Responses to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) mRNA Vaccines
abs: Rheumatic diseases are chronic autoimmune, inflammatory disorders with complex immunopathogenesis. In patients with these conditions, anomalies in their immune architecture can poise them to respond atypically to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) mRNA vaccines. Additionally, with the observation that a more robust vaccine immune response occurs in the younger ages, there is a critical unmet need to determine how the interplay between the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and an auto-reactive immune architecture in children and young adults with rheumatic diseases can affect their underlying disease immunome and alter the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) specific immune rheostat. We aim to identify the qualitative and quantitative immune changes in children and young adults with clinically well-controlled rheumatic diseases in comparison with age-matched healthy controls after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination. Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis, an archetypical T cell-driven disease, and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, a B-cell driven systemic autoimmune disease, will be studied to determine the interplay between these two contrasting autoimmune milieus and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. We will characterise the immune responses of subjects with rheumatic diseases, age-matched healthy vaccinees and COVID-19 convalescent patients using humoral and T-cell based mechanistic and functional approaches. We have previously identified that a SARS-CoV-2 specific immune rheostat is essential for a harmless resolution of COVID-19 infection with a T effector response being balanced by an enrichment of a regulatory T cell subset and will be examining this in subjects with rheumatic diseases after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination. This project has the immediate clinical translational potential to determine the need for a booster and its timing to ensure continual protection by examining the SARS-CoV-2 specific humoral and cellular responses in children and young adults with rheumatic diseases.
kw: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines; immune rheostat; humoral and cellular responses; rheumatic diseases; children and young adults

title: Fabrication and in vivo evaluation of next generation, AI based bioactive devices for repair and regeneration of dental tissues
abs: Two suboptimal treatment methodologies have plagued dental surgeons for decades. The first one being root canal therapy which involves amputation of dental pulp followed by filling the pulp chamber with an inert material called Gutta Percha leading to loss of reparative ability of the tooth. The second being dental implants which are tailored to augment well with the bone but not with the soft tissue leading to bacterial adhesion and failed implant. Topography of a biomaterial surface dictates the behaviour of surrounding cells. It has also been observed that topography of the material surface acts in a way previously reserved for drugs and growth factors. Physical surface modification of existing biomaterial surfaces would therefore be more attractive than modifying the biomaterials with drugs or growth factors which requires extensive data on long term safety for FDA clearance. Identifying the right topography for a given medical application is a herculean task as nature does not prescribe an optimal topography for a given application. Using our Cellompic chip (Patent WO2021107879A1) technology we have invented topographically modified scaffolds for dental pulp regeneration and dental implant abutments. The overall goal of this proposal is to reproducibly fabricate and investigate these devices in suitable animal models for effective repair and regeneration of dental tissues. Finally, this proposal aims to productize these devices for Phase 1 clinical trials.
kw: Surface topography, Dental Pulp, Dental Implant, Regeneration

title: A comprehensive study of NOTCH2NLC-related neurological disorders
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: GC-containing repeat expansions in the NOTCH2NLC gene have been associated with neurological diseases, including neuronal intranuclear inclusion body disease (NIID), essential tremor (ET) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). Phenotypic manifestations of NOTCH2NLC GGC expansions are heterogenous, and the prevalence across neurological disorders is unknown. Repeat lengths of >60 to 500 units have been reported pathogenic, but the pathophysiological role and prevalence of “intermediate-length” GGC repeats ( >40 units) remains unknown. Furthermore, the influence of repeat composition and repeat interruptions on clinical expression requires further investigation. To address these gaps, we aim to comprehensively study NOTCH2NLC-related neurological disorders using a combined approach incorporating long-read sequencing, family studies and genotype-phenotype correlation with imaging and blood-based biomarkers. Using repeat-primed polymerase chain reaction, we will screen 600 “enriched” cases with neurological disorders and 2000 healthy controls for repeat expansions in NOTCH2NLC. Cases carrying longer repeats ( >40 GGC repeats) will undergo further long-read sequencing (LRS) to quantify repeat length and interrogate repeat composition. Suitable cases with longer/pathogenic expansions ( >40 units) will undergo detailed clinical phenotyping, family studies, and clinical follow-up with imaging and blood-based biomarkers. LRS performed on these cases will provide more accurate information on repeat composition (e.g., repeat interruptions) that may act as disease modifiers. First-degree relatives will also be screened for the presence of longer GGC repeats to provide important information on the stability of allele size in different generations. This will be the first comprehensive study investigating the prevalence and role of NOTCH2NLC repeat expansions in neurological disorders. Questions concerning the role of intermediate-length repeat expansions and the influence of repeat composition and repeat interruptions on clinical expression will be addressed in this timely study. Findings from this study will contribute to our understanding of the mechanistic properties underpinning NOTCH2NLC GGC expansions and contribute to improved genotype-phenotype correlation and resolving genetically unexplained cases.
kw: NOTCH2NLC, neurogenetics, neurological disorders, neurodegeneration

title: Testing the Role of Peripheral Scleral and Choroidal Remodelling in Low, High and Pathologic Myopia
abs: High myopia (HM), or extreme near-sightedness, can progress to pathologic myopia (PM), which is a leading cause of blindness worldwide. PM is due to progressive, lifelong and extreme eye elongation with subsequent eye wall (sclera) thinning, allowing for focal outpouchings (staphyloma), which arise concurrently with vision-threatening changes (e.g. myopic macular degeneration, MMD). Only a better understanding of the underlying tissue remodeling changes in PM will allow for preventive therapies. Both scleral and choroidal remodelling have been suggested to underlie staphyloma formation, chorioretinal damage in MMD and myopic choroidal neovascularization (mCNV). However, the underlying causal mechanism behind progression of HM to PM is unknown, and insight is lacking regarding the timing and location of remodelling that drives progression. Specifically, defocus/hyperopia in the mid-periphery has been suggested to drive myopia and lead to the prolate eye shape (and counteracting this defocus may be a potential preventive treatment). We now have novel imaging modalities: Fourier-domain mode-locked ultrawidefield optical coherence tomography (FDML UWFOCT that is able to acquire images wider, deeper and 17 times faster than existing clinical systems), ophthalmodynamometry (ODM) coupled with OCT to measure scleral rigidity and a polarization sensitive OCT (PSOCT) that have all been validated in humans in vivo, and have established a cohort of >1,500 HM and PM subjects seen by the PI over the course of his initial CSA-Inv grant from which to draw. We therefore hypothesize that eye shape changes (a macroscopic, late manifestation of scleral remodelling), scleral collagen anisotropy (a microscopic, early manifestation of scleral remodelling) and choroidal vascular remodelling in the mid-peripheral regions of HM eyes differ from that found in PM eyes, may drive progression of HM to PM, and progression of myopia in general, and may serve as an imaging biomarker for assessing risk, and direct timing of localized therapeutic and prophylactic treatments.
kw: choroid; myopia; pathologic; remodelling; sclera

title: Thermogel Enhanced Retinal Cell Therapy for Age-Related Retinal Degenerative Disease.
abs: Vision Impairment due to age-related macular degeneration and inherited retinal dystrophies is a major global health issue. Irreversible loss of vision occurs in advanced disease, due to the loss of retinal pigment epithelial and photoreceptor cells. With no current effective clinical treatment, regenerative cell-based therapy represents an intuitive restorative approach for vision recovery. However, several key challenges remain to be addressed, before retinal cell therapy can be adopted as clinical standard-of- care. This includes (i) Poor survival and functional integration of cells into the diseased host retinal micro-environment, (ii) Sub-optimal surgical techniques for retinal cell transplant, and (iii) Lack of suitable large animal disease models to assess pre-clinical efficacy. Our patented biodegradable thermogel platform have been shown to function both as a vitreous substitute and ocular drug delivery platform. We hypothesized that it can be used for the sustained delivery of neuro-protective growth factors to augment the outcome of retinal cell therapy. In this proposal we aim to develop an innovative, combinatorial cell and polymer-based neurotrophic factor delivery platform, for validation in non-human primate retinal disease models. Specifically, we aim to (i) investigate the use of neurotrophic factors such as Rod-derived Cone Viability Factor to promote cell survival using in-vitro iPSC retinal cells, (ii) investigate the use of thermogelling polymer as an intra-operative surgical adjunct for retinal cell transplant, and (iii) develop non-human primate (NHP) disease models for assessment of thermogelling polymer in-vivo. This proposal builds on the team’s established track record in biomaterials, in-vitro culture of iPSC derived retinal cells and cell transplantation into NHP disease models. This represents an unprecedented opportunity to harness the combined promise of advanced biomaterials, iPSC technology and robust pre-clinical validation – to advance the field of regenerative cell therapy, and help develop novel therapies for otherwise blinding and incurable retinal degenerative disease.
kw: Retinal Cell Therapy, Hydrogel, Age-related Retinal Degeneration

title: Tracking the evolution of malaria drug resistance in the Greater Mekong Subregion
abs: Here we proposed to study molecular mechanisms that renders the malaria parasites insensitive to the current front line chemotherapies; artemisinin combination therapies (ACTs). We wish to explore genome-wide gene expression patterns (transcriptomes) and genomes of the resistant parasites to characterize the malaria parasites, Plasmodium falciparum, cellular physiology that mediate/underlines resistance to the ACTs. First, we will carry out genome-/transcriptome-wide association studies (G/TWAS) and population expression quantitative trait loci eEQTLs with three large-scale epidemiological datasets covering the P. falciparum populations in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) from the time of emergence (2011) to its spread and establishment (2018). These results will be cross-referenced with in vitro studies using Adaptive Laboratory Evolution (ALE) approaches with freshly adapted P. falciparum parasites carrying relevant genetic backgrounds potentiating drug resistance phenotypes. The main goal of these studies will be to identify drug resistance transcriptional profiles (DRTPs) of P. falciparum that provide global insights onto the complete resistance mechanisms and at the same time identify transcriptional markers of drug resistance (TMDRs) that signal emergence and spread of drug resistance within the GMS and beyond.
kw: drug resistance; malaria; genetic epidemiology

title: Targeting NELF-KAT2B mediated transcriptional plasticity in breast cancer
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Cancer cells undergo transcriptional reprogramming to fuel tumour heterogeneity, promote metastasis, and resist therapeutic pressures. Given the limitations of targeting selected aberrations in a heterogenous genomic landscape, the plasticity of transcriptional regulation offers an attractive therapeutic opportunity. NELF (Negative elongation factor) performs critical functions in transcription regulation. Previously, we reported a role of NELF in regulating cell fate plasticity in embryonic stem cells (Hu et al., Nature Cell Biology 2020). Here, we uncovered another novel function of NELF in promoting pro-metastatic transcriptional reprogramming in breast cancer. Using breast cancer cell lines, xenograft and patient-derived models, we demonstrated that NELF ablation inhibits tumorigenesis and metastasis, particularly epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and stemness-associated genes. Through integrative -omics analyses, we identified the histone acetyltransferase, KAT2B, as a key target of NELF. KAT2B expression is enriched in breast cancer stem cells (CSCs), and KAT2B inactivation reduced EMT and stemness properties, similar to NELF ablation. Notably, high KAT2B expression associated with poorer relapse-free survival in breast cancer patients after chemotherapy, consistent with its metastatic/CSC-promoting function. In Aim 1, we will investigate the mechanism by which NELF promotes pro-metastatic transcriptional reprogramming via a possible partnership between NELF, BRG1 and H3.3 to establish a permissive chromatin landscape for cancer progression. In Aim 2, we will harness the state-of-the-art mass spec technology, qPLEX-RIME, to interrogate NELF interactome changes during EMT. Our preliminary results revealed a rich network of NELF interactors, including several novel partners. We will perform mechanistic and functional studies to investigate the oncogenic roles of these proteins in association with NELF. In Aim 3, we will elucidate the role of NELF-KAT2B in controlling breast cancer stemness and chemoresistance, using cell line and animal models. Since NELF-deficient and Kat2b adult knockout mice are viable, our preclinical work raises the exciting prospect of a targeted therapeutic with minimal toxicity.
kw: chromatin; stem cells; cancer; epigenetics

title: Molecular dissection of the role of IL11 in chronic kidney disease and analysis of a therapeutic IL11 antibody effects on renal regeneration and reversing kidney failure
abs: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is prevalent and, despite best medical management, remains a progressive condition. Ultimately, CKD leads to kidney failure requiring renal replacement therapy that is associated with a large healthcare cost in Singapore and around the world. In CKD, tubulointerstitial fibrosis, which occurs when tubular epithelial cell (TEC)-centered intrinsic renal regeneration fails, is a strong predictor of disease progression and poor clinical outcome. In recent years, I have developed a strong interest in interleukin 11 (IL11), which was recently shown to stimulate renal fibroblast activation. In preliminary studies that led to this grant application, I discovered that IL11, which is strongly upregulated in mice with diseased kidneys, drives partial epithelial to mesenchymal transition (pEMT) of TECs, preventing their proliferation. In addition, I found that both Il11ra-/- and Il11-/- mice are protected from pEMT, renal fibro-inflammation and kidney failure and that anti-IL11 therapy is more effective than anti-TGFꞵ in protecting mice against the consequences of severe acute kidney injury (AKI) . Informed by my preliminary data, I hypothesize that IL11 may play an extended role in multiple CKD pathologies, in particular driving TECs into a pEMT state and preventing kidney regeneration. If proven, this would change our understanding of IL11 in the kidney. In this grant, I will test my hypotheses in two Specific Aims: (1) Therapeutic targeting of IL11 signaling using anti-IL11 in a mouse model of acquired CKD and (2) Molecular dissection of IL11 in the pathobiology of AKI and CKD. Importantly, in Aim 1 I will study whether ageing or diabetes impacts the efficacy of anti-IL11 therapy for CKD. This proposed research is novel, innovative, and highly translational and it is hoped that these studies will identify a new, safe, and effective approach for reversing CKD, which is an unmet medical need.
kw: Interleukin-11, chronic kidney disease, fibrosis, acute kidney injury, kidney regeneration

title: Investigating the mechanistic interplay between CYP39A1 and LOXL1 variants in  exfoliation glaucoma pathogenesis
abs: Exfoliation syndrome (XFS) is the world’s most common cause of glaucoma, affecting ~80 million people worldwide. It manifests as abnormal exfoliative deposits in the eye, impeding drainage and triggering increased ocular pressure. This progresses to exfoliation glaucoma (XFG), which has an aggressive course. Despite its prevalence, how exfoliative deposition occurs remain unknown. We recently conducted a large-scale exome sequencing study involving 20,000 participants, and observed that loss-of-function (LoF) germline mutants of CYP39A1 confers a 2-fold risk of developing XFS. We also found CYP39A1 expression to be significantly downregulated in XFS tissue. As CYP39A1 activity regulates cholesterol efflux, we examined XFS tissue for alterations in cholesterol homeostasis, and discovered that exfoliative deposits were cholesterol-rich, suggesting that pathogenic activation of cholesterol efflux was an important feature of XFS. Intriguingly, a large proportion of asymptomatic carriers of CYP39A1 LoF mutants co-carried LOXL1 protective mutations, suggesting that LOXL1 mutations could protect against disease by modulating the effects of CYP39A1 LoF. This proposal aims to elucidate the mechanistic interplay between CYP39A1 and LOXL1 variants in XFS. We will first determine how LOXL1 variants influence CYP39A1 LoF- driven cholesterol efflux, and then characterize specific binding partners of LOXL1 variants to define the mechanism-of-action. Longitudinally, we will find key pathways affected by CYP39A1 LoF by profiling patient aqueous humor and studying them in ocular cell lines. We will then determine if the effects can be reversed by LOXL1 variants. Finally, we will characterize newly discovered variants of LOXL1 to ascertain if they protect against XFS. Our experiments will deepen the understanding of the roles of LOXL1 and CYP39A1 in XFS pathogenesis, enabling the development of novel therapeutic strategies for XFG/XFS. Data generated from characterizing of novel LOXL1 variants can also be used to stratify patients at risk for XFG, enabling early intervention and improving clinical outcomes.
kw: glaucoma; genetics

title: Dissecting and overcoming drug resistance in leukemia using functional and genomic approaches
abs: Most patients diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) die of the disease due to the development of resistance to existing chemotherapy or targeted therapy. This problem underscores the compelling need to understand relapse emergence mechanisms and identify effective targeted strategies to overcome leukemia relapse. Recently, by using dynamic BH3 profiling (DBP) that measures rapid change in drug-induced apoptotic signaling, we identified drugs that can overcome resistance to venetoclax, a selective BCL-2 inhibitor and active drug in leukemia (Bhatt et al. Cancer cell 2020). Through mechanistic studies using patient-derived xenograft models of venetoclax resistance and paired-wise samples from venetoclax and azacytidine clinical trials, it was revealed that venetoclax resistance emergence is (1) accompanied by reduced sensitivity of mitochondria to apoptotic signaling mechanisms, (2) altered expression and interaction between BCL-2 family proteins on a case by case basis, and (3) independent of recurrent mutations in common leukemia genes. By building upon these findings, we hypothesize that acquired resistance emerges through non-mutational drug resistance mechanisms underlying the survival of drug-tolerant “persister” cells due to altered tumor microenvironment. To address this, we propose utilizing Watermelon library — a lentiviral construct containing both an expressed barcode and an inducible histone-2B (H2B-mCherry) florescent dilution system to identify either pre-existing or drug-tolerant persister cell populations. In Aim 1, we will determine clonal evolution of resistance to clinically advanced leukemia targeted therapy in vivo using a high-complexity barcoding system and by measuring the proliferative index of resistance subclones. In Aim 2, we will determine whether mitochondrial apoptotic sensitivities (priming) and phenotypic heterogeneity contribute to the emergence of drug resistance. In Aim 3, we will finally determine whether relapsing clone carries chemical vulnerabilities observed in the pre-existing clone or if they acquire new pathway dependencies using dynamic BH3 profiling.
kw: Acquired resistance, leukemia therapy, acute myeloid leukemia, BCL-2 family, apoptosis, mitochondria, Single-cell RNA sequencing

title: RNA Therapeutics against RNA m6A Methyltransferases as Cancer Therapy: Case Study in Acute Myeloid Leukemia and Multiple Myeloma
abs: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and multiple myeloma (MM) are common forms of blood cancer. A major pathogenic cause of these diseases is dysregulation of gene expression. Post-transcriptional modifications to RNA are important regulators of gene expression. RNA m6A methyltransferases (METTL3, METTL5, METTL16, and ZCCHC4) have been linked to cancer, representing novel therapeutic targets. For example, METTL3 is highly expressed in AML/MM and is essential for their growth by promoting translation of oncogenes. Owing to the high structural similarity of their cofactor binding pockets, selective targeting of individual member by small molecules is highly challenging. RNA therapeutics, including antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) and small interfering RNA (siRNA), are an emerging drug modality acting on a genetic basis. Recent advancements in chemical modifications have led to clinical successes, with regulatory approvals for 10 drugs over the past five years. We have obtained preliminary results showing that METTL3/METTL5 expression can be effectively knocked down by ASO/siRNA, leading to inhibition of cancer cell growth, in cell culture and in a mouse xenograft model. Based on these promising data, we hypothesize that RNA therapeutics against RNA m6A methyltransferases can be an effective cancer treatment. With a team combining expertise in nucleic acids chemistry, extracellular vesicles, transcriptome profiling, and hematology, we propose to develop RNA therapeutics against RNA m6A methyltransferases for AML and MM. There are three areas of focus: (i) In vitro functional studies of RNA m6A methyltransferase knockdown and further screening/optimization of ASOs/siRNAs; (ii) development on targeted delivery of RNA therapeutics to AML and MM cells; (iii) in vivo study of RNA therapeutics against RNA m6A methyltransferases. Success of the project shall lead to the generation of proprietary RNA therapeutics for further pre-clinical development. Insights gained from the project will serve as a basis for future development of innovative precision medicines.
kw: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia (AML); Multiple Myeloma (MM); Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO); small interfering RNA (siRNA); Cancer Therapy; RNA m6A Methyltransferase

title: Involvement of G-proteins and F-actin in the cellular targeting of LRRK2 in Parkinson’s disease
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. PD is associated with dopaminergic neuronal loss and development of alpha-synuclein-containing Lewy body inclusions (particularly in the substantia nigra). Among several known genetic contributors to PD, pathogenic leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) mutations are most common, accounting for 20-40% of familial cases. This extremely large and conserved protein kinase has many unusual features, including the presence of a GTP binding domain that can regulates protein kinase activity. In spite of the significant efforts to unravel LRRK2 kinase function involving groups worldwide, we have a rudimentary understanding of the link between LRRK2 and cellular structures, particularly relating to mitochondrial dysfunction, a common theme among other PD causative mutations. The proposal has three specific aims which will investigate how a common mutant of LRRK2 [G2019S] is connected both to the actin network and mitochondria. These aims stem from our preliminary data showing that (full length) LRRK2 is strongly associated with F-actin in cells. This remarkable finding has been validated by two different techniques and have mapped the LRRK2 domains involved. We have also investigated the LRRK2 GTP binding domain which we show binds SmgGDS (a GDP dissociation factor). These preliminary observations rely on the careful use of the BioID technique, which uniquely provides a window on the cellular nano-environment around a test protein. We will (1) attempt to demonstrate the in-vivo and pathophysiological relevance of LRRK2-actin axis in mediating neurotoxicity of dopaminergic neurons. (2) Explore whether SmgGDS acts as a GTP-GDP exchange factor (GEF) for either LRRK2 or the mitochondrial G-protein Miro (or both). This would be a key contribution to understanding PD in the context of LRRK2 contributing to metabolic dysfunctions. The successful delivery of the above aims will provide information of immediate clinical relevance.
kw: Parkinson's disease; LRRK2; protein kinase; SmgGDS; neurodegeneration; Miro

title: Transnasal CNS delivery of MDM2 and MDMX dual inhibitor using the Minimally Invasive Nasal Depot (MIND) technique
abs: Background: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) is the commonest cause for brain tumor-related death in children. No effective cure exists to date and median survival is less than a year upon diagnosis. A major limitation in developing treatment options is the inability of most therapeutic drugs to cross the blood brain barrier. A novel Minimally Invasive Nasal Depot (MIND) technique has been developed to overcome this by placing drug depots in the submucosa of the olfactory cleft, to achieve transnasal-transcribriform drug delivery into the central nervous system. This project aims to evaluate the efficacy of injectible and drug-eluting implant formulations of a novel MDM2-MDMX antagonist (ATSP-7041), by delivering it using the MIND technique to murine models of DIPG. Aims: 1) To compare tumoricidal activity of ATSP-7041 injected by the MIND technique against the ICV infusion technique (positive controls) and gel-only MIND depots (negative controls). 2) To evaluate the tumoricidal activity of ATSP-7041 when delivered as a drug eluting implant with the modified MIND technique. Hypotheses: 1) I hypothesize that ATSP-7041 delivered by the MIND technique will lead to superior tumoricidal results compared to negative controls. 2) I hypothesize that DIPG mice receiving the ATSP-7041 implant will have superior tumor size reduction compared to negative controls. Methodology: DIPG murine models will be developed using orthotopic xenografting techniques and human DIPG cell lines. In the first experiment, DIPG mice will undergo the MIND technique and have ATSP-7041 (suspended either in gel or saline) given as depot injections. In the second experiment, an ATSP-7041 drug eluting implant will be fabricated and placed with a modified MIND technique in DIPG mice. Tumor progress in both experiments will be monitored by bioluminescent imaging as well as histopathological analysis upon sacrifice, and compared against appropriate controls. Safety and tolerability of interventions will also be monitored.
kw: transnasal delivery;blood-brain barrier;diffuse midline glioma;diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma;MDM2 antagonist;MDMX antagonist

title: Role of Pirin in the development and progression of colorectal cancer via regulating ferroptosis
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most prevalent cancer and the second leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide. Cetuximab is approved for the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) with wild type KRAS. However, patients with KRAS cannot benefit from cetuximab treatment. Red meat was classified as “probably carcinogenic” in humans. A body of evidence suggests that heme iron is the critical component of red meat, which promotes CRCs development and therapy resistance. However, the underlying mechanisms of heme iron mediates its effects on oncogenesis are not understood. What are the cellular sensors of heme iron? We find that compared with the adjacent normal tissues, levels of Pirin (PIR), an oxidative stress (OS) sensor and nuclear iron-binding protein, together with levels of iron Fe3+ are upregulated in CRCs, especially of the CMS3 subtype. Patients with high expression of PIR has the highest proportion in CMS3 with KRAS mutation. Knocking down PIR in CRC cells, led to dramatic increasing of genes which regulate ferroptosis. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent non-apoptotic cell death and RAS-selective lethal 3 (RSL3) could selectively trigger iron-dependent cell death of RAS mutant cancer cells. Therefore, inducing ferroptosis could be a useful strategy for the CRC patients with KRAS mutation. KRAS mutation and Reactive oxygen species (ROS) will induce nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) to PIR promoter to enhance the expression of PIR. Based on these results, we hypothesize that high levels of PIR may mediate ferroptosis resistance which contributes to development and resistance of KRAS mutant CRCs. By Identifying the roles of PIR in CRC and understanding the relationship between PIR and ferroptosis in KRAS mutation CRCs and establish PIR as a translational regulator of ferroptosis and a prognostic factor with therapeutic potential and clinical value.
kw: Colorectal cancer; KRAS mutation; Pirin;  Ferroptosis

title: Spatial and functional mapping of host-microbe interactions in human colorectal cancers
abs: Colorectal cancer (CRC) phenotypes and variations in immunotherapies are influenced by tumour microenvironments (TME), which are complex organizations of different host cell types. The TME is also colonized by diverse bacterial species collectively forming the tumour microbiome, but how these microbes relate to host cell organization and signalling is poorly understood. We hypothesize that spatially organized interactions between different host cells and microbes within CRC tissue promote oncogenic signalling and contribute to tumour pathology. Host-microbe interactions in CRC have been described in model systems but not in situ in the context of the intact human CRC TME. We propose new experimental and analytical approaches for simultaneous spatial mapping of the human transcriptome and microbial species in CRC, building on current capabilities in the Genome Institute of Singapore. This involves charting how cell types and/or expressed genes are physically distributed and organized within tissues using multiplexed RNA FISH (MERFISH), hence revealing host-microbial interactions. We will also validate these host-microbial functional relationships via in vitro organoid models with patient-derived cancer cells and microbial strains. Our work will lead to atlases detailing the host-microbial interactions that potentially contribute to CRC. In the longer term, this will be a powerful resource to build on, especially when this technology is further applied to longitudinal cohorts or in case-control studies of non-responders to chemo- or immunotherapies.
kw: Colorectal cancer; microbiome; spatial transcriptomics

title: Investigating the clinical roles of a novel transcriptional complex in multiple myeloma
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Recent studies reveal that novel transcription complex p52:ETS1 plays an important role in telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) reactivation in cancers which harbour mutant TERT promoter. However, it is not clear whether this novel transcription complex also regulate expression of other genes involved other processes in normal physiology. Also little is known in which type of cancers does p52 specifically binds to ETS1. We hypothesize that p52 and ETS1 exhibit critical implications in B cell compartment. This is based on our preliminary data that mutations in sites of p52 involved in binding to ETS1 promotes changes in B cell physiology. B cell dysfunctions are associated with onset and development of multiple myelomas. Therefore, we aim to discover the new targets of p52 and ETS1 in cancer cells lines. We also hypothesize that this newly discovered transcription complex might play an essential role in B cell biology and also in B cell malignancies. Thus, understanding in detail the transcriptional program driven by the interaction of p52 and ETS1 will allow us to discover specific genes involved in onset of MM. Based on the specificity of this complex in B cell malignancies, we will develop drugs to disrupt this interaction. Drug screening of small-molecule inhibitors targeting p52:ETS1 interaction will open up new avenues for developing the next generation of drugs to target B cell malignancies like MM where there are currently no precision drugs.
kw: multiple myeloma; drug screening;ETS1;non-canonical NFκB signalling

title: SIROLIMUS-COATED BALLOON VERSUS STENT GRAFT FOR THROMBOSED ARTERIOVENOUS GRAFT (SUSTAIN Trial)
abs: A functioning dialysis vascular access is critical to the delivery of lifesaving haemodialysis (HD). Arteriovenous graft (AVG) is a surgically created vascular access used for HD in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). AVG thrombosis due to underlying flow-limiting stenosis of the graft vein junction and outflow veins is a common complication. Thrombosed AVG can be treated with thrombolysis combined with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) with good immediate success rates. However, the mid-to-long term patency rates following PTA have been suboptimal. Greater understanding of the pathogenesis of venous neointimal hyperplasia in AVG has led to the development of novel interventions to retard the process. Stent grafts have been used in the treatment of graft vein junction stenosis, and its therapeutic efficacy has been demonstrated in several randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The reported access circuit primary patency (ACPP) rates of stent graft vs. PTA were 34.2% vs 21.8% at 6-month for thrombosed AVG. Therefore, international guideline has suggested the use of stent graft in preference to PTA alone to treat graft vein junction stenosis. Recently, drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty have been used in AVG, with favorable outcomes compared to PTA with plain balloon. PTA with the first generation paclitaxel DCB showed modest improvements in ACPP in AVGs. Sirolimus DCB is a second-generation alternative. In a small local pilot study, it has been demonstrated to result in a 6-month ACPP rate of 55% for thrombosed AVG. Compared to stent graft, sirolimus DCB is more affordable and will not impede future secondary vascular access creation, hence may be a better treatment modality for patients with thrombosed AVG. We propose a 2-parallel arm randomized non-inferiority trial to compare the efficacy of sirolimus DCB to stent graft in maintaining the ACPP of thrombosed AVG at 6-months.
kw: arteriovenous graft, drug-coated balloon, stent graft

title: Improving Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease and Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Using Deep Learning Analysis on Coronary Artery Calcium Imaging
abs: To combat the healthcare burden posed by cardiovascular disease (CVD), clinicians use prediction tools such as the Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk Score (ASCVD), Coronary Artery Disease Consortium (CAD2) or Computed Tomography (CT) coronary artery calcium (CAC) scores (CACS) to patients at risk of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) or CVD events. However, these tools have poor predictive ability and are labour- and time-intensive. Our overall aim is to to improve detection of subclinical obstructive CAD and improve CVD risk prediction. In Aim 1 we calibrate the ASCVD and CAD2 scores to a local cohort. In Aim 2 will develop and validate a DL algorithm using CT images (DL-CAC) for CVD and CAD risk prediction. In Aim 3 we will investigate complex CAC patterns/characteristics in relation to obstructive CAD CVD risk. We hypothesize that: 1) local calibration improves prediction of the ASCVD and CAD2 scores; 2) DL-CAC improves prediction of obstructive CAD and CVD risk across local and international cohorts; 3) AI-aided mapping of CAC patterns reveal novel insights to what CAC characteristics signal high risk. The primary outcome is myocardial infarction (MI). CT scans will be input into a convolutional neural network. Complex CAC characteristics will be identified and extracted. Each MI case or non-MI control is tied to his/her respective images data. The DL model will be trained to predict the right outcome. Associations of complex CAC characteristics will be assessed using AI and regression models. Comparisons of performance in CVD prediction among DL-CAC, CAD2, ASCVD and CACS will use area under the ROC curve (AUC) and Net Reclassification Improvement. Integrating Al and CAC information into clinical practice will provide a scalable, precise, efficient and cheaper risk prediction model to be translated to better health and economic outcomes.
kw: Artificial Intelligence; Risk Prognostication; Coronary Artery Disease; Coronary Artery Calcium; Cardiac CT; Deep Learning

title: RAPID-DKD: MicroRNAs and Axon Guidance Pathway Proteins association with Rapid Progression in Diabetic Kidney Disease
abs: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) in Singapore, straining healthcare services and expenditure. There are various phenotypes of DKD and the presence of albuminuria does not consistently predict worsening renal function. Among patients who develop DKD progression, onset and rates of renal function decline vary. Despite optimized lifestyle and existing pharmacological interventions, patients with DKD are still at risk of developing ESKD. Furthermore, current measures of monitoring disease progression (e.g. creatinine, estimated glomerular filtrate rate, eGFR, urine albumin-creatinine ratio) do not empower physicians adequately to predict rate of renal function loss, and time to ESKD. A recent discovery of 17 novel circulating microRNAs (miRNA) and six axon guidance pathway (AGP) proteins were found to be associated with increased 10-year risk of ESKD, in patients with early and late DKD (type 1 and 2 diabetes mellitus). We hypothesize that these 17 novel plasma miRNAs and six plasma AGP proteins are associated with eGFR decline in type 2 diabetes patients with late DKD. We aim to (i) validate the association of these plasma miRNAs and AGP proteins with eGFR decline; (ii) correlate these miRNAs with identified plasma proteins from proteomics analysis with eGFR decline; and (iii) identify more potential pathways/targets associated with rapid DKD progression. We aim to recruit 300 patients with stage G2-G4 chronic kidney disease secondary to DKD, who will be reviewed at baseline and followed prospectively for 3 years at approximately 6 monthly intervals. In addition to clinical assessments, blood samples will be collected at each visit for miRNA expression analysis to validate association with eGFR decline and rapid progression at 24 months. Correlation of these miRNAs with identified plasma proteins (through high resolution mass spectrometry and SomaScan Assay), including AGP proteins, with eGFR decline will be assessed.
kw: diabetic kidney disease; microRNA; biomarker; proteomics

title: Staphylococcus aureus Network Adaptive Platform trial (SNAP)
abs: Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest pathogen implicated in healthcare-associated infections in Singapore. Mortality from S. aureus bacteraemia (SAB) typically range between 15% and 20%, which can be caused by penicillin-susceptible, methicillin-susceptible or methicillin-resistant S. aureus (PSSA, MSSA or MRSA). Current management of SAB is variable with limited randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evidence. At the time of design, conventional RCTs make assumptions about plausible effect size, incidence of primary outcome, and sample size – holding these assumptions constant until trial completion. Therefore, serially testing treatment options via traditional RCTs is rigorous but inefficient and expensive. In contrast, adaptive platform trials incorporate multiple statistical and design features not reliant on pre-trial assumptions. Platform trials enable multiple questions to be evaluated simultaneously and sequentially, and evaluate interaction between different treatment options, to rapidly determine optimal treatment for a disease. The Infectious Disease Clinical Research Networks of Australia and Singapore have assembled a world-leading team to enrol 6,000 SAB patients into the S. aureus Network Adaptive Platform trial (SNAP) to answer multiple clinical management questions. In the initial design, we aim to determine the outcomes of benzylpenicillin versus (flu)cloxacillin for PSSA bacteraemia, cefazolin versus (flu)cloxacillin for MSSA bacteraemia, and vancomycin versus vancomycin plus cefazolin for MRSA bacteraemia, as well as efficacy of early stepdown to oral antibiotics for all disease subgroups. The trial will “adapt” to accumulating evidence in real time through frequent interim analysis. For example, as soon as a treatment option is concluded to be clinically superior to its comparator, the old comparator will be dropped and a new comparator may be added for further investigation. This process of “response adaptive randomisation” ensures trial patients constantly receive the best available treatment once they have been identified. We view SNAP as the vanguard of novel trial methodologies for infectious threats by antimicrobial-resistant pathogens.
kw: Staphylococcus aureus; adaptive platform trial; antibiotics; antimicrobial resistance; bacteraemia

title: Saline enema and treatment of meconium inspissation of prematurity. Impact on establishing enteral feeds, gut microbiome, inflammation, immunity and developing brain in ELBW (extremely low birth weight) infants
abs: Meconium obstruction of prematurity (MOP) has become a recognized cause of bowel dysfunction and intestinal obstruction in extremely low birth weight infants (ELBW< 1.0 kg) and possibly over growth of pathogenic bacteria in the gut. The primary aim is that Twice-daily high-volume Saline Enema (SE) is an effective and safe intervention to reduce the time to reach full enteral feeds in ELBW infants with MOP defined as infants with failed bowel opening for 48 hours+ clinical signs or symptoms of MOP/abnormal abdominal X ray/feed intolerance or those who subsequently develop MOP in the first 2 weeks of life, as compared to conventional management, initially with glycerine suppositories (GS), failure of it leads to contrast enema and laparotomy.The secondary aims are a) SE will be an effective treatment for MOP b) has protective effect on the gut microbiome and inflammatory and immune response in ELBW infants. 90 ELBW infants born over 3 years in KK Hospital (KKH), Singapore will be enrolled and randomized at 48 hours or later to receive SE or GS. A standardized accreditation and administration protocol will be used .The treatment group will receive SE at 48 to 72 hours of age or later and continued until infant reaches full feeds(110 ml/kg/day).Infants will be followed up to 36 weeks of gestation or discharge. The maternal and infant characteristics including the data pertaining to secondary aims will be collected.Data pertaining to gut microbiome,inflammatory and immune mediators will be collected. Study is a validatory trial aiming to confirm the finding of our pilot RCT. This protocol has the potential to become the standard of care in ELBW infants with MOP. Additionally, significant healthcare cost savings will be realized alongside an improved understanding of the gut microbiome, immune and inflammatory response pertaining to the gut.
kw: Saline enema; Glycerine suppository; ELBW; MOP; Prematurity;Meconium

title: Collaborative Model of Care between Orthopaedics and Allied Healthcare Professionals (CONNACT)
abs: With a rapidly aging population, osteoarthritis is expected to become the 4th leading cause of global disability by 2020. Established guidelines for knee osteoarthritis strongly advocate lifestyle changes such exercises and weight loss as first line treatment reserving surgery as the last resort. Our current model of care is doctor-centric and inefficient leading to suboptimal use of allied health intervention for effective lifestyle and behaviour changes resulting in unnecessary surgery. Redesigning the model of care by moving away from costly surgical treatment through the optimization and synergizing of proven non-surgical treatments is key to deliver value-based care. The study is designed using an effectiveness-implementation hybrid study design utilizing a mixed methods approach. The hybrid study has dual aims. The primary aim is to evaluate the clinical effectiveness (pain, function and quality of life) of a 12-week multidisciplinary (Orthopaedics, Physiotherapy, Dietetics, Psychology) personalized, community-based program for patients with knee osteoarthritis through a pragmatic randomized controlled trial. The secondary aim is to obtain data that will inform the context for implementation and guide future wider scale application. We hypothesize that this multidisciplinary program is clinically more effective in the treatment of knee osteoarthritis at 12 months compared to standard care. The primary outcome is the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS). Secondary outcomes include quality of life (QOL) scoring, functional and psychological assessments. An economic evaluation will be undertaken to evaluate both the short and long-term cost effectiveness. A qualitative component through interviews with patients, healthcare providers and stakeholders will evaluate the acceptability, feasibility and scalability of this program for further refinement and large-scale implementation.
kw: knee osteoarthritis

title: Buddhist Ecological Thought in Early Modern Southeast Asia
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: This interdisciplinary project will create the first digital archive and historical study of a neglected corpus of Pali ecological and cosmological writing composed in Thailand and Burma between 1100–1750 CE. Following Lynn White Jr. and others, historians and scholars of religion have debated whether our climate crisis originates, in part, from medieval Christian theological perspectives on the natural world. Academic environmentalists, such as Mary Evelyn Tucker, have subsequently looked to Asian traditions, particularly Buddhism, for a new metaphysics that is more compatible with our environmental concerns. However, these studies almost only focus on the Pali canon and other early Buddhist literature and ignore the later intellectual history of the Buddhist tradition. This project redresses the balance by digitising, editing, and studying fifteen Southeast Asian, Theravada Buddhist works that describe the loka (‘world’), the physical universe and the relationships between living beings within it. The project will collect these works, encode them as XML files, and host them on a digital repository. It will use natural language processing techniques (the Passim library) to analyse the circulation of quotations and textual passages both within the corpus and between it and earlier Pali Buddhist literature. Based on this analysis and through a historically-minded close reading of the texts, the project will explore the circulation of ecological thought in the corpus and the intellectual development of certain ecological and cosmological concepts. Moreover, the project will address the overarching question of whether this corpus changes our understanding of Theravada Buddhism’s compatibility with the ideals of modern environmentalism.
kw: Buddhism; Ecology; Cosmology; Pali; Theravada

title: Designing mobile-friendly cartograms for visualising geospatial data
abs: Cartograms are geographic maps in which areas (e.g. countries or provinces) are rescaled in proportion to a thematic mapping variable (e.g. population size or gross domestic product). Cartograms are called contiguous if neighbouring regions in geographic space remain neighbours on the cartogram. Unlike conventional bar or pie charts, contiguous cartograms can accurately represent spatial trends, resulting in insightful visualisations that can be the basis for further spatial statistical analysis. Cartograms have become a standard topic in cartography textbooks. In Singapore, cartograms are on the geography syllabus mandated by the Ministry of Education. The Singapore Department of Statistics can also benefit from innovative data visualisation with cartograms. Currently, cartograms are still a rarity compared to other types of thematic maps (e.g. proportional-symbol maps or dot-density maps). We argue that the main reasons for the infrequent use of cartograms are: • severe distortions of geographic space if the thematic mapping variable is heterogeneously distributed. • the lack of robust and easy-to-use software to create cartograms. • a dearth of established design principles for cartograms displayed on electronic (especially mobile) devices. Guidelines in the cartogram literature have so far mostly focused on the display on printed paper. Meanwhile, mobile devices have become a common medium for viewing maps and infographics. Digital displays create new, unexplored possibilities beyond the traditional constraints of pen and paper. Our proposed research eliminates these obstacles so that users can easily turn raw data into a cartogram that effectively communicates statistics to non-expert readers. We are going to: [1] adopt a new cartogram design in which the constraint of strict contiguity is relaxed so that geographic distortions are less severe. [2] improve an existing cartogram algorithm so that it can handle a broader variety of data. [3] conduct experiments to compare the effectiveness of different design choices for the electronic display of cartograms. Our proposed research specifically addresses the following scientific challenges. (1) Reduce cartogram distortions by relaxing contiguity: We will generalise our algorithm to relax the constraints of contiguity if it is hindering the readability of the cartogram. The sizes and positions of regions with small areas will be indicated by vertices in the contiguity graph. This change in the cartogram design reduces the overall distortion and effectively creates more space to interact with the cartogram on electronic devices. (2) Robust cartogram software: We will adopt the framework of the fast flow-based algorithm developed by us. The algorithm calculates a continuous map projection that guarantees that the projected geographic regions constitute a contiguous cartogram. The algorithm is provably correct if the geospatial input data are polygons with infinitely fine resolution. Real-world data

title: Rethinking AI: An algebraic framework for machine reasoning
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: This project proposes "algebraic machine reasoning", a new machine reasoning framework that is well-suited for solving fluid intelligence tasks. Our framework is fundamentally different from deep learning. In contrast to solving an optimization problem (e.g. minimizing a loss function or maximizing a reward function, which is a key paradigm in deep learning), what algebraic machine reasoning does is to solve a computational problem in algebra. We shall use methods from both commutative algebra and computational algebra, and leverage numerous algebraic algorithms that are already implemented in existing computer algebra systems. The fundamental algebraic objects of interest are the ideals of some suitably initialized quotient of a polynomial ring. As part of re-thinking AI approaches, and in response to criticisms by leading AI experts on the limitations of existing works in machine reasoning for tacking fluid intelligence reasoning tasks, we propose to define concepts algebraically as ideals. In this proposal, we will explain why such an algebraic formulation indeed captures our human intuitive understanding of "concepts", and more importantly, how machine reasoning is realized very concretely as algebraic computation. Crucially, the additional algebraic structure that ideals satisfy allows for much "richer" operations on concepts, beyond the usual set-theoretic operations, thereby allowing us to capture the "rich" expressiveness of human reasoning. As part of preliminary progress, we have successfully solved a well-known fluid intelligence reasoning task without needing any training data! This project builds upon our promising preliminary progress. Our project is divided into three closely related work packages. WP1: Foundational theory for algebraic machine reasoning. To understand what reasoning tasks can be solved by our algebraic framework, we first have to understand the possible reasoning subroutines that our framework can solve. Our main overall goal for WP1 is to develop a foundational theory on the expressiveness of algebraic machine reasoning: We shall characterize the types of reasoning tasks that our algebraic framework can solve, and explore the limitations of our framework. Concretely, we propose to (i) systematically examine the possible reasoning subroutines on concepts; (ii) introduce and study concept maps and concept transformations, which are analogous to morphisms in algebra; and (iii) analyze properties concerning the hierarchy of concepts. WP2: Inductive reasoning for fluid intelligence tasks. In inductive reasoning, the extraction of common patterns from multiple concepts is a core aspect of human fluid intelligence. In WP2, we propose to solve this "pattern extraction" problem via the computations of what is known in algebra as "primary decompositions". Informally, primary decompositions yield the factorization of a concept as an intersection of simpler concepts, which are called primary components of the factorization.
kw: Machine intelligence; machine reasoning; algebraic methods in AI; inductive reasoning; fluid intelligence

title: Prediction-to-Mitigation with Digital Twins of the Earth’s Weather
abs:
The increasing number and intensity of extreme weather events due to human-induced global warming (IPCC, 2021) is placing an immense pressure on societies worldwide. Recent examples are the heatwaves, and droughts that hit Southeast Asia, Australia, California, Italy and Greece, associated with raging wildfires, and the flooding that struck Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands, leading to loss of life, and billions in damages. Two natural questions arise from these and similar events: 
1.	how can extreme weather be more promptly, accurately, and effectively monitored and predicted? 
2.	what action can policy makers take to ensure societal impacts are substantially mitigated? 
To address the first question, we urgently need critical advances in retrospective reanalysis, extended-range and seasonal weather forecasting. The second question is more involved as it requires a significantly better understanding of the impact that mitigating measures have in preventing damages due to extreme weather events,

title: Embedded Non-volatile Memories Based on the Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistor
abs: In this proposed research, we aim to achieve NV-FeFET that can operate at sub-1.5 V supply voltage with 10 times improved cycling endurance (over state-of-the-art) at 10 year data retention time. We will use a materials-to-system architectures approach to address the scientific challenges in non-volatile ferroelectric field-effect transistor (NV-FeFET) technology. We argue that a vertically integrated approach is essential because vertical NV-FeFET technology is still in its nascent stages (which necessitates accurate feed-forward and feed-back across different levels of design abstraction), and because they are not simple drop-in replacements at the circuit and architectural levels (which calls for suitable design techniques that consider their unique characteristics). Therefore, as highlighted in Figure 1, our proposed research activities will investigate the design (Task 1) and experimental (Task 2) aspects of vertical NV-FeFET technology. For the experimental tasks, we plan to investigate and develop the NV-FeFET device materials and fabrication processes that can achieve characteristics that are desirable for future generations of non-volatile memories for HPC applications. We will also investigate approaches to fabricate vertical NV-FeFETs to achieve ultra-high integration density. Our experimental efforts will be complemented by the proposed research activities that explore the design aspects of mem-transistor technology from devices to architectural levels of design abstraction. To enable the proposed design space exploration, we intend to build a unique, hierarchical modeling and simulation framework for vertical NV-FeFET technology that can capture the relationships between (i) materials choice, (ii) device structure, parameters, and electronic behavior, and (iii) the design and architecture of memory circuits and systems implemented using vertical NV-FeFET technology. We will also calibrate our simulation framework, unique in its kind, against experimental measurements of NV-FeFET devices we will fabricate in this research and those that have been reported. Our calibrated simulation framework will then be used to correlate circuit and architectural behavior to device parameters, which will guide the experiments conducted to optimize the NV-FeFET characteristics. Note that our approach is similar to the Design Technology Co-Optimisation (DTCO) methodology that is widely adopted by the industry.
kw: Ferroelectric; Non-volatile electronic memory; Non-volatile ferroelectric devices; Micro- and Nano-electronics

title: Ultrafast Photochemical Dynamics of Liquid Water
abs: The interaction of high-energy radiation with aqueous solutions and cellular matter leads to the photoexcitation and photoionization of liquid water. The resultant transient radicals and the hydrated electron photoproducts initiate a cascade of reactions with other molecules, including biomolecules, to form the basis of radiation chemistry and radiation biology. For example, the strongly oxidizing radical products, the water radical cation (H2O•+) and the hydroxyl radical (OH•), are responsible for oxidative stress in biological systems and corrosion in nuclear reactors, whereas the hydrated electron (eaq–) can trigger genomic damage by dissociative electron attachment. Despite the important roles that they play in water radiolysis, however, the elementary steps in the ultrafast chemical reaction dynamics of these highly reactive species remain largely unknown. This is because the high-energy photons that are needed to access the electronically excited states (~7 – 10 eV) of liquid water by single-photon excitation lie beyond the standard repertoire of techniques in ultrafast spectroscopy. Further compounding this challenge is the ultrashort timescale on which these dynamics occur, thereby placing stringent requirements on the required time resolution of experiments; based on theoretical simulations, resolving some of the dynamics would require experiments with sub-10-fs time resolution. Here, we propose to investigate the sub-picosecond photochemical dynamics of liquid water by using ultrafast optical pump-probe spectroscopy. As a start, we will design and construct a new experimental apparatus that will be dedicated to the proposed studies. The apparatus comprises a vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) beamline that delivers ~0.1-microjoule, ~5-fs pulses, with photon energy tunable between ~7 – 10 eV. These VUV pulses will initiate the photochemical dynamics in a colliding liquid water jet target. The VUV-induced dynamics will be monitored by transient absorption spectroscopy, with probe pulses spanning the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to the short-wave infrared (SWIR), providing spectral coverage for the absorption resonances of various transient species of interest, such as H•, OH•, H3O•, H2O•+, eaq–, and electronically excited eaq–. Based on the absorption cross-sections of these species and the parameters for the VUV pump pulse, we expect differential absorption signals of ∆A ~ 10^–2 – 10^–3, suggesting that our proposed experimental approach is feasible. With this unique apparatus, we will first investigate the ultrafast photodissociation dynamics of liquid water in the first- and second electronically excited states, accessed by tuning the VUV pump to ~8.0 and ~9.6 eV, respectively. According to theoretical simulations and experiments, O–H dissociation occurs on the sub-10-fs timescale for water molecules in the gas phase but remain hitherto unresolved in liquid water. Our investigations will allow us to elucidate the effect of hydrogen bonding and solvent
