title: Dynamic control of radiative cooling in smart windows
abs: In the United States, in 2013, the nation’s total primary energy consumption was about 97 Quads (quadrillion Btu). The building Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning was accounted for 13.6 Quads and in particular windows associated energy consumption in buildings was estimated at about 3.95 Quads. An ideal smart window should have high solar modulation ability (ΔTsol) and switchable front side long-wave infrared emissivity (εFront) to cater to the dynamic energy saving demand for different seasons. However, in the current smart window design, consideration of εFront regulation is missing. In this project a tunable emissivity thermochromic (TET) smart window with switchable εFront will be investigated. Compared with conventional smart window regulating solar transmission solely and current radiative cooling materials with fixed emissivity, TET smart window panel opens a new venue for energy-saving buildings for dynamic climate conditions. Our preliminary results suggested the proposed TET windows outperformed the best reported conventional thermochromic smart window once the new performance index Δε was added. In this project, aided with optical and thermal simulations, the selective solar spectral regulations effects on energy saving will be studied systematically and the high self-regulating power of ΔεFront (0.7) and ΔTsol (30%) samples will be fabricated and upscaled. This project aims to give a new generation of smart window with both solar transmission and radiative cooling regulation via materials, achieving the most dynamic control and maximized energy saving for the countries with four seasons.
kw: Radiative Cooling Regulation, Smart Windows, Thermal Management, Building Energy Savings, Broadband Optical Modulation, Phase Change Materials

title: HeadsUp Computing: Towards the Next Interaction Paradigm
abs: Interaction paradigms have a significant influence on the way we work and live. Existing interaction paradigms impose significant physical constraints on their users, either limiting them to a sedentary position in an office environment (desktop computing), or transforming them into smartphone zombies (mobile computing). In this proposal, we aim to lay the foundation for a new Heads-Up interaction paradigm (Heads-Up Computing, or Heads-Up) that can effectively minimize the interference caused by interacting with devices during everyday movement and activities. Once realized, it can significantly change the way we work and live. Heads-Up Computing is made possible by combining a wearable platform that includes a head worn device and a hand worn device with a voice + gesture based multimodal interface. This proposal adopts a progressive approach to work towards this vision. As part of our deliverables, we will establish a fully functional working hardware and software prototype of the Heads-Up messaging application which uses a Heads-Up display, voice and gesture style of interaction to allow users to receive and respond to messages, from multiple stakeholders in various daily scenarios. Moreover, we will create a resource interaction model, a quantitative database where the human's information in-take rate for daily tasks (specified by Activities of Daily Living, or ADL) is measured and recorded; the data will be gathered through a series of field and controlled experiments. In addition, we will empirically evaluate and validate the Heads-Up messaging application system under the various daily activities and assess improvements from situational impairment. We will also create a set of guidelines for designing interface/interaction for various Heads-Up situations. Finally, we will demonstrate resource aware interactions in the Heads-Up messaging app based on the resource interaction model.
kw: HeadsUp Computing; Next Interaction Paradigm; Human Centred Design; Wearable Devices; Synergistic Interaction; Voice and Gesture based Multimodal Interface

title: Intercalated 2D Materials for Enhanced Thermoelectric Transport
abs: While the design of thermoelectric (TE) devices has been substantially improved with nanofabrication progresses, the ZT figure of merit of the core material is far from the thermodynamic limit defined by the Carnot efficiency. The challenge lies in identifying the key factors that affect the thermal and electronic transport in TE materials. The band structure of the material is a key descriptor to understand and modulate the TE properties. Promising TE materials should ideally exhibit a set of properties such as: high band degeneracy to enhance the density of states (DOS) at Fermi level (EF); covalent bonding ensures high carrier mobility by reducing phonon scattering and localization; large unit cell with heavy atoms and anharmonicity for low thermal conductivity while Rashba effect, topological states and strong spin-orbital coupling are desirable. In this proposal, we aim at implementing energy filtering and band engineering through intercalation in low dimensional materials. Layered confined nanostructures offer inherently many of the aforementioned properties. It is therefore a natural step forward to investigate their potential as high-performance TE materials. By introducing foreign species (atoms/ions) into the lattice, we will induce doping as well as scattering centres and strain. The conjunction of these effects will enhance the energy filtering of carriers on one hand and enhance the Rashba effect in selected materials due to the stress resulting in the band structure engineering on the other hand. Our initial target will be to achieve a ZT~2 at 500 K therefore overcoming SnSe. Our key technological objectives are to develop effective growth and fabrication techniques on various type of substrates for producing high-quality crystalline and polycrystalline 2D Bi2O2Se and analogues to achieve mm2 scale for device fabrication. Moreover, we will study the intercalation process and relate to the band structure and transport properties to determine the key factors for ZT optimization. This partnership gathers the scientific, technological, and engineering resources to achieve this goal and set a national platform for TE research. The outcome will be analysed in the framework of an industrial partnership to devise thermopile-based sensors.
kw: thermoelectric properties, Seebeck coefficient, figure of merit, 2D materials, Chemical vapour deposition

title: Advancing Wireless Research at Scale with Light-Weight Software Defined Radio
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: This project proposes a light-weight and flexible radio design based on commercial wireless devices, called SDR-Light that strikes the balance between flexibility, deployability, and programmability. It is driven by the technique of signal emulation in the PI’s pioneering works. In essence, the technique offers flexibility to commercial radios by emulating various signal waveforms, i.e., approximating arbitrary signals using low-cost commercial devices, which significantly lowers the barriers between specific wireless technologies and the universal SDR tools. In this proposal, the idea above is extended in flexibility, deployability, and programmability. In flexibility, instead of designing signal emulation solutions for each pair of wireless technologies as in the preliminary work, we will study more general models that support a family of wireless technologies that share common features in modulation. In deployability, we will provide APIs and libraries that can hide the complex details of underlying signal emulation and provide users with a unified access interface for heterogeneous platforms. In programmability, we will explore abstraction layers design that can make SDR-Light well interoperate with existing network protocols and stacks. To demonstrate the real-world applications of SDR-Light, we further explore the potential applications of SDR-Light to be the national wide IoT infrastructure through Lamppost as a Platform (LaaP). The flexibility provided by SDR-Light is extremely suitable for the IoT infrastructure. We will identify some cutting-edge research problems for LaaP to perform well in a heterogeneous, large-scale, and dense IoT environment.
kw: Signal Emulation, Wireless Networking, Software-defined Radio

title: Multiplex proteomic and transcriptomic analysis of host immune responses in exhaled breath condensate – a Proof-of-Concept study
abs: VAP is diagnosed in 5–40% of patients receiving mechanical ventilation and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. The diagnosis is based on findings of pulmonary infiltrates on a chest radiograph with at least one additional criterion of leukocytosis, fever, or purulent respiratory secretions. However, this often misclassifies a variety of non-infectious conditions, resulting in the misdiagnosis and overuse of broad-spectrum antibiotics in patients that do not have true VAP. The lack of precise data on the longitudinal immunological changes that occur after mechanical ventilation (MV), and their causal relationship with the onset of VAP, is one of the reasons why VAP remains a notoriously challenging diagnosis to this day. In this project, we first aim to characterize the longitudinal immunophenotype in patients who undergo mechanical ventilation (MV) using proteomic and transcriptomic multivariate systems analysis. Second, we aim to compare the immunophenotype in patients who develop VAP vs patients who do not develop VAP. To do this, we will recruit patients intubated for airway protection or for non-infectious causes of respiratory failure and collect endotracheal aspirate, peripheral blood +/- bronchoalveolar lavage fluid every 48-72 hours for up to 2 weeks post-MV. These will be sent for proteomic and transcriptomic analyses using the Olink Target 48 Cytokine assay and RNAseq, respectively. We will then perform multivariate analysis and use machine learning to identify unique host signatures that may aid in predicting the onset of VAP and differentiating VAP from other non-infectious lung conditions. The advancement of systematic bioinformatics approaches in combination with longitudinal sampling will provide a unique opportunity to comprehensively examine molecular-level changes in the immune system during the development of VAP. This may overcome the current limitations in VAP diagnosis and management.
kw: Pneumonia; Proteomics; Transcriptomics; Immunology

title: Connecting caregivers with community services: The Care buddy platform
abs: Informal family caregivers of persons with dementia (PWDs) have multi-dimensional needs. However, few receive support from community care services. We aim to develop, evaluate and implement a web-based integrated intervention (Care buddy) for these caregivers. We have already developed an initial prototype of this intervention. We will upscale this work by converting the existing prototype into a one-stop integrated intervention for caregivers of PWDs and by bringing caregivers into closer partnership with the wider ecosystem. The integrated intervention will consist of computerized adaptive testing to monitor needs of caregivers and PWDs and match them to Care buddy app/web resources, telemedicine and linkages with home care services, integrated client management portal for better coordination of care among multiple informal and professional caregivers, linkages with helpline and a chatbot, home-management of PWDs’ behavioural problems and physical symptoms, decisional support for advance care planning and for tube feeding vs comfort feeding, online synchronous/asynchronous (peer) social support for caregivers, self-care strategies for caregivers to recognize and address burnout and distress, and remote monitoring of wellbeing of PWDs. We will conduct a comprehensive needs assessment of informal and professional caregivers, develop the prototype and assess its usability (Aim 1). We will then assess feasibility, acceptability, and satisfaction with the intervention (Aim 2). Next, we will assess the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of the intervention through a multi-center 2-arm RCT (Aim 3). Lastly, we will scale up the intervention at multiple centers across Singapore, and assess any organizational and individual barriers to adoption (Aim 4). The intervention will address the spectrum of needs of caregivers of PWDs from diagnosis to bereavement, and will be a one-stop solution for caregivers of PWDs. The proposed intervention is expected to improve caregiver outcomes and reduce health care costs for PWDs.
kw: caregiver; artificial intelligence; dementia; community care; intergrated care;

title: Precision Medicine in Liver Cancer across an Asia-Pacific Network 2.0 (PLANet 2.0)
abs: Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) contributes the 4th highest cancer mortality globally and is highly lethal with a mortality-to-incidence ratio of 0.98, which is the highest for any solid tumour. The major barrier to better therapeutic outcomes is the absence of validated predictive and early diagnostic biomarkers. Our novel strategy of multi-region sampling of surgically resected HCC in Precision Medicine in Liver Cancer across an Asia-Pacific Network (PLANet 1.0) confirmed the highly heterogeneous landscape of HCC at the molecular level and unraveled unprecedented insights including an onco-fetal re-programing phenomenon in HCC related to immune evasion pathway. Study Design: PLANet 2.0 serves as a natural development in progressive scientific enquiries, where we leverage on 2 investigator-initiated clinical studies in early and intermediate/advanced HCC respectively with best-in-class therapeutics Atezo+Bev and SIRT; as well as a high-risk surveillance cohort. This allows longitudinal bio-sample collection and the opportunity to elucidate and validate diagnostic/predictive biomarkers with correlates to clinical outcomes. Specific Hypotheses: That (1) the reconstruction of the tri-dimensional, spatially-resolved landscape of the highly heterogenous tumour microenvironment (TME) of HCC will reveal co-localization of biomarkers that drive underlying mechanisms of tumour development and response to therapy and that (2) these mechanisms offer novel, actionable biomarkers/targets in HCC. Methodology: We will utilize multi-regional sampling and multi-omics investigations (Theme 1) to uncover and validate molecular, cellular and immunological cues underpinning HCC development, recurrence, response and resistance, with a focus on three-dimensional spatially-resolved transcriptomics in the TME (Theme 2) and immune-suppression mechanisms in the tumour immune microenvironment (Theme 3). Theme 4 will conduct proof-of-concept mechanistic investigations to validate biomarkers. Theme 5 will create an organised data structure and architecture for the program and an integrated data platform to facilitate the derivation of machine-learning based models. Conclusions: Our integrated, multi-omics approach correlated with clinical outcomes provides an unparalleled opportunity for discover and validation of HCC biomarkers that directly impact clinical practice.
kw: Hepatocellular carcinoma, Precision medicine, Onco-fetal reprogramming, Predictive biomarkers, Immunotherapy, Novel targets

title: Project Carer Matters 2
abs: Background: Project Carer Matters (PCM)2 leverages on technological enablers to deliver integrated, personalised and cost-effective care to patients aged ≥65 and their caregivers. Aims: To develop, implement, and evaluate a care model that (1) supports self-management of needs and stressors, (2) creates a safe home environment for ageing-in-place, and (3)forges deeper connections between the patient-caregiver dyad and the community. Hypotheses: PCM2 will reduce hospitalisations, emergency department visits, nursing home applications, and caregiving hours by 25%. Caregivers will experience reduced caregiving stress, sense of isolation, and increased quality of life by 25%. Methodology: PCM2 utilizes an AI-driven mobile application that comprises a one-stop library to provide personalised educational resources based on users’ needs; health chatbot for care triage; social platform for caregivers to seek assistance; and virtual reality to increase caregivers’ empathy. PCM2 also comprises an automated sensor-enabled fall detection and rescue system, and telehealth for home-based chronic disease monitoring. Research approach: A Delphi technique will be used to seek expert validation of our solutions. We will pilot our solutions using a convergent, mixed-methods approach to test the feasibility and acceptability of our solutions before our implementation. We will use a Hybrid Type II-Effectiveness Implementation framework to test the effectiveness of PCM2 and our implementation strategy amongst eligible patients and caregivers, following them up for 6 months after index discharge. Feasibility: PCM2 is compatible with the needs and wishes of patients and caregivers—to be empowered to care for themselves at home. Aligned with the hospital’s strategic vision to deliver care anytime and anywhere, PCM2 will be integrated with existing hospital and cluster-wide digital infrastructure to ensure sustainability and scalability. Importance to science: PCM2 is an innovative model that leverages on technology and stakeholders at across ecosystems, drawing stakeholders in to support caregivers, to address the multi-factorial needs of patients-caregivers.
kw: Caregivers; Elderly; Caregiver burden; Digital health; Activation; Predictive analytics

title: PEACE - Preparation for End-Of-Life with Advance Care Education
abs: Importance: Caregivers, acting as proxy decision makers find it difficult to follow patient's wishes for advance care planning. It is unknown whether easy-to-use, caregiver facing advance care planning (ACP) interventions can overcome barriers to planning in busy care settings. Objective: To compare the efficacy of an interactive, caregiver-centered ACP website (PEACE) with an easy-to-read advance care plan website (ACP) to increase planning values discussions and documentation. Design, setting, and participants: We propose a comparative effectiveness randomized clinical trial conducted at multiple wards within NUHS cluster. Inclusion criteria for patients will be those warded for a serious, life-limiting illness. The inclusion criteria for caregivers are people identified by the clinical team or patient as primary caregiver for the patient. Interventions: Participants will be randomized to review PEACE plus an easy-to-read ACP or the ACP alone. There will be no clinician and/or system-level interventions or education. Research staff will be blinded for all follow-up measurements. Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome will be new ACP documentation (ie, legal forms and/or discussions) at 9 months. Secondary outcomes include patient-reported ACP engagement at 3 months, 6 months and 12 months using validated surveys of behavior change process measures (ie, 5-point knowledge, self-efficacy, readiness scales) and action measures (eg, surrogate designation, using a 0-25 scale). We will analyse for intention-to-treat, mixed-effects logistic and linear regression, controlling for time, health literacy, race/ethnicity, baseline ACP, and clustering by physician.
kw: advance care planning, health services, digital health, caregivers, shared decision making

title: PhishShoal: An AI-based Anti-Phishing Platform for Monitoring and Analysing Runtime Phishing Campaigns
abs: Phishing attack is a cybercrime where attackers (or phisher) create a fake website to imitate a legitimate website (e.g., PayPal, Amazon, Bank of Neverland, etc.), stealing credential information. Existing phishing solutions are usually passive, i.e., they alarm phishing when a phishing URL comes. Moreover, they alarms without any explanation. In this project, we propose an anti-phishing platform, PhishShoal, for providing an explainable phishing detection system and a continuous phishing threats monitoring for the whole Internet. Based on detected phishing webpages, we learn and built models to (1) provide dynamic and static analysis on existing website, reporting whether a website has been compromised, and (2) report whether a website has the potential to be compromised, and the best defending solution to existing enterprises.
kw: phishing, runtime monitoring, threat intelligence, AI, explanation

title: Advanced Porous Materials and Membranes for Liquid-Phase Hydrocarbon Separations
abs: Purification of hydrocarbon isomers – molecules which possess nearly identical chemical and physical properties and differ only in the spatial arrangements of their constituent atoms – is one of the world’s most challenging and energy-intensive separations. In this project, we propose to design novel advanced porous materials (encompassing metal-organic frameworks and covalent organic frameworks) as alternative sorbents for xylene fractionation and gasoline upgrading. Unlike prevailing sorbents, the flexibility of advanced porous materials provides a potential mechanism to adjust porous nanospace at the sub-angstrom level, which may garner benchmark selectivities for these demanding isomeric separations. In this project, we will use a hybrid strategy integrating experiment, computational study and state-of-the-art in-situ characterization techniques to identify and generate prototype sorbents with dynamic (flexible) structures. We will use multiscale modelling from the molecular to macroscopic level to develop suitable sorbents and membranes. The resultant materials may be deployed as drop-in replacements within the incumbent simulated moving bed separation process or serve as foundation for more energy- and space-efficient processes. To complete the development loop, we will fabricate scaled-up columns and membranes, which may be further evaluated by interested industry partners.
kw: Separation Engineering; Porous Materials; Adsorption Separation; Membrane Separation; Xylene Fractionation; Gasoline Upgrading

title: Advanced Infrared Optoelectronics and Applications with Emerging Quantum Materials
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: The low exciton binding energy and requirement for lattice matching in traditional compound semiconductors have restricted the operation temperature and working wavelength of infrared (IR) optoelectronics. So far the established mid-IR photodetectors based on narrow-gap semiconductors can only operate at short mid-IR wavelength with cryogenic cooling. Quantum cascade lasers and photodetectors could be engineered to selected wavelengths in the mid-far-IR (MFIR) range but are very expensive due to the stringent crystal growth requirement. The emergence of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) provides a promising platform and has shown near- to mid-IR photodetection and visible to near-IR lasing at room temperature. The strong quantum confinement, large intra- and inter-layer exciton binding energy, ease in forming heterostructures and flexibility in choice of 2D semiconductors and semimetals, together with exciton energy tuning will facilitate the realization of room-temperature-operated optoelectronics at MFIR range. On the other hand, plasmonic or dielectric based metaoptics has demonstrated a strong capability for light manipulation at nanoscale and has shown not only functionalities of traditional optics but also unprecedented properties such as polarization sensitivity, electrostatic tunability, and gigantic non-linear and spin-Hall effect. In this proposal, we will explore the rich quantum phenomena in 2D TMDC based semiconductors and topological semimetals, in combination with metaoptics, to overcome the bottlenecks of the lack of lasers and photodetectors in the important MFIR range. The proposed work will provide new insights into excitons and polaritons and their interactions at very low energy levels at the interface of metaoptics , and new methodologies for MFIR light generation and detection. The plethora of potential applications enabled by low cost, compact, room-temperature-operable mid-far-IR photodetectors and lasers will impact the semiconductor, aerospace, and medtech industries as well as providing solutions for pollution monitoring, combating coronavirus and in national security and defence.
kw: 2D optoelectronics; IR photodetector; IR laser; metaoptics; 2D materials;  TMDCs.

title: Targeting the developmental origins of liver disease and its progression to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
abs: Background: Our recent work on generating a single cell atlas of human hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) identified an unexpected “oncofetal” reprogramming of the HCC-tumor microenvironment (TME) into an immuno-tolerant ecosystem that promotes growth and survival of cancer cells (Cell 2020). Importantly, we also identified the emergence of similar fetal-like signatures in cirrhotic liver samples and in a mouse model of partial hepatectomy. Hypothesis: Growth-promoting, immune-tolerant oncofetal microenvironment is established earlier via the reactivation of developmental programs during inflammatory liver disease, which drives the creation of a tumor-permissive niche that supports growth and survival of malignant cells. Methodology and approach: We will utilize multimodal single cell -omic approaches to simultaneously capture the transcriptome and epigenome at single cell resolution (scRNA/ATAC-seq) of “functional” disease-associated cell-states (DACs) during longitudinal disease progression in the human liver to HCC. We will perform high dimensional chromatin architecture analysis to mechanistically probe the function of the 3D genome, and investigate the role of altered RNA editing in specification of DACs. We will employ mouse models of NASH/NAFLD/cirrhosis and HCC to validate the function of candidate genes, pathways and regulatory interactions in driving the progression of early liver disease to cancer. Specific Aims: 1) Comprehensively characterize the transcriptome and regulome of normal versus disease associated cell states (DACs) during liver disease progression (normal -> NASH/NAFLD -> cirrhosis -> HCC) at single cell resolution; 2) Characterize and validate the spatial architecture of disease/HCC-associated cell states, vis-à-vis the microenvironment; 3) Determine the evolution of the epigenome and the epi-transcriptome by assessing alterations in 3D genome architecture and RNA editing during liver disease progression; 4) Functionally validate novel biomarkers and putative drivers of disease progression. Successful completion of this research will lead to the identification of novel prognostic biomarkers and microenvironment-associated therapeutic targets aimed at prevention, and treatment of HCC.
kw: cancer prevention, liver disease evolution, fibrosis, cirrhosis, steato-hepatitis, developmental origin, HCC, single cell genomics

title: Reinvigorating Natural Killer cells in the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (RINK-TME)
abs: Natural Killer (NK) cells kill tumor cells without prior sensitization and modulate anti-tumor functions of other immune cells. Compared to T-cell, NK cell-based immunotherapy manifests several advantages such as more favourable safety profiles and readiness to be prepared as off-the-shelf therapeutics to treat patients without inducing severe side effects and graft-versus-host disease. However, the efficacy of NK cell immunotherapy is far from satisfactory for the treatment of human solid tumors due to the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that dampens their responses. Here, we propose to investigate how NK cell activation is suppressed by the TME in solid tumors derived from treatment-naïve patients through an unbiased characterization of NK cells and their interactions with TME using state-of-the-art immune-profiling technologies. We aim to define immune signatures of NK cells in solid tumors and identify pathways and molecules attributed to their dysfunction. We will also explore the potential of newly uncovered targets in reinvigorating NK cell functions. The specific aims of our research program are: 1. To characterize NK cell subsets, their activation and dysregulation in human solid tumors focusing on treatment-naïve samples 2. To define and validate immune signature and pathways associated with NK cell dysfunction in human solid tumors and correlate them with clinical data 3. To identify intervention pathways and explore their potential in reinvigorating NK cell activation in preclinical models This proposal involves a multidisciplinary team of scientists, clinicians, bioinformaticians and bioengineers to uncover novel insights into NK cell -TME interaction and to exploit newly acquired knowledge to identify novel and important pathways and molecules and explore their potential in reinvigorating NK cell anti-tumor function. This proposed research will place Singapore in a strategic position in the immunotherapeutics market with clear economic and health benefits leading to better treatment for patients.
kw: Natural killer cell; tumor micro-environment; immunosuppressive; cancer immunotherapy

title: Identification of structural and functional roles of RNA in TNFR signaling: key for designing next generation drugs for cancers and immune disorders.
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is an important regulator of inflammation in development and physiology. Abnormal TNF signaling is a major risk factor for many human ailments ranging from rheumatoid arthritis (RA), metabolic syndrome (MS) to cancers, where inflammation is an underlying cause. Currently, the annual global cost of cancer care alone is upwards of $5 trillion. Cancers and MS are also the leading killers in Singapore. Not surprisingly, targeting TNF itself has been a therapeutic option in some of these disorders like RA. But systemic therapy targeting TNF is very costly, causes general immune suppression, and does not work for many chronic inflammatory conditions besides RA. Given TNFs pivotal role in physiology, “precision” anti-TNF drugs that work selectively, in many ailments besides RA are badly needed. However, unlike with precision oncology, several gaps in our understanding of the TNF pathway have prevented us from developing “precision anti-TNF drugs” which work in cell/context specific manner. This begs the question; have we identified and characterized all the components that regulate TNF signaling? Given that only 2% of the genome codes for proteins, and a large number of RNAs are induced during inflammation, is it possible that we have totally missed looking for RNAs as structural and regulatory components of TNF signaling? Recently developed cutting edge single-cell methods tell us that components like RNAs and RNA-binding-proteins (RBPs), regulate TNFR signaling, in a cell type specific manner, and hence could be exploited to make “precision anti-TNF drugs”. Herein, we aim to comprehensively identify, understand and delineate the cell-type specific roles of RNAs and RBPs, hitherto undiscovered components of TNF signalling, in inflammation, development and cancer. Our studies will identify novel targets that selectively block unwanted effects of systemic anti-TNF therapy in ailments besides RA and help remodel “cold tumors” for effective immune or chemotherapy.
kw: NFkB; IKK; Signaling; Cancer; Inflammation; Liver

title: Developing innovative toolkits for elucidating the fundamentals of electrochemical CO2-to-chemicals conversion
abs: Electrochemical CO2 conversion is a paradigm changing technology, whereby CO2 is not simply discarded as waste, but used as an important feedstock for the sustainable production of commodity chemicals that are indispensable to modern society. In this process, a device known as an electrolyzer uses a catalytic system to convert CO2 and renewable electricity into products like ethylene – a precursor for everyday plastics. Currently, the performance of state-of-the-art electrolyzers still falls below the level required for practical application. However, developing more efficient systems is often slow and labour-intensive, hampered by a lack of strong fundamental design rules. Firstly, the ability to identify and study active sites (reaction hot spots) on catalytic materials is a key knowledge gap, which will inspire new catalyst design strategies. Secondly, clearer insights into the reaction mechanism on these active sites is needed for understanding how to channel CO2 conversion towards specific target products. Finally, the catalytic reaction interface for CO2 conversion is often complex and poorly understood. Elucidating this reaction interface is essential for understanding how to control the local reaction environment to maximize system performance and longevity. To tackle this, the overall goal is to develop innovative toolkits for understanding these fundamental aspects, divided according to 3 main objectives . (1) Understanding how catalysts work. Current efforts on studying active sites have been predominantly computational, with little experimental verification. We aim to establish scanning tunneling microscopy-based methodologies, which allows for the unprecedented ability to identify and study CO2 conversion active sites at the atomic scale. (2) Deciphering reaction pathways. Numerous proposed CO2 conversion product formation mechanisms exist, which lack strong experimental evidence. Here, the goal is to utilize strategic isotopic labelling together with state-of-the-art mass spectrometry tools to shed crucial new insights into the mechanisms of multi-carbon product formation. (3) Elucidating the complex reaction interface. The catalytic reaction interface is typically inhomogeneous and ill-defined, thus has been difficult to study via conventional means. Therefore, the objective is to construct model systems that enable systematic and well-defined studies of the catalyst-ionomer-CO2 triple phase reaction interface. These toolkits will be a comprehensive platform for fundamental study of existing and newly developed catalytic systems. Success of the research in this proposal will lead to key fundamental insights, which will form the basis for new theoretical models and experimental methodologies. Crucially, this will be key to enabling the rational design of catalytic systems with unprecedented activity, selectivity and durability. title: Engineered bacteriophages for hospital-acquired antibiotic-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus infections
abs: This project entails developing a battery of recombinant phage targeting specifically Staphylococcus aureus and Klebsiella pneumoniae infections and colonisation. Limitations such as bacterial phage resistance and the threat of horizontal gene transfer are overcome by using genetically modified phages. We chose to focus on these two pathogens based (i) urgent clinical need, (ii) contrasting Gram positive/negative bacterial models (iii) patterns of colonisation and infection models, and (iv) expertise and preliminary data of the team. This project covers from early phage discovery to pre-clinical.
kw: Bacteriophage, phage, therapy, Klebsiella, Staphylococcus, infection, colonization

title: Strategies for Overcoming Obstacles to Cybersecurity Innovation Diffusion and Adoption in Financial Services Sector in Singapore & Israel: An Interdisciplinary Study
abs: Empirical evidence on threats materialised in recent years suggests that readily available cybersecurity solutions, such as products and services, and even legal requirements, benchmarks and processes, if followed, can effectively mitigate most cyber threats. Good intentions and good products unfortunately never suffice. New and innovative technologies can only assist in cybersecurity if the relevant organisations deploy and use them, and use them effectively, efficiently and correctly. Legal solutions can only be effective if organisations adhere to the regulations in a committed manner and not just aiming for superficial compliance. The hypothesis of this project is that organisations under-utilise the continually improving technological solutions, and often only or barely meet legal requirements and benchmarks as regulations are seen as compliance burdens and costs to organisations. Since it is impossible for any regulator to oversee every single organisation’s internal workings and compliance methods, organisations may sometimes strategise and aim for the cheapest means to comply, or even opt for sub-standard compliance. This interdisciplinary research project will identify and study the specific considerations, systemic issues, incentives, and obstacles that slow down, inhibit, or prevent enterprise adoption of superior cybersecurity solutions (of all forms) in core infrastructure areas, both in Singapore and Israel, whether or not mandated by legislation. The research will leverage current Innovation Studies and theoretical, legal and policy frameworks and study the banking, finance and insurance sectors.
kw: Adoption of cybersecurity innovations, law, regulations, financial services sector

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Risk Assessment of Renal Masses in Radiologic Images
abs: Aim: To develop a software that interprets ultrasound (US) and computer tomography (CT) images of kidney in the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) in public healthcare sector. Its application in US will allow polyclinic doctors to prioritize referrals of patients with newly diagnosed renal masses to urologists, while its application in CT will allow urologists to provide more details in patient counselling on treatment options. Over time, the accuracy of prediction by this software will continuously improve by machine learning, with the eventual goal to replace biopsy of renal masses in equivocal cases. Background: Renal masses ranges from tiny cysts which are mostly benign to solid tumors with significant risk of malignancy. There are no reliable signs to indicate the presence of kidney masses or to differentiate cancers from benign masses. There are two clinical and logistic hurdles in patients’ journey upon finding a renal mass. First, the huge referral loads to the urologists as there are no reliable clinical parameters for triage and polyclinic doctors must consider every case as possibly kidney cancer. Second, patients with equivocal CT features are often reluctant for biopsy due to invasiveness and bleeding risks. These problems prompted the PI to start this project. Methodology: Deep neural network (DNN) and semantic segmentation technologies will be used. The DNN will be trained to recognize renal tumors on US and CT images, and predict the likelihood of cancer. Prediction will be based on regression models from clinical databases, prepared by the PI. Project collaborator will develop the software algorithms using these regression models. The accuracy of prediction will be continuously improved as the software refines the models from validation and reading of new cases over time. The software will be an add-on to PACS, so new cases with are fed to it immediately and anonymously.
kw: Renal masses, Ultrasound, Computer Tomography, Artificial Intelligence

title: Advancing DNA-Delivery for Gene Therapy
abs: Gene therapy holds great promises for the future of medicine by allowing the introduction of healthy genes to compensate for defective ones in patients. Furthermore, new functionalities can be introduced, exemplified by reprogramming of immune cells to attack tumours. This revolutionising therapy depends on efficient delivery of DNA to human cells, but delivery methods are limited to short DNA sequences. This is becoming a bottleneck as more elaborate constructs and gene circuits are required for the field of gene therapy to reach its full potential. Here, we propose to establish a novel platform that enables reprogramming of bacteriophage to deliver large, custom DNA sequences to mammalian cells. Phage are particularly attractive vehicles as they are spacious, robust, genetically inert, and simple to produce. The platform will facilitate engineering and directed evolution of phage genomes to create mutants for cell-specific delivery. We will employ this system to deliver better regulated CAR-T cell therapy to live animals, thereby rendering cell-therapy into non-invasive gene therapy.
kw: Gene therapy; cell therapy; phage technology; genome engineering; CAR-T.

title: Development of Predictive Maintenance and Intelligent Alert system for Cloud-based Waste Water Samplers for Pandemic Cluster Surveillance.
abs: This project aims to exploit the use of machine learning and A.I. in preventive maintenance and failure analysis of a waste water sampling system, as well as anomaly detection in its operating environment. Moreover, it aims to prevent sampling process disruption, by using an on-premise controller to take over the cloud-based control system in the event of cellular network failure. Today, waste water sampling is controlled and scheduled by a cloud system. However, in the event of cellular network breakdown, the control process will be disrupted. A technician is then required to visit the site and troubleshoot. In addition, a sampler’s motor often chokes due to over sampling and the harsh waste water environment, halting the sampling process. In both scenarios, this leads to a gap in sampling data, which is highly adverse for research such as virus detection. We propose to design an intelligent add-on circuit with A.I.-based controller that can be added to an existing waste water sampling system. Sensors will be deployed to collect information on the operating environment of the waste water sampling system. Data analytics will be performed and an artificial neural network trained and optimised to detect possible failures or anomalies in near future, so that preventive maintenance can be carried out. An Application Programming Interface (API) will be added onto the cloud system so that third party devices can securely read sampler status and sensor information. Singapore Polytechnic has a tripartite collaboration with an experienced industry partner W2 Industrial (W2) and the National Environment Agency (NEA) to enhance Singapore’s existing waste water sampling system, which includes a Real Time Unit (RTU) interface, cloud communication, sampling processes and scheduling. Significant preliminary research has been done, and discussions undertaken with relevant users to understand user requirements. The project has been found to be technically feasible. The significant technical development of this project between the background IP and possible translation outputs is TRL 3 to TRL 7.
kw: Covid-19; Water Samplers; Predictive Maintenance; Intelligent Control; Cloud-based Monitoring

title: Cost Effective Durable Antimicrobial Film with Multiple Antimicrobial Surface Strategies
abs: Touch surfaces that are contaminated with microbes are a common mode of transmission for pathogens. Pathogens can stay viable on surfaces for days to months if the surface is suitable for microbial growth. Antimicrobial coatings and films are specially engineered to kill such microbes reducing their spread. Antimicrobial coating products sold in the current market generally have a short lifetime, requiring frequent re-application. This incurs high labour costs in addition to the high cost of the coating. There is also little information about its efficacy in real life environment where human traffic volume, temperature and humidity vary. Our project seeks to address these two critical issues by building on the results of our recent internal project where we have developed a solution-based doped antimicrobial nanowire coating recipe on glass substrate. The developed coating is proven to be transparent, self-cleaning, highly antimicrobial, more durable, more cost effective and potentially faster acting than benchmark commercial coating that is widely applied in our public premises currently. The developed coating adopts multiple antimicrobial surface strategies, making it suitable for use under a wider range of environments. External antiviral lab test using human coronavirus (CoV-OC43) on one of our coatings shows a high antiviral efficacy > 99.9% in reducing viral titer after 24 hours contact time. We propose to further study the antimicrobial mechanism of the developed coating and further improve its efficacy (with reduced contact time) and durability through surface modification. We will also modify the coating process so that it can be applied onto polymeric substrates to produce flexible antimicrobial film. The films with adhesive on the back can then be simply pasted onto any surface, widening its range of application. Various field tests to ascertain efficacy of the scaled-up antimicrobial film will be conducted in hospital and at places with different human traffic volumes. We also plan to coat HVAC filters to enhance its microbe filtration efficiency. External lab tests are crucial to validate our film / coating’s efficacy. Our industry collaborator has agreed to bear the cost of these tests in kind and is ready to license this intellectual property upon successful completion of this project with good results.
kw: Antimicrobial, anti-coronavirus, nanowires, coatings, films, durable, cost-effective

title: Modular bioreactor with nano-needle magneto-transfection technology for end-to-end CAR-T cell manufacturing
abs: There are >2.25 million new cancer patients in South-East Asia annually. Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cell (CAR-T) therapy is a promising treatment where T cells undergo intracellular delivery or transfection and are genetically engineered to destroy cancer. However, current CAR-T manufacturing requires substantial space and labour which lead to high treatment prices. Here, I propose a modular bioreactor integrated with automated nano-needle magneto-transfection technology for end-to-end CAR-T manufacturing. This platform could significantly reduce manufacturing costs and time to expand the use of cell therapy in Singapore’s anti-cancer health agenda and strengthen Singapore as a regional hub for cell manufacturing.
kw: Modular bioreactor, CAR-T cells, cell manufacturing, end-to-end, cell therapy, cancer

title: ParcelDrone – A Modular, Self-powered Multirotor Approach to Aerial Parcel Delivery
abs: Today, drones are deemed as a potential tool to augment or even replace conventional land-based delivery platforms. This is due to advancements in drone technology that have enabled benefits such as speedy parcel deliveries to customers by undertaking an optimal path to escape obstacles such as tall buildings and bypass traffic congestions. However, present practical delivery solutions for high altitude delivery are mainly parachutes. Despite being a cost-effective solution, parachutes are unable to perform accurate landing with high repeatability due to the lack of controllability over the system after deployment. On the other hand, even though multirotor platforms are able to land with high precision, it consumes high amount of energy to do so. Additionally, existing multirotor platforms are fixed in their build, limiting the payload size and weight variation. This implies that a fleet of drones is required in order to cater to different parcel specifications, which is impractical. This project proposes a learning-based, plug-and-fly multirotor system called ParcelDrone that converts the parcel into an autonomous delivery drone. The ParcelDrone consists of multiple, decentralized propeller modules which the user can conveniently attach along the circumference of the parcel without blocking the propeller slipstream. This modular approach enables full system scalability to any parcel size and weight. The ParcelDrone can be also self-powered as it will also be able to harvest energy during its free-fall descent from high altitude to perform a low-impact landing of the parcel. There are several challenges to this innovative solution. Firstly, each propeller module should be designed as an independent flying agent that have all its critical components contained within a compact housing. This also includes developing a reliable and secure attaching mechanism between the parcel and the module. Secondly, to fully modularise the system in both hardware and software, the propeller modules would need to employ a learning-based decentralized control that enables the propeller modules to operate independently while accommodating variations in the parcel’s center of gravity without communicating with other existing modules on the parcel. This allows scalability without increasing computational cost, unlike a centralized control system. Thirdly, the control module of the system should be designed with a single circuitry that enables toggling between thrust producing and energy producing operation. This allows the system to harvest energy during the descent and store it in a power storage system and expend the energy as the parcel is nearing the ground. A preliminary system was fabricated to validate the feasibility of the modular concept using a rudimentary version of the decentralised controller. Results showed that the system can cater to any parcel specification and achieve both altitude and attitude control with a high level of manoeuvrability. The signif

title: The Computational Design of Catalysts by Balancing Stability, Efficiency, and Cost-Effectiveness: A Case Study using Fuel Cells
abs: Singapore will pivot to a green hydrogen-based economy to reduce the republic’s CO2 footprint. Fuel cell vehicles will be an important fulcrum in this hydrogen economy. Current fuel cell vehicles use precious metals like platinum as catalysts. Pt-based materials while meeting performance and stability criteria, are twice as expensive as required from a techno-economic viewpoint. Replacing Pt with inexpensive, earth-abundant alternatives which meet performance, stability, and cost metrics has remained an enduring challenge. Notwithstanding advances in the computational design of catalysts, prevailing methods cannot determine the stability of nanoparticles effectively. Moreover, these methods do not connect reaction rates at individual active sites to device-level metrics like the rate per mass. We propose a hierarchical materials informatics-based workflow to identify bimetallic nanoparticles which meet four device-level criteria for vehicular fuel cells identified by the US Department of Energy. We will leverage this workflow to find those nanoparticles which have (1) current densities > 0.44 A/mg, (2) half the cost of an equivalent Pt nanoparticle, (3) stability within 50 meV from the convex hull under reaction conditions, and (4) 100% selectivity for oxygen reduction to H2O. The core hypothesis in our materials-informatics workflow is that the stability of individual active sites in nanoparticles dictates their inherent reactivity. This hypothesis, corroborated by experiments, enables us to construct a hierarchical workflow to evaluate nanoparticle stability under electrochemical conditions. Using the alloy stability model conceptualized by the PI, we build an iterative loop between reactivity and stability determinations. Our workflow ensures that more sophisticated methods to determine nanoparticle stability under aqueous electrochemical conditions are only deployed for the most promising materials which meet the performance, stability, cost metrics stated above. As a proof of concept, we present preliminary results using our materials informatics workflow to design PtAu nanoparticles. From a scientific context, successes in our effort will spawn a new paradigm to design catalytic nanoparticles which simultaneously considers performance, stability, and cost relate constraints. These advances will improve the veracity of computational predictions and close the materials gap between computational models and their structures under reaction conditions.

title: 2D Dielectrics for 2D Semiconductors
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Realizing advanced two-dimensional semiconductor electronics requires overcoming two crucial challenges: dielectric integration and contact engineering. Quantum applications impose more stringent conditions including cryogenic operation and atomically clean interfaces. Conventional approaches inevitably introduce severe surface damage in atomically thin materials. State-of-the-art solutions remain unsatisfactory in either quality, compatibility or scalability. We propose liquid metal reaction synthesized ultrathin oxides as protection/seed layers for subsequent dielectric deposition. Paired with indium alloys contacts, we will achieve 2D semiconductor devices of unmatched quality, suitable even for demanding low-temperature quantum transport studies. This solidifies Singapore’s strengths in semiconductor electronics and seeds emerging interest in quantum technologies.

title: Multi-compositional heterogeneous electrocatalysts for thermoelectric driven hydrogen production
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Recent years, Singapore has put its reliance on solar photovoltaic deployment to transition to a low-carbon future. While, challenges remain in harnessing solar power including space constraint, intermittency sunshine and solar deployment cost. Through electrolysing water, hydrogen is currently made to produce renewable power as a vital clean energy carrier. In parallel, natural or waste heat are one of the most accessible renewable energy sources, which can be ideally utilized to produce electricity with efficient electrocatalysts for low-cost water splitting. We propose to develop multi-compositional heterogeneous electrocatalysts for thermoelectric driven water splitting. This can be accomplished using highly efficient thermoelectric materials through controlling multi-compositional disordered unit cells in semiconductors and temperature-dependent superionic phase functionalized electrocatalysts on porous bio-microstructured electrodes for substantially enhanced electrocatalytic hydrogen generation.
kw: Inorganic Chemistry, Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment, Materials Science, Materials Chemistry, Biomaterials

title: Direct Laser Writing of Phase-change Semiconductor Microstructures
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Current semiconductor-based phase-change metal chalcogenides (MC) encounter bottleneck on generating complex 2D/3D micro-/nanostructures with tunable optical/electrical properties as lack of chemically-stable resists/resins. The objective is to 3D-print MC-based thermal/electrical-responsive 2D/3D micro-/nanostructures (e.g. 3D woodpiles/honeycombs) using self-formulated photoresists via direct laser writing (DLW). The customized photoresists are polyol-based, involving sol-gel condensation and photopolymerization during DLW to accomplish properties-tunable 2D/3D MC micro-/nanostructures for user-demand outcomes (viz. optically maneuverable or structurally switchable features). It aims to explore advanced MC-based photoresist materials to expand additive manufacturing capabilities for platforms with potential in optical modulators, sensors, supercapacitors, and data storage. Proposed project contributes to materials exploration and processing, leading to sustainable growth of precision engineering and additive manufacturing in Singapore.
kw: 3D Printing; Phase Change Semiconductor Materials; Metal Chalcogenides; Materials Science; Surfaces and Interfaces

title: Pioneering inverse nonlinear metasurfaces for quantum information processing
inst: IHPC - Institute of High Performance Computing
abs: Nonlinear optical effects are widely applied for quantum state preparation and qubit manipulation. Many materials with high nonlinear coefficients are promising for quantum information processing, and the respective metasurfaces are designed aiming to replace bulky optical components. However, patterning these nonlinear materials is challenging, and limits the nonlinear conversion efficiency. Here, we propose inverse metasurfaces where the nonlinear optical materials and insulators are inverted enabling etchless thin-films of nonlinear materials. Patterning insulator mitigates the problems of rough sidewall scattering and fabrication non-uniformity, thus enabling high-efficiency quantum information processing and strengthening the quantum capabilities in Singapore.
kw: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics (Flat Optics, Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials; Statistical and Nonlinear Physics)

title: Atomically Precise Synthesis of Single-Wall Carbon Nanotube Fragments
abs: Single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are regarded as promising functional materials due to their outstanding physical properties. However, current production and sorting methods have reached their limits to achieve atomically precise SWCNTs. Therefore, the potential high-performance of SWCNTs can barely exerted in their integrated devices due to insufficient purities. Recently, organic synthesis provides a reliable and promising alternative route to achieve atomically precise SWCNTs. The synthetic SWCNT fragments can not only serve as templates for the control growth of SWCNTs via chemical vapor deposition, it may also be expectable that SWCNTs can be obtained via polymerizations of these fragments. To date, as an emergent research topic, many aspects of atomically precise SWCNT fragments remain elusive. Through this project, we aim to generalize a series of synthetic strategies towards SWCNT fragments with unique topologies and subsequently investigate their properties and applications at more accurate unimolecular/supramolecular levels. Our long-term goal is to use these building blocks for the synthesis of SWCNTs with well-defined diameter and edge structure.
kw: Chemistry; Materials Chemistry; Organic Chemistry; Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials

title: Enhancing Infrared-to-Visible Upconversion by Controlling Exciton Flow in Sensitizer and Annihilator
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) detection has applications across industrial, agricultural, medical, military, security, and scientific fields. A promising way to produce inexpensive SWIR detectors is to sensitize silicon with a thin-film coating that performs infrared-to-visible upconversion. Under light of moderate intensity, upconversion may be achieved by triplet-triplet annihilation, but major bottlenecks remain, such as limited diffusion lengths and back energy transfer of excitons. Here, we aim to improve exciton diffusion by engineering the ligands and physical arrangement of the nanocrystal sensitizer (absorber) and reduce the back energy transfer by distancing the emitter from the sensitizer with an exciton buffer layer.
kw: photon upconversion; triplet-triplet annihilation; colloidal quantum dots; nanoplatelets; exciton diffusion; infrared detection

title: Improving 3D recognition performance with minimum extra costs for vision guided robotics
abs: 3D recognition is a key technique that has wide applications in vision guided robotics (VGR), e.g., autonomous vehicles, navigation, surveillance and beyond. There remain huge performance gaps between machine learning models and humans for 3D recognition. We here aim to improve the accuracy and robustness of 3D recognition models with minimum extra costs. Our hypothesis is that learning good low-level geometric features is crucial to 3D recognition and low/middle level representations are typically shared across different datasets and even different tasks. Therefore, for improving the accuracy, we propose to exploit 3D unlabelled data by developing novel implicit function based unsupervised feature learning for 3D pre-training. We also propose to leverage 2D data and 2D recognition model by developing novel cross-domain knowledge distillation methods. For improving the robustness, we propose few-shot learning for tackling open-set generalizations, which is achieved by designing higher-order potential functions to exploit geometric constraints. The proposed methods aim to bridge the research gaps exist in the community.
kw: Physical Sciences, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

title: Surface-Clean Cu2O Nanocrystals with Various Morphologies for CO Electroreduction
abs: The main significance of the proposal is for developing a surfactant-free method to precisely synthesize ordered Cu2O nanocrystals with various morphologies, where clean surface largely enhances their catalytic activities. The morphology of Cu2O nanocrystals determines their intrinsic catalytic properties and hence plays a crucial role in influencing the Faradaic efficiency and current density in electrochemical CO reduction. Generally, surfactants are essential in altering the morphology of Cu2O by controlling the stability and growth rate of different facets in a thermodynamical or kinetical way. However, the adsorbed surfactant capping agents on the surface of catalysts often block the access of reactant molecules to the surface atoms and disturb the charge transfer, hence decreasing the catalytical performance. Therefore, a grand challenge in this realm is how to alter the morphology of nanocatalysts, while maintaining their colloidal stability without the surfactant. In this proposed research project, we will develop a morphology controlled synthesis strategy for the preparation of surfactant-free Cu2O nanocrystals toward greatly enhanced electrocatalytic CO reduction. In our design, we will utilize different precursor concentration and reductant injection speed to change the morphology of Cu2O nanocrystals in an aqueous solution with good colloidal stability. We will systematically study the growth mechanism to achieve different morphologies, which are expected to exhibit better Faradaic efficiency and current density than conventional surfactant-coated ones. The proposed project will create the knowledge for the bottom-up synthesis of surfactant-free nanocrystals with desired functionality for enhanced catalytic performance.
kw: Catalysis; Electrochemistry; Environmental Chemistry; Materials Chemistry; Surfaces and Interfaces

title: 3D Printed Functional Bio-Laser System for Multiscale Neural Cell Therapy
abs: Cell-based therapies hold great promise for a myriad of clinical applications in neurological disorder, neurodegenerative diseases, and health technologies. In particular, cell sorting technology lays the key foundation of pharmaceutical production and neural cell therapy. However, high-quality cell sorting and profiling in organoids remain a crucial bottleneck in cell manufacturing due to the complexity of inherent variability. Current methods relying on fluorescent labelling cannot provide multidimensional cellular interactions, limiting the sorting capacity and bioinformation. This project aims to address the current challenges by proposing a non-destructive modality for distinguishing high-quality stem cells and their progeny through an additive 3D-printed multifunctional biolaser device. The novel concept of biological microlasers is introduced here by taking advantage of photonic resonators to amplify and differentiate subtle bio-signals. The goal is to establish a multiscale cell sorting and multidimensional profiling biosystem, from single cell level to organoid, while reducing the problem of variability and heterogeneity. In the first aim, a multiscale 3D printed biolaser will be developed through additive manufacturing. The multidimensional optical fingerprint will be imaged through the laser biochip, including five optical features with distinctive spectrum across the visible ranges (polarity, chirality, mechanical resonance, light-scattering profile, and refractive index). Extended functions for biomarker-labeled cells will also be integrated. In the second aim, we aim to establish the laser-fingerprint of induced progenitor stem based on the biolaser system, including undifferentiated and differentiated cells (astrocytes, neurons, oligodendrocytes). Deep learning-based cell library based on multiparametric analysis will be established to enhance the accuracy and sorting efficiency. Downstream differentiation efficacy of the cells will also be investigated and cultured into organoids of interest. Finally, extended application for high-throughput sorting brain cancer-related 3D organoids and drug screening will be completed in the third aim. We aim to realize organoid sorting derived from both iPSCs with different heterogeneity and activity. Subsequently, high-content drug screening of organoids will be demonstrated through addictive 3D printing and laser fingerprinting. In brief, our approach enables multiscale sorting of cells and organoids while reducing the problems related to the huge heterogeneity of cell therapy. A new precision cell phenotyping technology will be established upon success, leading Singapore closer towards effective cell therapies and drug discovery for glioblastoma and neurological disorder treatments.
kw: bio-manufacturing; 3D printing; cell therapy; microlaser; organoid; multiscale sorting

title: Origami AlGaN/GaN optoelectronics for ultraviolet hemispherical electronic eye systems
abs: Human eyes are remarkably delicate vision organs and have inspired biomimicry with numerous designs and applications in various areas. Human eyes can be regarded as an excellent platform of single-lens imaging system, which consists of one convex lens and one curvy image sensor. The most advantage of single-lens imaging system is its prominent simplicity, which makes it very useful for applications that require stringent geometry design such as endoscope. This is a clear advantage when compared to a planar array of light detecting devices. Semiconductor photodetectors are indispensable optoelectronic devices which convert light signals into electrical signals. They have numerous advantages such as simple device structure, high dark and photo current ratio, and easy fabrication. However, the planar nature of semiconductor fabrication techniques makes it difficult to implement hemispherical eye systems, which mimic human eyes. Ultraviolet imaging has a variety of scientific and industrial applications such as remote sensing, forensics, astronomy, and medical systems. However, most of the hemispherical eye systems has been built on conventional semiconductors (e.g., silicon and gallium arsenide), restricting its use for detection and imaging through ultraviolet light. This is due to the absence of high-quality free-standing wide bandgap semiconductor materials with good single crystallinity and mechanical durability. Hemispherical geometries provide unique imaging advantages over their planar counterpart (e.g., focal-plane array), such as low aberrations and a wide field of viewing angle. Therefore, various attempts have been made to realize artificial hemispherical eye systems. The simplest approach was to mount optoelectronic components on either a flexible printed-circuit board or curved mold surface. However, it could only achieve hemicylindrical shapes and low degree of curvatures. The second approach was to mount deformable optoelectronic components on thin polydimethylsiloxane layer, followed by a flow of gas or liquid to adjust zoom capability. Although this technique offers a control knob to vary the degree of curvature, the bulge setup places increased burden on assembly and testing. Recently, curvy and shape-adaptive imagers were developed using conformal additive stamp printing. This technique enables the direct printing of the fabricated optoelectronic pixel array onto convex and concave surfaces, but large area transfer-printing is limited due to deformation of balloon stamp. In this proposal, we aim to develop a completely new ultraviolet hemispherical eye system based on aluminium gallium nitride/gallium nitride photodetectors. Most of the current hemispherical eye systems is limited to visible and infrared spectral wavelength regions due to the lack of high-quality flexible wide-bandgap semiconductor materials which can detect ultraviolet light.
