Development of sc-CUT&RUN will set a new paradigm for robust, high throughput measurement of epigenetic heterogeneity in various biological contexts. A further sub-aim is to combine sc-CUT&RUN with single-nuclei RNA-sequencing (sn-RNAseq) in the same cell to enable epigenomic-transcriptomic correlation.In Aim 2, we will investigate the epigenetic selection and adaptation of tumor cells that lead to acquired drug resistance. We will perform sc-CUT&RUN on patient-derived tumor cells before, during and after drug treatment, to evaluate pre-existing intra-tumor heterogeneity, as well as epigenetic response of individual cells that lead chemoresistance. Insights into trajectory of epigenetic response to cancer drugs will shed light on the multistep fixation of drug resistant epigenetic states. Finally, in Aim 3, we will test novel strategies to prevent the development of drug resistance by targeting the epigenetic landscape. Resistance promoting epigenetic changes identified from Aim 2 will be genetically or pharmacologically targeted to prevent drug resistance. Pre-empting these epigenetic changes early in disease progression may be an effective treatment strategy to circumvent resistance and improve survival of cancer patients.
kw: single cell analysis, histone, chromatin immunoprecipitation, drug resistance, epigenetics, tumor heterogeneity

title: Mechanisms of decline in vascular cognitive impairment
abs: Aims : To leverage upon human cohort studies conducted by the Memory Aging & Cognition Centre (MACC) as well as the technical and analytical capacity of the Centre for Imaging Research (A*Star-NUS) and Cardiovascular Research Institute (CVRI), to address the problem of Vascular Cognitive Impairment a common chronic illness which constitutes a major clinical and economic burden world-wide. Methods and Approach : To develop biomarkers by characterizing neuropsychological patterns, exploring mechanisms, in particular vascular processes (cerebrovascular lesions, cardiac and vascular),accounting for cognitive decline in these individuals, so as to develop therapeutic interventions to prevent cognitive decline in high risk patients. Hypotheses : High risk groups will show characteristic neuropsychological trajectories and be associated with brain, cardiac and vascular markers of disease. Specifically, a) brain MRI and cardiovascular markers will provide prognostic information on cognitive decline; b) circulating biomarkers of proven diagnostic and/or prognostic importance in heart failure and acute coronary disease will be useful in identification and risk stratification in patients with early and advanced cognitive impairment in that plasma concentrations of one or more of these markers will correlate with (i) measures of cognitive function and/or (ii) brain MRI changes. Moreover, both baseline and serial change in, one or more of these biomarkers, will add additional predictive information on progression. We aim to improve understanding of Vascular Cognitive Impairment.
kw: Vascular Cognitive Impairment;Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Cardiovascular Imaging; Blood Biomarkers

title: Therapeutic targeting IL-11 signaling to treat NASH and phenotypic dissection of fibro-inflammatory liver disease in Singaporeans
abs: Hepatic fibrosis is common in liver diseases and leads to cirrhosis and liver failure. There are no approved therapies for treating liver fibrosis, which represents an unmet clinical need. In Singapore, and Asia more generally, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is common. In Singapore, it has been suggested that a ‘lean or low BMI NASH’ phenotype may exist that occurs at lower body mass indices than in Caucasians, similar to type 2 diabetes: ‘lean diabetes’. While liver fibrosis can be reversed as seen after the use of antiviral therapies in hepatitis, the reversal of liver fibrosis in NASH and other liver conditions is not possible. Liver fibrosis is driven by the transformation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) into fibrogenic, pro-inflammatory myofibroblasts and HSC activation is a defining pathology underlying NASH1–3. In recent studies we discovered that HSC transformation is centrally dependent upon the autocrine activity of the Interleukin-11 (IL-11) cytokine, that IL-11 is upregulated in many fibrotic human liver diseases and that IL11RA deleted mice are protected from liver fibrosis and methionine choline deficient diet-induced NASH. This novel finding follows on from our breakthrough discovery published in Nature in 2017 where we showed IL-11 was centrally important for cardiac fibrosis4. In the project described here we will build on our very strong preliminary data and use newly developed therapeutic antibodies and human disease relevant murine models of fibro-inflammatory liver diseases (Specific Aim 1), apply advanced molecular techniques in our recently generated reporter mice strains (Specific Aim 2) and study liver steatosis, fibrosis and inflammation using elegant MRI techniques in a deeply phenotyped Singaporean cohort (Specific Aim 3). These complementary Aims will help us develop a better understanding of fibro-inflammatory hepatic dysfunction in a local Singaporean context and to explore IL-11 as novel therapeutic target and paradigm for fibro-inflammatory liver diseases.
kw: NASH, fibrosis, therapy, cytokine, liver

title: Bedside to bench and back again: evaluating Neisseria spp. as novel respiratory pathobionts using systems biology
abs: Chronic respiratory disease is a major health and economic burden to individuals and societies. These diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and bronchiectasis are challenging to diagnose and treat; due to clinical heterogeneity, multiple endo-phenotypes and their overlap. Consequently, a personalised approach accounting for microbiomes requires exploration particularly in bronchiectasis: a chronic and irreversible heterogeneous airway disease of high Asian prevalence. In work performed by the PI, we have identified an Asian-bronchiectasis phenotype whose microbiome is dominated by the bacterial taxa Neisseria. This phenotype associates with poorer clinical outcome compared to Pseudomonas, a well-established bronchiectasis pathogen. Neisseria is best known as a cause of meningitis and gonorrhoea and only limited case reports suggest it as an airway pathogen. Using clinical isolates derived from airway specimens of Asian bronchiectasis patients demonstrating our deleterious clinical phenotype, we have established an animal model of Neisseria lung infection that demonstrates significant inflammation and tissue destruction. In this proposal, we extend our studies to address three key issues related to Neisseria airway pathogenesis. First, we will elucidate mechanisms by which Neisseria establishes airway infection using our animal model and systems biology illustrating it as a novel respiratory pathogen. Next, we will determine its role in the development of bronchiectasis using an animal model at high risk of disease: a Multicilin (Mci) mouse mutant, deficient in airway cilia, a key risk factor for bronchiectasis. Finally, we will validate our animal findings in human cohorts and translate discovered biomarkers and mechanisms of Neisseria lung pathogenesis including a prospective assessment of its immunological consequence. The novel mechanisms elucidated and new approaches developed will permit improved patient stratification and a deeper understanding of Asian phenotypes of pulmonary disease: an understudied field with significant implications for patient care and clinical outcome.
kw: Bronchiectasis; Microbiome; Pathobiont; Endophenotype; Precision medicine

title: The role of Yap/Taz expression in the development of non‐alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)
abs: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a pandemic associated with obesity and diabetes. NAFLD initially presents with hepatosteatosis, but can progress to steatohepatitis (NASH), fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Currently, the mechanism(s) for inflammation and fibrosis in NASH is not known; moreover, there is no available pharmacologic therapy for NASH. Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activators with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ) are transcriptional effectors in the Hippo signaling pathway that are increased in liver injury and fibrosis. We recently found that both proteins were induced in dietary and genetic models of NASH and associated with the induction of inflammation and fibrosis markers in the liver, macrophages, and hepatic stem cells (HSCs). Additionally, siRNA knockdown in hepatic cells and HSCs, as well as in macrophages from macrophage-specific Yap/Taz double knockout mice decreased expression of inflammation and fibrosis genes. Thus, Yap/Taz expression in hepatocytes, HSCs, and macrophages may have important roles in the pathogenesis of NASH. We hypothesize that expression of Yap/Taz in these cell types play critical roles in the inflammation, fibrosis, and metabolic changes of NASH. Accordingly, we plan to generate and employ mouse models of liver-, macrophage-, and HSC-specific deletion and overexpression of Yap/Taz: Specific Aim 1: To determine the role of hepatic Yap/Taz expression in NASH progression Specific Aim 2: To determine the role of Yap/Taz-regulated changes in macrophage polarization in NASH progression Specific Aim 3: To determine the role of Yap/Taz expression in HSCs in NASH progression Our studies will lead to better understanding of the relative contributions of Yap/Taz-mediated transcription in hepatocytes, macrophages, and HSCs in the pathogenesis of NASH. Yap/Taz expression also potentially could serve as a marker for NASH severity. Elucidating the specific role(s) of Yap/Taz in these different cell types could lead to the identification of new molecular targets for the treatment of NASH.
kw: non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, steatohepatitis, yap/taz, liver, macrophage

title: Comprehensive interrogation of the epigenetics promoter and enhancer landscape in HCC to identify aberrant regulatory mechanisms associated with HCC
abs: Overall survival in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains exceedingly poor due to the dearth of efficacious systemic therapies for this complex malignancy. There are still no validated biomarkers to date and this translated to the inadequacy of extant investigative approaches. Additional and more comprehensive exploration of HCC is therefore required to address this urgent unmet clinical need. The epigenetics enhancer and promoter landscape as well as chromatin organization remain unexplored in HCC. We aim to conduct a comprehensive interrogation of the promoter and enhancer landscape to elucidate deregulated regulatory mechanisms associated with HCC at the epigenetics level. We hypothesize that aberrations in these key regulatory elements are significant drivers in HCC tumorigenesis and will help us identify critical pathways and biomarkers directly impacting on the clinical trajectory of HCC. Specifically, we will perform global epigenomics profiles of primary HCC to identify key promoters and enhancers involved in driving HCC, elucidate aberrant promoter-enhancer interactions and interrogate the chromatin organization in non-viral and Hep B-driven HCC. In addition, we will investigate the co-dependence between phylogenetic and phyloepigenetic trees responsible for the intra-tumoral heterogeneity in HCC evolution. We will adopt ChIP-seq technology (both modified histone marks and CTCF) and Hi-C chromosomal conformation techniques to pursue the aims of this study. Pipelines for these epigenetic techniques have been established and successfully applied in our lab. Through comprehensive analysis of the global epigenetic promoter and enhancer landscape, we seek to unravel novel biomarkers and therapeutic approaches for HCC. Importantly, this epigenomics study leverages on the comprehensive multi–omics platform in HCC already established by our NMRC TCR National Flagship Program in Liver Cancer. Our prospective multi-disciplinary and multi-institution translational-clinical program collects multi-region samples from resected HCC in a surgical cohort and interrogates the genomics, immunomics and metabolomics of HCC to guide Precision Medicine strategies.
kw: HCC, epigenomics

title: Metastatic triple-negative taxane-resistant/refractory breast cancer: Investigating the role of Bexarotene in inducing susceptibility to chemotherapy by differentiating cancer cells from a mesenchymal-like to an epithelial-like phenotype (BEXMET)
abs: Background: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), as defined by its ER negative, PR negative and HER2 negative status, is biologically aggressive and has limited systemic treatment options, often compounded by treatment resistance, hence conferring an overall poorer prognosis. Cell state transitions, e.g. epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET), govern the functional behavior of cancer cells, such as proliferation, invasiveness, metastatic potential and resistance to chemotherapy. Our preliminary studies revealed Bexarotene (retinoid) as a potent MET inducer, verified in TNBC cells in vitro and in animal models, rendering greater chemotherapy sensitivity. Bexarotene is used in the treatment of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Hypothesis: Bexarotene induces MET in cancer cells in metastatic TNBC patients (thereby increasing chemotherapy susceptibility). Specific Aims: 1. To characterize the RNA and protein profiles of serial biopsies of the selected lesion: before, during and after Bexarotene administration 2. To evaluate early safety and tolerability signals of the Bexarotene-Capecitabine combination Approach/Methods: This is a single-arm study of Bexarotene-Capecitabine in 20 taxane-resistant/refractory metastatic TNBC patients. Bexarotene is dosed daily with a 2-week lead-in before Capecitabine is commenced. Capecitabine is started on week 3 for 14 consecutive days every 21 days. Bexarotene is dosed for 7 days of every 21-day cycle of Capecitabine, coinciding with the rest weeks from Capecitabine, i.e. weeks 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20. Four tumour biopsies are scheduled: 1) week 0 before starting Bexarotene, 2) week 2, 3) week 4, and 4) after week 20. Biopsies are submitted for histopathological review, transcriptomic (RNASeq) and protein (immunohistochemistry) profiling.
kw: triple-negative breast cancer; mesenchymal-to-epithelial (MET) transition; retinoid

title: Investigating the Genetic and Phenotypic Architecture of Advanced Primary Angle Closure Glaucoma for Stratified Disease management
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, with primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) a major form of glaucoma in Singapore and Asia. While we have made considerable advances in understanding the epidemiology, risk factors, imaging features, and clinical phenotypes of PACG, one of the key unanswered questions is who is at greatest risk for developing advanced PACG/blindness. Current strategies for patient stratification are inadequate to identify those who progress to advanced disease. Our recent work has demonstrated that angle closure exhibits substantial clinically heterogeneity. However, such approaches are inadequate in their abilities to stratify patients as they do not account for both within-disease and across-disease heterogeneity. Our group have also identified eight genetic loci associated with PACG; however, they have all been identified using a broad categorization of PACG. It is thus not known if there are specific genetic variants that confer susceptibility to development of advanced PACG. In this proposal, we hypothesize that specific anatomical features and rare variants of moderate-large effect sizes confer susceptibility to the development of advanced PACG. To address our hypothesis, we will perform comprehensive phenotyping of advanced PACG to identify specific factors associated with severe disease (Aim1). Next, we aim to identify genetic variants that confer susceptibility to advanced disease/blindness by performing targeted sequencing of the known PACG-loci in these subjects (Aim 2). Finally, we aim to build a multimodal artificial-intelligence driven patient stratification model to identify earlier those individuals at risk of developing advanced PACG disease (Aim 3). It is hoped that this project will lead to improved disease stratification of PACG and facilitate early administration of prophylactic treatments to those at the greatest risk of developing advanced disease.
kw: Primary angle closure glaucoma; patient stratification; anterior segment optical coherence tomography;  Ophthalmic genetics; imaging; artificial intelligence

title: Translational program in ocular surface and dry eye
abs: Ocular surface inflammatory disease (OSID) is a heterogeneous group of conditions that affects approximately 300 million people globally. Corneal blindness, a result of end stage OSID, is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide. The commonest cause of OSID is dry eye, which affects up to a third of the adults in Asian countries. In the ongoing CSA which will end in late 2017, important findings such as tear and meibum lipids have been characterized, and novel tools such as automated analysis of meibography and thermography-based tear-evaporimetry have been evaluated. Research publications have propelled the Singapore group to one of the top three most frequently published groups internationally in the dry eye domain. Reputation has increased, resulting in an invitation to participate in an international expert consensus panel (Dry Eye Workshop 2), frequent overseas invited lectures by the industry, and invitation to join the Asia Dry Eye Society council. To further improve patients’ lives, dry eye cannot be addressed by improving tear stability alone, and the inflammatory process will need to be treated. Current treatment of inflammation is unsatisfactory (has adverse effects, lack efficacy or uncomfortable). We aim to build on the existing achievements in the current CSA and focus on investigating the basis of inflammation in dry eye, the immune-regulatory environment of the ocular surface; and translating molecules already identified to real therapy for dry eye patients. Specifically, we will investigate the immunology of graft-vs-host disease, a group of patients with very severe, sight- threatening OSID, elucidate small lipid molecules and role of microbes in dry eye, chart levels of inflammatory mediators after commencement of therapy, and survey for patient preferences in topical anti-inflammatory drugs. The proposed CSA will critically facilitate all existing translational efforts and grant projects by supporting the research team trained over the years.
kw: ocular surface; inflammation; immune cells; tear lipids; microbiome; quality of life

title: OPA1 as a novel therapeutic target for reducing myocardial infarct size and preventing heart failure
abs: Study rationale: Ischaemic heart disease (IHD) and the heart failure that results are the leading causes of death and disability in Singapore and worldwide. As such novel therapies are required to reduce myocardial infarct (MI) size and preserve left ventricular systolic function (LVSF). Mitochondria undergo fission in response to acute ischaemia/reperfusion injury (IRI), and preventing this process can reduce MI size. Here, we investigate whether targeting the mitochondrial fusion protein, OPA1, to inhibit mitochondrial fission, as a novel therapeutic strategy for cardioprotection. Hypothesis: OPA1 is a novel therapeutic target for reducing MI size and preventing heart failure. Objectives and methodology: 1. To investigate the effects of genetic and pharmacological modulation of cardiomyocyte OPA1 levels on the susceptibility of the heart to acute IRI. 2. To use Super-Resolution Microscopy and Focused Ion Beam and Array Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy to investigate the effects of modulating cardiomyocyte OPA1 levels on mitochondrial movement and morphology in the adult heart. 3. To investigate the effects of modulating cardiomyocyte OPA1 levels on the changes in mitochondrial function and cardiac metabolism which occur in response to acute IRI, in order to elucidate the mechanisms though which OPA1 protects the heart. 4. To use induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes reprogrammed from human fibroblasts obtained from dominant optic atrophy patients to investigate the effects of OPA1 deficiency on mitochondrial function and susceptibility to acute IRI in human heart tissue. 5. To use high-throughput screening to discover novel protein/chemical agent for upregulating OPA1. Expected outcomes: We hope to identify OPA1 as a therapeutic strategy to reduce MI size and prevent heart failure, the expected benefits of which would be to improve clinical outcomes in patient with IHD thereby alleviating patient morbidity and mortality in Singapore and worldwide.
kw: Cardioprotection; acute myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury; Mitochondrial morphology

title: An Innovative and Patient-Centric Research Program Targeting the Ageing Singaporeans: The PopulatION HEath and Eye Disease PRofile in Elderly Singaporeans (PIONEER) Study
abs: This research program is innovative; patient-centric; clinical health services driven; and community-focused. It includes three studies. The first one will determine the epidemiology of age-related eye diseases, vision impairment, presbyopia, the aging visual function system; their relationship with multimorbidity, associated consequences and burden; and the comprehensive impact of age-related eye diseases and aging visual function system in the presence of multimorbidity. It is hypothesised that the prevalence of major age-related eye diseases, VI, and presbyopia is substantially high in older Singaporeans ?70 years but different across the three ethnic groups; the association of visual function is different across different eye conditions and changes in these parameters are predictive of the presence and severity of VI; individuals with multimorbidity are likely to have VI; increasing number of comorbid conditions is associated with VI and age-related eye diseases in a step-ladder fashion; and eye diseases, in the presence of multimorbidity, are associated with poor patient’s and carer’s QoL with high personal and societal costs. Using a RCT, the second study will investigate the effectiveness of eye screening with customised post-screening support and eye-specific literacy compared to routine eye screening in elderly people of low SES. We theorise that compared to the usual screening, this new model has a superior post screening referral adherence; is cost effective; and results in significant improvements in eye care management; self-efficacy; vision, and vision-specific QoL. The last project is cluster RCT evaluating the clinical and cost-effectiveness of an innovative eye care intervention (ResCare) which provides onsite eye testing; and a personalised clinical treatment pathway for elderly people in public-funded residential care facilities. We hypothesise that compared to usual care, ResCare will demonstrate a superior improvement in vision; wellbeing, and vision-related QoL; depression and falls; and will be cost effective.
kw: Elderly Vision impairment; Ocular conditions; Visual system; Multimorbidity; Residential care; Underprividged

title: Characterization of immune evasion in NK/T-Cell Lymphoma
abs: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (NKTL) is an aggressive EBV-associated neoplasm more prevalent in South East Asians than in other populations. It is commonly refractory to conventional chemotherapy, and new treatment approaches are urgently required. Immune checkpoint inhibitors affecting the Programmed Death 1 (PD1) pathway show promise in early clinical trials for NKTL, suggesting an important role for the immune system in modulating these tumours. However, PD1 is only one of many pathways employed in cancer immune evasion and new immunotherapy approaches are being tested in various cancers. The interplay between these different immune evasion pathways as well as the role of EBV in immune regulation is not understood in NKTL. This information will be relevant to the incorporation of immunotherapy into NKTL treatment. In this grant, we aim to study immune evasion in NKTL in 2 sections. Section 1 is a pathological characterization of immune evasion markers in clinical NKTL samples. Our previous gene expression studies on NKTL revealed elevated expression of immune modulatory genes. We will validate the protein expression of these transcripts, and study their relationship to Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), as well as novel immuno-oncology targets such as TIM3 and VISTA. We have established a multispectral imaging assay to quantify these molecular markers in tumour and immune cells in the microenvironment of NKTL, to identify appropriate immuno-oncology trial strategies. In Section 2, we will decipher the role of EBV in immune evasion in NKTL by modulating the expression of EBV proteins and miRNA in NKTL cell lines, and analyzing their effects on immune evasion molecules of therapeutic interest. Overall, this grant will help clarify the clinical relevance of immune evasion pathways in NKTL and identify pertinent immune regulatory targets for future clinical trials.
kw: Natural Killer / T-cell lymphoma, EBV, PDL1, immune evasion

title: Genetic origin of adverse drug reactions in Singaporean breast cancer patients
abs: More than 90% of breast cancer patients receive systemic therapy and adverse reactions caused by such treatment are not uncommon. Occurrence and severity vary greatly among individuals and clinically validated biomarker for adverse reactions is not yet available. The proposed project aims to identify genetic variants that influence susceptibility to aromatase inhibitor-induced bone density loss and taxane-induced febrile neutropenia among breast cancer patients in Singapore. Breast cancer patients are recruited from six public hospitals in Singapore as part of the ongoing Singapore Breast Cancer Cohort Project. Participants are asked to donate blood or saliva sample and DNA are extracted and stored at a central laboratory. Socio-demographic data, lifestyle and reproductive risk factor are collected using a structured questionnaire and clinical data such as tumor characteristics and treatment can be retrieved from hospital-based breast cancer registry. For patients treated with aromatase inhibitor, baseline and follow-up measurements of bone mineral density will be retrieved from medical record. A text mining algorithm for electronic medical record will be developed using the surgical data systems directorate database at National University Hospital. With this tool, occurrence of neutropenia among patients receiving taxane will be identified from discharge summary and accompanied laboratory results. With a cohort of 10,000 patients in the next two years, we propose to 1) identify rare variants that can distinguish patients who may suffer from extremely severe ADRs in 500 Chinese patients treated with aromatase inhibitor and 500 Chinese patients treated with taxane-based chemotherapy using whole exome sequencing technology and 2) complement the rare coding variants with information from common and typically low risk genetic variants through whole genome array with customized coding, known genetic loci fine mapping and pharmacogenomics loci imputed to local population reference panels.
kw: breast cancer; adverse drug reactions

title: Rapid Triage for Serious Infections in Infants Younger than 3 Months Using A Novel Heart Rate Variability Tool
abs: Febrile infants <3 months present a diagnostic dilemma to paediatricians and emergency physicians. Tension remains between the need for early aggressive intervention among patients with suspected sepsis and the global phenomena of increasing antibiotic resistance. Current triage tools are insufficient. A non-invasive triage tool to detect infants at risk of serious infections (SI) would reduce unnecessary investigations and unwarranted interventions. We aim to develop a novel artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool including heart rate variability (HRV), and evaluate its utility in predicting serious infection (SI) among febrile infants aged <3 months in KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) Emergency Department (ED). We hypothesize that HRV provides incremental diagnostic information and a novel triage tool incorporating HRV is superior to current triage tools in discriminating infants with SI from those without. This is a prospective observational study to be conducted in KKH, ED. We will include infants <3 months presenting with a rectal temperature >38oC between Jan 2019 and Dec 2020. SI includes sepsis (including bacteremia), meningitis, lobar pneumonia (confirmed radiologically), osteomyelitis, abscess and urinary tract infection. HRV will be monitored for 5 minutes using a single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). The ECG signal will be extracted and processed to obtain HRV data. Performance indicators are the area under receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, which will be compared between the novel and current existing triage tools. If successful, including HRV information will improve triage precision for febrile infants with SI, allowing resources be focused on the sickest infants.
kw: Serious infections; Sepsis; Triage

title: Deubiquitinating enzymes of the Hippo Pathway and their potentials as cancer diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: The turnover of many cellular proteins is regulated via ubiquitination pathway which selectively targets proteins for degradation in the proteasome. The substrate specificity of protein ubiquitination is mediated by ubiquitinating enzymes, but the process is reversible by deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) which remove ubiquitin from the ubiquitinated proteins. The Hippo pathway is an emerging tumor suppressor pathway and dysregulation of this pathway results in tissue overgrowth and cancer development. Although Hippo components are regulated by protein phosphorylation, recent studies suggest that Hippo components are also destabilized by ubiqutination-dependent proteasome degradation, and several ubiquitinating enzymes were identified to target Hippo components. However, not much work on DUBs has been shown to regulate Hippo components. Several recent studies have revealed a few deubiquitinating enzymes regulating Hippo pathway components, including USP9X identified in our lab. The research on deubiquitination of Hippo pathway components is still nascent but represents an exciting new area of the Hippo pathway. To identify DUBs for the Hippo pathway, we searched our protein interacting network of the Hippo pathway constructed in the lab through proteomic analysis. Several DUBs (USP9X, USP15 and USP22) were identified as high confident interacting proteins of the Hippo pathway and we have published recently USP9X as a tumor suppressor stabilizing LATS kinases and other upstream Hippo components to suppress tumor growth. Since deubiquitinating enzymes play important roles and are potential drug targets for various diseases including cancers, this proposal aims to study the hypothesis that these DUBs regulate the Hippo pathway to control cell proliferation and tumor growth, offering novel opportunities for alterative targets for cancer treatment and new diagnostic methods.
kw: Hippo Pathway, Ubiquitination, Deubiquitination, USP22, USP15, Cancer

title: Validation of the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 among those with mental and physical illness in Singapore
abs: Disability has increasingly become an important indicator of disease burden and for evaluating the effectiveness of health interventions. With the significant increase in healthcare treatment and community mental health care programmes across the country, there is an urgent need to evaluate the effectiveness of these programmes using reliable and accurate measures that are able to capture all aspects of patients’ functioning and disability that are comparable not only across health conditions, but also across treatments and programmes of care. The current study aims to validate the WHODAS 2.0 in patients diagnosed with schizophrenia spectrum, depression, anxiety disorders and diabetes, to assess the divergent, concurrent and known-group validity of the WHODAS 2.0 against disease-specific and other known measures, to examine test-retest reliability and agreement between three modes of administrations (self-report, rater-administered, and proxy-administered), to develop and evaluate a crosswalk conversion algorithm between WHODAS 2.0 and the other functioning scales and mapping the relationship between the WHODAS 2.0 and the EQ-5D utility scores, and to compare the responsiveness to change of the WHODAS 2.0 against disease-specific and other known measures over 1 -year follow-up. A cross-sectional study will be conducted among outpatients at the Institute of Mental Health and National Healthcare Group Polyclinic. Data on WHODAS 2.0, generic and disease-specific measures, socio-demographic characteristics, clinical history and service utilization will be collected. Findings from this study will provide evidence to clinicians and researchers about the psychometric properties of the WHODAS 2.0 that can be used to assess the disability of patients with mental and physical conditions in an Asian patient population. This measure also will allow comparisons of burden of disease and quality-adjusted life years in Singapore in future.
kw: WHODAS

title: Evaluating the Clinical Utility of Immune Phenotypes in Schizophrenia
abs: The investigation of immune system abnormalities in schizophrenia has become a burgeoning area of research as recent landmark studies have identified associations between immune genes and increased risk of schizophrenia (Sekar et al., 2016; Shi et al., 2009). This new evidence has lent added weight to the immune hypothesis of schizophrenia and has opened up a new therapeutics window in schizophrenia (Kinney et al., 2010). In this study we hypothesize that immune system abnormalities present in schizophrenia are associated with clinical subtypes; antipsychotic responsive, clozapine responsive and clozapine resistant, each with its unique immune profile. Aims: 1. To examine and identify distinct immune profiles (including immune-related genes, proteins, cytokines, immune cell populations and their functions) of healthy controls, patients with schizophrenia who responded to first and second line antipsychotics (antipsychotic responsive), to clozapine (clozapine responsive), and who did not respond to clozapine (clozapine resistant). 2. To identify the immune markers that are associated with symptom severity, and/or clinical improvement.
kw: Schizophrenia; Immune; clozapine; response; resistance; biomarker

title: A Non Human Primate Model for Intrauterine Haematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation for Beta-Globinopathies
abs: Inherited monogenic diseases affect one-percent of births, many of which causes irreversible pathology in-utero or perinatally. Intrauterine therapy is an evolving strategy with several advantages over post-natal approaches due to unique ontological opportunities existing only during fetal life such as ability to induce donor-specific tolerance (DST) and avoid immune rejection. We have established a developmentally, physiologically and clinically-relevant non-human primate (NHP) model for intrauterine gene transfer applicable to enzyme deficiency syndromes, but not to haemopoietic disorders. Here we extend our studies to explore intrauterine haemopoietic stem cell therapy (IUHSCT) of relevance to thalassemia. The hypotheses are that (i) development of self-tolerance occurs at 0.45 gestation in the fetal macaque, and (ii) that IUHSCT around this time will lead to long-term donor HSC engraftment and DST at curative levels for thalassaemia (~20%). Specifically we will: 1. Establish the immune ontogeny of fetal macaques between 0.3-0.6 gestation to determine the critical time where thymic processing of selfantigen and development of self-tolerance is achieved. 2. Test the ability of IUHSCT to achieve DST and curative level of engraftment for thalassaemia in NHP with or without post-natal boosting, and map immune responses through immuno-monitoring. The successful completion of this proposal will guide the development of a clinical protocol for IUHSCT for beta-thalassaemia, a disease of high priority in our region. By addressing IUHSCT in these clinically-relevant models, we address a range of genetic diseases of perinatal onset and/or where no curative or satisfactory post-natal treatment exists. This approach would be applicable to genetic diseases for which HSC transplantation is of benefit.
kw: Thalassaemia, Haemopoietic Stem Cells, Immune Ontogeny, Non Human Primate

title: Timely Identification of Developmental and Behaviour problems In Toddlers (TIDBIT)
abs: Timely identification and early intervention for developmental problems have good promise for better outcomes in children. The Health Booklet (HB) – a parent-held child health record, is Singapore’s main tool for developmental surveillance. It contains developmental milestone checklists for parents to complete at different age intervals from 0 to 6 years old, which aids primary care professionals to conduct routine developmental surveillance at well-child checkups, and determine if a child is at risk of developmental problems. The study aims to examine the effectiveness of the routine developmental surveillance process for identifying children at risk of developmental problems at 18-months-old. It explores the use of the HB checklists as a screening tool, and the use of overseas-developed parent-filled developmental screening tools in the Singapore context. A longitudinal within-subjects study design will be used. Children who are 18-months-old will be recruited from the primary care setting (Target N=1050). Parents will be asked to complete the HB checklists, two overseas-developed general developmental screening tools – ASQ and PEDS/PEDS:DM, and an autism-specific screening tool – M-CHAT-R/F, before their child’s well-child check-up. The children will go through usual care at well-child check-ups with primary care doctors and nurses, and data on the outcome of the check-up will be collected. Children who are identified as “at-risk” by usual care, HB checklists, ASQ, PEDS/PEDS:DM or M-CHAT-R/F, will be invited to complete standardized assessments for development and adaptive behaviour, within 1-3 months of the screening. At 30 months old, all children will be screened with the same tools, and children identified as “at-risk”, will be invited to complete the same standardized assessments. The detection rates of usual care, HB checklists, ASQ, PEDS/PEDS:DM, and the M-CHAT-R/F for children at risk of developmental problems or autism will be compared. The acceptability by parents for completing the parent-filled screening tools independently will be compared.
kw: Child Development; Screening; Surveillance; Developmental delay; Autism Spectrum Disorder

title: TO-ChERIsH: Trajectory of Cardiovascular Ageing, Its Determinants and Impact on Health
abs: Background: Cardiovascular (CV) ageing is a heterogeneous process that exhibits great variation with advancing age among individuals. Some individuals develop ageing-related deteriorations in CV structure and function resulting in CV disease (CVD) (unhealthy CV ageing) while others have relatively preserved CV health with chronological ageing (healthy CV ageing). Determinants of either CV ageing trajectories remain unknown. We hypothesize that investigations of CV ageing trajectories will unravel determinants of unhealthy and healthy CV ageing. Our hypothesis is based on data (2014-2017) from a community-based cohort of elderly individuals with CV imaging and bio-specimens that showed a spectrum of CV functions ranging from preserved to unhealthy measurements, that correlated with lifestyle (physical activity), systemic conditions (diabetes mellitus) and circulating metabolites (such as amino acids and acyl-carnitines). Traditional risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and physical activity, could not fully account for the extent of CV ageing observed. Specific Aims: (i) To determine rates of change in CV ageing over time via CV imaging markers; (ii) To assess if circulating metabolites markers present in archived blood samples (2000-2004) are associated with CV ageing 15 years later (2014-2017) and rates of CV ageing progression (2018-2021) and how these differences vary by gender, physical activity and diabetes mellitus; (iii) To determine impact of CV ageing on development of clinical CVD and overall physical, cognitive and functional health outcomes. Methodology: Participants from 2014-2017 will return in this proposal (2018-2021) for repeat biodata, CV imaging markers, and bio-specimen collection. Baseline and change in CV imaging and metabolite markers will be analysed from archived (2000-2004, 2014-2017) and fresh bio-specimens, adjusting for longitudinal covariates. Significance: Distinguishing trajectories of healthy versus unhealthy CV ageing will reveal determinants and impact of CV ageing. Targeting CV ageing may therefore improve burden of CVD and important ageing-related health outcomes among ageing populations.
kw: aging; cardiovascular

title: Therapeutic exploration of pro-oxidant and mitophagy-related strategies for Parkinson's disease with Asian-related LRRK2 risk variants
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Studies on Parkinson’s disease (PD) causative genes, including Parkin and LRRK2, and related factors, such as reactive oxygen species (ROS) provide invaluable clues for the understanding and treatment of the disease. Defective Parkin-dependent mitophagy is linked to the pathogenesis of PD, whereas boosting mitophagy may provide beneficial effect to PD patients. Our previous study demonstrates that ROS contribute to initiating mitophagy by recruiting Parkin translocation to mitochondria, and additionally drive mitophagy progression thereafter, suggesting ROS modulation as a potential therapeutic strategy for neurodegeneration. LRRK2 G2019S mutation, linked to PD in Caucasian population, causes mitochondrial abnormalities which may be attenuated by Parkin. We have identified that patients who carry the LRRK2 haplotype, constituting of S1647T, R1628P and G2385R variants, developed PD significantly earlier than non-carriers in Asia population. The LRRK2 haplotype may be utilized to establish the first Asian relevant PD model. The interaction between mitophagy and PD caused by this haplotype is a novel pursuit in the scientific community, providing substantial room for therapeutic discoveries. We hypothesize that mitophagy may provide beneficial effects on Asian-related PD. We aim to establish in vitro and in vivo PD models carrying Asian-related LRRK2 haplotype and study the effects of ROS on mitophagy and its related neurodegeneration in such models to test therapeutic potential of stimulating mitophagy in PD. The knowledge gained from patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), utilizing a wide range of research methods including confocal microscopy, flow cytometry and electronic microscopy, will be brought to in vivo models for pathological and behavioural study in attempt to identify potential drug compounds that may interfere with the pathophysiological events implicated in PD. Together, our study outcomes would clarify the role of ROS-mitophagy axis in the pathogenesis of PD and yield potential chemical candidates to halt or slow PD progression in a local setting.
kw: Parkinson's disease; LRRK2; risk variants; mitophagy; pro-oxidant

title: Mild Behavioral Impairment: Structural-Connectivity Patterns and Influence on Cognition in amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) are common in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and are associated with poorer cognitive outcomes. Mild behavioural impairment (MBI) is a diagnostic construct which identifies individuals with persistent late-life NPS (≥6 months) and there is an emerging conceptual framework which support MBI as an early non-cognitive manifestation of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the prevalence of MBI and its pathophysiology and influence on cognition in MCI remains unclear. MBI could potentially be used to identify pre-dementia patients who are at risk for AD. In a cross-sectional cohort, we will study the local prevalence and characteristics of MBI among MCI (amnestic and non-amnestic) patients seen consecutively in our memory clinic over 1-year. All subjects will undergo neuropsychological assessments (NPA) at baseline and 6-month time points for the diagnosis of MBI. In a prospective longitudinal cohort, we will study the pathophysiology of MBI and its influence on cognition over 1-year in only amnestic MCI (aMCI) subjects. 150 aMCI subjects (75 with MBI (aMCI+MBI), 75 without MBI (aMCI-MBI)) with structural and resting-state functional-MRI within a 6-month window will be recruited from 3 ongoing studies. We will enrich this cohort with 40 aMCI subjects with known cerebrospinal fluid amyloid (CSF Aβ1-42). All subjects will undergo NPA at baseline and 1-year follow-up. We hypothesize that MBI is prevalent among MCI subjects locally, aMCI+MBI subjects have greater grey matter atrophy and functional disconnectivity in limbic and AD-related regions and lower CSF Aβ1-42 at baseline and poorer cognitive performances at 1-year follow-up, compared to aMCI-MBI. Our study findings will support MBI as an early manifestation of AD. The characterization of behavioural and cognitive profiles of MBI and its role in determining cognitive decline will enable prompt detection of aMCI+MBI patients and timely targeted cognitive behavioural interventions to improve NPS, quality of life and stabilize cognitive decline.
kw: Alzheimer’s disease; Mild behavioral impairment; Neuropsychiatric symptoms; Mild cognitive impairment; Magnetic resonance imaging; Functional connectivity

title: Mesenchymal stem cell exosomes in combination with hyaluronic acid for treatment of knee osteoarthritis in rabbits
abs: Osteoarthritis (OA) has a heavy global socioeconomic impact on both personal and societal levels, with rates expected to rise in the coming decades in tandem with an aging population. Currently, there is no effective treatment for OA, and joint replacement surgery is the end-stage surgical option. The limited longevity of current prostheses however, generally limits its use to patients above 50 years old. Cell-based therapies utilizing mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have obtained promising results, but still require cell isolation and as a result lack off-the-shelf availability. Increasingly, the therapeutic efficacy of MSCs has been attributed to the secretion of extracellular vesicles, particularly the exosomes. In our prior work, we showed that weekly intraarticular injections of human MSC exosomes effectively repair the osteochondral defects and alleviate pain and degeneration in immunocompetent rat models of osteochondral defect and surgically-induced OA models respectively. To circumvent the need for multiple injections for better clinical translation and to further improve the therapeutic efficacy of MSC exosomes, we aim to develop a combination therapy based on MSC exosomes and clinically used hyaluronic acid (HA) carrier that could be injected in a minimally-invasive manner in a single-stage procedure. Given that HA is commonly used as viscosupplementation and carriers for cells, we hypothesise that an exosome-HA combination therapy would be able to exert synergistic anti-inflammatory and regenerative effects to attenuate OA progression and promote cartilage regeneration. In this proposed study, we aim 1) to investigate the combined effects of MSC exosomes and HA on chondrocytes in vitro; and 2) to evaluate the in vivo therapeutic efficacy of exosome-HA combination therapy in an immunocompetent rabbit model of knee OA. Our long-term goal is to develop human MSC exosomes as a safe, off-the-shelf and patient-friendly therapy for OA treatment in patients.
kw: Exosomes, osteoarthritis, treatment, cartilage regeneration

title: To decipher the molecular mechanisms regulating Protein Regulator of Cytokinesis 1 (PRC1) protein and Wnt signaling to tackle early recurrent human hepatocellular carcinoma
abs: Partial liver resection of HCC commonly leads to disease recurrence and the pathophysiology of this is only poorly understood. Our present project aims to investigate the role of PRC1 and WNT signaling components in early recurrent disease. Our Aims 1 and 2 related to deciphering the molecular interactions between PRC1 (Protein regulator of cytokinesis 1) and the canonical Wnt pathway in promoting early HCC recurrence and to validate the clinical value of the expression of WRRAGs (Wnt-regulated recurrence-associated genes) and PRC1 in the primary HCC tumor tissues for predicting the risk of early recurrence. Although HCC is a major medical burden, treatment options are still limited. The proposed Aim 3 in this study to identify and characterize potential novel small molecule inhibitors of PRC1 using genetically engineered PRC1-expressing yeast strains as a rapid and efficient screening system aims to provide novel systemic targeted therapies for HCC. Our proposal will lead to an overall better understanding of the molecular mechanisms leading to HCC recurrence after surgery, its easy detection and alternate treatment options. The proposal therefore has the potential to lead to enhanced survival in patients with resectable HCC and those with recurrent HCC after resection.
kw: PRC1, WRRAGs expression, Wnt/β-catenin, SILAC analysis, interactome, hepatocellular carcinoma

title: Role of T-cells in the pathogenesis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS): Identification of a unique immunologic signature
abs: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), the most common glomerulopathy resulting in end stage kidney failure in children, is a heterogeneous disease. Current protocols tend to treat FSGS as a single entity, and this may explain the lack of response to treatment with subsequent progression of the disease. We have recently reported a subgroup of FSGS patients with a specific immunological profile of T-cell exhaustion which could account for their favourable response to rituximab (anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody) therapy. This was further supported by significant downregulation of CD8 memory T-cells in FSGS patients with steroid dependent nephrotic syndrome (SDNS) compared to minimal change disease (MCD) and healthy controls. Moreover, our preliminary results showed higher expression of CXCR5 T follicular helper (Tfh) cells in FSGS compared to MCD and controls. We therefore hypothesized that T-cell activation plays a role in the pathogenesis of immune-mediated FSGS associated with increased expression of CXCR5 Tfh-cells and subsequent T-cell exhaustion, characterized by decreased expression of memory T-cells and downregulation of stimulated CD154 and IFNγ. Activation of T-cells could produce circulating metabolites that increase podocyte permeability and hence proteinuria. The primary aim of this study is to elucidate the T-cell events of this immune-mediated subset of FSGS patients by firstly, investigating the nature of the dysregulated T-cell activation, and in particular the co-stimulatory pathways involved in upregulation of CXCR5 by analysis of upstream transcription factors, cytokine profile, and T-cell subsets. The secondary aim is to identify the circulating metabolites with subsequent in-vitro validation using albumin permeability assay and podocyte injury assay. Delineating the immunological mechanism underpinning this difficult disease in this subgroup of FSGS patients will allow us to stratify the patients according to their specific immunological signature and the corresponding treatment regimes.
kw: T-cell activation; Primary nephrotic syndrome; Circulating metabolites

title: The IFIT Family in Breast Cancer: Evaluation of Expression Patterns, Functional Roles and Potential Use as Prognostic Indicators
abs: Breast carcinoma is the commonest cancer in women worldwide, and a leading cause of malignancy-related deaths. In Singapore, its incidence has tripled over the past 40 years, while its mortality rate has remained relatively unchanged for the past 25 years. This underlines the importance of a deeper understanding of breast cancer, and to discover better markers for patient prognostication. The interferon induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats (IFIT) family consists of four members. Previous studies have mainly focussed on their roles in immune response to viral infections. In our preliminary experiments, we found that silencing IFIT1 or IFIT3 in human breast cancer cells decreased tumour cell migration and invasion through Matrigel. Further, elevated IFIT1 or IFIT3 in breast cancer tissue was associated with reduced patient survival and increased risk of tumour recurrence. Contrastingly, knocking down IFIT5 increased the migratory and invasive characteristics of breast cancer cells. Thus, this project aims to determine the differential biological roles of IFITs in breast cancer, identify candidate downstream signalling mechanisms, and evaluate the potential use of IFITs as prognostic indicators in breast cancer patient survival and disease relapse. Knockdown/knockout and overexpression of IFIT members will be performed to investigate their functional roles in vitro using human breast carcinoma cells and in vivo using a SCID mouse model. Transcriptomic and proteomic studies will be performed using microarrays and mass spectrometry analyses to identify candidate downstream pathways, which will then be selected for experimental verification. Expression of IFITs in breast cancer tissue samples will be examined and analysed for associations with clinicopathological features. Survival analysis will evaluate the potential use of IFITs to predict patient survival and breast cancer recurrence. Together, the study will deepen our knowledge on IFITs in breast cancer as well as assess the potential use of IFITs in prognostication for breast cancer patients.
kw: Breast cancer; IFIT1; IFIT2; IFIT3; IFIT5; prognostic markers

title: Novel therapeutic interventions to target GATA4-related pathways in hepatocellular carcinoma
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third commonest cause of cancer mortality worldwide. In 2007, the multi-targeting tyrosine kinase inhibitor sorafenib became the first FDA-approved systemic therapy for advanced HCC with modest overall survival (OS) benefit. This year (2017), regorefenib was reported to improve OS in sorafenib-treated advanced HCC. All other drugs tested have failed to improve on survival results in the past 10 years. HCC is partly caused by impaired terminal differentiation of hepatocyte in liver. We have identified a highly deleted candidate tumour suppressor gene GATA4 in HCC (68% deletion in TCGA and 44% in Singapore cohort), making GATA4 deletion more frequent than TP53 deletion and mutations. By time-of-flight cytometry (CyTOF), we confirmed an immunosuppressive microenvironment in GATA4-deficient HCC, including an abundance of CD4+ Foxp3+ Treg, M2-like macrophages, and exhausted CD8+ T cell. Our functional studies showed that GATA4 overexpression significantly downregulated CCL20 expression, normally highly upregulated in HCC. Tumoural GATA4 expression is also positively correlated with CEBPA and HNF4A. Functional analyses including CRISPR-mediated knockout prove that GATA4 acts upstream of CEBPA and HNF4A. We aim to 1) develop a novel spontaneous GATA4-deficiency HCC models and humanised HCC models to recapitulate GATA4-deficiency in human HCC, 2) test the combination of anti-CCL20 antibody and immune checkpoint inhibitors in the novel preclinical GATA4-deficient mouse models, followed by the mechanistic studies and biomarker studies of treatment responses, 3) testing the efficacy and investigate potential biomarkers and therapeutic outcome of MTL-CEBPA and MTLHNF4A alone and in combination with checkpoint inhibitors in in vitro and novel in vivo models. Our key strategy is to elucidate mechanistic interactions in GATA4-deficient HCC within the ‘seed’ and with the ‘soil’ and how to therapeutically intervene to retard HCC oncogenesis by targeting the HCC or its microenvironment but likely by combination synergistic targeting of both.
kw: hepatocellular carcinoma; humanized mouse model; tumour microenvironment; immunotherapy; therapeutic antibody; RNA drug

title: A Prospective Study to develop a Genomics-Immunomics-Phenomics Platform for Precision Medicine in HCC
abs: Tumor heterogeneity (both inter- and intra-tumor heterogeneity) is important for tumor evolution, disease progression, and treatment response. Previous unsupported assumptions of intra-tumor homogeneity have hindered the development of efficacious systemic therapeutics for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In our recently published study, we confirmed that significant intra-tumor heterogeneity is found in HCC. Such heterogeneity may be elucidated at the level of genome/epigenome/transcriptome, as well as at the metabolome and clinical phenotype levels, where interaction between the genes and the environment is played out. We hypothesize that an integration of genomic heterogeneity with multiple downstream layers/datasets (e.g. epigenetics, transcriptomic, immunomics, metabolomics and clinical phenotypes) will allow a more coherent understanding of molecular pathways, tumor evolution and disease progression. Additional insights can be expected if such vertical integration is carried out in the context of a prospective study that follows the clinical trajectory of the disease, thus allowing for longitudinal integration of datasets as well, and mitigating the significant impact of inter-patient variability. To achieve this, we propose to leverage on the current NMRC TCR Flagship Program in Liver Cancer, which is a multi-center prospective genomic-immunomic study that follows a surgical cohort of patients from resection of HCC to cancer recurrence. From this program, sequential tissue and humoral samples will be collected for targeted and untargeted serum, urine and tissue metabolomics. In addition, mass spectrometry imaging will also be performed on tissue sections to quantify micron-scale metabolic heterogeneity. This proposal adds metabolomics to the program, as this will give information closer to the tissue phenotype. A systems-based approach will be applied to integrate metabolomics data with the other datasets in order to identify critical pathways in HCC and to discover metabolic biomarkers that are predictive of disease outcomes.
kw: Hepatocellular carcinoma, immunomics, metabolomics, genomics

title: Simultaneous profiling of circulating tumor cells and tumor in relation to immunotherapeutic response in cancer
abs: Immune checkpoint inhibitors are promising in cancer patients but responses are difficult to predict. Tumor re-biopsies are limited by tissue and access issues. Peripheral blood immunophenotyping is limited to only peripheral immune cells (PIC) given the paucity of circulating tumour cells (CTC). This proposal seeks to integrate analysis of CTC and tumor to predict outcomes from immunotherapy treatment underpinned by a clinical study: CTC-IMMUNITY. Specific Aim 1: Simultaneous Profiling of PIC, CTC and CTC clusters in relation to Response and Prognosis. Using label free enrichment methods for CTC from blood, we hypothesize that the relative expression of cancer and immunologic proteins in CTC, CTC clusters and PICs can be profiled, and are relevant to clinical outcomes. In patients undergoing immunotherapy, blood samples will be enriched for CTCs, CTC clusters and PICs and subjected to RNA expression analysis. Differential RNA expression from each component and relevant relationships will be assessed in relation to data from CTC-IMMUNITY (immunotherapy response). Specific Aim 2: Assessment of Germline Polymorphisms that Contribute to Immunotherapy Resistance and Prognosis. Germline polymorphisms have been described to contribute to drug resistance. We hypothesize that germline polymorphisms contribute to immunotherapeutic resistance as well. From the same blood draw for CTC enrichment during PDL-1/PD1 therapy, we will also extract germline DNA to sequence for BIM del polymorphism and polymorphic variants of PDL-1/PD-1 that may contribute to resistance. This will be correlated to tumor response to PDL-1/PD-1 inhibitors treatment in CTC-IMMUNITY. The 2 studies above will build on the prior CSA that has successfully contributed to bringing to market a local CTC isolation platform. They will allow the testing of additional applications for the CTC platform and the development of novel CTC assays for cancer applications. This effort will leverage on Singapore’s strengths in medical engineering and biology.
kw: Circulating tumor cells; circulating biomarkers; cancer; immunotherapy

title: Deciphering the tumor microenvironment of primary TKI resistant EGFR mutant NSCLC
abs: Extending the observations on genomic determinants of primary resistance to EGFR TKI (Lai et al JCO 2019; Tan A WCLC 2019), this proposal aims to further characterise immune microenvironment of both naive and TKI resistant EGFR mutant NSCLC specifically to facilitate the design of rational combinations of immune modulators. Emerging clinical data suggest a need for angiogenic approaches in combination with platinum based chemotherapy and checkpoint blockade (IMpower150, Mok et al Lancet Resp Med 2019). Our preliminary RNA-seq data of EGFR TKI resistant samples suggests subsets of "inflammed" EGFR M+ tumors that are associated with shorter time to progression on TKI. In silico dissection of immune subsets further delineates myeloid derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) so a predominant cell population. In this proposal, we aim to apply state of the art immuno-monitoring (cyTOF or symphony flow cytometry) on primary resistant tumors, extend the transcriptomic and genomic datasets, through designing a clinical protocol to systemically interrogate biospecimens of EGFR mutant NSCLC undergoing immunotherapy and combinations thereof. There are ongoing discussions with industry partners (Pfizer, AZ, MSD) to design a proof of concept phase I/Ib trial specifically to address this major unmet need for lung cancer in Asia.
kw: TKI resistant; EGFR; NSCLC

title: Dissecting the role of long noncoding RNA product SGHRT and targeting it for heart failure
abs: Cardiac regeneration involving limited proliferation of pre-existing cardiomyocytes (CMs) holds the promise for novel and game-changing therapeutic strategies for heart disease. While current therapy only delays disease progression, regenerative therapy promises instead to reverse the course of disease. In neonatal mouse CMs that retain their proliferative potential, there is effective regeneration and repair response to injury up to post-natal D7. Much still remains to be discovered for the regulation of dedifferentiation and proliferation of post-natal adult CMs. We previously performed single RNA-seq in failing and non-failing adult CMs and identified lincRNA Sghrt as a nodal gene within co-regulatory gene networks. Sghrt knockdown increased marker expression of dedifferentiation and cell cycle entry in post-natal CMs in vitro. Similarly, Sghrt knockdown increased dedifferentiation markers in neonatal mouse CMs in vivo; and Sghrt knockdown improved cardiac function in an adult mouse model of disease, together with evidence of CM dedifferentiation. In human ES-derived CMs, we now find that SGHRT deletion also results increased CM dedifferentiation. Together, these results point to a role for SGHRT in regulating CM dedifferentiation. Here, we aim to further characterize the role of mouse Sghrt in CM dedifferentiation and proliferation using (a) a conditional knockout and (b) a humanized mouse models that we have now generated. In assessing their response to myocardial stress by pressure-overload and myocardial infraction, we aim to determine the therapeutic value of targeting SGHRT in human cardiac diseases. Furthermore, we will characterize the role of human SGHRT in hES-derived cardiomyocytes and Engineering Heart Tissue (EHT) in response to oxidative stress. Finally, we aim to dissect the mechanism of SGHRT as a novel mitochondrial micropeptide in the regulation of cardiomyocyte dedifferentiation. Understanding the biology of how SGHRT regulates CM dedifferentiation and proliferation will allow us to develop a rationale approach to target SGHRT for human HF.
kw: Heart Failure, Epigenetics, Regeneration, Repair, Long noncoding RNA

title: A new model for glaucoma screening and management of stable glaucoma patients in the community in Singapore– learning from experience in the UK.
abs: Aims: To improve on our current existing glaucoma screening and community eye care models by analyzing the Cambridge models and incorporating Artifical Intelligence (AI) and innovative tools. Hypothesis We can improve on our current models and community glaucoma screening with better protocols, allied health training and upskilling, as well as the use of Artifical Intelligence (AI) and innovative tools such as automated anterior segment imaging, optical coherence tomography and fundus photography in the community. Methodology and approach Study the Cambridge Community Optometry Glaucoma Service (COGS), community and hospital allied network glaucoma evaluation scheme (CHANGES) and Glaucoma Automated Tests Evaluation (GATE) models, analyze their pros and cons and learn from their experiences. Aside from exploring the COGS and CHANGES models in the UK, we will be conducting a research study on the accuracy afforded by Optical coherence tomography (OCT RNFL) utilized for screening and referral refinement in Cambridge. We will critically evaluate our current protocols and improve on them based on the UK experience and incorporate the use of innovative Artificial Intelligence tools and automated devices developed in Singapore Eye Research Institute (SERI) to aid our current protocols. Devices include: automated optical coherence tomography (OCT), portable anterior segment imaging (anterior chamber depth estimation), fundus photography with fundus camera and risk profiling of these images using deep learning. We are developing a new AI algorithm to detect glaucoma from automated fundus photographs and optical coherence tomography in Singapore Eye Research Institute, as well as our own automated OCT and portable anterior segment imaging. Outcome measures to be evaluated in Cambridge and Singapore: Accuracy of OCT as a screening and referral refinement tool, patient satisfaction, Doctors and patient acceptability

title: Collaborative Solutions Targeting Antimicrobial Resistance Threats in Health Systems (CoSTAR-HS)
abs: The Collaborative Solutions Targeting Antimicrobial Resistance Threats in Health Systems (CoSTAR-HS) programme was initiated on 1st April 2017 after successfully clinching an NMRC Collaborative Centre Grant award (NMRC/CGAug16C005). The initial founding institutions were the Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health (SSHSPH) and National University Hospital (NUH) under the National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore General Hospital (SGH), and the Communicable Diseases Centre currently the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID). The new partner institution for this renewal is the National University Polyclinics (NUP) a key partner for much needed research on AMR in primary care. Major individual institutional research accomplishments are listed in this section, while collaborative accomplishments which are naturally greater are listed in the following section. CoSTAR-HS represents a complementary collaborative framework and programme bringing together distinct and overlapping research and organizational competencies in NUHS, SGH and NCID. Besides enhancing research infrastructure and capacity within the individual partnering institutions, investigators within CoSTAR-HS have also leveraged on this large-scale programme to secure further competitive and/or programmatic funding, organize larger clinical and laboratory-based studies as well as more nuanced health systems and implementation science-type studies, many of which are currently still underway.

title: Singapore COVID-19 Vaccination in Children (SGCoVaC)
abs: There is an urgent need for data on vaccines in children to ensure maximum clinical and public health benefits while minimizing the risk of side-effects. The emergence of variants requires more data to better understand the potential utility of boosters and/or multivalent COVID-19 vaccines in children. The proposal aims to study COVID-19 vaccination and boosters in children. It will assess adult or paediatric dose BNT162b2 (Pfizer–BioNTech/Comirnaty®) vaccine dilution protocol for children, evaluate immune responses at 2 months after one dose BNT162b2 vaccination in children and investigate the utility of alternate dosing schedule in children. In addition, it will also assess COVID-19 vaccination in immunocompromised high risk vulnerable children. Five cohorts will be recruited. First cohort will be composed of healthy children who will be given BNT162b2 as per standard schedule (two doses 3 weeks apart). Second cohort will be composed of healthy children who will receive the COVID-19 vaccine using a delayed schedule (two doses 2 months apart). The third cohort will be composed of immunocompromised children who will receive COVID-19 vaccine as per national recommendation. The fourth cohort will compose of healthy children 6m to 4y who will receive COVID-19 vaccines as per national recommendation. The fifth cohort will compose of children 6m to 18y who will receive COVID-19 booster(s) as per national recommendations. Safety and immunogenicity data will be collated over 9 to 15 month follow up. The proposal will generate paediatric COVID-19 vaccine data to inform the public health risk benefit of alternate dosing schedules and booster(s) in children. Finally, it will provide important immune response data of COVID-19 vaccination in immunocompromised children and the need for future boosters to ensure better protection for children at high risk of severe disease.
kw: COVID-19, Public Health, Vaccination, Children

title: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for next generation wireless communications
abs: In the recent period, a brand-new technology was brought to the attention of the wireless research community - the “Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces” (RIS). Following the recent breakthrough on the fabrication of programmable metamaterials, reconfigurable intelligent meta-surfaces have the potential to materialize the intelligent software-based control of the environment in wireless communication systems, when coated on the otherwise passive surfaces of various objects. In this project, we investigate three important aspect of RIS, first we will develop statistical channel models and signal models that capture the inherent characteristic of transmission environment with RISs. With these proposed models, we will be able to perform tractable channel characterization, and transparent interpretation to the effects of scattering and array characteristics on channel capacity and diversity. Next, we will design practical algorithm and verify our hypothesis that RIS-based systems can provide up to 300% higher energy efficiency, and 100% higher throughput than currently deployed massive antenna systems. Moreover, we will also demonstrate that by increasing the number of RIS reflecting elements, a RIS-based system can achieve performance comparable to the fundamental theoretical limits from the theoretical and optimization perspective. Finally, we will also investigate a network scenario where there are multiple RISs and multiple users distributed across the network. Moreover, advanced AI techniques will be employed in the development of these algorithms to overcome large-scale optimization problem. Our research will bring RIS on step closer to reality, for RIS being a brand-new and transformative technology that has the potential of fundamentally changing how wireless networks are implemented and optimized today, this project will transform the future landscape of wireless communications.
kw: Reconfigurable intelligent surface, intelligence reflecting surface, holographic MIMO surface.

title: Robust Design of Institutions: An Implementation Theory Approach
abs: This proposal focusses on the interaction among agents that occurs within the framework of an institution. In particular, we assume that a central authority (a planner) has the power to commit to an institution, that is, to a specific set of rules that govern what actions agents may take, and what the consequences of these actions are. Having committed to an institution, the planner however cannot dictate the outcomes that result, since outcomes are determined by the actions agents take and these cannot be a priori controlled. For an institution to deliver socially desirable outcomes, the design of the institution has to provide the agents with the right incentives. A natural way to ensure the correct incentive structure is to approach the design problem from the perspective of implementation theory, which treats an institution as a mechanism specifying action sets to agents, and maps each profile of actions chosen by the agents to a specific outcome. The theory of implementation attempts to answer two questions. First, can one design a mechanism that successfully structures the interactions of agents in such a way that, in each state of the world, they always choose actions which result in the socially desirable outcomes for that state? Second, if agents possess information about the state and interact through a given mechanism, what properties do the resulting outcomes, viewed as a map from states to outcomes (and called social choice correspondences), possess? In answering these, the consequences of a given mechanism are predicted through the application of game theoretic solution concepts. Game theoretic solution concepts prescribe how rational agents behave in a strategic situation and draw upon two aspects of rationality to varying degrees. These are (i) agents play best responses to their beliefs, and (ii) that those beliefs are correct, the so-called rational expectations assumption. The most standard solution concept used in implementation theory is Nash equilibrium. This is called Nash implementation. Nash equilibrium captures both aforementioned aspects of rationality. If one drops the latter requirement ((ii) above) and retains only the former ((i) above), one moves into the realm of rationalizability, which only asks what are the strategic implications that come solely from common knowledge of rationality. Due to the restrictiveness of the rational expectations assumption, rationalizability is substantially weaker than Nash equilibrium, and is therefore a more robust solution concept as it demands less coordination among agents. We thus investigate the conditions for implementation in rationalizable strategies, which is far less exploited than Nash implementation. Although the theory of implementation has been quite successful in identifying the social choice correspondences which can be implemented by some institution, it has also been criticized. title: CSK-NLP: Leveraging Commonsense Knowledge for NLP
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: Commonsense is essential in our daily lives. For instance, one sees a cloudy sky and may decide to carry an umbrella, foreseeing potential rain. Such knowledge and reasoning are often taken for granted by humans, thus, its importance overlooked. As yet, however, few works have taken advantage of commonsense knowledge and reasoning. Therefore, we plan to imbue existing language models, like BERT, GPT, with commonsense knowledge using task-specific and/or commonsense knowledge-based fine-tuning. We surmise such an approach would have a widespread performance boost across myriad of NLP tasks, such as dialogue generation, natural language inference, and more, where commonsense knowledge and reasoning may supplement the domain knowledge often missing in training data.
