title: Supply Chain (SC) 4.0 – Digital Supply Chain Development via Platform Technologies
abs: The program consists of implementable projects with immediate benefit to Singapore’s supply chain landscape. The post-COVID world will see digital technologies playing a critical enabling role in delivering improvements for more resilient supply chains and the proposed program is set to assist and accelerate the transition journey for supply chain players and eventually fully prepare Singapore for further unprecedented supply chain challenges. There are three work packages and seven projects under this program with the following technical deliverables. • WP1: Federated microservice-based supply chain collaborative platform will be developed and deployed on the Cloud which enables manufacturing to achieve supply chain business excellence via connecting transactional real time shop floor data from upstream and downstream partners, as well as multi-sided B2B collaborative planning. Data governance factors and mechanisms for complex, federated and secured digital platform ecosystem are also designed to instil digital trust into the collaborative platform. The trust will be further enforced through a game-theoretic framework and dynamic watermarking for authentication and onboarding for IoT devices in a connected supply chain network. • WP2: On top of federated microservice-based supply chain collaborative platform, value-added business functions would be built to demonstrate the supply chain collaborative planning. A supply network analysis and optimization toolkit software which will allow identification of key bottlenecks, resource scheduling, route, and productivity optimization of assets. This will ensure that FMCG and pharmaceutical supply chains are responsive and resilient to unforeseen changes in the market. On top of this software, a methodology and software to interpret order queries in natural language and response using an Advanced Available-to-Promise process, to enable automatic translation of natural language queries into machine-formatted orders and facilitate the automation of the order management process. Furthermore, to incorporate both historical data and external environment data for better demand forecasting, automated feature engineering toolkits will be developed to analyze the big data captured in all nodes of a supply chain and for accurate prediction enabling smooth production planning, scheduling and stable production. • WP3: Brownfield warehouse automation and digitalization solutions including automated vanning/devanning prototypes with computer vision and motion planning algorithms for flexible and automated operations, and integrated software algorithms for optimal robot path planning taking into account the whole active fleet and energy considerations enable sustainable operations.

title: Neutrophils and Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Formation in Lupus Nephritis
abs: Renal involvement is common in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Neutrophils are increasingly recognized to play a role in lupus nephritis immunopathogenesis. Neutrophils can undergo an active cell death program known as NETosis. Accumulating evidence, from classical pathological analysis to our recent preliminary data suggest that neutrophils, particularly low-density neutrophils (LDNs), contribute to lupus nephritis through increased propensity to undergo NETosis. The Principal Investigator has found that the increased frequency of LDNs in SLE is associated with disease activity. The most striking characteristic of LDNs is that they are predominantly platelet-bound and this is attributed to Toll-like receptor 7, for which expression is upregulated in LDNs. Based on these findings, we described the neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR), calculated from the full blood count, that is a novel surrogate for LDNs. NPR was associated with past and current flares of lupus nephritis in a cohort of 250 SLE patients. To more clearly define if neutrophils, low-density state and NETosis are associated with the class and activity of lupus nephritis, we will perform multiplex immunohistochemical and messenger RNA analysis of kidney biopsy tissue from SLE patients with lupus nephritis. Through this study, we will examine if LDNs and NETosis in the kidney and blood are good prognostic markers of lupus nephritis.

title: Healthy living through personalized monitoring of eyelid care
abs: Specific aim: To assess acceptance and convenience of a method of monitoring eyelid warming for meibomian gland dysfunction. Methodology: To prospectively evaluate the prototype that sends off a signal to a digital database/calendar with each use of eyelid warming in dry eye patients from Singapore National Eye Center. This is a device that is linked to a commercially available USB-Eyemask. Approach: This is highly feasible since we have a working prototype. Impact: This will allow more people with dry eye to be treated in the community, and when this is linked to incentives, will promote preventive medicine. This thereby reduces unnecessary referrals to tertiary or specialised centres.

title: Enhancing cognitive reserve in the community: Exploring the effects of Sensory Environment and Playfulness on Depression and Cognition (SEPDC) among older adults
abs: Sensory and cognitive declines that advance with ageing negatively affect almost all aspects of the older adults’ daily functioning. This interdisciplinary study employs an original framework informed by the novel theoretical constructs in occupational therapy and environmental gerontology to investigate the effects of Sensory Environment and Playfulness on Depression and Cognition (SEPDC) among older adults, and their capacity to enhance cognitive reserve in the community. The hypothesis is that sensory environment and playfulness have indirect effects on cognition through depression. Moreover, the sensory environment can moderate the effect of playfulness on brain health. Following NIH Stages for theory-based intervention development, this study employs quantitative survey and path analysis to examine direct and indirect effects of exposure (sensory environment, playfulness) on outcome variables (self-rated memory, cognition) through intermediates (depression, loneliness) (NIH Stage 0). The study provides a proof of concept on the hypothesized psychosocial pathways to brain health, focusing on 20 public housing neighbourhoods in Singapore. Establishing the empirical validity of these theoretical pathways in the population will identify the relevant focal variable(s) for intervention development. This would be done in two phases. Phase 1 comprises nested cross-sectional survey design with random assignment of standardized cognitive testing (N=400-500 participants). Phase 2 collects biospecimens and eye-tracking data from n=20 participants from all 20 neighborhoods to verify aggregated survey data. Participants will be matched for similar outcome variables and demographics across all neighbourhoods. Saliva samples will be collected to measure interleukin levels (indicators of physiological stress). Eye-tracking data (gaze, pupil dilation, blink rate, fixations) will be collected on short walks in community for comparison with subjective measures of sensory environment. If our hypotheses are supported, subsequent phases of the study will develop and pilot interventions focused on the interactions between sensory environment and play using implementation science (NIH Stages I, III & V).
kw: sensory environment; playfulness; depression; cognition; ageing-friendly neighbourhoods

title: Identification of microRNA biomarkers in women predictive of reproductive senescence and longevity
abs: Assisted reproductive techniques success rate hovers at around 30–40% and rapidly drops with increasing maternal age due to the inevitable decrease in oocyte numbers and quality. Yet effective therapeutics to combat reproductive ageing in woman is sorely lacking. The tools to predict a woman’s reproductive success and longevity remain very limited. In current clinical practice, this is only determined by her age and one serum ovarian reserve marker, Anti-mullerian hormone (AMH), which is far from ideal. We thus hypothesise that miRNAs can be accurately quantified in follicular fluid and cumulus/granulosa cells, and we have preliminary data that demonstrated the feasibility of isolating and quantifying miRNAs from embryo culture media. This raises the attractive possibility that miRNA expression in these biomaterials—which would otherwise be discarded during ART procedures—could identify unique markers specific for ovarian senescence. These molecular footprints coupled with the woman’s demographic characteristics can be used together to build a framework, via machine learning, that will provide predictive power to infer true ovarian age and oocyte quality that will inform accurately on reproductive lifespan and health-span. We aim to 1) identify reproductive longevity miRNA biomarkers in follicular fluid, cumulus/granulosa cells and plasma, and 2) derive a framework via machine learning that can predict ovarian senescence using the miRNA expression profiles and clinical data obtained. We can use the presence of these stable miRNAs in follicular fluid and cumulus/granulosa cells to assess oocyte health and ovarian senescence in a non-invasive manner. The miRNA expression profiles will also gave us molecular insights into the effects of reproductive ageing and serve as a springboard for future mechanistic studies to study ovarian senescence and discover novel ovarian senolytics for reproductive longevity and health.
kw: Reproductive senescence; reproductive longevity; miRNA

title: Novel AI-driven ageing biomarker based on retinal photos for mortality risk stratification
abs: Globally, the number of persons aged 80 years or over is projected to increase more than threefold between 2017 and 2050. This aging population is likely to result in an increased burden of cardiovascular and chronic diseases with significant healthcare associated costs. In this context, the early identification of individuals at risk of mortality due to these diseases would allow early health interventions such as lifestyle modifications or targeted treatments. However, to date there are few robust aging biomarkers adopted in clinical practice, mainly because the invasive, high-cost, or time-consuming nature of their measurements limit their values as clinically useful biomarkers. On the other hand, retinal photographs can be easily acquired by non-mydriatic retinal cameras. Using latest neural network architectures, we propose to apply deep learning (DL) on retinal photographs to predict biological age, which may better capture physiological changes associated with aging process, compared to chronological age. We hypothesize that biological age can be accurately predicted using DL algorithms based on retinal images, and this predicted biological age is able to stratify individuals’ mortality risk above and beyond chronological age. We will determine the associations between the DL-predicated biological age and all-cause, cardiovascular disease, and cancer-related mortality using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to adjust for chronological age and other major risk factors. We will use datasets for training and validating our DL algorithms from multiple sites, including Singapore, UK, US, Australia, Korea and China, totaling more than 500,000 retinal photographs. We aim to provide the evidence that a DL-predicted probability score derived from retinal photographs can well estimate individuals’ biological age and stratify mortality risk in populations.
kw: deep learning; biological age, biomarker, retina; mortality

title: Advocating CPAP for Taxi drivers to Improve Vigilance and Employability (ACTIVE)
abs:
As the upper age limit for taxi drivers in Singapore is being raised, there is an increasing number of elderly taxi drivers on the road. Ageing is a major risk factor for obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) ─ a leading cause of disrupted sleep and excessive daytime sleepiness. We advocate widespread treatment for taxi drivers with OSA. With better sleep quality and vigilance, road safety would not be compromised by having more elderly taxi drivers. This approach replaces punishment-based accident preventive measures with prevention.

ACTIVE (Advocating CPAP for Taxi drivers to Improve Vigilance and Employability) is an applied science project to improve the vigilance and blood pressure of taxi drivers by treating OSA. A total of 50 taxi drivers above the age of 60 will be recruited for an overnight sleep study. title: Development of miobiotics to maintain healthy ageing gut microbiota
abs: Intestinal microbiota plays a crucial role in the host’s ageing process. Commensal bacteria such as Clostridia and Bacteroidia generate fermentation products for intestinal epithelial cells, while gram-negative facultative anaerobes such as members of Proteobacteria could be detrimental to the host's health. Proteobacteria however uniformly increases as we age and lead to chronic low-level inflammation known as inflamm-ageing and age-associated pathologies in the elderly. To reduce the number of Proteobacteria and increase saccharolytic bacteria, various dietary approaches have been examined. Both prebiotics and probiotics have limited effects on proteobacteria composition; while antibiotics, although effective would kill other commensal bacteria and generates resistant strains. To overcome these limitations, we propose the use of “miobiotics”, a novel dietary constituent that selectively reduces proteobacteria in the gut of an ageing person. Proteobacteria has an energy-efficient pathway to incorporate nitrogen through ammonium when the ammonium levels are high, whereas other bacteria incorporate ammonium at the expense of ATP at low ammonium concentrations. The age-related reduction of kidney function leads to an increase in urea retention and gut ammonium which generate selection pressure that favours proteobacteria growth. α-ketoglutarate (AKG) is a metabolite that could aid in the incorporation of ammonium in most bacteria and thereby limiting the gut ammonium concentration below the threshold that could favours proteobacteria growth. AKG is a good miobiotic candidate as it is safe, and our preliminary isotope tracing data suggest that it reduces gut ammonium levels. Hence, we propose to examine the efficacy of AKG as a miobiotic candidate in lowering gut ammonium levels and thereby reducing the proteobacteria count and blood inflammatory markers in a preclinical setting. We also propose a tag-along clinical study that examines the effect of AKG in middle age human gut microbiota. These studies will generate critical preliminary data for miobiotics clinical trials in the elderly.

title: Targeting SPTLC3-generated d16:1 sphingolipids for healthspan extension
abs: Aging is a physiologic state that predisposes patients to age-related diseases, and is the single largest risk factor for diabetes, dementia, and cancer. Recent decades have uncovered molecular hallmarks of aging, but none have identified actionable processes that can be therapeutically addressed to improve healthspan. One of these hallmarks, dysregulation of metabolism and nutrient sensing, is an important component of age-related decline. We identified a metabolic process (regulation of sphingolipid chain length) associated with aging, diabetes, and dementia in humans, and have evidence that this pathway can be targeted to improve healthspan. This proposal will test the hypothesis that d16:1 sphingolipids, produced by the enzyme SPTLC3, attenuate chronic inflammation and reduce age-related diseases, such as diabetes and dementia. We will utilize a newly-generated knockout mouse model, coupled with state-of-the-art mass spectrometry technology, to determine the functional consequences of altering d16:1 sphingolipid content. Results from this study can be rapidly translated into positive health outcomes with the introduction of dietary modifications and development of supplements, followed by pharmacological approaches that target SPTCL3.

title: Gamified fitness for healthy living
abs: Sedentary lifestyle is a leading risk factor for non-communicable diseases and a major underlying cause for death, disease and disability. A key reason for the physical inactivity is owing to the lack of motivation to adhere to sustained workouts. To overcome this, we propose a gamified fitness programme using smart textiles to monitor joint range of motion and muscle kinematics. Our smart textile aims to leverage on digitizing body parameters for a more immersive workout experience. Particularly, our smart textile seeks to overcome the limitations of conventional gaming controls through these 2 means: (1) Our smart conformable e-textile enables hands-free gaming for enhanced experiences, and (2) Our technology provides sensing capabilities to directly measure muscle effort. Importantly, this unique product proposition will lead to higher user engagement and adoption. Ultimately, our hypothesis is to improve the population fitness by increasing the access and adherence to physical activity. We intend to validate our hypothesis by measuring the general fitness level, muscle strength and heart performance before and after the a month-long programme. Questionnaires will also be developed to determine the adherence rate to physical activity, and its perceived self-efficacy.

title: Community Based and Participant-led Initiatives to Increase Civic Engagement Among Older Adults
abs: This study validates asset-based approaches to interventions aimed at increasing the civic engagement of older adults living alone. Older adults living alone experience greater levels of loneliness and lower levels of well-being due to their lack of social connectedness. There is thus a need to develop sustainable and impactful interventions to increase their civic engagement. While existing programmes endeavour to do so, many assume that older adults should be passive consumers of initiatives and hence (1) do not leverage on the resources of older adults, and (2) deprive older adults of the agency to shape initiatives. Thus, such initiatives are not sustainable (relying on external resources) and do not sufficiently engage older adults in meaningful ways. A pilot study is hence proposed to assess an alternative, asset-based approach. Based on data and findings from the Singapore Life Panel®, the pilot tests two hypotheses: i. As social and civic engagement improves – in terms of participation but more importantly in terms of the co-curation and driving of such initiatives – the psycho-social well-being of older adults living alone improves. ii. Such improvements in well-being will be mediated by improvements in resilience, cognitive function, and social connectedness. A randomized controlled trial is proposed to assess the impact of a pilot intervention developed with these issues in mind. Two groups of 50 participants who live alone within the ages of 55-75 will be randomly selected from a particular neighbourhood, with one group forming the intervention group and the other the control group. The pilot involves providing the intervention group with the resources and infrastructure to develop and run community-based initiatives to increase civic engagement. Pre and post tests will be conducted to track psycho-social well-being and assess impact. Proof of concept will be achieved if improvements in well-being are observed among the intervention group.

title: Gamification in eHealth intervention to enhance learning and self-care management for post-stroke care
abs: Background: Gamification is the method of applying game elements to motivate people to be engaged in targeted behaviors. Despite its popularity, there is limited application of gamified electronic health (eHealth) intervention for stroke care to enhance learning and self-care management. With the aging population in many countries throughout the world including Singapore, there is increasing attention on healthy aging and healthy living. Thus, there is a need to explore novel approaches in eHealth to enhance learning and self-care management to promote healthy living among stroke survivors. Specific aims: • To develop and evaluate the efficacy of a gamified eHealth in improving knowledge and improve self-care behaviors of stroke survivors. • To explore the users’ perceptions, facilitators, and barriers to using gamified eHealth intervention. We hypothesize that: i. Stroke survivors who use the gamified eHealth for one month will have: a. improved knowledge about stroke care; b. improved self-efficacy; and c. improved self-care behaviors. ii. Informal caregivers who use the gamified eHealth for one month will have: a. improved knowledge about stroke care; and b. enhanced ability to help survivors perform self-care. Methodology: A mixed methods study design is proposed. The design thinking theory and theory of gamified learning are used as the underlying conceptual framework to explain the development and evaluation of the gamified eHealth intervention. A total of 30 eligible stroke survivor and caregiver dyads from a community hospital will be invited to use the intervention for one month. Quantitative data will be collected at baseline and at the time of hospital discharge. Semi-structured qualitative interviews will be conducted one month after hospital discharge. Additional user statistics will be collected to ascertain eHealth usage after hospital discharge. The findings of this study can provide useful insights to inform the use of technology in health education and self-care management during post-stroke rehabilitation.
kw: eHealth; gamification; stroke care; education; self-care management; rehabilitation

title:
Systematic identification and functional analysis of synergistic
small molecule combinations targeting aging
abs: Aging population dramatically growing worldwide. Aging remains the biggest risk factor for chronic diseases, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular and neurodegeneration. The prevalence of age-related pathologies late in life has a huge impact on life quality and health care costs. Despite the complexity of aging, recent research has shown that small molecules intervening in the aging processes can substantially increase the healthy lifespan of model organisms, including mammals. However, the clinical use of small molecules is limited due to their lower efficacy, toxicity and severe side effects. Thus, there is an urgent need for small molecules that have effective anti-aging activity but with minimal side effects. However, biological redundancies in complex biological networks of aging limit the efficacy of many single-target drugs therapies. Implementation of combination therapies that simultaneously target multiple aging processes may overcome many limitations of a single drug target and achieve more effective strategies to increase healthy longevity. We propose to identify the small molecules that synergistically target aging processes. We will develop a discovery-driven “Pair to Pool” (PTP) high-throughput method to identify the anti-aging synergistic small molecules. We will screen the small molecules in budding yeast chronological aging, which is the well-established model system for investigating the intervention of human post-mitotic cells aging. We will perform transcriptomics, metabolomics, proteomics and chemical genomics profiling to uncover the modulation of biological aging processes that lead to synergistic effects. We will integrate the functional profiling data that may contribute to discovering the uncharacterized genes and pathways involved in aging. We will proactively publicize the comprehensive functional data for future investigation or follow-on research. We will validate anti-aging synergistic combinations in human cell lines. Eventually, this project will identify effective synergistic combinations to improve the efficacy and reduce the undesirable side effects of chemotherapy to increase healthy longevity.
kw: Health Sciences, Aging Biology, Aging Interventions, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Genetics

title: A molecular prevention strategy for cancer-free ageing
abs: Cancer is a major disease that afflicts the aged, due to the accumulation of mutations over the life-time. This debilitating disease is on the rise and is expected to double by 2040, mainly affecting the ageing population. Advances in treatment modalities, in particular, the immune- and targeted-therapies, though having transformed cancer treatment, will be insufficient to counter the disease burden and to keep-up the quality-of-life of the cancer stricken ageing population. Revolutionary measures are therefore necessary to delay or even prevent the onset of cancers and to keep the population cancer-free as they age. We propose here an avant-garde molecular prevention approach to obviate cancer development, by enhancing our body’s tumor-suppressive mechanisms. This approach is based on two important observations: that elephants, which are highly cancer-resistant, express multiple copies of the master tumor suppressor gene p53; and that transgenic mice expressing an additional copy of p53 are highly resistant to carcinogen-induced cancers. We have therefore developed a compound mouse model in which a 3rd copy of p53 is inducible in adulthood, to mimic and evaluate a p53-prophylactic regimen. Continual p53 induction led to a significant delay in the development of E-Myc-induced lymphomas, without compromising normal physiology, providing genetic evidence that a p53-prophylactic strategy could be a way forward in our efforts to delay the development of cancers in the aging population. We have further established a method to produce p53 encapsulated in extracellular vesicles (EVs). These p53EVs are capable of transferring p53 into recipient cells and activate the endogenous p53 pathway. We propose here to i) expand on p53-prophylaxis in the human-relevant Li-Fraumeni model, and ii) evaluate the pharmacological properties of the p53EVs, as a preamble to embark on p53EV-based tumor prophylaxis in the future. Success will establish the concept of molecular cancer prophylaxis through mild p53 activation.

title: Laser spatiotemporal photoplethysmogram and computational method for extended chronic cardiometabolic therapeutic care
abs: Existing methods of managing chronic cardiovascular hypertension and diabetes mellitus (DM) involve obtrusive brachial sphygmomanometers and blood samples from finger pricks. These intrusive methods result in poor compliance due to inconvenient lifestyle interruptions and invasive daily blood sampling, leading to poor compliance and resurgence of preventable ailments in chronic sufferers. Our work in continuous and non-occluding Blood Pressure (BP) and Blood Glucose Level (BGL) estimation uses our developed Time-Differentiated Dual-point Photoplethysmogram (TD2PPG) and Diffuse Speckle Pulsatile Flowmetry (DSPF) signals to acquire non-invasive and non-occlusive pulsatile blood flow in ambulatory individuals. The team’s work in applying TD2PPG and DSPF proves good assessment of BP and BGL changes, however this novel modality has not yet been validated on ambulatory individuals. This goal is to develop a robust cardiometabolic monitoring Artificial Intelligence (AI) to achieve a cohesive therapeutic efficacy monitoring by integrating a new generation of advanced biooptical sensor modality, computational bioinformatics intelligence to diet/pharmaceutical compliance adherence. Specific aims: 1) Develop a novel biooptical sensor system by combining our TD2PPG and DSPF sensors into a new system – Laser Spatiotemporal Photoplethysmography (LSPPG). 2) BP/BGL correlation using the new LSPPG modality by training the against traditional BP and BGL meters. 3) Develop a framework for continuous BP and BGL correlation as a potential auxiliary measure to detect blood glucose variations, predict hypo/hyperglycemic events and Time-in-Range (TIR). 4) Implement our LSPPG/AI-ML modality on long-term ambulatory individuals for monitoring/tracking of therapeutic compliance and as a potential tool for improving efficacy in clinical interventions. Our proposed technology does not involve radial/brachial occlusion nor finger-prick blood sampling, and is thus unobtrusive to regular lifestyles, leading to improved compliance. Successful implementation of our proposed system could one day be used as a diagnostic and real-time monitoring aid to improve clinical outcomes and compliance of at-risk individuals.

title: AI and Healthy Ageing: Developing AI-based Computational Framework and Approaches to Define Healthy Ageing in the Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Study (SLAS) Cohort
inst: IHPC - Institute of High Performance Computing
abs: Lifespan extension has brought new challenges. The main issue is to tackle increasing numbers of elderly visiting healthcare institutions. We are greatly promoting ageing-in-place in Singapore as 70% of the older population is living in the community. Older adults are expected to prolong their healthspan and maintain the productivity. However, poor understanding of healthy ageing may plague efficient health program/service designs. We aim to develop AI-based computational framework and approaches to help formulate novel ways of defining healthy ageing in the Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Study (SLAS) Cohort. Our hypothesis is that healthy elderly will display specific determinants from non-healthy agers and that gradation of determinants will follow the progression of age-related conditions. Our consortium already possesses more than 10 years longitudinal samples from elderly Singaporean (n>3000; 55-94 years). The collection of clinical information and its follow-up data (nutritional, socio-economic, cognitive, physical, medical history, lifestyle, activities, medication, hospitalization, comorbidities, frailty, mortality) would allow the most stringent stratification of Asian elderly. The proposed idea is innovative. In contrast to traditional theory-based and hypotheses-driven approaches, the proposed AI-based framework and approaches define healthy ageing by using all available data in the cohort without any prior assumption. Traditionally we applied association or correlation and principal component and factor analyses, in contrast, the AI-based approaches will select markers and predict health outcomes in a train-test manner to formulate novel phenotypes of healthy ageing. It is transformative as it will (i) be more integrated to the general concept of healthy ageing (ii) produce a plethora of new links between functional systems and healthy ageing (iii) contribute to the well-being of the elderly (iv) unravel areas of healthy ageing that require the strongest research focus (v) provide reference for future healthy ageing program design.
kw: Healthy Ageing, AI, Machine Learning, Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Studay

title: Conglomerating the Effects of Physical Activity on Cardiovascular Longevity in Ageing
abs: Background: Physical activity has been traditionally used to maintain health, promote total well-being and prescribed as part of holistic approach to disease treatments such as cardiovascular disease. In ageing adults, activity has purported benefits including improvements in aerobic capacity and skeletal muscle function. However, ageing is frequently accompanied by changes such as sarcopenia and dysmetabolism. These changes result in heterogeneous effects of activity that impact on traditional targets of physical activity such as body mass index (BMI) (due to sarcopenia), rendering traditional targets inaccurate as targets reflective of activity outcomes in older adults. Therefore, we hypothesize that the human metabolome represent the convergence of all factors associated with activity and sum of all physiological processes in ageing adults, useful for measuring the effect of activity on ageing adults, and possibly surpassing the role of BMI as the conventional target. Methods: We propose to perform a longitudinal investigation of a subset of an established cohort of aged community adults without clinical cardiovascular disease, to investigate the changes in the metabolite biomarkers that occur among participants with low versus high levels of physical activity, in relation to their cardiovascular function (as outcome), and comparing the metabolite biomarkers to other traditional targets such as BMI. They will have repeated time-point annotation of cardiovascular, skeletal muscle, circulating metabolomics, and pertinent diet, lifestyle, physical activity and risk factors over one year as proof of concept for this proposal. This will include the development of machine learning technology to converge these multimodal biological inputs, then onwards for efficient data extraction for determination of optimal cardiac health. Significance: This proposal fills a gap in dispensing activity as a lifestyle action towards longevity. Exploring the use of metabolomic biomarkers advances the science for personalized medicine in activity prescription and targets, especially among older adults with complex physiology.
kw: ageing; cardiovascular; biology; molecular; longevity; machine learning

title: TargEted TheRApy for blooD Cancer II (TETRAD II)
abs: Established in 2017 under the RIE2020 Centre Grant (Collaborative Pot), TETRAD (Targeted Therapy for Blood Cancer) brings together haemato-oncology clinician researchers and scientists from Singapore General Hospital (SGH), National Cancer Centre, Singapore (NCCS), National University Cancer Institute, Singapore (NCIS), and Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH). With a shared vision to be united against blood cancer , TETRAD has since made significant strides towards achieving its common mission of establishing a national collaborative platform of international renown to advance translational research and clinical care in blood cancer . An Executive Committee, comprising the Centre Grant Core and Theme Leads was formed to provide leadership and mentorship and to co-ordinate research capabilities among the institutions, with the objective to provide a platform for sharing research ideas, strengthening blood cancer research and promoting collaboration. Subcommittees were formed to facilitate organisation and execution of activities and each subcommittee is led by an EXCO member with representatives from the various institutions. An Advisory Board comprising local and international research leaders was set up to advise on strategic directions on research and governance. The infrastructure of TETRAD is centred on two interdependent cores: (i) Developmental Therapeutics Core and (ii) Genomic Biomarker Discovery Core. The research is organised into five themes: (i) Novel Targets and Biomarker Identification, (ii) Molecular Targeted Therapy, (iii) Cellular Immunotherapy, (iv) Antibody-based Therapy, (v) Overcoming Drug Resistance.

title: MOlecular Markers, MEchaNisms and their TherapeUtic Manipulation in CardioVascular Disease (MOMMENTUM-CVD)
abs: The National University Heart Centre, Singapore (NUHCS) and its research-dedicated arm, the Cardiovascular Research Institute (CVRI), were established at the direction of the Ministry of Health in 2007. An international advisory panel, convened in 2008, recommended CVRI undertake a wide-ranging spectrum of translational activities from laboratory-based basic research through to observational and interventional clinical studies. CVRI appointed its inaugural Director, Professor Mark Richards, in October 2009. Over the period 2009-2021 CVRI/NUHCS has continuously expanded its complement and bandwidth as further detailed below, to mature into an internationally recognized contributor to translational cardiovascular research. The first CVRI Centre Grant (SGD 6M; 2010-13) was acquired via a competitive, internationally peer-reviewed process and commenced operations in mid-2010. From that time wet-lab facilities and cohort-scale clinical studies have been established and expanded into an extensive research infrastructure supporting an exciting portfolio of research with particular strengths in coronary heart disease, heart failure and cardiac valvular disease. Successive 4-year, $10M Centre Grants were acquired by CVRI/NUHCS for 2013-17 and 2017-21. NUHS and the Yong Loo Lin School of medicine, under the leadership of successive supportive Deans and Chief Executives including Professors John Wong, Yeoh Khay Guan and Chong Yap Seng, have authorised core funding to CVRI, enabling pilot work and consolidation of key infrastructure. Recently Dean Prof Chong Yap Seng has initiated the Translational Research Programmes (TRPs) aimed at synergistic, trans-campus integration of research in a range of disciplines. The Cardiovascular TRP is directed by senior CVRI Principal Investigators, Professor Roger Foo (basic science) and Assoc Prof Mark Chan (clinical research). CVRI comprises a central element of the Cardiovascular TRP. \ Over the last decade the NUHCS Centre Grants have provided essential foundational support allowing generation of platforms (detailed in section 2.3 RIE2025 Research Strategy Plans) and pilot data to fuel successful acquisition of multiple contestable grants and contracts with industry. These have included a Translational Clinical Research (TCR) grant of SGD 9 M over 2013-2018 on genetics and epigenetics and experimental models of heart failure (HF) held in partnership with the Genome Institute of Singapore (GIS) and the A*STaR Institute of Medical Biology (IMB). Prof Richards is a STaR awardee (SGD 9.5 M; 2014-2019) investigating the biology and clinical management of post-myocardial infarction adverse ventricular remodelling. This resource has produced results and competencies subsequently triggering the current major Health Services Development (HSDP) grant AMI-HOPE led by Assoc Prof Mark Chan, funded at over SGD13 million, aimed at beneficial updating and streamlining of post-myocardial infarction management island-wide. title: Centre for Mental Health Research: Population, Clinical, Systems and Services Research Programmes
abs: The Institute of Mental Health (IMH) is the largest mental health care provider and the only state mental health institute serving the entire population of Singapore. It has an inpatient facility of about 2,000 beds and serves over 46,000 outpatients in the community. The Institute has a wide range of clinical expertise for treating various mental disorders that span from childhood disorders to those afflicting the elderly. At IMH, there is an ongoing, concerted effort to continue achieving research excellence through a transdisciplinary and integrated approach that brings together research expertise from diverse fields. With funding from the National Medical Research Council s (NMRC) Centre Grant (CG) in the form of two funding tranches of $16 M since 2012, we have successfully built a physical and organizational research infrastructure, established the requisite human research capital, and developed our research portfolio. Leveraging strategically on the strengths and expertise of our researchers and collaborators, we have built two main research programmes (i) the Programme for Mental Health Policy Studies (PMHPS) and (ii) the Psychiatric Phenomics Research Programme. The CG has helped further the development and expansion of our research in the following areas: 1. Building strategic collaborations both internationally (University of Hong Kong, Tilburg University, University of Auckland, Stanley Center for Psychiatric Research at Broad Institute and Technische Universitat, Germany) and locally, with academic medical centres, hospitals, ministries, and care providers in the community. Local collaborators include the Singapore Bioimaging Consortium, A*STAR, Duke-National University of Singapore (NUS), Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health (SSHSPH), NUS, Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore Management University, Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) and Work, Safety and Health Institute, Ministry of Manpower (MOM). The successful collaborations have led to research projects funded by the Ministry of Health (MOH), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Ministry of National Development (MND), National Council of Social Services (NCSS) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) as well as philanthropic grants from Temasek Foundation (TF) and Tote Board, and also pharmaceutical grants from companies like Janssen Private Limited among others. In the past 5 years, the PMHPS Core has undertaken studies with funding amounting to $13.7 M. 2. Building expertise and expanding our portfolio in psychiatric epidemiology including six epidemiological studies on the general population have been initiated/ conducted to examine the prevalence of (i) mental disorders among adults (ii) dementia and depression in the elderly, (ii) mental health literacy, (iii) health and lifestyle behaviors, (iv) diabetes knowledge, attitides and pricatices (v) psychological morbidity related to Covid-19, and (vi) youth mental health. title: Towards Optimal Health and Human Potential for Children & Women – Beyond Integrative Translational Healthcare Research
abs: KK Women s and Children s Hospital (KKH) is the only dedicated Women s and Children s Hospital in Singapore and is part of the SingHealth healthcare cluster. It has the largest paediatric, obstetric and gynaecological (OBGYN) clinical workload in Singapore, with 830 beds, and is a major referral centre for paediatric, obstetrics and gynaecology care. It provides services ranging from routine antenatal care and childbirth, through neonatal care from term down to extreme pre-term babies and extending through childhood to cover general paediatric care and developmental services to tertiary services in women and children. Our research teams are in a unique position to care for and study a patient population spanning from healthy pregnancy and childhood all the way to high complexity tertiary and quaternary level conditions in women and children. This unique situation enables us to have clear perspectives on epidemiology, coupled with a very operational and practical world-view that enables us to better identify and solve problems through patient-oriented research. KKH has close affiliations with other hospitals in the SingHealth cluster and community partners throughout Singapore. KKH is also the only hospital which trains students from all 3 medical schools and with faculty holding academic positions in Duke NUS Graduate Medical School, NUS Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine and Nanyang Technological University (NTU) Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine, giving it a reach to the medical community and healthcare landscape which is uniquely broad and places us in a position to engage and impact our catchment population and on the community as a whole. The high clinical volume and sophisticated clinical subspecialties enable us to deliver top quality care and take clinical management to the peak of evidence-based medicine. It drives us towards efficiencies of care and enables us to identify unmet needs facing Singapore healthcare today and find solutions to these problems. We occupy a unique position in Singapore which enables us to drive cutting-edge research and which makes us the partner of choice for Duke-NUS, NUS, A*STAR and other institutes of higher learning and research entities in Singapore and abroad. We have progressive hospital senior management who emphasize innovation, improvement and positive change. The over-arching goals of our research are to improve the health of women and children in Singapore. The KKH Centre Grant, entitled Improving the Outcomes of Women & Children Health in Singapore An Integrative Translational Research Programme has evolved through two iterations, starting with the first Centre Grant call based on the national Research, Innovation & Enterprise (RIE) 2015 plan. The initial Cores of Genomics, BioImaging, Translational Immunology were supplemented in RIE 2020 by expansion of Cores to include omics, Health Services Research and Medical Technology.

title: IMplementing a PArtnership for Cardiovascular Trials-2 (IMPACT-2)
abs: The IMplementing a PArtnership for Cardiovascular Trials-2 (IMPACT-2) Collaborative Centre Grant (CCG) RIE2025 Program is a joint application between the 3 Heart Institutes in Singapore (SG) - the National Heart Centre, Singapore (NHCS), National University Heart Centre, Singapore (NUHCS), and the National Healthcare Group Heart Institute (NHGHI). Being the only 3 tertiary Heart Institutes in the nation, the IMPACT-2 CCG Program represents the nation s combined and coordinated efforts to advance cardiovascular (CV) research to the international level. The previous IMPACT-1 CCG RIE2020 Program established 6 new facility cores across NHCS and NUHCS, and put in place new research infrastructure to support clinical studies recruiting patients across the 2 national heart centres. The proposed IMPACT-2 CCG Program will strengthen and further develop these facility cores, and will extend the collaborative partnership to involve the newly established NHGHI, thereby establishing a nationwide research network to support multicentre clinical studies recruiting patients across the 3 Heart Institutes. In this section, we provide an overview of these three Heart Institutes, and the research capabilities that have been established by previous Centre Grants (CG) awarded to NHCS and NUHCS, and the previous IMPACT-1 CCG. Crucially, the IMPACT-2 CCG Program will strengthen, build-on and extend the research capabilities put in place by the NUHCS and NHCS main CGs, and the IMPACT-1 CCG, and will NOT duplicate research capabilities already present at the 3 Heart Institutes.

Crucially, the IMPACT-2 CCG Program will strengthen, build-on and extend the research capabilities put in place by the NUHCS and NHCS main CGs, and the IMPACT-1 CCG, and will NOT duplicate research capabilities already present at the 3 Heart Institutes.

title: TargEted TheRApy for blooD Cancer II (TETRAD II)
abs: Established in 2017 under the RIE2020 Centre Grant (Collaborative Pot), TETRAD (Targeted Therapy for Blood Cancer) brings together haemato-oncology clinician researchers and scientists from Singapore General Hospital (SGH), National Cancer Centre, Singapore (NCCS), National University Cancer Institute, Singapore (NCIS), and Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH). With a shared vision to be united against blood cancer , TETRAD has since made significant strides towards achieving its common mission of establishing a national collaborative platform of international renown to advance translational research and clinical care in blood cancer . An Executive Committee, comprising the Centre Grant Core and Theme Leads was formed to provide leadership and mentorship and to co-ordinate research capabilities among the institutions, with the objective to provide a platform for sharing research ideas, strengthening blood cancer research and promoting collaboration. Subcommittees were formed to facilitate organisation and execution of activities and each subcommittee is led by an EXCO member with representatives from the various institutions. An Advisory Board comprising local and international research leaders was set up to advise on strategic directions on research and governance. The infrastructure of TETRAD is centred on two interdependent cores: (i) Developmental Therapeutics Core and (ii) Genomic Biomarker Discovery Core. The research is organised into five themes: (i) Novel Targets and Biomarker Identification, (ii) Molecular Targeted Therapy, (iii) Cellular Immunotherapy, (iv) Antibody-based Therapy, (v) Overcoming Drug Resistance.

title: Operational profiling and digital twinning of harbour craft for holistic test-bedding, life-cycle optimization and future design enhancements
inst: TCOMS - Technology Centre for Offshore & Marine Singapore
abs: The transformation of a full electric harbour craft fleet requires a holistic understanding of the combined effects of vessel hydrodynamics, propulsion system behaviour and whole-of-life operating profile of the various classes. In this regard, TCOMS and SIT seek to contribute to this evolution through our expertise in naval architecture, as well as how vessel operational profiles drive vessel design. Together with industry partners across the different harbour craft types, we will carry out: i. Operational profiling of representative harbour craft from each vessel class within the consortium, taking into account the interactions between vessel sub-systems and the overall response of vessels in real-world conditions. This will help provide a first-principles-based design envelope for the design of a full electric harbour craft. ii. A digital twin of the new harbour craft will be developed, coupling the hull hydrodynamics with the shipboard systems. Through quantifiable performance metrics, this digital twin provides a holistic test-bedding platform for the craft, enabling optimization and whole-of-life analyses of the various real-world operating scenarios. As the design of the vessel is carried out progressively, component models of particular systems (e.g. hull) can be developed concurrently as the pilot vessel goes through the design cycle, and can be used for local design improvements / enhancements in the earlier phase of the project. This will benefit the pilot vessel design as well as accuracy of the DT in the later part of the project. iii. Upon commissioning of the harbour craft by the industry partners, fine-tuning of the digital twin will be carried out using data from live operations. The validated digital twin will provide stakeholders with a platform to carry out scenario analyses, and the data and knowledge generated from the Digital Twin can be used to identify areas where design improvements can be made to evolve future designs. Through in-service calibration, the stakeholders will also be able to take into consideration any degradation in the performance of the vessel, including the shipboard systems. Also, should the consortium identify areas where design modifications (following operationalisation) would bring about significant benefits, these can be applied to the pilot vessel to improve the full electric harbour craft developed in this project. The digital twin will pave the way for future cyber-physical modelling and simulations where outputs from the digital twin can be used to provide decision support and in turn, provide control feedback to the vessel towards the desired outcome.

title: An experimental medicine decipher of a minimum correlate of cellular immunity
abs: The world is currently living through a coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, caused by the novel severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2). Millions of people have been ill with COVID-19 and billions more are suffering from the socioeconomic disruption associated with disease control, where rising unemployment and reduced trade have caused financial hardships whilst the world awaits a preventative vaccine. Vaccine development, despite its speed remains impeded by the lack of well-defined correlates of protection. Furthermore, the gap in knowledge on the correlate of protection is uneven between humoral and cellular immunity. Conventionally, assessment of immunity has relied almost exclusively on antibody measurement whereas it remains unclear how much virus specific T cells are needed to protect against re-infection. This limitation is not peculiar to the novel SARS-CoV-2 but is applicable to many other known viruses, including the highly prevalent dengue virus; the only licensed dengue vaccine, Dengvaxia, has shown limited efficacy due at least in part to lack of dengue virus-specific T cells. Consequently, many initially promising vaccine candidates fail to show desired efficacy only when they reach late phase and costly clinical trials. Deciphering the quality and quantity of T cells needed to protect against symptomatic infection would thus fill a critical gap in knowledge. To address this gap in fundamental knowledge, we have assembled a team of investigators with proven track record in experimental medicine, virology and immunology to bear on this critical knowledge gap. Our overarching goal is to define, the threshold of T cells that would confer protection against an attenuated viral infection. We will develop upon our success with using the live attenuated yellow fever (YF17D) vaccine as a model to study viral infection in human volunteers. If successful, our study could form a minimum threshold of T cells needed to prevent viral infection.
kw: Vaccine; correlate of protection; cellular immunity; experimental medicine.

title: Room-temperature, gate-tunable ferromagnetism in a 2D semiconductor.
abs: Recently, much attention has been paid to ferromagnetism in two dimensional (2D) materials. Several intrinsic 2D ferromagnets have been discovered. But such ferromagnetis only exists at very low temperature and the ferromagnetic ordering cannot be effectively changed by and electric field, etc. However, both are needed to a) demonstrate topological magentism and practical device applications Therefore, there is urgent need to develop new 2D ferromagnets whose magnetism can survive up to room temperature and which can be controlled by the electric field effect. Here we propose to dope magnetic elements atomically into nonmagnetic 2D semiconductors to create semiconducting ferromagnets (the so-called dilute magnetic semiconductors, DMS). We will use black phosphorus (BP) as the prototype 2D semiconductor and cobalt (Co) as the magnetic dopant to start with. The reason for this choice are as follows: (1) BP has been shown to be a very good semiconductor with high electron mobility and more importantly, can be efficiently controlled by electric field; (2) Our previous theoretical calculation has shown that a small amount of Co doped into monolayer BP can generate above room temperature ferromagnetism, which forms the foundation of our proposed research; (3) BP has inherently anisotropic structural and electronic properties, which allows us to further explore magnetic anisotropy and textured magnetic states based on it. We will implement our proposed research by a combination of techniques including micro-nano device fabrication and characterization, electron microscopy imaging, theoretical simulation, etc. Finally, we will demonstrate a prototype memory device with enhanced efficiency and electric-field controllability based on our proposed materials system.

title: Heterologous Prime-Boost-Boost Vaccine Combinations for Long-Term Humoral and Cellular Immunity Against COVID-19
abs: PRIBIVAC is an adaptive, randomised, subject-blinded, controlled trial to assess the immunogenicity and safety of heterologous boost COVID-19 vaccine regimens (intervention groups 1-4) compared with a homologous boost regimen (control arm). We hypothesise that one or more heterologous prime-boost-boost COVID-19 vaccine combinations will produce humoral and cellular immunity that is non-inferior to a homologous prime-boost-boost vaccination against wildtype SARS-CoV-2 and/or 1≥ variants of concern. A total of up to 600 eligible adults, who have already received the second dose of a homologous prime-boost vaccination with BNT162b2 or mRNA-1273 at least six months will be enrolled at the NCID research clinic and will be randomized into 4 intervention groups and 1 control group. The booster vaccine for the control arm will be the homologous mRNA vaccine, while for individuals randomised to intervention group 1 the mRNA booster vaccine administered will be heterologous to the primary series. The booster vaccine candidates for intervention groups 2–4 will be an alternative COVID-19 vaccine. New intervention groups may also be added depending on what COVID-19 vaccines are authorised for use in Singapore, and may include new vaccines or vaccines targeting SARS-CoV-2 variants. Participants will receive the blinded vaccination on study day 0 / visit 1. Participants will be observed for 30 minutes in the clinic after vaccination as per standard clinical practice. Participants will be monitored and followed up for AEs at Day 28 and SAEs throughout the study by physical examinations, laboratory tests and self-reporting. Blood samples will also be taken at the follow-up visits at days 0, 7, 28, 180, 360 post-enrolment for evaluation of immunogenicity and/or safety. Safety and futility will be reviewed by DSMB after the first 10 participants in each of the intervention arms have completed assessments at study day 28.

title: Explore novel platform and mechanism for electric manipulation of valleytronics
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: The overall objective of this proposal is through theoretical approach to discover new physical mechanisms for electric manipulation of valley degree of freedom, to predict realistic material platforms, and to investigate their distinct physical properties, which will pave the way for designing novel valleytronic devices. The electronic conduction or valence bands of a solid material may feature multiple energy extremal points, known as valleys, in the momentum space. This endows the low-energy carriers with a new degree of freedom, namely, a carrier (electron or hole) can be labelled by the valley it belongs to. Although the concept is well known in 3D semiconductors such as Si, it flourished relatively recently, with the advent of 2D materials. It was proposed that in 2D materials such as gapped graphene or monolayer MoS2, the valley, as a binary degree of freedom, can be effectively manipulated to encode and to process information. This generates the field of valleytronics. Like spintronics, the valleytronic devices are expected to have great advantages of low power consumption and low heat generation, thus the field has attracted tremendous interest in the past decade. However, despite the considerable progress, there is an outstanding challenge for the field — the lack of electric gate control of the valley. The gate control is important for practical applications, because it has the crucial advantages in compactness, scalability, power efficiency, and compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Unfortunately, it is exactly forbidden by symmetry in the existing valleytronic platforms based on 2D hexagonal materials with time-reversal-connected valleys. Thus, it is difficult to solve this challenge in the current valleytronics paradigm. The objective of this project is to tackle the challenge by jumping beyond the existing paradigm. Via symmetry analysis, theoretical modelling, numerical simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) based first-principles calculations, we will propose new platforms to achieve electric gate control of valley and will reveal their unique physical properties. This will open a new paradigm for valleytronic research and will form the basis for designing novel valleytronic devices. Specific Aims Specifically, we have the following objectives in this project. (a) Explore gate-controllable valleytronic platforms. Since the electric gate control is forbidden for time-reversal-connected valleys, our idea is to explore new platforms where the valleys are not connected by time reversal, but by certain crystalline symmetry. Via symmetry analysis and theoretical modelling, we will establish a set of conditions required for such platforms, and identify the allowed coupling between valley and other degrees of freedom (e.g. layer, spin, and polarization). title: Atomic Scale Study of Domain Switching in Two Dimensional Ferroelectrics
abs: Academic significance: The applications of ferroelectric materials stem from the ability to switch polarized domains by applying an electric field, which is highly useful in digital data storage and processing applications. 2D ferroelectric materials offer the prospect of overcoming thickness-related depolarization effects in conventional ferroelectrics, and present enticing prospects for energy-saving device configurations and size scaling in next-generation electronic and electromechanical device technology. However, there are fundamental issues that need to be solved before these can be deployed commercially, especially with regards to ferroelectric phase control and stability. Intellectual merits: The microscopic origin of ferroelectricity in 2d ferroelectric material arises from atomic displacement, but how that correlates to the dynamic switching behaviour of ferroelectric domains remains poorly understood. There is a need to understand how domain walls that separate regions of different polarization move during ferroelectric switching. Understanding domain structure is useful for engineering multiconductance levels, which are essential for recording synaptic weight in neuromorphic computing. Another pertinent problem is ultrathin ferroelectrics (eg. α-phase In2Se3) has poor device stability and sometimes show short retention time, thus engineering domain structure to allow robust ferroelectric device operation is needed. Objectives: The aims of this study are to achieve atomic level insight into ferroelectric domain switching mechanism in 2D ferroelectrics, and to understand how ferroelectric device properties such as coercive field, memory retention and stability relates to the domain microstructure and phase change in ferroelectric films. Ultimately, we wish to achieve highly stable and efficient 2D ferroelectric device operation. Methodology: We have previously established a research program to grow large area 2D ferroelectric, polycrystalline In2Se3 and SnS films. Leveraging on our expertise in surface imaging science with high spatial resolution, we propose an experimental platform to study the switching dynamics of embedded ferroelastic/ferroelectric domains in these ferroelectric semiconductor films using a combination of real-time probes from atomic scale to macroscopic scale, as well as phase-field modelling at different length scales. Significance and broader impact: Understanding domain structure and domain wall motion, which is crucial for polarization switching, helps to optimize film growth and device architectures, as well as predict and mitigate device failures. This will be highly useful for implementing 2D ferroelectrics in next generation in-memory computing and neuromorphic memory.

title: Optimizing spin channel in spinel oxides for efficient oxygen electrocatalysis
abs: Transition metal spinel oxides have raised as promising catalysts for oxygen electrocatalysis which has been involved in many renewable and eco-friendly energy technologies, such as water electrocatalysis and fuel cells. The unique AB2O4 frame of spinel enables first-row transition metals to reside in both A and B sites; therefore, spinel oxides exhibit the first-rank cost-effectiveness among various transition metal oxides (TMOs), making them advantageous to acquire practical applications. To improve the catalytic activity of spinel oxides, researchers have found that controlling the cation type and optimizing cation coordination geometry are beneficial for both oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). More recently, the dependence of oxygen electrocatalysis on the spin channel in TMOs has been sporadically reported and the theoretical origins of spin-enhanced electrocatalysis are raising interests. Generally, the unpaired spin in the crystal lattice of catalysts, if uniformly reoriented in a ferromagnetic (FM) ordering, can effectively create a spin-polarized channel to enhance the charge transfer mobility along the oxygen catalysis process, boosting the reaction kinetics. Besides, the aligned spin configuration may also influence the binding energy of key reaction intermediates through spin-orbital coupling, resulting in altered reaction thermodynamics. Therefore, the spin channel can affect both the kinetics and thermodynamics of oxygen electrocatalysis. This is the main hypothesis of this proposal that the oxygen electrocatalysis on spinel oxides can be further fine-tuned by optimizing the spin channel in the lattice. To date, this has not been systematically studied and constitutes the basis of this research proposal. This project aims to gain fundamental understandings on how the spin-polarized channel evolves with the change of spin configuration (spin magnitude, distribution, ordering etc.) and how it affects the intrinsic catalytic activities of spinel oxides towards OER and ORR. The spin-polarized channel will be created and tuned by altering the spin configuration in the spinel lattice. Although, several spin-dependent phenomena of OER on TMOs have been reported, this is the first systematic study to explore and uncover the fundamentals of spin channel in the abundant and cost-effective spinel family. The critical fundamental understanding of the spin channel and its role, either positive or negative, in affecting the kinetics and thermodynamics of oxygen electrocatalysis remain elusive. This will require a correlation of results obtained using theoretical simulations and experimental techniques. Both theoretical and experimental studies will be pursuit as part of this project. title: Wide temperature-range supercapacitors, from electrode materials design to energy storage mechanism
abs: Electrochemical double-layer supercapacitors are important energy storage devices, with high power density, intrinsic safety, and long cycle life. Supercapacitors can be operated at a wider temperature than other energy storage devices such as batteries. However, their low-temperature performance still suffers due to a significant increase in internal impedance that causes voltage drop and a sharp reduction of power density. Mesoporous carbons with optimized pore size and pore structure allow the mitigation of these detrimental effects. Highly conductive graphene sheets will also effectively mitigate this problem. On the other hand, high-temperature operation of supercapacitors is highly dependent on the stability of electrolyte as well as the electrode being mechanically stable with high thermal and electrical conductivity. In this proposal, both electrode materials and electrolytes suitable for wide-temperature range supercapacitors will be extensively studied. Using the “perfect” graphene sheets and multi-dimensional carbon structures we have developed, we will demonstrate prototype devices with superior performance at both low and high temperatures. We will also use state-of-art in-situ characterization techniques as well as numerical simulations to gain fundamental understandings. In-situ Raman spectroscopy, Electrochemical Quartz Crystal Microbalance (EQCM), variable temperature in-situ transmission electron microscope (TEM) and simulations will be performed. We will focus on the investigation of the different electrolyte’s distribution on the electrode surface, microstructure of the electrode interface, ion desolvation kinetics, and charge storage mechanism. In this project we aim to achieve: • Ultra-high quality few-layer graphene sheets (1-8 layers) at 100 grams/batch level using our scalable methods to produce few-layer graphene sheets (NTU Technology Disclosure #2020-259). The graphene has >104 times better electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity than the commonly used graphene oxides and reduced graphene oxides, critical for supercapacitor applications. title: Explainable Deep Learning Models for Synthesis of Conversational Speech with Emotional Intelligence
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: This project seeks to address 3 research problems. 1) What are the main contributing factors that influence the linguistic prosody and affective prosody in conversational speech? 2) What are the controlling factors for speech prosody in conversational speech synthesis? 3) How to computationally model speech prosody in state-of-the-art speech synthesis systems? The answers to these scientific problems will allow us to implement state-of-the-art deep learning models for expressive speech synthesis with emotional intelligence. To address the research problems, we propose to work on 5 sub-tasks, 1) Understanding prosody: Speech conveys information not only through phonetic content, but also through its prosody. Prosody is one of the defining features of expressive speech, that one uses to convey meaning and emotion, and to make the speech lively. However, prosody has not been the center of speech synthesis research, there is little study to relate linguistic study of prosody to computational model for conversational speech. In this task, we would like to understand the interaction between discourse prosody with syntax, semantics and pragmatics, and the contributing factors that influence the linguistic prosody and affective prosody in conversational speech. 2) Situation-aware speech prosody modelling: We will take a corpus-based approach to study the relationship between conversational context and speech prosody, and develop a computational model of prosody for spoken dialogue. Despite the progress, speech synthesis today is mainly designed for text reading or storytelling, where prosody model is built to associate only with the text script. It has not taken the interlocutor’s response or feedback into consideration. In human-machine dialogue, the dynamic of the conversation plays an important role in the rendering of speech prosody. In this task, we will study the prosodic aspect of speech expression in conversation, and incorporate this understanding into situation aware speech prosody rendering. 3) Acoustic-prosodic entrainment: We will further study acoustic-prosodic entrainment, an important aspect of spoken dialogue. Entrainment has been observed in numerous domains and for multiple levels of human-human communication. In addition, many studies have shown associations between entrainment and desirable dialogue characteristics. It takes place at almost every level of human communication: lexical, syntactic, stylistic, acoustic-prosodic and phonetic. We will motivate the study by theoretical models such as Giles’ Communication Accommodation Theory, which proposes that speakers promote social approval or efficient communication by adapting to their interlocutors’ communicative behaviour and Chartrand and Bargh (1999)’s study, which describes entrainment as a purely automatic process. title: Towards Ultrahigh-Endurance On-Memory Selector Kit (TUSK)
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: Three lessons of 3D Xpoint memory (3D-XPm) device trials – that is device endurance is key to realizing a transistor-replacement memory technology, that switching endurance of traditional amorphous-3D-XPm device is insufficient, and that deeper level of insight into device degradation is desirable – must be applied to the next phase of transistor-replacement research. This phase will investigate ovonic-threshold-selector (OTS) 3D-XPm device roll-out and optimization in high read/write settings, as well as complete picture based on device degradation, such as device mechanism and effects of preparation/characterization conditions on device characteristics. To address the issue of device endurance, systematic analysis of the integration of devices under high read/write settings is essential but rarely shown for 3D-XPm devices. Furthermore, because of the inherent structural complexities of atomic species in such systems, the understanding of device mechanism tends to be poor, rendering further device optimization related to switching endurance difficult. Feasibility of device integration and theoretical studies will be crucial to optimizing device endurance with the real-world OTS devices and full picture based on device degradation. Our group has helped advanced the use of nanometre-sized architectures to study device characteristics of phase-change memory. During previous studies, we made significant progress on our original aims, demonstrating that nanometre-sized architectures show faster nucleation and growth than bulk materials. We have also shown preliminary use of nanometre-sized architectures to enhance device characteristics related to switching endurance with OTS 3D-XPm devices. This proposal will leverage three important trials to explore key knowledge gaps that will arise in the next phase of transistor-replacement memory work: the memory-System development, memory Testing and array ARchitecture (STAR) trial (Dr. Loke, as chair) will assess the feasibility of integration of ovonic-threshold-selector (OTS) device and phase-change-memory device under high read/write settings. The memory Manufacturing INvolving Design (MIND) trial (Dr. Loke, as chair and Dr. Naga, as co-chair and collaborator) will examine the mechanism of OTS device related to device degradation. The memory Manufacturing Allowing crosspoint-based Patterning and Specified testing (MAPS) trial (Dr. Loke, as chair and Dr. Cai, as co-chair and collaborator) will evaluate the effects of preparation/characterization conditions on OTS device characteristics associated with device degradation. All 3 trials will use crystalline (c-) 2D materials, and track robust outcomes, to allow us to 1) investigate c-2D material as a switching medium in studies of the feasibility of device integration under high read/write settings, and 2) examine the use of c-2D materials for theoretical studies that will provide a complete picture based on device degradation.
