title: A BIODEGRADABLE ARTERIAL-CENTRIC ANASTOMOSIS DEVICE FOR MICROVASCULAR SURGERY
abs: Globally, hard and soft-tissue loss from disease and trauma is often replaced by free-tissue flap-transfer requiring blood vessel anastomosis. These microsurgical anastomoses are performed by devices or hand-suturing, the latter being technique sensitive and has a steep learning curve. Existing devices are non-biodegradable and used more popularly for veins. Other limitations include difficulties with use in arteries, device palpability over skin, device extrusion, infections and limitations during growth in children. We aim to design and produce an anastomosis device (coupler), that is biodegradable and user-friendly, to anastomose both arteries and veins in microsurgery. Coupler design is performed using the CAD/CAM software SOLIDWORKS. Biodegradable materials Poly Lactic-co-Glycolic Acid (PLGA) and Magnesium-Calcium alloy respectively, will be used for 3D printing of the designs. Upsized 3D-printed prototype coupler will be tested and calibrated in finite element analysis and in vitro experiments. Inherent viscosity, decomposition and degradation property tests of the PLGA and electrochemical corrosion tests for the Magnesium-Calcium alloy will be performed. Actual-sized 3D-printed prototype coupler using the respective materials will be tested in rabbits for efficacy and vessel-anastomosis time. Controls are rabbits with hand-sutured vessel anastomosis. The animals will be sacrificed at various time point for open exploration of the anastomosis site. Vessel and surrounding tissue histology will be examined for biodegradability and inflammatory changes. Samples from the serum, liver, thymus gland and spleen will be analysed for biocompatibility and toxicity of PLGA/Magnesium-Calcium alloy. Computational fluid dynamics studies and incorporation of blood perfusion sensor in these couplers will be performed to assess flow and perfusion of free flaps in future studies. This novel coupler provides a faster and cheaper alternative to hand-sutured vessel anastomosis. It can be broadly applied to other aspects of surgery requiring vessel anastomosis, decreasing surgery duration and improving patient outcomes. (292 words)

title: Non-Invasive and Rapid Screening of COVID-19 Using Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) in Exhaled Breath
abs: COVID-19 causes specific changes in biochemical pathways and therefore detectable changes in exhaled breath VOC profiles. Based on initial clinical studies, the differential VOCs identified for COVID-19 detection are able to achieve a sensitivity of 85% and specificity of 97%. We hypothesize that by collecting more clinical data and incorporating machine learning algorithm, the accuracy of breath VOC analysis can be increased further. In this study, we planned to extend a clinical trial in Dubai to collect the exhaled breath of COVID-19 infected individuals using Breathonix’s BreFenceTM Go platform to build a machine learning model for the prediction and validation of COVID-19. Due to its good vaccination program, many individuals in Dubai had been vaccinated with the COVID-19 vaccine and hence allowing us to study the effect of the vaccine on the infection. Upon completing this study, an AI-based model using breathalyser technology that allow us to screen for COVID-19 more accurately will be developed (Specific aim 1) and the validation of such rapid and non-invasive point-of-care screening methods are critical as countries begin to ease restriction measures and economies begin to recover. New knowledge pertaining to how COVID-19 variants (Specific aim 2) and vaccination (Specific aim 3) affects the body, which in turn leads to a change in the VOCs level exhaled in the breath, will be obtained. With these information, it will provide insights for scientists and healthcare professionals to develop new protocols to better manage and treat individuals who are infected with COVID-19.

title: Safe testing platform for evaluation of vaccine/drug candidates against novel, pathogenic viruses
abs: Research on finding a cure for pandemic outbreaks is like a ‘Catch 22’, because of the pathogenic nature of novel viruses. Scientists are required to work within biosafety cabinets of class III inside BSL3 (biosafety level 3) facilities that have special features, for example, controlled directional airflow, ventilation system, room exhaust. The infectious rate and unknown dangers of the virus also has hampered research efforts. There is an urgent need to provide a safe testing platform for research personnel and clinicians who are involved in finding a cure for pathogenic viruses. This exposure to live viruses is unavoidable for medical personnel and doctors, however, researchers or drug companies who are working on potential vaccines/drugs/kits need not handle live viruses. It involves needless risks and costs in training of personnel and in providing the right containment facility. In view of the economic and public health costs of these pandemics, it is imperative that the scientific community is pre-emptive in finding methods to be ready to face future outbreaks. We propose to provide a safe platform for ex vivo testing of potential vaccine/drug candidates or diagnostic kits against pathogenic viruses, which eliminates the requirement of BSL3 facility. The platform will be initially designed to test for SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is the causative agent of the current pandemic of COVID-19; however, it will be applicable to other pathogenic viruses as well. Using recombinant DNA technology, and baculoviral (insect virus) expression system, we will generate pseudoviral particles designed to express pathogenic viral proteins or subgenomic RNA sequences. These ‘pseudovirions’ will be replication defective and can be safely used in a BSL1 facility, as their hosts are insect cells and they naturally do not infect human cells. For example, pseudovirions that express the mRNA of COVID-19’s spike protein could be used to check if synthetic siRNAs can bind to and inhibit the protein’s production within a cell. The proposed solution would provide a safer working environment for the scientific community and accelerate the screening process of potential new cures. It will also be useful for facility-limited research companies and institutes to use this method to test out their ideas on potential vaccines without the inherent risks involved.

title: Asian 3D Skin Platform for Asian-Specific Formulation Development
abs: Current skin models, even those that are ECVAM-validated, behave as more penetrable skin barriers which allow for actives to pass through too quickly. An enhanced or improved version is needed for more accurate assessment of the penetration kinetics of drugs and actives, and for better understanding of their performance and toxicity. This project aims to provide a skin model that is made by culture of Asian skin cells in a three-dimensional (3D) distribution and structure that closely mimics live, physiologically healthy Asian human skin with a functional skin barrier function. The majority of skincare and cosmetic manufacturers locally are SMEs, which have limited resources and capability for in-depth formulation development and penetration studies / efficacy optimisation. They would usually adopt ready formulations from ingredient suppliers. Furthermore, overseas brands that want to tap into the Asian market will be keen to explore Asian-specific formulations to ease their entry. To meet these needs, this project also aims to develop Asian-specific formulations that are ready for industry adoption, such as emulsion-free formulations. In addition to being a more accurate testing platform to study penetration of actives, the proposed skin model is intended to be used as a surrogate model of live human skin, on which to assess safety profiles of the Asian-specific formulations we will develop in this project. Our proposed enhanced Asian skin model will be a first for the Southeast Asian context, bringing direct testing relevance for cosmetics and skincare actives to markets in the region. Our proposed model will also exhibit superior accuracy in terms of corresponding barrier and permeability characteristics to that of live human skin. With this enhanced skin model, we will also demonstrate feasibility of its application to a testing workflow to assess formulations developed in-house, establishing a continuous process from formulation development to assessment.

title: Design and development of portable handheld Non-invasive Near InfraRed (NIR) based device for AVF (Arteriovenous Fistula) maturation and blood vessel strengthening for dialysis patients.
abs: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) occurs when a person’s kidneys have deteriorated to a point that requires renal replacement therapy. Every five hours, one person in Singapore needs a transplant or has to start dialysis. Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis are the two best alternatives to a kidney transplant. Dialysis helps by remove excess solutes from blood, replacing the function of the dysfunctional kidneys. Hemodialysis requires arterial blood to be drawn from the patient, which is fed into a dialyzer to remove toxins, and the blood is then returned to the patient, taking several hours. Permanent vascular access (VA) is crucial for haemodialysis to be carried out. However, native vasculature cannot withstand continual cannulation, thus arteriovenous fistulae (AVF) are created surgically. The AVF is formed by directly connecting an artery to a vein via an anastomosis. AVFs cannot be used immediately for hemodialysis. They require time to mature. Typically, it is recommended to allow a maturation period of about 3 to 4 months, however, the time period differs from person to person and can only be determined through observation and monitoring of the AVF. One of the most frequent complications in AVFs is adverse maturation. In fact, at least 33% of AVFs never reach proper maturation. While the AVF matures, hemodialysis patients rely on either peritoneal dialysis or dialyzing through a temporary catheter, which has a very high risk of infection. For a disease that has a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 6.2%, it is compelling that ESRD urgently requires cost-saving solutions to improve clinical outcomes and reduce financial burden. In addition, the incidence of diabetes which is the leading cause of kidney failure (accounting for 42% of kidney failure events) is increasing at a CAGR of 11.7%. As this disease population balloons, the need for hemodialysis and vascular access is likely to increase. The National Kidney Foundation Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (K/DOQI) provides guidelines to help improve diagnosis and treatment of kidney disease at all stages and defines an AVF as mature if the AVF (i) has a blood flow rate >600ml/min; (ii) is >6mm in diameter;.and (iii) is <6mm from the skin surface. AVFs mature through a process known as vascular remodelling. Vascular remodelling refers to the homeostatic alteration of blood vessels in response to changes in blood flow rates and conditions. Upon the creation of the AVF, the vascular resistance in the patient’s body falls, leading to immediately higher blood flow rates. Vascular remodelling then primarily occurs through venous dilation and wall thickening to bring the flow rates back down. Vascular remodelling can occur both inwards and outwards. Inward vascular remodelling refers to an increase in vessel thickness coupled with a decrease in lumen size. Conversely, outward vascular remodelling refers to the increase in vessel thickness coupled with an increase in lumen size. A neoint

title: A Novel Cellular Immunotherapy Approach Combining a Compact Anti-GD2 molecule (IFL-GD2) with Expanded, Activated Natural Killer (NKEXP) Cells and Antibody-Coupled T-Cell Receptor (ACTR) T Cells for Childhood Neuroblastoma
abs: Abstract: Neuroblastoma is the commonest extracranial tumour in children and more than a third of patients present with very difficult-to-treat advanced metastatic disease. Thus, despite recent advances, neuroblastoma still accounts for significant proportion of childhood cancer deaths. GD2 is expressed on most cases of neuroblastoma and anti-GD2 antibodies have been shown to be very effective in treating minimal residual disease. However, its efficacy in treating refractory disease is still under study with limited success. In this study we aim to establish the safety and efficacy of a novel Anti-GD2 molecule (In-Vivo Functional Ligand (IFL)-GD2) in combination with Expanded, Activated Natural-Killer(NK) Cells and CD16-41BB-CD3zeta T-Cells in a pre-clinical mouse model of neuroblastoma. IFL-GD2 molecule is an ScFv-Fc construct that is more compact than conventional monoclonal antibodies to allow better tumour penetration. It is also engineered to enhance Antibody-Dependent Cellular-Cytotoxicity(ADCC) when engaged with effector cells. Expanded, Activated NK cells have been shown to have cytotoxic activity - currently under study in Phase II clinical trials, its main limitation is its lack of persistence despite robust initial in-vivo expansion. CAR-T cells have been shown to have excellent cytotoxicity and can persist for extended periods but do not express Fc receptors to engage antibodies. CD16-41BB-CD3zeta T-cells are T-cells with an engineered Fc-receptor which allows binding with antibodies. As CD16-41BB-CD3zeta T-cells have demonstrated efficacy and persistence in early clinical trials, they may provide a deeper and longer lasting remission. With a stepwise approach, IFL-GD2 molecules will undergo large scale production and further purification before further in vitro and in vivo testing in neuroblastoma cell lines and xenograft models. In preparation for Phase I clinical trial initiation, safety and antibody dosing levels will also be determined in combination with Expanded, Activated NK cells and CD16-41BB-CD3zeta T-cells as the main effector cells.

title: A Phase 1, open-label, non-randomised, interventional, single group assignment study of SingaCell in patients with haematological malignancies
abs: Hypothesis and Rationale Transplantation of C7 expanded UCB graft plus a second un-manipulated cord following myeloablative conditioning in patients with haematological malignancies will provide sustained engraftment with the majority demonstrating engraftment with cells from the C7 expanded cord. Aims 1) Evaluate the safety and efficacy of C7 ex vivo expanded CD34+ cells from CBU#1 and infuse together with the CD34– lymphoid cells (from CBU#1) at the point of transplantation along with the higher cell dose non‐manipulated UCB unit (UCB#2) in patients with haematological malignancies following conditioning therapy. 2) Assess the cumulative incidence of patients with neutrophil engraftment at 42 days following transplantation and source of engrafted cells. The Solution: Novel HSPC expansion technology We have identified a novel small molecule, designated C7, with the use of which we are able to expand HSPC, including rare and highly self‐renewing subpopulations that express CD90 and CD49f from frozen‐thawed, non‐enriched UCB grafts. The intention is somewhat similar to the understanding of the use of double cord blood transplant and ex vivo expansion to overcome the cell dose limitation. Methodology & Approach Conduct a Phase 1 Clinical Trial in adult patients with haematological malignancies Importance to science or medicine To our knowledge, this is the only clinical trial in Singapore that is looking at stem cell expansion technology from umbilical cord blood to date. This is currently a niche area with great potential. Potential to not only be translational and improve patient care and outcome but to possibly be a starting point to mimic the use of similar technology to expand other immune cells from cord blood or from adult peripheral blood.

title: Feasibility study using a single operation to acquire nearshore topographic and bathymetry data
abs: Design and modelling tools for coastal and flooding protection which are able to utilize high resolution, and highly accurate geo-spatial data exist in basic form and are being developed further by various vendors to produce reliable flood forecasts in minutes for planning and operational purposes. Such tools require a robust, unified set of data in the inter-tidal zone to produce accurate results for design purposes. Having a unified set of data available for the inter-tidal zone nationally helps to close the gap which presently exists between the domains of the SLA survey maps and MPA Charts due to different datums and varying techniques being used in the inter-tidal zone. The inter-tidal data in combination with SLA and MPA data in the areas adjoining the inter-tidal zone could serve to provide an initial, robust set of high resolution data at the coastal areas for evaluating potential sites and land-use. Most of the suggested survey techniques are non-intrusive in nature and hence would have minimal impact should they be conducted within the Coastal Protection Reserve. Thus, the ability to efficiently collect and produce a reliable, high resolution, accurate and unified dataset which is easily transferable to MPA charts or SLA maps for the purpose of coastal protection can only be seen as beneficial and useful to the industry.

title: Organic thin‐film energy sources for highly distributed nanopower generation
abs: This Proposal seeks to develop fundamental breakthroughs in both doping science & technology and morphology science & technology of charge-doped functional polymer semiconductors for next-generation nanopower sources in indoor photovoltaics, flexible thermoelectric generators, and printed polymer micro-batteries, which together will open up new possibilities for Internet-of-Things, wearable electronics, healthcare monitors, and others. In particular, this will enable highly-distributed self-generation to be achieved in leave-alone, printable systems which continually harvest room light (indoor photovoltaics), or heat flow across small temperature gradient (thermoelectric generators) to provide power, supported by printed, ‘air safe’, polymer batteries. Although the specific bottlenecks for each of the power sources are different, an underlying set of challenges underpin them. We believe this stems from two scientific gaps for organic polymer materials: lack of general understanding of, and technological capability in, (a) doping control over the requisite wide range from ultralow (sub-10^16 cm^‒3) to intermediate to high levels (10^21 cm^‒3), together with work function design, and (b) morphology stabilization in multi-component systems in the nm to 10-nm length scale, compatible with scalable manufacturing. Therefore we believe these could be tackled holistically. Over the years, we have developed unique insights to some of these issues in related devices: light-emitting diodes, transistors and solar cells, which we believe provide strong foundation to tackle these new challenges. Our overarching strategy is to exploit present first-mover advantage in the self-compensated, charge-doped polymer platform that we have pioneered, and low-thermal-budget thermal crosslinking that we have recently demonstrated (unpublished). The former allows us to design materials with the required work function and doping level, at will, and with good ambient processability and stability, which are not possible previously, overcoming a major fundamental hurdle. The latter allows us to stabilize morphology for films up to hundreds of micron, not possible with photocrosslinking due to limited optical absorption depth. These provide our competitive edge. We anticipate key innovations will be achieved in new understanding of materials motifs, and their integration into the self-compensated, charge-doped polymer platform, and practical devices. Preliminary data suggest this may be feasible. The success in this Project will not only contribute to manpower talent for the advanced manufacturing and engineering sector of Industry 4.0, but also the innovation/knowledge base that would continue to make Singapore an attractive place to anchor advanced manufacturing and/or R&D activities.
kw: plastic electronics; organic semiconductors; thin-film thermoelectric generator; polymer micro-batteries; indoor photovoltaics; Internet-of-Things

title: Optimizing Feeds for Singaporean Red Snapper Aquaculture
abs: Red snapper is a high-value food fish species cultured in Singapore. However, there are no commercial feeds that are specifically formulated to meet the nutrient requirement of this species. Rather, the present production of red snapper relies on commercial feeds that are generic for marine carnivorous fish species, which generally contain high levels of fish meal and fish oil, leading to elevated feed costs. Furthermore, lacking of a tailored diet holds back productivity and increases risk of disease. Therefore, any improvement in profitability and productivity of the red snapper aquaculture industry warrants the development of cost-effective and optimal feed formulations by using alternative ingredients that are locally available. This project will lead to the development of optimised and cost effective diet formulation for red snapper. Firstly, various aspects of the nutrient requirement and utilization by red snapper will be determined so that it is understood what the species requires for optimal growth and health. The results from this first component will form a knowledge base for the evaluation of alternative ingredients and the formulation of practical feeds. Subsequently, alternative raw materials will be evaluated for their nutritive values and their suitability to replace fish meal and fish oil in practical red snapper feeds. Alternative raw materials, including those available locally, will be characterized and screened for their nutritional compositions and digestibility coefficients. Then feed formulations will be developed by using low levels of fish meal and fish oil combined with selected alternative ingredients for juvenile and grow-out fish. The feeding trials for each of the life-stages will be carried out to assess digestibility, growth, feed conversion, and nutrient retention. Cost benefit analysis will be performed to evaluate the cost effectiveness of the feed formulations. Finally, the feed formulations will be validated by on-farm feeding trials. The optimized diets are expected to improve feed conversion ratio by 20% and benefit red snapper aquaculture operations in Singapore and the broader region through improved productivity and profitability.
kw: optimal feed; nutritional requirement; cost effectiveness; tropical aquaculture; alternative raw materials; sustainable feed

title: Developing Genetic Resources for Red Snapper, an Important Marine Food Fish for Singapore
abs: Red Snapper (Lutjanus erythropterus) is an important and high-value Singaporean aquaculture species that is attracting substantial interest and new industry investment. To significantly boost local production, lower farming risk and increase consumer availability, industry requires access to quality and genetically improved snapper seedstock. Currently, however, the Singaporean industry is plagued by poor quality seedstock. There is no information broodstock genetic diversity, what their provenance and actual taxonomy are, and how traits would respond to selection. Moreover, there also are no genomic resources to enable development of efficient breeding programs for Red Snapper. This project will address these deficiencies and deliver to industry genetically selected and diverse founder broodstock based on modern genomic tools and knowledge on how commercial traits (growth, survival, flesh quality traits) respond to selection. It will do this through a series of science-driven and inter-linking activities proven effective in enabling instigation of breeding programs for other species (i.e. barramundi, black tiger prawn), based on animals cultured in three important aquaculture farms of Singapore (project collaborators). These activities include i) the first reference genome for the species as the foundation of subsequent genomic analyses; ii) genetic audits on farmed and wild populations to establish levels of genetic variability captured and where new genetic diversity will be sought; iii) development of a Red Snapper 70 K SNP genotyping array to allow estimation of heritability, correlations and genomic breeding values for commercial traits at harvest within farms; and iv) the establishment of high genetic merit foundation breeding populations, selected from 150,000 individuals from six different countries which will be allocated to industry collaborators and MAC/SAF’s hatchery facilities. Results from this project will be directly translated into industry through the availability of disease-free and high-quality seedstock supply and through a workshop for farmers, investors and students on the culture of Singaporean Red Snappers.
kw: Food security, table fish, omega-3, high-quality fillet, genetic diversity, selective breeding, agri-tech, aquaculture

title: Flora Fauna SG - AI for Image Recognition of Flora and Fauna
abs: We propose to build a complete system consisting of a mobile app and a backend database that can recognize plants and animals from images and photographs taken. This will be the first mobile app that focuses specifically on large-scale plant and animal recognition in Singapore, with its very high biodiversity. For the AI plant classifier, we have developed a proof-of-concept prototype using the ResNet [1] architecture which is able to recognize 15 plant species with a top-3 accuracy of 92.6%. In our proposed system, we will build a robust classifier that can recognize more than one 300 common plant species and 225 common animal types from images and photographs. We will need to overcome three main challenges. First, the main challenge in developing a visual recognition system targeted at real-world applications is the ability of learning classifiers incrementally. The initial classifier will be trained on a pre-collected dataset prepared by our team. As people start to use our app to recognize plants, more and more images will be uploaded by the users to our server, which can be utilized to refine the initial classifier. We will leverage recent work to select a subset of images from both original samples and new samples to refine the existing model. The loss function also needs to be re-defined in order to reduce the catastrophic forgetting phenomenon. We will design a state-of-the-art deep learning based incremental learning techniques and integrate them into our plant identifier system. The second challenge is that the number of samples for each plant species can be quite unbalanced. To solve this issue, we will explore zero-shot learning techniques to classify data based on very few or even no labelled examples. The third challenge lies in the interaction between the plant identifier and the app users. Ideally, a user should upload a high quality image of a plant, based on which our system is able to make a prediction with high confidence. However, in practice, as app users are not AI experts, the images uploaded by them might not be always be good enough for our system to make a robust prediction. We will implement techniques that will perform automatic quality assessments of photos through machine learning techniques, such as a convolutional neural network, and provide interactive guidance on the app to aid the lay user in taking better images.
kw: Image Recognition, Image Classification, Mobile App

title: Design and Fabrication of a Cooler vest for Tropical Climate
abs: Workers working outdoors in hot and humid climate like Singapore face tremendous heat stress. To address this, SIT, LTA and SMRT will collaborate to explore how existing (safety) vest can be incorporated with cooling technologies to provide acceptable thermal comfort to their workers. Current market does not have a cooling vest that is lightweight, portable and provide sustained cooling. Products based on traditional cooling methods are typically bulky with short operating time. Recently, thermoelectric cooling (TEC) elements, which make use of the peltier effects, have shown great potential in cooling wearables due to their lightweight, solid state, and adjustable cooling power. At this point in time, it is deemed that the TEC technology is developed sufficiently and there are sufficient literatures to prove the potential of this technology to bring thermal comfort to civilian workers. However, a product that meets the requirement for local civilian workers working under hot and humid environment has not yet been developed and are not available freely. This project thus proposed to develop cooling vests using TEC technology to meet civilian workers requirement. To achieve the stated aim, the team will take a five-pronged approach. First, a complete market survey and evaluation of current products will be undertaken to form a baseline to evaluate the final designed cooler vest. Second, the team will work on designing a cooler vest based on optimal placement of off-the-shelves TEC. Third, the internal TEC design will be studied and optimized. In parallel, efforts will be put into sourcing for a suitable power generation solution to power the cooler vest. Lastly, attention will be paid to the garment design to ensure efficient heat transfer and ergonomic comfort. To support these approaches, the team will build a realistic numerical model to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the design process. The cooler vest prototype fabricated will be subjected to actual users’ evaluation to provide valuable feedback during the design process. The resulting cooling vest can be used in many industries, for example construction, engineering and services industry to name a few. SMRT, LTA and SIAEC have given an estimation of about 7500 workers benefitting from this technology. With the rise in number of rail workers and the high proportion of workers in the construction sector in Singapore, the impact on successful completion will be significant.
kw: Thermoelectric coolers, peltier effect, cooler vest, combat heat stress

title: Remote monitoring of hybrid power and propulsion systems for smart ships
abs: Adoption of comprehensive monitoring and maintenance strategies for shipboard machinery and systems improves ship operation, sustainability and profitability. Recent developments show that performance monitoring of ship systems has a great potential at the cost of signiﬁcant data requirements. In this respect, this project aims to develop a novel methodology for intelligent, system-level modelling for the monitoring of main engine performance utilising data acquired through reporting and sensoring systems, for a novel hybrid powering and propulsion system. Acquired data representing the engine’s new conditions are input to the model and model output reﬂects a gauge of their normality, when compared to the original dataset, for analogous operating conditions. This aids the dynamic detection of ship machinery incipient faults, contributing to the minimisation of ship downtime and increase of its operability. The case application of this modelling technique is on actual ship machinery raw data, complemented by a sensitivity analysis. The case will demonstrate the applicability of the developed methodology in the identiﬁcation of more efficient patterns of ship operation. The case ship will be a new harbour tug used for shipyard operations, which features a unique hybrid powering and propulsion system. The proposed work programme comprises 5 Work Packages (WPs). In WP1 detailed specification and requirements for the monitoring system architecture will be derived. In WP2 the sensoring system for monitoring of machinery performance will be installed onboard the test (case) ship, and initial tests will be carried out for its calibration and correct performance. In WP3 the data analytics and AI/ML computation models will be developed and tested against existing data as currently gathered. In WP4 extensive tests of the prototype (system onboard the ship and of the algorithms) will be carried out, including sensitivity analyses, for calibration and verification purposes. Finally, in WP5 the final fine-tuning of the system developed is to be carried out. SembCorp Marine act as industry collaborators for this project with their experience as systems’ integrators and designers, through their R&D Division. SembCorp will make significant in-kind contributions (manpower), and be involved in the development of actual sensoring system on-board their harbor tug for test bedding. The focus of the proposal is on developing systems and architecture for data collection, aggregation, transmission, and application of ML either remotely or in site (edge computing) to derive useful insights on vessel performance.
kw: Smart ships; remote monitoring; hybrid propulsion; optimised operation; sustainability; environmental protection

title: Developing Improved Anti-oxidative Product from Mellow Fermented Multifunctional Seaweed Ingredients
abs: There is a large market (valued in the hundreds of billions annually) with a predicted annual growth of 5-10% for naturally-sourced cosmeceutical ingredients and health food products. In addition, there is an established demand from local industries for active ingredients from botanical products for personal care and food, based on the technical needs posted by the Ministry of Trade and Industries. As the region has untapped agricultural potential for the harvesting of seaweed and marine algae species, by bridging Southeast Asian suppliers to global markets, we can add value by processing active naturally-derived ingredients to optimise their anti-oxidative, anti-diabetic, anti-aging and anti-microbial properties. Thus, this project aims to develop mellow-tasting multifunctional seaweed-based active ingredients with enhanced anti-oxidative properties relevant for multiple health product markets by a novel fermentation process using a fungal probiotic (Eurotium cristatum, previously used in tea and soya residue) on regionally sourced seaweed or algae species (e.g. Ulva spp.). We plan to proceed to develop a cosmeceutical product, a food product and the upscaling of the fermentation process for industrial purposes. The fermentation process will undergo multi-variable optimisation, followed by an assessment of the health-related properties using a panel of industry-standard tests, assessment of safety, and measurement of sensory properties including smell and texture to ensure consumer acceptability. We have conducted the feasibility study regarding the fermentation of seaweed (Ulva spp) using Eurotium cristatum. The preliminary results indicate that the Ulva spp contains nutrients for the fermenting Eurotium cristatum. It is found that DPPH inhibitory activity of seaweed is increased by 13% and the smell disappears after fermented 13 days. Therefore, this study points out the high potential for success of this project. We are very confident of the significant technical development of this project in terms of Technology Readiness Level for commercialisation building on the Background IP. Targeted improvement is from TRL 4 to TRL 6-7.
kw: seaweed fermentation, Eurotium cristatum, multifunctional ingredient, antioxidant, anti-aging

title: An Artificial Intelligence Enabled Wearable TCM Pulse Analyser for Heart Failure Detection
abs: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death for both men and women, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). In the U.S., one in every four deaths is a result of CVD. In Singapore, 17 people die from CVD every day. CVD accounted for 30.1% of all deaths in 2017. Recently, many research works mentioned that continuous monitoring of the pulses would help to prevent the CVD at the early stage as well as to alarm users when the pulse signals become unusual so as to avoid situations like stroke, myocardial infarction, and sudden death. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) pulse diagnosis has been used by TCM physicians to assess patients’ health conditions for more than 2,500 years. We propose to develop a wearable TCM pulse analyser enabled with artificial intelligence for self-monitoring of cardiovascular disease like heart failure. The pulse analyser will be developed based on a novel micro tubular epidermal sensor, which can accurately sense and collect wrist arterial pulse signals. Various micro tactile sensor structures will be explored and fabricated using in-house facilities. An easy-to-use mechanical structure to hold the sensor and to control the exerting pressure will also be designed and fabricated. Both electronics and firmware will be developed for pulse signal reading and processing. Various filters and algorithms will be explored to de-noise and remove signal drift. The signal processing sub-system will further control the adjustment of the pulse signal collection at three positions (Cun, Guan, Chi) and three depths (Fu, Zhong, Chen). Finally, we will also develop pulse pattern feature extraction, selection, and classification models with a premier focus on heart failure diagnosis based on TCM theory. We will use techniques such as time-domain feature extraction, wavelet decomposition, and ensemble-learning method combining Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM), deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Fuzzy Neural Network (FNN) to enhance the predictive performance. We believe that our edge on in-house microsensor fabrication capability, using the latest microfabrication techniques, and access to the related background IP, will enable us to develop a highly accurate and sensitive three-depth and three-position pulse analyser with wireless communication and artificial intelligence to process and analyse the data. The developed wearable TCM pulse analyser will be a viable healthcare product for health-conscious consumers and people with a high risk of heart failure.
kw: Artificial Intelligence; Heart Failure; Wearable Electronics; Microfluidic Pressure Sensor; Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: A Modular Reconfigurable Intelligent Autonomous Mobile Robotics System (AMRS) for Industry Application and Research Training
abs: This proposal presents the development of a modular autonomous mobile robotic (AMRS) platform that is designed to provide cross-discipline industries with improved capabilities, and the robotics system can be easily reconfigured with ready add-on modules to operate within a range of different environmental conditions. The proposed modular AMRS comprised of four modular systems; The first module is the basic robot base platform & drive mechanism. The robot base platform can be reconfigured to two-wheel differential-drive, four-wheel skip-drive, or four-wheel mecanum-drive. The second is the sensors fusion module. The sensors fusion system can be configured with 3D Lidar, 2D LIDAR, Vision, ultrasonic and IR sensors; use for navigation, obstacle avoidance, and 3-D pattern reconstruction, and map building. The 3rd module is the robotic actuator joint; the manipulator can be configuring from two-degree-of-freedom to 6-DoF, in articulated form or SCARA form. The fourth module is the open-source ROS/ROS2/ROS-I software and control architecture. To test the AMRS system's underlying performance and capabilities, a prototype will be developed using our TP patented drive mechanism technology (Patent No. S102201709761U), and the intelligent charging station (IDF No. RTDIDF003). The results of this testing will validate the system proposed positioning accuracy.
kw: Modular robot, Autonomous robot, Intelligent System, Modular actuator, path planning, Differential Drive, Mecanum Drive, skip drive

title: Rapid and Non-Enzymatic Detection of Microbial Contamination in Water Samples
abs: Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) are used in many countries for seafood cultivation. It is crucial to monitor microbial pathogen populations in aquaculture systems in order to avoid mass mortality due to disease outbreaks. Effective microbial detection systems are thus critical for ensuring high-yield and high-quality aquaculture produce. Currently, the microbial presence in RAS systems is monitored by visualization of water turbidity and observation of fish behaviour. These methods are not precise to determine the level of microbial contamination in water samples. Although there are other methods to determine microbial content, such as ATP-luciferase assay and culture-based bacterial plate count approaches, these methods have their deficiencies and require specific instrumentation. Hence, they are seldom deployed to monitor microbial contamination in aquaculture farms. Lack of vigilance and frequent monitoring practice can lead to overgrowth of pathogens, resulting in massive disease outbreaks and mortality in the aquaculture farms. This proposal describes a new transition metal chemistry-based approach for detecting microbial presence, which is intended for water cleanliness verification. The assay is quick, portable and easy-to-use. Therefore, it is especially suited for microbial testing of water quality in resource-scarce locations where access to equipment and centralised laboratories is problematic. Added advantages of this unique chemistry include easy adjustment to allow quantitative measurements with spectrophotometry and applicability in general hygiene monitoring. We believe that this rapid microbial biomass test will be beneficial to the aquaculture industry. It could also be deployed in water treatment plants, the military, and in some areas of recreational use, for example, camping, hiking, and adventure expeditions in remote locations.
kw: Non-enzymatic, instrument-free, detection, ATP, microbial biomass, transition metal complexes, multidentate ligands

title: Autonomous Neuromorphic Vision System for Advanced Manufacturing
abs: Manufacturing remains a key pillar of Singapore’s economy and continues to increase its importance, come post COVID-19. Higher usage of machine vision, a critical component of factory automation, will ensure automated quality assurance of product along its manufacturing process. However, even with the adoption of deep learning technology into machine vision, there are still gaps pertaining to cost and inspection performance that prevent full exploitation of it, to maximize its effectiveness. To overcome these gaps, a unique autonomous inspection system that models all possible lighting conditions that accentuate the desired product defect characteristics and learns this defect on-the-fly without any need for high number of image datasets is proposed. Key innovations on a universal illumination module that leverages on patented programmable illumination control for producing defect-focused image, and silicon-based Neuromorphic AI hardware and firmware for real-time defect characterization will be developed, with consideration for being low-cost, configurable, compact and portable to meet diverse manufacturing sectors’ needs. The proposed Neuromorphic AI incorporates a custom hardware and firmware to provide AI-on-the-edge cognitive co-processing functionalities. This Radial Basis Function Artificial Neural Network (RBF-ANN) based AI hardware is low power and does not require high power, high-speed and high throughput computational hardware commonly used by any Deep Learning platforms. It implements machine learning on-the-fly, cognitive pattern recognition and inference capability to infer defects from image features. The on-the-fly machine learning ability is a unique feature which differentiates from other Artificial/Deep Neural Networks implementations. This ability allows supervised training of RBF-ANN with the required knowledge dataset, and for a pre-trained RBF-ANN to learn on-the-fly (supervised or unsupervised), new knowledge and appends autonomously to its existing knowledge pool. Thus, a pre-trained ANN gets smarter over time with newly available knowledge. The second unique feature demonstrates the fact that the RBF-ANN is a universal approximator, with the uniqueness of having a simple and fixed three-layer architecture being implemented as a hybrid low power MCU-based hardware and firmware solution as compared to the complex many-layers DNN that requires high power, high-speed and high throughput computational hardware. The last but the most important feature is the fusion of unique front-end illumination designed to enable defects of manufactured parts and components being accentuated distinctly from the noisy background with the back-end Neuromorphic AI that processes this specially-treated image for on-the-fly training and subsequent inference to achieve real-time performance of high accuracy and consistency that meets the stringent manufacturing inspection criteria.
kw: Machine Vision, Universal Illumination, Programmable Control, Cosmetic Surface Defects, Neuromorphic AI Silicon Chip, RCE-ANN, Defect-Specific Illumination Library.

title: An Adaptive Compensatory Framework – How Social Cognition Changes with Aging
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: The main objective of the study is to examine age-related changes in social cognition—the ability to decode, understand, and react to social signals (e.g., gaze and emotional expressions) from other people. Adopting a life-span perspective, we will be examining older adults (aged 60-90) and younger adults (aged 18-30) on a range of social cognitive abilities, such as integration of multiple social cues to understand others’ referential intents and inferences about others’ mental states (i.e., theory-of-mind, ToM), as well as investigating the behavioral and neural correlates of age-related differences in social cognition. We propose an integrative neurocognitive account of aging and social cognition, suggesting that the level of social cognitive functioning will change as an outcome of both the structural and functional changes of the aging brain and an individual’s life course experience. The ability to perceive, process, and act upon social cues appropriately is found to be a critical predictor of individual social competency and mental health across the human lifespan. Importantly, deficits in social cognitive processes could have adverse effects on social relationships and well-being in older adulthood. Social disconnectedness in older adults in turn will impact their physical health, mental well-being, and cognitive functioning. Most of the past studies on aging focused on factors such as general cognitive abilities, and little research has focused on how lifelong accumulation of cognitive-enhancing experiences (e.g., SES, bilingualism, social motivation) may attenuate social-cognitive decline in aging. In addition, neuroimaging results provide evidence that with age, there are structural and functional changes in the brain regions recruited for cognitive function, and recent studies have highlighted marked age-related changes in some social-cognitive abilities, such as emotion recognition and socially relevant decision-making. Despite the importance of social cognition across the lifespan and emerging research in related areas, there are several important research gaps in the psychological and neurocognitive perspectives of social cognition in normal aging that remain to be addressed. First, the complexity of social cognition and its multifaceted nature call for a multiple-level investigation of different components of social-cognitive processing and which components are most vulnerable in older adults. Second, studying social cognition and the related brain structural and functional network will cover a key gap. Third, the developmental trajectory of social cognition across the lifespan (adulthood) and the impact of individual life course variables on the psychological and neural correlates of social cognition in the context of aging has not been examined previously. title: Study of the Mechanisms Governing the Nucleation and Growth of Metal-Organic Frameworks
abs: Unlike zeolites or other porous materials, MOFs possess a well-defined, and highly porous crystalline structure, whose pore sizes, chemical compositions, and framework designs are precisely tunable. Because of these reasons, they are excellent candidates for many industrial applications such as gas storage, separation, catalysis, sensing, and drug delivery. The functionality of MOFs can be further enhanced by the inclusion of nanoparticle (NP) guests into the MOF host framework, forming hybrid (NP@MOF) colloidal materials. For example, MOF encapsulation of NPs increases the stability of the enclosed catalytic NP while a porous structure can provide a reactant-specific selectivity and locally (at NP surface) enrich the reactant concentration and thus increase the reaction rates. Our present understanding of how these industrially important MOFs nucleate, grow, and encapsulate NPs is based on indirect methods or post-synthesis characterization techniques. Because these current laborious trial-and-error approaches cannot track the growth trajectories of individual MOF nanocrystals in real-time, they reveal very little about the pathways through which MOF crystals form. Lack of mechanistic insight makes it almost impossible to predict the outcome of new synthesis processes by generalizing the finding from other but similar systems. The situation is further complicated due to the lack of reliable theoretical approaches that could have aided the design of MOF systems. All theoretical approaches require proper experimental guidance because it is hard to computationally account for non-classical nucleation and growth pathways that are often present for materials with open framework structure, such as zeolites, MOFs, and COFs (covalent organic frameworks). Reactive-force-field MD simulations that account for simple bond-formation and bond-breaking can only capture simple processes that are in nanoseconds time-scale and are unable to simulate the processes that occur in a sequence of multiple steps and last from several seconds to minutes. Calculations based on density functional theory require the detailed knowledge of the state, which again can only be resolved if the intermediate states are known. Therefore, the nanoscale mechanisms governing the synthesis of MOF-based nanomaterials is essential for fine-tuning their properties but remains elusive with many unresolved intermediate steps. To resolve these intermediate steps, we have to directly observe the formation dynamics of MOFs in real-time with sub-nanometer resolution. Here, with the aim of understanding the general rules that govern the formation of MOFs and MOF-based systems, we propose to use in situ TEM direct imaging in liquids to provide the detailed mechanistic insights into (1) the nucleation and growth of MOFs from solution; (2) dynamics of NP encapsulation by MOFs. title: Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning
abs: In this project, we will investigate new algorithms to enable effective and efficient self-supervised learning. First, we will formulate new methods that can learn effective global- and local-aware representation from predicting flow fields and motion uncertainties in unlabelled videos. Novel approaches will be formulated to cope with ambiguity and complexity of motions extracted from in-the-wild videos. Second, we will investigate novel methods to facilitate the learning of a deep network by distilling valuable knowledge from heterogeneous self-supervised pretext tasks. Third, we will explore new joint optimization of deep clustering and feature learning techniques to allow highly efficient and stable online self-supervised learning.
kw: Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning, Computer Vision

title: BlockChain I/O: A framework for cross-chain interoperability
abs: As described above (in Research Details), we want to address the following scientific objectives in the project in the context of blockchain interoperability: (i) decentralized yet defragmented identities, (ii) fine grained access control and (iii) support for cross-chain general transactions. The cornerstone of our approach is to build on top of existing systems, rather than to replace them using a framework that unifies blockchain systems to provide a simple, scalable, secure interface for accessing and manipulating data. For handling identity, we envision a different form of modularity which involves an ID Authorization Platform, itself built on a blockchain, which helps as an identity aggregator, where users can determine sharing policies that are subsequently enforced using smart contracts, without the need for explicit participation from the user on every occasion. We note the mutual dependency among identity and access control. To that end we propose the decoupling of access control from user smart contracts and implement it as a system contract. And for policy specification, we explore declarative language which is friendly for human interpretation and can also be more readily used to express typical regulatory requirements by relying on templates. For transactional guarantees, we foremost propose to translate the idea of mini-transaction abstraction from database literature, along with the primitives of read-only transactions, to support atomicity and diverse degrees of concurrency. A major bottleneck in realizing these in a self-contained manner is the communication bottleneck. To that end, we disentangle the issue of communication, and abstract it as a separate publish/subscribe service which can, in principle, even be achieved over a (multi-)cloud infrastructure. Thus, in contrast to existing approaches which attempt to address these issues considering blockchains in isolation and competing with existing It infrastructure, we embrace the idea of a symbiotic coexistence of blockchain technology with the traditional IT infrastructure stack. This viewpoint augurs well with our objective, where we envision blockchains becoming part of the mainstream, and is also the underpinning of our approach, and why we are confident of its feasibility and practical impact.
kw: Blockchain; Interoperability; Identity Management; Access Control; Transactions

title: Efficient String Reasoning for Software Vulnerability Detection
abs: Software development is always error-prone, resulting in applications that are vulnerable to attacks by malicious users. Furthermore, the global accessibility of modern software enables an attack at some place to be performed from some other place in the world. Therefore, cyber-security is “today the most significant battleground between attackers and those with computer resources and data to defend, and it is likely to remain so for the foreseeable future”. To detect cyber-security vulnerabilities, the state-of-the-art technique is Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) because of its capability of automatically generating test cases with high coverage and thus detecting corner case bugs/vulnerabilities. The efficiency of the DSE technique relies on its two core techniques: constraint solving and interpolation. Constraint solving techniques help generate automatically test cases that witness the real attacks while interpolation techniques make the whole DSE framework scalable while preserving the high coverage. Given the rise of security attacks on web applications, web browser engines, JIT compilers, IoT applications, etc., the two techniques need to be adapted to handle a new kind of constraints which is of string data type. Although there exist DSE techniques for software applications and string solving techniques for a rich set of constraint language, they are still not precise, efficient, and scalable enough. In this project, we will propose 1) an efficient string solving technique for a more expressive string constraint language, including real-world complicated regular expressions and 2) an efficient interpolation technique for these kinds of string constraints in order to support the detection of modern security attacks. In addition to proposing fundamental and core techniques, we will also examine the applicability of these techniques to different domains such as web security, IoT security. The proposed techniques will allow us to achieve both precision and scalability for software security analysis techniques. This in turn helps ensure the safety and security of modern software systems in Singapore’s Smart Nation ambitions.
kw: Symbolic Execution, String Solving, Interpolation Techniques, Formal Semantics, Web Security, IoT Security

title: Multidimensional simulation of rarefied gases in astronautics and microflows
abs: This project focuses on the numerical simulation of rarefied gas dynamics, which is an important branch of fluid mechanics, and plays an essential role in astronautics (such as the re-entry flow for retrievable satellites) and micro-electro-mechanical-systems (such as flow sensors, resonators). An accurate simulation of rarefied gas dynamics requires solving equations in gas kinetic theory, whose fundamental mathematical model is the Boltzmann equation, which governs the seven-dimensional distribution function (1D time, 3D spatial variable, and 3D velocity variable). The aim of this project is to find an accurate numerical approximation of this high-dimensional Boltzmann equation, and apply the method to engineering problems such as space shuttles and electric comb-drives. Currently in the literature, it shows that such a simulation for a practical problem is still far from feasible. The success of this project will be a significant step forward and make the full three-dimensional simulation tractable in a cluster of moderate size (less than 100 nodes). Efficient numerical methods depend on efficient discretization of both spatial and velocity variables. For the spatial variable, we plan to take the method of discontinuous Galerkin to achieve high order. Our discretization of the velocity variable will take the idea from the classical moment method, which was originally proposed as a modelling tool. The moment method is efficient in most cases. However, in our preliminary studies, it is found that for high speed flows, the method may fail to converge. Therefore, the research questions we are going to address in this project include: 1. Fix the convergence issue of the classical moment method; 2. Develop fast algorithms to discretize the Boltzmann equation; 3. Implement spatial-velocity joint adaptive method to increase numerical efficiency; 4. Parallelize the algorithm with good load balancing. It is worth emphasizing that the successful solution to the first question will be a significant contribution to applied mathematics and theoretical fluid mechanics. The strategy to fix the convergence issue comes from a deep understanding of the general moment system through our preliminary works. In general, such a fix requires choosing the parameters in the discretization in a non-classical way, and it must be coupled with the hyperbolicity fix in our previous works to obtain robustness. Then, the fast algorithms for the Boltzmann equation will be based on this work, and we are going to couple it with the Hermite spectral method for the collision term, the steady-state preserving technique, and the discontinuous Galerkin method to get fast algorithms for the complete Boltzmann equation. The adaptive method will follow the general strategy to perform mesh refinement/coarsening and increment/decrement of basis functions. title: Modelling and simulation of wetting dynamics on solid surfaces
abs: Wetting of a solid surface is an example of the moving contact line problem in classical fluid mechanics. It concerns with the dynamics of the contact line, which is the intersection of a fluid interface (e.g. liquid-vapour interface) with a solid wall, on a solid substrate. Understanding the wetting dynamics is of practical importance, as it is relevant to many industrial applications such as ink-jet printing, coating, micro-fluidics, transport of droplet by electric field, etc. It is also of scientific interest as the problem contains many interesting mathematical and physical phenomena e.g. the formation of singularities, hysterical behaviour etc. This project focuses on two problems: (1) electro-wetting on dielectric, and (2) wetting dynamics on elastic substrate or membrane. The latter generalizes the classical fluid-structure interaction (FSI) problem which has been limited to the case of a single-phase fluid coupled with some deformable structures. This work will lead to a better understanding of the interface profiles, singularities in the electric and stress fields, and the detailed physical process near the moving contact line. For both problems, we have studied the static interface profiles and obtained some preliminary results. In this project, we will focus on the dynamical problems and develop mathematical models and efficient numerical methods to simulate the respective wetting process. These are very challenging problems in both mathematical and numerical aspects. The problem of electro-wetting involves the coupling of the two-phase fluid dynamics with the solution of the electric field in an irregular domain, while the problem of wetting on deformable substrates involves the coupling of fluid dynamics with the deformation of solid substrate. In both problems, the static solutions are computed based on the minimization of the free energy of the respective system. For the dynamics, we derive the boundary/interface conditions based on the consideration of energy dissipations and thermodynamics laws. The numerical methods will be based on weal formations in which the interface and contact line conditions can be naturally imposed. We use alternating numerical schemes in which the solution of the fluid dynamics is decoupled from the solution of the electric field in the problem of electro-wetting and the deformation of the substrate in the second case. In addition, the time-dependent irregular fluid domain poses a challenge in the simulation. We will use a moving mesh method and construct the mesh at each time step so that it fits the evolving interfaces. As interesting applications, we will study the singular behaviors of the electric field and the curvature of the interface at the contact line, the saturation of the contact angle in electro-wetting, the formation of cusps at the contact line on elastic substrate/membrane, the stick-slip motion of the moving contact line, etc.
kw: moving contact lines; electro-wetting; fluid-structure interaction; finite element methods

title: Learning Robotic Perception without Strong Supervision
abs: Many sub-problems within robotic perception are extensively studied by the computer vision and robotics communities, and impressive results have been shown in recent years with the use of deep learning. However, most existing state-of-the-art deep learning models are trained on huge amount of data with labeled ground truth. This is commonly known as strongly supervised learning. This is because a deep network, i.e. neural network is essentially a universal function approximator parameterized by a set of learnable weights that maps an input to an output. The deep network is trained by minimizing the sum-of-squares loss between the predicted output from the deep network and the given ground truth over the learnable weight parameters. Since it is typical for a deep network to consists of millions of learnable weight parameters, the number of training examples must be large for the learning to be effective. An insufficient amount of training dataset easily leads to overfitting, where the learned deep network cannot generalize well to unseen examples during inference. To fulfil the requirement of training deep networks with huge amount of ground truth, several datasets are created. These datasets consist of many training examples for strongly supervised deep learning to be effective, and a different training dataset with large amount of training examples is needed for each task and each domain. However, the process to label the ground truth training datasets is often labor intensive, time consuming and costly, since every detail in the ground truth data must be carefully labeled. Furthermore, the labeling of every new task is a context switch that requires the labeller to pay attention to very different details of the data. Despite the success of deep learning on many different computer vision tasks, the requirement of fully supervised learning with huge amount of ground truth training data prohibits the use of deep learning for many tasks, where huge training ground truth datasets are either unavailable or impossible to obtain. In view of this limitation, the objective of this research proposal is to study and propose methods to train deep networks for important robotic perception tasks on datasets without or with very few fully labeled ground truth. This research goal is largely inspired by the fact that human beings do not require so many ``training" data to learn a task. We focus our study of training deep networks without strong supervision on two important areas in robotic perception: (1) Deep learning for 3D point clouds. More specifically, we will work on the three sub-tasks of 3D point cloud-based (i) weakly-/semi-supervised and few-shot semantic segmentation, (ii) weakly-supervised and in-category semi-supervised 3D object detection, and unsupervised and weakly-supervised rigid/non-rigid point cloud registration problems. title: AI-Lyricist: A Music-Informed Automatic Lyrics Generation System for Language Learning
abs:
Automatic lyrics generation (ALG) is a challenging and important research problem with many potential applications. Despite some initial attempts from music information retrieval (MIR), natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) research communities, ALG is still a nascent idea that has yet to be developed into an established concept.
Our research questions stem from research in psychology and neuroscience which has shown that language learners benefit from singing in a foreign language. We have developed a mobile app titled “Singing and Listening to Improve Our Natural Speaking (SLIONS)”, the first of its kind to transform this idea into practice. Our initial experimental data are encouraging. However, the language teachers’ and students’ feedback has led us to solve a more general research problem, formulated as generating novel yet meaningful lyrics given a MIDI file which reflects the user’s preference and the required vocabulary as input. Our proposed AI-enabled solution seeks to achieve a performance similar to a professional lyricist. We envision that our solution will have many potential applications in educational and medical settings, such as personalized language learning and therapy.

title: Topology-based featurization for machine learning models in materials informatics
abs: The great importance of materials innovation and design cannot be overemphasized. Currently, data-driven materials informatics provides a great promise for material innovation. However, the lack of an efficient featurization or feature engineering has significantly hindered the performance of machine learning models in materials informatics. In this project, we propose a topology-based featurization framework for material informatics. We propose to use topological data analysis (TDA), in particular, persistent homology (PH), for the quantitative characterization of material structures. Unlike previous molecular descriptors, persistent homology, which is deeply rooted in algebraic topology and computational topology, is able to embed geometric information into topological invariants, thus provides a bridge between geometry and topology. Essentially, TDA provides a new representation of material structures. Further, a series of newly-developed TDA models, including weighted PH, interactive PH, persistent cohomology, and bipartite-graph-based PH, are considered for the incorporation of physical, chemical and interactional properties of the materials into topological representation, for the first time. In particular, bipartite-graph-based PH is proposed for the detailed characterization of interactions between hybrid components, i.e., organic and inorganic parts of materials, and interactions between material layers. These TDA models enable us to put structure and physical properties on the same footing, thus significantly improving the feature engineering performance. Moreover, topological features, which are suitable for machine learning models, are generated from the TDA results. Various approaches, including barcode statistics, binning approach, persistent landscapes, persistent path, etc, can be considered to convert persistent barcodes (or persistent diagrams) information into quantitative feature vectors, or 2D/3D representations. Distance measurements or metrics, including Gromov-Hausdorff distance, Wasserstein distance, bottleneck distance, etc, can be defined on persistent barcodes, and further used in similarity learning and metric learning models. Finally, our TDA-based learning models will be validated on established material datasets and used in halide perovskite property analysis and material design. Specifically, halide perovskites have been hailed as one of the top emerging optoelectronic materials for solar cells and light emitting devices. Motivated by the great success of TDA models in biomolecular structure characterization and featurization (TDA-based learning models have consistently delivered state-of-art results in drug design and D3R Grand challenge competition), and our recent results on topological characterization and classification of perovskite structures, we will validate our TDA-based learning models using various established perovskite datasets, including those for the reap-rest-recovery cycle analysis, stability eng

title: Investigating the importance of cholesterol homeostasis for neuronal function.
abs: Both age-associated declines in cognitive function and neurodegenerative conditions are often associated with pathological changes in neuronal lipids. Thus, ameliorating these changes may provide a novel avenue for counteracting such conditions and for improving quality of life for the rapidly aging populations that now characterize highly developed countries, including Singapore. This is not a simple task, however, as we do not fully understand how cellular lipid compositions are established and maintained. In this proposal, we will meet this challenge by elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the intracellular trafficking of cholesterol, a lipid that is essential for normal brain function and whose dysregulation has been linked to a variety of neurological disorders, including neurodegenerative conditions. Cholesterol is critical for the structural integrity of cellular membranes and for many physiological functions, including neuronal activity. Cells either synthesize cholesterol de novo in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) – the organelle responsible for the majority of membrane lipid biosynthesis – or acquire it from external sources. In the brain, developing neurons produce cholesterol de novo. By contrast, mature neurons lose the ability to synthesizing it, and instead acquire cholesterol from glia-derived apolipoprotein. Regardless of its source, cholesterol is highly enriched in the plasma membrane (PM), where it represents approximately one half of all lipids. Thus, cells must constantly monitor the levels of cholesterol in their PM, and adjust levels of cholesterol biosynthesis or uptake to maintain PM homeostasis. This is thought to be mediated, at least in part, by communication between the PM and the ER. Despite decades of research into cholesterol metabolism, we still do not know how cells mediate crosstalk between the PM and the ER to regulate PM cholesterol homeostasis. In our preliminary studies, we found that a new family of evolutionarily conserved and ER-anchored lipid transfer proteins, the GRAMD1s (GRAMD1a, GRAMD1b, GRAMD1c), detect the amount of cholesterol available in the PM and transport cholesterol from the PM to the ER at sites of contact between these cellular structures (ER-PM contact sites). GRAMD1s therefore facilitate ER-PM crosstalk. Strikingly, recent human genetic studies, including genome-wide association studies, have identified links between one of these proteins, GRAMD1b, and both intellectual disability and schizophrenia. Our overarching hypothesis is that lipid transfer proteins, including the GRAMD1s, play critical roles in the delivery and exchange of cholesterol between the PM and other cellular compartments, and that disruption of this process causes neuronal dysfunction. title: ORIGIN, FUNCTION AND MOLECULAR BASIS OF SKELETAL MUSCLE FIBRE DIVERSITY
abs: Skeletal muscle is a major organ of the human body, comprising around 40% of an individual's body mass. It is essential both for posture (tonic muscle) and movement (phasic muscle) and also plays an important role in the storage and generation of energy and as a source of endocrine signals. Skeletal muscle fibres are typically classified as fast-twitch or slow-twitch, reflecting differences in their physiological and metabolic properties that correlate with the expression of distinct isoforms of myosin motor proteins. Muscle fibre-type composition depends upon both genetic and environmental factors. During embryonic development, muscle progenitors are genetically programmed to acquire particular fibre-type identities, but fibres remain plastic throughout the lifetime of an individual, responding to the effects of neural stimulation, mechanical loading, exercise and disease. Fibre-type composition has an important impact on the susceptibility to metabolic disease whilst muscle wasting diseases such as Duchenne's muscular dystrophy (DMD) and age-related muscle wasting (sarcopenia) preferentially affects fast-twitch fibres Understanding the molecular basis of fibre-type identity is thus of both clinical as well as fundamental biological significance. Over the past fifteen years, we and others have elucidated some of the signaling pathways and gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that control the specification of muscle fibre types in the developing zebrafish embryo. Whereas in amniotes muscle growth proceeding exclusively through hypertrophy with no new muscle fibres formed after birth, in fish, MSCs continue to generate new fibres throughout the life-course of the animal, an indeterminate mode of growth that contributes to variation in body size. In contrast to the detailed understanding of embryonic myogenesis, rather less is known about the origins and diversification of muscle fibres during post embryonic growth, knowledge of the processes underlying secondary myogenesis in the zebrafish remains fragmentary.This project aims to address this knowledge gap by undertaking an in-depth molecular and functional characterization of specific muscle fibre-types in the adult zebrafish. Our preliminary studies have revealed previously undescribed diversity within the superficially located slow-twitch fibres of the adult fish as well as distinct patterns of myosin gene expression in a previously poorly characterized population of smaller presumptive slow-twitch fibres, the function of which is unknown. We hypothesise that each of the populations of muscle fibres defined by these distinctive patterns of myosin gene expression is physiologically and functionally specialized and that this specialisation is underpinned by distinct transcriptional programmes under the control of specific gene regulatory networks.
