title: Super-Intensive Urban RAS Systems for Biofloc Shrimp Culture
abs: Biofloc technology has shown to be commercially attractive when applied to traditional pond culture. However, the feasibility of utilizing biofloc technologies in indoor aquaculture production systems such as RAS remains unclear. A super high-density indoor shrimp production system combining elements of RAS and Biofloc is proposed to address the pain points of shrimp aquaculture in Singapore. This stackable semi-automated design focuses on minimizing land, water, and manpower while utilizing ex-situ feed valorisation with accumulated biofloc waste. Preliminary findings of biofloc used in our indoor RAS mud crab (Scylla serrata) farm have shown better animal growth as compared to RAS systems alone. An estimated profitability simulation comparing the return on investment of the proposed design (3.1 years), and the annualized yield per square meter (21kg) has been provided as a gauge of the commercial viability of our proposal. Furthermore, this proposal also focuses intently on the molecular identification of microbial diversity in biofloc samples obtained from the system and the intestines of shrimp through 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing technology. Identifying microorganisms important for biofloc technology and animal health are an important step in research on immunity, disease resistance and nutrition for successful shrimp aquaculture.
kw: Biofloc, Aquaculture, Shrimp, Microbiome, Recirculation Aquaculture System

title: Profiling of circulating exosomes in ischemic stroke for a nanoplasmonic stroke diagnostic device.
abs: Specific aims: • To identify suitable exosomal based markers of ischemic stroke, leading to a platform for rapid diagnosis of ischemic stroke. Secondary Aim: • To develop serum markers predictive of clot characteristics that will impact the endovascular thrombectomy technique. i.e fibrin vs red blood cell (RBC) rich clots • To profile serum markers to determine the underlying etiology of ischemic stroke, which will have impact on the long-term treatment decisions. Hypothesis: Exosome surface markers and its contents (miRNA and proteins) contain markers which are specific for ischemic stroke. This can be used in a novel technology (APEX) to create a blood based platform for the rapid diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke. Methodology:Acute stroke patients who are amenable for thrombectomy will be included in this study. The clot extracted, blood drawn from around the clot (peri-clot) and blood from a peripheral vein which is typically discarded, will be stored for analysis. This will allow us to isolate exosomes and subsequently determine specific markers which are raised in increasing concentration in the peripheral blood, peri-clot blood and blood clot. Using the amplified plasmonic exosome (APEX) technology created by the team, we will leverage in situ enzymatic conversion of localized optical deposits and double-layered plasmonic nanostructures to enable sensitive, multiplexed population analysis. We will be able to detect exosome-bound markers directly from blood with superior sensitivity (~200 exosomes) to profile and identify specific diagnostic and prognostic markers for ischemic stroke and its underlying cause. POTENTIALBENEFITS: There is a lack of non-radiological stroke biomarkers. The study will be able to discover a blood-based marker for ischemic stroke diagnosis. It will also help to pre-determine the clot characteristics, which is important for acute treatment decisions. In addition, it will identify the source of the blood clot causing the stroke, which has major implications for long-term pharmacological treatment.
kw: acute stroke; biomarker; diagnosis; serum; etiology

title: Deciphering the tumor microenvironment of primary TKI resistant EGFR mutant NSCLC
abs: Extending the observations on genomic determinants of primary resistance to EGFR TKI (Lai et al JCO 2019; Tan A WCLC 2019), this proposal aims to further characterise immune microenvironment of both naive and TKI resistant EGFR mutant NSCLC specifically to facilitate the design of rational combinations of immune modulators. Emerging clinical data suggest a need for angiogenic approaches in combination with platinum based chemotherapy and checkpoint blockade (IMpower150, Mok et al Lancet Resp Med 2019). Our preliminary RNA-seq data of EGFR TKI resistant samples suggests subsets of "inflammed" EGFR M+ tumors that are associated with shorter time to progression on TKI. In silico dissection of immune subsets further delineates myeloid derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) so a predominant cell population. In this proposal, we aim to apply state of the art immuno-monitoring (cyTOF or symphony flow cytometry) on primary resistant tumors, extend the transcriptomic and genomic datasets, through designing a clinical protocol to systemically interrogate biospecimens of EGFR mutant NSCLC undergoing immunotherapy and combinations thereof. There are ongoing discussions with industry partners (Pfizer, AZ, MSD) to design a proof of concept phase I/Ib trial specifically to address this major unmet need for lung cancer in Asia.
kw: EGFR TKI resistant; NSCLC;

title: Multi-dimensional frailty in community-dwelling elderly – the Singapore Chinese Health Study
abs: Frailty is age-related decline and deterioration in physiological reserves, resulting in a state of limited capacity to maintain homeostasis and increased vulnerability to stressors of daily living, and is an indicator of vulnerability to adverse health outcomes. A multi-dimensional conceptual definition of frailty has been proposed, which describes frailty as a dynamic pre-disability state that includes physical frailty, psychological frailty (defined as decline in cognition, mood and motivation) and/or social frailty (defined as decline in social activities, relations and support). There is a pressing need for studies that investigate the different domains of frailty in a cohesive manner in a single population. Therefore, the overall aim of this proposal is to take a broad, integrated and holistic approach in examining the independent and joints effects of frailty across the physical, psychological and social domains. Our first aim is to measure the co-existence of frailty across the three domains and to study the effect of this multi-dimensional frailty on the development of adverse ageing outcomes in community-dwelling elderly. Our second aim is to study the influence of midlife environment factors (including lifestyle and diet), genetic variants and midlife blood biomarkers on the development of multi-dimensional frailty at late-life. This proposal is nested in 5,000 participants who are aged 65 to 100 years old from the Singapore Chinese Health Study, a well-characterized cohort with more than 20 years of follow-up and with well-established cohort databases, as well as archived biospecimens (blood and urine) collected more than 15 years ago. This proposal will advance knowledge about frailty in terms of phenotype diversity, etiologic heterogeneity and factors underpinning pathophysiologic pathways. Findings will also provide the scientific evidence and foundation for a multi-dimensional approach so that personalized and targeted interventions can be implemented for individualized care and management for the frail elderly.
kw: physical frailty; psychological frailty; social frailty; ageing; healthcare; disability

title: Protein supplementation in critically ill children: A pilot randomized controlled trial
abs: Protein malnutrition is prevalent among critically ill children and associated with poor clinical outcomes. Current guidelines for provision of protein in daily management of critically ill children in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) are based on limited and not high-quality evidence. The current protein supplementation approach, “one-size-fits-all” nutrition prescription, may not be appropriate for every critically ill child. Given the heterogeneity of the patients admitted to the PICU, a targeted approach based on individuals’ needs represents a potential advancement in PICU care. Our central hypothesis is that protein supplementation in PICU care leads to improved clinical outcomes in subgroups of patients only. We propose a dual-centre pilot randomized controlled trial in Singapore with two major aims: (1) To obtain key information for planning and conducting a large-scale multicentre study in Asia; and (2) to evaluate the benefit of protein supplementation to critically ill children with body mass index (BMI) z-scores on PICU ≤ -2. The main clinical outcome of interest is total number of days of hospital stay (from PICU admission to hospital discharge). Two protein supplementation regimes (≥ 1.5g/kg/day vs. standard care) will be randomly allocated to PICU patients with body mass index (BMI) z-scores ≤ -2. We will determine the effect of protein supplementation on total length of hospital stay and other clinical outcomes, and assess the impact of protein supplementation on acquired functional impairment of PICU survivors 6 months after hospital discharge. In addition, we will explore whether muscle ultrasound is a biomarker for protein balance in pediatric critical illness. Upon completion of this study, we will have strong preliminary data to plan, refine our study approach, and execute a future large multi-centre study across Asia. These data will ultimately guide protein provision and nutritional

title: Investigating the effect of adiposity on skin barrier function in a general population cohort
abs: Obesity is a major public health problem, and known to be associated with a range of chronic diseases including chronic inflammatory skin diseases such as atopic dermatitis (AD). We hypothesize that adiposity promotes skin epidermal barrier dysfunction through activation of inflammatory cytokine pathways, leading to loss of anti-microbial peptides and barrier lipids in the stratum corneum, and that these molecular processes are linked to the development of abnormal skin microbial colonization and worsening of atopic dermatitis. However, our understanding of the relationships between adiposity and skin barrier dysfunction has significant limitations. While adiposity is associated with cytokine disturbances in blood, whether adiposity directly influences inflammation in skin is not known. Furthermore, no study has evaluated the microbial disturbances in obese individuals, or whether this is linked to underlying disturbances in the molecular and physiological profile of the skin. We therefore aim to address these knowledge gaps by carrying out experiments among study participants in an ongoing general population cohort to address specific aims. We will determine whether skin concentrations of selected inflammatory cytokines, anti-microbial peptides and lipid metabolites relevant to epidermal biology and skin barrier dysfunction are different between lean and obese participants. We will also characterize the skin microbiome profile of study participants and investigate how microbial composition relates to disturbances of inflammatory cytokines, anti-microbial peptides, and metabolic variation in skin, observed in obese individuals. In addition, we will quantify serum proteomic profile of study participants and determine whether systemic inflammatory signatures relate to cytokine and microbial composition of the skin, and to skin barrier function in lean and obese individuals. Finally, we will assess the potential causal relationship between obesity, and the identified molecular, microbial and functional disturbances in skin biology, through quantification of these biomarkers in obese participants before and after weight loss.
kw: obesity, skin barrier function, epidemiology, microbiome

title: Differentiating the Fine Reactivity Difference of Functional Saccharides
abs: Saccharides are a major class of biomolecules involved in numerous biological activities. Modulation of saccharides or saccharide segments leads to therapeutic agents such as vaccines and antibiotics with billion-dollar commercial success. However, despite of the enormous applications and potentials, understanding of saccharide-related biological processes and development of saccharide-based pharmaceuticals remain challenging. A major problem lies on the lack of efficient chemical synthetic tools for access to saccharides and their derivatives. It is difficult to selectively functionalize the many hydroxyl (OH) groups present in saccharides because the reactivity differences of the various OH groups are very small. (A) Aims: We seek to integrate the powers of molecular recognitions and N-heterocyclic carbene organic catalysis to create new catalytic technology for precise differentiation and regio-selective functionalization of saccharides, and thus to achieve short-route and scalable access to industrially important saccharide-derived products (B) Hypotheses: (a) the OH groups on saccharides can be differentiated through molecular recognitions; (b) combined molecular recognition and NHC catalysis can amplify the reactivity differences of OHs to realize regio-selective reactions. (C): Methodology: We will introduce three driving forces (e.g., tunable substrates, catalysts, and supramolecular receptors) to amplify these otherwise small reactivity differences and thus to realize selective reactions. The overall objectives will be achieved through three interlinked subprojects, concerning selective functionalization of monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and short-route synthesis of saccharides conjugates and derivatives. (D: Feasibility: The proposed research is supported by our preliminary studies (showing that with different NHC catalysts/conditions, acylation reactions can selectively occur on specific OH group) and earlier studies by the PIs. (E) Importance: Our concise synthetic routes will make saccharide-based medicines more accessible, and provide crucial research tools to investigate biological processes for developing new medical solutions. Our research will generate new knowledge in understanding chemical moieties with similar reactivities, molecular recognitions, and saccharides.
kw: saccharides and saccharide-based products; regio-selective functionalization; pharmaceuticals; molecular recognition and non-covalent interaction; N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) organic catalysis; advanced manufacturing

title: Deciphering the Mechanisms of RNA Modifications in Plants
abs: More than 160 distinct RNA modifications have been discovered to date. Although most of these modifications are identified in high-abundance noncoding RNAs, such as rRNA and tRNA, recent technical advances have enabled the precise detection of several RNA modifications and their transcriptome-wide distribution, new functions and players in low abundance RNAs, including mRNA. These efforts are leading to the discovery of RNA modifications associated with hitherto unknown gene regulatory mechanisms, resulting in the birth of the epitranscriptomics field that focuses on deciphering the function of RNA modifications. Despite recent advances in understanding RNA modifications in mammalian cell systems, molecular functions of the epitranscriptome in multicellular organisms are largely unclear. We and others have recently shown that RNA modifications affect key plant developmental traits, including seed development and plant stature. However, their underlying molecular mechanisms in plants are so far largely unknown. In this proposal, we aim to apply a holistic approach including an array of novel strategies to systematically characterize mRNA modifications, using the most abundant N6-methyladenosine (m6A) mRNA modification as a major example, to uncover their function and regulatory network in plant development and environmental responses. We will also explore the relationships among different mRNA modifications and their effects on plants. The proposed approaches for this project are highly feasible because of the solid preliminary studies and well-established experimental platforms. This project will unravel the mechanisms underlying biological and genetic effects of plant epitranscriptome, and define a hitherto unknown conceptual framework for the regulatory roles of RNA modifications in plants. This will also provide significant insights into the molecular mechanisms of cognate RNA modifications in multicellular eukaryotic organisms. In addition to the above scientific merits, achievement of the objectives in this proposal will reveal new gene resources and novel regulatory mechanisms pertaining to agriculturally important traits. The derived knowledge will enable either classical breeding or targeted genome editing of desirable traits for economically important plants in Singapore, such as leafy vegetables and rice.
kw: RNA modifications; epitranscriptome; m6A; Arabidopsis; rice; leafy vegetables

title: Risks and Solutions: Marine Plastics in Southeast Asia- RaSP-SEA
abs: The overarching aim of this programme is to reduce plastic leakage in the Southeast Asian sea, support the development of a sustainable and circular plastic resource flow, and reduce the impacts of plastic pollution on livelihoods, marine habitats, and wildlife. Working regionally with Malaysian and Thai partners, RaSP-SEA team will build capacity, generate knowledge, and test innovative solutions under three interlinked, interdisciplinary themes in Singapore. 1. Modification and transformation of plastics in the environment: Ecological sampling will reveal the life cycle and dispersion of plastics in water, sediments, and key coastal habitats. Work will be augmented by partnerships with ongoing citizen science initiatives to better collect, categorise, record, and remove beach litter. Data will be used to highlight the key categories of plastic pollution to identify possible sources and fate of plastics in the environment, which will facilitate the development of targeted interventions and help transboundary modelling. Utilising oceanographic modelling, we will use a combination of fore/ hindcast time simulations to inform the origin, movement, and destination of marine plastic pollution. We will also use novel satellite tracking devices to replicate plastic bottles, which have recently been trialled by project partners in India. Real-time data hosted on the web will afford significant media and outreach opportunities and in addition will inform oceanographic models with empirical movement data for plastic in the marine environment. 2. Hazard, risk, and impacts: We will develop assay protocols for the detection and quantification of plastic presence and associated persistent organic pollutants in fish/shellfish informing ecological studies of trophic transfer in the human food chain. At sensitive coastal habitats, we will assess damage to ecology and associated ecosystem services and create an urgently needed regional baseline of wildlife-plastic interactions (e.g. ingestion and/or entanglement). A web-based sharing platform to collate evidence of these interactions from diverse stakeholders will augment the database and foster extensive engagement for the project. 3. Intervention, mitigation, and adaptation: Taking an interdisciplinary approach, we will investigate multiple solutions to either hasten plastic recovery from the environment, or avoid it reaching the marine environment. Through extensive stakeholder engagement, we will gather possible solutions and compare their logistical and financial feasibility across the three study countries. Placing importance on capacity building and enabling investment in sustainable livelihoods within communities. Overall, the team has sufficient track record in the collection and identification of marine plastic waste, exploring the impact of microplastics on living systems and developing future technologies for reducing the amount of plastic waste in the marine environment.

title: Mobile collaborative robot platforms with vision feedback and adaptive and learning soft end-effectors for coning/de-coning wharf operations
pi: Pablo Alvaro Valdivia y Alvarado Gutierrez
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: The autonomous adaptive system proposed by our team involves advanced grasping and manipulation as well as collaborative behavior of mobile robots. To achieve the goals of the proposed project, our team will work on four work packages (WP). Work package 1 (WP1) will focus on the design and development of advanced soft grippers with embedded tactile sensing capable of robustly grasping a wide range of commercial cones, Work package 2 (WP2) will focus on vision and tactile enabled object classification/learning to identify cone types and provide feedback to plan end-effector poses and manipulator trajectories, Work package 3 (WP3) will focus on cone manipulation (including storage), and Work package 4 (WP4) will focus on task planning and collaborative robot behaviors for the entire system. A group of collaborative mobile robots will operate around horizontal transports on the wharf side once a container has been loaded. Each mobile unit is outfitted with Lidars and RTK GPS and a high payload hyper-redundant cooperative manipulator outfitted with a soft gripper unit. The mobile robots will cooperate to perform coordinated coning and de-coning operations while minimizing operational footprint and optimizing cycle times. The nature of our approach also enables seamless scaling of the operations (e.g. short and long containers or work on multiple horizontal transports in a queue) which will enable a high degree of adaptability.
kw: Automation, Robotics

title: Achieving Functional Cure of Chronic Hepatitis B
abs: The biology of different stages of Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) is still not well understood but insights are likely with deep multidimensional phenotyping comprising genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics , microRNA, immunology and virological characterisation, an opportunity we are well placed to explore with our well established cohort. However the main focus will be on functional cure of CHB defined as HBsAg loss, not achievable with current therapies. The objectives of our proposal is the understand the virological and immune mechanisms involved in functional cure by examining the liver microenvironment with state of the art technologies such as single cell analysis, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and epigenetics in patients with/without functional cure. By using liver organoids from CHB patients, and new tools to visualise functional changes in the liver microenvironment we will create a new platform to understand and the mechanism of functional cure. As the key to CHB is an indepth analysis of epigenetics of cccDNA, four factors found in the HBV TCR to be important in viral replication will be investigated to understand their direct or indirect relationship to HBV. Concurrently, a validated target for HBV such as HBx-DDB1 interaction and a potential target HBc-cccDNA interaction will be a particular focus for assay development, computerised modelling, and medicinal library development as possible new classes of antiviral agents. An artificial intelligence platform (QPOP) and the expertise of the Experimental Drug Development Centre will guide strategy and hit selection. Finally, new mechanisms of action, and new antiviral agents can be tested out in the humanised mouse model which is being developed as a model-of-choice for CHB with chronic HBV infected hepatocytes and a fully matched immune system. Clinical trials will test proof of principle studies particularly for the unmet needs of an oral transcriptase inhibitor and a CpG immunomodulator.

title: A smart sensor for indoor airborne microbial monitoring
abs: We aim to develop a sensor device for analyzing overall airborne microorganism level in indoor environment. It utilizes microfluidic technology to capture and concentrate airborne microbial particles, and quantify the total microbial amount through detection of cell autofluorescence. The device allows fully automated microbial detection without the needs of chemical reagents or other consumables. Obtained data can be transmitted and shared for further analysis. The device can be used for both industrial and domestic applications as environmental monitoring tools for hygiene control.

title: Evaluation of safety of a novel wound dressing patch for the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers in a phase 1 clinical trial
abs: Foot ulcers are a chronic problem in patients suffering from diabetes. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) if left untreated end up in lower limb amputations. Current methods to improve healing in chronic DFUs have met with limited success. Billions of dollars are spent annually on treatment of wounds in general and the problem is growing worldwide due to an aging population and rise in the incidence of diabetes and obesity. We have studied a stem cell derived from the human umbilical cord Wharton’s jelly (hWJSC) that has unique properties that can be used for the treatment of DFUs. These stem cells are non-controversial, can be harvested painlessly in abundance from discarded umbilical cords, hypo-immunogenic, non-tumorigenic, and secrete important molecules for wound repair. These molecules include cytokines involved in the crucial processes of angiogenesis, lymphangiogenesis, cell migration and re-epithelialization which are the main obstacles to the repair of ischemic DFUs. These hW JSCs attach and grow readily in the stem cell niches created by biodegradable polycaprolactone (PCL) nanomeshes. Since cells function best at nanoscale levels in vivo, we have taken advantage of these properties of the hWJSCs and nanoscaffolds and developed a wound dressing patch made up of a PCL nanoscaffold impregnated with hWJSCs for improvement of wound healing. In both in vitro scratch-wound assays and preclinical in vivo mouse diabetic models we reported that our wound dressing patch encouraged the healing of both surgical and diabetic wounds. We have also attempted to make our patch clinical grade and have developed the preliminary protocols to make it cGMP-compliant for human clinical application. We now wish to complete the cGMP-compliance protocols, carry out all neccessary validation tests, obtain DSRB and HSA clearance and conduct a Phase 1 clinical trial to evaluate its safety on patients with DFUs at the Khoo Teck Puat hospital.
kw: Stem cells; wound healing; diabetic foot ulcers; Cellular Therapy; Clinical Trial; cGMP

title: Metastatic Triple-Negative Taxane-Resistant/Refractory Breast Cancer: Investigating the Role of Bexarotene in Inducing Susceptibility to Chemotherapy by Differentiating Cancer Cells from a Mesenchymal-Like to an Epithelial-Like Phenotype (BEXMET)
abs: Background: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), as defined by its ER negative, PR negative and HER2 negative status, is biologically aggressive and has limited systemic treatment options, often compounded by treatment resistance, hence conferring an overall poorer prognosis. Cell state transitions, e.g. epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET), govern the functional behavior of cancer cells, such as proliferation, invasiveness, metastatic potential and resistance to chemotherapy. Our preliminary studies revealed Bexarotene (retinoid) as a potent MET inducer, verified in TNBC cells in vitro and in animal models, rendering greater chemotherapy sensitivity. Bexarotene is used in the treatment of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Hypothesis: Bexarotene induces MET in cancer cells in metastatic TNBC patients (thereby increasing chemotherapy susceptibility). Specific Aims: 1. To characterize the RNA and protein profiles of serial biopsies of the selected lesion: before, during and after Bexarotene administration 2. To evaluate early safety and tolerability signals of the Bexarotene-Capecitabine combination Approach/Methods: This is a single-arm study of Bexarotene-Capecitabine in 20 taxane-resistant/refractory metastatic TNBC patients. Bexarotene is dosed daily with a 2-week lead-in before Capecitabine is commenced. Capecitabine is started on week 3 for 14 consecutive days every 21 days. Bexarotene is dosed for 7 days of every 21-day cycle of Capecitabine, coinciding with the rest weeks from Capecitabine, i.e. weeks 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20. Four tumour biopsies are scheduled: 1) week 0 before starting Bexarotene, 2) week 2, 3) week 4, and 4) after week 20. Biopsies are submitted for histopathological review, transcriptomic (RNASeq) and protein (immunohistochemistry) profiling. Significance: Overcoming treatment resistance in TNBC metastatic patients is an unmet clinical need. Here, we propose to prove the re-directing of the TNBC phenotype from mesenchymal-like to epithelial-like with Bexarotene in a clinical setting, forming the basis of future clinical trials to evaluate the efficacy of the Bexarotene-Capecitabine combination.
kw: triple-negative breast cancer; mesenchymal-to-epithelial (MET) transition; retinoid

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Develop a Customised Prediction Model for Successful Induction of Labour
abs: Background Induction of labour (IOL) is performed in ~30% of pregnant women. Successful IOL is marked by active labour and vaginal delivery. Complications include failed induction requiring caesarean delivery, prolonged hospital stay and, in women with caesarean scars, uterine rupture. Currently, there is no objective measure to predict the likelihoods of successful IOL versus complications. Maternal and fetal biometry and pre-induction cervical assessment are individually associated with successful IOL, but prediction based on these values is largely subjective. There is an unmet need for objective assessment tools utilizing historical and evolving physiological data to improve prediction of IOL outcomes and to increase precision of labour management. Aim To use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to develop an individually customizable prediction model for successful IOL. Hypothesis AI can predict IOL outcomes accurately based on historical and evolving physiological data, and can be used to develop personalized labour management. Methods and Analysis We will conduct a prospective pilot study of patients admitted for IOL over 12 months. Inclusion criteria include gestation 37 weeks or more, cervical score ≤5/10, one previous caesarean section with no contraindications to IOL. Exclusion criteria include gestation less than 37 weeks, multiple pregnancies, and contraindications to vaginal delivery. On admission, transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound measurements of lower uterine segment thickness and cervical length will be performed by the research sonographer. Pre-induction cervical score and intrapartum parameters (e.g. rate of cervical dilatation) will be collected in a standard proforma and analysed with select AI tools which will be trained to predict vaginal delivery and rank individual parameters in order of influence on final outcomes. The primary outcome is vaginal delivery. Results from this pilot study will be used to apply for further competitive funding to validate this prediction tool at the national level and across various hospital clusters; and also develop an AI application for labour management.
kw: Artificial Intelligence; Prediction; Induction of Labour; TOLAC; Caesarean Section

title: Elucidation of the pathophysiology of preterm birth and intrauterine growth restriction in a prospective preconception cohort study
abs: Preterm birth (PTB), defined as delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, affects 10 to 15% of all pregnancies around the world. Fetal growth restriction, defined as a pathological restriction of the genetic growth potential of a fetus, results in low birth weight (LBW) of the baby < 2500 g. These conditions result in significant neonatal morbidity and mortality. The etiologies are diverse, rendering risk factor prediction models inaccurate. Hence, the ability to predict and prognosticate pregnancies destined to be PTB or LBW is lacking. Metabolomics offers a powerful holistic approach to examine the metabolic alterations in disease. We hypothesize that pregnancies resulting in PTB and LBW have a different maternal plasma metabolic profile compared to matched healthy pregnancies. We will use an unbiased ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectroscopy (LC-MS/MS) metabolomics to comprehensively profile the mothers’ plasma. We will perform an age and BMI-matched nested case-control study, using samples drawn from an existing preconception cohort study in Singapore. This is an exploratory study using 20 cases of PTB and 20 cases of LBW, which will be individually matched with 40 controls of healthy pregnancies, according to maternal age and BMI. Analyses will be performed at each of the following timepoints: at preconception, first trimester (≤13 weeks’ gestation) and third trimester (28-32 weeks’ gestation). An unbiased, global approach (untargeted LC-MS/MS) will be combined with a knowledge-based approach in the search for biomarker candidates. This longitudinal study approach, from preconception to early pregnancy to the third trimester prior to adverse neonatal outcome onset, will allow us to determine non-invasive molecular signatures. This provides potential candidates for further targeted investigation as early screening biomarkers of PTB and LBW in preconception and pregnant women. This may also offer potential insight about the underlying metabolic dyshomeostatsis as the disease evolves with time, offering novel targets for intervention.
kw: Preconception

title: A Multicenter, Adaptive, Randomized Blinded Controlled Trial of the Safety and Efficacy of Investigational Therapeutics for Hospitalized Patients with COVID-19
abs: COVID-19 is a respiratory disease caused by a novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) and causes substantial morbidity and mortality. Several clinical trials utilizing novel drugs and repurposing older agent have been implemented to investigate the treatment of adults hospitalized with severe COVID-19. There is evidence that the humoral immune responses are variable between individuals and delayed in some cases. It may therefore be that viral replication leads to extensive tissue damage and inflammatory responses in the lungs and other organs before the development of neutralizing antibodies. Augmentation of the humoral immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection using passive immunotherapy in hospitalized patients may thus improve the disease course and reduce the time to recovery. This study is an adaptive, randomized blinded controlled phase 2 trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of multiple investigational agents aimed at modifying the host immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection or directly enhancing viral control in order to limit disease progression. This study is a multicenter trial that will be conducted in 16 countries and expected to enroll about 1012 subjects around the world. All subjects will undergo a series of efficacy, safety and laboratory assessments. Discharged patients will attend study visits at Days 28 and 90 when blood samples are collected. Nasal swabs will be obtained on Day 0. Primary endpoint is defined as the time from randomization to sustained recovery, being discharged from hospitalization followed by being alive and home for 14 consecutive days prior to Day 90. Though the agents studied may or may not prevent these outcomes in any participating individual, there is an anticipated benefit to society due to insights that will be gained about the investigational agent as well as the natural history of the disease, especially if a safe, efficacious therapeutic agent can be identified during this global COVID-19 outbreak.

title: IL-11 and non-small cell lung cancer: clinical associations and transcriptome analysis
abs: Lung cancer is one of the top 3 most common cancers in Singapore of which non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the commonest subtype. Treatment modalities include surgical resection, chemotherapy, radiation therapy and targeted therapy, but survival from NSCLC remain suboptimal. There is a need to identify biomarkers for better screening for lung cancer, and novel therapeutic targets to improve survival. Interleukin 11 (IL-11) is a cytokine that has been shown to increase NSCLC tumor growth, and its expression in non-small cell cancer tissue correlates with prognosis. The mechanism through which IL-11 affects tumor biology and the full scope of downstream effects from IL-11 is not completely understood. We aim to study IL-11 in NSCLC by evaluating IL-11 expression in resected NSCLC tumor, and correlating IL-11 expression with expression of other genes in a comprehensive transcriptome analysis via RNA sequencing. We expect that the analysis will yield potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets for this disease. The specific aims for this study are to: (1) identify clinical factors that may be associated with interleukin-11 (IL-11) expression in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and (2) identify genes that correlate with IL-11 expression in NSCLC. Patients, who are scheduled to undergo surgical resection for histologically-proven or suspected NSCLC will be recruited from National Heart Center Singapore, National Cancer Center, and Singapore General Hospital, and blood and tissue from 40 patients with confirmed NSCLC will be evaluated for IL-11 and related cytokines via Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and RNA sequencing. Genes that correlate with IL-11 expression will be identified. These genes will be targets of further study, as they may be related to the tumor-promoting properties of IL-11 that can be potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.
kw: Non-small-cell lung cancer; interleukin 11; RNA sequencing

title: Multimodal Personalized Training System for Neurocognitive Preservation and Enhancement for the Elderly: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abs: With Singapore’s rapidly ageing population, the rate of neurocognitive decline is expected to escalate. This situation is worsened by the immense cost and low efficacy of treating irreversible neurocognitive disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease. Fortuitously, it is possible to enrich old-age cognition and quality of life with cognitive training, thereby preserving cognition and delaying onset of severe neurodegeneration. Existing research suggests that neuroplasticity can be augmented in older adults by combining physical exercise with cognitive training. However, such local multidimensional programs are operationally expensive and do not target cognitive preservation well. Our aim is to develop and evaluate the efficacy of a novel personalized multimodal early intervention program that employs stationary cycling and generalizable cognitive task training for Singaporean older adults. The system will be personalized using machine learning technologies, and run by elderly-friendly user interfaces. To test intervention efficacy, we adopt a 3-arm randomized controlled clinical trial involving cognitive-cum-physical (multimodal) training, cognitive-only training, and active control groups. Our first hypothesis is that compared to cognitive training-only and active-control groups, participants in cognitive-cum-physical training group will perform significantly better on the objective neuropsychological measure (i.e. RBANS) after a thrice-weekly 12-week training program. We further hypothesize that the cognitive-cum-physical training group will perform significantly better on RBANS than both cognitive-only and active-control groups after 24 weeks of training. This study is noteworthy for its implication to translational medicine. Study success offers an implementable and evidence-based means for preserving or enhancing old-age neurocognitive ability. The technological program may also be used to complement existing local multidimensional programs and reduce operational costs. Our team of clinicians and technologists has an established professional record of delivering similar translational research work. Remarkably, early collaboration with an industry partner places us in a strategic market position to take our system from research to effective commercialization.
kw: Neurocognition; Personalized Medicine; Multimodal; Brain-Computer Interface

title: Identification and characterisation of dedifferentiating colorectal cancer transcriptomic targets using single cell RNAseq
abs: Cancer stem cell markers such as LGR5 have been identified. Interestingly, treatment to eradicate cancer stem cells only leads to temporary eradication of LGR5+ cells, with LGR5+ cell recovery occurring on cessation of ablative treatment, leading to the suggestion that mature differentiated cancer epithelial cells possess the ability to dedifferentiate into cancer stem cells. Aim Our aim is to identify novel transcriptomic biomarkers in Consensus Molecular Subtype 2 (CMS2) colorectal cancer which may serve as candidates for dedifferentiation to cancer stem cells. We also aim to functionally characterize novel transcriptomic biomarkers in patient-derived 3D organoids and xenograft models. Hypothesis We hypothesize that dedifferentiation of cells into cancer stem cells is a major contributor to maintenance and propagation of CRC as well as resistance to targeted therapies. Methodology Our methodology utilises single-cell RNAseq to determine the transcriptomic landscape of CMS2 cancers. We will use computational approaches to recapitulate known CSC markers, identify novel markers of cells which have the potential for dedifferentiation, and finally, seek to identify the mechanism by which these markers interact to result in CRC stemness through dedifferentiation. Functional characterisation of transcripts will be performed in organoid and PDX models. Finally, depletion of dedifferentiated target cells in organoid models will be performed to identify the putative dedifferentiating cell. Approach Our study chooses to focus on CMS2 cancers because this subtype recapitulates non-cancer homeostasis in intestinal stem cells. Tumorigenesis via the cancer stem cell pathway is central to this subtype of colorectal cancer, as it overexpresses Wnt and Myc, which are also associated with non-cancer homeostasis. Our study focuses on generating a transcriptomic landscape using a single-cell approach in order to understand the cellular hierarchy in a highly heterogeneous cancer environment. Transcriptomic targets are tested on patient derived organoids and xenografts to most accurately reflect the patient’s cancer environment.
kw: colorectal cancer; dedifferentiation; cancer stem cells; transcriptome

title: TrisailTM: A Percutaneous Tricuspid Valve Repair/Replacement Device
abs: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) has been identified as an important unmet clinical need given its prevalence and adverse prognostic impact. Although the association between severe TR and mortality has been established, few patients receive isolated tricuspid surgery (current treatment option) due to the high operative risk. Hence, a percutaneous and less invasive approach to repair/replace the tricuspid valve is an attractive alternative to treat TR. Current percutaneous options have several drawbacks such as the use of a bulky device, technically complicated procedures, requiring advanced imaging and disruptions to the normal anatomy. In this project, the proposed tricuspid valve repair/replacement device is elegant, robust and requires a less complicated deployment process compared to existing technologies. The technology consists of an anchoring device to secure the position of the device and a coaptation structure for the native tricuspid valve leaflets to coapt. There is also no placement of sutures and pledgets onto the tricuspid valve, eliminating the risk of injuring the native valve. Here, the proposed technology can potentially provide a minimally invasive and less complex way to treat TR and improve patient outcomes, addressing a clear unmet clinical need. In this project, the aim is to develop a percutaneous tricuspid valve repair device and a delivery catheter, and to bring the technology to first-in-animal. To achieve this, the team plans to develop a percutaneous tricuspid device and delivery system under the SMART grant, followed with preclinical studies in the NHIC and SPRING-TECS phase. The funding of this I2Start is expected to result in the successful completion of prototyping, preclinical animal studies and spinning out a company to bring this technology to the next stage.

title: A Multicenter, Adaptive, Randomized Blinded Controlled Trial of the Safety and Efficacy of Investigational Therapeutics for Hospitalized Patients with COVID-19 (ACTIV3)
abs: COVID-19 is a respiratory disease caused by a novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) and causes substantial morbidity and mortality. Several clinical trials utilizing novel drugs and repurposing older agent have been implemented to investigate the treatment of adults hospitalized with severe COVID-19. There is evidence that the humoral immune responses are variable between individuals and delayed in some cases. It may therefore be that viral replication leads to extensive tissue damage and inflammatory responses in the lungs and other organs before the development of neutralizing antibodies. Augmentation of the humoral immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection using passive immunotherapy in hospitalized patients may thus improve the disease course and reduce the time to recovery. This study is an adaptive, randomized blinded controlled phase 2 trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of multiple investigational agents aimed at modifying the host immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection or directly enhancing viral control in order to limit disease progression. This study is a multicenter trial that will be conducted in 16 countries and expected to enroll about 1012 subjects around the world. All subjects will undergo a series of efficacy, safety and laboratory assessments. Discharged patients will attend study visits at Days 28 and 90 when blood samples are collected. Nasal swabs will be obtained on Day 0. Primary endpoint is defined as the time from randomization to sustained recovery, being discharged from hospitalization followed by being alive and home for 14 consecutive days prior to Day 90. Though the agents studied may or may not prevent these outcomes in any participating individual, there is an anticipated benefit to society due to insights that will be gained about the investigational agent as well as the natural history of the disease, especially if a safe, efficacious therapeutic agent can be identified during this global COVID-19 outbreak.

title: The next generation of spintronics with 2D heterostructures
abs: Data intensive industries have shown tremendous development in the last three years, and therefore the demand for low-cost data storage and computing hardware keeps increasing. Traditional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) technology, however, is going to approach its limit after decades’ improvements due to the quantum confinement. Charges can be easily scattered if further reducing the transistor size due to imperfections in the surfaces of the channels, slowing their flow and generating heat dissipation. The problem is common to all transistors based on traditional three-dimensional (3D) semiconductors. The emerging two-dimensional van-der-Waals materials based spintronics provides a COMS compatible platform, which paves a new way to drive the development of highly efficient and low power memory devices. For example, the 19, 000% tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) ratio, the key parameter to evaluate the performance of a magnetic tunneling junction (MTJ), was observed in graphite/CrI3/graphite MTJ structures, which is an order of magnitude larger than previously reported MgO based MTJ [Song 2018]. This benefits from the natural advantage of 2D material, free of chemical bond, and therefore robust against surface defects as compared to 3D counterpart. However, the current devices work only in low temperature. Based on recent advances in material engineering in our team and others, we will put such devices to room temperature for practical usage. In addition, the spin-valley contrast properties discovered in 2D vdW transition metal dichalcogenides (ex. MoS2) enable the utilization of the new degree of freedom (DOF), spin-valley DOF, of electrons. The proposed spintronic devices can adopt topologically protected spin-valley current, whose non-dispersion nature leads to a new generation of low power-consumption electronics. Moreover, because 2D vdWs have only a limited ‘vertical’ dimension, and flat surfaces free from defects, electrons are less prone to scattering and charges can flow relatively freely through them. The facile wafer-scale growth, transfer, and modification of 2D semiconductors, ferromagnets and their heterostructures promise lower cost than the ones built up by the use of traditional 3D semiconductors, implying the great economic potential.
kw: Spintronic; 2D heterostructures

title: 3D Nanostructured Optics with Designer Elements (NODE) to Shape and Control Light
inst: Singapore University of Technology and Design
abs: Advances in nanofabrication coupled with strategic designs of nanostructure geometries have demonstrated exciting new capabilities in manipulating light. We have contributed to this endeavor through the control of color, polarization, phase and directional beaming of light. Despite the rapid progress in the field of nano-optics, most nanostructures are still fabricated using semiconductor processes optimized for planar 2D layers. Conversely, 3D printed nanostructures remain largely unexplored especially in visible-light optics because of challenges in nanoscale 3D printing at sub-wavelength dimensions. In this proposal, we aim to develop high-resolution processes in two-photon lithography (TPL) to more precisely sculpt 3D nanostructured optical elements. The study of novel 3D designs with unique optical properties will lead to what we call 3D Nanostructured Optics with Designer Elements (3D NODE). These elements will be designed to enhance our ability to independently shape and control several properties of light. In particular, we aim to extend our control of light towards generating and detecting the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light in different wavelength ranges. Discovered in 1992, light’s OAM promises 100x faster internet due to its unbounded number of twisted wavefront modes. Properties of this “twisted light” will be readily applied in two application areas: (1) Its high data encoding capacity will be applied for the first time to anti-counterfeiting security prints, and (2) its formation of an annular beam will be used to overcome the diffraction limit to enable contactless probing at the single-transistor level in semiconductor electronics. We envision 3D NODE to have significant impact in numerous other areas where non-standard optical elements are needed, e.g. user designed elements in optical fibers, and diffractive elements or interconnects in optical neural networks. This 5 year investigation will fuel the development of core technologies and inventions that align with Singapore’s growth areas in advanced manufacturing, optics and electronics.
kw: 3d nanofabrication; 3D nano-optics design; two-photon lithography; orbital angular momentum; anti-counterfeiting

title: ViCollAR: A System for Next-generation 3D Data Visualization using Collaborative Augmented Reality
abs: With the increasing importance of data in organizations from a wide span of sectors, various data visualization technologies have been developed to help people view and understand the data. However, most of existing data visualization technologies are normally done in 2D forms, e.g. pie chart, bar chart, etc, which limits the dimensions of data to be visualized for each single time. The users still rely on the traditional keyboard and mouse to interact with the visualized data, and therefore it is hard to achieve high efficiency of data manipulation. More importantly, most of these existing visualization systems can only support single users which barriers the collaborations and co-operations between group users. Different from the existing 2D-based data visualization technologies, the proposed project aims to deliver the next-generation system for 3D data visualization using collaborative Augmented Reality (or "ViCollAR" in short). The system, ViCollAR, will enable multiple users to work with data in an immersive, interactive and collaborative way by: (i) creating an immersive AR environment for all the users where the computer generated virtual 3D images from the data being visualized are superimposed on the real physical world; (ii) enabling all the users view and interact with the 3D graphical marks rendered from the data using their bare hands; and (iii) allowing all the users freely navigate through the same immersive environment and conduct collaborative operations on the same data being visualized. It is comprised of three key function modules with each of them responsible for the configuration, the coordination and the execution of 3D data visualization tasks respectively. Different types of data, e.g. database, csv files, etc, will be supported in ViCollAR. ViCollAR will also provide friendly user interface for users to customize the properties for the 3D data visualization tasks. Additionally, ViCollAR can be fused with machine learning and data analytics to unlock the potential of big data. Compared with the existing data visualization technologies, ViCollAR owns unique advantages which can be summarized as follows. • ViCollAR provides users with the most natural way to directly interact with the visualized data using their bare hands, thus can significantly improve efficiency and productivity; • ViCollAR allows the users to move around in the real environment while viewing and interacting with the visualized data, thus it removes the space constraints on the users; • ViCollAR supports collaborative operations on the same visualized data made by multiple users immersed in the same AR environment, thus it promotes team works and productivity.
kw: 3D Data Visualization, Augmented Reality, Collaborative Operation, Human Computer Interaction

title: Herbal Product Development by 3D Skin Model and Liver-Immune Co-Culture System for Skin Allergy
abs: 1. Specific aims: To develop a novel and safe herbal product with high effectiveness for ACD treatment To optimize the formulation and preparation method by efficacy study through quantification of biomarkers generated in a new in vitro liver-immune co-culture system and 3D skin model To establish a stringent analytical method for quality control of the herbal product To file an Invention Disclosure Form of intellectual properties referring the optimized formula of herbal product 2. The hypotheses A Herbal product for allergic contact dermatitis treatment can be developed, and the product tested on a novel in vitro Liver-immune co-culture system and an established 3D skin model 3. Methodology & approach and feasibility of the study: Formulation and preparation method of herbal product will be optimized by efficacy study through liver-immune co-culture system and 3D skin model Gene expression related to ACD disease will be quantified by qRT-PCR and RNA-seq. Quality control of herbal product will be conducted qualitatively and quantitatively by HPLC and HPLC QTOF-MS Preliminary data has shown that TP is able to establish the quality control method by HPLC and HPLC-QTOF-MS. Structure of active ingredients in the two major herbs have been identified using MS2 spectrums with the absence of reference substances. Concentrations of active ingredients in the other two herbs have been determined by HPLC. We have already successfully established the in vitro live-immune co-culture system. Functionality of HepRG in the proposed system has been fully tested in the validated ACD disease model. Inflammatory markers (IL8 and IL1ß) and co-stimulatory marker CD86 are significantly downregulated after treatment with the two major herbal combination extract, indicating the strong efficacy. Recent studies reveal that in 2016, the cost to the health system to treat ACD patients was $314 million globally and the annual economic burden is conservatively estimated at $5.3 billion. Currently oral antibiotics are heavily used in the treatment of ACD but exert severe side effects. The desire for an effective treatment of CAD with minor side effects has remained unfulfilled. Radix Arnebiae and Dictamni Cortex have been individually formulated into various prescriptions in the treatment of dermatitis for thousands of years with minimal side effect. The long period of traditional use and empirical evidence is proof of their safety and effectiveness, which prompted us to propose a novel herbal product with the combination of four herbs for ACD treatment. title: Model-based energy utilization monitoring and optimization system for energy efficiency in industrial spray dryers
abs: Spray drying is the most frequently used drying technique to produce powders. However, the average energy efficiency of industrial spray dryers is only around 50%, leaving a wide scope for the optimization of energy usage. Unfortunately, the goal of energy efficiency in a typical spray drying production facility is not straightforward as conditions that affect processes, operations, and priorities are constantly in flux, resulting in challenging decision-making. The aim of this collaborative project is to optimize the energy efficiency of industrial spray drying processes by developing a system comprising energy utilization monitoring and data-based models combined with optimization methods. To achieve this aim, the project team will: i. Perform a mass and energy balance on the spray dryer to calculate its specific energy consumption and, by comparing it to the theoretical benchmark, its energy efficiency ii. Design a system that will display the spray dryer’s energy utilization data in real-time iii. Develop a data-based model of the spray dryer and identifying the variables that may be used to improve energy efficiency iv. Formulate an optimal energy use strategy that adheres to operational constraints and one that will not compromise product quality v. Quantify predicted energy savings if different heat recovery methods are implemented vi. Deploy the models and reporting mechanisms in MS EXCEL We propose a methodology that combines the strengths of data mining, modelling, and optimization to maximise energy efficiency of a spray dryer in a manufacturing setting. A combination of data- and steady-state mechanistic models will be used to form a robust model ecosystem. The data-based model approach involve specifying the model structure and the associated variables, informed by process knowledge and data correlations. Potential models will be validated by comparisons against process data obtained from the manufacturing plant of the project collaborator, Abbott Manufacturing Singapore (AMS). Once an applicable model is established, the inverse problem to determine parameters that can be used to optimize energy utilization will be tackled next. In parallel, a steady-state mechanistic model of the spray dryer will be developed, essentially a reconciliation of the measured data via mass and energy balances. This steady-state model will be used to benchmark dryer energy efficiency, based on a theoretical thermodynamic model of a spray dryer extended by using phase equilibrium relationships. title: Optimising Surgical Management and Patient-related Outcomes of Epiretinal Membrane: Predictive Analytics and Randomised Trial
abs: Epiretinal membrane (ERM) is a common age-related eye disease that can cause significant visual impairment with adverse impact on quality of life. Clinical management of ERM is currently hampered by two major challenges. First, it is difficult for clinicians to predict prognostic outcomes for ERM patients being managed conservatively or considered for surgical intervention. A major unmet medical need is therefore to develop a new method to improve prognostic assessment for patients with ERM. Second, surgeons are often faced with a dilemma when they manage patients with concomitant ERM and cataract, because it is unclear which surgical approach is the most appropriate for these patients. Combined cataract and ERM surgery is a popular choice, but this approach may result in unnecessary surgery being performed for ERM that may not contribute significantly to visual impairment. Emerging evidence suggests that cataract surgery alone, which is a cheaper and potentially safer option with faster visual rehabilitation, may achieve similar visual outcome as compared to combined surgical approach for many of these patients. Thus, another major unmet medical need is quality evidence to determine the best surgical approach for patients with concomitant ERM and cataract. In this project, we will conduct a large, multi-ethnic, prospective clinical cohort study of 1,000 patients with ERM. Based on comprehensive clinical and multimodal retinal imaging data, we will develop, with the use of predictive analytics and machine-learning, an algorithm that provides accurate risk prediction for clinically meaningful prognostic outcomes. In addition, we will conduct a pilot randomized controlled trial to evaluate a new surgical approach that may achieve similar visual outcome while reducing the number of unnecessary ERM surgery for patients with concomitant ERM and cataract. Taken together, we anticipate our study to generate impactful data that will greatly optimise the surgical management and patient-related outcomes of ERM.

title: Optical coherence tomography-based novel outcome measures for disease monitoring in intraocular inflammatory and infectious diseases
abs: Uveitis or intraocular inflammatory and infectious diseases (IOID) is a major cause of blindness across the world. Detection and evaluation of inflammatory activity is essential to the management of uveitis, but yet continues to be largely dependent on subjective clinically assessed outcome measures. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) has provided an alternative option of non-invasive, quantitative imaging of structural changes involving the vitreous, retina and choroid. Choroidal vascularity index (CVI) and vitreous haze index (VHI) are both objective outcome measures based on OCT. They are shown to be robust disease biomarkers in previous studies but their use is limited by manual image processing. This study aims, firstly to develop a fully automated algorithm to derive CVI and VHI and secondly to validate and compare automated CVI and VHI with current clinical and imaging outcome measures for diagnosis and disease activity monitoring in IOID. The proposed study will be cross-sectional and longitudinal in nature with subjects with IOID and control group. Two study visits at 6 months interval are required and subjects will be undergo full ophthalmological examination and imaging tests including OCT, fundus photo and flaremeter. We will collaborate with external software engineers for development of image analysis algorithm based on machine learning model trained by manual analysis. Automated CVI and VHI will be calculated and compared with clinically assessed outcome measures for its performance in diagnosis and disease activity assessment. Outcome from this study will fulfil an urgent unmet need to develop better outcome measures for the assessment of IOID. Application of this study can advance care of uveitis patients in two ways: first for use as endpoints in clinical trials with a view to drug development and licensing; second to make better informed treatment decisions in routine clinical practice to reduce the morbidity associated with under- and over-treatment.

title: Silk Sleeve Device for Improving the Graft Bonding at the Bone Tunnel for Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Reconstruction – A Phase I/II Study
abs: The Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) is one of the most frequently injured knee ligaments, and ruptures of the ACL can cause significant pain, loss of function and healthcare costs. Surgical reconstruction with tendon graft remains the gold standard treatment for ACL ruptures. However, less than the optimal healing of the tendon graft within the surgically created bone tunnel remains a fundamental problem. The proposed solution involves the use of a silk fibroin (SF) based sheath, loaded with nanoparticles of low-crystallinity hydroxyapatite (nHA), and sleeved onto tendon autografts to complement their use and promote enthesis formation. This osteoconductive Tissue Interface Augmentation (TIA) device has been shown to be efficacious in our bench studies, biocompatible for its intended purpose (ISO10993: Biological evaluation of medical devices), and is subsequently studied in the porcine model. It has been shown that nHA stimulated tissue infiltration of host bone tissue, resulting in bone tunnel narrowing with new mineralized tissues. Consequently, there was enhanced graft-to-host integration progressively over the 9 months preclinical study, which potentially resulted in overall mechanical properties closer to that of the native bone-ACL-bone construct. In this first-in-human, double-blinded and randomized trial, the conventional ACLR will be compared with ACLR incorporating TIA. Primary outcomes are safety, knee stability after 1 year, while secondary outcomes are tunnel size, MRI evaluation, and knee survey. The aim is to determine clinical safety and efficacy of the TIA device in improving and accelerating osteointegration of tendon graft, leading to enhanced overall joint stability and shorter recovery period. It is hypothesized that patients treated with the TIA device will have early postoperative outcomes that are better than patients treated by conventional ACLR using autografts. With patent filed and expressed commercial interest from the Singapore MedTech Accelerator Program, there is great commercial potential in this technology locally and internationally.

title: Safety Of The Ingestible Magnetically Inflated Balloon Capsule (IMI-BC) For The Treatment Of Obesity
abs: Background Intragastric balloons (IGBs) are an established treatment option for obesity. They are not completely accepted by patients as they require endoscopic or catheter assistance for insertion and/or removal. We developed a novel ingestible magnetically inflated balloon capsule (IMI-BC) that can be administered and activated without endoscopic/catheter assistance. An external sensor tracks the location of the IMI-BC within the gastrointestinal tract (GIT). Prior animal and human trials have been performed, demonstrating feasibility of inflating the IMI-BC using an external hand-held magnet. Aims and hypotheses The study aim is to demonstrate safety of the IMI-BC in animal and human trials. Our hypothesis is that the IMI-BC can be safely ingested and excreted without any treatment-related adverse events. Methodology In the survival animal study, 5 live female pigs will swallow the IMI-BC. After activation of the IMI-BC, diet will be resumed. An external sensor will perform daily tracking of the IMI-BC’s progression till its complete excretion from the GIT. Subsequently, necropsy will be performed to evaluate for adverse events. In the human trial, 5 healthy volunteers will swallow the IMI-BC in an outpatient setting. After activation of the IMI-BC, diet will be resumed. An external sensor will perform daily tracking of the IMI-BC’s progression in an outpatient clinic, till its complete excretion. Subsequently, gastroscopy and colonoscopy will be performed to evaluate for adverse events. Study Feasibility The study team, comprising of doctors and engineers, has performed similar animal and human trials using the IMI-BC. Should the subjects develop complications, the study will be halted and appropriate medical treatment administered. Clinical Application Our novel IMI-BC is superior to other IGBs available in the market. Unlikely current devices, our IMI-BC’s compact size allows for easily ingestibility. No endoscopic/catheter assistance is required for insertion/inflation. This provides a convenient, cheaper and comfortable treatment method for patients.
kw: Obesity; Intra-gastric balloons

title: The role of uteroplacental inositol in inhibiting preterm labour-onset and rupture of membranes
abs: Preterm birth (PTB) complicates 10% of livebirths, of which a third is associated with preterm pre-labour rupture of membranes (PPROM). PTB is the leading cause of perinatal mortality and morbidity, with many survivors displaying long-term sequelae. Majority of PTBs occur in women with no apparent risk factors and there are at present no suitable PTB prevention measures for them. Recent small trials suggest that antenatal inositol supplementation may reduce PTB risk but the mechanism of effect is unknown. This proposal seeks to establish the biological plausibility for this effect and enable targeting of treatment to specific subgroups of women. We hypothesize that the placenta is the primary focus of inositol action; a premature or accelerated decline in placental inositol content during gestation will increase the risk of PTB and PPROM through the promotion of eicosanoid production and pro-inflammatory activity within the uteroplacental environment, which induces uterine contractions and reduces the tensile strength of amnio-chorionic membranes. This study will leverage on NiPPeR, the largest RCT of an inositol supplement, and the only one where placenta was collected. We aim to 1) associate placental inositol with eicosanoid and inflammatory factors, and assess impact of the NiPPeR intervention, 2) determine the effects of inositol and inositol-treated-placental-conditioned-media on amnio-chorionic membrane tensile strength and myometrial contractility, 3) assess if longitudinal maternal plasma and urinary inositol measures represent biomarkers for improved PTB prediction and if they can stratify women who may benefit from inositol prophylaxis. This innovative study employs advanced technologies and data science, utilizes unique biosamples from an intervention trial with extensive phenotypic data, thus, providing an unprecedented opportunity to address how inositol can suppress PTB, and bring novelty to PTB prediction and prevention. The evidence gathered will provide critical scientific underpinning for design of definitive inositol RCTs for PTB reduction with substantial impact worldwide.

title: To establish a predictive artificial intelligence (AI) based model using immune-phenotype correlation for disease stratification and prognosis in patients with ocular tuberculosis (OTB).
abs: Ocular infections from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) may masquerade as infective and non-infective entities with insidious and chronic clinical course. The clinical presentation of OTB is heterogeneous and Mtb is rarely found in ocular fluid samples. This renders the diagnosis of OTB challenging, complicating clinical decision making and counselling about the management and prognostication of disease. The treatment of OTB requires a combination of anti-tubercular therapy (ATT) and immunosuppression. However, the evaluation of treatment response is complexed due to the paradoxical clinical response to ATT as well as evolving trends in Mtb antibiotic resistance. Due to the lack of reliable randomized controlled trials (RCT), it remains uncertain whether the current treatment methods are effective. Thus, there is a clinical need to develop well-defined evidence-based guidelines for the management of OTB. Fundamentally, there are three hypotheses regarding the mechanism of TB-associated ocular inflammation. First being an inflammatory response to intra-ocular Mtb infection, second being an Mtb-driven autoimmune response, and lastly a remote immune priming by Mtb in the periphery. Based on these, the diagnosis and treatment of OTB are aimed at the detection and elimination of latent Mtb infection using anti-inflammatory medications with adjunctive ATT. Herewith, we aim to evaluate the immune cell signatures from biological samples in patients with established clinical phenotypes of OTB, derive clues that would point to the likely one of the three possible pathways contributing to each phenotype, and conclusively establish its pathologic mechanisms. The overall aim of this study will be to develop an OTB management algorithm using clinical, laboratory, imaging and immunotyping data, enabling early detection and prevention of TB related vision loss. This study may lead to new paradigm shift in the understanding and management of OTB.

title: Transmission Potential of Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2-infected Persons
abs: Aim: The asymptomatic/pre-symptomatic phase of COVID-19 could have a significant role in the transmission of SARS-CoV-2. The primary aim of this study is to determine the SARS-CoV-2 attack rate among household close contacts of asymptomatic/pre-symptomatic index cases. Methodology: Among the household close contacts, secondary transmitted cases (incident cases) will be identified, being defined as those who have a negative entry swab (as well as a negative serology test result, if it was performed) at the start of their Quarantine Order (QO), followed by either a (i) positive exit swab/serology test result at the end of their QO, or (ii) positive “symptomatic swab” if they had developed symptoms during their QO period and were referred for testing. Serology testing will be performed at the start and end of the QO for household contacts of asymptomatic/pre-symptomatic cases who do not have prior serology test results, and positive serology results will be further confirmed using S-Flow (SIgN). Whole-genome sequencing will also be carried out for all positive samples to identify potential transmission linkages. Analysis endpoints and clinical significance: The primary analysis endpoint of this study is to determine the rate of confirmed secondary transmission from asymptomatic/pre-symptomatic index sources to household close contacts. A secondary analysis endpoint will be to establish predictors of transmission. The findings gathered from this study would contribute to the ongoing national control efforts on the COVID-19 outbreak.

title: Th17 and natural killer cells as modulators of the central nervous system in childhood epilepsy
abs: Epilepsy is common and current treatments are directed after epilepsy is established. Anticonvulsants are first line but in one-third, epilepsy persists. Refractory epilepsy requires complicated & expensive treatments. Ideally, treatment should target epileptogenesis - the underlying process that creates and perpetuates epilepsy and leads to refractory epilepsy. We urgently need to understand mechanisms in epileptogenesis, in order to develop treatments to prevent development of epilepsy & progression to refractory epilepsy. Inflammation plays a key role in epilepsy. Our pilot work shows increased T-helper 17 (Th17) and CX3CR1+ Natural Killer (NK) cell- mediated pro-inflammatory processes in refractory epilepsy. Th17 and CX3CR1+NK modulation of immune dysfunction in epilepsy is a coherent target for further research. Aim 1:Determine Th17 and CX3CR1+NK mediated immune dysregulation between established refractory and non-refractory epilepsy. Hypothesis 1:Refractory epilepsy patients have upregulation of Th17 and downregulation of CX3CR1+NK cells in the peripheral immune system, compared to non-refractory epilepsy. Aim 2:Determine CX3CR1+NK mediated immune dysregulation in the peripheral immune system and central nervous system in refractory epilepsy. Hypothesis 2:In refractory childhood epilepsy, Th17 up-regulation and CX3CR1+NK down-regulation is present in both peripheral immune system and central nervous system. Aim 3:Determine Th17 and CX3CR1+NK-mediated immune dysregulation in the development of epilepsy and progression to refractory epilepsy. Hypothesis 3:In first afebrile seizure or newly diagnosed epilepsy, Th17 and CX3CR1+NK dysregulation is associated with disease progression. Exploratory Aim:Explore the roles of the microbiome and genetic factors in non-refractory and refractory childhood epilepsy. Our innovative approach will provide a deeper understanding of the immune system’s role in epilepsy to identify therapeutic targets to dampen and prevent induction of the innate response and the adaptive immune response, in order to develop clinical treatments to reduce the evolution to epilepsy, reduce clinical seizure severity and prevent development of refractory epilepsy.
