title: Identifying peripheral inflammatory and miRNA signature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) in CNS-derived circulating exosomes: impact of Apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) in disease progression
abs: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a hallmark of aberrant brain aging in later life with no current curative therapies or reliable blood biomarkers for its pre-symptomatic screening and diagnosis. The present proposal aims to identify mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD-specific inflammatory and protein biomarkers and miRNA signature in CNS-derived circulating exosomes which provide a novel way for studying cell-to-cell communication in the brain, and to investigate the potential driving effect of ApoE4 polymorphism as the strongest genetic risk factor of AD. Among participants in the Singapore Longitudinal Aging Studies wave 2, we performed clinical characterization of disease status, measurements of cognitive function, and neuroimaging at baseline and 4-year follow-up. These provide basis for the due completion of the proposed study in which we will randomly include 200 MCI patients (equal numbers of ApoE4 homozygous and ApoE3 homozygous) and 100 age-(+/-2 years) and gender-matched controls with normal cognitive function. CNS-derived circulating exosomes will be isolated by Exoquick® Technology from plasma and quantified for AD-pathogenic and functionally specialized synaptic proteins, autolysosomal and inflammatory proteins, and AD-specific miRNA signature by Luminex, ELISA, immunohistochemistry, and qRT-PCR. We hypothesize that pre-existing inflammation, altered protein levels, and differential miRNA sets in exosomes are closely related to MCI and predictive of AD conversion. ApoE4 may be a primary driver of pathogenic protein accumulation and endosomal and lysosomal deficit formation. Age, sex, ApoE4, and identified exosome biomarkers may discriminate MCI and AD progression with high sensitivity and specificity. This study may facilitate the development of a non-invasive and cost-effective screening blood test which could assist the diagnosis of MCI and AD, before referring patients to cerebrospinal fluid test or neuroimaging. Once confirmed in larger elderly populations, these biomarkers may bring potential therapeutical opportunities for AD via vectors for small-molecule delivery considering that exosomes can pass the blood-brain barrier.
kw: Alzheimer's disease; extracellular vesicle; exosome; ApoE4; biomarker; mild cognitive disorder

title: Deep Profiling and in Situ Mapping of CD39+ and CD38+ Immune Cells in Asian Triple Negative Breast Cancers: Building A Prognostic Model for Precision Medicine in the Era of Cancer Immunotherapy
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Our previous studies identified CD39+ and CD38+ immune cells as the predictive biomarkers which are superior to other known biomarkers to predict the responsiveness of anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy in lung and liver cancers. Anti-PD-L1 therapy was just approved by FDA in 2019 to treat PD-L1-positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic Triple Negative Breast Cancers (TNBC). We therefore aim to accurately quantitate and perform deep phenotyping of the CD39+ and CD38+ immune cells populations from both blood and tumour samples of TNBC patients, to ascertain their association with survival and responsiveness to both standard therapy and immunotherapy. We hypothesize that the precise quantification of the CD39+ and CD38+ immune cells populations in TNBC could yield prognostic and predictive models for both standard therapy and immunotherapy. In order to deeply profile and in-situ map the CD39+ and CD38+ immune cells, prospectively 50 TNBC patients in Singapore General Hospital (SGH), will be recruited and their fresh-frozen tumour samples and blood will be analysed using 24-markers Flowcytometry (CyTEK) and reciprocally validated with Multiplex-Immunofluorescence (MIF) in the matched FFPE samples. The selected immune-subsets will be further validated on tissue microarrays (TMAs) constructed from 400 TNBC diagnosed between 2003 and 2015 in SGH. The prognostic value of each of the CD39+ and CD38+ subsets will be evaluated by the improvement of the proprietary prognostic model which was previously published and built by our group. Lastly, the prognostic and predictive power will be tested on an independent cohort of initial biopsies from 200 and 50 TNBC patients received standard chemotherapy and anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy respectively. Inclusion of data generated from CD39+ and CD38+ immune cells as novel panel to the prognostic/predictive model can equip pathologists and oncologists with a better tool to evaluate TNBC patients, ultimately improving clinical management and patients’ quality of life in the era of immunotherapy.
kw: cancer immunology, breast cancer, immunotherapy, tumor microenvironment

title: Algorithm for diagnosis of peripheral blood films via deep learning and computer vision.
abs: Aims: Investigation into the feasibility of using deep learning algorithms in an Artificial Intelligence based software to improve the efficiency and accuracy of peripheral blood film (PBF) interpretation in the clinical laboratory setting in major hospitals. Hypotheses: Deep learning algorithms trained through computer vision via convoluted neural networks can be used in identification and classification of haematopoietic cells on a PBF to form an accurate clinical diagnosis. Methodology: Labelled and validated data is fed into deep learning rigs for artificial intelligence based software to be trained. A total of 120,000 annotated cells are required for training the software. 2 randomized control trials (RCT) will be done with double blinding of reporting haematologist/medical technologist, comparing outcomes of software-guided cell interpretation and blood film diagnosis versus human interpretation (gold standard). The data of the RCT includes breakdowns by class of detection, such that the performance of the software on each class of cell can be examined in greater detail. Approach: This is lead by National Healthcare Group (NHG) in collaboration with a local startup, Gallenco. NHG has the medical expertise and a large dataset of images of peripheral blood cells and Gallenco has the software programming capability. Feasibility: PBFs are currently reviewed by the laboratory technologists; films with abnormal characteristics are escalated to the haematologist. The software will facilitate standard screening and reporting of PBF duties by a laboratory technologist/haematologist and reduce the total bench time required, potentially saving man hours and improving the workflow in flagging up serious cases that might otherwise have gone undetected due to observer error or fatigue. This allows doctors to intervene earlier, translating into improved patient outcomes and reduced patient length of stay. The software can be transposed to mobile applications and in tele-haematology, where remote laboratories can send digitized films electronically for interpretation and validation

title: Targeting hepatic estrogen-related receptor alpha (ESRRA) for activating lysosomal biogenesis and function during non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and aging
abs: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a spectrum of progressive liver disorders that starts with hepatosteatosis (NAFL), evolves to steatohepatitis (NASH), and can eventuate in cirrhosis. With the recent rise in obesity and diabetes worldwide, the prevalence of NAFLD has increased dramatically. In Singapore, the prevalence of NAFLD is more than 50% adults. It is noteworthy that increasing age is associated with more severe histological changes and poorer clinical outcomes in NAFLD patients. While hepatosteatosis is relatively benign, the inflammation and fibrosis that occurs in NASH leads to disease progression. Currently, there are no approved pharmacological therapies for NASH. Estrogen-related receptor alpha (ESRRA) is a member of the nuclear hormone receptor superfamily. Our analysis of the hepatic transcriptomes from NAFLD patients and a diet-induced NAFLD mouse model strongly suggested that downregulation of ESRRA and lysosomal genes were closely associated with NAFLD progression. Our preliminary data in several other NAFLD mouse models (diet-induced and genetic) also demonstrated this association. Genetic knockout of ESRRA and pharmacological inhibition with XCT790 in mouse liver, and studies in mouse/human hepatic cell lines showed decreased lysosomal number and function while ESRRA overexpression in vivo increased lysosomal protein expression. Furthermore, ESRRA and lysosomal genes were down-regulated in livers from aged mice. Accordingly, we hypothesize that impairment in ESRRA regulation of lysosome function is a novel pathway that contributes significantly to the development of NAFLD and aging. We thus propose the following Specific Aims: 1) To investigate hepatic ESRRA regulation of lysosomal biogenesis and activity; 2) To investigate hepatic ESRRA function in NASH; and 3) To investigate the effect of hepatic ESRRA activation in NALD during aging. These studies will delineate the important role of ESRRA regulation of lysosome biogenesis and activity during NASH and aging, and provide a promising drug target for these conditions.

title: Mitochondria Transfer in Erythroblastic Island Niche in Homeostatic and Stress Erythropoiesis
abs: Erythropoiesis occurs in a specialized microenvironment in the bone marrow, termed Erythroblastic Island (EBI). EBI contains a central macrophage surrounded by several erythroblasts and the central macrophage functions to mediate the proliferation, differentiation, and enucleation of erythroid cells. Interestingly, recent studies have demonstrated the intercellular transport of functional mitochondria between various cell types. In the context of erythroid maturation, however, it remain largely unknown whether mitochondria can be transported from erythroid cells to the EBI niche, as well as the biological functions of mitochondria transfer. More importantly, investigating the mechanisms and functions of mitochondria transfer in erythroid maturation sheds light on novel approach in the ex vivo expansion of transfusable RBCs, as well as the discovery of the emergence machineries in the context of stress erythropoiesis, which will lead to the identification of novel targets for the therapy of anaemia of chronic diseases. Here, we reconstituted EBI in vitro and demonstrated different modes of mitochondria transfer in the EBI. Subsequently, we showed that mitochondria transfer in vitro is highly associated with native EBI marker expression and activated macrophage is required for erythroid maturation. Hence based on the preliminary data, we hypothesize that mitochondria transfer in the EBI might be associated with recovery from stress erythropoiesis caused by hemolytic anemia. Therefore we propose this project aiming to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of mitochondria transfer in (1) homeostatic erythroid differentiation via in vivo bone marrow transplantation model, and (2) stressed erythropoiesis via phenylhydrazine induced hemolytic aneamia mice model and patient samples.

title: Targeting lnc-BATE1 in adipose tissue as a therapeutic strategy for obesity
abs: Activation of brown fat and beige fat has been tightly associated with improved metabolic health and is therefore considered as an attractive therapeutic approach against obesity and its associated diseases. Emerging evidence has shown long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play an important role in BAT biology. Our previous work has established lnc-BATE1, a BAT-enriched long-noncoding RNA, as an indispensable factor for brown adipocyte development and gene program maintenance. We hypothesize that lnc-BATE1 plays a significant role in promoting browning program in white fat and may be effective in preventing obesity development. In order to test this hypothesis, we will conduct an in vivo study by using an aP2-lnc-BATE1 transgenic mouse model to overexpress lncBATE1 in adipose tissue. In this proposed research, we will (Aim 1) characterize the metabolic phenotype of aP2-lnc-BATE1 transgenic mice at physio-pathological conditions and (2) investigate the molecular mechanism used by lnc-BATE1 to modulate adipose tissue function. This proposed study will leverage on the cutting-edge RNA technologies, mouse physiology study, and computational analysis in an integrative project. The outcomes from this study will fully determine the role of lnc-BATE1 in brown fat development and during WAT browning. This will test the concept of the lncRNA-based therapy for obesity-related metabolic diseases.
kw: Lnc-BATE1; Brown adipose tissue; White adipose tissue; WAT browning program; obesity; Clinical potential

title: Phase 1 study of Pressurized IntraPeritoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy (PIPAC) with Paclitaxel in Peritoneal Carcinomatosis for Gastric Cancer
abs: Peritoneal Carcinomatosis (PC) is a miserable disease with poor treatment outcome and the most common site of metastasis in gastric cancer (GC). Current therapeutic options have limited efficacy and/or limited by poor repartition, limited tissue penetration and significant morbidity. Pressurized lntra-Peritoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy (PIPAC) is a novel drug delivery technique taking advantage of physical laws (gaseous nature, hydrostatic pressure) with superior pharmacological properties (homogeneous distribution, deeper tissue penetration). It is applied through minimally invasive laparoscopy with a recent systematic review showing promising results. Paclitaxel is highly effective intraperitoneally in GC. However, there is no data on PIPAC with paclitaxel. We are completing a pre-clinical study on PIPAC-paclitaxel in swine. Based on these results, we aim to perform a first-in-human, phase I 3+3 dose escalation clinical trial with PIPAC-paclitaxel. The primary aim of this Phase I study is to determine the Maximal Tolerated Dose (MTD) of paclitaxel administered as PIPAC for advanced GC. The secondary aims are to determine the safety profile and tolerability by assessment of dose limiting toxicities and the adverse event profile, evaluate the clinical and pathological response, identify the pharmacokinetic profile, assess peritoneal tissue concentrations and depth of penetration and perform correlative studies on blood, urine, peritoneal fluid and tissue. Our hypothesis is that PIPAC-paclitaxel can be administered over a wide therapeutic dose range with minimal systemic toxicity, and that MTD will be limited by local toxicity. This study will serve as a basis for future clinical trials for PIPAC-paclitaxel which would include combination with systemic chemotherapy, adding a promising therapeutic option in the treatment of peritoneal carcinomatosis for GC.
kw: Peritoneal carcinomatosis, Peritoneal metastasis, Pressurized Intraperitoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy, Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy, Paclitaxel

title: Small Fiber Neuropathy: Classification and Search for Etiology
abs: INTRODUCTION Small fiber neuropathy (SFN) is a disease that exclusively affects the small nerve fibers, causing heterogenous symptoms of pain, paresthesia, and/or autonomic symptoms such as constipation, or orthostatic hypotension. Diagnostic tests and criteria only became available in the past decade, and a well-defined subtyping system is not available. The cause is presumed to be autoimmune in nature due to patients' favourable response to intravenous immunoglobulin treatment. Genetic mutations have also been found in recent literature. This study aims to look for immunological and genetic biomarkers. By further understanding the etiology, subtyping and targeted treatment can be formulated. METHODS This study aims to recruit 80 SFN patients and 20 controls. Their clinical symptoms will be recorded, questionnaires to document pain and symptom severity, and disability scores will be administered. The blood sample of patients with SFN will be taken and sent for immunological testing and genetic testing. Immunological testing will include testing for antibodies against sodium channels, potassium channels and Trp channels, while proteomics will also be performed to look for other associated antibodies. Mass spectrometry will also be performed to look for soluble immune compounds. Genetic testing will be performed by Sanger sequencing, and whole exome sequencing in select patients. Patients will be followed up for 18 months. If they decide for a trial of intravenous immunoglobulin treatment, post-treatment bloods and questionnaires will be taken. Clinical, immunological and genetic correlations will be evaluated.

title: Small Fiber Neuropathy: Classification and Search for Etiology
abs: Specific Aims: Small fibre neuropathy (SFN), a neurological disease characterized by dysfunction in nociception, temperature, and autonomic modalities in a stocking-glove distribution, results from damage to unmyelinated nerve fibres in peripheral nerves. The prevalence of SFN is 52.95 per 100,000 population. Diabetes, amyloid, sarcoidosis, toxic substances and vitamin deficiency (B12) are common causes of SFN in our patients, but in 50% no cause is determined (idiopathic). Here, we focus on idiopathic SFN. Hypotheses: We hypothesize that autoimmune mechanisms and genetic mutations, especially involving sodium channels, contribute to disease pathophysiology in at least a subset of patients with idiopathic SFN. Our goal is to quantify and qualify the clinical features and pathophysiology of idiopathic SFN with a particular emphasis on autoimmunity and genetic mutations, and to develop a pragmatic work-up. Methodology: Patients confirmed to be diagnosed with SFN will be recruited from the Neurology, Rheumatology and Pain Services, with a target sample size of 80 patients. Clinical features, demographics, pain and disability scores will be obtained. Serum samples will be obtained and tested for antibodies again sodium channels by Western blot, and their genetic mutations by whole exome sequencing. Patients who test negative for sodium channels antibodies will be further screened for other potential target antibodies by proteomic techniques. If genetic mutations are detected by whole exome sequencing, the results will be validated by Sanger sequencing. The laboratory and clinical results will be compared and analysed by SPSS. Approach: Patients with confirmed diagnosis of definite small fiber neuropathy based on the current clinical criteria from National University Hospital Neurology, Rheumatology and Pain Services; and Ng Teng Fong General Hospital Neurology Service, will be approached for recruitment. Our target sample size is 80 patients. Clinical, autoimmune and genetic results will be compared and analysed. Feasibility and importance to science or medicine: SFN is a type of neuropathic pain that is under-diagnosed and diagnosis and treatment are still not concrete. Patients present with severe pain which oftentimes cannot be controlled with the usual neuropathic pain medications. Understanding the ethology of the disease will help in targeted diagnostic and treatment strategies for SFN. Our autonomic and small fiber neuropathy service is one of the major players and a tertiary referral centre in Asia and worldwide, and has produced unofficial guidelines and protocols for other neuromuscular services globally. This research will advance the knowledge of SFN allowing the development of official guidelines and marking Singapore and NUHS as an international referral centre for SFN and neuropathy.

title: Studies on low-cost and novel therapies for NASH
abs: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the leading cause of liver disease worldwide and occurs in approximately 40% of the adult population in Singapore. NAFLD frequently accompanies obesity and diabetes, and represents a disease spectrum that includes hepatosteatosis, steatohepatitis (NASH) and cirrhosis. While hepatosteatosis is thought to be relatively benign, NASH requires intervention in order to prevent its progression to cirrhosis. Currently, there is no available pharmacologic therapy to treat this condition. Since my last CSA application 5 years ago, we have identified three very promising and low-cost potential treatments for NASH: 1) Thyroid hormone (TH) stimulates hepatic autophagy,b-oxidation of fatty acids, and mitochondrial turnover. Additionally, the intrahepatic concentration of T3, the active form of TH, was decreased in a rodent model of NASH. Our studies in diabetic patients with NAFLD, showed that levothyroxine can decrease hepatosteatosis. 2) Short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota can stimulate hepatic autophagy and oxidative phosphorylation, suggesting that they may be able to reduce hepatosteatosis and improve NASH. 3) Vitamin B12/folate decreased serum homocysteine levels and hepatic inflammation and fibrosis. We also observed hyperhomocysteinemia and hepatic protein homocysteinylation in a mouse model NASH. Accordingly, we hypothesize that TH, SCFAs, and vitamin B12/folate can prevent and/or treat NASH. If so, what are the underlying molecular, cell signaling, and metabolic mechanisms for their beneficial effects? We will employ a dietary rodent model of NASH progression that we developed as well as a primate model of obesity for these studies. Since NASH also involves macrophage and hepatic stellate cell activation to cause inflammation and fibrosis, we also will study the effects of these compounds in these cells during NASH. We anticipate our studies will generate important new insights into the pathogenesis and treatment of NASH, and provide the foundation for future clinical studies.
kw: β-oxidation, NAFLD, Obesity, Short chain fatty acid, Homocysteine, Autophagy

title:
A novel multi-species lyophilized powder is safe and effective for use in
oral immunotherapy for prawn allergy
abs: Background: Food allergy has been recognized as the next global allergy epidemic. Oral immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment of food allergy. Although effective in peanut allergy, this approach has not been investigated in prawn allergy. Prawn allergy is highly prevalent in Asia, affecting 5.2-16% of the population and accounts for the majority of emergency room food triggered anaphylaxis events in children>6 years, and is the main cause of fatal food-induced anaphylaxis in Australia. Currently there is no effective treatment for shellfish allergy apart from life-long avoidance. This study aims to establish the efficacy and safety of a novel lyophilized multi-species powder for development of an pioneering oral immunotherapy treatment for prawn allergy. Hypotheses: A novel lyophilized multi-species prawn powder is effective and safe for diagnosis of species-specific prawn allergy, and can be developed for prawn oral immunotherapy. Aims 1. To optimize a lyophilization process that preserves the antigenic profile of Penaeus Monodon/L vannamei, with preservation of major and minor allergens and their allergenicity and immunogenicity 2. To confirm safety from microbial contamination, and evaluate the shelf-life by evaluating stability of allergenic and immunogenic properties 3. To confirm clinical reactivity via oral challenge Methodology: Allergenic profile of lyophilized cooked Penaeus monodon/L vannamei will be determined with SDS-PAGE, and correlated with raw and cooked P monodon/L vannamei. Allergenicity and immunogenicity will be analyzed with ELISA and skin prick tests with sera from known prawn-allergic patients. Stability and safety of lyophilized powder will be assessed with serial plate counts at sequential time periods at a range of temperatures. In-vivo reactivity will then be confirmed via oral challenge. Significance: Development of a safe and efficacious standardized product for delivery of prawn protein is important for standardization of oral challenges, and a crucial step before the progression to development of prawn oral immunotherapy.

title: Deciphering the Molecular Pathogenesis of Enterovirus 71: Towards Effective Treatment Options to Fight Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease
abs: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common, highly contagious viral infection that affects mostly infants and young children. It occurs worldwide but affects more prominently the Western Pacific region with recurrent cyclical outbreaks and large scale epidemics. With no treatment or vaccine widely available, HFMD is both a public health concern and a serious economic burden for societies. Coxsackievirus type A6 (CA6) and A16 (CA16), and enterovirus 71 (EV71) are the main causative agents responsible for HFMD and belong to the Picornaviridae family. Generally mild and self-limiting, EV71-associated HFMD may result in more severe, sometimes fatal, clinical outcome with neurological complications. The lack of therapeutic and prophylactic options to treat HFMD caused by EV71 infections is closely associated to our limited understanding of the pathogenesis. Vaccine development has so far relied on the traditional empirical approach of whole virus inactivation, which does not require extensive knowledge of the disease mechanisms. However, such knowledge will be required for the next generation of vaccine candidates, subunit in nature. Similarly, the drug development portfolio would greatly benefit from a deeper understanding of the pathogenesis at the molecular level for target-based drug development, in particular for strategies targeting host factors that may limit the likelihood of drug resistance. This proposal aims to decipher the molecular mechanisms involved in EV71 pathogenesis, including neuropathogenesis and immunopathogenesis. Using unique in vitro and in vivo models, this research programme harnesses cutting-edge, innovative technologies and expertise from various fields including virology, neurobiology, cell biology, immunology, and molecular biology, to tackle the disease from various angles and in a holistic manner. This project addresses major gaps in our current knowledge of EV71 pathogenesis and will identify critical host factors and viral determinants that may represent novel drug targets and vaccine candidates.

title: A versatile Singapore-based proprietary transgenesis platform for the biopharmaceutical and soft commodity sector
abs: Novel cell-based products with multifunctional attributes are driving innovation in the medical, biopharmaceutical and soft commodity industrial sectors. In this context, the production of protein therapeutics and the generation of genetically modified organisms greatly benefits from our ability to control genetic manipulation of host genomes with synthetic transgenes, hence making precise and safe genome engineering a crucial component for the development of many new products. Our proposal focusses on the safe delivery of multi-transgene expression cassettes into host genomes to achieve genetic enhancements. The approach capitalizes on our existing propriety transgenesis platform derived from the bacteriophage lambda integration system. The platform delivers both efficient derivation of seamless transgene cassettes and their precise in vivo insertion into a specific target sequence present in the human genome. In order to further enhance the performance of this platform for Singapore, the proposal has the following main aims: platform improvements with respect to efficiency and specificity using novel integrases, the broadening of applications for biomedical sectors with endogenous and artificial docking sites in a variety of commercially relevant cell types, and the platform expansion towards applications in the soft commodity sector using economically important microalgae. To achieve these aims, we have assembled a new team that will deliver the generation of novel integrase variants with enhanced specificity and efficiency, improvements for seamless transgene vector production and the production of biologics. Furthermore, the research will lead to the establishment of novel transgenesis platforms for microalgae, which are highly relevant to feed and aqua farming. The expected results are highly relevant for innovative approaches towards the production of novel cell-based products and organisms, and in particular open an opportunity to generate novel platforms on the basis of microalgae as key components of sustainable energy, food and soft commodity strategies including the corresponding intellectual property rights.

title: Spin Orbit Coupling based IntelligencE TechnologY (SOCIETY)
abs: Artificial intelligence (AI) is currently being widely used in multiple devices, including Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices, intelligent sensors and smartphones. However, the power consumption of AI devices still needs to be reduced by taking approaches combining hardware and software. There is great potential in neuromorphic computing (NC), which mimics the energy-efficient operations of the human brain’s neurons and synapses. However, further advances in hardware are needed. Among several candidates for this technological application, Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) based devices offer power saving, endurance, speed and compatibility with complementary metal oxide semiconductors (CMOS). Despite this potential, there are few studies on using SOC devices for NC applications. We have recently made significant progress in understanding domain wall (DW) motion control in DW devices. In this proposed programme, we will develop SOC-based DW devices and the related science and technology to demonstrate their potential for NC. We will design, fabricate and analyse CMOS-compatible synaptic devices, neurons and exploratory synaptic FET devices. Furthermore, we will design and develop SOC materials with increased charge-spin conversion efficiency to further reduce the power consumption of neuromorphic elements. Finally, we will integrate different combinations of synaptic devices and synthetic neurons in NC prototypes and carry out technological translation. To achieve these objectives, we will collaborate with industry and form a team of experts representing different disciplines in Singapore and overseas. The lead PI’s team will develop synaptic elements and neurons using SOC-based DW magnetoresistive devices. The team-PIs will work on the new materials, devices and prototypes of intelligent applications. The teams have relevant expertise in their proposed areas and are supported by collaborators with complementary expertise. We are working in tandem with GlobalFoundries, Singapore, to ensure that the technologies that we will develop are compatible with commercial fabrication processes and that the technology benefits a foundry in Singapore.

title: Towards On-Chip Topological Quantum Devices
abs: Following recent efforts to advance quantum information science and technology, the search for Majorana Fermions in condensed matter has become a focus of intense research worldwide. This is largely due to their potential as ‘decoherence free’ carriers of quantum information, promising scalable quantum computing architectures. However, to harness the much-coveted non-Abelian statistics of Majorana Fermions for on-chip quantum logic, Majorana bound states need to be created and spatially controlled by local electrostatic and magnetic fields. Here, we propose a stable Majorana platform in van-der-Waals heterostructures of atomically thin quantum spin Hall insulators and layered van-der-Waals superconductors. In these heterostructures, a unique parameter set promises feasibility of an electrostatically controlled topological phase transition - key for the control and manipulation of Majorana bound states. Towards this end we propose van-der-Waals engineering of topological quantum devices. Complementary Majorana bound state detection, using both electron transport and local probe spectroscopies, down to milliKelvin temperatures and high magnetic fields will allow unprecedented insight into the electronic signatures of Majorana bound states in quantum spin Hall insulators. Ultimately, this will allow us to tailor proof-of-principle on-chip logic devices in which Majorana Fermions can be induced and controlled towards the demonstration of topological quantum logic. A realization of such prototype devices in a technologically relevant material system – promising the integration with the conventional silicon platform – would constitute a major milestone towards the realization of scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Geobag Seawall to Replace Traditional Seawall
abs: This project aims to overcome Singapore’s vulnerability for sand by looking into the use of geobags (a generic name that includes geo-bags of various sizes, geo-tubes and geo-containers), which are filled with treated excavated material, as an alternative to using sand for permanent seawall construction to protect the coastline. By adopting this alternative design and construction method, the volume of sand needed in seawall construction could potentially be reduced by about 25%, thus leading to costs savings for imported materials, seawall foundation, and installation method.

title: Centre of Excellence for Autonomous and Remotely Operated Vessels (CEAOPS)
inst: TCOMS - Technology Centre for Offshore & Marine Singapore
abs: The capability development proposed as part of the CEAOPS brings together the physical-numerical model of the metocean environment, systems-level intelligence for the port operating environment and / or group of vessels, and risk-based decision frameworks. To date, MASS developments have largely been “vessel-centric”, aimed at the autonomous or remote control of a single vessel, where the smart systems are used to replace direct human operators. While this may suffice for operations along a fixed route or in areas with low vessel traffic, it is not enough to ensure safe and efficient operations in a complex environment where a heterogeneous mix of MASS and conventional vessels operate in restricted waters. In addition, interaction effects in multi-vessel scenarios must be properly accounted for in close-quarters operations, given the current practice of using historical trajectories for predicting future vessel path. To our knowledge, there is also limited efforts to harness environmental information at a systems level to optimise safety and efficiency. The proposed capability developments are thus significant steps beyond the current MASS development efforts. In the coupled physical-numerical modelling of the metocean environment, sensed data from field measurements and possibly other vessels will be assimilated into advanced numerical models to provide accurate forecasts of the forcings on the vessel at both global and local levels. These in turn can be used to derive accurate coupled responses in multi-vessel scenarios and structural loadings on the vessels’ hull, respectively. The fusion of environmental prediction capabilities into vessel global response and structural models can be used to optimise safety and efficiency during operations, as well as through life management. This incorporation of environmental awareness into vessel motion and structure models bridges across traditional “discipline-focused” developments that is commonly found in the industry. Concurrently, physical-numerical modelling approaches are also used to integrate field data into models of vessel motions (manoeuvring and seakeeping) and vessel hull structure. The resultant digital twins are subsequently used in combination with the metocean model described in the previous paragraph, to provide enriched datasets that include “edge cases” such as challenging sea states, near-miss scenarios or other conditions deemed too high-risk for actual testing. Thereafter, data-driven models are derived and combined with risk-based decision support frameworks, as well as systems-level intelligence, to provide guidance and advisory to the vessel operators and owners. These intelligent systems models will have the ability to self-learn and improve their knowledge with time and every encounter with operational challenges. The overall approach can be considered amongst the first development efforts to merge physical-numerical models, data-driven methodologies, self-learning capabilitie

title: An Integrated Smart Solution to Lift Safety Monitoring and Fault Predictive Diagnosis
abs: SoftGrid, together with their Co-PI from SIMTech, proposed two portions of work package for lift condition monitoring and diagnosis, and energy anomaly pattern discovery by power signals, to cover Work Area 2. Work Package A: Artificial Intelligence for Lift Condition Monitoring and Diagnosis Work Package B: Artificial Intelligence for Energy Anomaly Patterns Discovery by Power Signals for Lift Fault Detection Current research on Artificial Intelligence for Lift Condition Monitoring and Diagnosis With the rapid development of modern technology, more efficient maintenance approaches such as condition based maintenance (CBM) has been actively pursued in the industry in recent years. CBM can significantly reduce maintenance cost by reducing the unnecessary scheduled preventive maintenance operations where equipment outages are predicted and maintenance is carried out only when necessary. It is critical for improving safety, planning missions, scheduling maintenance, and reducing maintenance costs and down time. The current techniques can be categorized as exceedance detection and statistical analysis. a. Exceedance detection Exceedance detection detects abnormal events by monitoring whether a set of operation parameters exceed the predefined threshold under certain circumstances. The set of operation parameters to be monitored and the corresponding thresholds are specified by domain experts in advance [4]. b. Statistical analysis Statistical distributions are fit on the normal sensor values. The anomaly is detected when the probability of the sensor value from the statistical distribution is low. As Compared to the exceedance detection technique, the more information can be provided by the statistical analysis technique [5]. These techniques are not enough for CBM requirement. Two important techniques in CBM are researched in diagnostics and prognostics [6]. Today’s concept of machine diagnosis comprises the automated detection and classification of faults, whereas machine prognosis is the automated estimation of how soon and likely a failure will occur. To ensure successful condition-based maintenance, it is necessary to detect, identify and classify different kinds of failure modes in the manufacturing process. Sensing technology is necessary in implementing the detecting system. Features are then extracted and selected to analyse the signals from all these sensors to assess the condition of the system. Another popular AI techniques for machine diagnosis are artificial neural networks (ANNs), fuzzy logic systems, fuzzy-neural networks (FNNs), neural-fuzzy systems and evolutionary algorithms (EAs). title: NCL Phase 2
abs: NCL aspires to be the cybersecurity experimentation platform to conduct and investigate complex and dangerous cybersecurity experiments and problems, with the goal of boosting performance and productivity of researchers and industry. The first phase of the National Cybersecurity R&D Lab (NCL) started in Nov 2016 and is expected to complete in Oct 2019. To support experimentation for cybersecurity R&D community, NCL's first phase focuses on building up an infrastructure for experimentation and engagement of local cybersecurity community. Going forward to the 2nd phase, we believe that to better serve the community, NCL should realign some of its focus. As the infrastructure stabilizes, we propose shifting the focus of NCL’s development from infrastructure to application services. In particular, to provide more automation and efficiency in environment provisioning. Additionally, to stay relevant, NCL should build up new capabilities by exploring and researching potential services and experimentation technologies, for example, on scenarios management and generation, traffic generation, provisioning mechanisms for trusted computing, etc. In phase 2, we propose NCL to have more active collaborations with the community, both locally and internationally, to develop NCL in a synergistic manner. This can be achieved via a grant-call mechanism.

title: Integrated on-chip planar coherent light sources
abs: In this program, we are aiming to develop the integrated on-chip planar coherent light sources for both visible light and fibre-optic communications by use of the emerging layered materials. Commercially, the visible light communication owns a fast-growing market size, which is expected to increase with an annual growth rate of 62.9% from USD 1.3 Billion in 2017 to USD 14.9 Billion by 2022. Meanwhile, the market value of optical interconnects will reach USD 13.0 Billion by 2022 due to the expanding carrier and enterprise networks. In this programme, the envisioned outcomes are (i) to understand light-matter interactions in the interesting layered materials and their optoelectronic devices; (ii) to produce the new family of coherent light sources based on two dimensional semiconductors with desirable emission features such as ultralow threshold, room temperature operation, tunable working bandwidth and high compatibility; and (iii) to integrate the proposed on-chip coherent light sources for visible light and fibre-optic communications. Our research deliverables are targeted to the global market of commercial coherent light sources for optical communications in both visible (390-780 nm) and telecom transmission windows (1200-1600 nm). In particular, the proposed on-chip coherent light sources working in telecom spectral range are fully compatible with Si-based photonic platforms. Most importantly, superior to two main competing on-chip light sources based on III-V (e.g. GaAs) and IV (Si, SiGe) semiconductors, respectively limited by compatibility with Si-based platforms and emission efficiencies due to indirect band gaps, the proposed devices employing ultrathin layered materials are highly compatible with Si-based integrated circuit techniques and own direct-bandgap emitting media with the expected near-unity quantum efficiencies. Moreover, the facile wafer-scale growth, transfer and modification of two dimensional semiconductors promise lower cost than the ones built up by use of traditional III-V and IV semiconductors, implying the great economic potential.

title: Singapore Gastric Cancer Consortium - Bringing Discoveries to Patients
abs: Gastric cancer (GC) is the 5th leading cause of cancer mortality globally. While GC age-adjusted incidence is declining, the absolute number of GC cases is expected to increase due to overall population growth and aging. GC is prevalent in Asian countries and in Singapore, GCs represent the 4th/5th highest causes of cancer death in males/females respectively. The Singapore Gastric Cancer Consortium (SGCC) is an integrative multidisciplinary national research program, which over the past decade has established Singapore as a global leader in GC research and treatment, establishing unique population cohorts, novel GC molecular classifications, insights into GC carcinogenesis, and innovative investigator-initiated clinical trials. In this renewal, we seek to take these discoveries back to patients, through five investigational themes in precision prevention, precision therapy and data-driven target identification. First, as early diagnosis is a major factor to improving GC outcomes, we have developed and will be validating novel methods for early detection and risk stratification in high-risk patients, with implications for population screening. Second, for advanced GC patients, we will combine information from molecular biomarkers, organoid platforms, and artificial intelligence to guide the rational and data-driven selection of optimal combination therapies and dosing. Third, we will deeply study the clinical challenge of GC peritoneal carcinomatosis, representing the deadliest and most treatment-refractory presentation of this malignancy. Fourth, using lineage-tracing technologies, we will probe potential GC cells-of-origin (“cancer stem cells”) to identify new therapeutic targets. Fifth, as intra-tumour heterogeneity (ITH) is a major barrier to successful GC treatment, we will apply single-cell technologies to comprehensively demarcate ITH evolution through distinct stages of gastric carcinogenesis and across different intra-tumour cell types. Findings from these themes will apply directly to GC patients, maintain Singapore’s leadership role in the GC field, form a rich training ground for new researchers/clinician scientists, and opportunities for industry partnerships.

title: Translational Asian Age-related macular degeneration program (TAAP): 4.2 To determine long-term outcomes, recurrence rates and treatment needs in PCV
abs: Over the past decade, in white populations with AMD treated with anti- VEGF therapy, the best visual outcome is achieved within 1-2 years, but visual ultimately declines after 3 years and often to worse than presentation.1-3 However, no long-term data on Asian patients with PCV have been reported. The reason for poor visual outcome has been attributed to sub-optimal treatment, recurrence leading to chronic exudation or haemorrhage, and development of scarring and/or atrophy. Our group has shown that recurrence in PCV is as high as 53% after 3 years and may be a key factor limiting long term visual acuity improvements.4 Other groups have reported even higher recurrence rates varying from 40-78.6% after 3 years of follow-up.4 However the risk factors for recurrence remain poorly understood. A key unanswered question from the recent RCTs is whether the ability of combination therapy to achieve higher polyp closure rate will translate into lower recurrence and better long- term visual acuity. Furthermore, there are concerns that higher PDT-induced polyp closure rates might come at the expense of choriocapillaris damage. To answer these important questions, we will conduct a 5-year follow-up examination of patients who have completed the EVEREST II, PLANET and PCV T&E studies. 1. HYPOTHESIS AND OBJECTIVES To determine long-term outcomes, recurrence rates, and treatment needs in PCV • Aim 1: To describe the long-term outcomes, recurrence rates and treatment patterns in PCV patients 5 years after first presentation. • Aim 2: To evaluate whether polyp closure within the first 12 months of therapy is associated with better long-term visual outcome. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that recurrence rate is high in patients with PCV and that polyp closure within the first 12 months is associated with better BCVA outcome at year 5. • Aim 3: To understand the risk of PCV/CNV development in the fellow eye.

title: Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography in Intra-Operative Assessment of Tumor Margins for Breast-Conserving Surgery
abs: Breast-conserving surgery(BCS) is performed for patients with localized/early breast malignancy. Current care for evaluating margins intraoperatively (e.g. frozen sections, clinical inspection or ultrasound/mammography) are inadequate and suffer from long-waiting time, interoperator variability and poor spatial resolution respectively. These result in high positive margin rates, resulting a need of second re-operation for patients. With re-operation rates of 20-70%, there is an unmet clinical need for an accurate and rapid intra-operative tool for margin assessment. Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography (MSOT) is an innovative optical imaging modality which works on the principle of “photoacoustic effect”. This hybrid technique of detecting sound waves from optical/light energy generates high resolution ultrasound-optical images with sufficient penetration. MSOT is able to provide biochemical information due to different light energy absorption rates for different tissues. With these advantages, it is hypothesized that MSOT can differentiate breast cancers (fat-replacing) from normal breast tissue (fat-containing). While MSOT has demonstrated good results in several in-vivo breast imaging studies, there is scarce literature to support its use in ex-vivo intra-operative tumor margin assessment. Currently, there is also no prototype/platform available for intra-operative imaging. Our study aims to construct a novel 360-degree full-view probe for intra-operative imaging and recruit breast cancer patients who are undergoing BCS. MSOT would be performed on excised breast tissue. The margin assessment results will be compared to histology in an agreement format with kappa values calculated. The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value will also be calculated. Accurate and rapid intraoperative evaluation of surgical margins would result in reduction of re-operation rates and its associated morbidity. Reduction in local recurrence rates will also reduce overall morbidity and mortality for breast cancer patients. Lastly, a reliable intra-operative tool will allow surgeons to opt for more conservative approach during surgery, leading to improved patient satisfaction and cosmetic outcomes.

title: Singapore lymphoma translational study (SYMPHONY)
abs: The proposed programme is a renewal of our NMRC-funded TCR program on peripheral T-cell (PTCL) and NK/T cell lymphomas (NKTL), which are more common in Asia. To date, therapeutic interventions are of limited efficacy and there remains a pressing need to improve diagnosis, therapy and patient selection. The current TCR has elucidated part of the underlying complexity of this disease. Identification of mutations in JAK/STAT pathway, epigenetic regulators and structural variations in the PD-L1 gene resulting in immune evasion, amongst others, pave the way towards a biology-driven strategy. Theme 1 builds on our findings that suggest immune checkpoint inhibition to be a major turning point in NKTL treatment and aims to identify next-generation biomarkers of response and resistance. In addition, strategies to enhance antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity of anti-CD38-directed therapy with Daratumumab will be explored. Theme 2 aims to develop novel, next generation hetero-tetrameric IgG bi-specific antibody (BsAb) constructs with broad applications for lymphoma therapy. In Theme 3, we aim to (i) target previously elucidated genetic mutations and the relevant driver oncogenic pathways using novel JAK-STAT inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, EZH2 inhibitors and HDAC inhibitors and (ii) identify rational combinations to overcome resistance. Theme 4 will develop more effective and cost-efficient diagnostic platforms and optimize drug therapies through computational genomics and integrative machine learning algorithm research. Through these 4 intercalated themes, we aim to translate and build on the progress we have made in addressing unmet clinical needs of T-cell lymphoma. The expertise and infrastructure we have built will allow us to investigate key strategic areas in B-cell lymphoma research where we may be internationally competitive.

title: Intra-gastric fundal and body injection of Botulinum Toxin A for weight loss, a Randomized Controlled Trial
abs: Worldwide obesity and diabetes has nearly tripled since 1975. Only 0.5% or less of the eligible population are undergoing bariatric surgery, and the most common reason for not undergoing surgery is the fear. Each kilogram of sustained body weight loss associated with a 16% relative reduction in diabetes risk and a 15% reduction in all-cause mortality. The fundus plays a role in the regulation of gastric capacity and hormone secretion. Our hypothesis is that intra-gastric injection of Botox into the fundus and body of the stomach may result in weight loss. This trial will be the first to investigate the effect of intra-gastric Botox injection on the fundus and body, with the longest follow-up. This trial will also be the first to characterize satiety/obesity hormone levels after intra-gastric fundus and body injections. The safety profile of Botox is excellent, with the only gastro-oesophageal reflux symptoms reported in previous studies. We plan a randomized study with 2 arms: 1) a treatment arm where patients will receive 300units of Botulinum Toxin A followed by lifestyle modification, 2) control arm where patients will ergo lifestyle modification only. We aim to recruit 9 patients in each arm. The injections will be performed in a concentric ring into the body and fundus of the stomach. Post-gastroscopy, patients will undergo a 12-week multi-disciplinary weight management programme. Outcome measures include body weight, body mass index, fat mass, blood pressure and lipid levels, food intake and satiety levels, Ghrelin and leptin levels, and fasting blood glucose/HbA1c/Insulin if patient is diabetic. While intra-gastric Botox injection it may play a role in patients in whom bariatric surgery is indicated but refuse to undergo surgery, in obese patients who do not meet the criteria for bariatric surgery and have failed other methods of weight loss, or as a bridge to surgery.

title: Preventing limb losses in Singapore through health literacy and healthcare improvements
abs: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are the leading cause of amputations and mortality among patients with diabetes. Worryingly, Singaporean statistics indicate a faster rate of ulcer deterioration and higher rates of amputations compared to most other countries. The current applied care model in Singapore is acute-centric and does not sufficiently consider strategies for prevention and self-care. The aim is to support more efficient prevention and management of DFUs and thereby reduce the number of DFUs and its progression to limb loss. The hypothesis is that this can be achieved through:òEvidence-based prevention;òBetter care co-ordination;òImproved understanding about the gaps in the provision and deviations from care guidelines; andòEnhanced self-care of people with DFUs or at risk of developing a DFU through an app-based educational program targeting patients, informal caregivers and foreign domestic workers The work by the national Diabetes Prevention and Care Taskforce to fight diabetes will be complemented by focusing on the prevention and management of DFUs. Current everyday care related to DFUs will be investigated to outline treatment pathways and identify possible gaps in the provision of care. Additionally, patients, informal caregivers and foreign domestic workers will be surveyed on their knowledge on preventing and caring for DFU and current care provision and monitoring.An app will be developed and evaluated supporting evidence-based practice through eLearning for the prevention and caring of DFUs directed towards patients, informal caregivers and foreign domestic workers. Health economic modelling will demonstrate potential gains through better healthcare coordination, evidence based prevention and more advanced self-care.Taken together, the proposed research activities will help to maximize the potential of available resources for preventing and caring of DFUs in Singapore, enable earlier identification of patients prone to develop microvascular complications, decrease the number of complications, and demonstrate savings in costs and improvements in quality-of-life.

title: "Long-term clinical outcomes, cost-of-care, clinical characteristics, re-admission rates, outpatient care and mortality in patients with coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure or atrial fibrillation in Singapore  (""SingCLOUD"" for Singapore Cardiac Longitudinal OUtcomes Database Study)"
abs: SingCLOUD was formed in 2013 for large-scale cardiac analyses of clinical and administrative data across all public health institutions (PHIs). It examines cost-of-care, clinical outcomes and measures of quality-of-care to help shape national policy making for patients with either proven or suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), congestive heart failure (CHF) and/or atrial fibrillation (AF). It uses the Business Research and Analytics Insights Network (BRAIN) platform - a federated data grid conceptualised by MOH and IMDA, which extracts, harmonizes, and integrates data across all PHIs.SingCLOUD uses BRAIN to federate data from six independent databases covering thirteen subject areas and a total of 7,057 data fields. In April 2015, data extraction for the SingCLOUD Pilot study was completed, and initial analysis completed in November 2017. This examined outcomes from index patients admitted to two hospitals, with outcomes tracked across the whole country, from 2007 to 2014. The next phase of the project is to extend the entire program for index patients across all hospitals and admissions beyond 2014 to 2016, and to include patients with AF, in addition to the current CAD and CHF cohorts. The aims of this proposal are to (1) establish one-year clinical outcomes, cost-of-care and quality-of-care in patients with CAD, CHF or AF, admitted to all public hospitals; and (2) study the association between adherence to guideline-recommended therapy and outcomes (including cost-of-care). To do so, this proposal will support the current IT infrastructure for SingCLOUD and extend the current analytics capability of SingCLOUD to SingCLOUD 2.0.

title: Role of Primary Care Networks in Diabetes Care Delivery in Singapore
abs: By 2050, 1 million Singaporeans will develop diabetes mellitus with cost burden of $1.8 billion. Existing care models will soon be inadequate to address the care needs. General practitioners (GPs) form 82% of primary care manpower but manage only 60% of patients with chronic diseases resulting in overcrowding in the public polyclinics. In 2018, a novel Primary Care Networks (PCN) model in Singapore was established and funded by the Ministry of Health to enable GPs to work with nurses and care coordinators to provide team-based care for people with diabetes as aligned to Wagner’s Chronic Care Model. Using mixed methods, this research proposal aims to understand the perspectives of PCN GPs, nurses, care coordinators, policy makers, PCN administrative and clinical leaders, cluster polyclinics leaders; and patients with diabetes on delivering, planning or receiving diabetes care in the PCNs. Participants will be recruited for focus group discussions and one-to-one in-depth interviews by the research team. Demographics will also be collected. This knowledge will allow us to better understand the care needs and goals of patients with diabetes, barriers and facilitators in PCN implementation, stakeholders’ roles, responsibilities, future plans for PCNs and their perspectives to see whether CCM elements exist in the PCNs. Case study methodology will be used to elicit key variations in the organizational structures and practice of selected PCNs. We will examine the diabetes quality outcome and process indicators delivered by PCNs in a cross-sectional study and benchmark with national and polyclinics’ data. Our research hypothesis is that those PCNs who perform well in quality indicators have CCM characteristics in their organizational structures, practice and stakeholders’ perspectives. The study findings can be used to develop an enhanced PCN model to help improve diabetes outcomes for people in Singapore and influence how policymakers plan for future support for the PCNs. title: Understanding and targeting Wnt signaling
abs: Wnt signaling is required for normal development, self-renewal of adult tissues, and is dysregulated in many diseases. Over the course of the previous STAR awards, my lab has contributed to our understanding of Wnt biology and pathophysiology. In collaboration with A*STAR Experimental Therapeutics Centre we developed ETC-159, a highly effective inhibitor of PORCN, that blocks Wnt secretion. ETC-159, now in clinical trials, has great potential to treat Wnt-addicted cancers. It also provides a powerful tool to gain new understanding of Wnt biology. Here we propose to build on our prior work on Wnt secretion and Wnt signaling. We will better define which patients might benefit clinically from PORCN inhibitors by studying the role of RNF43 mutations in human cancers. In the last grant period we characterized how pairs of Wnts could work together via Wnt synergy. Here we will exploit new findings that provide novel insights into downstream mechanisms and novel Wnt receptors involved in this Wnt synergy. Our studies of Wnt secretion revealed that essential Wnts in the gut come from intestinal stromal rather than epithelial cells; here we extend those studies to characterize these Wnt-producing cells in normal tissues and in cancer. Finally, we have carefully assessed the consequences of PORCN inhibition in normal and cancer cells in vivo. One key finding is the unexpected result that Wnt signaling represses differentiation signals in both normal and malignant tissues. Better understanding of the underlying mechanism of this process has the potential to provide key insights into how Wnt signaling controls the balance between proliferation and differentiation. This current proposal builds on the collaborations and tools generated over the past grant period to translate new knowledge on Wnt secretion into therapeutic advances.
kw: Wnt; cancer, β-catenin; drug therapy; intestine; signalling

title: Targeting innate immune sensors to develop novel immune-modulatory therapeutics
abs: Innate immune sensor proteins are at the apex of human immunity. They survey the cellular environment for potential pathogens, maintain the symbiosis with commensal microbiome and guards against incipient tumors. Upon detecting pathogen-derived ligands, they rapidly activate the appropriate immune response to fight infection. On the other hand, some sensors can detect signals from the commensal microbiome to inhibit inflammation and prevent auto-immunity. Hence, innate immune sensors function as ‘ON/OFF’ switches of immune response. They play a prominent role in human diseases involving disrupted immune homeostasis, such as obesity, metabolic disorders and cancer, which together represent a large healthcare burden in Singapore and globally. In this proposal, we leverage our existing expertise in innate immune regulation to present a detailed plan to study innate immune sensors, and use this knowledge to develop new immune-activating and anti-inflammatory therapeutics. In the first part of this proposal, we build upon our recent unpublished discovery of a novel, unusual immune sensor known as DPP9 that responds to bacterial tripeptides. We demonstrate that small molecule DPP9 inhibitors can function as pharmacologic activators of anti-cancer immunity in vivo. In the second, we describe a general technology that can identify novel immune sensors for secreted bacterial effectors in a high throughput manner. We will showcase how this technology can be used to identify host sensors that mediate the anti-inflammatory effect of a commensal bacterial species, Akkermansia muciniphila. Taken together, the work described here forms the basis for a comprehensive research platform that can generate novel insight into the fundamental mechanisms of human immunity. It also paves the way to developing new and more effective therapeutics for immune-related diseases and cancer immunotherapy.
kw: Innate immunity, cancer immunity

title: Holistic Management of HDB Flats against Spalling Concrete
abs: This project aims to mitigate concrete deterioration and enhance durability of existing concrete structures through several focus areas i.e. by identifying and detecting concrete cracks/damage, predicting the severity and probability of spalling concrete and applying the suitable prevention and repair strategies.
