title: Electron Microscopy for Catalyst Discovery and Innovation
abs: Sustainability of resources remains one of the greatest challenges in the world. Developing next generations of catalysts, which enable greener routes for energy and material production, is the key to answer that challenge. This proposal seeks to facilitate catalyst innovation by creating a catalyst microscopy program. The program will focus on establishing and applying a novel electron microscopy platform with key capabilities that allow catalyst materials to be studied atom by atom, while they are in their actual working environment. The detailed programme aims to first upgrade the existing aberration-corrected STEM in National University of Singapore (NUS), with the latest direct electron detectors and MEMS-based gas/liquid specimen holders. New microscopy methodologies afforded by the new detectors will allow atomic resolution imaging and analysis with a minimum amount of electron dose. This is critical for revealing unprecedented details on “beam sensitive” but catalytically important structures, such as ultra-small metal clusters, surfaces of oxides and metal-organic frameworks, etc. Local electronic structures of heavier single atoms in catalysts (e.g. Au, Pt, Pd, Ru, etc.) will become accessible in electron spectroscopy for the first time. Several specific catalyst research packages are proposed to study monometallic precious metal catalysts, bi- and multi-metallic catalysts and oxide catalysts, for various industrially important reactions. This program of this kind and the applicant’s interdisciplinary expertise in electron microscopy and catalysis are not yet available to the scientific community in Singapore at present. The proposed microscopy platform will be unique in the world if established today. The catalyst research enabled by the new platform will lead to improved water and air quality in the region and bring a technological edge to the chemical industry in Singapore. The microscopy capabilities can also be of great benefit when applied with other important classes of materials, including batteries, solar cells, semiconductor quantum dots, transistors, light emitting devices, etc. It will help Singapore to strengthen the leading position in energy and environmental related technologies.
kw: Electron microscopy; Heterogeneous catalysis; Sustainability;

title: Reducing the harm of mechanical ventilation by using dialysis to remove carbon dioxide in the form of bicarbonate
abs: Each year, mechanical ventilation is provided to approximately 20 million intensive care patients across the globe. Although life-saving, mechanical ventilation causes lung injury that may develop into the acute respiratory distress syndrome, which affects more than 20% of ventilated intensive care unit (ICU) patients. Low tidal volume ventilation reduces lung injury, but often leads to harmful carbon dioxide (CO2) accumulation. Today, CO2 can only be removed directly from blood using extracorporeal CO2 removal (ECCO2R) devices, which are complex, expensive, require placement of large bore catheters, and are not widely available. Therefore, there is an unmet need for simple, minimally invasive CO2 removal which is widely available. In contrast to ECCO2R, dialysis equipment is found in most ICUs. Supported by NMRC-TA funding, we have developed a low bicarbonate dialysate that removes CO2 in the form of bicarbonate, and have shown that this dialysate lowers arterial CO2 levels in a hypo-ventilated porcine model. However, our prototype dialysate exposed recipients to a high dialysis dose. This was because our dialysate still contained some bicarbonate to ensure it had a biocompatible pH, preventing maximisation of the dialysis gradient. In work funded by a NHIC Joint Medtech grant, we created a large nanoparticle that can control dialysate pH and doesn’t cross the dialysis membrane, allowing us to create a novel dialysate containing no bicarbonate. In this proposal, we aim to test the hypothesis that our novel dialysate will remove >90 ml/min of CO2 without exceeding a conventional dialysis dose. We will test this in a large animal model of dialysis. We expect to demonstrate that conventional dialysis systems can be successfully modified to remove clinically important quantities of CO2, essentially bringing ECCO2R to all ICUs capable of providing dialysis.
kw: Extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal; respiratory dialysis; acid-base;strong ion difference

title: Singapore lYMPHoma translatiONal studY (SYMPHONY)
abs: The proposed programme is a renewal of our NMRC-funded TCR program on peripheral T-cell (PTCL) and NK/T cell lymphomas (NKTL), which are more common in Asia. To date, therapeutic interventions are of limited efficacy and there remains a pressing need to improve diagnosis, therapy and patient selection. The current TCR has elucidated part of the underlying complexity of this disease. Identification of mutations in JAK/STAT pathway, epigenetic regulators and structural variations in the PD-L1 gene resulting in immune evasion, amongst others, pave the way towards a biology-driven strategy. Theme 1 builds on our findings that suggest immune checkpoint inhibition to be a major turning point in NKTL treatment and aims to identify next-generation biomarkers of response and resistance. In addition, strategies to enhance antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity of anti-CD38-directed therapy with Daratumumab will be explored. Theme 2 aims to develop novel, next generation hetero-tetrameric IgG bi-specific antibody (BsAb) constructs with broad applications for lymphoma therapy. In Theme 3, we aim to (i) target previously elucidated genetic mutations and the relevant driver oncogenic pathways using novel JAK-STAT inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, EZH2 inhibitors and HDAC inhibitors and (ii) identify rational combinations to overcome resistance. Theme 4 will develop more effective and cost-efficient diagnostic platforms and optimize drug therapies through computational genomics and integrative machine learning algorithm research. Through these 4 intercalated themes, we aim to translate and build on the progress we have made in addressing unmet clinical needs of T-cell lymphoma. The expertise and infrastructure we have built will allow us to investigate key strategic areas in B-cell lymphoma research where we may be internationally competitive.
kw: Non Hodgkin Lymphoma; Immune Checkpoint; Targeted Therapy; Biomarkers; Artificial Intelligence

title: Early Detection and Novel Treatment Through Epigenomic Studies in Endemic Asian Cancers
abs: It is well-known that Asian-prevalent cancers are often associated with a pathogen or carcinogen. For example, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is associated with Hepatitis B and C viruses, gastric cancer Helicobacter pylori, and nasopharyngeal cancer Epstein-Barr virus. Increasingly, more and more studies are pointing towards epigenomic changes that are associated with chronic carcinogenic exposures – these causative changes may be manipulated not only for diagnostic detection but also for therapeutic intervention using emerging epigenetic drugs. For scientific studies, we propose to study the underlying epigenomic changes related to chronic exposure to their respective carcinogen – liver fluke (Opisthorchis viveriini) for biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma) and aristolochic acid for hepatobiliary cancer. More specifically we will profile and study DNA and histone modifications as well as RNA-seq (expression) in these cancers and carcinogen exposure in model systems, on both the bulk and single cell level. For translation studies in biomarker development, we will focus on DNA hydroxy-methylation and methylation, non-coding RNA (e.g. miRNA, lncRNA) all of which can be further validated in a very large number of liquid samples like plasma and urine. These biomarkers will have potential for both early detection screening and disease monitoring. For translation studies into novel drug development, we will particularly pay attention to epigenetic targets and epigenetic drugs. These findings, coupled with further molecular, biochemical, proteomic, in vitro and in vivo studies will hopefully shed light on how chronic exposures of these agents contribute to epigenomic changes and subsequently tumorigenesis. Our studies will also allow us to explore the accumulative strength of combining epigenetic drugs and other forms of treatment modalities. Through these studies, we will take our research to a greater height, from making new breakthroughs to translating research findings to clinical applications, and preventing or reducing the cancer risks in different populations.
kw: Cancer; Carcinogen; Epigenomic; Tumorigenesis; Biomarkers; Therapy

title: Targeted Cell-Based Therapeutic Program for Corneal Blindness
abs: Visual loss is a global burden. Corneal diseases are the leading cause of vision loss. Whilst the only treatment option is the replacement of damaged corneas through transplantation using cadaveric donor corneas, the global shortage of donor tissue and its sustainability amidst a growing aging population is of utmost concern. Our aim is to develop innovative strategies to treat corneal stromal opacities and corneal endothelial dysfunction. This program will establish targeted cell-based therapy to restore corneal tissue functions and corneal clarity, ultimately aimed at vision recovery. Success of this program will be a paradigm shift to the conventional corneal transplantation. There are two broad themes. (1)Regenerative therapeutic program for corneal stromal opacities using cultivated corneal stromal keratocytes (first successfully cultivated by PI’s team), umbilical cord lining mesenchymal stem cells (UCL-MSC) generated in compliance to good manufacturing practice by an industrial collaborator and MSC exosomes on animal models of corneal stromal haze/opacities. (2)Corneal endothelial cell (CEC) therapy for corneal endothelial dysfunction using cells on bioactive hydrogel as a scaffold carrier for tissue-engineered endothelial keratoplasty, cells cultivated with FDA-approved Rho-kinase inhibitor, Rhopressa, to improve cell quality and regenerated CEC from putative endothelial progenitors identified in transition zone of posterior limbus, for treating bullous keratopathy in a rabbit model, respectively. Experimental outcomes will be instrumental to translate into novel therapeutic approach for corneal diseases and we expect the deliverables to broadly impact on the global shortage of donor tissue in Singapore and worldwide. Our long-term goal is to develop Translational Regenerative Medicine to treat corneal blindness, which can attract multi-disciplinary, entrepreneurial, bio-manufacturing and academic platforms for the benefit of disease treatment and management.

title:
S.P.A.R.T.A.N trial
Sarcopenia Prevention And Reversal with physical Training And Nutrition in distal radius fracture patients
abs: Sarcopenia is a newly recognised triad of poor physical function, muscle strength and muscle mass resulting in poor quality of life, falls, hospitalisations, disability, and mortality. Singapore’s geriatric population will grow to 1.7 million in 2030and sarcopenia will adversely affect the quality of life of up to 860,000 Singaporeans and add significant burden on our healthcare system and costs. Longitudinal studies on pathology, etiology and intervention in the asian populations are lacking. This study primary aim is to determine if exercise and nutrition interventions can reverse or prevent sarcopenia by improving Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) and patient reported quality of life scores in an enriched cohort of distal radius fracture (DRF) patients. Its secondary aims are to study the risk factors, incidence and economic impact of sarcopenia. This study’s long-term goal is to guide screening, education and intervention of sarcopenia with widespread public implementation. Primary hypothesis: Nutrition and exercise intervention can reverse and prevent sarcopenia in the DRF patient by improving SPPB and quality of life scores. Secondary hypothesis: Wrist fracture is a predictor of preexisting or developing sarcopenia This is a single blinded randomized control trial recruiting newly diagnosed DRF patients above the age of 50 in TTSH. The interventional arm will consist of nutritional evaluation, dietary prescription and physiotherapist taught resistance training regime. Data on demographics, functionality, frailty, co-morbidities and objective muscular, adipose, bony and biochemical markers will be collected during study period. The results of this study will enable us to implement public and community measures to combat the incidence of sarcopenia, therefore affecting the following factors: 1. Increase quality of life 2. Decrease number of hospitalizations, falls, loss of function/independence, need for long term carer or placement 3. Decrease healthcare expenditure by patient (Consultations, treatment, hospitalisation, carer) and by government (Long term placement, disability)
kw: Sarcopenia, Performance, Quality of Life

title: A pilot study of postprandial intestinal perfusion in premature infant and its role in feeding intolerance and necrotizing enterocolitis.
abs: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a major cause of mortality in premature infants, especially in those with very low birth weight (VLBW). It generally occurs after reaching full-volume feeding, but the underlying mechanism is not clear. Our recent animal study suggests that premature gut has an insufficient postprandial splanchnic hyperemia (PSH) which is unable to meet the increased oxygen demand after feeding, leading intestinal hypoxia and NEC. However, this theory is yet proven in human. Objectives: we aim to determine: 1. Whether the prematurity is associated with insufficient PSH. 2. Whether the insufficient PSH is associated with bowel hypoxia after feeding. 3. Whether infant with insufficient PSH tend to develop feeding intolerance and NEC. Methods: 40 infants with gestation age from 25 to 40 weeks will be recruited to test for intestinal perfusion by ultrasound Doppler, and bowel oxygenation by near-infrared spectrometer (NIRS) before and after first, half and full volume of feeding. The data will be correlated with patient’s clinical profile of feeding intolerance and incidence of NEC. This study will reveal the role PSH in the feeding-induced hypoxia in premature gut, and provide the preliminary data on the association of PSH with feeding intolerance and NEC. If such association was proven in future large-scale study, we would develop a novel method to predict high-risk infant using ultrasound and NIRS, and a new feeding strategy to prevent NEC /feeding intolerance by adjusting feeding regime based on the capacity of intestinal blood supply.
kw: Necrotizing enterocolitis; feeding intolerance; postprandial hyperemia; premature; NIRS; Ultrasound

title: Extending Health Span through Diabetes Health Literacy and Competency Assessment (HeaLiX health bot)
abs: Life-long patient education and empowerment are key strategies for the successful management of diabetes, recommended by evidence-based clinical guidelines. Currently, diabetes education is provided 1-on-1 or in small groups which are resource intensive and costly. Scheduled education sessions while valued, lack immediacy, timeliness, and flexibility of access. In Singapore, 36% of diabetes patients claim they did not receive diabetes education; and its effectiveness remains questionable. Local studies reported similar rates of general diabetes literacy between people with and without diabetes, raising concerns about patient competency in managing diabetes. Notably, 42% of patients with diabetes had knowledge that did not translate into self-care practices. A better way to provide effective diabetes education is needed. In light of financial and health workforce constraints, two strategies fit Singapore. First, given 100% smartphone ownership and mobile broadband subscription penetration, patient-facing technology such chat bots can be blended with usual care to augment our health workforce and to engage patients. Chat bots are currently used in healthcare for appointment-booking and information provision; and over 70% of consumers are willing to use it for learning about their health condition e.g. diabetes. Second, there are 246,800 domestic carers in Singapore — a significant resource. We hypothesize that carers of seniors with diabetes could be upskilled with diabetes health literacy and competencies via a health bot, to provide better care in line with Singapore’s Home and Community Care Masterplan. We will design, develop and implement a health bot to deliver state-of-the-art diabetes education to carers/patients to improve diabetes health literacy and competency by 80%, and to effect desired behaviour change for 80% of patients, resulting in better health outcomes. As a health intervention for carers/seniors with diabetes the health bot is scalable and low-cost. The future of healthcare is blended care — patients, healthcare professionals, and digital health, working together.
kw: Diabetes; Health literacy; Patient education; Competency; Behaviour change; Health bot

title:
EMPOWERing patients with chronic disease 
using profiling and targeted feedbacks delivered through wearable device (EMPOWER)
abs: Chronic diseases are the leading cause of deaths in Singapore. The rising prevalence in chronic diseases with age and Singapore’s rapidly aging population calls for new models of care to effectively prevent the onset and delay the progression of these diseases. Advancement in medical technology has offered new innovations that aid healthcare systems in coping with the rapid rising in healthcare needs. These include mobile applications, wearable technologies and machine learning-derived personalized behavorial interventions. Our overall goal is to improve health outcomes in chronic disease patients through delivering targeted nudges via mobile application and wearables to sustain behavioral change. Our objective is to design, develop and evaluate an adaptive interventional platform that is capable of delivering personalized behavioral nudges to promote and sustain healthy behavioral changes in senior patients with 3H (diabetes (hyperglycemia), hypertension and hyperlipidemia). Our aim is to assess the clinical effectiveness of real-time personalized educational and behavioral interventions delivered through wearable (FitBit) and an in-integrative mobile application in improving patient activation scores measured using the patient activation measure (PAM). Secondary outcome measures include cost-effectiveness, quality of life, medication adherence, healthcare cost, utilization and lab results. Together with the experts from the SingHealth Regional Health System and National University of Singapore, we will conduct a randomized controlled trial of 1,250 eligible 3H patients. This proposal aims to achieve sustainable and cost-effective behavioral change in 3H patients through patient-empowerment and targeted chronic disease care.
kw: Behavioural nudges; elderly; population health; machine learning; behavioural sciences

title: Defining the gene-environment interactions between the normal PNPLA3 or I148M variant and diet in producing liver and adipose tissue pathology in DIAMOND mice humanized with PNPLA3
abs: Background: PNPLA3 appears to be associated with NASH and progression of disease severity. However, the mechanisms remain unclear and need to be clarified. There is a paucity of data on the role of macronutrients in NASH. It is not known how dietary macronutrients interact with PNPLA3 in the development and progression of NASH. Aim: (i) To define whether the effect of PNPLA3 variants on development and progression of NASH is contingent on specific dietary macronutrients and (ii) To gain insights on the mechanisms involved in the development of the liver phenotypes associated with the PNPLA3 variants under different dietary conditions. Hypothesis: Hepatic expression of both PNPLA3 variants promote NASH under high fat-sugar enriched diet. The I148M variant further accelerates NASH and progression of fibrosis. Methods: DIAMOND mice will be randomized to liver-specific delivery of AAV-luciferase (AAV-luc) (controls), AAV-wild type or AAV-I148M PNPLA3 and then randomizing mice in each group again to receive chow diet, high-fat diet, sugar-enriched diet or a high fat-sugar enriched diet (Western diet). Mice will be followed to 8, 12, 20 or 36 weeks to determine if development of NASH, fibrosis and HCC are accelerated by either wild type or mutant PNPLA3. Assessment of specific pathways known to be associated with NASH development as well as an unbiased approach using lipidomic and transcriptomic data will be used to obtain inferences on how PNPLA3 interacts with diet to produce NASH. Rationale: The study will provide insights on which dietary macro-nutrients are most relevant for the development of liver disease in those with I148M variant- as well as wild type-PNPLA3 associated NASH. These are expected to inform future clinical guidance on dietary recommendations for NASH associated with specific PNPLA3 variants. Data outputs can also be used to identify novel PNPLA3-related therapeutic targets.
kw: NASH; fatty liver; PNPLA3; diet

title: Evaluating the effects of autologous protein solution using a mechanical model of primary osteoarthritis in rats
abs: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a global health issue. Of all the major joints in the body, the knee is the most commonly affected and contributes to significant economic and health burden in our country and worldwide. OA can be primary, with no identifiable cause or secondary, where the onset of OA is a direct result of a known injury. Primary OA is by far more common and is diagnosed in the absence of predisposing trauma or disease. As a final common pathway, OA develops from a vicious cycle of inflammation, driven by key inflammatory factors. These factors cause degradation of articular cartilage by stimulating production of enzymes that breakdown cartilage matrix. This promotes a positive feedback loop where more inflammatory factors are produced. This ultimately results in progressive cartilage degradation, causing advanced OA. There has been recent interest in biologic treatments for OA. These involve intra-articular (IA) administration of anti-inflammatory factors to break the cascade described above. One such treatment modality is autologous protein solution (APS). APS is prepared from a patient’s own blood and contains concentrated anti-inflammatory proteins. These proteins disrupt the vicious cycle of articular cartilage degradation. A recent preclinical study reported that treatment with a single IA injection of APS reduced cartilage degeneration in a medial meniscus tear (MMT) rat model of OA. However, the MMT rat model is a secondary OA model. Moreover, the intra-articular surgery to induce a MMT can incite additional, unwanted inflammatory processes and as such is not a suitable model to study the effects of an anti-inflammatory therapeutic product. There is a novel mechanical model of primary OA that has been created and validated recently. In this model, an extra-articular tibial osteotomy (TO) is used to create a varus mechanical axis which then causes medial joint overloading and OA development in rats. A TO, being an extra-articular procedure, avoids the unwanted effects of intra-articular inflammation that is seen in the other animal models such as the MMT or anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) model. For a MMT or ACLT model, the knee joint itself is violated to create the intra-articular injury and hence induces synovial inflammation. In the mechanical model, this is avoided. This could be a more accurate model for primary OA. To date, no animal studies have been performed to evaluate the effects of APS in a primary OA model induced by an extra-articular TO. Therefore, I hypothesize that treatment with a single IA injection of APS utilizing the above-mentioned primary OA model in rats will inhibit the progression of OA. I aim to evaluate the effects of APS using a mechanical model of primary OA in rats.

title: SarcoPenia Advanced detection and Remedy To Avoid New fractures
abs: Sarcopenia is a newly recognised triad of poor physical function, muscle strength and muscle mass resulting in poor quality of life, falls, hospitalisations, disability, and mortality. Recent European and Asian working groups on Sarcopenia defined it as low muscle strength together with low muscle mass and/or function. With Singapore’s geriatric population estimated to grow to 1.7 million in 2030, and with 20-50% of geriatric population being sarcopenic, this will adversely affect the quality of life of up to 860,000 Singaporeans and add significant burden on our healthcare system and costs. The distal radius fracture is an important timepoint for the screening and treatment of osteoporosis. Although this sentinel event is also associated with high incidence and prevalence of sarcopenia, it is neither screened nor treated. Literature has shown that in elderly patients, resistance exercise is an effective way to prevent muscle loss (38-40) and to improve muscle strength and gait (41-46), whereas nutritional intervention was observed to be a contributing factor(47-49). The SPARTAN trial is therefore a proof-of-concept study to determine the effectiveness of early intervention of sarcopenia in patients presenting with a recent sentinel distal radius fracture. Specifically, we aim to determine the effectiveness of a tailored resistance exercise and nutritional program compared with exercise alone or standard care in improving the primary outcomes of SPPB and FES-I, and secondary outcomes of muscle parameters, patient-related outcomes, clinical outcomes, cost savings, and inflammatory blood biomarkers. The results of our study thus have the potential for translation into a novel and viable standard of care to improve outcomes in the orthogeriatric population through early detection and treatment of sarcopenia in sentinel distal radius fracture patients. This study’s long-term goal is to guide screening, education and intervention of sarcopenia with widespread public implementation. This is in line with the Ministry of Health’s vision, from Healthcare to Health, where our vision is to ensure not only the quantity, but also the quality of life for our citizens of the future.

title: The Singapore lYMPHoma translatiONal studY (SYMPHONY)
abs: The proposed programme is a renewal of our NMRC-funded TCR program on peripheral T-cell (PTCL) and NK/T cell lymphomas (NKTL), which are more common in Asia. To date, therapeutic interventions are of limited efficacy and there remains a pressing need to improve diagnosis, therapy and patient selection. The current TCR has elucidated part of the underlying complexity of this disease. Identification of mutations in JAK/STAT pathway, epigenetic regulators and structural variations in the PD-L1 gene resulting in immune evasion, amongst others, pave the way towards a biology-driven strategy. Theme 1 builds on our findings that suggest immune checkpoint inhibition to be a major turning point in NKTL treatment and aims to identify next-generation biomarkers of response and resistance. In addition, strategies to enhance antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity of anti-CD38-directed therapy with Daratumumab will be explored. Theme 2 aims to develop novel, next generation hetero-tetrameric IgG bi-specific antibody (BsAb) constructs with broad applications for lymphoma therapy. In Theme 3, we aim to (i) target previously elucidated genetic mutations and the relevant driver oncogenic pathways using novel JAK-STAT inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, EZH2 inhibitors and HDAC inhibitors and (ii) identify rational combinations to overcome resistance. Theme 4 will develop more effective and cost-efficient diagnostic platforms and optimize drug therapies through computational genomics and integrative machine learning algorithm research. Through these 4 intercalated themes, we aim to translate and build on the progress we have made in addressing unmet clinical needs of T-cell lymphoma. The expertise and infrastructure we have built will allow us to investigate key strategic areas in B-cell lymphoma research where we may be internationally competitive.

title: Probing the Immunometabolic Factors of Influenza Vaccine Immune Response in Singapore Elderly
abs: Novel, effective influenza vaccination strategies are needed in the elderly who have the highest rate of influenza-related morbidity and mortality. Unfortunately, vaccine effectiveness in this segment of the population is greatly reduced due to immunosenescence and/or, inflamm-aging. The escalating incidence of metabolic syndrome, diabetes mellitus are factors that potentially contribute to immune dys-regulation, and we hypothesise vaccine response may be associated with key metabolic parameters. The increased severity of influenza in the elderly, decreased influenza vaccine performance and prevention of severe influenza in these populations are important knowledge gaps that need to be addressed. The DYNAMIC trial (funded by NHG CSCS) has just recruited a cohort of 220 community dwelling elderly with the aim to evaluate metabolic predictors (specifically diabetes mellitus and 25-OH D) of influenza-vaccine humoral immune response, as measured by haemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titer. Baseline and Day 28 post-vaccination serum and peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples are available for this multi-ethnic cohort. All study participants have received trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3). Data on subjects’ food history and physical activity habits are available. Our novel approach in the current proposal is to probe the various immunometabolic factors (including clinical metabolic phenotype) associated with collective cellular and humoral influenza vaccine-immune response. Assays will be performed on stored samples. These include metabolic markers (leptin, adiponectin), and pro-inflammatory cytokines at baseline. We will also determine associations between leptin-related gene and VDR (vitamin D receptor) gene variants with immune response as an exploratory aim in Chinese elderly, and validate in another comparable local cohort. This study has several translational applications, including developing targeted vaccine strategies such as using differing dose of vaccine, adjuvants in vaccine non-responders to improve vaccine immunogenicity and prevention of influenza-related complications in these populations.

title: DYNAMO: Diabetes studY on Nephropathy and other Microvascular cOmplications
abs: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a devastating complication of diabetes causing significant morbidity, mortality and human suffering. In Singapore, the incidence of DN as a cause of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) is among the highest in the world. Despite the substantial public health burden associated with DN, its molecular pathogenesis is poorly understood and no new drugs for DN have been introduced in nearly 20 years. Within the population of diabetics, only a subset develops DN indicating a strong familial contribution to this risk. Nonetheless, identification of genetic variants controlling DN susceptibility has been difficult. Furthermore, no reliable biomarkers exist to stratify high-risk patients before the onset of clinically apparent diabetic kidney disease. Capitalizing on a confluence of world-class expertise in research on diabetes and its complications in Singapore, the Diabetes studY of Nephropathy And other Microvascular cOmplications (DYNAMO) plans to employ multiple experimental approaches to identify new mechanistic pathways in DN, discover and validate new targets for DN treatment, and define novel biomarkers and strategies to stratify DN risk within the T2D population. These approaches include human genetics, targeted and non-targeted metabolomics, animal modeling, and urinary exosomes studies. DYNAMO also takes advantage of several established, well-characterized Singaporean patient cohorts, consisting of nearly 30,000 individuals with stored serum, genetic samples, urine, and retinal photographs for analyses. When sample sizes are limited, DYNAMO has assembled an international collaborative network to allow for the integration of data with the largest human genetics studies ongoing in the world. The strategic focus of our LCG incorporates cutting edge technologies to take a systems biology approach to target and biomarker discovery and validation. The work is based on world class science, substantial track record and prior work of the participating investigators, and a clear focus on unmet needs for DN in Singapore and globally.

title: Scalable Interventions to Cultivate Strategically Self-Regulated Learners
abs: Effective learning goes beyond acquiring content knowledge. It also involves the metacognitive process of thinking about one’s learning—exercising self-awareness, planning, actively monitoring one’s learning approaches, and taking control of the learning process. These are “21st century skills” identified by the Singapore Ministry of Education as key educational outcomes. Exercising metacognition during learning engages the regulatory system of the brain, which involves the prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex, and it is related to higher levels of motivation, learning, and academic performance. My research programme focuses on understanding and intervening to improve the metacognitive process of how learners regulate the resources available to them to learn effectively. This is especially important to study because millions of dollars are spent by governments worldwide on providing learners with greater quantities of higher-quality learning resources. However, our science cannot adequately explain how learners manage and use the various learning resources provided for them to learn—or how effectively or ineffectively they are doing so. I propose to, first, conduct large-scale surveys of Secondary School and Junior College students in Singapore to investigate how and to what extent learners at these education levels are naturally practising resource regulation (Aim 1). By combining cognitive theories of learning with cutting-edge social psychological intervention methods, I will design scalable psychological interventions that are effective at cultivating strategic resource regulation. I will empirically test these online interventions in Singapore schools using double-blind, randomized, controlled field experiments (Aim 2). Finally, I plan to develop an online platform that will house and deliver my interventions to Singaporean learners and teachers at scale (Aim 3). As a psychological interventionist with firsthand experience of the Singapore education system, situating my research programme in Singapore will enable me to transform the way our people learn at a significant scale.

title: Sea-level and land-level change in Southeast Asia: A geological approach to quantifying hazard from rising seas and earthquakes
abs: Like many places around the world, Singapore faces a threat from sea-level rise; however, local projections for the anticipated amounts and rates of sea-level rise are poorly constrained, owing to a lack of high-quality data from the region. A separate but related problem is the potential earthquake hazard in Singapore: despite the commonly-held belief that Singapore does not have earthquakes, tectonic faults cut across the island, and the earthquake potential of those faults is not known. Both sea-level rise and the possibility of earthquakes and tectonic deformation are hazards that must be assessed and mitigated, and both lead to changes over time in relative sea level (RSL), the difference in elevation between the sea surface and land. For those who aim to address questions of coastal tectonics, sea-level change, or the local isostatic response to the load of glacial meltwater, it is imperative to quantify the contribution of each of those processes to overall RSL change. An insufficient understanding of tectonic deformation can result in under-appreciation of the risk for coastal flooding, and insufficient constraints on RSL can allow us to overlook evidence for past tectonic deformation. Anticipating the future risk from both hazards requires geological observations that spatially and temporally constrain land deformation and sea-level change over thousands of years, and it requires modeling that will allow us to tease apart the signals of the various processes that drive RSL change. Until now, the few studies of RSL change near Singapore have been based on low-precision data and have simply assumed that the region is tectonically stable; none of these studies were capable of testing whether faults near Singapore were active recently. I aim to improve our understanding both of RSL and of tectonic hazards in Southeast Asia foremost by improving the available RSL data. By choosing sites strategically, using high-quality proxy data, and collaborating with modelers, I will address both the sea level and potential earthquake problems facing the Singapore region.
kw: sea-level rise; glacial isostatic adjustment; tectonic deformation; earthquakes; natural hazards; Singapore

title: Artificial Intelligence for Soil Recognition
abs: The overall aim of the project is to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) system to quickly and accurately classify local excavated soil. The AI system is envisioned to (1) increase the accuracy of in-situ local soil classification by truckload at the HDB Staging Grounds from 40% by the current visual inspection process to 90% by AI, and (2) result in manpower savings (approximately 1,800 man-hours annually for HDB Staging Grounds) by eliminating the need for time-consuming and laborious collection and laboratory-testing of soil samples. The technology aims to supports HDB Staging Grounds’ upcycling of surplus excavated soil generated by the construction industry, through increase in productivity and manpower savings at HDB Staging Grounds. By using excavated material instead of sand, this upcycling process has allowed HDB to reclaim land in a more environmentally sustainable manner and reduced Singapore’s reliance on imported sand. The technology aims to have a higher accuracy of in-situ soil classification (target 90% accuracy) than the current practice of visual inspection of each truckload (approximately 40% accuracy). By increasing the accuracy at which each truckload of excavated material is classified into “Good Earth” and “Soft Clay”, the excavated material can then be channelled for appropriate ground improvement and usage at the reclamation site to improve HDB’s land reclamation process. The technology could allow the HDB Staging Grounds to eliminate the need for collecting of soil samples at the construction site (currently requires 1,800 man-hours annually) and for the laboratory testing of the samples (average annual cost of $50,000).
kw: The project is to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) system to quickly and accurately classify local excavated soil.

title: ASTeRISK: Addressing Stroke and TIA Risk - A Management and Prevention Program.
abs: Stroke is a leading cause of serious, long-term disability; the effects of which may be prolonged with physical, emotional, social, and financial consequences not only for those affected. Poor management of risk factors increases the probability of stroke recurrence, and consequently, severity of disability. Thus, a more comprehensive approach to primary and secondary prevention of stroke is required that targets people at all levels of risk and is integrated with prevention strategies for other diseases that share common risk factors (Hankey, 2017). Despite improvements in the treatment of stroke and its risk factors (e.g. hypertension, hyper-lipidemia, ischemic heart disease, etc.) through medical advances, adherence to these measures is low. Psychological sequelae (e.g. depression, anxiety), perception of poor self-efficacy and poor health literacy are barriers to stroke survivors’ management of risk factors (Pearce et al., 2015). Psychosocial and behavioural interventions programs have been demonstrated to be effective in promoting adherence and reducing risk among stroke survivors by addressing psychological distress, encouraging behavioural change by empowering stroke survivors and their caregivers as well as increasing their health knowledge regarding stroke and its risk factors (Barlow et al., 2002; Cheng et al. 2014; Hafsteindottir et al., 2011; McDonald et al., 2002; Michie et al., 2009). This research study will optimise resource allocation with the implementation of a triage protocol to identify and assign stroke survivors to the appropriate intervention program in order to improve adherence to primary and secondary prevention of stroke across all levels of risk. The multi-faceted scalable program addresses the different barriers to adoption and adherence of stroke risk factor management: psychological distress (Heart), low self-efficacy and motivation (Mind) and health knowledge and awareness (Body). To empower self-monitoring and management among stroke survivors and their family caregivers, this study will utilise and refine existing mobile application and web-based health technology.
kw: stroke, risk management, prevention,

title:
A novel multi-species lyophilized powder is safe and effective for use in
oral immunotherapy for prawn allergy
abs: Background: Food allergy has been recognized as the next global allergy epidemic. Oral immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment of food allergy. Although effective in peanut allergy, this approach has not been investigated in prawn allergy. Prawn allergy is highly prevalent in Asia, affecting 5.2-16% of the population and accounts for the majority of emergency room food triggered anaphylaxis events in children>6 years, and is the main cause of fatal food-induced anaphylaxis in Australia. Currently there is no effective treatment for shellfish allergy apart from life-long avoidance. This study aims to establish the efficacy and safety of a novel lyophilized multi-species powder for development of an pioneering oral immunotherapy treatment for prawn allergy. Hypotheses: A novel lyophilized multi-species prawn powder is effective and safe for diagnosis of species-specific prawn allergy, and can be developed for prawn oral immunotherapy. Aims 1. To optimize a lyophilization process that preserves the antigenic profile of Penaeus Monodon/L vannamei, with preservation of major and minor allergens and their allergenicity and immunogenicity 2. To confirm safety from microbial contamination, and evaluate the shelf-life by evaluating stability of allergenic and immunogenic properties 3. To confirm clinical reactivity via oral challenge Methodology : Allergenic profile of lyophilized cooked Penaeus monodon/L vannamei will be determined with SDS-PAGE, and correlated with raw and cooked P monodon/L vannamei. Allergenicity and immunogenicity will be analyzed with ELISA and skin prick tests with sera from known prawn-allergic patients. Stability and safety of lyophilized powder will be assessed with serial plate counts at sequential time periods at a range of temperatures. Invivo reactivity will then be confirmed via oral challenge. Significance : Development of a safe and efficacious standardized product for delivery of prawn protein is important for standardization of oral challenges, and a crucial step before the progression to development of prawn oral immunotherapy.

title: Rapid Triage for Serious Infections in Infants Younger than 3 Months using a Novel Heart Rate Variability Tool
abs: Febrile infants <3 months present a diagnostic dilemma to paediatricians and emergency physicians. Tension remains between the need for early aggressive intervention among patients with suspected sepsis and the global phenomena of increasing antibiotic resistance. Current triage tools are insufficient. A non-invasive triage tool to detect infants at risk of serious infections (SI) would reduce unnecessary investigations and unwarranted interventions. We aim to develop a novel artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool including heart rate variability (HRV), and evaluate its utility in predicting serious infection (SI) among febrile infants aged <3 months in KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) Emergency Department (ED). We hypothesize that HRV provides incremental diagnostic information and a novel triage tool incorporating HRV is superior to current triage tools in discriminating infants with SI from those without. This is a prospective observational study to be conducted in KKH, ED. We will include infants <3 months presenting with a rectal temperature >38oC between Jan 2019 and Dec 2020. SI includes sepsis (including bacteremia), meningitis, lobar pneumonia (confirmed radiologically), osteomyelitis, abscess and urinary tract infection. HRV will be monitored for 5 minutes using a single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). The ECG signal will be extracted and processed to obtain HRV data. Performance indicators are the area under receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, which will be compared between the novel and current existing triage tools. If successful, including HRV information will improve triage precision for febrile infants with SI, allowing resources be focused on the sickest infants.

title: Mild Behavioral Impairment: Structural-Connectivity Patterns and Influence on Cognition in amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) are common in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and are associated with poorer cognitive outcomes. Mild behavioural impairment (MBI) is a diagnostic construct which identifies individuals with persistent late-life NPS (≥6 months) and there is an emerging conceptual framework which support MBI as an early non-cognitive manifestation of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the prevalence of MBI and its pathophysiology and influence on cognition in MCI remains unclear. MBI could potentially be used to identify pre-dementia patients who are at risk for AD. In a cross-sectional cohort, we will study the local prevalence and characteristics of MBI among MCI (amnestic and non-amnestic) patients seen consecutively in our memory clinic over 1-year. All subjects will undergo neuropsychological assessments (NPA) at baseline and 6-month time points for the diagnosis of MBI. In a prospective longitudinal cohort, we will study the pathophysiology of MBI and its influence on cognition over 1-year in only amnestic MCI (aMCI) subjects. 150 aMCI subjects (75 with MBI (aMCI+MBI), 75 without MBI (aMCI-MBI)) with structural and resting-state functional-MRI within a 6-month window will be recruited from 3 ongoing studies. We will enrich this cohort with 40 aMCI subjects with known cerebrospinal fluid amyloid (CSF Aβ1-42). All subjects will undergo NPA at baseline and 1-year follow-up. We hypothesize that MBI is prevalent among MCI subjects locally, aMCI+MBI subjects have greater grey matter atrophy and functional disconnectivity in limbic and AD-related regions and lower CSF Aβ1-42 at baseline and poorer cognitive performances at 1-year follow-up, compared to aMCI-MBI. Our study findings will support MBI as an early manifestation of AD. The characterization of behavioural and cognitive profiles of MBI and its role in determining cognitive decline will enable prompt detection of aMCI+MBI patients and timely targeted cognitive behavioural interventions to improve NPS, quality of life and stabilize cognitive decline.

title: Bio-inspired adhesives for wet environment: Molecular Designs to Applications
abs: A grand challenge in materials science is engineering strong and durable moisture-resistant adhesives, which are of great importance to various industrial and biomedical applications, such as marine and offshore coatings, flexible electronics, and tissue glue. Most synthetic adhesives systems suffer significant deterioration, even complete failure, in moisture and/or wet environments. Marine sandcastle worms and mussels have evolved highly effective adhesive strategies for wet surfaces using protein-based adhesives. The goal of this proposal is to define the fundamental design principles involved in bio-adhesion, achieve translation to synthetic systems, and pioneer a systems approach to wet adhesives that spans nano- to macroscale dimensions. The overall hypothesis of this proposal is that formulating a practical wet adhesive requires the creative translation and combination of three prominent features of marine bioadhesives: (a) polymer functionalities (e.g. Dopa (3,4-dihyhroxyphenyl-L-alanine)) that provide energetic wet surface bonding at the molecular level, (b) dense surface-active polyelectrolyte fluids (coacervates) that remain phase-separated from water, and (c) a triggered solidification process of the coacervate with tunable structure and mechanical strength To validate the hypothesis, this research will combine interfacial chemistry, micromechanics, spectroscopy, electrochemistry, and microfluidics to understand the bio-inspired adhesive systems at multiple length and time scales. The research will generate unprecedented and fundamental insights into designing bio-inspired wet adhesives for a broad range of real-world wet and moisture environments that will lead to: (1) a deeper understanding of adhesion mechanisms of bio-inspired moisture-resistant adhesives at the molecular level, and the development of a novel instrument that enables such investigation; (2) designs, structures, and properties of Dopa containing synthetic coacervate adhesives; and (3) delivery, processing, and testing of marine bio-inspired adhesives. The marine bio-inspired moisture-resistant adhesives developed will be critical to many fields and applications, such as marine and offshore anti-fouling and anti-corrosion coatings, flexible electronics, sensors, coatings for medical implants, tissue and dental/bone glues, as well as skin care products.

title: Robust Statistical Learning Under Model Uncertainty
abs: The recent data deluge has led to advances in machine learning algorithms that are impacting virtually every sector of society. However, these algorithms are invariably faced with challenges of uncertainty: Product recommendation systems must learn from noisy and corrupted data, self-driving cars are faced with unpredictable scenarios that they have never encountered before, large-scale sensor networks must be robust to individual sensor failures, and robotics tasks learned in simulated environments must transfer effectively to the real world, just to name a few examples. When learning algorithms are designed according to mathematical models that only provide a rough approximation of the real world, their performance is prone to deteriorate considerably in practice, possibly even violating critical constraints such as safety and security. In this project, our contention is that this issue of model uncertainty poses one of the most fundamental unresolved practical issues in modern machine learning, and warrants a profound re-thinking of how we extract information from data in a robust manner. In this project, we will address this fundamental challenge via the following inter-related goals: 1) Mathematically characterize the algorithm-independent learning limits dictating the extent to which performance degradation is unavoidable under model uncertainty, and determining when it can be circumvented; 2) Identify the key limitations of existing state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms in the presence of model uncertainty; 3) Develop statistical learning algorithms that are specifically targeted at achieving robustness with respect to model uncertainty, with rigorous guarantees. To achieve these goals, the PI will build on the expertise acquired during his PhD on model uncertainty and mismatch in the field of information theory, as well as his more recent work on large-scale statistical learning problems. This unique background complements Singapore's existing strengths in data science, and puts the PI in a strong position to make high-impact theoretical and algorithmic advances. Model uncertainty is prevalent in virtually all practical learning systems, but currently lacks a detailed understanding. By addressing this crucial issue, this project has the potential to re-shape practical learning methods in extensive applications where machine learning is used, and to help bring Singapore to the forefront of worldwide data science research.
kw: Machine learning; statistical inference; data science; model uncertainty; model mismatch; information theory

title: Cyber Forensics & Assurance R&D Programme
abs: Increasing demand for security and privacy is pushing manufacturers to provide cutting-edge security features in their products. The regular upgrade in the security features of the products pose a serious challenge for law enforcement agencies in the context of crime scene forensics. In this programme, we will explore three aspects of hardware-oriented cyber-forensic methods: (1) rapid recovery of data from damaged devices, (2) methods to overcome anti-forensic methods like data encryption, and (3) hardware assurance evaluation. The work will be based on established hardware security and failure analysis techniques, using powerful methods like fault injection attacks, side-channel attacks, scanning probe microscopy, e-beam probing, etc. The main advantage of the developed techniques is that these will be anchored at hardware level. Unlike software which can have weekly updates that sometimes make forensic methods obsolete instantly, hardware devices have longer lifetime and thus extending the applicability of the hardware techniques developed.

title: Study of Mitochondrial Maladaptation in Metabolic Inflexibility of Heart Failure
abs: Background: Heart failure (HF) is one of the leading causes of death globally. HF has been shown to present at least 15 years earlier in Southeast Asian patients, in comparison to their Western counterparts, thereby forecasting a significant socio-economic burden in the years ahead. Among HF cases, HFpEF (HF with preserved ejection fraction) with its characteristic diastolic dysfunction account for 50% of HF patients, and is steadily on the rise, projecting it to be the dominant form of HF. Specific aims: Recent clinical trials have implicated left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) as a prognostic marker for HFpEF, yet it is unclear as to how LVH results in diastolic dysfunction and HFpEF. Hypotheses: Cytosolic calcium overload (a feature of LVH) perturbs mitochondrial functionality, resulting in metabolic inflexibility in hypertrophied cardiomyocytes. Dysfunctional mitochondria together with loss in substrate selectivity between glucose and fatty acids would aggravate reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation and lipotoxic compound build-up contributing to increased sarcomere stiffness that culminate in diastolic dysfunction. Approach: Using induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology, due to its characteristic hypertrophic phenotype I plan to model LVH from patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Using this platform, I hope to gain insights into signalling pathways regulating mitochondrial dynamics and metabolic flexibility as well as identify molecular targets for therapeutic intervention. Understanding diastolic dysfunction of HFpEF, in context to LVH would help offer meaningful insights of this complicated disorder which is becoming more prevalent in rapidly ageing societies such as Singapore.

title: TO-ChERIsH: Trajectory of Cardiovascular Ageing, Its Determinants and Impact on Health
abs: Background: Cardiovascular (CV) ageing is a heterogeneous process that exhibits great variation with advancing age among individuals. Some individuals develop ageing-related deteriorations in CV structure and function resulting in CV disease (CVD) (unhealthy CV ageing) while others have relatively preserved CV health with chronological ageing (healthy CV ageing). Determinants of either CV ageing trajectories remain unknown. We hypothesize that investigations of CV ageing trajectories will unravel determinants of unhealthy and healthy CV ageing. Our hypothesis is based on data (2014-2017) from a community-based cohort of elderly individuals with CV imaging and bio-specimens that showed a spectrum of CV functions ranging from preserved to unhealthy measurements, that correlated with lifestyle (physical activity), systemic conditions (diabetes mellitus) and circulating metabolites (such as amino acids and acyl-carnitines). Traditional risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and physical activity, could not fully account for the extent of CV ageing observed. Specific Aims: (i) To determine rates of change in CV ageing over time via CV imaging markers; (ii) To assess if circulating metabolites markers present in archived blood samples (2000-2004) are associated with CV ageing 15 years later (2014-2017) and rates of CV ageing progression (2018-2021) and how these differences vary by gender, physical activity and diabetes mellitus; (iii) To determine impact of CV ageing on development of clinical CVD and overall physical, cognitive and functional health outcomes. Methodology: Participants from 2014-2017 will return in this proposal (2018-2021) for repeat biodata, CV imaging markers, and bio-specimen collection. Baseline and change in CV imaging and metabolite markers will be analysed from archived (2000-2004, 2014-2017) and fresh bio-specimens, adjusting for longitudinal covariates. Significance: Distinguishing trajectories of healthy versus unhealthy CV ageing will reveal determinants and impact of CV ageing. Targeting CV ageing may therefore improve burden of CVD and important ageing-related health outcomes among ageing populations.

title: A Randomised Controlled Trial Evaluating a Novel Individualised Treatment Strategy for Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative
abs: Carbapenem-resistant (CR) Gram negative bacteria (GNB) – which are resistant to carbapenems (a last-line potent antibiotic with a high therapeutic index) – are also resistant to all other beta-lactam antibiotics (1). Most CRGNB are also extensively-drug resistant (XDR) (resistant to all classes of antibiotics except polymyxins and/or tigecycline) or pan-drug resistant (PDR) (resistant to all antibiotics), resulting in a dearth of effective options against these life-threatening infections. Against CRGNB, standard therapy includes monotherapy (using polymyxins or tigecycline) or unguided antibiotics combination (polymyxins + carbapenem). Unfortunately, CRGNB can develop resistance after antibiotic monotherapy, resulting in the further development of pan-drug resistance. Unguided antibiotic combinations, selected anecdotally based on past experience, are also unlikely to be useful in our local setting, as effective antimicrobial combinations are bacterial-strain specific due to large variation in molecular mechanisms of resistance (2-8). Hence, we propose to evaluate the efficacy of a novel treatment strategy using in vitro antibiotic combination testing (iACT) to guide antibiotic combinations in the management of patients with CRGNB infections in a randomised controlled trial (RCT).

title: Application and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Deep Learning System to Detect Referable and Sight-threatening Retinal Diseases in the Singapore Integrated Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Programme (SiDRP): Screening Performance and Cost-effectiveness Analysis
abs: Screening for diabetic retinopathy (DR), a leading cause of visual loss, is a widely recommended strategy. In Singapore, patients with diabetes undergo DR screening via the Singapore Integrated DR Programme (SiDRP). In 2016, SiDRP screened nearly 80,000 people using a system of >20 professional technicians covering 18 polyclinics. With rising diabetes prevalence, SiDRP is projected to screen 200-250,000 people in the next decade and is thus challenged by issues related to availability of manpower and financial sustainability. Deep learning system (DLS) is a novel machine learning technology that utilizes artificial intelligence to detect not only referable DR, but also glaucoma suspect (GS) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD). We have trained a DLS to detect all 3 conditions, validated it using an independent sample of another 220,494 images, and found optimal diagnostic performance. However, whether this DLS can replace current DR screening model in SiDRP based on human/manual grading remains unknown. We hypothesize that the DLS will have similar or superior diagnostic performance, and enhance screening efficiency and productivity, ultimately saving cost and manpower. In this project we aim to evaluate 1) DLS diagnostic performance in detection of referable DR, GS, AMD via comparing referral accuracy of two new screening models (fully automated DLS, semi-automated DLS combined with manual grading) vs. current manual assessment of retinal images; and 2) cost-effectiveness of the two new models vs. current manual model. We will recruit 13,000 patients with diabetes over 3 years under SiDRP. All patients will undergo 2-field retinal photography (optic disc, macula fields), transmitted into a cloud-based system and assessed by two models of DLS (fully automated and semi-automated) as well as professional graders (current system) and retinal specialists (reference standard). We will compare diagnostic performance and costeffectiveness of the two new models to the current manual model.

title: Translational Asian Age-related macular degeneration Program (TAAP)
abs: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a major cause of blindness with significant socioeconomic and healthcare burden in rapidly aging populations in Singapore and Asia. An AMD subtype, polypoidalchoroidalvasculopathy (PCV), makes up 50% of AMD in Asians, but current treatment options for PCV remains limited. We propose a broad-based multi-disciplinary Translational clinical research program in Asian AMD and Polypoidalchoroidalvasculopathy (TAAP), integrating a team of retinal specialists, clinician-scientists, and basic scientists from across major research institutes in Singapore and globally. This “bench-to-bedside-to-population” has 5-linter-linked Themes that address key research questions and is aligned with clinical needs and strong industry interest: Theme 1 (Population Health) will characterize disease burden and identify risk factors of AMD/PCV in Asians to plan future public health policies and preventative interventions. Theme 2 (Pathophysiology) will examine novel pathophysiological mechanisms, metabolic and immune dysfunction and epigenetic changes in AMD with in-vitro and in-vivo experiments. Theme 3 (Novel Imaging Biomarkers) will exploit a multitude of novel imaging technology in collaboration with industry partners to develop and validate imaging biomarkers to guide personalized treatment. Theme 4 (Therapy) willtest and develop new therapeutic strategies for PCV through multi-centre clinical trials in Asia. Theme 5 (Quality Of Life) will determine the impact of AMD/PCV through studies in psychometric, behavioural, neuroscience and health economics and investigate the efficacy of a practical problem-solving therapy model on improving patient outcomes. TAAP will build on significant prior work (>10,000 population controls, >800 clinical AMD/PCV cases with biological samples and genetic data), an extensive international collaborative network with SERI and strong industry support. The broad-based research proposed has high potential for commercialization and significant clinical and population outcomes that will lead to blindness reduction from AMD by 20% within 10 years. TAAP is fully aligned to MOH’s priorities in “aging” and “precision medicine”.

title: End-of-life Management Protocol Offered Within Emergency Room: a multicentre study (EMPOWER)
abs: End-of-life (EOL) care has garnered increasing recognition and acceptance in the field of emergency medicine. Some emergency departments (EDs) in Singapore have instituted or plan to institute EOL care as part of their workflow. However, the EOL protocols are not standardised across all these EDs. The adherence to and quality of EOL care have not been formally measured in all institutions. Hence, gaps to improve the quality of care have yet to be determined. The aims are to systematically measure the current quality of EOL care in three Singapore hospital EDs and identify the quality gaps; formulate interventions to address these gaps and implement the improved EOL care; and measure the improvement post-implementation. We hypothesise that the current quality of EOL care in three EDs is suboptimal and the interventions planned will improve the quality of care provided. We plan to conduct an interrupted time series study to detect whether the interventions have an effect significantly greater than any underlying trend over time. The quality of care indicators to be measured are timely identification of patients who require EOL care, adequacy of symptom control based on compliance to prescriptions, opportunities to discuss and develop an individualised care plan, perceived quality of care by healthcare providers and next-of-kin, and cost effectiveness. Planned interventions include refining the protocol with collaboration of content experts in palliative care, education and training of healthcare providers, and addressing specific gaps identified to improve cost effectiveness. The results of this study will form the standardisation and foundation for establishing the national benchmark for quality of EOL care in Singapore EDs. (263 words)

title: Effects of selinexor in combination with ICE (ifosfamide, carboplatin, etoposide) and other chemotherapy agents in relapsed or refractory T-cell lymphomas
abs: Background: T-cell lymphomas (TCL) patients have a poor prognosis. ICE is standard salvage therapy but responses are low and not durable. A phase I study of selinexor in combination with ICE in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) TCL showed high complete response (CR) rates. Hypothesis and Specific Aims: We hypothesize that selinexor-ICE combination is (i) safe and (ii) efficacious at the recommended phase II dose (RP2D), that (iii) selinexor is synergistic with chemotherapy, and (iv) recurrent mutations in TCL tumours can be identified in plasma cell-free (cf) DNA. Our primary aim is to estimate the adverse events (AE) rates of selinexor-ICE in a dose expansion study. Secondary aims include complete response (CR) rates, overall response rates (ORR) and progression free survival (PFS) in a phase II study. We aim to perform drug combination assays to assess synergy of selinexor with chemotherapy and whole exome and amplicon sequencing on tumor and plasma samples, espectively. Methods: We will recruit 10 patients with R/R TCL into a phase I dose expansion cohort, which will function as stage I of Simon’s two-stage phase II study. If pre-defined safety criteria are met and 4 patients obtained a complete response (CR), we will recruit another 18 patients to the second stage of the phase II study. An international, multi-centre, retrospective review will provide corresponding CR, ORR and PFS for ICE alone. Selinexor will be tested in combination with chemotherapy on TCL cell lines to identify synergy. Recurrent mutations from tumor will be identified from cfDNA in patient’s blood at regular intervals during treatment and surveillance. Significance: Further safety and efficacy data are essential for selinexor-ICE, a potentially effective, novel treatment for TCL. Laboratory studies will identify synergistic drug combinations for developing rationally designed trials in R/R TCL. CfDNA may allow physicians to monitor disease status efficiently.

title: A study to identify markers of early retinal cell fate commitment in pluripotent stem cells in vitro.
abs: Clinical trials in patients with age related macular degeneration (AMD) have now shown that stem cell based retinal cell replacement therapy can successfully restore visual function. However, production of clinical grade retinal cells from pleuripotent stem cells (PSC) is a complex, time consuming and formidably expensive process. As a result retinal stem cell therapy remains inaccessible to most patients. To produce retinal cells, mixed PSC are subjected to retinal differentiation conditions until retinal cells are formed. This is followed by an extensive purification process to remove non-retinal cell impurities which escalates the time and cost of cell production. This purification process could be eliminated from the cell production protocol if committed retinal progenitors were selectively isolated from mixed PSC before differentiation, It has not been possible to use this approach thus far due to lack of selective surface markers of early retinal progenitors. Using an in vitro model of retinal development and single cell RNA sequencing analysis, we have now identified a list of cell surface targets that are differentially expressed in early committed retinal progenitors. Through this work, we propose to validate these cell surface targets as early committed retinal progenitor markers, by evaluating their ability to yield pure retinal cells in vitro if used for selective cell isolation from mixed PSCs. We have also identified novel transcription factors differentially expressed in early retinal progenitors, and part of this proposal will aim to understand the significance of these genes in early retinal cell fate commitment. Not only will this work enhance our understanding of retinal development; successfully validated cell surface markers of early retinal progenitors will pave the way for automation and up-scaling of retinal cell production, bringing down costs and making retinal stem cell therapy accessible to the growing cohort of patients who need it.

title: Artificial Intelligence Software for Emergency Neuro-radiological Diagnosis
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Background: It is desirable for radiological scans to be reported rapidly, accurately and automatically, as this would expedite medical treatment, improve patient outcomes, and reduce healthcare costs. Human clinicians are intrinsically limited by experience, time and fatigue, and they can be assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are AI algorithms that have demonstrated dramatic successes in computer vision, beating human experts. CNNs can be applied to analyse medical images and read radiological scans. Aim: The first aim of this study is to develop and optimize a three-dimensional CNN (3D CNN) that can analyse Computed Tomography (CT) brain scans for emergency neurological conditions such as stroke and traumatic brain injury. The second aim of this study is to deploy the developed 3D CNN in a large tertiary care hospital. Hypothesis: 3D CNN can be used to assist clinicians in the management of neurological emergencies by detecting and triaging abnormal scans. Method: In the first training stage, incoming CT brain data form patients who are scanned emergently at National Neuroscience Institute (NNI) will be collected for three months. This data will be used to train and optimize the 3D CNN to recognize common neurological emergencies such as acute intracranial haemorrhage. In the second evaluation stage, the 3D CNN software will be deployed alongside radiologists, and its ability to detect and triage abnormal CT brain scans will be measured. Feasibility: This proposal translates our prior laboratory work on 3D CNN to a clinical setting. Significance: Rapid and accurate diagnosis of CT brain scans is important in acute neurological emergencies. By expediting radiological diagnosis, this work can improve patient clinical outcomes in survival, morbidity, quality-adjusted life-years, and reduces healthcare and economic costs. This work can be used for any organ where CT and Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans are used.
kw: artificial intelligence, medical image analysis

title: Translational biomarker study of SAMIT: A randomized phase III Japanese clinical trial of adjuvant chemotherapy for gastric cancer
abs: Background Taxanes are active chemotherapeutic agents in the treatment of early and advanced gastric cancer. However, there are conflicting data in large randomized trials suggesting only a specific group of patients benefit from taxane chemotherapy. To date, there are no known predictive biomarkers to select patients appropriately for adjuvant chemotherapy. Stomach cancer Adjuvant Multi-Institutional group Trial (SAMIT), was a large randomized phase III trial conducted in Japan to study the benefit of adding paclitaxel to 5-fluoropyramidine based adjuvant chemotherapy in T4a/b gastric cancer. Specific Aims This is a translational study that aims to analyze transcriptomic data of primary gastric tumor resection samples from the SAMIT study to identify predictive biomarkers of paclitaxel chemotherapy in gastric cancer. Specific groups of genes associated with gastric cancer, genomic instability and immunogenic cell death will be selected and analyzed. Methodology Of the 1433 patients in the SAMIT trial, 556 cases had resected specimens’ paraffin-embedded blocks or slides available and will be included in this study. Samples were collected at the Kanagawa Cancer Centre and sent to Yokohama City University where mRNA was extracted and sent to Duke-NUS, Singapore. mRNA expression patterns will be studied using the NanoString ® platform and correlated with overall survival, progression free survival and clinicopathological features. The Nanostring panel is custom designed based on specific groups of genes which have been associated with response to therapy and prognosis of gastric cancer: 1) Oncogenic signaling pathway or known alterations in gastric cancer 2) Genome stability genes 3) Genes related to immune activation and immune evasion Clinical Relevance Identifying predictive biomarkers for paclitaxel chemotherapy in the treatment of gastric cancer will further the frontier of precision oncology by selecting the appropriate patients for this form of treatment in the future.
