title: SOCure: ASSURING HARDWARE SECURITY BY DESIGN IN SYSTEMS ON CHIP
abs: Chip-level hardware security has recently taken the center stage in informative articles for the public and other media, after being relegated to the scientific literature. This is due to the convergence of concurrent trends, such as the exponential diffusion of electronic identification for the access to personalized services (e.g., banking, electronic-ID), the dramatic reduction in cost and time for physical attacks to chips (due to technological advances). Concurrently, an exponential increase in the number of connected devices is taking place at the end of the mobile era and the beginning of the Internet of Things. Also, the semiconductor supply chain has become very fragmented geographically and in terms of players (driven by cost, and the rise of the semiconductor industry in some Asian countries). In perspective, chip-level hardware security is going to be even more crucial in developed economies and progressive countries that are massively adopting technologies to enable and simplify several types of secure transactions (e.g., financial, public services, medical records), including Singapore. Furthermore, even larger demand for hardware security is expected from the widespread diffusion of transactions managed by shared public ledgers, as in the case of blockchains (e.g., crypto currency, and prospectively many other services based on the analogous technologies). Bitcoin wallet hacking has been already demonstrated [DQB17], [D17], [D17a], and is a fundamental threat to the development of blockchain. The grand-goal of the SOCure project is to assure hardware security by design in Systems on Chip (SoC), introducing the unprecedented capability of withstanding the presence of untrusted on-chip Intellectual Properties (IPs), as well as physical attacks including advanced ones (e.g., invasive). The first capability permits to maintain existing system design methodologies of SoCs, allowing seamless integration in both existing and new architectures with no disruption in well-established industry design practice. Isolation among on-chip IPs is pursued through secure on-chip communications based on ultra-lightweight hardware. The second capability enables protection against physical attacks, which are now well known to be a fundamental and now widespread threat, and have been the focus of research only recently. On the architectural side, the SOCure framework pursues HW security with minimal area/energy overhead to be scalable and adoptable in systems with a wide range of complexity, from secure SoCs down to simpler systems such as secure Microcontroller Units. On the physical side, a thorough set of innovative techniques with low overhead and seamless integration with design flows is introduced to protect physical integrity and confidentiality of on-chip data. title: Development and test-bedding of Aquaporin InsideTM Membrane Technology for NEWater and Seawater Desalination Application
abs: Continuous efforts have been devoted to reducing energy and increasing the quality of produced water in RO desalination process during the past 50 years. Aquaporin-based biomimetic RO membranes have the potential to deliver game-changing energy reductions in wastewater and seawater treatment applications. However, to this day, industrial low-cost production technology of said membranes has not been fully developed for these applications. The biomimetic RO membrane essentially consists of two components: a porous support substrate providing mechanical support for the nanometer thin aquaporin-containing active layer. The method of integration of aquaporin formulation into the active layer and the compatibility between the substrate and active layer determine the water permeability, rejection, as well as the long-term operational stability of the membrane. Therefore, developing high performing biomimetic RO membranes requires tailoring the underlying support substrate to the active layer on top. The overall objective of this project is to develop, scale-up and pilot-test Aquaporin InsideTM low-energy high-flux BWRO and low-energy high-flux SWRO membrane. With the help of these membranes, we aim to reduce 20-40% energy consumption in both NEWater production and seawater desalination processes. It has been reported that the practical minimum specific energy consumption (SEC) is 1.56kWh/m3 for seawater desalination. Other than membrane filtration resistance, the 0.5-1kWh/m3 extra energy in the current process is also attributed to friction loss, concentration polarization, fouling, pump inefficiencies, etc.. Therefore, further investigation of implementation technology is equally important to membrane permeability enhancement. For this part of work, we aim to improve RO system design and operating conditions with the help of an RO system projection software which is customized for high-permeability aquaporin-based membrane developed in this project.

title: Whole Plant simulation using real-time data and feedback signal processing for model based control of wastewater processes with cognitive predictive capabilities.
abs: This proposal is a bold attempt towards developing a whole plant dynamic simulation model for Changi Water Reclamation Plant (CWRP), a wastewater treatment facility. This project will employ a suite of software packages for the development of a powerful and innovative tool that combines hydraulic, process and control system modeling with the SCADA screens for an exhilarating operational experience. The simulation model to be developed will include all relevant hydraulic and process components with appropriate property data defined; including instrumentation and control logic; and will validate, equipment capacity, storage capacities and dynamic facility performance capacity under comprehensive operating scenarios, and optimize operational processes. The model will run on real time data pulled from the SCADA historian. Data analytics employing statistical analysis, signal processing and filtering and forecast prediction will detect and replace anomalous data to be fed into the model and provide predictions on future performance. The simulation model will maintain its relevance to the current operation by constantly adjusting the model calibrations within defined ranges to match the observed performance. The model will be set to possess predictive capabilities to forewarn operator of impending process deviations and poor effluent quality and recommend steps for rectification. The simulation model can be run independently of the actual systems, thereby creating a digital twin which can be used as a “flight simulator” for operator training and scenario analysis to investigate impacts on operational changes on plant performance. The aim of the project is to provide PUB team and plant users the ability to explore and simulate various operational conditions using a dynamic simulation model to enhance water quality, optimize energy and chemical consumption, test operation strategies, and improve operator training.

title: A long flight endurance drone with AI/analytics-enabled detection capabilities
abs: Over the last few years, the use of industrial-grade drones to perform automated surveillance and inspection has grown tremendously in popularity. However, commercial application of drones is currently hindered by the short flight endurance (typically around 15-20 mins). This is primarily due to the low gravimetric energy density of lithium-polymer batteries (~175Wh/kg). The short flight endurance results in tremendous loss in productivity and severely restricts the potential application of drone technology due to lack of flight distance. On the other hand, hydrogen fuel cell systems are known to have 2.5-3x usable energy densities (450-500Wh/kg) as compared to lithium batteries. This allows fuel cell powered drones to be able to perform inspections of up to 2-4 hours, which greatly increases its field of use. In this project, we intend to integrate a world-leading fuel cell from a local company to greatly increase its flight time. The drone will be testbedded at PUB’s reservoirs to prevent illegal intrusion and fishing. To equit the drone platform with stable monitoring and accurate diagnosis capabilities, a small and light weight GPU-Enabled sensory and communication system will be proposed and integrated, as well as the backend video deep analytics by AI algorithm.
kw: Long endurance drone, robotics, automated-detection, analytics, surveillance

title: Development of New Smart Water and Adaptive Technology and Internet of Water Monitoring Things (NUSWAT-IoWT)
abs: Singapore is considered a water scarce country despite receiving an average rainfall of 2,400 mm/year [1]. As freshwater demands increase, continuous monitoring of the freshwater resources is crucial to enable fast detection of anomalies and allow swift responses. This proposal seeks to reduce the operational cost and improve the operational efficiency of our national freshwater monitoring effort. Currently, waterway monitoring relies on sparse sensor networks that lack the spatial resolution to detect local hotspots [2]. The project aims to develop a smart hybrid sensor network (SHSN), containing two static nodes and multiple robots, to estimate a spatiotemporally varying field of water quality parameters in waterways. We seek to quantify the system's performance and operational robustness and bring this technology to at least TRL 6 in collaboration with another industry partner. PUB currently possesses robots that automate spatial estimates using lawnmower paths [3]. Although this yields reasonable results for static fields, it is inadequate if the field dynamics is faster than the time needed for the robots to sufficiently cover the region of interest. We propose to test an adaptive sampling algorithm that plans the path using vehicle positions and uncertainties (currently modelled as Sparse Gaussian Process) in the predicted field. We will further improve the algorithm to include other models as needed and expend it to multi-robot sensing, based on what we learn in the field. Sensor cost is a major limiting factor preventing large-scale sensor node deployment. The project aims to mitigate this by developing cost-efficient water quality sensors. This includes a cost-efficient Chlorophyll sensor using a novel spectrometer from an industry collaborator. The complete sensor package will be test-bedded in the field to study its performance and resilience to biofouling, typical in long-term deployment.

title: Enhancing POlymer Crystallinity in MixEd Matrix Membranes by Incorporating Metal-Organic Framework Nanosheets for an Efficient CO2 Capture
abs: The urgent demand for natural gas sweetening and flue-gas purification has prompted the development of different technologies for efficient CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 separations, including adsorption, absorption, cryogenic distillation and membranes. Currently, amine-based absorption process using chemicals ranging from monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), and triethanolamine (TEA) dominates the CO2/CH4 separation market in natural gas industries owing to its high separation efficiency. However, this technology is largely limited by its large capital investment, high energy consumption and complicated maintenance. Adsorption and cryogenic distillation also experience similar challenges and they are particularly suitable for treating gases with a high CO2 content. Membranes offer more energy-saving alternatives by allowing mixtures to be continuously separated without a phase change. The energy savings of up to 50% can be realized in membrane-based separation processes compared to other technologies. Membrane materials play key roles in membrane technology. Therefore, the search for membrane materials with excellent separation performance and high resistance toward the harsh operational conditions has aroused great attention in recent years. Among various types of membranes, mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) have been proposed by using polymers as continuous phase and organic/inorganic fillers as dispersed phase to synergistically combine the merits of both components, i.e. a good processability and strong mechanic strength of polymeric materials; inherently high gas permeability and selectivity of filler materials. The main objective of this proposed project is to design and fabricate robust MMMs composed of porous metal-organic framework (MOF) nanosheets and highly permeable polymers for efficient CO2 capture. Chemically stable MOF nanosheets will be prepared in a bottom-up method, which guarantees their large production yield for future industrial applications. The intrinsic pores of CO2-selective MOF structures will provide fast gas permeation pathways, boosting the membrane gas permeation. Highly permeable polymers (> 3000 Barrer) can largely improve the gas treatment productivity in membrane units, possessing a huge potential of replacing current commercially available polymers with moderate or low gas permeability (< 100 Barrer). However, these polymers are semi-crystalline or amorphous in nature and often exhibit limited gas pair selectivity owing to the absence of efficient size-selective channels in final membranes. title: Optimization of Water Treament Plant operation with and AI Technologies
abs: Mitsubishi Electric launched INFOPRISMTM1 and Maisart®2. INFOPRISMTM is a consolidated management platform for social infrastructures with IoT technologies. Maisart® is an edgecomputing AI that can provide a localized and compact AI for process control. Maisart® is one of key technologies in INFOPRISMTM but it can be also used as an embedded technology for various equipment which cannot have a large scale computing. Those technologies contribute eliminating operator’s instructions for water and waste water treatment plant operation that result in energy and cost saving and improving reliability and repeatability of operation, because AI can propose more optimal operation such as energy saving to operators or automatically operate more efficient based on highly skilled operators’ knowledge and know-how AI learnt. Conventionally, these operations have been depending on skilled operators’ experiences and their intuitions. Therefore, it is difficult to succeed to those techniques to other operators with a short time. By taking those techniques into the plant operating system, the efficient, safe and stable plant operation can be achieved continuously. Newly developed compact AI, Maisart® as a brand of Mitsubishi Electric, is an edge-computing AI. Maisart® technology does not require large scale computer and internet access. Maisart® utilizes deep learning technology with unique algorithm developed by Mitsubishi Electric that is simply said “reducing the amount of AI neurons without accuracy deterioration”. Hence Maisart® can be realized as a compact AI. Mitsubishi Electric is developing AI guidance system, which is constituted with setpoint guidance and pre-caution, for water and wastewater treatment plant with Maisart technology. This proposal proposes further development of AI guidance system.

title: A pilot study on the use of in vitro activation of ovarian primordial follicles to treat women with premature ovarian failure.
abs: Advancement in fertility treatment has allowed more couples to have their own biological offspring. However, for women with primary ovarian insufficiency (POI), the current options are limited to adoption or oocyte donation. POI occurs in one percent of women under the age of forty, with affected women experiencing amenorrhoea and menopausal ranges of gonadotrophins (FSH). Many of these women entering POI have residual primordial follicles (PF) in their ovaries that are dormant. Recent evidence in both animal and human studies suggests that modulation of the PTEN and PI3K-AKT pathway can activate dormant follicles 1, 2. This approach, together with the disruption of the HIPPO signalling pathway allows stimulation of growth in dormant residual follicles. Indeed, this approach has been shown to be of benefit to women with POI, resulting in successful IVF live births 2 3. This proposal, a Pilot Study, aims to assess the use of In Vitro Activation (IVA) in women afflicted with POI and desiring IVF treatment, for which oocyte donation and adoption is not an option. Laparoscopic unilateral-oophorectomy will be performed, ovarian cortical tissue fragmented into 1mm3 and PF activated through 48 hours of treatment with a PTEN inhibitor and PI3K activator before retransplantation beneath the serosa of the fallopian tubes and remaining ovary. Weekly hormonal monitoring and ultrasound follicular-tracking under ovarian stimulation after activation of PF will be performed to assess for evidence of folliculogenesis, and IVF treatment performed to generate embryos for transfer. The successful demonstration of efficacy with this technique will open up fertility options not only for women with POI, but also older women between 41-45 years of age where PF pool is diminished, and cancer patients who had undergone ovarian tissue cryopreservation.
kw: Premature menopause, in vitro activation

title: Treating Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease through Modification of Microbiome-modulated Metabolites
abs: Background: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is rapidly becoming the most common cause of liver disease worldwide, whereby in Singapore, its prevalence is as high as 40%. It is of significant concern that the incidence and prevalence of NAFLD is expected to increase rapidly with the obesity and diabetes mellitus epidemics. The gut microbiome represents a significant environmental factor contributing to NAFLD. This is associated with increased microbiome-modulated metabolites, such as lipopolysaccharides (LPS), short-chain fatty acids (SCFA), and bile acid, which have been postulated to deregulate gut endothelial barrier function, leading to systemic bacterial translocation and subsequent hepatic inflammation. Aim: (i) To characterize the relationship between gut dysbiosis and microbiome-modulated metabolites in local NAFLD patients, (ii) To establish causality through creation of a microbiome-driven NAFLD animal model through induction with human microbiome. Methods: Through a pre-existing prospective NAFLD cohort (n=500), 100 patients with biopsy proven NAFLD would have their stools, as well biopsies of the liver, terminal ileum and cecum profiled for microbiome metagenomics and microbiome-modulated metabolites (LPS, SCFA, bile acids). Aliquoted samples from the above patients would be pooled and lavage into mice models, pretreated with antibiotics, to develop a gonotobiotic NAFLD murine model. Approach: The interplay between the gut microbiome and mediated metabolites amongst NAFLD patients is evident, although the causality and directionality of the interactions remain unclear. Thus to better study this interplay of factors, there is a need for translational animal models to recapitulate the physiology, histology, outcomes and transcriptomics changes seen in humans with NAFLD. While there have been numeral other NAFLD animal model1s, these models are dissimilar to human NAFLD by either requiring specific gene knockout, non-physiological dietary manipulation, and most models do not develop fibrosis, nor lead to hepatocellular carcinoma. Furthermore, our gut microbiome driven NAFLD model may better mimic all the clinical endpoints of NAFLD.

title: Development of a Programmable Chest/Abdominal Drain Fluid Regulator to Reduce Morbidity, Care Requirements and Improve Outcomes
abs: Pleural effusions and ascites occur in many disease states, resulting in poor symptom control and quality of life in sufferers. Removal of these collections of fluid via chest/abdominal drainage, alleviates symptoms rapidly, but are associated with complications such as re-expansion pulmonary oedema and systemic hypotension when unregulated. We proposed the creation of an automated device that can volume and rate-control this process. The aim of this grant proposal research is the creation of 4 device prototypes that can be adapted to existing chest/abdominal drains. The prototypes would be based on a prior patent co-invented by the grant applicant. The hypothesis is that the prototypes would be able to automate rate of fluid drainage over a range of fluid volumes, pressures and viscosity, accurately and precisely. The prototype will be developed in 2 phases to meet Class II requirements for device US-FDA approval. • Phase 1: The assembling of the 3 subsystems of the device prototype will be performed by collaborating engineers. These subsystems consist of the drainage mechanism, user interface and failsafe mechanisms. • Phase 2: Bench tests will be performed simulating real-life conditions in pleural effusions and ascites. The prototypes shall be able to demonstrate accuracy and precision in volume and rate control of drainage over a range of fluid volumes, pressures and viscosity. Refinement of the prototype will be performed during these bench tests to produce 4 prototypes that will meet regulatory requirements for first-in-man pivotal studies. The device is anticipated to generate annual cost savings of SGD 2.4 million for the nation by reducing inpatient length of stay. It will allow a reduction in time to symptom alleviation in sufferers, while decreasing physician and nursing workload. It will enhance home palliation of pleural effusions and ascites, easing the transition of care from hospital to community in terminally ill patients.

title: Assessing the correlation of Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) in assessing different grades of Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) tears with patient clinical outcomes: a bio-imaging clinico-translational prospective cohort study
abs: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears are the most common knee intra-articular ligament injury for sports athletes. The patient with an ACL tear will require almost 1 year before he or she can return to the sport of her choice. The diagnosis of ACL tears is made via MRI imaging along with clinical examination. There has been a mismatch of expectations and results in current ACL injury management, with the return to sports (RTS) rate for patients to pre-injury conditions being approximately 55% and in those patients, 25% will result in a repeat ACL tear. This is with the traditional dogma of early ACL reconstruction surgery with intensive post-operative rehabilitation. Recent studies have shown that conservative therapy with early aggressive physiotherapy alone can also provide good outcomes. However, current literature has yet to identify effectively which groups of patients or which types of ACL tears will respond favourably to conservative management and which types of tears will require early surgery. One of the main reasons is due to the lack of MRI techniques to accurately assess the viability and neural integrity of the injured ACL. This study investigates the use of Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) and its associated MRI imaging techniques as an imaging biomarker to accurately assess the viability and neural integrity of the injured ACL, with a proposal of a classification system and correlation with patient clinical outcomes. We postulate that this technology will eventually be used as a routine imaging technique to predict which modality of treatment (surgical or conservative) is suitable for the patient with an ACL tear.

title: The role of Yap/Taz expression in the development of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)
abs: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a pandemic associated with obesity and diabetes. NAFLD initially presents with hepatosteatosis, but can progress to steatohepatitis (NASH), fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Currently, the mechanism(s) for inflammation and fibrosis in NASH is not known; moreover, there is no available pharmacologic therapy for NASH. Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activators with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ) are transcriptional effectors in the Hippo signaling pathway that are increased in liver injury and fibrosis. We recently found that both proteins were induced in dietary and genetic models of NASH and associated with the induction of inflammation and fibrosis markers in the liver, macrophages, and hepatic stem cells (HSCs). Additionally, siRNA knockdown in hepatic cells and HSCs, as well as in macrophages from macrophage-specific Yap/Taz double knockout mice decreased expression of inflammation and fibrosis genes. Thus, Yap/Taz expression in hepatocytes, HSCs, and macrophages may have important roles in the pathogenesis of NASH. We hypothesize that expression of Yap/Taz in these cell types play critical roles in the inflammation, fibrosis, and metabolic changes of NASH. Accordingly, we plan to generate and employ mouse models of liver-, macrophage-, and HSC-specific deletion and overexpression of Yap/Taz: Specific Aim 1: To determine the role of hepatic Yap/Taz expression in NASH progression Specific Aim 2: To determine the role of Yap/Taz-regulated changes in macrophage polarization in NASH progression Specific Aim 3: To determine the role of Yap/Taz expression in HSCs in NASH progression Our studies will lead to better understanding of the relative contributions of Yap/Taz-mediated transcription in hepatocytes, macrophages, and HSCs in the pathogenesis of NASH. Yap/Taz expression also potentially could serve as a marker for NASH severity. Elucidating the specific role(s) of Yap/Taz in these different cell types could lead to the identification of new molecular targets for the treatment of NASH.
kw: non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, steatohepatitis, yap/taz, liver, macrophage

title: Systems for assessing mutational signatures in-vitro and discovering mutagenic exposures in tumours
abs: DNA mutations are a major cause of cancer. There are unmet needs for (1) improved testing of which compounds cause DNA mutations and determining what kinds of mutations they cause, ie their _mutational_signatures_ and for (2) searching for these signatures in human tumours. The latter is important for discovering which compounds are elevating cancer risk, which will lead to opportunities for prevention through education, regulation, and enhanced screening of exposed individuals. Indeed, widely varying rates of different cancer types across space and time provide prima facie evidence that environment strongly influences cancer risk. Use of mutational signature analysis will substantially improve understanding of the roles of mutagens in cancer risk and of the molecular epidemiology of cancer – improved understanding of the role of mutagenic exposures in explaining variation in cancer incidence across space and time. Here we propose renewal of the current funding, which supported (i) creation of a public database of mutations in >23,000 tumours, (ii) new approaches for computational analysis, (iii) experimental elucidation of several mutational signatures and their detection in human tumours, and (iv) application of mutational signature analysis to uncover widespread aristolochic acid mutagenesis in East Asia. The renewal will capitalize on these previous achievements by making computational aspects of mutational signature analysis widely available in the form of web applications and robust, portable software. These will provide critical infrastructure for other groups in their analysis of experimental induced mutations in cultured cells and of mutations in tumours. We will also make new discoveries in our own laboratory, by extending the database of mutations from > 23,000 tumours and mining it for as-yet undetected mutational signatures and linking these to experimentally elucidated mutational signatures. In particular we will characterize 100 additional, possibly mutagenic, compounds using the experimental system we developed with the current funding.
kw: mutational signatures; primary prevention; carcinogen safety testing; cancer epidemiology

title: Demonstration of integrated used water reclamation processes towards enhanced energy recovery and minimised sludge production
abs: The conventional activated sludge (CAS) process has been widely applied in municipal used water treatment for over 100 years. However, more and more concerns have been raised on its high energy consumption and huge excess sludge production which impairs environmental sustainability. It has been argued that substantial improvement in the energy efficiency is no longer achievable through further optimization of the activated sludge process. Therefore, it is absolutely necessary to develop new configurations of used water treatment plants with the considerations of enhanced energy recovery, reduced energy consumption and less excess sludge production in a more holistic manner. To address these today and future challenges, we propose to pilot-validate the two novel integrated used water reclamation systems for enhancing energy recovery, while minimizing sludge generation. In these integrated systems, an AnMBR with a treatment capacity of 60 m3/day will be employed as a lead stage for direct biogas production with minimized generation of waste sludge, and anaerobic effluent is then split into the two parallel processes for energy-efficient nitrogen removal, i.e. a step-feed mainstream anammox-MBR process of 20 m3/day and t-MBR of 40 m3/day, coupled with a RO unit for NEWater production, namely the mainstream AMX-MBR and t-MBR. The main purposes of this pilot study are to generate a comprehensive cost-benefit analysis in terms of energy consumption, energy recovery, sludge reduction, water quality as well as the design guidelines for further large-scale application.
kw: Anaerobic membrane bioreactor; step-feed mainstream anammox-MBR; t-MBR; RO; energy self-sufficiency; minimized sludge production

title: Productization of DTSS Inspection UAV Solution with Improved Specifications, Reliability and Data Processing Intelligence
abs: This research proposal aims to improve the TRL of a previously researched DTSS drone inspection solution from 6 to 8. The engineering and manufacturing issues of the solution will be addressed, and the solution will be improved with better reliability and be tested in operational environment repeatedly. The capability of drone in DTSS environment will be further improved in areas like location tagging accuracy and data collection variety and quality. Image and other types of data analytics will be developed to facilitate automated inspection result generation. The efficiency, convenience and safety of the system will also be improved so that minimal manual work is needed.
kw: UAV, GPS-less navigation, automated data analytics

title: National Satellite of Excellence in Trustworthy Software Systems
abs: The proposed National Satellite of Excellence (NSoE) will focus on certification and validation of smart systems, with the goal of building trust-worthy computing infra-structures for smart nation. Security certification of smart systems, clearly requires a rather broad range of capabilities, including modeling, testing, binary analysis, verification, vulnerability detection, and hardening. The proposed satellite of excellence will build upon the core capabilities developed in two previously funded research projects namely “Trustworthy systems from un-trusted component amalgamations” pursued at NUS, and the project “Securify” led by NTU. Both of these projects have developed workflows for certification of software systems via a combination of testing, analysis and verification. In the proposed center, we will pool together these core capabilities and enhance them to develop security certification workflows for embedded systems and IoT. To give a sharp focus on the research in the satellite of excellence, we could concentrate on one specific area such as software testing and verification for autonomous vehicles, if we can get access to the AV software. Security certification of software systems considers the use of tools / technologies for vulnerability detection and assessment. Certification guidelines usually provide a common criteria without providing guidance on how to meet these criteria. The research work in the proposed satellite will help build technologies which contribute to enforcing the certification criteria and its assessment. Moreover, we plan to give a specific tilt and focus to the research by engaging with CSA, DSO and other agencies on the testing and validation of software in one particular domain, such as driver-less cars (subject to the availability). Alternatively, the validation and certification flows can be used on software for IoT devices in various settings such as smart homes.
kw: Trustworthy Software, Software Security

title: From genes to products: Study and application of butterfly structural colors for biomimetic manufacture
abs: We propose to explore top-down and bottom-up approaches for the fabrication of nano-patterned materials with tunable fade-resistant colors and optical properties using biodegradable precursors. This technology can be used in diverse fields such as textiles, cosmetics, sensing, photonics, opto-electronics, and potentially also in the processed food industry. We will use insects, and particularly butterfly wing scale cells, to document the diversity of hierarchical biophotonic nanostructures that have evolved in these unique cells that are responsible for their striking iridescent (angle-dependent) and non-iridescent (angle-invariant) structural colors. The extremely organized cuticular skeletons of butterfly scale cells represent arguably the most complex cellular architectures seen in the animal kingdom but barely nothing is known about their development and genetic regulation. Our top-down approach will use newly developed high-resolution 3D printing methods, and chitosan, a material derived from shrimp shells but similar in composition to insect cuticle, to manufacture bio-mimetic material inspired by natural butterfly scales using etching and chitosan-spinning techniques, whereas our bottom-up approach will begin to explore the genetic and developmental basis of cuticle architecture and coloration via the description of single-cell transcriptomes followed by functional validation of candidate genes using CRISPR-Cas9. We will focus primarily on candidate transcription factors that might be coordinating scale color and scale cuticular architecture simultaneously. Scale colors and the associated hierarchical cuticular architectures will also be explored and teased apart with biophysical models, focused ion beams, and via synthesis of partial architectures to explore mechanisms that might control hue, saturation, brightness, iridescence, and other aspects of spectral tuning. Our combined approach to studying the biophysical, genetic and developmental processes that give rise to complex, hierarchical color-producing nano-architectures in the scale cells, will culminate in the exploration of approaches to bio-engineer these natural biodegradable materials in the lab, in a petridish.
kw: structural color; butterfly; biomimicry; chitosan; nano-fabrication; cell systems

title: High-throughput reprogramming of regulatory networks for cell conversions and treating complex diseases.
abs: Dysfunctional gene-regulatory networks are central to disease and can be reprogrammed for therapy. However, complex genetic interactions and the intractable number of potential combinations make it difficult find the most effective gene sets to target. We have developed powerful computational and experimental tools to overcome these bottlenecks. Specifically, our Mogrify platform enables the rapid computational prediction of regulatory genes that can convert between cellular states. Our Combinatorial Genetics En Masse (CombiGEM) platform enables massively parallel testing of these combinations via the efficient assembly of barcoded combinatorial perturbation libraries. Thus, predicted combinatorial genetic perturbations from Mogrify can be exhaustively tested experimentally via CombiGEM to discover key genetic networks to be reprogrammed for efficient cell conversions and to treat disease. The interdisciplinary team led by Dr. Rackham combines experts in cardiovascular disease (Dr Schaefer, Cook and Tryggvason), Technology development (Dr Lu and Rackham) and Cell Reprogramming (Dr Polo). Together they will combine the CombiGEM platform (invented by Dr Lu) and Mogrify (invented by Rackham) to answer important biomedical questions in cardiovascular and cell therapy. These cutting-edge technologies will be integrated for the first time, resulting in a powerful computational-experimental platform for reprogramming cell function. We have two highly complementary objectives that will uncover new biology and discover novel therapeutic targets. In Objective 1, we will computationally identify and experimentally validate key regulatory nodes that improve the efficiency of reprogramming fibroblasts into induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells and cardiomyocytes. In Objective 2, we will computationally identify and experimentally refine key regulatory nodes that inhibit the conversion of normal cells into diseased cells when these genes are perturbed. Specifically, we will block the conversion of vascular smooth muscle cells into foam cells and also inhibit the dysfunctional remodelling of epithelial cells under hypoxic conditions.
kw: Reprogramming; CRISPR; Stem cells; Combinatorial genetics; Cardiovascular disease

title: Singapore Cyber-security Consortium
abs: Modern Singapore society is highly reliant on software systems and information technology infra-structure. As a result, cyber-security issues and concerns permeate into our everyday lives. This makes it critical for us to co-ordinate research, manpower training, and translation activities in the area. Singapore Cyber-security Consortium was started in 2016 with 14 member companies and currently it has over 35 member companies. This proposal argues for the need to go a step beyond, and develop further the Singapore cyber-security consortium anchored at the National University of Singapore (NUS) to help encourage use-inspired research, translation, manpower training and technology awareness in the area of security.

title: Development of a Smart Control System for the Singapore Used Water Loop
abs: This research proposal is submitted by ST Marine as the lead partner, responsible for system integration and implementation, and Royal Haskoning DHV, as the technology provider and technical consultant. Currently, wastewater transport, wastewater treatment, sludge treatment and NEWater treatment are controlled separately. We propose to investigate, model and develop a automated control system for water reclamation plants for unmanned operation and/or decision support for operators, capable of integrated control of the solids module, liquids module and NEWater plant. This system will be developed based on Royal Haskoning DHV’s proven Aquasuite software, which is software for optimization and unmanned operation of water systems The requirements of PUB in this RFP 1803 can be met using the capabilities of current Aquasuite Software and to further develop a platform where all the different modules of the Aquasuite (PURE for wastewater treatment and FLOW for wastewater transport) can integrate into a Smart Solution to provide wholesome monitoring and control capability of the entire used water cycle. This integration is expected to save energy and increase the reliability and efficiency of the operations. The wastewater transport system can be used much smarter than only conveying wastewater from the sewer system to the reclamation works. Traditionally the locally controlled pumping stations are used primarily to empty the sewer system. The resulting flow rates could fluctuate significantly during different weather condition which has bad influence on the treatment processes or energy consumptions. One possible outcome of the research is to alter the pumps deployment, depending on the weather condition or ingress rate of sewage, to optimize critical processes in the sewer system and treatment works. The administrator can choose which process to optimize, e.g. energy consumption, treatment efficiency, water quality.
kw: Model Predictive Control, Wastewater Transport, Wastewater Treatment

title: Brown fat activation and browning Efficiency Augmented by Chronic COld and Nutraceuticals for Brown adipose tissue-mediated Effect Against Metabolic Syndrome (BEACON BEAMS Study)
abs: Specific Aims and Hypotheses: Having proven that brown adipose tissue (BAT) in adults can be acutely activated by cold and capsinoids, we will now investigate the effectiveness of chronic cold exposure and BAT-activating nutraceuticals in raising energy expenditure, fat oxidation, white adipose tissue (WAT) browning into beige fat to induce weight loss and improve metabolic syndrome regardless of initial BAT status.Methodology and Approach:We will recruit subjects with metabolic syndrome (n=80) and randomize them into 3 parallel intervention arms (n=20 each: daily cold exposure with cooling vest over 1 h, daily intake of BAT-activating nutraceuticals, or a combination of cold exposure and BAT-activating nutraceuticals) together with a control arm. We will employ BAT and WAT assessment protocols including infrared thermography (IRT), fat fraction MRI, 18F-FDG-PET and whole body calorimetry (WBC). The WAT browning mix of functional food spices consisting of capsinoids and curcumin will serve as a æfood-basedÆ method to induce thermogenesis through BAT. Subjects will be evaluated at baseline and re-evaluated at 12 weeks, following which all interventions will be discontinued and the subjects re-evaluated at 24 weeks to determine any reversal of browning, BAT, WAT, fat oxidation, metabolic rate and selected biomarkers. Importance to Science or Medicine:This research will reveal the nature of BAT and WAT plasticity under chronic cold and nutraceuticals. It will address establish the safety and efficacy of BAT-activating methods on accentuating metabolic rate and fat oxidation to counter obesity and diabetes independent of food intake and physical activity. Clinical Significance:In our obesogenic environment where energy dense food and physical inactivity are major factors driving the rising scourge of metabolic disorders, it fits our national interest to develop promising non-pharmacological, safe and natural BAT-activating approaches that tackle obesity and diabetes feasibly adopted by the general population.
kw: Brown adipose tissue; White adipose tissue; Browning; Imaging; Metabolic rate; Whole body calorimetry

title: INVESTIGATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL, GENETIC AND GUT MICROBIAL FACTORS UNDERLYING OBESITY AMONGST CHINESE, MALAY AND INDIANS IN SINGAPORE
inst: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital Pte Ltd
abs: Introduction: Obesity is a complex, multi-factorial disease that poses an increasing public health problem in Singapore. National health statistics show that Malay and Indian people are more susceptible to obesity, than Chinese. Furthermore, the effectiveness of weight loss interventions is variable between individuals, even within ethnic groups. The exact mechanisms underlying the differing ethnic susceptibility to obesity and the varying response to therapeutic intervention are not known. Hypothesis: Environmental, genetic and gut microbial factors contribute to the different risk of obesity amongst the major ethnic groups in Singapore, and also influence the weight loss and metabolic outcomes in response to dietary interventions. Aims and methods: I will first investigate whether known genetic factors (Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms, quantified by genotyping) and environmental exposures (dietary habit and physical activity, quantified by Food Frequency Questionnaires and triaxial accelerometry respectively) account for the increased risk of obesity amongst Malay and Indian, compared to Chinese people, amongst 5,000 participants of the Health for Life in Singapore (HELIOS) study. I will then use an extreme case-control design to quantify gut microbial composition in 150 obese cases and 150 lean controls, from amongst the three ethnic groups in Singapore, and investigate whether alterations in gut microbial composition are i. associated with obesity, and ii. account for the differences in obesity between Malays, Indian and Chinese. Finally, I will take advantage of an ongoing lifestyle intervention study (TOAST-T2D) to determine whether genetic variants and gut microbiome influence weight loss outcomes amongst 500 people undergoing dietary intervention for obesity. Significance: Understanding the basis of differences in obesity and weight loss may provide insights into the pathogenesis of obesity that would not only allow us to develop and improve public health strategies for the prevention of obesity, but also pave the way towards personalised medicine for the management of obesity in Singapore.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest through a National, Living, Learning, Pre-hospital Emergency Care Laboratory: Bundle of Ambulance-based Interventions
abs: Background: Singapore has more than 1800 out-of-hospital Cardiac Arrests (OHCA)/year. Changes implemented as a result of past research have increased OHCA survival from 2.5% (2001) to 11.0% currently, with potential for further improvements. Objectives: The aim of the proposed study is to increase OHCA survival. We will establish a national, living, and learning prehospital emergency care (PEC) laboratory, which can help improve clinical care as well as guide policy change for OHCA interventions. Design/Methods: 1. Information from various sources in the chain of clinical care for OHCA, such as the national ambulances, emergency departments, etc. will be consolidated. A simulation model will be developed to monitor performance, identify gaps and evaluate implementation of interventions. 2. Develop and evaluate the effectiveness of community programs such as mass, simplified cardio-pulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, installation of automated external defibrillators in residential blocks, a mobile phone app which alerts users of OHCA nearby and a card that measures CPR quality. 3. Develop and evaluate the effectiveness of ambulance based interventions such as high performance team CPR, new resuscitation drug, etc.

title: Youth Positive Mental Health: Getting the Full Picture
abs: Mental health promotion is based on the underlying principle that mental health is a positive concept and more than absence of illness. Given that most mental disorders have their onset during youth, interventions in this group are important. Population-based, youth-focused, non-clinical approaches to disease prevention are believed to be less stigmatizing and more accessible to young people. Although such interventions have shown beneficial effects, there exist several gaps in the appropriate measurement of youth positive mental health. The influence of current high social media exposure also needs to be considered. This study aims to identify youth positive mental health components in the contemporary setting. Using a sequential mixed-methods approach, this research will focus on positive mental health of Singaporean adolescents and young adults in the ages of 15-24 years and identify facets of youths’ life they associate with mental health. A modified Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) protocol will be employed. First, a systematic review will be conducted to develop a domain map for youth positive mental health, followed by qualitative investigation among youths to identify components of positive mental health. An item pool will then be generated to identify, catalogue, refine, and create candidate items for assessing youth positive mental health. Lastly, the item pool(s) will be administered in a community-based cross-sectional survey among youth populations to identify potentially modifiable determinants or high risk groups in relation to youth mental health. These data will be used for item reduction, and validation of a youth positive mental health tool. The findings of the study will not only establish the conceptual framework for youth positive mental health in the current setting, but also identify the factors that motivate and influence their mental health which can inform decisions on youth mental health promotion and evaluation in future.

title: A randomized trial on the impact of External Counterpulsation therapy on cerebral hemodynamic parameters in patients with symptomatic and severe steno-occlusive disease of intracranial internal carotid or middle cerebral artery and impaired cerebral vasodilatory reserve
abs: Primary aim- To evaluate whether Enhanced External Counter-Pulsation (EECP) therapy would lead to an improvement in cerebral vasodilatory reserve (CVR) in patients with severe and symptomatic stenosis of intracranial carotid (ICA) or middle cerebral artery (MCA). We hypothesize that EECP therapy would lead to at least 4-points improvement in CVR as compared to best medical therapy and reduce the risk of cerebral ischemic events by at least 10%.. Secondary aims- 1. To evaluate the impact of EECP on reducing recurrent cerebral ischemic event in the study population. 2. To evaluate the impact of EECP on neurocognitive performance in the study population. Background and hypothesis- Intracranial stenosis is widely prevalent among ischemic stroke patients in Singapore (seen in upto 50% patients). Despite a high risk of cerebral ischemic events, management of severe intracranial stenosis remains suboptimal and controversial. Intracranial stenting and surgical revascularization are associated with high early peri-procedural risks. EECP therapy appears to be a possible adjuvant therapeutic option for patients with severe intracranial stenosis. Methods- Patients with recently symptomatic severe stenosis of intracranial ICA or MCA with impaired CVR on transcranial Doppler (TCD) would be evaluated with acetazolamide- challenged single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT). Patients with impaired CVR would be randomized to receive best medical therapy (plus sham EECP) alone or best medical therapy plus EECP for 7 weeks. Detailed clinical, imaging and neuropsychological assessments would be performed by blinded assessors at 4 months. This project intends to generate the physiological and clinical data related to the changes in cerebral hemodynamic parameters, short-term reduction in stroke/TIA risk and changes in neurocognitive performance in patients treated with adjuvant EECP therapy. Our findings will lead to a larger well planned phase-3 efficacy study and open a new therapeutic option for patients at very high risk of cerebral ischemic events.

title: T cell receptor mediated immune therapy in chronic hepatitis B and hepatocellularcarcinoma.
abs: This is the renewal of a STAR grant entitled öT cell receptor (TCR) mediated immune therapy in chronic hepatitis B and hepatocellular carcinomaö awarded 5 years ago to ôestablish a clinical and scientific center dedicated to develop immune-based therapies for CHB and HCC patients in Singaporeö. My group has accumulated scientific knowledge, produced therapeutic tools and established a network of collaborations with academic and industrial partners that allow us to effectively translate HBV-specific TCR-T cell therapy from bench to clinical use. I propose here research projects that aim to increase the clinical efficacy of the TCR-T cell therapy both in the treatment of HBV related HCC and of HBV chronic infection. My objectives are to improve the selection of patients (Aim 1a), therapy administration (Aim 1b) and to develop a method to assess the efficacy of treatment (Aim 1c) in the therapy of HBV-related HCC.To achieve these goals, I propose to: 1a) Characterize the HBV transcriptome profile of HCC lesions and test its ability to guide TCR selection for clinical use; 1b) define the alteration induced in the tumor microenvironment by TCR-T cell therapy; 1c) explore the possibility to directly visualize TCR-T cell delivery in vivo and test whether TCR-T cell therapy can trigger a novel antitumor immunity.I also propose to facilitate the use of TCR-T cells in the therapy of chronic HBV infection (Aim 2) by exploring methods to program circulating T cells for anti-HBV activity that utilizes nanoparticles mediated TCR expression or the use of resting T cells.These projects will allow to consolidate our world leading position in the field of T cell therapy of persistent HBV infection and HBV-related liver cancer but might also have a more general impact in the immunotherapy domain against other persistent viral diseases (HCMV and EBV) and solid tumors.

title: Identifying distinct immune cell subpopulations in colorectal cancer using single cell transcriptomics and evaluating their spatio-biological interactions in fixed tissues.
abs: The tumor micro-environment comprises diverse cell populations, ecologically interacting and influencing overall tumor architecture, oncologic phenotypes and clinical behavior. Immune-tumor cell interactions (e.g. PD-1/PDL1 axis) are now viable targets in oncology with unprecedented regulatory approvals of immune checkpoint inhibitors in multiple cancer-types. However, in colorectal cancer (CRC), a globally prevalent cancer, results of clinical trials of drugs targeting PD1/PDL1 & CTLA4/B7 interactions have been disappointing. There is an unmet need to unravel the mediators of the immune millieu in colorectal cancer. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can identify and characterize distinct immune cell subsets and the transcriptional signatures of these immune cells make it possible to dissect the contribution of different cell types/states within the tumor micro-environment. Recently, we performed a proof-of-concept study with early-generation single-cell transcriptomic technologies(Li, Nat Genet '17) analyzing ~500 cells from 11 patients Building upon this work, we have entered into an academic-industry collaboration to generate single-cell transcriptomes from over 6,000 cells per patient from 50 CRC patients. Using data generated from this dataset, we seek to describe the diversity of immune cell subpopulations in colorectal cancer and their clinicopathologic and molecular correlates (Aim 1). We will FACS-sort major immune cell lineages and generate scRNASeq to describe major immune cell type subclusters and examine distinct gene expression profiles of these immune cell clusters. Next, we will validate these distinct cell states with mass cytometry and then describe the spatial context and interactions of immune cell subpopulations in fixed colorectal cancer tumor tissue (Aim 2) using archival FFPE tissue microarrays from both the 50 patients and a retrospective cohort of 158 genomic-ally annotated CRC patients. Together, we seek to understand the cellular heterogeneity composing the tumor microenvironment which is key to improving existing treatments, discovery of predictive biomarkers, and development of novel therapeutic strategies in colorectal cancer.
kw: single cell RNA sequencing, colorectal cancer

title: Focal Therapy for Prostate Cancer: Personalized Therapy to Maximize Functional Outcomes while achieving Oncological Success
abs: Aim: To determine whether there is a significant change in Expanded Prostate Index Composite (EPIC) scores post-procedure compared to pre-procedure. Hypothesis: No change in EPIC subdomain scores >4 points at any timepoint at 1,3, 6 or 12 months after treatment compared to baseline. Background and Methodology: Advances in imaging and targeted biopsy have improved the ability to differentiate intermediate and high-grade cancers from indolent ones. In the past, where systematic biopsy was deemed inadequate, clinicians turned to saturation biopsy methods such as trans-perineal mapping biopsies (TMB). TMB can create maps for targeted treatment but involve a large number of samples, tend to over-detect low-grade cancers, and can be associated with complications. Multi-parametric MRI (mpMRI) improves staging, preferably detects higher-grade cancers and MRI-TRUS fusion systems allow physicians to target these areas with fewer overall biopsy cores. This ability to better determine cancer grade and extent has led to a renewed interest in focal therapy (FT), a concept whereby one particular area of the prostate harboring clinically significant disease is treated instead of the entire gland, sparing collateral neurovascular bundle(s) and the urinary sphincter resulting in less morbidity than a whole gland approach. We propose a single arm phase II trial of MRI-fusion focal prostate cryotherapy in men with localized prostate cancer to establish oncological efficacy, safety and functional outcomes.

title: An Intensive, Practical, and Personalized Care Planning to Improve Glycemic Control, Clinical, Ocular, And Patient Centred Outcomes in Poorly Controlled Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy
abs: The prevalence of diabetes in Singapore is increasingly rising as are associated microvascular complications mostly due to poor diabetes management, suggesting that alternative and personalized interventions are urgently needed. Using a multi-site, longitudinal, and single blind RCT, the current proposal aims to evaluate the clinical, ocular, patient-centred and economic effectiveness of an evidence-based behavioural intervention, Problem Solving Treatment for Diabetes (PST-D), in patients with poorly controlled diabetes attending three tertiary hospitals, with the option for interested community-dwelling individuals with diabetes to participate, in Singapore. PST-D is a cognitive-behavioural intervention aims to teach individuals skills to cope with and solve problems related to their diabetes management. The intervention consists of one introductory session, up to eight weekly treatment sessions, and three monthly maintenance sessions; sessions will be conducted over the phone or face-to-face depending on the participant’s preference. During the sessions, participants will focus on one problem and will be taught and guided through the seven steps of problem solving. Participants will take an active role to make changes in their diabetes self-management behaviours. Participants will be randomly allocated to either the intervention group (PST-D + usual care) or the attention control group (sessions related to general health topics + usual care). Assessments will take place at baseline, 6, 12, and 18 months post intervention. We hypothesize that compared to usual care, those randomized to PST-D will have significantly greater improvements in cardio metabolic risk factors including glycated hemoglobin (primary outcome); and due to the sustained improvements in these risk factors, there will be a significantly lower proportion of incidence and progression of diabetes-related complications (DR, DN, DPN, and visual impairment) at 18 months in the PST-D group. Our personalized approach has wider applications. It can easily be adapted to other diabetes-related complications, such as kidney disease or for use with other systemic health conditions where disease progression can be tracked and behavioral factors can determine progression.
kw: Integrated care, personalized eye care, diabetes management, clinical outcomes, patient-centered, diabetic retinopathy

title: An AI assistant to radiologists that reads mammograms to automatically detect breast cancers and generate diagnostic reports: a technology combines the learning of images and free text
abs: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women both in the developed and less developed world. Worldwide over half a million women died from breast cancer in 2011. Due to the lack of effective preventive strategies against breast cancer, early detection is still the cornerstone for breast cancer control to improve patientsÆ outcomes. Mammography is currently the most effective tool for breast cancer screening and early detection of the disease. As mammogram reading is a repetitive and fatiguing task, studies have shown that the current approach suffers from high false positive and false negative rates. In addition, efficiency is another bottleneck of the current approach. In a double reading setting, each case may take up to 30 minutes for radiologists to finish reading the mammogram and writing up the diagnosis report. To address these issues, our project aims to develop a holistic Artificial Intelligent (AI) solution that can 1) diagnose breast cancer through reading mammogram images and 2) moreover, automatically generate a draft of diagnosis report for radiologists to approve or edit on. This project is an expansion of our prior work on medical notes processing with statistical models, published in AAAI, and our work on mammogram analysis, where we were ranked number two in an international challenge. We propose to detect breast cancer from mammograms by extracting cancer-related features and abnormal lesions with deep convolution neural network. We then employ recurrent neural network to translate the extracted features from the mammogram images to free-text and so to finally form the diagnosis report. We will be training these AI models with 10,000 de-identified patient data from NUH with active feedbacks from clinical experts to continuously improve the performance of our AI models. We target to have our AI model to achieve on par accuracies with human radiologists.
kw: Breast Cancer Diagnosis; Mammogram Analysis; Artificial Intelligence; Automatic Report Generation; Deep Learning and Active Learning; Natural Language Processing

title: Effects of Dapagliflozin and Metformin on Vascular Function in Newly-Diagnosed Treatment-Na?ve Type 2 Diabetes û A Randomized Controlled Trial (DMVascular Study
abs: The DMVascular study aims to address the impact of early medical therapeutics on vascular function. This stems from the provocative central hypothesis that reduction in cardiovascular risk with glucose-lowering therapies is a result of their beneficial effects on endothelial function, and absolute effect on the vascular risk profile, and is beyond glycaemic control. Recently sodium glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have been shown to lower cardiovascular risk and mortality within months of initiating treatment, suggestive of early haemodynamic or vascular function enhancements. The primary objective is to determine which vascular processes are specifically enhanced with Dapagliflozin (a SGLT2i) in comparison with Metformin and if its effect is the same in combination treatment in a randomized controlled study involving treatment-na?ve individuals. Our specific aims are to evaluate the effects of the intervention on: (Aim 1): microvascular and macrovascular function comprehensively inclusive of vascular haemodynamics at retinal and peripheral capillaries, radial artery, brachial artery, carotid artery and aortic artery; inflammation and oxidative stress in order to elucidate the specific pathway which is affected by SGLT2i; (Aim 2): the haemodynamics (involving blood pressure regulation) by studying the sodium equipoise, intrarenal renin-angiotensin and systemic sympathetic and parasympathetic systems; (Aim 3): leukocyte-endothelial interactions using bio-mimetic blood vessel-on-chip in-vitro models. Our proposed study is significant as this study has the potential to reveal SGLT2i and metformin specific vascular processes which can be exploited to uncover novel targets or to personalise/stratify patients who will benefit most from these medications. This approach is innovative as we propose to study all the interrelated vascular and haemodynamic pathways comprehensively using novel methods to evaluate the microvascular and macrovascular functions to gain a mechanistic insight into the positive effects with early therapeutics in newly diagnosed T2DM individuals.
kw: Diabetes, Vascular function, SGLT2 inhibitor

title: Effects of Dapagliflozin and Metformin on Vascular Function in Newly-diagnosed Treatment Naïve Type 2 Diabetes- A Randomised Controlled Trial (DMVascular Study)
abs: The DMVascular study aims to address the impact of early medical therapeutics on vascular function. This stems from the provocative central hypothesis that reduction in cardiovascular risk with glucose-lowering therapies is a result of their beneficial effects on endothelial function, and absolute effect on the vascular risk profile, and is beyond glycaemic control. Recently sodium glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have been shown to lower cardiovascular risk and mortality within months of initiating treatment, suggestive of early haemodynamic or vascular function enhancements. The primary objective is to determine which vascular processes are specifically enhanced with Dapagliflozin (a SGLT2i) in comparison with Metformin and if its effect is the same in combination treatment in a randomized controlled study involving treatment-naïve individuals. Our specific aims are to evaluate the effects of the intervention on: (Aim 1): microvascular and macrovascular function comprehensively inclusive of vascular haemodynamics at retinal and peripheral capillaries, radial artery, brachial artery, carotid artery and aortic artery; inflammation and oxidative stress in order to elucidate the specific pathway which is affected by SGLT2i; (Aim 2): the haemodynamics (involving blood pressure regulation) by studying the sodium equipoise, intrarenal renin-angiotensin and systemic sympathetic and parasympathetic systems; (Aim 3): leukocyte-endothelial interactions using bio-mimetic blood vessel-on-chip in-vitro models. Our proposed study is significant as this study has the potential to reveal SGLT2i and metformin specific vascular processes which can be exploited to uncover novel targets or to personalise/stratify patients who will benefit most from these medications. This approach is innovative as we propose to study all the interrelated vascular and haemodynamic pathways comprehensively using novel methods to evaluate the microvascular and macrovascular functions to gain a mechanistic insight into the positive effects with early therapeutics in newly diagnosed T2DM individuals.

title: Evaluating the clinical utility of immune phenotypes in schizophrenia
abs: Schizophrenia has a lifetime prevalence risk of about 1% and a third of patients with schizophrenia have been reported to be resistant to current antipsychotic treatments; thus, identification and further study of these subpopulations is crucial for development of appropriate treatment regimes. There have been increasing reports linking schizophrenia to immune dysregulation. Enriched immune-related genes and pathways have also been identified from recent studies and are congruent with the PI’s own work. Recent clinical trials using NSAIDs and other antiinflammatory agents have also produced interesting results, though conflicting at times. The present study seeks to extend the current evidence for immune dysregulation in schizophrenia as well as to examine its potential clinical utility. The first aim of this study is to comprehensively examine immune profiles in peripheral blood of healthy controls and patients with schizophrenia categorized by their pharmacological subtypes – antipsychotic responsive, clozapine responsive and clozapine resistant. As part of the immune profiles, we will examine immune-related genes, proteins, cytokines, and immune cell populations with respective function. The second aim is to correlate immune markers with pharmacological response. We hypothesize that each group will have distinctive immune profiles. We aim to recruit 200 participants; 50 per group in this observational study. Flow cytometry and functional assays will be performed for immune profiling. Results from this study will provide the identification of distinct immunology profiles for the subgroups of schizophrenia. This information allows the advancement in personalized treatment management in psychosis, and provides the evidence for personalised immune therapies. Upon successful identification of such immune biomarkers, the team will work on validation and appropriate studies to examine the efficacy of immunomodulatory agents in schizophrenia.

title: A Randomised Controlled Trial Evaluating a Novel Individualised Treatment Strategy for Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria Infections
abs: Carbapenem-resistant (CR) Gram negative bacteria (GNB) – which are resistant to carbapenems (a last-line potent antibiotic with a high therapeutic index) – are also resistant to all other beta-lactam antibiotics. Most CRGNB are also extensively-drug resistant (XDR) (resistant to all classes of antibiotics except polymyxins and/or tigecycline) or pan-drug resistant (PDR) (resistant to all antibiotics), resulting in a dearth of effective options against these life-threatening infections. Against CRGNB, standard therapy includes monotherapy (using polymyxins or tigecycline) or unguided antibiotics combination (polymyxins + carbapenem). Unfortunately, CRGNB can develop resistance after antibiotic monotherapy, resulting in the further development of pan-drug resistance. Unguided antibiotic combinations, selected anecdotally based on past experience, are also unlikely to be useful in our local setting, as effective antimicrobial combinations are bacterial-strain specific due to large variation in molecular mechanisms of resistance. Hence, we propose to evaluate the efficacy of a novel treatment strategy using in vitro antibiotic combination testing (iACT) to guide antibiotic combinations in the management of patients with CRGNB infections in a randomised controlled trial (RCT).

title: Focal Therapy for Prostate Cancer: Personalized Therapy to Maximize Functional Outcomes while achieving Oncological Success
abs: Prostate cancer is the third most frequent male cancer and the seventh most frequent cause of death in Singapore. The gold standard curative treatment of localized prostate cancer is whole-gland therapy with radical prostatectomy (surgical removal of the prostate gland) or radiotherapy. These methods are effective at curing cancer but result in collateral damage to adjacent structures resulting in impaired urinary continence and erectile dysfunction. In patients with cancer localized to one area of the prostate gland, focal therapy of just the dangerous cancer focus may allow a patient to maintain continence and erectile function and avoid the side-effects of radical treatment while achieving cure. We aim to evaluate the degree of preservation of continence and erectile function and early oncological outcomes in patients treated with focal cryoablation of the prostate. This is a phase II study of men with localized prostate cancer. Consenting men will undergo multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and targeted biopsy of suspicious lesions to select only those with: (1) mpMRI cancer focus < 3 ml in size, (2) involvement limited to one anatomic region (left, right or anterior gland), (3) localized cancer on mpMRI, (4) target lesion 4+4 and (53+3 cancer, to undergo focal cryoablation. The primary outcome, post-treatment functional status, will be tracked with standardized questionnaires performed at 0, 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. The secondary outcome, oncological success, will be assessed at 1 year with repeat biopsy and mpMRI. To demonstrate no significant deterioration in post-treatment functional outcome, we will recruit 27 men for this study. Our findings will establish the safety of focal cryoablation and be the basis of further research into the utility of this technique in achieving cure while preserving function in men with prostate cancer.

title: Clinical trial of rosuvastatin as an adjunct to standard treatment for drug-sensitive tuberculosis
abs: New approaches are needed to shorten treatment for tuberculosis (TB). Treatments working on host targets represent an important new approach. title: Detection of occult paroxysmal atrial fibrillation following ischemic stroke in a multi-ethnic Asian population and elucidating their significance in relation to recurrent stroke outcomes
abs: Detecting paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) in patients with ischemic strokes presenting in sinus rhythm is challenging because these PAF episodes are often short, occur randomly, and are frequently asymptomatic. Limited data are available on the incidence of undiagnosed PAF among Asian stroke patients. Our preliminary data reveal a high incidence of undiagnosed occult PAF (16%) among stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients in Singapore. These patients were older and have higher levels of pro-brain natriuretic peptide, high-sensitivity troponin T and platelet aggregation defect in the cyclooxygenase-1 pathway. The significance of brief bursts of PAF in relation to recurrent stroke risk is not known. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the incidence of occult PAF and their relationship with recurrent stroke outcomes in a multi ethnic Asian cohort of patients with ischemic stroke and TIA. Our secondary objectives are to investigate biomarker and echocardiographic predictors to improve the detection of AF in stroke/TIA patients. We hypothesize that occult PAF is under-diagnosed in Asian stroke/TIA patients and that the risk of recurrent stroke is higher in patients with a greater burden of AF especially when PAF are detected closer to stroke onset. Our secondary hypothesis is that neuroimaging patterns, vascular biomarkers and echocardiogram features can predict AF detection and stroke recurrence. This study, which transects across several multidisciplinary platforms in stroke neurology, digital health and translational medicine, aims to deliver key data on the burden of undiagnosed PAF and unlock the causes of stroke among Asians. Data derived from this study will provide critical insights on the biology of AF and stroke, and guide targeted screening of high-risk stroke patients for undiagnosed PAF.

title: A united airway approach in patients with asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis: identifying inflammatory endotypes to aid personalised management
abs: Background: Asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) with or without nasal polyps (NP) affects more than 300 million people worldwide. Their prevalence is rising, along with significant disease burden and costs. Data suggest that there is significant interaction between the two diseases, leading to increased disease burden. Asian patients with CRS have more T1-driven neutrophilic inflammation compared to Caucasians. Hence we need to study the immunopathologic mechanisms of severe airway disease in Asians, to identify new disease targets and treatment options. Specific aims: We will adopt a ôunited airway endotyping approachö to (1) determine the true prevalence of patients with uncontrolled, co-existing asthma with CRS, (2) identify specific inflammatory endotypes across the different disease combinations and severity, (3) to use the inflammatory endotype to guide personalised treatment, and assess the impact of this approach on clinical and healthcare utilization outcomes.Approach: A prospective prevalence study. We will screen for and target 4 groups with uncontrolled combined airway disease (a) severe asthma (SA) with CRSwNP (b) SA with mild/moderate CRS (c) mild/moderate asthma with CRSwNP (d) mild/moderate asthma and CRS. Disease control and severity is based on validated scores. Inflammatory endotypes are quantified by nasal and sputum eosinophil/ neutrophil cell counts, immunofluorescence for ciliary dysfunction and T2/T1/T17 cytokines measurements. Patients will be followed up longitudinally over 1 year to assess the impact of endotype-guided treatment compared to a historical control (case-matched) on clinical outcomes (asthma control, quality of life, exacerbations) and healthcare utilization (medication usage, clinic visits, sick leave, hospitalization, treatment costs).Significance/ Strengths: Our multidisciplinary team will identify specific inflammatory endotypes in Asians, that can be used to guide targeted treatment. This might lead to discovery and development of new predictive biomarkers and disease targets. This might guide and change workflow practice, leading to better clinical outcomes and cost savings.
