title: Three-dimensional imaging in ex vivo skin and non-invasive skin imaging: novel clinical applications in skin cancers and hypohidrotic sweat disorders
abs: The aims of the project are to establish platforms for 3-dimensional visualization and data analysis in ex vivo skin and non-invasive bedside imaging to improve the diagnosis and management of dermatological disorders. This is to improve upon the current practice of 2-dimensional analyses in histology and imaging, which are prone to sampling error and are deficient in information on tissue architecture, structure and cellular interaction. These techniques will be validated and applied to skin cancer and hypohidrotic sweat disorders, respectively, to evaluate their clinical utility. These platforms can be expanded to other diseases in the future. Our hypothesis is that such novel approaches will significantly improve the understanding of pathology and accuracy of diagnosis of these important diseases and thereby enhance patient management outcomes. In the first component of the project, we aim to develop the technique of 3D whole-tissue histology in human skin cancers through the processes of optical clearance, immunofluorescence staining and 3D imaging. Subsequently, we will evaluate the effectiveness of the technique in determining surgical margin clearance, subtype of cancer, and the presence of high-risk malignancy features of nerve and blood vessel invasion. We hypothesize that 3D whole-tissue histology is significantly more accurate than conventional histology in the evaluation of these features, which are crucial in the management of skin cancers. In the second component of the project, we aim to develop a clinical software platform for 3D and automated analyses in a non-invasive imaging modality, the Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT). We will validate its accuracy and subsequently evaluate its clinical utility in hypohidrotic sweat disorders, a potentially-fatal condition of particular relevance to Singapore. The software platform will first build the OCT images 3-dimensionally and enable such a 3D volume to be digitally sectioned and segmented into the various skin layers. Clinical- and research-relevant information that will be provided in a visual and quantitative manner consists of skin surface topography, epidermal thickness and dermal composition. Subsequently, automated identification of certain skin structures will be performed by the software, and this project will focus on identifying normal and pathologically-blocked sweat ducts. We envision this platform in non-invasive imaging to be an important adjunct to clinical and research practices, in particular, hypohidrotic sweat disorders.

title: Developing chromosomal 1q21.3 amplification as a circulating biomarker and actionable target for monitoring and treating breast cancer recurrence
abs: Despite advances in therapies for breast cancer, many patients still develop recurrence and die of metastasis years after treatment. Distant recurrence is often diagnosed late when symptoms arise, by which time the disease is no longer curable. There is a pressing unmet clinic need to develop non invasive diagnostics such as cell free DNA assay to monitor disease status so that tumor recurrence can be detected and treated earlier to improve the patient’s survival outcomes. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that treatment resistance and metastasis are attributed to the distinct and rare, aggressive subpopulation of cancer cells, known as tumor-initiating cells (TICs). Using an integrated genomics approach, we have identified a chromosomal region, chr1q21.3, to be amplified in patient’s breast tumor sphere populations and this gene amplification event is highly enriched inup to 75% of recurrent tumors, in both ER positive and ER negative tumors. We have designed a plasma cell free DNA assay to detect the chr1q21.3 amplification using digital PCR and this cfDNA assay is able to identify the breast tumor chr1q21.3 amplification with high sensitivity and specificity, and is able to predict relapse in patients with both early and late stage tumors. Importantly, we show that ch1q21.3 consists of important genes linked to signaling pathways crucial for metastasis, chemoresistance and tumor recurrence. In this proposal, we aim to develop further our cfDNA assay to increase the sensitivity for detecting disease recurrence and pursue more clinical validation in both retrospective and prospective studies. Also, we seek to investigate the functional role of chr1q21.3 amplication in tumor recurrence and chemoresistance and to develop a therapeutic strategy to target chr1q21.3-amplified tumors. Our ultimate goal is to develop both diagnostic and therapeutic solutions to target tumor recurrence, which we hope will provide a true clinical benefit to improve patients’ survival.
kw: Breast cancer, liquid biopsy, gene amplification, cell free DNA, tumor recurrence, therapeutics

title: The role of human fetal antigen presenting cells in tolerance and immunity
abs: Intra-uterine stem cell therapies are potentially curative treatments for inherited genetic disorders such as haemoglobinopathies, but currently limited by immune-rejection . A key challenge is to determine a window-of-opportunity that will allow graft tolerance, which is linked intimately with the developing immune system and its functional competence. Antigen presenting cells (APCs) such as dendritic cells and macrophages are critical regulators of immune system, responsible for both self-tolerance directing immune responses. Recently, we defined the temporal and spatial development of APCs during early fetal development and started to address their role in regulating tolerance and immunity. We have now shown that fetal APCs exert a critical role in mediating immunological tolerance and inhibiting T-cell activation through a unique metabolic pathway involving arginine availability. Our aim is to extend our characterization of the fetal immune system and precisely map the development of all immune cells. We will focus on fetal tissue-resident T cells to establish their unique functional properties. Extending our finding on fetal DC immunosuppressive state mediated by Arginase-2, we will investigate how metabolic pathways modulate immune cell differentiation and functions. Firstly, we will first generate a fetal immune atlas through the integration of index sorting single-cell RNAseq and CyTOF analyses, and obtaining combined gene and protein expression analyses to identify novel markers, cytokine and growth factor requirements that will predict their functional specialisations. Secondly, we will characterize fetal immune metabolism through mass-spectrometry, and study how it modulates fetal immunity through in vitro studies to determine activatory/suppressive effects and precursor potential.Detailed understanding of the establishment of the fetal immune system and how fetal APCs exert tolerogenic and immunogenic effects will allow us to develop better strategies for prenatal transplantation, reveal the mechanisms underlying fetal susceptibility to infections and feto-maternal tolerance, and form the basic foundation for future APCs-based immunotherapies.

title: Needs assessment of HIV self-testing amongst high-risk MSM and heterosexual men in Singapore: a mixed-methods study
abs: HIV/AIDS remains an important public health concern in Singapore, and despite ongoing efforts to encourage populations at risk to undergo regular testing, a significant proportion of incident HIV infection is diagnosed at a late stage. In this project, we hypothesized that rapid result HIV self-testing (HIVST) has the potential to reduce barriers to HIV testing. To understand how to implement an effective HIVST intervention and improve testing rates among high-risk men in Singapore, we are proposing a mixed-methods study to understand the needs for HIVST amongst high-risk men-having-sex-with-men (MSM) and heterosexual men (HSM) and also gather relevant perspectives from other stakeholders in the healthcare and non-governmental sectors. The study has the following specific aims: a) to elucidate barriers and facilitators to and delivery preferences for HIVST among high-risk MSM and HSM through qualitative in-depth interviews; b) to gather perspectives on feasibility and implementation preferences among other stakeholders in the healthcare and non-governmental sectors through focus group discussions; c) to assess the knowledge, attitudes and uptake (KAP) of HIVST among high-risk men through a quantitative survey which includes a discrete choice experiment (DCE) to elicit preferred choices of interventions. The mixed-methods approach applies both the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to explore with all stakeholders the various constructs required for effective implementation of HIVST and the Health Belief Model (HBM) to help assess perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits and barriers and understand cues of action. Key outcome of this study is to obtain evidence-based information on how to develop and implement an effective HIVST intervention in Singapore in hope of improving testing rates among high-risk men.

title: Assessing the impact of enhanced primary care services for people with chronic conditions in Singapore
abs: The overarching objective of this research program is to examine how the primary care system in Singapore can be best enhanced to meet the challenges presented by rapid demographic shifts. Singapore is experiencing an ageing population with more chronic conditions, with a consequent increased demands on the healthcare system, especially on high cost hospital services. A promising solution is to balance existing acute care capabilities with an enhanced primary care sector. However, it is unclear whether such an effort will significantly alleviate system stress, improve outcomes, and be sustainable in the Singapore context. Because this objective is difficult to address through conventional research designs, we approach the challenge using a simulation model linked to new and existing data sources. The model will represent the dynamic phenomena that promote or inhibit development of enhanced primary care, and will allow stakeholders to engage in in-silico experiments to consider the implications of various policy options. First, we will survey international and local primary care initiatives in order to develop a deep understanding of the scope to improve chronic care delivery. This will include a systematic literature review of models of care, as well as case studies of chronic care projects in Singapore and abroad. Second, insights will be represented in a conceptual model developed with stakeholders that will serve as the framework for guiding further work, including data collection, simulation and analysis. Third, we will collect and analyse new data to provide key inputs to a simulation model: (1) choice experiments to examine (a) the impact of service characteristics on patient choice of service venue, and (b) the willingness of providers to treat patients with service needs as well as to participate in alternative practice structures; and (2) a population survey to estimate the prevalence and incidence of categories of health needs.

title: Investigating paracrine STAT3 signalling in colorectal peritoneal carcinomatosis to derive novel therapeutic strategies
abs: Peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC) is a common form of metastasis confined to the abdominal cavity in 15% of colorectal cancer patients. Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) for PC capitalizes on radical surgery coupled with the use of intraperitoneal chemotherapeutic agents to eliminate microscopic disease. Following the introduction of CRS and HIPEC 20 years ago, outcomes for patients with PC have improved greatly although most patients will continue to recur within the abdominal cavity and die of local complications. Current models propose that paracrine signalling plays a key role in promoting PC but the exact mechanisms are unclear. Using unbiased gene expression profiling of colorectal cancer cell lines treated with cell-free ascites collected from patients with colorectal PC, we have identified STAT3 activation as a key signalling pathway in promoting PC in vitro and in vivo. We have also successfully established a novel mouse model of colorectal PC dependent on paracrine signalling activated by ascites. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesized that aberrant STAT3 activation plays a key role in colorectal PC and could be therapeutically relevant in a large number of clinical situations including neo-adjuvant, intra-operative, adjuvant and prophylactic settings.Our specific aims are: 1)To determine the role of paracrine signalling including STAT3 activation in PC2)To identify the factors inducing STAT3 activation in PC cells 3)To determine the prognostic significance of STAT3 activation in PC Being one of the few clinical groups to perform CRS and HIPEC in Asia, we plan to capitalize on the advantage of having one of the largest wealth of clinical experience and patient load to interrogate the underlying biology of colorectal PC in the area of paracrine signalling. This could potentially change the standard of care of patients with colorectal PC.

title: RolE of ARNI in VEntricular Remodeling in HypertenSivE LVH (REVERSE-LVH)
abs: In Singapore, one in every two adults in their 60s has hypertension and consequently at risk of hypertensive heart disease, a leading cause of heart failure and cardiovascular death. Currently, management of hypertension relies primarily on achieving peripheral blood pressure targets. However, optimal blood pressure targets are controversial. Given the inherent limitations of peripheral blood pressure measurement and management, a more reliable marker is needed not only for drug development, but also to monitor progression and drug response in individuals with hypertensive heart disease. Consequent to the increased afterload from hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) occurs as an adaptive response to maintain wall stress and cardiac output. Ultimately, this initially compensatory response fosters evolution to heart failure as a result of myocyte death and myocardial fibrosis. REMODEL is an ongoing observational study that aims to establish the determinants of cardiac fibrosis in hypertension. All participants recruited have no prior history of heart failure, myocardial infarction or other cardiovascular target organ events. The registry contains the highest quality baseline data including 24-hour continuous ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, comprehensive cardiac and aortic phenotyping with cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging and tonometry and a biobank of frozen serum and DNA samples. The current proposal, REVERSE-LVH (RolE of ARNI in VEntricular Remodeling in HypertenSivE LVH), is an extension of REMODEL that aims to assess, for the first time, the potential of a anti-hypertensive and anti-heart failure agent (valsartan/sacubitril combination) with anti-fibrotic properties in hypertensive LVH using state-of-the-art cardiac imaging by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. A total of 200 patients with hypertension and LVH will be randomized to valsartan/sacubitril combination or to valsartan alone. The primary endpoint is regression of myocardial fibrosis volume after 1 year of treatment. REVERSE-LVH will advance knowledge regarding the pathophysiology of myocardial response to hypertension and test a treatment strategy of targeting the myocardium rather than blood pressure.

title: OPTIMISING THE ASSESSMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE IN GLAUCOMA USING ITEM BANK AND COMPUTER ADAPTIVE TESTING SYSTEMS
abs: Glaucoma is a common and potentially blinding eye condition, disproportionately affecting Asians. Patients with glaucoma have increased risk of falls, and reduced visual functioning, mobility and independence and emotional well-being. Understanding the impact of health conditions and the effectiveness of treatment therapies from the patient’s perspective is becoming increasingly important, and patient-reported outcomes data is becoming essential to guide clinical care, support patient-provider decision-making, and for practice improvement, performance evaluation of organizations, and as a metric for value-based payments. While several questionnaires exist to measure glaucoma-related quality of life (QoL), modern psychometric methods have revealed serious psychometric short-comings with these instruments. Moreover, current questionnaires in ophthalmology are paper-pencil based, meaning they are static, inflexible, burdensome to administer and answer. Fortunately, item banking and computer adaptive testing (CAT) provide a solution to these problems. An item bank is a large pool of questions calibrated on the same linear scale using item response theory. Item banks are operationalized by CAT, which is ‘smart’ technology that adapts the items asked based on participants’ responses to previous items. CAT minimizes measurement error and reduces test length without loss of precision and reliability. Evidently, a comprehensive, culturally valid and precise instrument is urgently required to assess the impact of glaucoma and efficacy of related treatments from the patient’s perspective in Asia. Fortunately, pioneering work in this area has commenced. PI Fenwick has created 300 glaucoma-specific items housed within 12 QoL domains, globally referred to as GLIBQoLS (GLaucoma Item Banks for Quality of Life in Singapore). The validity, efficiency and clinical applicability of GLIBQoLS are now ready to be assessed, resulting in a valuable, highly sought after instrument for use by ophthalmologists, researchers, healthcare organizations and policy planners. Therefore, the objective of this proposal is to psychometrically and clinically validate GLIBQoLS in Singaporean patients with glaucoma.

title: Role of non-canonical NF-kB signaling in the transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming of malignant cancers
abs: Deregulation of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway has been causally linked to many diseases including cancer. However, how it regulates gene expression programs in malignant cancers through non-coding, cis-regulatory DNA and chromatin interactions remains uncharacterized. The primary objective of this proposal is to elucidate how altered cis-regulatory elements during aberrant non-canonical NF-κB signaling drive transcriptional programs of malignant cancers. Using multiple myeloma and B-cell lymphomas which display constitutive non-canonical NF-κB activity as disease models of study, we aim to (1) investigate how new transcription factor binding partners bind cooperatively at cis-regulatory elements, (2) identify key enhancer RNAs (eRNAs) which regulate transcriptional programs that drive the malignant progression of these cancers and (3) characterize chromatin interactions underscoring these cancer-activating cis-regulatory elements as well as validate the functional impact of targeting their regulators. We postulate that aberrant non-canonical NF-κB activation results in novel transcription factor interacting partners and activates a specific subset of non-coding, eRNAs which regulate transcriptional programs that are critical for the malignant transformation of cancer cells. We will perform NF-κB2 chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) coupled with RNA-seq analyses to examine the genome-wide cooperativity between non-canonical NF-κB and new transcription factor interacting partners and to identify an eRNA signature associated with malignant cancer progression. Causal cis-regulatory elements identified will subsequently be examined in circular chromosome conformation capture (4C)-seq studies to characterize cancer-activating chromatin interactions regulated by non-canonical NF-κB signaling. The proposed research will address the role of altered cis-regulatory elements as potential cancer biomarkers and identify key epigenetic regulators which can be putatively targeted for future cancer therapy. The approach of using disease-associated eRNA signatures can also be applied to discover more sensitive biomarkers of other cancers or disease types. Hence, this research has important clinical implications in the future prognosis and treatment of cancers as well as other human diseases.

title: Sex Chromosome Aneuploidy associated infertility: A paradigm for investigating the determinants of germ cell 'identity'
abs: Sex chromosome complement underpins fundamental biological differences in sex and sex-linked diseases. Sex chromosome aneuploidy syndromes, which include Klinefelter (XXY), Double-Y (XYY) and Turner (XO) syndrome form the largest class of aneuploidies in humans, and these are associated with germ cell loss and infertility. It is traditionally accepted that the gonadal environment determines germ cell transcriptional "identity". We have shown that sex chromosome complement of germ cells can also influence their identity. During genome-wide reprogramming, female germ cells undergo X chromosome reactivation and demethylate the genome to a level that is lower than that in males. Our findings also reveal that female and male germ cells show differential gene expression from early stages in development - between embryonic day (E)9.5 and 11.5. This time period overlaps with X chromosome reactivation in females and precedes gonadal sexdetermination. Analysis of sex chromosome aneuploid mouse germ cells reveals a "sex-reversed" pattern of gene expression and X-dosage. The mismatch between number of X chromosomes and gonadal sex may be causal in germ cell loss in sex chromosome infertility. An in-depth analysis of germ cell transcriptional identity is lacking, and a number of issues remain unresolved: - Contributions from the gonadal 'milieu' versus sex chromosome complement, in influencing germ cell transcription profiles are relatively unknown. • Ontogeny of X-reactivation in the mammalian germ line is poorly understood. • Influence of X dosage on germ cell DNA methylation dynamics have not been studied. • Transcription and methylation analysis of human Klinefelter and Turner syndrome germ cells has not been performed. We aim to answer these questions by generating high-resolution expression and epigenetic maps of germ cells through a combination of approaches (e.g. incorporating sex chromosome aneuploid mouse models, RNA-, bisulphite- and ChIP-sequencing). This analysis will inform the management of patients with sex chromosome aneuploidy syndromes and infertility in general.
kw: sex chromosome aneuploidy, infertility, germ cells, dosage compensation, next generation sequencing

title: Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Discovery in EGFR mutant NSCLC and Nasopharyngeal Cancer
abs: Immunotherapy using immune checkpoint inhibitors has entered mainstream anti-cancer therapeutics in 2015 and has gained approval in the palliative setting in a growing list of solid tumors since then. The current global goal is to improve further upon the results of single agent anti-PD1/PDL1 with different combination regimens in the bid to improve both response rates and durability of response. Despite the global pace of development of this class of drugs in solid tumors, data of efficacy is relatively lacking in Asia-centric cancers such as EGFR mutant (EGFRm) NSLCLC. This BMS-backed IIT aims to determine the level of efficacy of the combination of nivolumab and ipilimumab in EGFRm NSCLC. In addition, this study aims to determine factors that can predict for response and survival benefit to help improve selection of future patients for such therapies. This is a randomised phase 2 study of nivolumab versus nivolumab-ipilimumab combination in patients with advanced EGFRm NSCLC who failed standard EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Blood and tumor biospecimens will be procured at base-line and during the course of study treatment to help determine predictive and prognostic biomarkers of benefit with the use of these therapies.
kw: EGFR mutant NSCLC, NPC, nivolumab, ipilimumab

title: First in Human, Single Ascending Dose Study of Ty008 in Zika Virus Infected Patients
abs: Zika virus (ZIKV) has emerged to become a major global health concern. Generally a mild disease, the greatest concern of Aedes-borne ZIKV is the risk of congenital infection that result in fetal malformation, such as microcephaly. Vector control alone is unlikely to sustainably prevent ZIKV transmission as ZIKV causes chronic infection of the urinary tract and reproductive organs leading to person-to-person sexual transmission. Vaccine development is likely to face the same challenges as dengue vaccine with studies showing that ZIKV is susceptible to antibody-dependent enhancement of infection (ADE). A therapeutic that can reduce the risk of chronic or congenital infection would significantly reduce global Zika burden and the life-long impact of congenital infection.Several studies have explored the potential of drug repurposing to address antiviral therapeutic gap against ZIKV. While such drugs have the potential to reduce the viral burden, it is unclear what degree of antiviral effects they would have on the fetus. Conversely, IgG1 antibodies are actively transported across the placenta via neonatal Fc receptor (FcRN). Human IgG1 antibody thus have the potential to be therapeutic in both mother and fetus.To address the challenge of emerging infections including ZIKV, Tychan Pte Ltd is establishing a framework for rapid response. Two key components of this framework are: (1) Developing an integrated platform for rapid production of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs); (2) Integrating safety and efficacy testing with the manufacturing process. In this context, Tychan has rapidly produced a therapeutic antibody (TY008) that shows remarkable in vitro ZIKV neutralizing activity and in vivo anti-ZIKV efficacy. The goal of this proposal is to examine the potential of TY008 in preventing congenital malformation and demonstrate safety in non-clinical studies while, simultaneously, defining the safety and efficacy of TY008 in reducing viremia in a phase 1/1b clinical trial in Singapore.

title: Case Control Nigrosome-1 and Connectivity MRI Study in Parkinson’s-Linked Asian LRRK2 Gene Carriers
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: BackgroundParkinson’s disease (PD) patients show dopaminergic denervation in the substantia nigra (SN), with maximum cell depletion in nigrosome-1. There is growing evidence of excellent diagnostic accuracy of 3D high resolution susceptibility-weighted MR imaging (HRSWI) at 3T in radiologically delineating the healthy nigrosome-1. Recent functional connectivity studies (rsfMRI) show abnormalities in preclinical PD stages. We have previously identified common Asian-specific leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) gene risk variants in Chinese PD patients, with accelerated motor progression compared to non-carrier patients, suggesting that these genetic risk variants may facilitate neurodegeneration.Specific AimsUtilizing a case control methodology, we will establish clinical utility of 3T nigrosome-1 HRSWI in a large PD cohort compared to controls, and evaluate if quantitative grading of nigrosome-1 signal intensity correlate with motor scores and connectivity abnormalities, and differentiate asymptomatic Asian genetic carriers of LRRK2 variants from noncarriers.HypothesesWe hypothesize that loss of nigrosome-1 will accurately differentiate PD from controls, correlate with motor grading and connectivity abnormalities, and differentiate asymptomatic Asian genetic carriers of LRRK2 variants from non-carriers.Methodology & Approach300 subjects will be screened and 200 subjects (100 PD, 100 controls) recruited. All subjects will have genotyping for Asian specific LRRK2 gene variants, clinical evaluation with the Hoehn and Yahr and Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale, and undergo HRSWI optimized for nigrosome-1 detection in the midbrain and rsfMRI. Two blinded neuroradiologists will visually grade the nigrosome-1, and inter-rater agreement assessed. Loss of nigrosome-1 signal intensity against other parts of the SN will be quantified through voxel intensity ratio from regions-of-interests measurements. Functional motor neural network modulations will be extracted from rsfMRI.Clinical SignificanceNigrosome-1 imaging is an attractive, practical radiological biomarker for PD, with potential utility as a surrogate quantitative biomarker in disease progression, preclinical/prodromal genetic carriers and in correlation with abnormalities on functional connectivity.
kw: Parkinson disease; Gene Carriers; Neuroimaging; MRI; Brain

title: Developing and testing a cancer-specific, local health preference-based utility instrument for cost-effectiveness analysis in Singapore
abs: This research project aims to develop a localized utility instrument for cost-effectiveness analysis of cancer treatments The specific aims are: 1) to develop an algorithm for the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer’s Quality of Life Utility Measure-Core 10 Dimensions (QLU-C10D) instrument, based on the health preferences of Singaporeans (primary objective); and 2) to assess the psychometric properties of the new utility measure. We hypothesize that members of the local public can discriminate and value different health problems related to cancers and treatments, and that the QLU-C10D score generated using the local scoring algorithm is valid, reliable and more sensitive and responsive than the generic EQ-5D-5L score in local cancer patients. The first study aim will be accomplished by conducting a cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey of 700 members of the general public to elicit their health preferences. The survey will be a discrete choice experiment (DCE) asking respondents to choose between health profiles differing in health state and survival time. Modeling analysis will be performed to estimate a function for predicting the utility value of each QLU-C10D defined health state. The second study aim will be achieved by a survey of 350 cancer patients from the National Cancer Centre Singapore (NCCS) to assess their health outcomes using the QLQ-C30 (from which the QLU-C10D descriptive system is developed) and EQ-5D-5L questionnaires. The QLU-C10D score will be calculated using the local scoring function and its construct validity and test-retest reliability will be assessed and sensitivity and responsiveness compared with those of the EQ-5D-5L score. The new utility measure will contribute to the local health services research aiming to improve services provision and outcomes for cancer patients.

title: A Multi-Site Randomized Controlled Trial of a Stepped-Care Intervention for Emergency Department Patients with Panic Attacks and Panic Disorder
abs: Panic disorder is a chronic and disabling psychiatric disorder that is characterized by recurrent panic attacks. Results from our previous studies indicate that up to 50% of Accident and Emergency (A&E) patients with chest pain meet the criteria for panic-related anxiety, but fewer than 1% are currently diagnosed or treated in the local A&E. A stepped-care model, which focuses on providing evidence-based interventions in a resource-efficient manner, is the state-of-the art for treating panic patients in medical settings such as primary care. Stepped-care has not been previously implemented in the A&E setting. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) aims to evaluate the clinical, patient-centered, and economic effectiveness of a stepped-care intervention for patients with panic-related anxiety presenting to the A&E in Singapore’s largest public hospital. The three-year study will follow a two-stage parallel group RCT design with two arms: 1) an enhanced care pathway consisting of a stepped-care intervention for panic attacks and panic disorder; and 2) a control arm consisting of screening for panic attacks and panic disorder in the A&E and discharge. We will randomize 212 patients recruited from the Singapore General Hospital A&E. Screening will be done at the first stage, followed by baseline assessments and blocked randomization in a 1:1 ratio for patients with a confirmed diagnosis of panic attack or panic disorder at the second stage. Masked follow-up assessments will be conducted at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Clinical outcomes will be panic symptom severity and rates of panic disorder. Patient-centered outcomes will be health-related quality of life, daily functioning, psychiatric comorbidity, and health services utilization. Economic effectiveness outcomes will be the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of the stepped-care intervention relative to screening alone. The study results will be used to recommend the most cost-effective and clinically meaningful strategy for treating panic patients in the A&E.
kw: panic attacks, panic disorder, stepped-care, cost-effectiveness

title: A phase I Investigator Sponsored Trial of Selinexor (KPT-330), a Selective Inhibitor of Nuclear Export / SINE™ Compound and ifosfamide, carboplatin, etoposide (ICE) in patients with relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma
abs: Treatment outcomes for patients with peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) are poor with conventional chemotherapy regimens. Second line regimens such as ICE (ifosfamide, carboplatin, etoposide) are administered with the goal of cytoreduction occasionally prior to stem cell transplantation (SCT) however many patients do not achieve a response. Novel therapeutic strategies are needed. Selinexor is a selective inhibitor of nuclear export which has shown pre-clinical activity in T-cell lymphomas and has been shows in vitro to sensitise cells to topoisomerase II inhibitors such as etoposide. We hypothesize that the combination of selinexor and ICE will be safe and effective in inducing responses in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) PTCL. We propose a phase I study with the primary objective to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of selinexor when given in combination with ICE in patients with R/R PTCL. Secondary objectives include assessing response rates, progression-free survival, overall survival and feasibility of stem cell collection after selinexor-ICE. This will be a single centre, phase I study with a standard “3+3” design. Selinexor will be orally administered on days 3, 5 and 7 of each chemotherapy cycle and ICE will be administered on days 1-3. Three dose levels (DL) of selinexor will be tested; 40mg, 60mg and 80mg. Three patients will be recruited onto DL1 and if no cycle 1 dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) are observed, dose escalation will continue to the next higher DL. If 1/3 DLT is observed then 3 additional patients will be enrolled in the same DL. If no DLT is observed from the additional 3 patients, then dose escalation will continue. If any DLT is observed from the additional 3 patients, then the previous lower dose will be chosen as the MTD. Patients will receive 2 to 6 cycles of selinexor and ICE and SCT if eligible.
kw: lymphoma, chemotherapy, phase I

title: Fundamental Performance Limits for Statistical Learning Algorithms
abs: It is a well-known that no object can travel faster than the speed of light c. In other words, c is a fundamental limit. The aim of my research program also concerns fundamental limits. However, it is positioned to answer the following question that is salient today's data-rich environment: Can one systematically derive fundamental achievability and impossibility results for the performances of various statistical machine learning tasks? While many of the state-of-the-art algorithms perform reasonably well in practice, one aspect that researchers have neglected is the derivation of fundamental performance limits, without regard to computational complexity considerations. While c is not attainable in the design of vehicles, our research program aims to show that the performances of some machine learning tasks can come close to their ultimate limit. The specific aims I will focus on are as follows: Develop fundamental performance limits for 1. Learning rankings and hidden communities; 2. Assessing the classification and generalization performances of deep belief networks; 3. Dictionary learning and sparse coding; and 4. Inference in the presence of privacy and security requirements. The techniques used will primarily be information-theoretic (IT) in nature. This allows us to establish of achievability and impossibility results in the absence of computational complexity requirements. The research program has the potential to revolutionize the way data scientists think about approaching statistical machine learning problems. Just as the Shannon limit in information theory has guided the design of communication systems, the research agenda here will guide the design of machine learning algorithms. Today, time-consuming parameter tuning for training deep neural networks has led to astounding improvements in object classification. If impossibility bounds are available, practitioners gain crucial intuition on how to improve algorithms. Our research program will firmly place Singapore on the world map in its quest to be a BigData hub.
kw: Machine learning;Information theory;Dictionary learning and matrix factorization;Deep learning;Learning rankings and permutations;Privacy and security

title: Analytics for Dynamic Urban Risk and Disaster Impact Modeling
abs: The ability of our cities to thrive in the face of uncertain future risks will depend on our ability to predict the consequences of such disasters so that we can mitigate them, and our capacity to effectively respond and recover from them when they occur. The proposed research addresses this dual challenge: (1) The risk profile of many Asian cities is rapidly changing due to climate change, urbanisation, and new patterns of vulnerability. The development of large-scale risk analysis models that can account for such dynamics will enable us to anticipate future trends in risk and guide our cities towards a resilient trajectory. This will be accomplished by creating and integrating nested models for dynamic hazard, dynamic exposure and dynamic vulnerability. Multi-level agent-based modelling, remote-sensing and machine learning techniques will be used to develop urban-scale dynamic risk simulations applicable to a broad range of cities and hazards. This represents significant advancements in probabilistic risk analysis and is expected to lead to new methods for the analysis and design of resilient infrastructure systems, financial protection (insurance) products, and policy decision-support tools. (2) In the immediate aftermath of a disaster, the first estimates of overall impact are based on an ad-hoc combination of predictive models, fly-over reconnaissance missions and field reports. The proposed work focuses on the integration of predictive models with new “big-data” streams such as satellites, distributed sensors, drones and crowd-sensing, in order to get disaster impact estimates with greatly increased accuracy and precision. New approaches for model-based machine learning, geostatics and Bayesian statistics will be used to analyse and transform these data into effective decision-support tools for disaster response and recovery planning. This second research component is linked to the first, since it is through the study of post-disaster consequences that new indicators of pre-disaster vulnerability can be identified.
kw: Disaster risk modeling;Probabilistic risk analysis;System reliability;Machine Learning;Remote Sensing;Geostatistics

title: Exploring the inflammatory signatures underlying progression of knee osteoarthritis: A prospective study
abs: Background. Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of disability; however, treatment is palliative. No drugs have demonstrated adequate symptoms and disease modification due to two main reasons: 1) poor understanding of the pathogenesis; 2) failure to consider OA as a heterogeneous disease. Inflammation plays important roles in the pathogenesis of OA, and patients with an inflammatory phenotype of knee OA may have better response to anti-inflammatory treatments. Further unravelling the mechanistic pathways underlying the inflammation in OA will inform of how to phenotype. Aim. We aim to build on the longitudinal follow-up of an existing cohort of patients with early knee OA to recognize and differentiate inflammatory phenotypes of OA, who are at faster rate of structural progression. Methods. To follow-up at a 4-year time point, on 139 patients with frequent knee pain who have given detailed symptoms, and knee imaging (radiography, and magnetic resonance imaging) at baseline. Live peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), serum, urine and synovial fluid at baseline were collected. At follow-up, patients will be invited for clinical data, biological samples, radiographs and MRI. Structural progression will be defined by validated radiographic and MRI criteria. We will evaluate the association of pro-inflammatory biomarkers with structural progression. We will explore the immunological signatures in defining inflammatory phenotypes of knee OA that may lead to progression. We will use an agnostic approach starting with RNA sequencing of the cell pellet from synovial aspirate, followed by targeted single cell mass cytometry in peripheral blood, and comparison on immune cell subsets on individual basis. We will also explore metabolic pathways that may explain OA pathogenesis. Clinical Significance. This project will provide insight knowledge of knee OA in terms of underlying inflammatory pathological processes, associated biomarkers, and potential targeted therapies. New knowledge may offer individualized therapeutic approach for success in clinical trial to treat subgroups of OA patients with specific inflammatory markers.
kw: Knee Osteoarthritis, inflammation, progression

title: Novel device for transdermal delivery of triamcinolone in the treatment of nail psoriasis: A randomized intra-patient left-to-right study.
abs: The purpose of this study is to evaluate treatment response of psoriaticnails following treatment with a microneedle drug delivery device toadminister topical steroids compared to conventional topical steroidapplication.It is hypothesized that topical steroid application via amicroneedle drug delivery device may have superior treatment effectscompared to conventional topical steroid application with no increasedadverse effects. This is a 4-month, prospective, randomized controlledtrial to evaluate treatment response of nail psoriasis following treatmentwith a self-dissolving microneedle drug delivery patch to administertopical steroids to psoriatic nails. Affected psoriatic nails from subjectswill be randomized to receive microneedle device delivered topicalsteroids on one hand and control treatment (topical Daivobet® gel) onthe other hand. Daivobet® gel is currently the standard topical treatmentrecommended as initial topical treatment of psoriatic nails. The studyparticipants will be randomly assigned to two groups in a 1:1 ratio. Onegroup will receive drug delivery patch on their right hand and controltreatment on their left hand while the other group will receive drugdelivery patch on their left hand and control treatment on their right hand.The Nail Psoriasis Severity Index (NAPSI) scoring will be administeredby two independent dermatologists blinded to the treatment assignmentat baseline and follow-up visits (2-month and 4-month visits). AverageNAPSI nail score of the affected nails on each hand will be analyzed.This is calculated from the total NAPSI nail score of psoriasis-affectednails divided by the number of affected nails. Other clinical informationsuch as Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI), Dermatology Life QualityIndex (DLQI) and Nail Psoriasis Quality of life 10 (NPQ10) will also bemeasured at baseline and follow-up visits.
