title: Earlier Assessment of RheumatoLogical diseases to ImprovE Recognition and outcomes (EARLIER)) Study
abs: Background: Connective tissue diseases (CTDs) have a disproportionately large disease burden despite their low prevalence. Rheumatoid arthritis and “other musculoskeletal diseases” account for 55 and 410 per 100,000 years lost to disability (YLD) worldwide. Taken together their disease burden exceeds that of asthma, ischemic heart disease, tuberculosis, or HIV/AIDS. Despite this heavy disease burden, the diagnosis and treatment of CTDs have not received as much attention as other disabling conditions. This may partly be due to the low of prevalence of CTDs, and the protean manifestations that make them difficult to diagnose. This is unfortunate as early diagnosis, which leads to early treatment within a “window of opportunity” in the first months of symptom onset, has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with CTDs.To address this gap, this study aims to:1. Cross-culturally adapt 2 validated questionnaires that screen for CTDs:• The “Connective Tissue Disease Screening Questionnaire” (CSQ) which screens for the following CTDs: Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Systemic Sclerosis, Sjogren’s Syndrome, Myositis, and Mixed Connective Tissue Diseases• The “Patient Self-Reported Screening Questionnaire for Axial Spondyloarthropathy” which screens for spondyloarthritis (SpA) - henceforth referred to as the Hamilton SpA questionnaire2. Test the diagnostic accuracy of the adapted questionnaires in Singapore3. Develop a shorter questionnaires based on the CSQ and Hamilton SpA questionnaires for use in general population surveysMethods: We will adapt the 2 screening questionnaires for use in Singapore by carrying out a rigorous process of forward and backward translation, expert panel review, and patient cognitive debriefings. We will test the diagnostic accuracy by prospectively administering the crossculturally adapted questionnaire to patients referred from primary care to the Singapore General Hospital for evaluation of possible CTD (n=1,300). We will then develop shorter versions of these questionnaires to be used in the general population.

title: Ultra-protective pulmonary ventilation supported by low flow extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal (ECCO2R) and prone positioning for ARDS; a pilot study (U-Protect study).
abs: Critically ill patients are at increased risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), the most severe form of respiratory failure. While mechanical ventilation is lifesaving, it paradoxically perpetuates underlying pathology, a process described as ventilator induced lung injury (VILI). VILI can be minimised using low tidal volume (6ml/kg predicted body weight) lung protective ventilation (LPV). However, recent evidence suggests volumes lower than 6mls/kg, targeting plateau pressures under 28 cmH2O, maybe more effective. Tidal volumes below 6mls/kg create carbon dioxide (CO2) retention, which can cause raised intracranial pressure, right heart dysfunction, and immune dysfunction. Extracorporeal CO2 removal (ECCO2R) devices are machines that remove CO2 directly from blood, using similar principles to dialysis. Until recently, ECCO2R was only available in a few specialist centres, limiting access for most patients with ARDS and preventing exploration of the full potential. The Prismalung is a new, commercially available low-flow ECCO2R device that can be used in any intensive care unit capable of providing dialysis.We hypothesise that ECCO2R, provided by Prismalung, can support ultra-protective ventilation (1-3ml/kg predicted weight), resulting in plateau pressures (Pplat) consistently below 25 cmH2O, when compared to conventional LPV. Fifty patients with severe ARDS will be recruited and randomized to receive ultra-protective ventilation or conventional lung protective ventilation. All other interventions will be standardized 25 cmH2O in the intervention arm. As a secondary outcome, we will collect blood samples to compare markers of lung injury and inflammation between both arms. Additional secondary outcomes will include, length of stay in ICU, cardiac function, illness severity, sedation use and mortality. We expect to show that ultra-protective ventilation creates lower airway pressures in ARDS, halting progress of VILI, accelerating recovery, and ultimately reducing the overall impact of ARDS.

title: The impact of Zika and other mosquito-borne viral infections on pregnancy outcome: a prospective longitudinal cohort study
abs: Mosquito-borne viral infections (MVIs) are endemic in many countries worldwide, including Singapore, with about 500 million people infected each year, including many women of childbearing age. Yet there is a lack of high quality studies to critically assess their impact on pregnancy. The Zika virus (ZIKV) outbreak in South America, has been associated with microcephaly and adverse pregnancy outcomes, however, the absolute Zika-specific pregnancy risk has not been conclusively quantified. Recently Singapore has documented a sharp rise in local ZIKV transmission with predictions of an ensuing outbreak over the coming 18 months, which represents a unique opportunity for research. Dengue (DENV) and Chikungunya (CHIKV) viral infections are also common in Singapore. The majority of these MVIs are asymptomatic making determination of pregnancy risk even more difficult. Our proposed prospective, longitudinal cohort study with multiple time point measurements across gestation is novel in this field. The study will seek to determine (1) if maternal infection with the South East Asian strain of ZIKV, regardless of symptoms, increases the risk of congenital anomalies including central nervous system malformations, and perinatal demise, (2) if maternal MVIs reduce the chance of an uncomplicated live birth at term and increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth and fetal growth restriction. If this is borne out, reliable testing for these viruses in antenatal care will be needed to guide critical decision making on management, reduce psychological morbidity, patient counselling and to avoid unnecessary intervention. Singapore, with its extensive expertise in MVIs, coupled with an organized antenatal care infrastructure starting from early pregnancy, and local expertise in setting up and running world-class birth cohort studies, is well-placed to lead this field. This study will effectively address current uncertainties surrounding the effect of MVIs on pregnancy, and will have significant worldwide public health impact.

title: Deep Phenotyping and Genetic Landscaping of Primary Open Angle Glaucoma
abs: Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide, with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) being the most prevalent form. The genetic etiology of POAG has not been fully understood, and lowering intraocular pressure is so far the only effective treatment. Recent genome-wide association studies conducted by our group and others have identified several common genetic variants associated with the risk of POAG, but these loci are mostly located in non-coding regions and account for only a small fraction of disease heritability. Our objective is to establish a large-scale DNA biobank for POAG, linking with rich glaucoma functional and structural phenotypic data, to comprehensively characterize the genetic profiles of POAG, in particular protein-changing variants and loss-of-function mutations in the entire genome. We hypothesize that low frequency protein-changing variants could be significant contributors to POAG susceptibility. In this proposed research, we aim 1) to perform deep phenotyping in 800 cases of POAG using state-of-the-art ocular imaging to build up a well-characterized cohorts; 2) to systematically characterize the role of low-frequency coding variants underlying POAG through conducting whole-exome sequencing in 800 POAG cases and controls, followed by a novel integrative analysis of sequencing and genome-wide array data; and 3) to employ systems genomics approaches and trans-ethnic meta-analyses to prioritize disease risk genes and fine-map functional variants. The discovery of protein-changing mutations will revolutionize the field of glaucoma genetics and may lead to the development of genetic tests for high-risk individuals who will benefit from timely interventions to slow the rate of disease progression of disease. Fine-mapping functional variants, followed by future validation experiments may open new avenues for drug targets. This will facilitate precision medicine, tailoring treatment or prevention strategies according to individuals’ unique characteristics in the future.

title: Beyond surviving colorectal cancer: how cancer survivors can influence the attitudes of their family members towards screening and play a role to support those with cancer
abs: AIMSTo determine:1.Screening rates and barriers amongst the first degree relatives (FDRs) and spouses of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and if tailored intervention could increase their adoption of screening modalities 2.Quality of life (QoL) of CRC patients through the first 18 months following their diagnosis3.Feasibility of a survivorship program for CRC survivors to support new CRC patients in their initial stages of treatment to improve their QoL.HYPOTHESES1.Screening rates amongst the FDRs and spouses of patients with CRC are suboptimal and tailored interventions can improve their screening rates.2.Patients with CRC have poor QoL in the earlier stages of their treatment, and their QOL would worsen with additional treatment3.A survivorship program is feasible and may improve the QoL of new CRC patients. METHODOLOGYThe study will be conducted at the various hospitals across Singapore with a recruitment target of 300 patients, 150 spouses and 100 FDRs. All patients with CRC will be approached upon diagnosis and the QoL instruments would be administered at various timepoints over the subsequent 18 months. A randomized trial to contact the FDRs would be performed while spouses would be recruited during the patients’ appointments with oncologists. Barriers towards screening will be ascertained and a randomized trial to determine if tailored interventions targeting cost, and/or logistical barriers would improve their adoption of screening modalities will be performed. Once the QoL of the CRC patients has reached pre-operative levels, they would be invited to join a survivorship program to assist and guide new CRC patients to cope with treatment during the initial phases. SIGNIFICANCE OF THE STUDYThis study will determine what interventions could improve the screening rates amongst the FDRs and Spouses and if CRC survivors could improve the QoL of new CRC patients.

title: Cell Based Therapy in Lung Cancer
abs: Lung cancer is common and lethal, locally and globally. Clinical outcome is typically dismal and new therapies are urgently needed. Immunotherapy is an emerging therapeutic strategy in oncology but has not been explored thoroughly in lung cancer. Natural killer (NK) cells can distinguish neoplastic and normal cells; they can exert direct cytotoxicity against different tumor types and their anti-cancer potential is being tested in clinical trials. The laboratory of Prof. D. Campana at the National University of Singapore has developed unique methods to activate, expand and modify NK cells to increase their anti-tumor capacity. These technologies have been adapted to large-scale conditions that currently support ongoing early phase clinical trials. Our overall objective is to develop novel NK cell based immunotherapies for the most common subtype of lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) by pursuing the following specific aims:1)To test the cytotoxicity of activated, expanded NK cells against NSCLC cell lines in vitro2)To test the cytotoxicity of activated, expanded NK cells against NSCLC cell lines in murine models3)To determine whether NK cell cytotoxicity can be enhanced by monoclonal antibodies and/or small moleculesThe proposed bench work will be done under the direct supervision and mentorship of Prof. D. Campana and in collaboration with investigators in NCCS and in A*STAR. Promising combinations will be developed further in the setting of Phase I clinical trials in patients with advanced cancer.

title: Earlier Assessment of RheumatoLogical diseases to ImprovE Recognition and outcomes (EARLIER)) Study
abs: Background: Connective tissue diseases (CTDs) have a disproportionately large disease burden despite their low prevalence. Rheumatoid arthritis and “other musculoskeletal diseases” account for 55 and 410 per 100,000 years lost to disability (YLD) worldwide. Taken together their disease burden exceeds that of asthma, ischemic heart disease, tuberculosis, or HIV/AIDS. Despite this heavy disease burden, the diagnosis and treatment of CTDs have not received as much attention as other disabling conditions. This may partly be due to the low of prevalence of CTDs, and the protean manifestations that make them difficult to diagnose. This is unfortunate as early diagnosis, which leads to early treatment within a “window of opportunity” in the first months of symptom onset, has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with CTDs. To address this gap, this study aims to:1. Cross-culturally adapt 2 validated questionnaires that screen for CTDs:•The “Connective Tissue Disease Screening Questionnaire” (CSQ) which screens for the following CTDs: Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Systemic Sclerosis, Sjogren’s Syndrome, Myositis, and Mixed Connective Tissue Diseases•The “Patient Self-Reported Screening Questionnaire for Axial Spondyloarthropathy” which screens for spondyloarthritis (SpA) - henceforth referred to as the Hamilton SpA questionnaire2.Test the diagnostic accuracy of the adapted questionnaires in Singapore3.Develop a shorter questionnaires based on the CSQ and Hamilton SpA questionnaires for use in general population surveysMethods: We will adapt the 2 screening questionnaires for use in Singapore by carrying out a rigorous process of forward and backward translation, expert panel review, and patient cognitive debriefings. We will test the diagnostic accuracy by prospectively administering the cross-culturally adapted questionnaire to patients referred from primary care to the Singapore General Hospital for evaluation of possible CTD (n=1,300). We will then develop shorter versions of these questionnaires to be used in the general population.

title: Biological Effects of Olfactory Receptors and Cytokines in Atopic Dermatitis
abs: Background:Egg and cow’s milk (CM) allergies affect up to 3% of all children and evidence shows that many are outgrowing these allergies later in life or not at all. The introduction of highly denatured allergenic proteins in baked egg and milk products into the diets of these children has been shown to alter the course of disease by hastening development of oral tolerance to unheated egg and milk if consumed regularly. A wheat flour food matrix used in baked egg and milk products decreases in vitro antigenic activity to heat-resistant ovomucoid and casein respectively. However a similar tolerance to wheat alternatives such as rice or whey flour has not been observed. Aims (1)To determine the differential antigenic properties of potential wheat alternatives as food matrices for baked milk and egg in vitro(2)To identify suitable wheat alternatives which have a similar matrix effect on egg and cow’s milk proteins during baking that would enable children with a wheat allergy or celiac disease to safely ingest baked egg or baked milk.(3)To identify potential biomarkers which would predict tolerance to various wheat alternatives as food matrices for baked egg and milk MethodsThe antigenic properties of the wheat and wheat alternative baked products will be analysed in vitro using SDS-PAGE immunoblotting, ELISA and IgE immunoblotting techniques. Double blind placebo-controlled oral food challenges with wheat and wheat alternative baked products will then be performed in egg and milk allergic children to determine clinical tolerance. Potential biomarkers for the prediction of oral tolerance will then be identified.ImpactThe identification of suitable safe wheat alternatives as food matrices for baked egg and milk products would be essential in improving the quality of life and nutrition for children with egg and milk allergies, and hasten development of eventual tolerance to both these allergenic foods.

title: OPA1 as a novel therapeutic target for reducing myocardial infarct size and preventing heart failure
abs: Study rationale: Ischaemic heart disease (IHD) and the heart failure that results are the leading causes of death and disability in Singapore and worldwide. As such novel therapies are required to reduce myocardial infarct (MI) size and preserve left ventricular systolic function (LVSF). Mitochondria undergo fission in response to acute ischaemia/reperfusion injury (IRI), and preventing this process can reduce MI size. Here, we investigate whether targeting the mitochondrial fusion protein, OPA1, to inhibit mitochondrial fission, as a novel therapeutic strategy for cardioprotection.Hypothesis: OPA1 is a novel therapeutic target for reducing MI size and preventing heart failure.Objectives and methodology:1.To investigate the effects of genetic and pharmacological modulation of cardiomyocyte OPA1 levels on the susceptibility of the heart to acute IRI. 2.To use Super-Resolution Microscopy and Focused Ion Beam and Array Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy to investigate the effects of modulating cardiomyocyte OPA1 levels on mitochondrial movement and morphology in the adult heart.3.To investigate the effects of modulating cardiomyocyte OPA1 levels on the changes in mitochondrial function and cardiac metabolism which occur in response to acute IRI, in order to elucidate the mechanisms though which OPA1 protects the heart.4.To use induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes reprogrammed from human fibroblasts obtained from dominant optic atrophy patients to investigate the effects of OPA1 deficiency on mitochondrial function and susceptibility to acute IRI in human heart tissue.5.To use high-throughput screening to discover novel protein/chemical agent for upregulating OPA1.Expected outcomes: We hope to identify OPA1 as a therapeutic strategy to reduce MI size and prevent heart failure, the expected benefits of which would be to improve clinical outcomes in patient with IHD thereby alleviating patient morbidity and mortality in Singapore and worldwide.

title: Unifying Spectral Networks and Sparse Representations for Big Data Science
abs: The 4th industrial revolution, the digital intelligence revolution, has just started and its success will deeply depend on turning “big data” into meaningful knowledge. Big data in this project refers to massive amounts of data on large-scale networks such as Facebook with 1.6 billion of users generating text messages, pictures, and videos. Such generated volumes of data are unprecedented in human history and they have the great potential to reveal new scientific discoveries (in physics, biology), develop intelligent systems (autonomous cars), and offer highly personalized services (for medical treatments). However, despite a few important successes in image and speech recognition, major challenges are still to be overcome to unlock the full potential of big data in all areas of science, government and industry. A major limitation of most current mathematical algorithms is to analyze separately networks and data content. Actually, current algorithms focus on either geometrical structures of networks, or data content processing tasks. But networks and data content are two essential complementary sides of big data and should be integrated into the same framework to boost the overall data analysis. Hence, the major goal of the proposed project is to bridge the gap between network analysis with (non-linear) spectral graph theory and data content analysis with (non-convex) sparse representation. We plan to achieve such objective by formulating a mathematical framework whose foundations lie on variational optimization methods, providing the necessary background to also expand linear to non-linear spectral operators, and convex to non-convex sparse representations. Such proposed framework will be universal enough to advance specific fundamental analysis tasks like unsupervised clustering, supervised classification, data visualisation, recommender system and data matching. Eventually, the computational models developed in this project will be applied to expose new insights about brain functionality in neuroscience and communication principles in media networks.

title: Metabolomics of progressive diabetic kidney disease in young-onset type 2 diabetes – a prospective study.
inst: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital Pte Ltd
abs: BackgroundYoung-onset type 2 diabetes (YT2D) is increasingly prevalent largely due to childhood and adolescent obesity. YT2D is an emerging clinical challenge. It is associated with poorer metabolic control, limited pharmaco-therapeutic options (partly attributable to ill-understood pathobiology), early glycemic treatment failure and ominously, an accelerated trajectory towards diabetic complications (e.g. diabetic kidney disease (DKD)), with great personal, family and societal consequences. Therefore, greater understanding of YT2D is crucial to inform appropriate intervention strategies. Recent novel observations from our group suggested that metabolomics strongly predicted DKD progression (over and above baseline eGFR and albuminuria) in older-onset (mean:48 year old) individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2DM). HypothesisWe hypothesize that metabolomics are also prospectively predictive of renal-progression among YT2D.AimsWe will perform targeted plasma and urine metabolomics (lipids, acylcarnithines, amino-acids and organic acids) measurements at baseline among YT2D and follow them up prospectively for DKD progression.Subsequently, to validate any signals observed in an independent prospective cohort of YT2D.MethodsThis study will ride-on our two on-going, well-phenotyped diabetic cohorts (combined N~7,000) with rich cryo-preserved bio-resource. Similar to other well-known cohorts dedicated to young-onset diabetes (SEARCH and TOADY), YT2D is defined as non-classical type 1 diabetes, with onset <=40 year old. In our discovery cohort (SMART2D, N=2,058, recruited between 2011-2014), we have identified 664YT2D. They will be classified as DKD progressor (N~159) or non-progressor (N~505) according to KDIGO’s (Kidney Disease–Improve Global Outcome) recommendation after ~3 year follow-up. Baseline plasma and urine metabolomics, along with clinical parameters, will be used to identify predictors of renal-progression.Metabolites which show discriminative-ability will be validated in our second independent prospective cohort of >=418 YT2D (identified from a source-population of N~5,200 recruited between 2002-2016). Scientific and clinical significance.Our data will improve the risk-stratification of DKD and gain insights into the patho-biology of YT2D.
kw: young onset type 2 diabetes, diabetic kidney disease

title: Nature-inspired digital devices and networks for multi-scale environment sensing
abs: The overarching goal of this research proposal is to create highly sensitive mechanical sensors that directly encode mechanical stimuli into digital signals. My research program will incorporate fundamental mechanical, materials and electrical engineering to create new libraries of digital sensors that mechanically sense environments at different length scales. The proposal is divided into 3 aims: Aim A: Rationally design and characterize hierachical structures for use in mechanosensors I plan to develop optimal materials and fundamental design rules for creating discrete mechanosensors. I will engineer materials with microstructures that enable the material to exhibit negative Poissons' ratios. This remarkable material property confers high compressibility that is essential for ultrasensitive mechanical sensors. Aim B: Design and construct low-power digital circuits as sensor interface circuitry Digital signals offer noise robustness and power-efficiency. I plan to design and integrate digitization circuits that allows for scaling of mechanosensors developed in Aim A to massively large arrays without a proportional increase in power requirements. Aim C: Integrate mechanosensor devices into large-scale networks for sensing applications With the library of digital mechanical sensors, I aim to construct large-scale sensor systems that can be used to sense environments at various length scales such as in robotic skin or sensor microchips. I will explore various digital encoding and decoding schemes for efficient information transmission in large networks of these sensors. My proposal will generate power-efficient, robust artificial mechanosensors that are scalable to large integrated systems that are crucial to the sensing needs of emerging biomedical and technology applications.

title: Development of Humanized Mouse Model to Study Human Specific Immune Responses, Pathogenesis and Drug Discovery of Human Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Background & Aims— Existing animal models often fail to predict the efficacy of the therapeutics to treat autoimmune diseases, particularly Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) in humans. This is largely because studies of human immunopathogenesis, and resulting pathological symptoms have been hampered by the lack of human specific preclinical animal models. In this project, we propose to further improve humanized mouse technology for human SLE study and drug testing. Specifically, we aim to: a) Identify and correct the immune defects in current humanized mouse; b) Establish and characterize human SLE mouse model and perform drug testing; c) Validation of new drug targets in SLE humice with industry and academic labs. Methodology— Functional human immune system will be engineered in mouse by the transplantation of human stem cells and human cytokine treatments. Compounds/autoantigens will be used to mimic environmental factors to induce SLE in humanized mouse. Immunological, histological and gene editing approaches will be applied to systemically characterize and compare pathological and genomic aspects of SLE humanized mice and human patient samples. Collaborations will be established with biopharmaceutic companies and academic laboratories to test the drugs under development and to identify new biomarkers and drug targets for SLE. The application of the improved humanized mouse model in other diseases will also be explored. Expected outcome— Findings from humanized mouse models will significantly contribute to the understanding of human specific immune responses, pathogenesis, host responses, organ failure and other disease outcomes in SLE. These insights will be crucial for the development of anti-SLE drugs and intervention strategies. Furthermore, the establishment of a robust and highly predictive preclinical system for assessing drug efficacy will be of immense interest to the pharmaceutical industry and could reduce the chances of drugs failing in human clinical trials.

title: Combinatorial Strategies to Enhance Immunotherapy of Viral Associated Tumours
abs: Immunotherapy holds great promise as a novel approach to cancer treatment, because of its potential to evade genetic and cellular mechanisms of drug resistance, and to target tumor cells, while sparing normal tissues. Results of clinical trials with infusions of autologous T lymphocytes engineered with T-cell receptor (TCR), specific for antigens expressed on cancer cells, provided compelling evidence of their clinical potential. Clinical success has been, however, so far limited only to specific malignancies (B-cell lymphomas and melanoma), due to lack of targetable tumor-specific antigens and is not efficient in solid tumors due to the immunosuppressive effect of the tumor microenvironment. Our aim is to maximize treatment benefits and minimize side effects of T cell immunotherapy by enhancing anti-cancer therapeutic targeting and efficacy. In Sub-Project [1] we will i] Expand the repertoire of cloned TCRs recognizing HBV or EBV epitopes; ii] Redirect T cells towards high-affinity viral antigens expressed by tumors clinically relevant in Asia. In Sub-Project [2] we will define and modulate the expression or genes/isoforms associated with T cell exhaustion by Antisense OligoNucleotide [AON] and CRISPR-based approaches, to revert the immunosuppressive effects of the tumor microenvironment. In Sub-Project [3] we will implement a microfluidic-based model of tissue microenvironment to study the combinatorial effects of epigenetic- and immune-therapy. Finally, in Sub-Project [4], we will test our combinatorial immunotherapeutic strategy in vivo using Patient Derived-Xenografts and humanized mouse models of HBV- and EBV-associated cancers. The combined expertise present in different research institutes across Singapore and two companies (Lion TCR–Singapore and IONIS Pharmaceuticals–San Diego, USA) will allow us to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, balancing safety with anti-tumor activity, and to deliver results with significant impact on survival and quality of life of cancer patients.

title: Studying Zika Virus Pathogenesis and the Development of Therapeutics, In Vitro Cell Culture Model and Mouse Model that Display Various Diseases Phenotypes
abs: On 1st Feb 2016, the World Health Organization declared Zika virus (ZIKV) a global emergency. ZIKV is a member of the family flaviviridae, other members in the same family are west nile, dengue, yellow fever viruses. ZIKV was previously thought to cause only a mild febrile disease in only 20% of the infected humans. However, in the recent outbreaks report an increased incidence of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) in adults and microcephaly in feti associated with the disease sounded the global alarm. Singapore is currently experiencing an ZIKV outbreak and therefore, there is an immediate need to develop therapeutics and vaccines. From the experience of dengue vaccine development, the making of a ZIKV vaccine will likely take decades. This is especially so as there maybe risk associated with testing of vaccines in pregnant women. In addition, GBS is an autoimmune disease that is likely caused by the binding of the cross-reactive ZIKV antibodies to nerve cells, thereby leading to temporary paralysis. Therefore, administration of vaccine to adults may induce GBS. Hence, more basic understanding of virus pathogenesis is required to develop a safe vaccine. Our research project is aimed at studying the pathogenesis of ZIKV (projects 1-3), development of therapeutic agents such as drugs against virus non-structural proteins (project 2), identification of potent neutralizing antibodies against the virus particles (project 3) and the development of in vitro human neuroprogenitor cell and in vivo mouse models to test the efficacy of therapeutics (project 1). The information generated from this study can also aid in the future development of a safe vaccine.

title: Understanding and Targeting High-Risk Myeloma
abs: Multiple myeloma is the second most common haematologic malignancies and has a rising incidence in Singapore. Significant advances have been made in the treatment of myeloma over the last decades with an improvement in overall survival from 4 years to about 10 years now. However, there remain a high-risk group of myeloma patients whose survival is still at about 2-3 years despite this improvement. We, and others, have contributed to definition of this group of high-risk patients, through the studies of genetics. Its is widely accepted that 2 of the defining genetic characteristics of this group of patients is 17p13 deletion and t(4;14). In terms of gene expression profiling, genomic instability and impairment of DNA damage response is a common defining molecular signature. However, the basis of them being high-risk disease is not clear. In addition, there is significant heterogeneity and the presence of resistant clones manifesting as residual disease is a clinically relevant source of relapse. In this proposal, we aim to better understand the biology of 17p13 deleted and t(4;14) myeloma in order to identify and define therapeutic strategies that can be tested in the clinic. In addition, we seek to understand drug resistant clones under treatment pressure, so as to identify ways to overcome drug resistance. I believer but targeting these 3 areas of significant challenge and unmet medical needs in clinic will bring about the next leap in outcome improvement in myeloma.

title: The TRIUMPH program for people with poorly controlled diabetes in primary care in Singapore – A Feasibility Study. (TRIUMPH: Team-care to Reduce resistance to Insulin initiation Using a new care Model to engage T2D Patients to achieve optimal Health outcomes)
abs: We propose an innovative phase 1 health services study to refine, develop and pilot test a clinic-based intervention to support the timely initiation of insulin in primary care. This is a critical step in translational research, which embeds evidence based practice into the setting where the large majority of people with type 2 diabetes (T2D) receive most of their clinical care. Aims:Insulin initiation is often delayed amongst people with T2D who have glycaemic levels out of target, despite maximal oral therapy for long time. Our overarching aim is to improve the glycaemic control of these people via a new care-delivery model in primary care that specifically addresses the complex underlying patient, physician and system factors. We will pilot a complex intervention involving a trained primary healthcare team engaging patients using validated patient decision-support aids (PDA) within an appointment-based service in polyclinics.Method: The TRIUMPH Program is multi-faceted, involving training of polyclinic teams (family medicine residents, family physicians and diabetic nurse educators) at two sites. The program will empower teams to engage target patients using multi-lingual PDAs. Patients will be identified by case-finding using the polyclinic IT-based clinical information system. Participating patients will be linked to the Resident Continuity Clinic (RCC) within a polyclinic to ensure regular review and continuity of care. Multimethod, mixed qualitative-quantitative evaluation will allow us to understand the processes and uptake rate of the innovative model of care, contextualize and improve them. Staff and patients will participate in focus groups and interviews to capture their feedback on the Program. Cost and clinical outcomes including HBA1c and quality of life will be collected pre and post. The study outcome will be a robust, well-defined intervention and a robust evaluative framework for phase 2, to underpin a subsequent fully powered step-wedge trial to test effectiveness and cost effectiveness.

title: Exercise-induced stress CMR for detection of coronary artery disease
abs: Background and Clinical Significance: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is able to assess multiple aspects of cardiac physiology, perfusion and tissue characteristics with great accuracy and spatial resolution with inherent advantages over SPECT, which involves radiation, in detecting significant coronary artery disease (CAD). Up until recently the lack of CMR-compatible exercise stress equipment has precluded physiological assessment of the heart by CMR using safe and low-cost physical exertion techniques. In the last year, the NHCS has invested in new, state-of-the-art CMR-compatible cycle ergometer with real-time CMR imaging using a first-in-Singapore 64 channel 1.5T system that paves the way for new studies of CMR exercise in the clinic, which has been suggested as the next major step in non-invasive assessment of the cardiovascular system. This offers a one-stop diagnostic test for comprehensive assessment of cardiac function, perfusion, wall motion and viability with superior image quality for detection of ischaemic-causing CAD and could potentially minimize unnecessary invasive coronary angiography.Specific aims: • To develop and test the feasibility of exercise-induced stress CMR protocol for assessment of changes in cardiac volumes and function with physical exertion in healthy individuals.• To assess the diagnostic accuracy of exercise stress CMR to detect ischaemic-induced coronary artery disease with reference to coronary fractional flow reserve (FFR)Method: • For specific aim 1, 20 healthy volunteers will undergo scan – rescan CMR and CPET.• For specific aim 2, 88 patients with SPECT positive and referred for coronary angiogram will be recruited for exercise-induced perfusion CMR.

title: Understand the complex network of pre-diabetes, diabetes and complications: disease progression and trajectory modelling using big retrospective data sources
abs: The growing healthcare burden related to diabetes and other chronic diseases is one of the biggest challenges to the sustainability of existing healthcare systems. This study aims to explore the complex disease progression network centered by diabetes, reveal hidden links between diabetes and other chronic diseases, predict risk at individual level and project disease burden at population level. Instead of focusing on diabetes alone, we look at the whole spectrum of multiple chronic diseases, intending to find patterns otherwise missing if studied alone. Relying on multiple data sources including retrospective databases and disease registry, we are able to conduct advanced temporal analysis besides conventional cross-sectional analysis. It is possible to translate the longitudinal information into a journey of disease progression for individual patient, i.e., how a patient starts healthy, develops pre-diabetes, then progresses to diabetes, and finally deteriorates to various complications over the years. Individual trajectories are aggregated up to population level and form a complex network of disease progression. Various analytical techniques are then applied to discover connections hidden in the disease network. Longitudinal analysis is applied to explore dominant trajectory and its variants, and identify possible triggers of progression from diabetes to different complications. Clustering techniques are used to group patients with similar progression trajectory. Clustering results could be used to design bundle of care for specific segments. Microsimulation model is constructed to simulate individual patient’s disease progression in the next decade or further. Simulation results can then be used to predict patient’s risk of getting diabetes or complications. Results can also be aggregated at population level to get an estimation of future disease burden. Additionally, the simulation model can be applied to pre-evaluate some interventions by running what-if scenarios. The study is expected to add value to diabetes prevention and management thereby preserving a sustainable healthcare system.
kw: Pre-diabetes; Diabetes; Diabetes complications; Chronic disease progression; Disease trajectory clustering; Microsimulation

title: A randomized control trial with interactive smart phone app to restore optimal weight in women with recent gestational diabetes
abs: Gestational diabetes (GDM) complicates about 20% of pregnancies in Singapore. These women are at high risk of developing type 2 diabetes years after pregnancy; seven times more likely than normal. Achieving a healthy weight post-delivery is key to reduce the risk of future diabetes. This proposal, from a multidisciplinary team, intends to create a unique seamless care model to restore optimal weight post-delivery in women with recent GDM. The innovation examined in this randomized control trial is an INTERACTIVE SMART PHONE APP. The APP monitors weight, dietary habits, and exercise activity patterns, giving feedback and provide practical personalized lifestyle coaching that is culturally appropriate and customized to the Singapore context. If efficacy is confirmed in this RCT, the APP can be easily scaled up as a cost-effective way to potentially prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes in Singaporean women. Additionally, measurement of markers of cardiometabolic risk will give indications on future cardiovascular health, utilizing an underused opportunity to improve women's health.
kw: Gestational Diabetes, Prevention, Weight, Smart-phone application, Randomized control trial

title: Barriers and facilitators to retention in HIV care and treatment among patients on antiretroviral therapy at a specialist outpatient clinic in Singapore
abs: Background: As the national referral centre for HIV management in Singapore, the Communicable Disease Centre plays an important role in providing clinical care and treatment as well as counselling and support to PLHIV. In 2014, the clinic observed approximately 15% of missed clinic appointments by patients who seek HIV care at the clinic. Retention in HIV care is crucial as it will improve the health outcomes of people living with HIV, leading to better quality of life and also reducing HIV transmission to others. In order to better understand the barriers to assessing HIV care among PLHIV who are lost to care so as to improve retention in care, we propose to conduct a qualitative descriptive study. Findings from this study will be used to develop future interventions to improve access and increase retention in care for PLHIV.Aim: 1) To identify facilitators and barriers to retention in HIV care among patients on ART who are lost to follow up and those who remain engaged in care at CDC. 2) To explore recommendations for future interventions to reduce barriers for PLHIV so as to improve access and increase retention in HIV care.Methods: The study consists of a maximum of 60 in-depth interviews (IDI) with 1) Group A: PLHIV on ART who have dropped out of care; 2) Group B: PLHIV on ART who are consistently engaged in care; 3) Group C: Key informants (healthcare providers, staff and volunteers of patient support groups) who provide care for PLHIV.

title: The trajectory of pre-death grief in dementia family caregivers and its effect on caregiving
abs: The demand for nursing home in Singapore has increased steadily in recent years, especially from persons with dementia (PWD). This can be a cause for concern considering that dementia already has a 10% prevalence in Singapore and with dementia being an age-related disease, its absolute numbers are expected to soar with our rapidly ageing population. To avoid the escalating societal cost associated with building more nursing homes, we need to better support the emotional needs of family caregivers so that they can maintain PWD in the community for a longer time.In this proposal, we wish to uncover an unmet emotional need of dementia caregivers (pre-death grief, PDG) that may adversely affect caregiving. We define PDG as the emotional responses as caregivers mourn the psychological death of PWD. Based on the hypothesis that persistently high PDG can have greater impact on caregiving, we aimed to assess how the trajectory of PDG affects the risk of major depression in caregivers (using mixed-effect logistic regression) and nursing home placement of PWD (using Cox regression). Additionally, we will test, using mixed-effect linear regression, whether PDG improves with currently available social interventions (such as day-care attendance or assistance from foreign domestic helper). We hypothesize that PDG, unlike caregiver burden, may worsen with these interventions. To achieve the study aims, we will recruit 200 caregivers to complete self-administered questionnaires at 0, 6 and 12 months. By showing how PDG can lead to caregiver depression and premature nursing home placement of PWD, the results of this study will provide the groundwork to guide our approach to better support the emotional needs of caregivers in current services, to implement strategies for early detection and intervention for caregivers at high risk of adverse outcomes, and to conduct future research on the efficacy of grief counselling.

title: Identification and Validation of PRDM15, a novel epigenetic target in oncology
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: Non-Hodgkin’s Lymphomas (NHLs) are the most prevalent form of adult hematological cancer. NHLs are very heterogeneous both in terms of genetic/epigenetic makeup and survival rates. Currently we lack targeted therapies for high-grade B-cell lymphomas, such as the MYC+ double- or triple-hit (DH/TH) cases (aberrantly expressing MYC+BCL2 and/or BCL6), making the identification and validation of novel therapeutic targets of great clinical relevance.PR-domain containing proteins (PRDMs) are a class of sequence specific transcriptional co-regulators which have been associated with deletions, mutations, epigenetic silencing or overexpression in multiple cancer types. We have recently focused our attention on PRDM15, due to its overexpression and essential role in B-cell lymphomagenesis, making it a very attractive drug target. Our unpublished preliminary data demonstrate that: 1) PRDM15 is essential in MYC-driven lymphomas, but dispensable in normal physiological conditions in the adult mouse; 2) PRDM15 oncogenic functions are relevant both during tumor initiation and maintenance; 3) depleting PRDM15 with Antisense Oligonucleotides (ASOs) inhibits the growth of human lymphomas in vitro and in vivo.We here propose to further characterize PRDM15 in order to establish it as a novel and validated target in oncology. To this aim we will: 1) assess PRDM15 oncogenic properties; specifically we will establish its role in sustaining B-cell lymphomagenesis in clinically relevant models; 2) dissect PRDM15 mechanism of action; specifically we will determine the PRDM15-regulated cistrome, its protein binding partners and its downstream effectors; 3) target PRDM15 with ASOs for therapeutic intervention, taking advantage of cell-penetrating antisense oligonucleotide-chemistry, with proven efficacy in clinical studies; specifically we will utilize ASOs to induce Prdm15 pre-mRNA degradation in NHLs and other cancer types overexpressing PRDM15.We strongly believe that the proposed studies will lead to conclusively establish PRMD15 as a novel validated target in oncology and to further development into clinically compatible therapeutic interventions.
kw: Lymphoma, Solid tumors, epigenetic, transcription, Antisense Oligonucleotide

title: Proteomic and structural characterization of the Chlamydia – host interactome
inst: CREATE - Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology (CREATE-SMART)
abs: Chlamydiae bacteria cause a range of globally and economically important human diseases for which no vaccines exist. C. trachomatis causes the most prevalent sexually transmitted disease in many parts of the world including Singapore. It is also the leading cause for noncongenital infertility and noncongenital blindness worldwide. C. pneumoniae is a major cause of pneumonia. Given its public health importance in the Singapore context, it is striking that there is no research lab working on Chlamydia in Singapore. Chlamydia is an obligate intracellular pathogen that replicates in a vacuolar compartment within host cells. The pathogen secretes an arsenal of virulence factors to manipulate the host cell machinery in order to survive and replicate in the intracellular environment. The Chlamydia effectors that mediate these are poorly understood. This work aims to expand our understanding of Chlamydia effector function by determining their host interactomes. We have developed techniques and workflows for proteomic and structural analysis of effector interactomes which we will apply to Chlamydia in this study. In Aim 1, we will use affinity-purification coupled mass spectrometry to analyse C. trachomatis-host interactions. In Aim 2, we will use host cytoskeleton-specific baits to pull down against Chlamydia-infected human cell lysate to identify effector proteins that target the host cytoskeleton. In Aim 3, we will perform structural analysis of effectors and effector-host interactions identified in this study. This work utilizes advances in quantitative proteomics to study host-pathogen interactions, particularly for organisms such as Chlamydiae which are not amenable to genetic manipulation due to their obligate intracellular lifestyle. These proteomic assays are high-throughput and can be used to explore genome-wide interaction partners. The studies here will fill a critical void in our understanding of Chlamydia effector function and identify candidates that can be targeted for therapeutic intervention.
kw: Chlamydia, infectious disease, proteomics, pathogen host interactions

title: A phase II single arm trial to access the efficacy of ASLAN001 plus capecitabine in previously irradiated, progressing central nervous system (CNS) metastases for HER2 positive breast cancer patients
abs: Brain metastasis in breast cancer (BMBC) has very poor prognosis. The focus for this group of patients is on palliation as well as therapeutics that offer meaningful clinical benefits. A few phase II studies have demonstrated the activities of either lapatinib alone or in combination with capecitabine for treatment of brain metastases after radiosurgery and/or WBRT. Nancy Lin et al showed CNS responses of around 5-20% with lapatinib single agent or lapatinib with capecitabine. While the combination showed activity, it was associated with significant grade 3-4 toxicities. Newer agents should be researched for this exclusive group of patients. This provides the basis for this phase II trial which also uses small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor ASLAN001 (a potent, specific, adenosine triphosphate competitive inhibitor of the tyrosine kinases of the cell surface receptors human epidermal growth factor receptor HER-1, HER-2, and HER-4) in combination with capecitabine for evaluation of CNS response rate in previously irradiated, progressing CNS metastases. This is a single arm, single center, phase 2 study. A total of 29 eligible HER2 positive breast cancer patients with irradiated, progressing brain metastasis will be enrolled to receive ASLAN001 400 mg orally BID with capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 orally BID for days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle. Treatment will continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The secondary objectives include evaluation of the clinical benefit of ASLAN001 in combination with capecitabine in systemic disease (outside CNS), and evaluation of the safety and tolerability of ASLAN001 in combination with capecitabine. Baseline brain imaging using either magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be performed; non-brain imaging with a CT will also be performed in the same settings. Radiological imaging to assess disease status will be performed at baseline and every 2 cycles until disease progression.
kw: brain metastasis, HER2+ breast cancer

title: Role of chemokine ligand-receptor (CXCL12-CXCR4) signaling in osteoblast/osteoclast function, and its modulation by icaritin and estrogens in bone remodeling and osteoporosis
abs: Current health burdens of menopausal osteoporotic fractures are set to rise exponentially. The risk of death is 20-24% in the first year after a hip fracture, 40% are unable to walk independently, 60% will require assistance a year later and 33% will remain totally dependent. Estrogens benefit bone homeostasis by regulating the function of osteoclast and osteoblasts. Imbalance of these two bone remodeling cellular processes results in osteoporosis, and consequent low trauma fractures. Besides estrogens, the importance of the immune system for regulating bone remodeling is becoming more compelling. Notably, preliminary findings from our lab suggest that the chemokine receptor, CXCR4, may play a critical function in bone health. CXCR4 is a cell surface receptor for a chemokine known as C-X-C chemokine ligand 12 [CXCL12; stromal derived factor 1 (SDF-1)]. CXCL12-CXCR4 is a member of a large family of structurally related chemokine ligand-receptor system that plays a key role in bone marrow biology. Interestingly, we have also preliminary data showing that icaritin, a compound released in serum after consumption of prenyl flavonoids from a medicinal herb Epimedium (EP), can positively affect bone remodeling by modulating CXCR4 expression. We hypothesize that CXCR4 and its ligand CXCL12 are novel regulators of bone remodelling; and defining their role, alone, and in relation to other signaling pathways may lead to the development of novel drugs, such as icaritin, for post-menopausal osteoporosis. The overall aim is to use icaritin as a tool to elucidate CXCL12-CXCR4 ligand receptor signaling mechanisms and their interaction with estrogen and other signaling pathways. We intend to perform a cognate series of experiments involving cellular models, ovariectomized and CXCR4 gene deletion rat models, and a human randomized placebo-controlled clinical study on the effects of icaritin on osteoporotic bone microarchitecture and osteoblast/osteoclast function.
kw: CXCR4, osteoporosis, bone remodelling, estrogen

title: Repurposing trimetazine to treat cancer cachexia
abs: Cancer cachexia is an unmet medical need with limited therapeutic options. In advanced cancer, cachexia is present in up to 50% of patients and contributes to 25% of deaths. Using both human and murine cachexia models, we recently found that fatty acid oxidation (FAO) drives cancer cachexia. Pharmacological inhibition of FAO with etomoxir rescued muscle and weight loss in three different in vivo models. However, etomoxir is not approved for human use because of concerns over hepatotoxicitiy Trimetazidine is an safe and widely used drug for angina pectoris that also has activity as a FAO inhibitor. Our proposal seeks to evaluate the potential of repurposing trimetazidine in the treatment and prevention of cancer cachexia.Specific Aim 1: We seek to determine the efficacy of trimetazidine in maintaing or rescuing muscle mass and body weight in preclinical models of cancer cachexia. To do so, we will administer trimetazidine at different doses in three well-established murine models of cancer cachexia. We will also initiate trimetazidine treatment at different time intervals (before, during and after onset of cachexia). In doing so, we will evaluate the effectiveness of trimetazidine in preventing or treating cancer cachexia.Specific Aim 2: We seek to investigate the pharmacodynamic/metabolic effect of different dose-schedules of trimetazidine on biomarkers of FAO in cancer patients. To do so, we will evaluate safety and serial metabolic alterations in FAO activity in four different cohorts of cancer patients (one without treatment and three at different doses of trimetazidine). Data on weight, muscle strength and quality of life will also be collected.Together, efficacy signals of trimetazidine in treating cachexia in preclinical models, and the clinical pharmacodynamic and metabolic effects of trimetazidine at different doses in patients will inform the design of a phase 2 clinical trial to repurpose trimetazidine to treat cancer cachexia.
kw: cancer, cachexia, trimetazine

title: Intrauterine Reduction in Growth Velocity as a Predictor of Poor Perinatal Outcome in Term Appropriately Grown Fetuses
abs: Background: Current research on intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) has focused on the poorer outcome of fetuses with an estimated fetal weight (EFW) of less than 10% and abnormal Doppler measurements. However, there are still babies born with birthweights of more than 10% whose postnatal outcome is poor but unexplained. Hypothesis: We postulate that fetuses who start the 2nd trimester on a normal EFW but reach the third trimester on a lower than expected EFW and with a birth weight that is within normal range represent a group of IUGR fetuses which could potentially remain undetected but are at a risk of poor perinatal outcome. The placenta may play a role in this. Aims: To identify term “appropriately-grown” fetuses with an intrauterine reduction in growth velocity and correlate them to their perinatal outcome. To correlate outcomes with maternal angiogenic factors and placenta histopathology. Methods: Singleton fetuses with an EFW of more than 25% at the 2nd trimester and a reduction in the EFW of more than 15% between the 2nd and 3rd trimester will be recruited. Pregnancies will be dated by first trimester crown-rump length measurements. The EFW will be calculated using the Hadlock formula. Only cases of cephalic presentation without contraindications for a vaginal delivery will be considered. Umbilical, uterine and middle cerebral arteries blood flow Doppler will be evaluated. Maternal angiogenic factors will be collected. The placenta will be examined histopathologically for evidence of placental under-perfusion. Perinatal outcome data (emergency delivery for non-reassuring fetal status and neonatal metabolic acidosis) will be recorded. Significance: This will be the first ever study that looks at the intrauterine reduction in growth velocity as a possible risk factor of poor perinatal outcome. This may revolutionize our understanding of IUGR and help improve the identification of fetuses at risk
kw: intrauterine growth reduction, perinatal outcome

title: Correlation of Genomic Clonal Architecture and Clinical Outcomes in Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukaemia Treated with Hypomethylating Agents
abs: Chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia (CMML) is a clonal haematologic malignancy that usually occurs in the elderly and carries poor prognosis. Most patients progress to succumb to complications of cytopenia or acute leukaemic transformation. Allogeneic stem cell transplantation offers the only curative approach but many patients are not eligible. Recent therapeutic trials with hypomethylating agents (HMAs) such as 5-azacytidine have shown limited response in a subset of patients. Somatic mutations and epigenetic dysregulation have been implicated in CMML, but the exact molecular mechanism of leukaemogenesis is not well characterized. Aims: Our study aims to identify recurrent somatic mutations in CMML and establish their association with prognosis, to characterize evolution of clonal architecture during treatment with HMAs, and to explore the possible effects of mutation allelic burden in different haematopoietic cellular compartments in CMML at diagnosis on clinical phenotypes. Hypotheses: We hypothesize that specific mutational patterns define clinical presentation at diagnosis and prognostic outcome in CMML patients, and that sub-clones harboring differential mutation allelic burden evolve during treatment with HMAs. Methodology and Approach: We will obtain genomic data from next generation sequencing performed on CMML samples at diagnosis and at defined time points during treatment with HMAs. We will then analyze somatic mutation burden and establish clonal architecture using bioinformatics algorithm, and correlate the findings with clinical outcomes.Clinical Significance: The dismal prognosis of CMML reflects the lack of rational therapies for the genetically complex disease in which detailed molecular events are not well defined. Our study will provide insights into cooperation of various somatic mutations in the pathogenesis of the disease, and lead to a thorough understanding of clonal evolution and the development of drug resistance. This will establish a basis to rationalize strategies to overcome resistance, with a potential discovery of new therapeutic targets that may lead to clinical trials.

title: Small-scale Wireless Devices for Bioelectronic Therapies
abs: Since the first pacemaker was implanted over 50 years ago, bioelectronics have undergone rapid miniaturization and are now routinely used to control biological processes at the cellular scale. This increasing precision has led directly to new therapies (e.g. retinal implants), and it is now envisioned that small, wireless devices could be the basis for new treatments more precise and effective than drugs for disorders such as cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and depression. Medical devices today, however, are large and bulky. They are unable to target small organ structures implicated in many of such disorders, and lead to consequences such as surgery, patient discomfort, device failure, and adverse tissue response. This proposal focuses on techniques for creating wireless bioelectronic devices at the scale of a single millimeter. At this scale, devices will be able to interface with critical, but previously inaccessible, tissue structures such as visceral peripheral nerves and deep-seated tumors, and enable delivery methods that circumvent conventional surgery. Our approach is centered on a wireless technology for powering small-scale, deeply implanted devices that overcomes the long-standing “power bottleneck” for realizing these devices. It incorporates low-power integrated circuits, soft materials, and minimally invasive delivery methods with the goal of demonstrating two specific new therapeutic modalities enabled by this approach: nerve stimulation and photodynamic therapy. This work establishes a platform for prototyping future bioelectronic therapies and demonstrates the therapeutic promise urgently needed to drive their clinical translation.
kw: Wireless powering;Bioelectronics

title: Atomic Manipulations in 2D Materials for Quantum Computation Applications
abs: Miniaturization of conventional transistors has been at the heart of commercial success for semiconductor companies over decades. Rapid advances in nanotechnology have enabled vast increases in the density of electronic components within integrated circuits. However, with device sizes fast approaching the atomic-scale, conventional transistor behaviour is strongly impacted by the emergence of quantum phenomena. Whilst posing a roadblock for technological progress, the miniaturization of electronic devices towards the ultimate atomic limit creates opportunity to exploit the quantum degrees of freedom for an entirely new computational paradigm – quantum information processing. I propose using atomic manipulations by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) on the surfaces of novel 2D electronic materials – such as graphene and the transition metal dichalcogenides – to construct adatom nanostructures for the confinement of individual electron spins to within atomic length scales. Promising long spin life- and coherence times – common to spins in carbon-based materials – I will investigate the potential of spin quantum bits (qubits) to process and store quantum information. Integration and coupling of individual spin-qubits within gate-tuneable 2D materials based device platforms will allow studying their electronic and spin properties down to millikelvin temperatures and high magnetic fields in research facilities that are worldwide unique. Ultimately, this project will develop schemes for qubit initialization, read-out, and manipulation – prerequisites for quantum computing applications.

title: Zika Virus in Pregnancy in Singapore - A Multi-Centre Prospective National Longitudinal Study
abs: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection has recently been named as a public health emergency by the World Health Organisation in light of its possible association with fetal central nervous system malformations as well as possible association with Guillain-Barre syndrome. At current, further evidence is still needed to establish a definite causal link between these associations. Evidence on serology testing for Zika infection in the local population of Singapore is also lacking. In addition, there are currently no drugs to treat nor vaccines to prevent acquisition of the Zika virus. This study thus aims to study the immune response to the virus infection to better understand the interplay between the virus and the pregnant host immune system. This might give rise to vaccine or therapeutic strategies to prevent or fight an outbreak in Singapore and to better specific treatments for infected people. The study will also allow us to evaluate the impact of Zika infection on pregnancies in terms of fetal malformations by following these pregnancies up antenatally and in the neonatal period. Knowledge from this study will therefore help to add to the existing limited amount of information in the literature, and further help to establish the presence or absence of a link between ZIKV and fetal CNS malformations.

title: Preparedness versus Paranoia: Media Exposure and Singaporeans’ Awareness and Responses to the Zika Outbreak
abs: In May 2016, Singapore experienced its first imported case of ZIKV. Soon after, Singapore experienced a sudden surge in locally transmitted incidences of the ZIKV. This research will look into the current ZIKV outbreak, and examine the communication techniques used by mainstream news sources, along with social media sources, to illicit nuanced views of how media has been used to report outbreaks, and how the general public is engaged with the Zika issue on social media. The research will involve a survey to gather knowledge, attitudes, perceptions, and beliefs regarding the ZIKV outbreak. The study will involve two parts. The first will involve a comprehensive content analysis of all the mainstream news sources in Singapore to understand (e.g. Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram). The findings will provide valuable insights into how Singapore media has framed the news surrounding the outbreak and how Singaporeans have reacted on social media via posts and comments on Zika-related issues. The research findings from will provide knowledge which will allow health authorities and communication stakeholders to make informed decisions in terms of engaging the general public during health emergencies and future outbreaks.The study findings will have implications for development of policy and public health communication guidelines.
kw: Public Health Messaging, Zika Perceptions, Disease Prevention, Risk Communication, Social Media, Public Opinion

title: Epidemiology of Zika virus and other Aedes-borne infections in Singapore
abs: Zika is a mosquito-borne virus transmitted by same vector which transmits dengue, the latter being endemic in Singapore. A Zika outbreak is currently ongoing in Singapore, and while mostly presenting with mild illness, may cause neurological damage to the fetus and other complications in adults. However, due to reduced testing in primary care, subsequent identification of the infection will become difficult, increasing the challenges for accurately studying the epidemic and transmission by case reporting alone. This proposal will investigate the epidemiology of Zika virus infection in Singapore through a population-based cohort study. In this study, we will conduct: 1) outbreak-driven sampling where we aim to recruit index patients and their close contacts, residents of known Zika outbreak areas, and migrant workers of worksites and dormitories implicated in Zika outbreaks and 2) a multi-stage random cluster sampling approach where participants are randomly recruited from control areas which did not have detected cases of Zika virus infection. Subjects will be interviewed for identification of clinical symptoms and potential risk factors, and subsequently followed-up with weekly symptom reporting. RT-PCR to test urine samples will be used to identify active infection, with serological assays to detect incidence of Zika virus over the study period.This study will answer the question as to whether outbreak measures were successful in truncating the course of the current Zika outbreak, and shed light on the true proportion of clinically recognized, subclinical, and asymptomatic Zika virus infection in Singapore. In addition, this study will enable the estimation of seroincidence in Zika and non-Zika outbreak areas in Singapore, and both environmental and behavioral risk factors that may contribute towards Zika virus infection. Study results will also advance understanding of the transmission dynamics of Aedes-borne infections and the effect of outbreak response and other interventions.

title: Data-Driven Strategic Collaboration
abs: The objective of this proposal is the development and analysis of cooperative game theory (CGT) in a data-driven environment. A cooperative game is simply a function v assigning values to subsets (also called coalitions) of agents. Traditional analysis of cooperative games focuses on coalition formation - finding a revenue maximizing agent partition, or coalition structure - and revenue/cost division – finding a payoff vector satisfying certain guarantees with respect to coalitional values. While traditionally applied to economic settings (e.g. markets, or cost sharing scenarios), its generality makes cooperative game theory applicable in several domains. Unfortunately, the cooperative game model suffers from two major limitations: it is generally computationally intractable to compute cooperative solution concepts; furthermore, in its traditional formulation, cooperative game theory requires complete information about the underlying game in order to provide any fairness/optimality guarantees. This proposal aims at addressing these two major issues, formalizing and testing a data-driven theory of collaborative behavior, and studying its applications in various domains. Forgoing the full information assumption in CGT allows one to reason about optimality and fairness in the context of existing data, premising guarantees on data accuracy, rather than a preconceived notion of agent behavior. Adapting canonical learning theoretic techniques such as PAC learning, active learning and data analysis to the CGT domain is a first major challenge. Ultimately, this proposal aims at providing a new paradigm for reasoning about large-scale collaboration via algorithmic mediation; thus, finding scalable algorithmic solutions for collaborative settings is of utmost importance. Going beyond theoretical analysis, I intend to conduct extensive experiments on real datasets, both existing and generated by user behavioral studies. Finally, this proposal explores cooperative value theory as a method for quantitative algorithmic transparency and discrimination, an emerging topic in the security/privacy community.

title: An Innovative and Patient-Centric Research Program Targeting the Ageing Singaporeans: The PopulatION HEath and Eye Disease PRofile in Elderly Singaporeans (PIONEER) Study
abs: This research program is innovative; patient-centric; clinical health services driven; and community-focused. It includes three studies. The first one will determine the epidemiology of age-related eye diseases, vision impairment, presbyopia, the aging visual function system; their relationship with multimorbidity, associated consequences and burden; and the comprehensive impact of age-related eye diseases and aging visual function system in the presence of multimorbidity. It is hypothesised that the prevalence of major age-related eye diseases, VI, and presbyopia is substantially high in older Singaporeans ?70 years but different across the three ethnic groups; the association of visual function is different across different eye conditions and changes in these parameters are predictive of the presence and severity of VI; individuals with multimorbidity are likely to have VI; increasing number of comorbid conditions is associated with VI and age-related eye diseases in a step-ladder fashion; and eye diseases, in the presence of multimorbidity, are associated with poor patient’s and carer’s QoL with high personal and societal costs. Using a RCT, the second study will investigate the effectiveness of eye screening with customised post-screening support and eye-specific literacy compared to routine eye screening in elderly people of low SES. We theorise that compared to the usual screening, this new model has a superior post screening referral adherence; is cost effective; and results in significant improvements in eye care management; self-efficacy; vision, and vision-specific QoL. The last project is cluster RCT evaluating the clinical and cost-effectiveness of an innovative eye care intervention (ResCare) which provides onsite eye testing; and a personalised clinical treatment pathway for elderly people in public-funded residential care facilities. We hypothesise that compared to usual care, ResCare will demonstrate a superior improvement in vision; wellbeing, and vision-related QoL; depression and falls; and will be cost effective.

title: MECHANISMS OF ABERRANT BRAIN STEM CELL BEHAVIOUR: IMPLICATIONS IN AGING AND CANCER
abs: The broad objective of the proposed research is to provide unifying principles of brain stem cell self-renewal that account for aberrant brain stem cell behavior in human disease. Neural stem cells (NSCs), capable of self-renewal and multi-lineage differentiation, are responsible for the cellular complexity and proper development of the mammalian central nervous system. The aberrant behavior of these stem cells results in disease, for example the process of aging impairs NSC self-renewal, neurogenesis and cognition in human, while the uncontrolled self-renewal activity of NSC-like glioma cells (glioma stem cells, GSC) results in tumorigenicity and terminal differentiation blockade of GSC. Our limited knowledge of how aging impairs NSC function and the lack of effective treatments for glioblastomas underscores an urgent need to study the molecular changes that contribute to brain stem cell aberrancies. To identify molecular alterations that compromise NSC activity during aging, I propose two unique premature aging mouse models, namely the inducible telomerase deficient (TERT-ER/ER) mice and the GFAP-creERT2::TRF2::GFAP::GFP mice, which rely on the induction of telomere (protective caps at the end of chromosomes) dysfunction and DNA damage (hallmark features of aging) in the NSC and niche astrocytes (that support NSC function). These mouse models will be used for the isolation of NSC and niche astrocytes for unbiased transcriptomic, lipidomic and proteomic analyses for pathway identification, as well as functional validation. Given the remarkable plasticity of glioma cells and the druggability of the epigenetic pathway, I also propose to identify epigenetic regulators that promote self-renewal and tumorigenicity of the pre-malignant c-myc::p53DN human NSC using an unbiased in vivo ORF epigenetic screen. The epigenetic targets will be further validated in patient-derived GSCs. Collectively, my proposal will uncover mechanisms of brain stem cell self-renewal that are deregulated during aging and gliomagenesis, guiding the development of brain stem cell-based therapeutic intervention.
kw: AGING;TELOMERE/TELOMERASE;NEURAL STEM CELL;BRAIN CANCER STEM CELL

title: A Time Based Assessment of Children Advertising Guidelines on Child Food Consumption and Preferences in Singapore
abs: The research is a longitudinal extension to our current NMRC HSR project (HSRG/0046/2013 grant: A Time-Based Assessment of Children’s Advertising Guidelines on Child Food Consumption and Preferences in Singapore).This project aims to understand the impact of the latest Advertising Standards Authorities of Singapore (ASAS) Advertising Guidelines mounted in January 2015 on children’s food consumption-related attitudes and exposure to advertising via three research methods: 1) Content analysis of food advertising on three popular national TV channels to provide information on the evolving content of food marketing and guideline adherence; 2) cohort-based surveys conducted with schoolchildren nationwide to measure attitudinal changes toward different types of foods and consumption/perception of food; 3) family panel study to understand changes in family food attitudes and consumption.This proposal attempts to further existing work on three fronts:(1) Longitudinally assess the evolving advertising landscape in terms of content, frequency, thematic execution and message characteristics pre and post guideline launch. We propose additional online media tracking to examine parallel advertising content shifts to new media.(2) Measure cohort-by-cohort shifts in healthy and junk-food attitudes and intended consumption pre-guidelines, post-, and longitudinally.(3) Assess family food consumption attitudes and behaviours via tracked panels.The previous NMRC project was limited to two years and provided before-and-after snapshot of the ASAS guidelines. The extension will allow the team to further work longitudinally (3-5 years of data collection) and expand the scope of advertising exposure to online media.Overall, understanding how the advertising ban influenced target populations enables policy makers to further shape national policies. These longitudinal nationwide studies can help determine sustained effects of policies on Singapore children and families. The findings can provide stronger frameworks for health promotion & aid in potential adjustments to existing policies and health-promotion campaigns.
kw: Health communication, child health, child advertising, obesity management, Public Health, Food Advertising and Promotion

title: Multiphase Evaluation of Healthier Choice Symbol (HCS) Logo
abs: In efforts to promote a healthy diet, the Singapore Health Promotion Board (HPB) supplements traditional nutrition labelling with the Healthier Choice Symbol (HCS), which identifies food items as healthier choices. Despite their use for nearly fifteen years, no published studies have assessed the role of the logos in influencing food choice. That is the goal of this effort. We propose the following: •Aim 1: To use market data to quantify the association between implementation of the HCS logos on specific foods and subsequent purchases of those foods and on overall calories and macronutrients purchased. •Aim 2: To use a four arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) and a web grocery store to assess the causal effect of the HCS logos on diet quality either alone or in combination with one of two complementary FOP labels: 1) Calories or 2) Physical Activity Equivalents (PAEs), where the latter provides a graphical display of how long one would need to engage in a certain activity (e.g., jogging) to burn off one serving of the product. •Aim 3: To conduct a two arm RCT to test the extent to which diet quality can be further improved via a smart shopping algorithm (SSA) that allows customers to reconfigure their food basket to meet healthy eating targets, including percentage reductions in calories, fat, sodium and/or sugar purchased.This proposal addresses a key priority area under HPB's five-year plan (improving diet quality). As a result, the findings of this study have a high likelihood of adoption should they be shown to be effective.
