title: Understanding the Patient Experience of Genetic Testing: In-Depth Patient Interviews and Questionnaires
abs: The primary goal of our study is to understand the process and benefits of genetic counselling and testing from the patient’s perspective. Such knowledge has never before been collected in an Asian population, yet, it will benefit clinical geneticists and genetic counsellors, locally and internationally, to learn which aspects of clinical cancer genetic services that patients regard as most important and beneficial. The study will employ two phases. Firstly, one-to-one in-depth qualitative interviews with BRCA1/2 tested patients to understand the fears and concerns that patients have during the process of genetic counselling and testing. The interview questions will be designed to uncover patient’s motives for and against BRCA1/2 testing and their willingness to share their results with biological relatives. Secondly, using a validated clinical genetics-specific Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROM), the Genetic Counselling Outcome Scale (GCOS-24), a short self-completion questionnaire designed to evaluate patient-reported benefits of genetic counselling. GCOS-24 measures patient empowerment, where patients gain greater control over decisions and actions affecting their health. GCOS-24 will be administered before and after genetic counselling to measure patient-reported outcomes derived from cancer genetic services. Qualitative interview data and quantitative PROMs data gathered in this study will be the first-of-its-kind in Singapore and will play a crucial role in evaluating clinical genetic services in Singapore. With the growing awareness and demand for clinical genetic services in Singapore, this information is necessary to assess and evaluate the clinical and economic impact of clinical genetic services before appropriate policy interventions can be designed to meet the needs of patients who require genetic screening services. Findings will also be useful to inform further development and promotion of cancer genetic services as new models of disease prevention and health promotion.
kw: Genetic Testing, interview, PROMs

title: Defining and evaluating norms for health and social service (HASS) use for population health segments
abs: BackgroundIn view of expected growth of the older population in Singapore in the next decades, the volume and complexity of needs for health care services is expected to increase, which amplifies stress on the current healthcare system. One approach to addressing this challenge is to consider services utilization in relationship to needs based on “population segmentation” and to plan and evaluate new services in light of unmet needs.Specific Aims and HypothesesPrimary Aim 1: to establish health and social service (HASS) norms for population segments as defined by the Simple Segmentation Tool (SST) via a modified-Delphi methodology Primary Aim 2: to evaluate the concordance between the types of HASS that patients in each population segment actually utilize versus the types of HASS normatively defined for each population segment over a 3-month period from the point of hospital discharge.Primary Hypothesis: The concordance between the actual utilization of different types of HASS versus normative HASS is not better than fair. Secondary Aim: to assess the association between concordance of normative HASS and incidence of adverse outcomes which includes emergency department visits, unplanned hospital readmissions, nursing home placement, and all-cause mortality over a 12-month period from point of hospital discharge for all population segments. Secondary Hypothesis: Patients with disagreement between normative HASS and actual utilization of HASS will have higher incidence of adverse outcomes.Methodology We will use a modified-Delphi methodology to develop HASS norms and conduct a follow-up study of inpatients to evaluate the concordance between the types of HASS utilized and norm HASS, and to evaluate the association between this concordance and adverse outcomes in each population segment.
kw: population segmentation, health and social service needs

title: Development of a novel utility measure using discrete choice experiments to assess the impact of glaucoma treatments from the patient’s perspective
abs: The prevalence of glaucoma is estimated to reach 80 million by 2020, and half of the world’s glaucoma cases will live in Asia. In Asian ethnicities, glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness. It is currently difficult to assess the cost-effectiveness of treatment modalities for glaucoma because generic utility instruments, such as the ED-5D, lack content relevant to glaucoma. In preliminary work, we have developed the first glaucoma-specific utility instrument (GUI-S) for use in an Asian context, using discrete choice experiment (DCE) methodology. The current proposal aims to psychometrically and clinically validate the GUI-S (Phase 1) and then use the validated instrument to determine the differential impact on utilities of the two main types of glaucoma treatment performed in Singapore (Phase 2). Both phases will be cross-sectional studies where 300 glaucoma patients (in each phase) will be recruited from glaucoma clinics at the Singapore National Eye Centre.Our specific aims are:Aim 1: To administer the GUI-S to glaucoma patients and estimate overall utility values for all possible health states defined by the GUI-S instrument.-Hypothesis: Utility values will be higher for better health states and lower for worse health states in the GUI-S.Aim 2: To determine how well the GUI-S discriminates across glaucoma severity levels (criterion validity) and correlates with other multi-attribute utility instruments (MAUIs) (convergent validity).-Hypothesis: The GUI-S will have acceptable criterion and convergent validity. Aim 3: Using the validated GUI-S, to understand the cross-sectional impact on utilities of two different glaucoma treatment modalities (i.e. topical eye drops only; and combined phacoemulsification/trabeculectomy surgery phaco-trab] without eye drops).-Hypothesis: Utility values will be higher in the phaco-trab group compared to the eye drop group due to a less complex treatment regimen and fewer side effects.
kw: Glaucoma, Utility, Quality of life, Patient-reported outcome measure, Validation

title: Diabetes Lifestyle Intervention using Technology Empowerment (D'LITE Study)
abs: The aim of this project is develop and evaluate a Smartphone Mobile App and Remote Programme in Behavioural, Diet and Lifestyle Interventions for Prevention and Management of Early Diabetes and Pre-Diabetes. The increasing prevalence of Diabetes is a major concern in Singapore and many countries around the world. Current treatment of Diabetes is reactive and often late in the disease process, leading to higher healthcare cost. Management of Diabetes needs to move upstream to the prevention of disease, screening and early detection of those at-risk (or Pre-diabetes), and then optimal control of the condition once it has been diagnosed to prevent further complications downstream. Diet and exercise are considered fundamental in the prevention and management of early Diabetes. There are major gaps in the current intervention for those screened and newly diagnosed or at risk. Current methods of follow-up are resource-intensive, costly, time-consuming, have high default rate and limited reach, and are not scalable to the population needing it, even as community health screening increase in frequency and reach. They also do not tackle the root causes of the problem, which are essentially poor diet and lifestyle habits. Our hypothesis is that a locally developed and targeted Smartphone Mobile App, combined with remote coaching, will be able to: (1) effect positive changes in health-related behaviours and lifestyle choices, (2) prevent and manage diabetes at scale, (3) significantly improve health outcomes and save costs. The methodology and approach would be to: (a) develop a Smartphone Mobile App and Remote Intervention Programme targeting Pre-diabetes and Diabetes, (b) conduct qualitative and quantitative studies on the App and Remote Intervention Programme in terms of actual utilisation and efficacy in effecting behavioural change, (c) conduct randomised controlled trials to compare health outcomes, (d) evaluate this innovative approach versus traditional approaches, including a cost-effectiveness analysis.

title: HOMe-based HEart Failure Self-Management Programme Study (The HOM-HEMP Study): A Randomised Controlled Trial
abs: AimsThe primary aims of this study are to develop and examine the effectiveness of a nurse-led, home-based self-management psychosocial education programme with integration of a smartphone app, entitled HOMe-based HEart Failure Self-Management Programme (HOM-HEMP), on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), anxiety and depression symptoms, self-efficacy, self-care behavior, social support and clinical outcomes including unplanned service use among older patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) in Singapore. The study also aims to explore the usability and effect of the component of mHealth (i.e. smartphone App) on the above study outcomes by comparing Experimental Group A (HOM-HEMP without App) and B (HOM-HEMP with App).Methodology The HOM-HEMP is designed a six-week home-based psychosocial education programme comprising of a specifically developed Heart Manual and a supplementary smartphone app. A stratified, three-arm randomised controlled trial will be used. A consecutive sample of 213 older patients with CHF will be recruited from the Cardiac Wards of National University Hospital. They will be randomly assigned to the control group, or experimental group A (HOM-HEMP without App) or the experimental group B (HOM-HEMP with App). A research nurse will be delivering the HOM-HEMP to the participants in the experimental groups, while another research assistant who is blinded to participants’ group assignment will be responsible for data collection. Data will be collected at baseline, at 6 weeks immediate after the intervention, and at 3 and 6 months from the baseline. At the end of the programme, a process evaluation will be conducted to assess the acceptability, strengths and weaknesses of the HOM-HEMP based on the participants’ perspectives. IBM SPSS 24.0 will be used to analyse all quantitative data, while content analysis will be used for qualitative datasets. We hope this project will add new option for health care deliveries to further inform health care policy in Singapore

title: Identification of women at high-risk of breast cancer in Singapore: Towards more effective primary prevention
abs: Currently, breast cancer screening is broadly based on age – all women above age 40 are recommended to attend mammography screening. Early detection of breast cancer is known to save lives. However, the benefit of mammography screening in Singapore is negated by low participation rate and adherence – only 66% of the target group of women ever had a mammogram, and half of them do not come back for screening at regular intervals. My studies aim to address the rising breast cancer incidence in Singapore and lukewarm response to mammography screening (low participation and adherence) by identifying high-risk women, through integrating mammographic density, lifestyle and genetic data. While lifestyle factors have been extensively studied in Western populations, the full range of genetic factors for breast cancer, and how they can be combined with other risk factors such as mammographic density to best predict risk in Asian populations, is still unknown. My research program will concentrate on understanding of the mammographic density as a step in identifying women at high risk of breast cancer in Singapore. The specific questions that I ask are: I) How important is mammographic density as a breast cancer risk/prognostic factor to different ethnic groups? II) Why do women with dense breasts have higher risk of developing breast cancer? III) What are the determinants of mammographic density? IV) Are there environmental effect modifiers of mammographic density? V) Apart from signature breast cancer genes (BRCA1/2), can we use other breast cancer genes for risk-based screening? The effectiveness of breast cancer prevention in terms of cost and lives saved can be substantially enhanced through targeting prevention at those most likely to benefit. Singapore has the potential to take the lead in a paradigm shift in breast cancer screening, by taking a risk-based approach over the conventional age-based regime.
kw: primary prevention;human genetics;mammographic density;mammography screening;epidemiology;risk prediction

title: Multivalent Energy Storage for a Sustainable Future: A Quest beyond Lithium-Ion Technologies
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Creating a sustainable energy future while protecting our environment is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. As we move towards renewable but intermittent energy sources such as solar and wind power, we need advanced battery systems that can store excess energy during peak production and release it on demand during times of shortfall, in order to power homes, industries, electric vehicles, etc. Unfortunately, lithium-ion batteries, which are commonly used in small portable electronics today, are unable to meet the high-energy demands of these large-scale stationary and mobile applications. My vision is to go beyond conventional lithium-ion technologies and develop high-energy batteries based on multivalent ions such as magnesium (Mg2+) and aluminum (Al3+), which not only carry 2 or 3 times the charge of lithium (Li+) per ion, but are also 30 to 50 times cheaper than lithium. As a result, magnesium- and aluminum-ion batteries can potentially offer energy densities that are 3 to 4 times higher than lithium-ion batteries today at a much lower cost. In this proposal, I will study multivalent magnesium– and aluminum–sulfur batteries in-operando (during real-time battery operation) for the first time to elucidate their underlying electrochemical mechanisms. These complex mechanisms are not well understood, yet they are crucial to improving the poor cycling performance of such batteries today. In particular, I will carry out in-operando transmission electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy to investigate electrochemical plating and stripping in magnesium/aluminum anodes (-) as well as dissolution and structural changes in sulfur cathodes (+). The overarching goal is to generate new scientific knowledge that will provide insight towards materials design for the development of high-performance multivalent battery prototypes. Such batteries have the potential to transform the global energy storage landscape and lead to widespread adoption of renewable energy for a sustainable future.

title: Comparing a convenient positional therapy device to CPAP for treatment of positional obstructive sleep apnea, a crossover randomized controlled trial
abs: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with cardiovascular risks and significant daytime sleepiness that impair function and quality of life.The first line treatment is continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy but many patients struggle with it. Studies found poor CPAP adherence and patient acceptance. Reasons include treatment inconvenience, significant side effects and cost. Up to 75% of Asian OSA patients have ‘positional OSA’ where breathing abnormalities are reduced in a non-supine sleeping position. For these patients, positional therapy (PT), the avoidance of supine sleep, is an attractive strategy. However, traditional PT methods have failed as they were cumbersome and poorly tolerated. Recently, convenient and affordable PT devices have been invented. Preliminary studies suggest they are efficacious in reducing breathing abnormalities with high rates of treatment adherence.However, there is no published randomized controlled trial comparing these devices to CPAP. The objective of our study is to evaluate if a convenient PT device is non-inferior to CPAP in the treatment of positional OSA. Our primary aim is to measure changes in daytime sleepiness with the Epworth sleepiness scale between the two treatments. We plan to recruit 40 positional OSA patients in a crossover randomized controlled trial. Each 20-patient group will crossover to the alternative intervention after 8 weeks with a 1 week washout period. Our secondary aim is to measure changes in quality of life and the apnea hypopnea index (AHI), as well as to compare treatment adherence and patient preference. Without loss of treatment efficacy but with higher adherence, PT devices can be offered as first line treatment to positional OSA patients, many of whom are struggling with current standard CPAP. As a cost-effective, accessible and convenient solution, wider adoption is expected. This potentially reduces cardiovascular risks, improves quality of life of the individual and has significant socioeconomic benefits.

title: Randomized controlled trial of LUtein as a novel Neuroprotective Adjunctive therapy to improve visual outcome of rhegmatogenous Retinal detachment (LUNAR Trial)
abs: Retinal detachment is a major cause of blindness, particularly among contemporary Asian populations due to the high prevalence of myopia. Without timely treatment, retinal detachment invariably results in blindness. As the only effective treatment is surgery, much effort has been invested to enhancing surgical outcome of retinal detachment repair. Advances in new instrumentations, viewing systems and refined surgical techniques have all contributed to improved rate of retinal re-attachment (anatomical outcome). Nevertheless, successful re-attachment of the retina after surgery does not always restore vision (visual outcome), especially when retinal detachment involves the macula (“macula-off” retinal detachment). The reason for poor visual outcome is believed to be due to apoptosis of photoreceptors, which may occur early and rapidly after the onset of retinal detachment. Neuroprotection has therefore been considered a valid strategy to improve visual outcome of retinal detachment surgery. Lutein is a promising potent neuroprotective agent for the retina, and has been shown in preliminary clinical and laboratory studies that it could salvage photorecepters in retinal detachment. We hypothesize that oral intake of lutein soon after onset of retinal detachment could prevent photoreceptor neurons from dying and thus limit the loss of vision. To test such hypothesis, we propose to conduct a double-masked, randomized controlled trial to evaludate the efficacy of lutein as an adjuvant therapy to improve visual outcome for surgical repair of primary rhematogenous retinal detachment involving the macula in Asian Singaporeans. The potential clinical and scientific significance of this trial is clear. It may provide first evidence that pharmacological neuroprotection can be used as an effective therapeutic modality in the clinical management of retinal detachment, and result in a paradigm shift in clinical practice, ultimately leading to better visual outcome and quality of life for patients undertaking surgical repair of retinal detachment.

title: Mechanistic investigation of the regulatory role of dengue virus subgenomic RNA on epidemiological fitness.
abs: The four serotypes of dengue virus (DENV-1 to -4) results in 400 million infections annually. The sole dengue vaccine that has been licensed in several countries have limited efficacy in protecting against infection. Consequently, the partial immunity in vaccinated individuals may exert unique evolutionary pressure on DENV upon infection that drives emergence of strains with increased epidemiological fitness. Understanding the genetic determinants of epidemiological fitness would thus be important for identifying DENV strains with greater potential for epidemic spread. We have recently identified nucleotide changes in the 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) that altered production of subgenomic flavivirus RNA (sfRNA) and showed mechanstically that sfRNA binds TRIM25 to inhibit type-I interferon (IFN) expression for improved DENV fitness. This sfRNA-mediated inhibition of interferon induction, in part, explains the molecular basis of the 1994 dengue outbreak in Puerto Rico. Our findings thus provide unique mechanistic insights into the determinants of epidemiological fitness of DENV. Herein, we propose to build upon our seminal findings and extend our investigation to examine how sfRNA shape DENV evolution and epidemiology at a global scale. We will determine the interactome of sfRNA from different strains of DENV with clearly documented epidemiological or clinical phenotypes, both in human cells and Aedes mosquitoes. Molecular investigations on the key host proteins that bind DENV sfRNA will then clarify the function of such interactions and how they contribute mechanistically to enable epidemiological fitness. Such detailed understanding of the sfRNA-host protein interactions and how they regulate DENV fitness epidemiologically would enable evidence-based approach to target public health measures on DENV strains with greater potential for epidemic spread. Such an approach would augment exisiting dengue prevention efforts through vector control and complement virologic surveillance efforts in a post-dengue vaccination era.

title: Development of a Point-of-Care Test to Diagnose Zika Virus Infection
inst: IBN - Institute of Bioengineering and Nanotechnology
abs: Zika virus is an emerging infectious agent with severe socioeconomic impact due to its potential interference in fetal brain development. The rapid and accurate diagnosis of Zika infections is an essential component of overall public health strategy for managing and containing this disease. Accurate diagnosis of Zika infection is complicated by its similarity to dengue fever, another viral disease that is prevalent in Southeast Asia. We aim to develop a diagnostic kit based on the lateral flow assay for rapid and cost-effective diagnosis of Zika infections at the point-of-care setting. We will generate specific antibodies that can detect the Zika NS1, a likely early biomarker of Zika infection, without cross-reactivity to dengue or other Flaviviruses. In addition, we will generate viral proteins that will specifically capture anti-Zika IgM and IgG for serological tests to diagnose the later phase of the infection. The dual test approach has been successfully used to diagnose dengue infections and should be applicable to the diagnosis of Zika infections. The paper-based rapid assays will be validated by assessing clinical samples that have been diagnosed for dengue or Zika by the polymerase chain reaction. We aim to advance our rapid test to market with the help of commercial partners.

title: Development of multiple serological platforms for differentiation of Zika and dengue virus infections
abs: Although it is not a totally new virus, the recent outbreaks and rapid global spread of Zika virus (ZIKV) has caught the international community by surprise. There are many challenges in the response to the ZIKV outbreaks internationally, and more recently in Singapore. One of them is the lack of a reliable serological diagnostic method. This is highly important for ZIKV infection because most infected individuals don’t develop clinical symptoms, hence will likely miss the narrow window of laboratory diagnosis based on virus detection, and there is significant antibody cross reactivity between ZIKV and other flaviviruses, especially dengue virus (DENV). With the increasing evidence linking ZIKV infection and neurological disorders such as microcephaly and Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS), there is an urgent need for serodiagnosis of ZIKV infection, especially among pregnant women. Traditional serological tests, mostly ELISA based, using various ZIKV antigens have encountered major problem of cross reactivity with antibodies from other flavivirus infection. Here we proposed to address this major gap and urgent need using multiple new technology platforms which address the main cross reactivity issue by replacing the conventional one-antigen-one-reading antibody test format with a multiplex format which will give comparative readings on multiple antigens. For this study, we will focus on our development of differentiation serological tests for ZIKV and DENV specifically, but the same strategy and technological platforms can be extended to other viruses in future. One of the approaches employed in this proposal will target ZIKV infection-specific anti-host antibodies which will not only serve as novel biomarkers for serological diagnosis, but may also shed new light to better understanding of ZIKV pathogenesis.

title: A Non Human Primate model for intrauterine haemopoietic stem cell transplantation for beta-globinopathies
abs: Inherited monogenic diseases affect one-percent of births, many of which causes irreversible pathology in-utero or perinatally. Intrauterine therapy is an evolving strategy with several advantages over post-natal approaches due to unique ontological opportunities existing only during fetal life such as ability to induce donor-specific tolerance (DST) and avoid immune rejection. We have established a developmentally, physiologically and clinically-relevant non-human primate (NHP) model for intrauterine gene transfer applicable to enzyme deficiency syndromes, but not to haemopoietic disorders. Here we extend our studies to explore intrauterine haemopoietic stem cell therapy (IUHSCT) of relevance to thalassemia. The hypotheses are that (i) development of self-tolerance occurs at 0.45 gestation in the fetal macaque, and (ii) that IUHSCT around this time will lead to long-term donor HSC engraftment and DST at curative levels for thalassaemia (~20%). Specifically we will:1.Establish the immune ontogeny of fetal macaques between 0.3-0.6 gestation to determine the critical time where thymic processing of self-antigen and development of self-tolerance is achieved.2.Test the ability of IUHSCT to achieve DST and curative level of engraftment for thalassaemia in NHP with or without post-natal boosting, and map immune responses through immuno-monitoring.The successful completion of this proposal will guide the development of a clinical protocol for IUHSCT for ?-thalassaemia, a disease of high priority in our region. By addressing IUHSCT in these clinically-relevant models, we address a range of genetic diseases of perinatal onset and/or where no curative or satisfactory post-natal treatment exists. This approach would be applicable to genetic disesaes for which HSC transplantation is of benefit.

title: Elucidating the modulatory effects of anti-inflammatory therapy on immune cell metabolism and ER stress.
abs: With close human-animal interaction from shrinking natural habitats, outbreaks with previously unknown zoonotic pathogens are emerging at a quickened pace. New vaccines are slow to develop in the pipeline from lack of monetary incentives. Alternatives such as drugs that can alter host responses that contribute to pathogenesis, are potential strategies to reduce disease burden. I haverecently unravelled the determinants that differentiate symptomatic from asymptomatic viral infection outcome using the Yellow Fever live attenuated vaccine (YFLAV). Symptomatic individuals, unlike those who remain without symptoms, respond to infection with an early activation of the innate immune response. Higher viral burden as indicated by viraemia levels were not associated with symptomatic infection, supporting my hypothesis that host factors underpin the early activation of innate immune response to YFLAV infection. I have further defined a susceptibility factor for symptomatic infection: Transcriptomic and metabolomic data from my current CSA work revealed that lymphocytes of subjects with symptomatic infection had elevated levels of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress with metabolic compensation as adaptation. Upon YFLAV infection, increased metabolic demand results in maladaptive ER stress that triggers reactive oxygen species (ROS) response. This resultant oxidative stress initiates early innate immune and proimflammatory responses. Metformin, a comonly used drug for diabetes and obesity with a wide therapeutic window, has immunomodulating activity which I postulate could sustain adaptive ER stress despite infection to attenuate the inflammatory response that drives symptomatic outcome. Metformin prophylaxis could form a first line defense against any emerging infection to reduce overall disease burden without the need for a definite pathogen-specific therapeutic. This proposal aims to demonstrate the modulation of metformin on immune cell metabolism and ER stress in healthy volunteers.
kw: Vaccine, Live attenuated

title: Comparison of the role of epidural analgesia versus non-epidural analgesia in postnatal depression and persistent pain development: a randomized controlled trial CODEPAD (Collaborative Outcomes of DEpression and Pain Associated with Delivery)
abs: Postnatal depression (PND) affects 15% of women resulting in severe socioeconomic burden, maternal suicide risk and associated with newborn cognitive impairment. Our pilot cohort study found that PND was present in 12.7% (62/490) at KK Hospital and epidural analgesia as an independent risk factor (10.0%) that reduced the risk of PND by nearly half compared to those who chose non-epidural analgesia (19.3%) (p=0.037,OR=1.95). Persistent pain (PP) after childbirth affects 10% of women resulting in poor recovery and functional disability. Severe labour pain mediated by oxytocin may activate central sensitization especially in women with pain and psychological vulnerability with central nervous system pathway dysregulation, as possible pathophysiologic mechanisms, resulting in PND and PP.The primary aim is to determine whether epidural analgesia compared to non-epidural analgesia will reduce the risk of PND. We will also determine the association of PND and PP and construct a model with risk factors such as psychological vulnerability (fear-avoidance, anxiety, stress), pain vulnerability (pain catastrophizing, central sensitization), pain severity and analgesic choice that influence PND and PP development. The interplay of psychological and pain pathways will also be investigated through targeted serotonin, monoamine and oxytocin candidate gene polymorphism approach, for PND and PP. We will recruit 1326 term women at KK Hospital in this randomized controlled trial. A phone survey will be performed at 6 to 10 weeks post-natal to determine the primary outcome of PND, PP and investigate the possible association of both.This trial could produce results that recommend revisions in the use of epidural analgesia, as well as, elucidate psychobiological basis for PND and PP. The relationship between PND and PP will guide us in future studies on model validation, potential novel risk stratification and identify modifiable risk factors as therapeutic targets.
kw: epidural analgesia, childbirth, depression, pain

title: Translational Research in Vascular Biomarkers of Dementia: Discovery, Validation and Assessment of Clinical Utility
abs: Due to increasing recognition of the pathogenic role of small vessel disease in both vascular dementia (VaD) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the overarching aim of this renewal application is to extend work done in the last CSA to (i) discover novel markers of vascular function and disease; and (ii) assess the clinical utility of vascular biomarkers. This proposal consists of:Project 1 – Postmortem studies Cerebrovascular disease (CeVD) is a common pathological finding in the brains of dementia patients, but the nature and extent of their involvement in dementias remain unclear. Here, we propose a combination of histological, proteonomic and lipidomic approaches to study the biochemical substrates of CeVD in AD and VaD brain tissues.Project 2 – Peripheral biomarkers of CeVD in cognitive impairmentInformed by data from Project 1, and leveraging on a large, longitudinal study of local elderly subjects (also led by the PI), we propose to study putative markers of vascular diseases, and correlate with changes in neuroimaging and neuropsychological assessments to evaluate their utility in predicting cognitive decline and CeVD development.Project 3 – Peripheral biomarkers as predictors for the development of AD in diabetic patientsGiven the well-known associations between Type II diabetes mellitus (T2DM), vascular disease and dementia, this project proposes to measure, in the longitudinal cohort, a wide range of serum biomarkers associated with inflammation, T2DM and AD, in order to elucidate shared, novel patho-mechanisms in T2DM and AD. The three projects are designed to be highly complementary and to leverage on existing studies, resources and collaborations. It is expected that the projects will provide validated, clinically useful biomarkers, and add further insight into the pathogenic role of CeVD in cognitive impairment and dementia.

title: A randomised controlled trial of annual versus biannual influenza vaccination in the elderly
abs: Haemagglutination-inhibition (HI) titres and seroprotection levels (HI?1:40) decline steadily in the elderly following vaccination with the standard-dose inactivated trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine (IIV3) in the elderly. Within 6-12 months, levels are not significantly different from pre-vaccination. The pattern of influenza infections is different in Singapore and other tropical countries compared to temperate climates. Biannual epidemics and year-round virus activity is commonly observed. Year-round seroprotection is likely to be important to reduce influenza infections in this environment.The core of this research proposal is a randomized, observer-blind, active-comparator controlled, single-centre, Phase IV trial in 200 participants. Adult aged ?65 years will be enrolled and assigned to one of two groups in a 1:1 ratio. The control group will receive IIV3 at day 1, and an active-comparator (Tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis vaccine) at day 180. Participants in the experimental group will receive IIV3 containing the same influenza strains at day 1 and day 180. Endpoints are immunological, and include measures of HI and viral micro-neutralization titres at 4 time points after the initial vaccination up to Day 360. Plasma and peripheral-blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) will also be stored for exploration of immunosenescence and inflammaging. The primary statistical hypothesis is that there is no difference in the proportion of participants sero-protected at day 208 post-initial vaccination in the experimental compared with control group. Participants will be monitored for PCR-confirmed influenza infection and unscheduled healthcare utilization throughout their involvement in the study. If a day 180 booster improves year-round seroprotection, the TROPICS1 trial will provide the basis for a larger clinical trial to confirm a reduction in influenza infection rates. This has the potential for a significant public health impact.
kw: Influenza; Seasonal; Vaccine; Elderly; Tropics

title: Retinal cell therapy for Age-related Macular Degeneration
abs: Aims: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) lacks effective treatment and in recent years replacement of pathological retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) with healthy tissue has been studied. Traditionally available stem cell therapy using RPE derived from human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) and human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) is associated with immunogenicity, mutagenesis, and ethical concerns. More recently, a sub-population of RPE cells in the retina has been identified to have proliferative potential, namely adult human RPE (ahRPE).Our project aims to improve the current ahRPE cell product by making it serum-free. Secondly, we seek to develop a more efficient method to generate clinical grade homogeneous ahRPE cells.Hypotheses: We hypothesize that ahRPE is the ideal cell source for human transplantation therapy. AhRPE is isolated and cultured from recently deceased adult human donors and can be expanded to RPE with morphological, phenotypic, and functional characteristics similar to native RPE.Approach of the research proposal: Our approach is to understand and study the difference in biology of ahRPE cells from fully differentiated RPE cells using advanced molecular tools. This will allow us to gain further insight into how ahRPE subpopulations can be more effectively differentiated and cultured.Methodology: We have obtained robust protocol to dissect ahRPE from human cadavers which can be maintained in vitro, and has features of native RPE. We will also identify unique surface markers for ahRPE using fluorescent probes to help us isolate ahRPE stem cells more effectively. We plan to study the biology and physiology of ahRPE cells using molecular biological tools. This includes single cell RNA-seq and single cell Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin seq, secretomes analysis and immunostaining. Finally, we will establish functional assays to ensure that our ahRPE culture is of clinical grade. This will include immunohistochemistry, gene expression profiling and measurement of trans-epithelial resistance. We will use RPE derived from hESCs and hiPSCs as well ARPE-19 cell line as controls.
kw: adult-human-RPE, age-related macular degeneration, cell therapy

title: Repurposing Trimetazidine to Treat Cancer Cachexia
abs: Cancer cachexia is an unmet medical need with limited therapeutic options. In advanced cancer, cachexia is present in up to 50% of patients and contributes to 25% of deaths. Using both human and murine cachexia models, we recently found that fatty acid oxidation (FAO) drives cancer cachexia. Pharmacological inhibition of FAO with etomoxir rescued muscle and weight loss in three different in vivo models. However, etomoxir is not approved for human use because of concerns over hepatotoxicitiy Trimetazidine is an safe and widely used drug forangina pectoris that also has activity as a FAO inhibitor. Our proposal seeks to evaluate the potential of repurposing trimetazidine in the treatment and prevention of cancer cachexia.Specific Aim 1: We seek to determine the efficacy of trimetazidine in maintaining or rescuing muscle mass and body weight in preclinical models of cancer cachexia. To do so, we will administer trimetazidine at different doses in three well-established murine models of cancer cachexia. We will also initiate trimetazidine treatment at different time intervals (before, during and after onset of cachexia). In doing so, we will evaluate the effectiveness of trimetazidine in preventing or treating cancer cachexia.Specific Aim 2: We seek to investigate the pharmacodynamic/metaboliceffect of different dose-schedules of trimetazidine on biomarkers of FAO in cancer patients. To do so, we will evaluate safety and serial metabolic alterations in FAO activity in four different cohorts of cancer patients (one without treatment and three at different doses of trimetazidine). Data on weight, muscle strength and quality of life will also be collected.Together, efficacy signals of trimetazidine in treating cachexia in preclinical models, and the clinical pharmacodynamic and metabolic effects of trimetazidine at different doses in patients will inform the design of a phase 2 clinical trial to repurpose trimetazidine to treat cancer cachexia.
kw: Fatty acid oxidation inhibition, Cancer Cachexia

title: Fighting the Superbugs: Development & Use of a Rapid Identification Pathway for Antibiotic combination Therapy against Extensively Drug-resistant Gram-negative Bacteria (XDR-GNB) Infections
abs: The advent of Extensively drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (XDRGNB-Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae) infections is a well-recognized problem in Singapore and worldwide hospitals. Infections with XDR-GNB are difficult to treat and have been associated with mortality rates as high as 40-50%. As there is a significant mortality benefit to administering appropriate and adequate therapy in a timely manner and XDR-GNB is usually sensitive to polymyxin B (last-line agent) only, routine laboratory tests that indicate resistance to all antibiotics are not helpful. As there are no more new antibiotics in the pipeline for XDRGNB, combination therapy has been advocated to be the mainstay treatment strategy. Therefore, identifying appropriate antimicrobial treatment are increasingly paramount and clinicians are presented with the challenge of selecting overwhelming permutations of antibiotic combinations and dosing regimens for patients. Antibiotic combination therapy has become the preferred empirical therapy against XDR-GNB. The time-consuming pathway of new drug development and approval coupled with well-known renal toxicities of polymyxins make it compelling to develop and assimilate a diagnostic and clinical algorithm in hospitals to identify and administer appropriate antimicrobial combinations to XDR-GNB infected patients in a timely manner.This proposal aims to study the feasibility of identifying bactericidal antibiotic combinations within 30h of XDR-GNB identification from clinical specimens via in vitro combination susceptibility tests that utilises ATP bioluminescence detection to quantify bacteria cells. The results will serve to improve the institution of appropriate antibiotic combination treatment against XDR-GNB infections and patient outcomes. This technology can be spurned off for commercialisation, which will be in high demand in transplant and oncological medicine. The development of this translational pathway can gain efficiency by assimilation in various healthcare institutions nationwide.
kw: Antibiotic combination therapy, Extensively Drug-resistant Gram-negative Bacteria Infections

title: Comparing a convenient positional therapy device to CPAP for treatment of positional obstructive sleep apnea, a crossover randomized controlled trial.
abs: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with cardiovascular risks and significant daytime sleepiness that impair function and quality of life. The first line treatment is continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy but many patients struggle with it. Studies found poor CPAP adherence and patient acceptance. Reasons include treatment inconvenience, significant side effects and cost. Up to 75% of Asian OSA patients have ‘positional OSA’ where breathing abnormalities are reduced in a non-supine sleeping position. For these patients, positional therapy (PT), the avoidance of supine sleep, is an attractive strategy. However, traditional PT methods have failed as they were cumbersome and poorly tolerated. Recently, convenient and affordable PT devices have been invented. Preliminary studies suggest they are efficacious in reducing breathing abnormalities with high rates of treatment adherence. However, there is no published randomized controlled trial comparing these devices to CPAP. The objective of our study is to evaluate if a convenient PT device is non-inferior to CPAP in the treatment of positional OSA. Our primary aim is to measure changes in daytime sleepiness with the Epworth sleepiness scale between the two treatments. We plan to recruit 40 positional OSA patients in a crossover randomized controlled trial. Each 20-patient group will crossover to the alternative intervention after 8 weeks with a 1 week washout period. Our secondary aim is to measure changes in quality of life and the apnea hypopnea index (AHI), as well as to compare treatment adherence and patient preference. Without loss of treatment efficacy but with higher adherence, PT devices can be offered as first line treatment to positional OSA patients, many of whom are struggling with current standard CPAP. As a cost-effective, accessible and convenient solution, wider adoption is expected. This potentially reduces cardiovascular risks, improves quality of life of the individual and has significant socioeconomic benefits.
kw: obstructive sleep apnea, positional therapy, sleep disordered breathing

title: Mechanism study of CoQ2 gene mutation in multiple system atrophy using induced pluripotent stem cell model
abs: Multiple system atrophy is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive autonomic failure, parkinsonism, cerebellar and pyramidal tract symptoms. Glial cytoplasmic inclusions of alpha-synuclein are a defining histologic feature. The pathophysiological mechanism underlying this disease is unknown, as there lack systematic function studies. Inspired by the successful modelling of other neurodegenerative disease – Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson’s disease and Huntington's disease with patient specific induced pluripotent stem cells, here we propose to study the multiple system atrophy pathogenesis mechanism using local MSA patient induced pluripotent stem cells. The aims include: 1) Set up the in vitro disease model of multiple system atrophy using CoQ2 V393A patient specific induced pluripotent stem cells derived neurons; 2) To investigate the roles of CoQ2 gene variant in human MSA pathogenesis using in vitro MSA cellular model. Currently, no therapy can reverse or halt progression of this disease. There is no effective neuroprotective therapy in MSA. Symptomatic treatment is restricted largely to parkinsonism and dysautonomia. This study will set up a specific disease model of MSA with CoQ2 gene mutation, further our standing of the pathogenesis of this disease, and contribute to early detection of the disease and identification of specific therapeutic targets.
kw: Multiple system atrophy, CoQ2, induced pluripotent stem cell, disease model

title: Optimizing the thrombectomy device and patient in acute stroke
abs: Introduction: Raised carbon-dioxide (CO2) vasodilates blood vessels. In acute ischemic stroke (AIS) this shunts blood away from the ischemic penumbra, with its already maximally dilated vessels, to less important areas resulting in larger infarcts. Aims: To determine if controlling the blood CO2 concentration in acute stroke will be able to prevent vasodilation of the surrounding non-ischemic regions and maintain perfusion to the ischemic penumbra.We adopt a 2-prong approach i) evaluating the relationship between the blood PaCO2 level, the size of the DWI infarct and perfusion imaging and ii) evaluating the relationship between the blood PaCO2 level and microRNA biomarker levels as a potential biomarker to diagnose or even prognosticate ischemic stroke. If the study is successful, it will pave the way for trials of altering CO2 levels to be used as a new modality in acute ischemic stroke treatment. Hypothesis: By controlling the CO2 concentration in AIS rats, we will be able to study the effect it has on the evolution of the infarct. We hypothesize that as blood PaCO2 level increases, the size of the DWI infarct and perfusion imaging will correspondingly increase. Simultaneously, we will obtain serial serum samples for microRNA analysis and correlate with serial MRI infarct size to develop a prognostic marker. methodology & Approach: Using 60 Sprague-Dawley rats, we will subject them to various CO2 concentrations (0-12%) until a steady PaCO2 state is observed in the blood gases. We will then induce cortical ischemia by endovascularly occluding the middle cerebral artery (M2). We will then perform serial MRI and MR-perfusion scans at hourly intervals up to 6 hours with concurrent serum samples obtained for microRNA analysis. After 6 hours, the rats will be euthanized and the brain tissue from the infarcted and contralateral normal side will be sent for evaluation by microRNA analysis.
kw: ischemic stroke, perfusion, pneumbra, MRI, MicroRNA, Sprague–Dawley rats

title: Role of IGF-1 Hormone in Modulating Noncoding RNAs in Oestrogen-Dependent Carcinomas
abs: Ovarian carcinoma is the leading cause of death among gynaecological tumours in Singapore. Endometriosis affects between 5% and 20% of women in their reproductive age with 1% undergoing malignant transformation to ovarian carcinomas of clear cell (OCCC) and endometrioid (ENOCa) histotypes. ARID1a mutation drives the transformation in 50% of OCCC and 30% of tumours. The exact driver(s) in ARID1a wild-type tumours remains uncertain. Epigenetic methylation, causing reversible and heritable changes in the gene expression due to DNA methylation without changes to the DNA sequences, may play a role. Our aims are to discover genomic mutations and epigenomic methylation changes in 1) a control “endometriosis” discovery set of women with severe endometriosis to establish baseline changes and 2) a “tumour” discovery set of chemonaive low and high stage OCC and ENOCa in comparison with assessment of ARID1a mutation status. The initial hypothesis is that epigenetic changes can drive malignant transformation in ARID1a wild-type tumours. Findings from the discovery set will allow for more incisive hypothesis generation. Our method is to perform laser capture microdissection on fresh tissue of eutopic and ectopic endometrial tissue, primary chemonaive OCCC and ENOCa for epigenome wide study with the Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip array and whole exome sequencing using the Nextera Rapid Capture Exome and Expanded Exome Kit. Unsupervised analysis will be used to identify potential genomic and epigenomic hotspots for validation and further study. Our approach is to use next generationg sequencing, the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip and Nextera Rapid Capture Exome and Expanded Exome kits. The clinical significance is to discover potential epigenomic changes driving malignant transformation to serve as potential diagnostic, screening or prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
kw: Endometriosis; Ovarian carcinoma; Malignancy transformation

title: Metabolomics in central nervous system inflammatory demyelinating disorders associated with myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies: Identifying biomarkers and exploring pathogenic pathways
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD) are a group of central nervous system (CNS) inflammatory demyelinating disorders (IDD) with clinical features overlapping with multiple sclerosis (MS). Approximately 70% of NMOSD patients have serum antibodies against aquaporin-4 (AQP4-Abs). AQP4 serostatus is used to distinguish NMOSD from MS as treatment differs. This distinction is challenging for AQP4-Abs seronegative NMOSD patients. A subset of seronegative patients has recently been described to have antibodies against myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG-Abs). MOG-Abs has also been described in acute demyelinating encephalomyelitis (ADEM) and MS. It is currently unknown if MOG-Abs represents a distinct disease, and biomarkers to monitor disease activity and guide treatment are lacking. Metabolomics is the large-scale study of metabolites, small molecules representing the downstream expression of genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics. Recently, metabolomics is able to separate relapsing remitting MS (RRMS) from secondary progressive MS. This novel approach has huge potential to identify biomarkers and disease pathways in CNS IDD. We hypothesize that metabolomics can; identify biomarkers in MOG-Abs NMOSD that can predict treatment response, demonstrate that NMOSD and ADEM patients with MOG-Abs have the same metabolic profile, demonstrate that MOG-Abs NMOSD patients have a distinctive metabolic profile different from RRMS and AQP4-Abs NMOSD patients.We will perform metabolomics to compare; MOG-Abs NMOSD patients grouped by treatment response, NMOSD and ADEM patients who have MOG-Abs, MOG-Abs NMOSD against AQP4-Ab NMOSD and RRMS patients. We will phenotype MOG-Abs NMOSD patients by identifying clinico-radiological characteristics, demographic factors, treatments and their effect on outcomes, and contrasting with AQP4-Ab NMOSD and RRMS patients.Clinical data will be obtained from international NMOSD and Oxford MS databases. Metabolomics experiments will be performed using nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and data analyzed by multivariate analysis.We hope this can inform on MOG-Abs pathophysiology and identify biomarkers that can guide treatment and monitor disease activity.
kw: metabolomics, neuromyelitis optica, multiple sclerosis, myelin oligodendrocyte

title: Comparison of the role of epidural analgesia versus non-epidural analgesia in postnatal depression and persistent pain development: a randomized controlled trial (CODEPAD)
abs: Postnatal depression (PND) affects 15% of women resulting in severe socioeconomic burden, maternal suicide risk and associated with newborn cognitive impairment. Our pilot cohort study found that PND was present in 12.7% (62/490) at KK Hospital and epidural analgesia as an independent risk factor (10.0%) that reduced the risk of PND by nearly half compared to those who chose non-epidural analgesia (19.3%) (p=0.037,OR=1.95).Persistent pain (PP) after childbirth affects 10% of women resulting in poor recovery and functional disability. Severe labour pain mediated by oxytocin may activate central sensitization especially in women with pain and psychological vulnerability with central nervous system pathway dysregulation, as possible pathophysiologic mechanisms, resulting in PND and PP.The primary aim is to determine whether epidural analgesia compared to non-epidural analgesia will reduce the risk of PND. We will also determine the association of PND and PP and construct a model with risk factors such as psychological vulnerability (fear-avoidance, anxiety, stress), pain vulnerability (pain catastrophizing, central sensitization), pain severity and analgesic choice that influence PND and PP development. The interplay of psychological and pain pathways will also be investigated through targeted serotonin, monoamine and oxytocin candidate gene polymorphism approach, for PND and PP. We will recruit 1326 term women at KK Hospital in this randomized controlled trial. A phone survey will be performed at 6 to 10 weeks post-natal to determine the primary outcome of PND, PP and investigate the possible association of both. This trial could produce results that recommend revisions in the use of epidural analgesia, as well as, elucidate psychobiological basis for PND and PP. The relationship between PND and PP will guide us in future studies on model validation, potential novel risk stratification and identify modifiable risk factors as therapeutic targets.
kw: Epidural analgesia, childbirth, depression, pain

title: A Non Human Primate model for intrauterine haemopoietic stem cell transplantation for beta- globinopathies
abs: Inherited monogenic diseases affect one-percent of births, many of which causes irreversible pathology in-utero or perinatally. Intrauterine therapy is an evolving strategy with several advantages over post-natal approaches due to unique ontological opportunities existing only during fetal life such as ability to induce donor-specific tolerance (DST) and avoid immune rejection. We have established a developmentally, physiologically and clinically-relevant non-human primate (NHP) model for intrauterine gene transfer applicable to enzyme deficiency syndromes, but not to haemopoietic disorders. Here we extend our studies to explore intrauterine haemopoietic stem cell therapy (IUHSCT) of relevance to thalassemia.The hypotheses are that (i) development of self-tolerance occurs at 0.45 gestation in the fetal macaque, and (ii) that IUHSCT around this time will lead to long-term donor HSC engraftment and DST at curative levels for thalassaemia (~20%). Specifically we will:1. Establish the immune ontogeny of fetal macaques between 0.3-0.6 gestation to determine the critical time where thymic processing of self- antigen and development of self-tolerance is achieved.2. Test the ability of IUHSCT to achieve DST and curative level of engraftment for thalassaemia in NHP with or without post-natal boosting, and map immune responses through immuno-monitoring.The successful completion of this proposal will guide the development of a clinical protocol for IUHSCT for thalassaemia, a disease of high priority in our region. By addressing IUHSCT in these clinically-relevant models, we address a range of genetic diseases of perinatal onset and/or where no curative or satisfactory post-natal treatment exists. This approach would be applicable to genetic disesaes for which HSC transplantation is of benefit.

title: Randomized Control Trial Comparing Proposed Algorithm and Current Best Practice in the Evaluation of Suspected Appendicitis
abs: Although the use of computed tomography (CT) has reduced negative appendectomy rates, its radiation risk remains a concern. Indiscriminate CT utilization subjects patients to unnecessary radiation and contributes to increased healthcare costs. The Alvarado Score (AS) is a clinical scoring system that assesses the likelihood of acute appendicitis based on patient history, physical examination findings and blood investigations.Based on analysis of a prospective database of 500 consecutive patients admitted to the Department of General Surgery for suspected appendicitis, we compared the diagnostic performance measures for CT scan and the AS and identified ranges where patients were unlikely to benefit from CT evaluation. We thus propose an algorithm for the management of acute appendicitis using the AS to guide CT utilization (Figure 1, attached in Supporting Documents). We hypothesize that this algorithm will reduce the proportion of CT utilization, significantly, from that of current best practice without compromising negative appendectomies in patients with suspected appendicitis. We propose a validation of our algorithm in the form of a phase 2 randomized control trial comparing the proposed algorithm compared to current best practice.Patients with suspected appendicitis recruited into the study from Singapore General Hospital will be randomized into 2 treatment arms:-i) Intervention Arm – Management as per proposed algorithmii) Control Arm – Current best practice (based on the individual discretion of attending surgeon)Primary outcome of interest is percentage of CT scans in each arm. Secondary outcomes include the percentage of missed diagnosis, negative appendectomies, overall length and cost of stay. If the proposed algorithm is validated and found to be of value, it can potentially be implemented nationwide as a standard protocol for the evaluation of suspected appendicitis. This may reduce unwarranted CT scans and health care costs as well as the burden of radiation induced complications in the future.
kw: appendicitis, CT scan, algorithm

title: whole exom sequencing to identify genetic variants associated with severe childhood obesity and tracking the changing prevalence o obesity related complications
abs: Susceptibility variants contributing to obesity are being uncovered by candidate gene approach, genome wide linkage studies, and genome wide association studies (GWAS), but the collective effect is small and does not explain most of the BMI heritability. We propose a whole exome sequencing (WES) approach to systematically interrogate coding variants and to identify novel obesity loci in 130 Chinese subjects from our existing cohort of Singaporean severe early-onset obese subjects, and an additional ~200 subjects will be recruited to augment this. Sequencing will be performed at high coverage (50X) on the Illumina-HiSeq platform. Statistical association tests will be performed for identified variants (single-variant analysis and gene-based mutational load test) using normal, lean (BMI between 18.5 and 23 kg/m2) adult Singaporean Chinese individuals as controls (N=500). A stringent approach will be undertaken to identify and prioritize novel obesity variants, including checks with genotype data, through bioinformatics tools for predicting functional effects and by re-sequencing and/or de novo genotyping of top hits. We will replicate top hits by targeted sequencing in 96 (out of 200 subjects) extreme obese Chinese children and through de novo genotyping in additional Chinese children with extreme BMI from childhood datasets from Singapore and China. We will study the in-vitro functions of the aberrant proteins of novel variants. Our secondary aim is to assess the change in prevalence of obesity related complications over 15 years by recruiting 350 severely obese children and compare against the complications prevalence data obtained from an NMRC funded childhood obesity study in 2001-2004. The identification of novel genes for extreme early-onset obesity can provide novel insights into human weight regulation mechanisms and new therapeutic targets for drug development, and also identification of high-risk children so that potential intervention measures can be implemented at an early stage of life.
kw: children, obesity

title: Autologous Endothelial Progenitor Cell therapy for reversal of liver cirrhosis
abs: iver cirrhosis constitute a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. This is driven by the high endemicity of viral hepatitis as well as the epidemic rise of fatty liver. While liver transplant is curative, the complexity of the procedure and the scarcity of donor grafts result in many patients missing out on transplantation and represent a major clinical gap. Autologous bone marrow mononuclear cell transplantation have been attempted in small cohorts of patients showing safety and potential benefit but has not been studied in proper randomised controlled study. Our own animal studies have shown that transplantation of nonparenchymal cells particularly those contributing to the sinusoidal endothelial lineage result in a dramatic reversal of cirrhosis and improvement in all clinical correlates of decompensated liver.We propose a randomised controlled study of 33 patients each in 2 arms, based on power calculation of potential efficacy from published studies. Endothelial progenitor cells are harvested by CD133+ MACS sort selection of bone marrow aspiration with mobilisation by SC GCSF. A minimum of 1x 10^7 cells are transplanted to one lobe of the liver via a percutaneous catheter. The primary outcome is improvement in at least 2 of 4 composite indicis including MELD score by 2 points, decrease in fibrosis using clinical, radiological or histochemical quantitation of liver biopsy at 3 months after transplantation. Secondary outcomes include improvement in portal pressure, liver function and survival up to 1 year. Controls are provided by contralateral lobe liver biopsy as well as control arm given monthly GCSFx3. The successful attenuation of liver cirrhosis with endothelial progenitor cell therapy will provide a critical treatment option that plugs an unmet clinical need, augmenting the capabilities of our national liver transplant programme which draws patients rom the region. It will also establish Singapore as a centre with capabilities for randomised controlled study in translational cell therapy.

title: Development of a quality of life scale in English and Chinese for family caregivers of patients with advanced cancers in Singapore
abs: “If you don’t measure it, you can’t improve it”, said an Institute of Medicine report on caring for patients with life-threatening illnesses and their families. Assessment of quality of life of caregivers is an important part of care for patients with advanced cancers. Yet, its practice is limited in Singapore and Asia. Our recent qualitative research in Singapore demonstrated substantial differences in quality of life concerns between Singaporean caregivers of patients with advanced cancers and their counterparts in western societies. There is a shortage of validated quality of life assessment scales for caregivers in Singapore. This study aims to develop and validate English and Chinese versions of a user-friendly quality of life measurement scale for assessment of family caregivers of patients with advanced cancers. A secondary aim is to establish the measurement equivalence between the English and Chinese versions. We will develop an initial version of a measurement scale (in English and Chinese) based on the findings from our recent qualitative study in Singapore. This will ensure that the scale contents are locally relevant. We will conduct cognitive interviews to ensure clarity and usability and to refine the initial scale. We will conduct a survey of caregivers to quantitatively assess the individual and collective characteristics of the scale items, including factor structure and measurement equivalence between the English and Chinese items. The scales will be modified according to the results, including the removal of items with limited or overlapping information contents, so as to keep the scales as short and user-friendly as possible. The study will involve 480 family caregivers.The proposed research will facilitate quality improvement programs and research on effectiveness of interventions to improve health care outcomes among family caregivers.

title: Trends in rehabilitation outcomes, survival and disability burden following inpatient rehabilitation and sub-acute care at community hospitals between 2006 and 2015
abs: AimsThe primary aim of this study is to evaluate trends in outcomes, survival and disability burden following inpatient rehabilitation and sub-acute care at community hospitals for specific conditions, including stroke and fractures, from 2006 to 2015. Secondary aims include examining trends in utilization of community hospitals for rehabilitation, sub-acute, chronic sick and respite care, and cost-effectiveness of post-acute rehabilitation and sub-acute care for the most common diagnoses for admission.HypothesesThe intermediate and long-term care (ILTC) sector in Singapore has expanded significantly in the past few years in order to address the health care challenges of an older demographic, as well as to contain health care costs. While, community hospitals’ data from 1996 – 2005 has shown declines in length of stay, and improved rehabilitation effectiveness and efficiency over this period, the effect of service expansion and other system level changes in the past decade on rehabilitation and sub-acute care utilization, and outcomes is unknown. MethodologyThe study is planned as a retrospective analysis of medical records data between 2006 and 2015 in all community hospitals in Singapore. Data on relevant socio-demographic, medical and rehabilitation details of all patients admitted in any of the following community hospitals, namely, Ang Mo Kio Thye Hua Kwan Hospital (AMK-THK), Bright Vision Hospital (BVH), St Andrew’s Community Hospital (SACH), St Luke’s Hospital (SLH), and Ren Ci Community Hospital (RCCH), will be obtained using an electronic data collection system.Significance to health services deliveryThis study will provide the data necessary to forecast future demand for sub-acute care and post-acute rehabilitation services through community hospitals in Singapore. In addition, we will be able to examine the effects of health system changes in utilization of these services as well as in outcomes, effectiveness and efficiency. This study will also help to benchmark our outcomes to international trends and service standards.
