title: Immunological profiling of paediatric patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis responsive to rituximab therapy: Linking the synapses and defining the key players
abs: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a devastating kidney disease with rapid progression to end-stage kidney failure. There is conflicting evidence as to the exact pathogenesis of this disease, that is, the role of the immune system acting on podocytes versus direct podocyte damage, partly because FSGS is probably a heterogenous disease. Our preliminary data demonstrated a hyporesponsive T-cell phenotype corresponding to a favourable response to rituximab therapy, an anti-CD20-monoclonal antibody, highlighting the possible role of B-T interactions in this subgroup of patients with FSGS. This was accompanied by significantly reduced T-cell production of the ‘inhibitory’ cytokines in FSGS rituximab responders in contrast to non-responders and controls where no immunological signature was apparent. This ‘disinhibited’ T-cell phenotype may possibly result in decreased inhibition of monocyte production of potential permeability factors. We therefore hypothesized that in a subgroup of immune-mediated FSGS, T-cells are important in the immune regulation of a cascade leading to production of a permeability factor ultimately resulting in proteinuria. This study aims to further characterize the subgroup of immune-mediated FSGS with T-cell hyporesponsiveness to activation (HT phenotype) by phenotyping the T- and B-cell subsets, and investigating the interplay of B-T interactions through T- and B-cell co-culture. In addition, we will study the defective regulation of T-cells on monocyte/macrophage production of putative permeability factor(s) in order to elucidate both the upstream and downstream immune effectors involved in pathogenesis of proteinuria in this subgroup of FSGS. We will subsequently validate the putative permeability factor(s) both in human podocyte cell cultures as well as an animal model of FSGS. The significance of this work lies in delineating, in detail, the dysregulated B-T-monocyte immunological axis in the subgroup of immune-mediated FSGS in order to identify unique immunological signatures to which targeted novel therapies can be developed, for patients with this difficult-to-treat disease.
kw: Rituximab, B-cells, Hyporesponsive T-cells, permeability factors

title: Self-Tonometry device for monitoring of intra-Ocular Pressure (STOP) for Glaucoma
abs: Aims Our primary aim is to develop a intra-ocular pressure (IOP)-measuring device to provide 24-hour monitoring of IOP for patients with glaucoma, a blinding ocular disease. The secondary aim is to determine the market potential of the device in preparation for commercialization. Hypotheses We hypothesize that, using trained artificial neural network, we can develop a novel device to measure an individual's IOP through the eyelids which will facilitate ambulatory IOP measurement in the community. This will aid to individualize glaucoma management and improve glaucoma screening to reduce glaucoma-related visual impairment. Methodology We intend to first conduct further studies on Rabbit eyes to collect more data to improve our current artificial neural network model. We will be using our working prototype on the eyes to obtain measurements across a pre-determined range of IOP using a standardized intra-luminal needle manometer. An advanced algorithm will be developed to eliminate the effect of the eye lid on the IOP measurement. In the subsequent step, we plan to conduct human clinical trials to compare the IOP measurement from the new device with Goldmann applantation tonometry, gold standard of IOP measurement in the clinical setting. We intend to conduct guided market surveys in collaboration with NUS Enterprise to determine the market potential of the device in preparation for future commercialization. Approach of research proposal Currently, we have already developed a prototype and obtained preliminary proof-of-concept data with computational models. To achieve future aims, I intend to complete a part-time MSc (Innovation Graduate Programme) from National University of Singapore over 2 years. The programme will provide a cross-disciplinary approach to address the clinical, engineering and commercialisation requirements. This is followed by a one-year long research fellowship at University of Minnesota to further refine the device as part of a multi-centre clinical trial.
kw: Glaucoma, Intraocular pressure, tonometry

title: Identification of a High Risk Pre-leukemic Methylome Profile in Healthy Individuals
abs: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) occurs disproportionately in the elderly population, with an increased risk seen in individuals harboring clonal hematopoiesis. Alterations in DNA methylation are commonly seen in cancers with compared with normal tissue. AML and MDS display a highly aberrant DNA methylation profile that appears to have evolved independently alongside genetic mutations. It may be surmised that prior to the development of AML and MDS, changes in DNA methylation may be observed in the hematopoietic cells of such high-risk individuals. Combining DNA methylation and mutation profiling may thus inform the risk developing AML and MDS in a more sensitive manner. With this aim in mind, we plan to perform targeted deep sequencing and methylated DNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeDIP-seq) in peripheral blood samples of Singaporean Chinese individuals collected a median of 10 years prior to the diagnosis of AML or MDS (Pre-leukemia group), and a randomly selected cohort of aged and gender matched controls.
kw: GIGYF2, Novel Mutation, Acute Myeloid Leukemia

title: Periodontal Health Condition and Its Impact on Diabetes Mellitus
abs: Studies suggest that the relationship between diabetes and periodontal disease is bidirectional; individuals with diabetes are more likely to develop periodontal disease and with increased severity when diabetes is uncontrolled or poorly controlled. Conversely, periodontitis may affect glycemic control in diabetics, leading to increased risk of diabetic complications. Periodontitis has also been associated with cardiovascular disease in many studies. While diabetes is an established risk factor for periodontal disease, the treatment of periodontitis in diabetics has shown to improve the metabolic glucose control in these patients. Poor metabolic control of diabetes is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular event(s) and coronary artery disease is known to be a major cause of mortality and morbidity in diabetics. Presently, the association between periodontitis and diabetes in our population is not well characterized. We hypothesize that a significant proportion of our diabetic patients has undiagnosed periodontal disease and periodontal treatment should improve their diabetic status. Similarly, with the increasing prevalence of diabetes, we postulate that there are undiagnosed diabetics among our periodontal patients and early detection may reduce clinical complications. The specific aims of this study are to:1. Determine the prevalence and severity of periodontitis in local diabetic patients and its correlation with diabetic complications.2. Evaluate periodontal, diabetic status and lipid profile before and after periodontal treatment in diabetic patients3. Screen periodontal patients for undiagnosed diabetes and pre-diabetes. We believe the proposed studies will be important because optimal periodontal health may improve diabetic control and reduce clinical complications. In turn, this should reduce disease burden, leading to lower overall healthcare costs. Identification of undiagnosed diabetes among periodontal patients is important because it enables early intervention and treatment. Lastly, the findings from our study may influence diabetes management by including oral health examination as an integral component of diabetic care.
kw: Periodontitis,Oral inflammation, Non-surgical periodontal treatment, Diabetes Mellitus, Early disease detection, Diabetic Complications

title: Pre-death grief in family caregivers of persons with dementia and its effect on caregiver depression
abs: Caregiver support in dementia care traditionally focuses on the emotion of stress, with emphasis on improving coping skills and reducing stress. However, the emotional experience of caregivers were much more complex than the mere emotion of stress and can be better understood with the concept of pre-death grief (PDG).PDG includes the whole array of emotional response as dementia family caregivers mourn for the psychologically absent patient and anticipate impending losses. It is prevalent among dementia caregivers and is associated with negative consequences like caregiver depression and caregivers’ desire to institutionalize the patient.Published studies on PDG in dementia caregivers were few and its longitudinal effect on nursing home admission of dementia patients was never explored.We aim to validate a PDG scale for Asian population (using construct validity, internal consistency, test-retest reliability and factor analysis) and develop a shorter version of the scale (using item response theory and computer adaptive testing). With the validated scale, we intend to assess the risk factors of PDG (using multivariate linear regression) and the effect of PDG on nursing home admission (using multivariate Cox regression). We will test whether the current dementia-related social services are sufficient to attenuate the adverse effect of PDG on premature nursing home admission (by testing interaction terms in Cox regression).We hypothesize that PDG is an important predictor of premature nursing home admission of dementia patients, but dementia-related social services available currently do not address this emotional difficulty among caregivers. If our hypothesis is true, this will highlight the need for new interventions focusing on the emotional experience of caregivers and drawing on our vast experience in treating the traditional, post-death grief. Such efforts will enhance our support of dementia caregivers and may reduce the societal cost related to premature nursing home admission of dementia patients.
kw: Pre-death grief, dementia, family caregiver, nursing home, Marwit-Meuser Caregiver Grief Inventory.

title: Development of Novel therapy for head and neck cancer
abs: Head and neck cancer is a common cancer in Singapore, nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) being the most common, followed by squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, larynx and hypopharynx. NPC is an aggressive tumour often diagnosed late, and despite combined modality treatments, many patients still relapse and have poor prognosis. There have been few breakthroughs in development of novel therapeutics for head and neck cancers. In our recent work, we showed that NPC has a relatively low mutational load, and are enriched for mutations of the epigenetic regulatory genes. The immune microenvironment in NPC is likely dominated by Epstein Barr virus related gene regulation leading to immune tolerance and T cell exhaustion, though detailed analysis of this immune compartment has not been done. For SCC, my laboratory has recently demonstrated that activation of MEK/ERK/MAPkinase pathway mediates resistance to cisplatin, and preliminary results of another study suggest that p53 mutants upon acetylation may activate apoptotic machinery and be responsive to cisplatin. In this proposal, we propose to (1) collect tumour samples from recently diagnosed NPC patients and patients refractory to standard treatment, applying whole genome methylation sequencing and RNA sequencing to map the transcriptome of NPC for the first time (2) analyse of the immune compartment to define relative contributions of T cells, myeloid cells and NK cells to the immune microenvironment (3) conduct a trial of mek and cisplatin combination in SCC patients and (4) understand the molecular underpinnings of p53 acetylation on specific mutants. To do this, we have assembled a team of outstanding and productive investigators who have (1) recognised expertise in EBV immunology, genomic analysis, translational immunology, deep understanding of head and neck cancer and ready access to patients and samples, clinical trial expertise and preclinical drug development, and (2) are already working closely together on existing collaborations.
kw: head and neck, phase I clinical trials, immunotherapy, genomics

title: Antenatal Risk Factors and Offspring Cardio-Metabolic Health in Mid-Childhood
abs: There is increasing evidence that the origins of cardio-metabolic health may be traced to vascular, metabolic, and other processes that start in utero programming. In the Barker’s hypothesis, also known as the “thrifty phenotype hypothesis”, intrauterine growth restriction due to fetal adaptation to metabolic and vascular processes is linked to the development of major metabolic and cardiovascular disease in late-life. A series of antenatal risk factors such as maternal obesity, excess gestational weight gain, gestational complications (i.e. gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia), pre-term birth, pregnancy exposure to air pollution have been widely studied to have an ill impact on intra-uterine fetal growth, which leads to offspring cardio-metabolic disease in the long run. Yet, the mechanistic pathways are not well understood because most studies investigating such relations were retrospectively designed and it is difficult to assess vascular and endothelial function via conventional approaches during pregnancy. In Singapore, we have been working on assessing vascular health in mothers and relate the morphological changes to different antenatal risk factors such as antennal depression and pregnancy complications. However, the birth cohort in Singapore is relatively new, smaller in sample size, and also with little data collected regarding a full set of antenatal risk factors. Project Viva is an ongoing pre-birth cohort of pregnancy women and their children enrolled between 1999 and 2002 at a multispecialty clinic in eastern Massachusetts. In this Harvard project, 2128 mothers had delivered a live singleton infant, and 1287 were followed up at 3 years postpartum and 1107 were followed up at 7 years postpartum. As for the 6 months’ attachment in Harvard Medical School, I will be working closely with the PIs and we aim to study a more systematic risk factors assessed during pregnancy and cardio-metabolic health in mid-childhood via assessing retinal microvasculature in the offspring at 12-15 years postpartum.
kw: antenatal risk facgors, cardio-metabolic health, mid-childhood, retinal microvasculature

title: Childhood Injury Surveillance and Control - No Child's Play
abs: Background Childhood injuries remain a significant obstacle in our pursuit for the well-being of our paediatric patients. When a young child presents with severe injury, the potential for a full life ahead is devastated, with far-reaching consequences. In Singapore, the current Trauma Registry has allowed us to look into the circumstances associated with injuries. However, more remains to be done to collect comprehensive data and translate this information into clinically meaningful injury prevention measures. Aims, Needs and HypothesesIn this multicenter study, we aim to (1) Align relevant trauma data collection methods, fields and clinically important outcome measures among children who present to Emergency Departments (EDs), using the compass of injury specialists and pediatric trauma databases in the United States. This will address pressing needs in the injury surveillance system. We also aim to (2) Study measures of effectiveness of injury prevention strategies, (3) Compare the evaluation and management of head injured children between the western population and that in Asia. We hypothesize that current prediction rules on paediatric head injury are not generalizable in many Asian countries. Finally, we aim to (4) Compare the evaluation and protective strategies for children subject to child abuse. Methodology We plan to align the data collection methods and fields with the pediatric trauma databases of Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN), and build a prospective injury surveillance in Asia, using the Pan Asian Trauma Outcomes Study (PATOS) platform. Variables from the demographics, mechanisms and outcome measures will be collected and analysed. This platform will allow for the exchange of prevention strategies and non-accidental injury protocols. Significance The acquisition of necessary skills and bridging collaborations with known childhood injury specialists holds promise in leading to a better understanding of childhood injuries, exchange of injury prevention strategies, and an eventual reduction in childhood mortality and morbidity.
kw: injury; trauma; child

title: Integrated Palliative Oncology for advanced cancer patients who have an unplanned hospital admission
abs: Advanced cancer patients have a poor quality of life and a high rate of unplanned hospital admissions. Palliative care has been shown to improve patient outcomes such as quality of life and symptom burden. Our long-term aim is to study the effect of Supportive and Palliative Care Review Kit (SPaRK) – a novel model of early palliative care in the acute hospital inpatient setting. To this end, we will conduct a pilot study to obtain the necessary data for the planning of a subsequent larger scale Phase III trial of SPaRK.The specific aims of this pilot study are: 1) to estimate the recruitment rate and ability of advanced cancer patients to complete the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy – General (FACT-G) questionnaire, which measures health-related quality of life (QOL) in the four domains of physical well-being, social/family well-being, emotional well-being, and functional well-being, 2) to obtain a tentative estimate of the effect size of the SPaRK model of care on change in patient QOL over 6 days, 3) to explore the responsiveness to change of FACT-G over 3 days and 4) to explore views of healthcare professionals and stakeholders on SPaRK as a model of integrated palliative care and oncology care service delivery. In the short term, the results from this study will be used to plan a larger scale Phase III study of SPaRK. In the long term, a resource-efficient and effective model of care needs to be developed for the aging population and rising palliative care needs of patients. If successful, this pilot study will lead on to the testing of SPaRK, which does not rely wholly on specialist palliative care manpower, but involves both specialists and non-specialists working together to provide palliative care, and hence can be feasibly scaled up across institutions and extended to non-cancer patients.
kw: Palliative Care, Oncology, Advanced Cancer

title: Whole-exome sequencing to identify genetic variants associated with severe childhood obesity, and tracking the changing prevalence of obesity related complications
abs: Susceptibility variants contributing to obesity are being uncovered by candidate gene approach, genome wide linkage studies, and genome wide association studies (GWAS), but the collective effect is small and does not explain most of the BMI heritability. We propose a whole exome sequencing (WES) approach to systematically interrogate coding variants and to identify novel obesity loci in 130 Chinese subjects from our existing cohort of Singaporean severe early-onset obese subjects, and an additional ~200 subjects will be recruited to augment this. Sequencing will be performed at high coverage (50X) on the Illumina-HiSeq platform. Statistical association tests will be performed for identified variants (single-variant analysis and gene-based mutational load test) using normal, lean (BMI between 18.5 and 23 kg/m2) adult Singaporean Chinese individuals as controls (N=500). A stringent approach will be undertaken to identify and prioritize novel obesity variants, including checks with genotype data, through bioinformatics tools for predicting functional effects and by re-sequencing and/or de novo genotyping of top hits. We will replicate top hits by targeted sequencing in 96 (out of 200 subjects) extreme obese Chinese children and through de novo genotyping in additional Chinese children with extreme BMI from childhood datasets from Singapore and China. We will study the in-vitro functions of the aberrant proteins of novel variants. Our secondary aim is to assess the change in prevalence of obesity related complications over 15 years by recruiting 350 severely obese children and compare against the complications prevalence data obtained from an NMRC funded childhood obesity study in 2001-2004. The identification of novel genes for extreme early-onset obesity can provide novel insights into human weight regulation mechanisms and new therapeutic targets for drug development, and also identification of high-risk children so that potential intervention measures can be implemented at an early stage of life.
kw: Obesity, Genetics, Childhood obesity, Functional validation, Exome sequencing

title: Development of a Novel, Non-invasive Serum MicroRNA Test for Detection of Gastric Cancer in a High Risk Population
abs: Gastric cancer (GC) is the 4th most common cancer and the 2nd most common cause of cancer deaths worldwide. Currently, endoscopy is the only reliable method for early diagnosis but limited as a screening test due to high cost and risk. A simple, less-invasive screening test for GC is highly desirable.MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small RNAs that regulate gene expression. It was found to be important in the pathogenesis of cancers. Recently, cancer specific miRNAs have been detected in body fluids such as blood. miRNAs are exceptionally stable in blood and can be readily measured using existing clinical lab workflows, making them excellent candidate disease biomarkers.Using an A*STAR proprietary qPCR technology and robust workflows with multi-layered technical controls, 75 informative miRNAs were identified to be significantly altered in GC. This will be the first bloodbased multivariate miRNA screening test for GC in the market. The primary objective of the study is to validate a panel of serum microRNA biomarkers and evaluate its utility for detection of gastric cancer in a high-risk population. Forms and mechanisms of actions of these miRNAs will also be investigated to discover potential predictors of treatment response and therapeutics. Lastly, the cost-effectiveness of the technology will be evaluated using health technology assessment methods.The study involves commitment of clinicians in many aspects including subject recruitment, scientific write-up and administrative-related matter. In recognition of their effort, CISSP application is submitted based on the respective FTE. The funding channeled to departments will be utilized to support various research-related activities in the hospital.

title: Evaluation of plaque characteristics, plaque inflammation and embolic potential with high resolution cerebrovascular ultrasonography, high resolution magnetic resolution imaging and Positron emission Tomography imaging in ischemic stroke patient with aymptomatic carotid stenosis
abs: Background and hypothesis- Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability in Singapore. Carotid atherosclerosis accounts for about 20% of ischemic stroke. The risk of recurrent stroke in carotid disease has traditionally been estimated on the degree of stenosis. It does not take into account the plaque morphology, plaque inflammation and its embolic potential. Accumulating evidence indicates that inflammation is of key importance in plaque destabilisation, local thrombosis, cerebral embolization and stroke. Carotid plaque inflammation can be evaluated with high resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) while its embolic potential may be determined with transcranial Doppler (TCD) for developing a model for risk stratification. We hypothesise that plaque inflammation (with MRI and PET) in recently-symptomatic ischemic stroke patients with carotid stenosis (>50% diameter reduction), combined with positive TCD-emboli monitoring will be associated with increased risk of recurrent stroke at 90 days, after adjusting for degree of lumen stenosis and other co-variates. Methods- It is a prospective cohort study. Ambulatory patients with ischemic stroke or TIA (within 7 days of clinical presentation) and carotid stenosis (>50%) will be identified, have baseline procedures (clinical assessments, high sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) measurement, carotid high resolution MRI, PET/CT, and cervical duplex ultrasonography) and followed for recurrent stroke for 90 days. All patients will receive medical and carotid revascularisation treatment in accordance with current guidelines as standard of care. Primary outcome will be assessed for ischemic event within 90 days not related to revascularisation. Secondary outcome will be any recurrent stroke, Myocardial infarction or death due to vascular events and modified Rankin Scale at 3 months. Conclusion: Advanced imaging of carotid plaque inflammation and assessment of embolic potential in patients with symptomatic carotid stenosis will help in improved risk stratification in patients presenting with recent cerebrovascular ischemia.
kw: Plaque, Emboli, Ultrasonography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging, Positron Emission Tomography

title: Clinician Scientist / Clinician Investigator Salary Support (CS/CISSP) Programme
abs: Aim: To establish the safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of escalating doses followed by dose expansion of Selinexor (KPT-330), a selective inhibitor of the nuclear export protein (XPO-1), in Asian Patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumor malignanciesMethods: An investigator initiated open-label, dose-escalation (Phase 1a) and expansion (Phase 1b) study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of KPT-330 and determine the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) in patients with solid tumor malignancies.Importance of research: Tight regulation of tumour suppressor proteins (TSPs) and growth regulatory proteins (GRP) is required within cells to prevent neoplastic transformation. Tumour cells can inactivate critical TSPs/GRPs by increasing the levels of nuclear export proteins like XPO1. First-in-class selective inhibitors of nuclear export (SINE) such as Selinexor (KPT-330) have been developed which can inhibit XPO1, resulting in the nuclear retention of key TSP/GRPs and forced reactivation of their function. Consistent with its mechanism as an activator of the major TSPs/GRPs including p53, pRB, BRCA1, and others, KPT-330 has shown broad and durable anti-tumor activity as a single agent, even at low doses in ongoing phase I studies in North America. Durable (> 3 months) disease stabilization and responses have been observed in haematological and heavily pretreated solid tumours. However, this compound has not been extensively tested in Asian patients or Asian type tumours and hence the need to evaluate its safety and tolerability in our Singaporean patient population.
kw: Selinexor, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, Solid, Metastatic, Tumor

title: Development of a Novel, Non-invasive serum MicroRNA Test for Detection of Gastric Cancer in a High-Risk Population
abs: Gastric cancer (GC) is the 4th most common cancer and the 2nd most common cause of cancer deaths worldwide. Currently, endoscopy is the only reliable method for early diagnosis but limited as a screening test due to high cost and risk. A simple, less-invasive screening test for GC is highly desirable.MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that regulate gene-expressions. Aberrant miRNA expressions are involved in the pathogenesis of cancers and tumor-specific circulating miRNAs were recently discovered. MiRNAs are exceptionally stable in body fluids and can be readily measured using existing clinical lab workflows, making them excellent candidate disease biomarkers.Using an A*STAR proprietary qPCR technology and robust workflows with multi-layered technical controls, we have analyzed the expressions of 578 candidate miRNAs in sera of 236 GC patients and 236 matched controls, the most extensive study performed to date. Seventy-five informative miRNAs were identified to be significantly altered in GC (FDR corrected p-values<0.01). Multivariate miRNA biomarker panels showed high diagnostic accuracy (AUC>0.90). The primary objective here is to validate the performance of our miRNA panels through multiple studies including, 1) a Singaporean case-control study (n=250), 2) an independent Korean case-control study (n = 280), and 3) a large prospective validation cohort (n= 5000) designed according to National Cancer Institute (US) biomarker development guidelines (6). The finalized test kit will be prototyped and analytically validated by A*STAR Diagnostic Development Hub and MIRXES (A*STAR/NUS Spin-off) in compliance with Singapore HSA and EU CE-IVD regulations. This will be the first blood-based multivariate miRNA screening test for GC in the market. Forms and mechanisms of actions of these miRNAs will also be investigated to discover potential predictors of treatment response and therapeutics. Finally, the cost-effectiveness of the technology and the likelihood of achieving returns on investment will be evaluated by Health Technology Assessment

title: Clinician Scientist / Clinician Investigator Salary Support Programme
abs: Lung cancer continues to be associated with the highest mortality in human cancers. The disease is different in East Asia compared to the West, most distinctive being the significantly higher incidence of never-smokers with adenocarcinoma, especially amongst females. Recent advances in the molecular classification of adenocarcinoma has important clinical implications, where ALK and EGFR mutant lung cancers – both seen commonly in never smokers – have become therapeutically amenable to corresponding tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI). Despite initial high responses to TKIs in molecularly selected patients, a subgroup of patients with intrinsic resistance (30-40%) respond suboptimally at the outset, while in the majority of others, acquired drug resistance invariably develops. In addition, there remain a significant proportion of adenocarcinoma patients without either of these genomic changes (about 30-50%) so called double negative adenocarcinoma, underscoring an urgent need to uncover new driver mutations that may be “druggable”. This TCR capitalizes on major recent advances made by the PIs within the TCR consortium and comprises of 3 synergistic translational themes. Theme 1 addresses the cellular basis of lung cancer, and examines the cellspecific context of molecular drivers and stem cell biology. Theme 2 garners the immense power of current sequencing technologies to unravel the mechanisms of drug resistance and to discover new driver mutations. Theme 3 involves purposefully designed hypothesis-testing clinical trials exploring novel therapeutics that will provide invaluable insights to overcoming TKI resistance. These trials facilitate the acquisition of relevant biospecimens that crucially provides material for our sequencing effort in Theme 2, thus allowing the possibility of linking detailed genetic information about each patient to drug response. The consortium pulls together top basic scientists, internationally recognized genomics experts and highly experienced clinician researchers to answer critical questions that have important diagnostic and therapeutic applications, ultimately to make tangible improvements to patient care.

title: The Eradication of Chronic Hepatitis B
abs: The team was awarded $25 million in search of a cure for hepatitis B. This program project grant comprises outstanding clinicians, physician-scientists and basic scientists who will work together across integrated themes to address an important health problem that affects the world in general.They are leaders in the field of HBV research who have made significant contributions to our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of chronic HBV disease both at a basic and clinical level. Their leadership and international standing is documented by publications in the highest impact Journals. They been invited to speak at international meetings and generated intellectual and recipients of independent peer reviewed grants. The Singapore Hepatitis B Consortium (SHBC) is a national translational group of 29 researchers and scientists who have been working collaboratively, now plan to focus on the eradication of Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB), through a comprehensive approach via three integrated themes of examining host/viral interactions, target discovery with validation, and experimental therapeutics. The SHBC has a proven track record. CHB has been considered difficult but not impossible to eradicate with current therapies. The SHBC plans to tackle this successfully by exploiting its joint expertise and strong working relationships using its unique capabilities and resources:• A 1458 patient cohort of long-term followup (mean 6.7years) CHB patients with 17,154 stored serums and 2,815 PBMC linked to laboratory and clinical outcomes. • A novel humanised mouse model of hepatitis B that is able to host both human liver cells and immune cells, and shown to harbour HBV infection, which now can be fully exploited for hypothesis testing, target validation and experimental therapeutics. • A state of the art cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) machine that is capable of simultaneously and sensitively probe >100 antigen specificities all in a single human blood sample• Strong expertise in intra-hepatic immunology• Established collaborations with many pharmaceutical companiesEstablished NUS Lab which performs molecular biology of hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication, virus-host interaction and/or antiviral development. Perform molecular biology work on cell culture, PCR, cloning, DNA, RNA and protein work.

title: Large volume intraoperative peritoneal lavage as a simple intervention to improve the survival of gastric cancer patients
abs: Gastric cancer is the third most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Surgery is the mainstay treatment for cure. The peritoneum is a common site of recurrence and the prognosis with peritoneal recurrence is dismal. Hence, any measure that can prevent peritoneal relapse will significantly improve treatment outcomes. Recent evidence suggests that extensive peritoneal lavage with large volume of normal saline after surgery before abdominal closure can reduce the risk of peritoneal recurrence and improve overall survival. This study aims to evaluate the benefit of extensive peritoneal lavage on survival and recurrence outcomes

title: Platelet inhibition to target reperfusion injury: The PITRI trial
abs: Clinical need: There remains a clinical need to improve health outcomes in patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) the leading cause of death and disability in Singapore and worldwide. One neglected therapeutic target is ‘myocardial reperfusion injury’ in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients treated by primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI). This results in microvascular obstruction (MVO) and cardiomyocyte death and contributes upto 50% of the final myocardial infarct (MI) size. Cangrelor, a potent intravenous platelet P2Y12 inhibitor with rapid onset and offset of action, has been demonstrated in experimental animal studies to reduce MI size when administered prior to reperfusion. Whether Cangrelor is effective in STEMI patients treated by PPCI is not known and is investigated in the Platelet Inhibition to Target Reperfusion Injury (PITRI) trial.Specific aim: To investigate whether Cangrelor administered prior to PPCI, can prevent MVO and reduce MI size in STEMI patients.Hypothesis: Cangrelor administered prior to PPCI will prevent MVO and reduce MI size in STEMI patients.Methodology: The PITRI proof-of-concept clinical trial will randomise 250 STEMI patients to receive either Cangrelor (single intravenous bolus followed by a 120-minute infusion) or matching normal/saline placebo, initiated prior to PPCI. The primary endpoint will be MI size at 6 months (measured by cardiac MRI). Secondary endpoints will include incidence and extent of MVO (cardiac MRI); and left ventricular size and ejection fraction (measured by cardiac MRI at 6 months).Expected outcome: If Cangrelor is shown to prevent MVO and reduce MI size, there is the potential to perform a large phase 3 clinical trial to determine whether it can improve clinical outcomes at one year (cardiac death and hospitalisation for heart failure), thereby demonstrating a real impact on health outcomes for IHD patients in Singapore and worldwide.

title: Targeting Brain Tumors: Improving lives through Precision Medicine
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Patients with grade IV glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) often show a median survival period of fifteen months despite advanced surgical intervention with chemotherapy and radiation treatment. Among the reasons for this highly infiltrative and recurrent disease lies in the molecular heterogeneity of tumors. The Cancer Genome Atlas effort recently showed that histologically identical GBM tumors can be molecularly subtyped, with each class corresponding to unique genomic aberrations and clinical outcome. While computational efforts reveal regulatory pathways of GBM, functional validation and the ability to stratify patient cohorts most likely to receive treatment benefit is lacking. We hypothesize that patient stratification methodologies will lead to improved clinical outcome. This forms the basis of precision medicine, where the NNI Brain Tumor Resource plays a key role. Our national resource contains patient-derived glioma cells, with the ability to create orthotopic xenograft mouse tumors that recapitulate the patient’s original tumor morphology, transcriptomic and karyotypic hallmarks. We will utilize a 3-theme approach of: (i) Testing stratification methods to identify key mechanisms corresponding to tumor cell invasiveness and proneural-mesenchymal transition, frequently observed in recurrent tumors, (ii) Establishing molecular profiling information of recurrent GBMs, which will create a “molecular reference baseline” crucial to guide treatment decisions, and (iii) Developing novel imaging probes and predictive biomarker profiles capable of distinguishing patient molecular subtypes. Complementing these imaging capabilities, we will develop real-time guided surgical technologies where maximal tumor resection will be explored through a combination of Raman spectroscopy and intraoperative magnetic resonance imaging, a capability established in very few clinical centers internationally. Collectively, our program will develop capabilities to identify patient cohorts most likely to receive treatment benefit from targeted therapy. This will in turn spare non-responders of chemotherapeutic side effects and financial cost. Our program seeks to improve clinical outcome through the application of precision medicine approaches.
kw: Gliblastoma multiforme, Precision medicine, Patient stratification, Guided surgery, Molecular imaging, Predictive biomarkers

title: An Immunological Study on the effects of radioembolization in combination with anti-PD1 therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the sixth most common form of malignancy worldwide and the second most common cause of cancer-related mortality. It has especially high prevalence in Southeast Asia, due to the high rates of viral hepatitis, including chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV). Escape from immune control is a critical hallmark of cancer that has recently come under intense scrutiny with the dramatic yet unpredictable successes of cancer immunotherapies, such as Merck’s Pembrolizumab (anti-PD1). Here, leveraging our current clinical practices, permitting us to perform a small clinical trial in collaboration with Merck, and our unique capacity to deeply probe antigen-specific T cell responses, we will investigate relationships between the antigen-specific T cell response to HCC and HBV in the context of transarterial radiombolization with Yittrium-90 microspheres and in combination with Pembrolizumab. In the process, a number of immunological mechanisms will be explored as we test the hypothesis that liver-localized radioembolization will stimulate tumour and/or HBV specific T cell responses that are associated with favourable patient outcomes and that can be boosted using anti-PD1 immunotherapy. In aim 1, we will use existing tools to evaluate T cell responses to known HBV, HCC tumour and other unrelated antigens in the blood before, during and after radioembolization treatment. In aim 2, we will use blood and liver tissues obtained from HCC tumour resection patients to compare profiles of antigen-specific T cells of patients with or without chronic HBV infection. This will allow us to validate strategies for identifying individualized blood-derived tumour-specific T cells used in aim 3. Finally, in aim 3, a clinical trial with deep exploratory analysis will be performed to assess the benefit of using Pembrolizumab in combination with radioembolization therapy. This study will help lead the way to the broader more effective usage of immunotherapy for cancer patients in Singapore.

title: Precision Medicine in Liver Cancer across an Asia-Pacific Network
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the 6th most common cancer in the world but the 2nd most important cause of cancer death. Because of its highly heterogeneous nature, the current approach to identifying druggable targets have not delivered efficacious therapies in HCC and is a main reason for the high case fatality. Even when surgical resection is potentially curative in early disease, tumor recurrence remains high and long term survival poor because of the absence of useful adjuvant therapy. To address these unmet needs, we bring together internationally recognized scientists from genomics and immunology and established clinician investigators in a synergistic team. This TCR capitalizes on recent collaborative advances made by the PIs in the consortium. We have shown through multi-region sampling of freshly resected HCC and phylogenetic analysis, that significant intra-tumoral heterogeneity exists and have identified the specific positions of known clonal drivers. Simultaneously we have analyzed the immune landscape of the tumor microenvironment with deep immune-phenotyping and found unique inter-patient immune landscapes predictive of clinical trajectory. In this TCR, Phase I is a prospective study that samples resected HCC from multi-ethnic sites within the established Asia-Pacific Hepatocellular Carcinoma (AHCC) Trials Group, which has enrolled approximately 1000 patients through 6 multi-center trials in 35 centers in the region. Clinical trajectories are tracked and genomic and immunological studies are repeated when tumors recur, to confirm clonally dominant driver mutations and immunological processes that are targetable. In Phase II these patients with recurrent tumors are enrolled in a proof-of-principle clinical trial using therapeutics selected or developed on the basis of discoveries in this study. Concurrently, representative pre-clinical models will be developed from the tissues sampled. We aim to combine these approaches to overcome the challenges posed by genomic heterogeneity and to guide the development of therapeutics and precision medicine in HCC.

title: The Glaucoma Initial Treatment Study: Comparing the Effectiveness of Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty with Topical Medication. A Multi-Centre, Prospective and Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. With ageing population, glaucoma morbidity will raise; causing increased healthcare costs for a condition in which visual loss is irreversible. From population-based studies, the prevalence of glaucoma was found to be 3.2% in Chinese Singaporeans with glaucoma the leading cause of blindness.Medications, in forms of topical eye drops, are used worldwide as the first line treatment to lower intraocular pressure (IOP) in glaucoma patients. However, topical medications are associated with numerous side effects, poor adherence and high long-term costs. Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT), also effective at lowering IOP, is a relatively new technique that appears to be more beneficial in patient centred quality of life outcomes. SLT has recently been proposed as a viable alternative to medications as the first line therapy for glaucoma. Although a number of smaller studies indicate that SLT and topical prostaglandins are equally effective at lowering IOP, these were generally underpowered and did not consider the impact of these two treatment modalities from patient-centred and health economic perspectives. Thus, whether SLT should be recommended more widely as the first line treatment for glaucoma, saving healthcare systems millions of dollars each year, remains unclear. We therefore propose a multi-centre prospective randomized trial, which will determine the optimum first line therapy for people with primary open angle glaucoma. This study will: evaluate treatment outcomes with respect to patient quality of life (QoL); provide detailed economics effectiveness analysis; and compare the clinical effectiveness with respect to degree of IOP lowering and rates of treatment failure over 2 years.Overall 400 patients will be recruited from Australia, Malaysia and Singapore. The trial in Australia is already funded by NHMRC Australia. This CTG application is to fund 120 subjects who will be recruited and followed up in Singapore from 3 hospitals.
kw: glaucoma,Selective laser trabeculoplasty, multi-centre prospective randomized trial, quality of life (QoL), optimum first line therapy

title: A phase I/II, multicenter, open-label study of oral FGF401 in adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma or solid malignancies characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression
abs: This is a ‘first-in-human’ study of FGF401 to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) or recommended phase II dose (RP2D) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma or other solid tumors characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression; and to estimate the preliminary anti-tumor activity of FGF401 in these populations. Based on preclinical studies, FGF401 is a highly potent, selective FGFR4 inhibitor, thereby making it a good candidate for use in the clinic. Positive prediction for sensitivity to FGF401 was identified to be associated with positive expression of FGFR4, KLB and FGF19.This study has been designed as a phase I/II, multi-center, open-label study starting with a phase I dose escalation part followed by a phase II dose expansion part. Oral FGF401 will be administered as per protocol on a continuous schedule until patient experiences unacceptable toxicity, progressive disease and/or treatment is discontinued at the discretion of the investigator or withdrawal of consent. A cycle is defined as 21 days.Adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma or other solid malignancies characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression will be eligible to participate in Phase I of the study. In Phase II, additional patients will be enrolled and stratified in 3 groups. Group 1 consists of adult HCC patients from Asian countries, characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression. Group 2 includes adult HCC patients from non-Asian regions, characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression. Lastly, group 3 targets adult other solid tumor patients, characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression regardless of geography.The study data will be analyzed and reported based on all patients’ data of the Phase I and Phase II parts up to the time when all patients have potentially completed at least six cycles of treatment or discontinued the study.

title: A phase Ib dose-escalation followed by a phase II singlearm study of the combination of LEE011 with letrozole for the treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative, advanced breast cancer
abs: Growth of hormone-receptor(HR) positive breast cancer(BC) is dependent on cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6(CDK4 and CDK6), which promote progression from the G1 phase to the S phase of the cell cycle. LEE011, an orally bioavailable CDK4/6 inhibitor, can potentially overcome resistance to endocrine therapy. In vitro studies have shown dose-dependent inhibition of proliferation across HR+ BC cell lines, with enhanced inhibition of tumour growth in combination with endocrine therapy such as letrozole in vivo.A global Phase III study is currently ongoing to assess the efficacy and safety of LEE011 with letrozole in postmenopausal patients with HR+ HER2-negative advanced BC. However, it enrolled patients predominantly from non-Asian countries. CLEE011A2115C (MONALEEASIA), a phase Ib dose-escalation followed by phase II single arm study of LEE011 with letrozole for the treatment of postmenopausal women with HR+ HER2-negative advanced BC, is intended to collect supplementary data in patients from Asian countries.The Phase Ib part consists of successive cohorts of patients receiving standard dose letrozole(2.5mg daily) with increasing doses of LEE011(400mg to 600mg once daily on days 1-21 of each 28 day cycle) to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended phase 2 dose(RP2D) of the combination. At least 12 patients will be enrolled in the Phase Ib part. The primary endpoint for the dose escalation part of the study will be the dose-limiting toxicity(DLT) rate observed during cycle 1. Dose escalation/de-escalation will be guided through a Bayesian Logistic Regression Model(BLRM) with escalation with overdose control(EWOC).Once the RP2D of LEE011 is determined, 100 additional patients will be enrolled in the Phase II part of the study. All patients will receive letrozole (2.5 mg) + LEE011(RP2D established from Phase Ib). The Phase II study will evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of LEE011 and letrozole in patients with advanced BC.

title: 3D Printed Scaffold Device for Ridge Preservation after Tooth Extraction - A Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial
abs: Following tooth extraction, the socket heals naturally with bone in 1 to 2 months. This healing process occurs with substantial reduction of the original height and width of the alveolar ridge. In a significantly resorbed ridge, bone augmentation procedures are necessary before dental implant placement. Autogenous bone is the gold standard for this purpose but the harvesting procedure results in additional morbidities and expenses. Ridge preservation techniques have been introduced, using xenografts, allografts or synthetic materials to fill the tooth socket immediately after extraction. While the current materials used have improved ridge dimensions to various extents, their osteoconductivity is suboptimal and unpredictable. They do not reduce vertical resorption of the bony walls and often interfered with the normal healing process. Polycaprolactone – tricalcium phosphate (PCL-TCP) is a bioactive, bioresorbable composite polymer that is non-toxic and tissue-compatible. This study aims to test the use of a novel 3D printed PCL-TCP device for ridge preservation, leveraging on its 3D shape that fits snugly in the tooth socket, high porosity and bioactivity to promote osteogenesis and reduce resorption. The hypothesis is that the insertion of a PCL-TCP scaffold in extraction sockets allows normal bone healing and better maintenance of ridge dimensions after 6 months compared to extraction sockets without a space filler. This will be a prospective, randomised controlled clinical trial in patients who require single tooth extraction and replacement with a dental implant. The study will compare the ridge dimensions and the quality and quantity of bone formed in tooth sockets, using histology and microcomputed tomography, in both groups after 6 months. The PCL-TCP scaffold to be used in this study will be fabricated by a local company, Osteopore International Pte Ltd. The market potential for this device is tremendous due to a growing demand for tooth replacement from an ageing population worldwide.

title: A phase II invesitigator-sponsored multi-institution study of ibrutinib in relapsed or refactory marginal zone lymphoma.
abs: Marginal zone lymphomas (MZL) are a group of indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma that has higher incidence in Asia than the West. They are related to infectious agents such a Helicobacter pylori or inflammatory conditions such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis and hence chronic antigen stimulation resulting in B-cell proliferation and subsequent transformation to B-cell lymphoma represents a putative pathogenic mechanism in MZL. Targeting the B-cell receptor pathway with ibrutinib, a Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is thus a rational treatment strategy for this lymphoma where no standard treatment options exist. The aims of this study are to evaluate the clinical efficacyof ibrutinib in patients with relapsed or refractory MZL in a phase II openlabel, multi-centre, clinical trial. Patients will receive ibrutinib at 560mg daily until disease progression, unacceptable toxicities or patient or investigator decision to end therapy. Computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography (PET)/CT scans will be performed at baseline and after every 8 weeks. The primary end point is overall response rate (ORR) and secondary endpoints are progression-free survival, overall survival, frequency and severity of adverse events encountered on study. Simon’s 2 stage minimax design will be used to determine the number of patients recruited on study. Twelve patients will be enrolled in the first stage of the study. If there are at least 3 responders, a total of 21 patients will be enrolled. The treatment will be declared ineffective if there are less than 8 responders in total. This design has a 90% power to detect an ORR of 50% at a 5% significance level.
kw: Ibrutinib, relapsed, refractory, marginal zone lymphoma

title: An open-label, single-arm phase 2 clinical trial of Regorafenib in patients with multiply recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
abs: Regorafenib is an oral multikinase inhibitor that blocks the activity of kinases involved in angiogenesis (VEGFR 1,2,3 and TEK), oncogenesis (KIT, RET, RAF1 and BRAF) and tumour growth (PDGFR and FGFR). Pre-clinical research data from patient derived xenografts at the National Cancer Centre Singapore indicates that Regorafenib has a high level of activity in Endometriod, Clear cell and other subtypes of ovarian cancer. Our data is also consistent with Bayer's internal data showing a extremely high level of activity in 5/6 of their ovarian PDX cancer cell lines. Whilst Regorafenib has been FDA approved for the treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer who have failed prior bevacizumab, its role in the management of ovarian cancer remains to be defined. In this prospective single arm, open-label, phase II clinical study, 34 patients with multiply recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer who progress after 2 initial lines of platinum based chemotherapy will be evaluated for Regorafenib safety and efficacy. This study aims to valid our earlier pre-clinical findings, bringing pre-clinical knowledge back to the clinic, to comple the cycle of research initiated by tissue donation the clinic, to comple the cycle of research initiated by tissue donation the clinic, to comple the cycle of research initiated by tissue donation from more than 50 NCCS and KKWCH patients.Primary Objective• Investigator assessed progression free survival (RECIST and/or GCIG Ca125 progression criteria)Secondary Objective• Tumour response rate (RECIST and/or GCIG Ca125 response)• Overall survival (in bevacizumab and non-bevacizumab exposed patients)• Safety and tolerability• Health related quality of life• Biomarker analysis (circulating cell free plasma DNA)

title: AR-V7 Splice Variant in Asian Patients with Castration- Resistant Prostate Cancer (CRPC)
abs: Abiraterone and Enzalutamide are two novel agents for the treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) that target the androgen pathway. Nevertheless, 20-40% of CRPC patients does not respond to these therapies or develop resistance to them after initial response. One of the postulated mechanisms for this resistance is the development/presence of androgen receptor splice variant-7 (AR-V7), a truncated form of the androgen receptor (AR) that lacks the ligand binding domain, which is the target of these agents.A study has shown that detection of AR-V7 in circulating tumor cells (CTC) from advanced CRPC patients is associated with resistance to the new hormonal agents. In a more recent report, it was reported that taxanes may be more efficacious than AR-directed agents in AR-V7-positive men. Another study showed that patients treated with taxane chemotherapy may actually have a reversion of their AR-V7 status, hence potentially enabling them to derive benefits from the hormonal agents subsequently. Whilst these results were interesting and potentially practice changing, it was done on small population of Caucasian patients and has not been replicated elsewhere.Thus, we are proposing a multinational, multicentre project to study the incidence of the AR-V7 in Asian population and how different treatments impact the patient outcomes. We aim to recruit 101 patients with CRPCfrom 5 countries over a 1-year period. Blood and tissue specimens will be collected at two timepoints (pretreatment, at disease progression) for extraction of CTC and analysis of AR-V7. Our primary endpoint is to determine the proportion of ARV-7 positive patients at baseline. Secondary objectives include determining PSA response rate, survival outcomes and the incidence of AR-V7 at the time of progression.With better understanding of the mechanism of resistance and response to androgen-directed therapies, we hope to improve treatment outcomes for these patients.

title: Development of novel therapeutics for head and neck cancer
abs: Program 1Cancer arises from aberrant cellular signaling as a result of overexpression of cellular receptors, mutations of cellular proteins, or silencing of tumour suppressor proteins. Small molecules and monoclonal antibodies have been developed to modulate crucial molecules involved with oncogenic signaling with successful application in EGFR-mutant adenocarcinoma of the lung, bcr-abl in CML, c-kit in GIST, PARP inhibitors for BRCA mutated breast cancer. With rapid screening and lead optimization, new agents have been developed against a variety of targets, making it imperative to design clinical trials that aim to prove inhibition in molecularly characterized tumours, optimally combine drugs, and with relevance to East Asia, to evaluate efficacy in Asian tumours. Our group has developed several of these drugs from first in human to phase II studies, and we are well positioned to lead this effort in Asia with successful partnerships drug developers. This program will amalgamate a team to conduct preclinical and early phase studies on several small molecules.Program 2An emerging class of anticancer drugs, histone deacetylase inhibitors, has been shown to acetylate histone proteins, thereby relaxing chromatin and inducing expression of genes. Other cellular proteins are also acetylated, and collectively small molecule histone deacetylase inhibitors exert pleiotrophic effects on aberrant oncogenic pathways to induce apoptosis and inhibition of cell proliferation. Despite demonstrating significant activity in cell lines and approval of prototype hydroxamic class panHDAC inhibitor vorinostat for treating peripheral T-cell lymphoma, as single agent therapy antitumour activity has been modest in clinical trials. Our preliminary in vitro work demonstrates highly synergistic activity with gemcitabine in cancer cell lines, and we are beginning to elucidate this mechanistically. We have found that glucuronidation is the main disposition pathway for belinostat and will pursue studies to determine the impact of polymorphisms on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of this group of molecules.
kw: head and neck cancer

title: Piezoelectric Photonics Using CMOS Compatible AlN Technology for Enabling The Next Generation Photonics ICs and Nanosensors
abs: In order to realize the next generation photonics ICs in "More-than-Moore" fashion, the CMOS photonics material AlN is explored to extend optical bandwidth, and provide better tunability and new functions for photonics ICs. Current existing photonics rely largely on the use of Silicon (Si). However, due to lacking of non-linearity, Si-photonics shows limited tunable performance. With an external electric field, refractive index of the AlN photonic components can be modified by this non-linearity. The other advantages of AlN over Si and SiN as new photonics materials in CMOS technology are piezoelectric tunning mechanism and wide optical band width (from visible light to mid IR). Such AlN based photonics components serve as good complement to existing Si-photonics to further realize functionalities previously impossible. By investigating various novel tunning mechanisms, integrated multilayered AlN/Si-photonics will become a new CMOS platform for many fundamental optical building blocks such as resonators, filters, coupler and memory etc. Utilizing these building blocks, complex photonics ICs with new functions like modulators and delay lines will be developed. Realization of ultracompact on-chip spectrometers operated in mid-IR region for environmental monitoring and biomedical sensing is another aim of this CRP program. Inputs and outputs from AlN ring resonators used in an in-plane spectrometer can be multiplexed into individual spectra through the use of non-linearity property in Aluminum Nitride. Secondly, 2D photonics crystals based AlN Fabry-Perot filter integrated on a CMOS chip will be developed as a mid-IR spectrometer working in free space. The multilayered Photonics ICs will leverage the low temperature process and integrate multiple AlN photonics layers on top of Si photonics layer and CMOS electronics layer. This novel technology platform will enable Singapore IC industry equipped with advanced Photonics IC technology which is promising in datacom and internet-of-thing (IoT) applications.

title: Drug Delivery for Eye Allergy
abs: We aim to jointly develop sustained-release formulations for improved management of eye allergy, via sub-conjunctival injection. It is hypothesized that drugs either delivered in a sustained fashion and/or having longer residence time within ocular tissues will entail lower dose requirements and thus lower frequency of administration. This collaboration aims to leverage on NTU’s expertise in both hyaluronic acid hydrogels and liposomes to encapsulate and deliver two drugs for ocular allergy management. Preparation of these formulations and in-vitro drug-release experiments will be conducted in NTU, to screen for promising candidates by drug-loading efficiencies and drug-release rates. Thereafter, a final screening will be conducted at Santen Pharmaceuticals to determine efficacy via pharmacokinetics and/or pharmacodynamics studies.The clinical end-goal for our work will be to address ocular allergies by replacing 4-times-a-day instillation of eyedrops with a once per 1.5 to 2 months sub-conjunctival injection of our formulation.

title: Mild Behavioural Impairment in pre-clinical Alzheimer's Disease: Correlation of Neuropsychological assessment and Resting state affective networks.
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Preclinical Alzheimer’s disease (AD) begins when AD pathophysiology occurs in a cognitively normal subject. Amyloid deposition has been postulated to occur years before subjects present with cognitive impairment. Recent advances in amyloid PET imaging have allowed in vivo detection of AD pathophysiology, hence enabling the diagnosis of preclinical AD. Preclinical AD subjects may present with mild behavioural symptoms which may predict future cognitive decline. However these specific behavioural symptoms are not well described at present. This knowledge gap results in under recognition of these patients with mild behavioural impairment and hence potentially delays diagnosis of early AD and treatment. Neuropsychological assessments of behavioural and mood domains allow detection of mild behavioural changes. Resting state affective networks also provide insight in the pathophysiology of these behavioural symptoms. This study aims to characterise the mild behavioural symptoms in preclinical AD and identify behavioral and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measures which may predict future cognitive decline. We hypothesise that subjects with preclinical AD who presents with mild behavioural symptoms will show increased connectivity in the resting state affective networks. In this case control study, 170 cognitively normal subjects will be recruited and they will undergo amyloid PET scan. Preclinical AD is defined as cognitively normal subjects with positive amyloid PET imaging and healthy controls are those with negative amyloid PET imaging. Mild behavioural changes will be assessed using neuropsychological and behavioural tests and their resting state affective networks will be correlated.These findings will be important in future research in preclinical AD which may potentially allow development of interventional strategies to prevent the progression to clinical AD.

title: Multi-level and High-fidelity Prints at the Nanoscale
abs: Huge profit of counterfeit and pirated products has irresistible attraction even at the price of heavy punishments. Although ever-increasing resources have been attracted to the related science and technologies, counterfeits are still well-nigh impossible to be warded off water-tightly. In this project, our objective is to transfer the developed techniques into practical applications through combining material science research, nanotechnology and information encoding algorithms into integrated optical nanostructures to achieve a multi-level information security technique applying to street-level, lab-level and advanced level applications. Recently, plasmonic nanostructures and metasurfaces have shown excellent capabilities in controlling the properties of electromagnetic waves, such as amplitude, phase, polarization, spin/orbital angular momentum, etc. In addition, upconversion materials provide a plenty of luxury to engineer the displayed color, such as doping type and level, wavelength and power of excitation source, which can be flexibly integrated with nanostructures. Therefore, we propose a revolutionary database-type colour print for multi-level and high-fidelity information display at the nanoscale by integrating upconversion materials, plasmonic nanostructures, metasurfaces, and other thin films. The target data or images will be encrypted into nanostructures as unintelligible configurations by employing both direct and indirect pathways. In comparison with traditional optical approaches, they show more advantages such as high resolution (beyond the optical diffraction limit), ultra-thin thickness (in the absence of bulk materials), more flexibility, and more degrees of freedom in encryption (polarization, wavelength, dispersion, lifetime, resonance, image distance, etc.). All the tunable parameters form a multi-dimensional basement of a pyramid-type optical image display technique. By randomly choosing and combining these parameters, a solid security “pathway” will be constructed. Our revolutionary technology will open up a new “optic” era of colour prints.
kw: Anti-counterfeiting;Plasmonics;Metasurfaces;Material growth;Up-conversion;Nanotechnology

title: Surgical PhotoAcoustic Nanotechnology (SPAN)
abs: The completeness of the surgical resection is a grand challenge in brain tumor surgery, which is largely due to the inability of surgeon to visualize microscopic tumor invasion at the tumor margin. We propose the development of Handheld Real-time Photoacoustic (HARP), for the detection and ablation of microscopic tumor residual at the tumor margin. The SPAN technology consists of two components: tumor-specific nanoparticle contrast agents and a hand-held real-time photoacoustic (HARP) imaging system. SPAN is expected to image tumor margin and infiltrates at the cellular level by taking advantage of the optical resolution afforded by photoacoustic microscopy and the strong photoacoustic signal from the contrast agents. At the end of resection, the tumor margin can be further treated with photothermal therapy to improve the clearance of all microscopic tumors due to the intrinsic photothermal response of the multifunctional contrast agents. Our focus is on high impact scientific and technological advancement of the field, and to lay the ground-work through intellectual property development and pre-clinical feasibility demonstration of HARP in image-guided surgery. In the long run, we will advance SPAN as an indispensable intraoperative tool for neurosurgeons and other surgeons, ultimately improving the clinical outcome and survival rates of cancer patients.
kw: Hand-held photoacoustic system;Photoacoustic microscopy;Nanoparticles;Image-guided surgery;Optical Imaging;tumor resection

title: Oxide Electronics Beyond Moore
abs: The science behind these proposed initiatives have been the strong role of electronic correlation and the interplay between spin, charge, orbital and lattice degrees of freedom found in the family of oxides which have given rise to fascinating phenomena such as high temperature superconductivity, colossal magneto-resistance, multiferroics, giant dielectric/piezoelectric behaviour in relaxors and novel magnetic phenomena which have become the basis for a whole new class of devices coming under the field of Oxide Electronics. The very strong Oxide Electronics team here was formed over the last six years in Singapore strengthened by an NRF CRP which ended in 2014. The proposal consists of 4 sub-sections- growth of functional oxides on silicon, demonstration of novel optical components on these functional oxides, novel low plasmonic loss materials based on oxides and nitrides discovered by the Singapore team and the development of an atto-joule magnetic switching device unique to oxide materials. This program leverages the prior CRP under which we have developed capabilities for the growth of multicomponent oxides with atomic control whereby films and heterostructures could be controlled at unit cell level (+0.1 monolayer). Novel discoveries by this team including defect mediated ferromagnetism, 2D electron gas at oxide interfaces with tunable electron density and magnetism, a very large spin-orbit interaction and potential for atto joule switching devices will be leveraged. The initial phase of the work will move towards design and optimization of electronic and opto-electronic devices based on these discoveries. In parallel, work will be started for fabrication of these devices on a silicon platform. This will require epitaxial growth of crystalline oxide layers uniformly on large silicon substrates (starting with 4 inches we will progress to 6 inches), etching techniques for nanoscale patterning of these devices and reliable metallization techniques. By the end of this program not only will new devices be demonstrated and optimized but will also be integrated with silicon.
kw: Oxide electronics;Beyond Moore;Integration on silicon;Ferroelectric modulators;Plasmonics;Atto-Joule switching

title: Clinical translation of whole genome sequencing to inform infection control and decrease mortality and morbidity from carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae infection.
abs: Introduction: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) are a global, antibiotic-resistant “superbug” threat with 40 to 80% mortality. Without safe, efficacious antimicrobials to treat CPE, infection control remains the main practical intervention to reduce CPE morbidity and mortality. Infection control is hindered by inability to accurately determine transmission pathways. Multiple seminal academic publications, based on retrospective studies, have confirmed the conceptual power of whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to inform infection control. Yet, WGS has rarely been applied practically to CPE infection control (or any other pathogens). Our group’s successful application of a virtual micro-array to analyze global and local CPE transmission had overcome the lack of plasmid phylogenetic methods, a previous barrier limiting WGS application to CPE control. In this proposal, we take the final step of clinical translation by prospectively applying and evaluating WGS for CPE infection control in one pilot hospital, TTSH.Aims and Methods: The overall aim is to assess if integration of WGS data by standardized protocols to inform infection control interventions would improve infection control outcomes. Specific outcome endpoints assessed, using interrupted-time-series analysis, pre- and post-WGS implementation, are (per 1,000 patients-days):1. Rates of CPE-carriage detection (Primary endpoint);2. Rates of clonal CPE-carriage with spatiotemporal overlap (Direct internal ward transmission);3. Rates of admission screening detection of CPE-carriage;4. Crude and attributable CPE mortality rates.Clinical significance:1. This study would provide “real-world” data for practical evaluation of the role of WGS for CPE infection control to enable planning of larger scale evaluations and scaling up implementation of WGS for CPE infection control.2. With increasing mass travel, rapid communication and international cooperation, global-level, One-Health strategies for CPE control will be facilitated by developing tools and repositories for analysis of CPE whole-genome data.
kw: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, Antimicrobial resistance, Whole-genome sequencing, Gram-negative bacteria, Plasmid, Infection Control.

title: Pregnancy after breast cancer: Attitudes of young women in the local context and outcome of interrupting endocrine therapy for pregnancy.
abs: Singapore, among the Asian countries, has a higher proportion of young women with breast cancer. 18% of breast cancer women are below 44 years of age. Treatment related fertility is an important issue in this group of young women with breast cancer, especially in the context of our ageing population, higher median age of child-bearing and a decreasing trend of child-birth.While conception after breast cancer does not seem to affect cancer outcome, definite evidence is lacking in estrogen receptor positive (ER+). Conducting a prospective clinical study of pregnancy after breast cancer is challenging due to the relatively small numbers and the emotional as well as preference-laden issues involved. Collaborative effort amongst international breast cancer groups from US and Europe namely International-Breast-Cancer-Study-Group (IBCSG), Breast-International-Group (BIG) as well as North-American-Breast-Cancer-Groups (NABCG) are underway and will be launching a study (POSITIVE) to address the issue of interrupting endocrine therapy to allow pregnancy. Feasibility study in the form of survey regarding fertility concerns, maternity desire and interest in the study was carried out in the participating countries. Overall, 37% respondents were interested in the study.My research aims to study the pertinent questions of fertility issues, maternal desire as well as study feasibility in the western context and compare it with that of local population via surveys and focus groups discussions (FGD). Through FGD, we can study the attitudes of breast cancer survivors towards pregnancy after breast cancer treatment. Through surveys, we can identify patients who will be interested to participate in the POSITIVE trial. Consequently, the objective is to establish important collaborative ties with International breast cancer groups and join in the international effort to carry out the study. This is crucial for Asian population especially when Asian has a high proportion of young women with breast cancer and the above international trial has not identified an Asian partner.
kw: Young women breast cancer, pregnancy, endocrine treatment

title: Proximal junctional kyphosis and sagittal malalignment: A cadaveric study to investigate the impact of sagittal alignment variations and instrumentation length on focal stress across proximal segments of a long spinal construct.
abs: Proximal-Junctional-Kyphosis (PJK) is a common, potentially devastating complication after spinal reconstruction for degenerative-kyphoscoliosis. In PJK compromise at cephalad segments of a long-spinal-construct lead to sequelae of segmental kyphosis and proximal-junctional-failure (PJF) associated with neurological deficits, which necessitates revision. Though complex pathogenic mechanisms are postulated, it is widely agreed that altered biomechanics/focal stresses at the upper instrument vertebrae (UIV) and proximal uninstrumented segments play a critical role in PJK development.Clinical reports highlight various predicting factors i.e. construct length and sagittal malalignment patterns that may predict PJK development. However biomechanical data on PJK etiology is limited. We propose a biomechanical study on a cadaveric model of a long spinal construct to study the impact of sagittal alignment variations and instrumentation length on focal stress at UIV and proximal segments. We have created a jig with a tilting/translating base able to alter specimen’s sagittal alignment. Six cadavers will undergo load testing, and outcome measures such as UIV and proximal segment intradiscal pressure and facet-joint pressure changes will be recorded at different thoracolumbar (TL) sagittal alignments. Cadavers will then be instrumented at different TL alignments to create construct models with distinctive sagittal profiles. The number of instrumented segments will also be altered. The constructs will then undergo repeat load testing and data recording. Analysis of outcome measures such as UIV and proximal segment force changes (i.e. facet-joint pressure and intradiscal pressure) will aid in identifying the ‘ideal’ construct length and sagittal alignment, with the least focal stress. As both construct length and sagittal alignment can be modified (via osteotomies and reduction methods) during surgery, knowledge from this study can aid surgeons in creating constructs with more ‘modulated’ proximal segment force changes, more resistant to PJK development. The knowledge can also aid in predicting PJK by identifying constructs with high proximal segment focal stress.
