title: Defining the Genetic Basis of Brugada Syndrome (BS) in A Geographically and Ethnically Diverse Cohort
abs: •Background. Brugada syndrome (BS) is an inherited channelopathy that has attracted great interest because of its association sudden death. It is estimated that BS is responsible for 4% of all sudden deaths and for up to 20% of sudden deaths in patients without structural heart disease. The genetic underpinnings of this disorder are complex and incompletely understood but it is known to be particularly prevalent in South East Asia. •Aim: To determine the profile of genetic mutations in all 14 genes associated with BS in cases and matched controls from geographically and ethnically distinct populations (South East Asia and United Kingdom).•Methodology. Case-control study utilizing cases and controls from South East Asia and UK, with next generation sequencing of 14 BS genes. Cases will be obtained via a recently established network of electrophysiologists in the Asia-Pacific region as well as the inherited cardiac conditions clinic at the Royal Brompton Hospital, a large tertiary referral center in London. Controls will be obtained from both Singapore and London (via their respective and established biobanking programs).•Summary. We have already laid the difficult and time-consuming groundwork for this study by establishing extensive regional collaborations in South East Asia, validating DNA collection via saliva (necessary to facilitate recruitment in South East Asia), and biobanking programs in both Singapore and London. This type of study is essential if genetic testing of BS is to translate into clinical workflows. Here I request funding carry out these studies across recruitment sites and to further my training in human genetics.

title: Phase II Study to determine the efficacy and safety of PIKA rabies vaccine containing the PIKA adjuvant with an accelerated regimen
abs: Every year, more than 100 million doses of post-exposure vaccine are administered in Asia to prevent the rabies. However, reports on death caused by rabies even after vaccination were not uncommon, mainly due to the late production of rabies virus neutralising antibodies (RVNA).According to animal studies, existing commercialized rabies vaccine could induce effective antibody production by 14 days after first vaccination and does not produce significant T cell immunity to contain the local infected cells. Three independent toxicity tests (acute toxicity, repeated allergic reaction test, chronic toxicity test) were conducted with mice, guinea pig and rhesus monkey in the independent GLP laboratories. The results have shown that both PIKA adjuvant and PIKA rabies vaccine are safe and well tolerated. In our recent study of Phase I trial conducted in Singhealth Investigational Medicine Unit, the results had demonstrated the safety profile and immunogenicity of PIKA rabies vaccine compared with the control vaccine Rabipur®. No serious adverse event (SAE) related to the trial was reported during the trial, and the adverse events (AEs) are comparable between PIKA rabies vaccine groups and control group. These results show that PIKA rabies vaccine is well tolerated and has comparable safety profile as the control vaccine. All subjects had reached 0.5 IU/mL at Day 14. Only 16.67% of subjects receiving the control vaccine had reached 0.5 IU/mL at Day 7. However, with an accelerated regimen, it was found that PIKA rabies vaccine has a better protection rate with 75% of subjects reaching 0.5 IU/mL at Day 7. This means that PIKA adjuvant vaccines were able to induce higher antibody titer production as early as Day 7. Thus, the proposed Phase 2 study is designed to investigate further on its efficacy profile of the investigational PIKA rabies vaccine under the accelerated regimen in healthy adult subjects.

title: Assessing the Volcanic Hazard for Singapore
abs: I propose to assess the volcanic hazard for Singapore by studying the past histories and present day eruptive dynamics of volcanic centers in SE Asia, in order to help mitigate their future impacts. Volcanic eruptions represent a constant threat to mankind; about 60 volcanic eruptions with fatalities were reported worldwide in the past ten years (Siebert et al., 2013). Singapore is surrounded by 745 volcanic edifices spread across SE Asia, 45 of which have erupted in the past fifty years. Of all the hazards presented by volcanic activity, volcanic ash is the most potentially impactful to Singapore, as it can be transported by wind over hundreds to thousands of kilometers. Although less lethal than other volcanic hazards, ash affects the lives of far more people and is highly disruptive to economic activity. Subject to variable winds, Singapore is within range of ash from eruptions occurring anywhere in SE Asia. A number of volcanoes remain severely understudied, in particular on Sumatra. Geological studies of volcanic deposits provide a window into the history and behavior of past eruptions: their frequency, magnitude, and variability in explosivity. Given that violent eruptions have recurrence intervals that are typically greater than 100 years, a threatening volcano is not one that has erupted violently in recent times. Large historic eruptions of the past millennia have had catastrophic consequences worldwide, killing tens of thousands of people due to a durable obscuration of sunlight and global cooling. Growing seasons were decreased by half, causing famines and outbursts of epidemics. The occurrence of explosive eruptions is controlled by a number of variables and processes that are linked by multiple feedback loops, which remain partly unresolved. I propose to address these issues with a multidisciplinary approach involving field work, petrologic, geochemical, and state-of-the-art textural analysis techniques.

title: Dimensionality Reduction for Recommender Systems: Unified Latent Co-representation of Multi-Modal Preference Signals
abs: One major scourge of current personalization and recommendation technologies is the sparsity of data. Algorithms that run on closed proprietary datasets are limited in predictive ability. The objective of this proposed research is to investigate how signals of user preferences that surface through various modalities (such as text, ratings, links, images, etc.) may be integrated holistically into a comprehensive knowledge base that can be used to improve recommendations. This overall objective naturally devolves into three closely related research aims: 1. We seek to institute continual data collection, extraction and curation services to model user preferences across a large collection of entities towrds the creation of a comprehensive knowledge base. 2. Through dimensionality reduction, we aim to integrate preference signals of various modalities into one shared representation, which unifies the primary relationships among instances and user preferences. 3. We would apply the knowledge base and dimensionality reduction to two use cases: (a) improving recommendation accuracy by incorporating the shared representation; and (b) developing novel visual recommendation services. The core of our approach is the development of dimensionality reduction based on probabilistic topic modeling and deep learning that optimize ordinal preferences. This methodology is novel in several respects. By modeling ordinal preferences, we generalize beyond ratings and co-occurrences to offer greater applicability to implicit feedback. By offering a unified co-representation of multi-modal data, we enable the use of various modalities of preference signals. By joining topic modeling and embedding, we offer greater semantic interpretability. By supporting Euclidean embedding, we enable applications such as visual recommender systems and fast retrieval through spatial data management. These comparative advantages are expected to push the boundaries of current dimensionality reduction and recommender systems towards greater use of multi-modal data as well as more visual elements in supporting personalization technologies.
kw: dimensionality reduction;visualization;recommender systems;probabilistic topic modeling;Euclidean embedding;deep learning

title: Ultra-protective pulmonary ventilation supported by low flow extracorporeal carbon dioxide removal (ECCO2R) and prone positioning for ARDS; a pilot study (U-Protect study).
abs: Critically ill patients are at increased risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), the most severe form of respiratory failure. While mechanical ventilation is lifesaving, it paradoxically perpetuates underlying pathology, a process described as ventilator induced lung injury (VILI). VILI can be minimised using low tidal volume (6ml/kg predicted body weight) lung protective ventilation (LPV). However, recent evidence suggests volumes lower than 6mls/kg, targeting plateau pressures under 28 cmH2O, maybe more effective. Tidal volumes below 6mls/kg create carbon dioxide (CO2) retention, which can cause raised intracranial pressure, right heart dysfunction, and immune dysfunction. Extracorporeal CO2 removal (ECCO2R) devices are machines that remove CO2 directly from blood, using similar principles to dialysis. Until recently, ECCO2R was only available in a few specialist centres, limiting access for most patients with ARDS and preventing exploration of the full potential. The Prismalung is a new, commercially available low-flow ECCO2R device that can be used in any intensive care unit capable of providing dialysis. We hypothesise that ECCO2R, provided by Prismalung, can support ultra-protective ventilation (1-3ml/kg predicted weight), resulting in plateau pressures (Pplat) consistently below 25 cmH2O, when compared to conventional LPV. Fifty patients with severe ARDS will be recruited and randomized to receive ultra-protective ventilation or conventional lung protective ventilation. All other interventions will be standardized across both treatment arms. Our primary outcome will be a Pplat ?25 cmH2O in the intervention arm. As a secondary outcome, we will collect blood samples to compare markers of lung injury and inflammation between both arms. Additional secondary outcomes will include, length of stay in ICU, cardiac function, illness severity, sedation use and mortality. We expect to show that ultra-protective ventilation creates lower airway pressures in ARDS, halting progress of VILI, accelerating recovery, and ultimately reducing the overall impact of ARDS.
kw: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Respiratory Failure, Extracorporeal Carbon Dioxide Removal, Ventilator Induced lung injury

title: Phase II study of Intravenous Vinorelbine in Patients with Relapsed Platinum Resistant or Refractory C5 High Grade Serous, Endometrioid, or Undifferentiated Primary Peritoneum, Fallopian Tube or Ovarian Cancer (VIP)
abs: It has been difficult to progress beyond platinum-based therapy for the treatment of ovarian cancer (OC) because OC is still largely treated as a single entity. A number of sub-classifications of the most common OC histiotype – high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC) suggest that more specific therapeutic approaches may be useful. Four molecular subtypes of HGSC – C1, C2, C4 and C5 which correlate with clinical outcome have been validated. The C5 subtype, comprises about 20% of HGSC, is associated with a poor outcome and potential oncogenic drivers have been identified. Recent preclinical experiments demonstrated vinorelbine targeted C5 subtype more effectively compared to the other subtypes. Several phase II trials of vinorelbine in recurrent OC have shown variable response rates of 3 – 29%, however, previous studies have involved “all-comers” and there has never been a trial involving patient selection based on pure HGSC and biomarkers of response. Our aim is to determine if targeting treatment based on the C5 molecular subtype with oral vinorelbine improves response rates and progression free survival. This open label phase II trial is a collaboration between Singapore and Australia for patients with platinum resistant or refractory C5 high-grade serous, high grade endometrioid or undifferentiated ovarian, primary peritoneal and fallopian tube cancer. A total of 36 patients with confirmed C5 HGSC based on the molecular classifier developed by the NATA accredited Bowtel Lab will be recruited and treated with 60mg/m2 oral vinorelbine until the appearance of significant treatment-related toxicity or disease progression. Dose modifications will be made based on a proforma. Simon’s Optimal two-stage design will be employed with a hypothesis of response rate <10% based on historical data; and the alternative hypothesis of response rates ?30% in patients with C5 HGSC following treatment with vinorelbine.
kw: platinum resistant ovarian cancer, high grade serous ovarian cancer, molecular subtyping, vinorelbine

title: Platelet inhibition to target reperfusion injury: The PITRI trial
abs: Clinical need: There remains a clinical need to improve health outcomes in patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) the leading cause of death and disability in Singapore and worldwide. One neglected therapeutic target is ‘myocardial reperfusion injury’ in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients treated by primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI). This results in microvascular obstruction (MVO) and cardiomyocyte death and contributes upto 50% of the final myocardial infarct (MI) size. Cangrelor, a potent intravenous platelet P2Y12 inhibitor with rapid onset and offset of action, has been demonstrated in experimental animal studies to reduce MI size when administered prior to reperfusion. Whether Cangrelor is effective in STEMI patients treated by PPCI is not known and is investigated in the Platelet Inhibition to Target Reperfusion Injury (PITRI) trial.Specific aim: To investigate whether Cangrelor administered prior to PPCI, can prevent MVO and reduce MI size in STEMI patients.Hypothesis: Cangrelor administered prior to PPCI will prevent MVO and reduce MI size in STEMI patients.Methodology: The PITRI proof-of-concept clinical trial will randomise 250 STEMI patients to receive either Cangrelor (single intravenous bolus followed by a 120-minute infusion) or matching normal/saline placebo, initiated prior to PPCI. The primary endpoint will be MI size at 6 months (measured by cardiac MRI). Secondary endpoints will include incidence and extent of MVO (cardiac MRI); and left ventricular size and ejection fraction (measured by cardiac MRI at 6 months).Expected outcome: If Cangrelor is shown to prevent MVO and reduce MI size, there is the potential to perform a large phase 3 clinical trial to determine whether it can improve clinical outcomes at one year (cardiac death and hospitalisation for heart failure), thereby demonstrating a real impact on health outcomes for IHD patients in Singapore and worldwide.
kw: Cangrelor; ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction; Primary percutaneous coronary intervention; Myocardial reperfusion injury; Microvascular obstruction; Cardioprotection

title: Aspirin for Dukes C and High Risk Dukes B Colorectal Cancers - An International, Multi-centre, Double Blind, Randomised Placebo Controlled Phase III Trial (ASCOLT)
abs: This proposal is for grant renewal funding for the ASCOLT Study (Aspirin for Dukes C and high risk B Colorectal cancer) an international collaborative group phase III clinical trial investigating the utility of low dose aspirin on improving outcomes in patients with resected Stage 2 and 3 colorectal cancer (CRC). The trial conceived and designed in Singapore, is led by an international collaboration from Singapore, UK and Australia with co-chairs Chia and Toh (Singapore), Ali (UK) and Segelov (Australia), involving more than 50 sites in 11 countries including Singapore, India, China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Australia, and New Zealand. Aim: To assess the effectiveness of Aspirin against placebo control in patients with dukes C or high risk dukes B colorectal cancer in terms of Disease Free Survival (DFS) and Overall Survival (OS) Primary endpoints- DFS among all eligible subjects (high risk Dukes B colon cancer, Dukes C colon cancer and rectal cancer patient sub-groups);- DFS among patients with colon cancer (high-risk Dukes B and Dukes C colon cancer).MethodsEligible patients will be randomized to either 200mg Aspirin or 200mg Placebo for 3 years, in a 1:1 ratio, using the following stratification factors: • Study centre• Tumour type (Dukes C colon, high risk Dukes B colon cancer & rectal cancer sub-groups) and• Type of adjuvant chemotherapy received (exposed/ not exposed to oxaliplatin)A total of 1200 patients will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio from approximately 50 centres in Asia. After randomisation, patient will undergo 3 monthly assessments for 3 years (month 3 to month 36) followed by 6 monthly assessments for additional 2 years (month 42 to month 60). The study is expected to recruit the last patient by 2018, with the last patient followed up until 2023.
kw: Aspirin, Colorectal, Cancer, Phase III

title: The Use of Atropine 0.01% in the Prevention and Progression of Myopia: ATOM 3
abs: Epidemiological data shows that 80% of 18 year old Singaporeans will become myopic (SE<-0.5D), and 15% will have high myopia (SE <-5.0D)1-3. High myopia is associated with ocular morbidity (eg. macular degeneration, glaucoma and retinal detachment) later in life4. Ways of tackling this problem include delaying the onset of myopia and preventing children from developing high myopia.The aim of this study is to evaluate the use of atropine 0.01% in pre-myopic and low-myopic children.Previous Atropine Treatment of Myopia (ATOM) studies suggest that atropine 0.01% daily slowed myopia progression by 58% over 2 years in children aged 6-12 years5, with less side effects (pupil dilation and near blur) compared to higher doses. We hypothesise that atropine 0.01% will also be effective in preventing the onset and progression of myopia in young Singaporean children at greater risk of developing high myopia (ie. with family history). We also hope to determine efficacy of lower frequencies of atropine.In this study, we hope to recruit 470 pre-myopic children (SE +1.00 to -0.49D) and 150 low myopic children (SE -0.50 to 1.25D). Pre-myopic children will be randomized to atropine 0.01% daily or placebo, while low-myopic children will be randomized to either atropine 0.01% daily, every alternate day or placebo. Included will be children aged 5-9 years old, preferably with 2 myopic parents (each with at least -1.00D of myopia). Children will be followed every 6 months for 2.5 years with a final (washout) visit at 3 years.Outcome measures in pre-myopic children will be the proportion of children developing myopia (SE <-0.50D) or low myopia (-0.50 to -1.50D) and in low-myopic children, outcomes measures will be a mean change in SE, and proportion of children with myopia (>1.50D) at 3 years.
kw: Atropine 0.01%, myopia, progression, prevention

title: Autologous Endothelial Progenitor Cell therapy for reversal of liver cirrhosis
abs: Liver cirrhosis constitute a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. This is driven by the high endemicity of viral hepatitis as well as the epidemic rise of fatty liver. While liver transplant is curative, the complexity of the procedure and the scarcity of donor grafts result in many patients missing out on transplantation and represent a major clinical gap. Autologous bone marrow mononuclear cell transplantation have been attempted in small cohorts of patients showing safety and potential benefit but has not been studied in proper randomised controlled study. Our own animal studies have shown that transplantation of nonparenchymal cells particularly those contributing to the sinusoidal endothelial lineage result in a dramatic reversal of cirrhosis and improvement in all clinical correlates of decompensated liver.We propose a randomised controlled study of 33 patients each in 2 arms, based on power calculation of potential efficacy from published studies. Endothelial progenitor cells are harvested by CD133+ MACS sort selection of bone marrow aspiration with mobilisation by SC GCSF. A minimum of 1x 10^7 cells are transplanted to one lobe of the liver via a percutaneous catheter. The primary outcome is improvement in at least 2 of 4 composite indicis including MELD score by 2 points, decrease in fibrosis using clinical, radiological or histochemical quantitation of liver biopsy at 3 months after transplantation. Secondary outcomes include improvement in portal pressure, liver function and survival up to 1 year. Controls are provided by contralateral lobe liver biopsy as well as control arm given monthly GCSFx3. The successful attenuation of liver cirrhosis with endothelial progenitor cell therapy will provide a critical treatment option that plugs an unmet clinical need, augmenting the capabilities of our national liver transplant programme which draws patients rom the region. It will also establish Singapore as a centre with capabilities for randomised controlled study in translational cell therapy.
kw: Liver stem cell, liver cirrhosis, bone marrow stem cell

title: An open-label Phase I dose-escalation study to characterise the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and maximum tolerated dose of BAY1143572 given in a once-daily or an intermittent dosing schedule in subjects with advanced malignancies (Part B).
abs: Myc is a proto-oncogene that has widespread influence on cell cycle progression, apoptosis and cellular transformation. Dysregulation of Myc signalling has been implicated in several tumour types but there is no effective therapies which target Myc. BAY 1143572 is a first in class and man orally given selective inhibitor of positive transcription elongation factor b (PTEFb) / cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9) which indirectly inhibits Myc. Preclinical models demonstrate efficacy of BAY 1143572 in myc-dysregulated tumors. Earlier dose-escalation study (Part A) of BAY 1143572 monotherapy showed manageable toxicity with dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) of on-target neutropenia. Pharmacokinetics (PK) of BAY 1143572 was found to be dose-proportional. Pharmacodynamic (PD) markers in blood demonstrate dose-dependent inhibition of PCNA and myc levels. We postulate that co-dosing of BAY 1143572 with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (GCSF) can circumvent neutropenia and increase the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of BAY 1143572 leading to greater myc inhibition and efficacy. We propose a multi-centre Phase I dose-escalation study of the combination of BAY 1143572 and GCSF (Part B) using continuous and intermittent schedules in patients with advanced solid tumours, with an expansion cohort at the MTD and/or recommended Phase 2 dose in gastric, triple negative breast cancer and DLBCL in up to 90 patients. Treatment will be given till disease progression, unmanageable toxicity or withdrawal of consent. The primary objectives will be safety and tolerability and PK. Secondary objectives will be efficacy. Exploratory objectives are evaluation of PD markers of target inhibition in blood and tumour biopsies and molecular profiling of tumours to identify predictors of response. PK data will be correlated with PD biomarkers to identify the biologically effective dose range.
kw: Clinical Trial, BAY 1143572, Phase I

title: In vivo efficacy study of ASLAN001, ASLAN002 and ASLAN003 in gastric cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma PDX models
abs: Gastric cancer (GC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are leading causes of cancer mortality worldwide, surpassed only by lung cancer. Both GC and HCC are highly prevalent in the Asia-Pacific region, where they remain a major health-care challenge. Most patients present at advanced stages as there is currently no practical screening method for achieving early diagnosis. Surgical resection is the first choice of treatment for early-stage GC and HCC; however, many cases are locally advanced or metastatic at the time of diagnosis and are thus unresectable. Several critical molecular signaling pathways such as hepatocyte growth factor receptor (c-met), vascular endothelial growth factor (VFGF)/VEGF receptor, ErbB receptors, Raf/MEK/ERK, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways are aberrant in GC. A considerable crosstalk and redundancy in signaling pathways are also observed in HCC and GC. Hence targeting single molecule or signaling pathway may have a limited efficacy. To be effective in HCC and GC therapies, new agents and novel therapeutic strategies must target various key signalling pathways. In this proposal we propose to evaluate the efficacy of ASLAN001 (a small molecule pan-HER inhibitor) and ASLAN002 (a small molecule c-met/RON inhibitor) in preclinical models of HCC and GC. In addition, combination of ASLAN001 and ASLAN002 and ASLAN001 and ASLAN003, a small molecule DHODH inhibitor, are also tested. Understanding the mechanisms of action of these therapeutic agents and methods of combining these drugs may help to increase their efficacy, reduce toxicity, and improve overall survival and quality of life in patients with HCC or GC.
kw: ASLAN001, gastric cancer, HCC

title: A phase Ib dose-escalation followed by a phase II singlearm study of the combination of LEE011 with letrozole for the treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative, advanced breast cancer
abs: Growth of hormone-receptor(HR) positive breast cancer(BC) is dependent on cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6(CDK4 and CDK6), which promote progression from the G1 phase to the S phase of the cell cycle. LEE011, an orally bioavailable CDK4/6 inhibitor, can potentially overcome resistance to endocrine therapy. In vitro studies have shown dose-dependent inhibition of proliferation across HR+ BC cell lines, with enhanced inhibition of tumour growth in combination with endocrine therapy such as letrozole in vivo.A global Phase III study is currently ongoing to assess the efficacy and safety of LEE011 with letrozole in postmenopausal patients with HR+ HER2-negative advanced BC. However, it enrolled patients predominantly from non-Asian countries. CLEE011A2115C(MONALEEASIA), a phase Ib dose-escalation followed by phase II single arm study of LEE011 with letrozole for the treatment of postmenopausal women with HR+ HER2-negative advanced BC, is intended to collect supplementary data in patients from Asian countries. The Phase Ib part consists of successive cohorts of patients receiving standard dose letrozole(2.5mg daily) with increasing doses of LEE011(400mg to 600mg once daily on days 1-21 of each 28 day cycle) to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended phase 2 dose(RP2D) of the combination. At least 12 patients will be enrolled in the Phase Ib part. The primary endpoint for the dose escalation part of the study will be the dose-limiting toxicity(DLT) rate observed during cycle 1. Dose escalation/de-escalation will be guided through a Bayesian Logistic Regression Model(BLRM) with escalation with overdose control(EWOC). Once the RP2D of LEE011 is determined, 100 additional patients will be enrolled in the Phase II part of the study. All patients will receive letrozole(2.5 mg) + LEE011(RP2D established from Phase Ib). The Phase II study will evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of LEE011 and letrozole in patients with advanced BC.
kw: breast cancer LEE011 letrozole

title: In vivo efficacy study of combination of Nexavar and BET inhibitor in Hepatocellular Carcinoma PDX model
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer death worldwide often presenting in the advanced stage when cure is not possible. Two randomized controlled trials of sorafenib in HCC patients showed an improvement in median overall survival of close to 3 months. As such, there is an urgent need for more efficacious systemic therapy. c-Myc is a master regulator of cell proliferation and metabolism and is central to the pathogenesis of HCC, by the coordinated upregulation of a transcriptional program influencing metabolic adaptation, cell division, and survival. Over-expression of c-Myc induced HCC, whereas inhibition of c-Myc expression resulted in the differentiation of tumor cells c-Myc transcription is positively regulated by members of the bromodomains and extraterminal (BET) domain family of proteins. This study aims to determine the in vivo antitumor activity of combination BET-BAY 002, a small-molecule compound with high potency against BET proteins, with sorafenib (Nexavar) in preclinical models of HCC.
kw: HCC, BET inhibitor, combination, sorafenib

title: Therapeutic Activity of ASLAN003 and ASLAN004 in Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma Cell Lines
abs: Peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCLs) are a heterogeneous group of lymphoproliferative malignancies more prevalent in Asia. PTCLs remain a poorly understood entity due to lack of molecular prognostic classifiers, and there are no effective treatment or targeted therapies available. With a poor outcome (3-year OS <50%) and rising incidence both in Asia and worldwide, PTCLs constitute an important medical problem with an immediate need for better therapeutics.ASLAN003 and ASLAN004 are two novel compounds from ASLAN Pharmaceuticals. ASLAN003 is a small molecule inhibitor of dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) that has successfully completed phase 1. Inhibition of DHODH leads to accumulation of p53 and p53-mediated apoptosis, and has been shown effective in B-CLL and solid tumors. ASLAN004 is a monoclonal antibody against IL13R?1 that blocks the binding and signaling of IL-4 and IL-13, and leads to down-regulation of anti-apoptotic molecules. Both of these ligands act through the JAK1/3-STAT6 axis. IL-13, IL13R?1 and IL13R?2 are highly expressed in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), and antibody?mediated neutralization of IL?13 as well as soluble IL13R?2 both inhibit the proliferation of CTCL cells. In this study, we propose to evaluate the therapeutic effect of both of these compounds in a panel of PTCL cell lines. We will also investigate the sensitive and resistant cell lines by various functional assays to better understand the mechanism of action of both drugs.
kw: PTCL, dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibitor, IL13R?1 monoclonal antibody

title: In vivo efficacy study of combination of panFGFR-inhibitor and SoC in 2 Ovarian Cancer PDX models
abs: Ovarian cancer is the leading cause of death from gynaecological cancer. Clear ovarian cancer is extremely common in Singapore and Asia and may be considered a predominantly Asian disease. Clear ovarian cancer is severely resistant to conventional chemotherapy and better treatments are urgently required. The fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signalling pathway is involved in regulation of cell proliferation, survival, differentiation, angiogenesis and tissue regeneration. Activation of FGFR signalling pathway is required for growth of ovarian cancer in vivo and it may play a role in chemotherapy resistance, suggesting that inhibition of this pathway may have therapeutic potential. In this study, we aim to determine in vivo efficacy of combination of panFGFR-inhibitor and standard chemotherapies (SoC) in ovarian cancer PDX models
kw: pan-FGFR, ovarian cancer, combination

title: Evaluating PI3K-AKT Oncogenic Activity in Non-Hodgkin’s Lymphomas – focusing on Peripheral T-cell lymphoma.
abs: The phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT pathway regulates cell growth, proliferation, and metabolism and is one of the most deregulated signaling pathways in human cancers. Genetic aberrations in this pathway, such as activating mutations of in the catalytic subunit of PI3K, deletion of the PTEN gene (encoding the phosphatase and tensin homolog), or genomic amplifications of upstream receptor tyrosine kinases, are identified in a wide range of human cancers. Given the central role of the PI3K-AKT pathway as an oncogenic driver of tumorigenesis, small molecules targeting this pathway are under active development as anti-cancer therapeutics. Indeed, a host of these kinase inhibitors that target key pathway components such as PI3K and AKT are at various stages of clinical trials. Non-Hodgkin's lymphomas (NHLs) are a heterogeneous group of lymphoproliferative malignancies with differing patterns of behavior and responses to treatment. Peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) consists of a group of rare and usually aggressive NHLs that develop from mature T-cells. Most T-cell lymphomas are PTCLs, which collectively account for about 10 percent to 15 percent of all NHL cases in the United States. Currently, there is no known effective therapeutic option for this group of cancers and the treatment modality is borrowed from the more successful cousin (B-cell lymphoma). Thus, a better understanding of the biology of PTCL is needed for the development of potential therapeutic agents that target oncogenic signaling pathways. In this study, we propose to evaluate the role of PI3K-AKT pathway in Non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas. We will investigate the PI3K-AKT activity in the various subtypes of PTCL as the first rational step for inhibiting this pathway in PTCL. Immunohistochemistry will be employed to determine the expression and activity of the PI3K-AKT pathway in this group of cancers.
kw: PI3-AKT pathway, Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma

title: Myopia 1: Sustained release formulation for atropine delivery
abs: Myopia, is the leading cause of impaired vision globally and the result of a growth change of the eye where the posterior part of the eye which is contained within the tough outer scleral shell, elongates forcing images formed by the cornea to become focused slightly in front of the retina. Myopia forces changes in lifestyle and in some older patients results in retinal pathology which can lead to blindness. In Singapore about 78% of children are myopic by the age of 18. Clinical studies carried out at the Singapore Eye Research Institute, SERI, and Singapore National Eye Center have established safe levels of atropine, a pan-muscarinic receptor blocking agent, that given as eye drops to children will suppress the growth of the sclera reducing the lifetime burden of myopia. Corroborating studies around the world have come to the same conclusion. However, important issues remain: Many children miss taking the eye drops, there are some side-effects such as headaches, and occasional problems with blurred vision which keep this treatment from becoming standard world-wide. The present studies hypothesize that a slow release drug strategy with atropine, weekly or monthly will allow the use of lower concentrations of atropine and at the same time increase dosing compliance. The Specific Aims for this application combines the technology developed at SERI and at NTU with expertise at Santen to determine the best system for loading atropine into liposomes and then regulate the release over days or weeks. Using technology that is basically approved will permit faster introduction into the clinic. The request is for one year of support to provide the necessary data for the slow release form of atropine to stop the progression of myopia in children. The next step will be human testing which will be carried out at SERI and SNEC.
kw: myopia, atropine, sustained release

title: Diagnostic Kit for Prediction of Spontaneous Miscarriage and other Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes
abs: Spontaneous miscarriage, preterm delivery and pre-eclampsia are serious adverse pregnancy outcomes. While women with threatened miscarriage have a higher risk of these adverse outcomes, not all such women develop these outcomes. Identification of the subgroup of women who are at a higher risk for these adverse pregnancy outcomes among those presenting with threatened miscarriage will allow clinicians to offer therapeutic interventions and provide anticipatory guidance. However, there are currently no screening tests for identifying ‘at-risk’ women. Our preliminary studies show that low serum progesterone and progesterone-induced blocking factor (PIBF) in women who present with threatened miscarriage, measured at presentation, predicted risk of spontaneous miscarriage before 16 weeks gestation, with suggested cut-off values of 35 nmol/L and 180 ng/ml, respectively. We propose to conduct a prospective cohort study of 1200 women with a singleton pregnancy presenting to KKH with threatened miscarriage between gestation weeks 6 to 10 to determine the association between serum and urine progesterone and progesterone-induced blocking factor with spontaneous miscarriage and various pregnancy outcomes (spontaneous miscarriage after 16 weeks gestation, threatened and actual preterm delivery, pregnancy-induced hypertension and pre-eclampsia). Measurement of urine PIBF, potentially a convenient, non-invasive, yet novel alternative to serum PIBF, is hampered by non-availability of a diagnostic kit. We propose to develop such a diagnostic kit, and in exploratory analyses, assess the association of urine PIBF with the primary and secondary outcomes. This study will provide an insight into the pivotal role of progesterone and PIBF in maintaining a healthy and successful pregnancy, and facilitate development of a screening test for early identification of women with a threatened miscarriage with a greater risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes throughout the rest of pregnancy.
kw: miscarriage, diagnostic, progesterone, progesterone-induced blocking factor, PIBF

title: Using continuous glucose monitoring data patterns to predict pancreatic beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity
abs: Diabetes mellitus is characterized by progressive beta-cell failure and insulin resistance, but these are not routinely measured in clinical practice due to technical challenges. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides information on blood glucose trends and rates of glucose change in routine clinical care for patients with diabetes. In this study, we examine the relationship between the CGM derived indices and pancreatic beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity. We will recruit 100 non-diabetic individuals of Chinese ethnicity, age 21-60 years and BMI 21-35 kg/m2. They will undergo mixed meal tolerance test to determine the glucose tolerance (area-under-the-curve for glucose). We will then select 25 individuals from low- and 25 individuals from high area-under-the-curve for glucose based on the median value. They will then undergo intravenous glucose tolerance test to estimate the beta-cell function, and hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp to estimate the whole body insulin sensitivity. Following this, they will wear a 7-day CGM to determine glucose variability. Data analysis will include correlation between glycemic variability and measures of beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity. A sample size of 50 will be adequate to give us 90% power with an alpha of 0.05 to detect a correlation R2 of 0.2 and above. The findings of this study might expand the current indication of CGM in the clinical care of patients with diabetes. In addition to providing daily glucose trends, it may be used in diagnostic, patient stratification and monitoring for drug efficacy in relation to beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity.
kw: continuous glucose monitoring, beta-cell function, insulin sensitivity

title: Phase II Study of AZD9291 in patients with advanced stage non-small cell lung cancer following prior EGFR TKI Therapy with EGFR and T790M mutations detected in plasma circulating tumor DNA
abs: About 50-60% of Asian patients with non-small cell lung cancer harbor epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations and EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) is the standard of care in this setting. However patients eventually develop acquired resistance and progress. The commonest mechanism of acquired resistance is a mutation in exon 20 of EGFR, T790M, seen in about 50% of cases. AZD9291 is an oral, potent, irreversible EGFR-TKI selective for sensitizing EGFR mutations and T790M resistant mutation with a minimal activity towards WT EGFR. In patients with T790M treated with AZD9291, the objective response rate (ORR) was 61% and the disease control rate (DCR) was 95%. Based on its efficacy and tolerability, AZD9291 has been granted accelerated approval by the FDA. The approval of AZD9291 will provide an impetus to re-biopsy patients with acquired resistance to determine EGFR mutation status. However, repeat biopsies are invasive and associated with risks. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in blood is a non-invasive method to assess EGFR status. We hypothesise AZD9291 will be efficacious in patients with EGFR sensitizing mutations and T790M detected in plasma ctDNA. The primary aim is to determine the ORR. Secondary aims are to (1) determine the progression free survival,
kw: non small cell lung cancer, third generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor, T790M

title: Assessing the Progression to Type-2 Diabetes (APT-2D): A Prospective Cohort Study Expanded from BRITE-SPOT (Bio-bank and Registry for StratIfication and Targeted intErventions in the Spectrum Of Type 2 Diabetes)
abs: The Bio-bank and Registry for StratIfication and Targeted intErventions in the Spectrum Of Type 2 Diabetes (BRITE-SPOT) aims to build a major resource that can support a diverse range of research intended to improve the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of T2D. BRITE-SPOT has been set up to prospectively collect clinical data and biologically relevant samples from individuals with, and at risk for type 2 diabetes (T2D), with the aim of delineating factors related to susceptibility, complications and response to treatment. Expanded from BRITE-SPOT, Assessing the Progression to Type - 2 Diabetes (APT-2D) is a prospective cohort with a focus on non-diabetics (normoglycemic or pre-diabetic), to expand the sample size and depth of metabolic phenotyping in these upstream groups, with the more targeted aim of delineating factors related to insulin sensitivity versus secretion, that relate to progression to T2D. 1,500 pre-diabetic and 800 normoglycemic participants will be followed for 3 years or up to conversion to T2D. Oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT) will be performed every 6 months to closely monitor disease progression. “Gold standard” physiology measurements such as euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamps (EHC, to assess insulin sensitivity) and frequently sampled intravenous glucose tolerance test (FSIVGTT, to assess insulin secretion) will be performed at baseline and conversion to T2D or at 3 years, whichever comes first. Thus, accurate measurements of insulin sensitivity and beta-cell function plus multiple plasma and serum samples collected longitudinally will generate an unprecedented disease progression cohort for biomarker discovery and validation. We hypothesize that there are distinct biomarkers in circulation that reflect the underlying mechanistic pathways specific to disease stage and reflect different trajectories in T2D progression. Characterization of subgroup-specific markers will facilitate efforts towards more targeted, effective interventions to improve outcomes for people with, and at risk for, T2D.
kw: Progression to Type 2 Diabetes, Biomarkers, Stratification, Insulin Resistance, Insulin Secretion, Trajectories

title: Effects of a Web/Smartphone-based Lifestyle Coaching Program on Gestational Weight Gain in Pregnant Women with Gestational Diabetes
abs: One fifth of pregnant women in Singapore develop gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). When poorly controlled, GDM leads to increased risk of maternal and perinatal complications and increased risk of diabetes for both mother and child. Lifestyle modification is the mainstay of management. 60% of our patients use on-line resources to help them manage their GDM. Mobile applications are effective in improving diabetes care and weight related behaviors through improved self-management. Jana Care has developed the Habits Program, a lifestyle coaching program (available on Apple app store or Google) which consists of interactive video lessons, diet, activity and weight tracking tools, messaging platform with coaches, daily tips and based on the Diabetes Prevention Program and Look-AHEAD Trial. It interfaces with the Aina device, a novel hardware sensor that plugs into any smartphone and can be used for glucose monitoring. The Habits Program is not designed for GDM. Therefore, we will work with Jana Care to develop a Habits Program for GDM considering the nutritional requirements and limitations on exercise during pregnancy, and the need to prevent excessive weight gain (as opposed to weight loss). We will customize the program for use in Singapore including translation (with modification of messaging) and incorporate a Singapore food database. We will then conduct a randomized clinical trial involving 300 women with GDM to compare conventional treatment with the Aina device for glucose monitoring to the Aina device supplemented with the Habits Program developed for GDM and a health coach. The primary outcomes are excess weight gain during the pregnancy. Secondary outcomes include glycemic control, requirement for insulin, maternal and fetal complications associated with GDM, and cost-effectiveness. This proposal will result in a unique clinical application for GDM that integrates lifestyle coaching with glucose monitoring and can be used to treat GDM with minimal manpower commitment.
kw: gestational diabetes, glucose monitoring, lifestyle modification, weight gain, pregnancy

title: A phase I/II, multicenter, open-label study of oral FGF401 in adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma or solid malignancies characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression
abs: This is a ‘first-in-human’ study of FGF401 to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) or recommended phase II dose (RP2D) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma or other solid tumors characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression; and to estimate the preliminary anti-tumor activity of FGF401 in these populations. Based on preclinical studies, FGF401 is a highly potent, selective FGFR4 inhibitor, thereby making it a good candidate for use in the clinic. Positive prediction for sensitivity to FGF401 was identified to be associated with positive expression of FGFR4, KLB and FGF19. This study has been designed as a phase I/II, multi-center, open-label study starting with a phase I dose escalation part followed by a phase II dose expansion part. Oral FGF401 will be administered as per protocol on a continuous schedule until patient experiences unacceptable toxicity, progressive disease and/or treatment is discontinued at the discretion of the investigator or withdrawal of consent. A cycle is defined as 21 days.Adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma or other solid malignancies characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression will be eligible to participate in Phase I of the study. In Phase II, additional patients will be enrolled and stratified in 3 groups. Group 1 consists of adult HCC patients from Asian countries, characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression. Group 2 includes adult HCC patients from non-Asian regions, characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression. Lastly, group 3 targets adult other solid tumor patients, characterized by positive FGFR4 and KLB expression regardless of geography.The study data will be analyzed and reported based on all patients’ data of the Phase I and Phase II parts up to the time when all patients have potentially completed at least six cycles of treatment or discontinued the study.
kw: FGF401, hepatocellular carcinoma, FGFR4, KLB

title: Development of a platform to bridge genomic information with phenotypic information for healthcare and healthcare research.
abs: A key enabling tool in precision healthcare is the integration of molecular data with associated clinical and phenotypic data. Unprecedented volumes of genomic data is being generated through –omic studies of human diseases, particularly cancer. This molecular information is derived from patient samples, each with unique phenotypes and clinical course. A key gap is the correlation of this information to learn more about the determinants of the clinical course of human diseases or indeed to influence and improve the management of human diseases. Achieving this will require a rich data-science platform that enables integration of genomic information with phenotypic information. Cancer forms a template disease for personalized –omic informed medicine leverage on in depth omics analysis of patient material combined with detailed phenotypic information of disease parameters and longitudinal effects of treatment. In collaboration with Systems, Applications & Products in Data Processing (SAP), a large German multinational software corporation that designs and maintains enterprise software, we seek to apply and build upon their existing healthcare platforms to customize and optimize a data science solution to integrate omic and phenotypic data, specifically focused on three domains: (1) integrating genomic information with phenotypic and longitudinal patient efficacy and toxicity outcomes (2) integrating genomic information with constantly accumulating biological knowledge from the biomedical literature. (3) integrating genomic information with global databases of ongoing clinical trials evaluating hypothesis of drugs with therapeutic selectivity in specific molecular subtypes. By developing platforms that integrate genomic information with these 3 layers of information platforms, it is envisaged that we can develop a comprehensive research and clinical decision aid tools that pools these “big data” sources together for transformative research and clinical care.
kw: Genomics, Data Science, Oncology

title: A multi-center, open-label study to assess the safety and efficacy of combination ceritinib (LDK378) and nivolumab in adult patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
abs: Despite the progress and efficacy of treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with targeted therapies against specific molecular oncogenic drivers, there is still a need for better treatment options for patients who developed resistance and to improve treatment outcome. Crizotinib has shown impressive activity in anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-rearranged/positive NSCLC but these cancers invariably progress, typically in less than a year. Therefore, other ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) with clinical activity in patients resistant to crizotinib are needed. Ceritinib is a more potent and selective ALK TKI, which can overcome crizotinib resistance.Aside molecular targeted therapeutics, recent studies have also demonstrated the efficacy of immunotherapy with PD-1 antibodies/blocking agents in NSCLC patients. Nivolumab is a fully human, IgG4 (kappa) isotype monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds specifically to PD-1 on activated immune cells and inhibits binding to its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2, thereby abrogating inhibitory signals and augmenting the host antitumor response.This open-label study aims to examine the effect of the combination of ceritinib and nivolumab in adult patients with Stage IIIB or IV NSCLC or relapsed locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC. The purpose of the dose-escalation phase is to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended doses for expansion (RDE) of ceritinib and nivolumab combination. The expansion phase will evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of the ceritinib and nivolumab combination in patients with (except ceritinib) or without previous ALK inhibitor therapy.Patients will be administered oral daily ceritinib and a fixed dose of nivolumab (given every 2 weeks) until he or she experiences unacceptable toxicity, progressive disease and/or treatment is discontinued at the discretion of the investigator, withdrawal of consent or due to any other reasons. A treatment cycle is defined as 28 days.
kw: Ceritinib, LDK378, Nivolumab, ALK, NSCLC

title: A phase II, multicenter, open-label study of EGF816 in combination with Nivolumab in adult patients with EGFR mutated non-small cell lung cancer and of INC280 in combination with Nivolumab in adult patients with cMet positive non-small cell lung cancer
abs: Despite the development of molecular targeted therapies against specific oncogenic driver mutations, we are still in need of other treatment approaches (improved/novel agents and/or combinations) for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients in order to address drug resistance and achieve better outcomes.Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), proven to be a key therapeutic target, is amenable to therapy with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). However, patients ultimately progress. In 50-60% of these cases, T790M mutation has been found to be the cause of resistance. Third generation (i.e. irreversible; WT EGFR sparing; with relatively equal potency for activating EGFR mutations L858R, ex19del and acquired T790M) are currently being evaluated in trials. Aside EGFR, mesenchymal-epidermal transition factor (c-MET) is also emerging to be a potential target in NSCLC. Even though these inhibitors have shown promising initial results, it seems that they would not be sufficient as single agents.Combination therapy involving targeted agents and immunotherapy may improve progression-free survival and ultimately overall survival in NSCLC patients. This phase II, open-label study seeks to determine if combination of Nivolumab with either the third generation EGFR TKI, EGF816, in EGFR T790M NSCLC patients who have developed resistance to EGFR TKI treatment or with the highly selective and potent c-MET inhibitor, INC280, in cMET positive (EGFR wild type) patients who progressed on chemotherapy provide clinically meaningful benefit over the single agent EGF816 or INC280 activity in similar populations observed in historical and/or ongoing trials.Patients will be administered a fixed dose of Nivolumab (every 2 weeks) in combination with daily oral EGF816 or INC280 until he or she experiences unacceptable toxicity, progressive disease and/or treatment is discontinued at the discretion of the investigator, withdrawal of consent or due to any other reasons. A treatment cycle is defined as 28 days.
kw: EGF816, Nivolumab, INC280, EGFR, cMet, NSCLC

title: A phase II investigator -sponsored multi-institution study of ibrutinib in relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma
abs: Marginal zone lymphomas (MZL) are a group of indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma that has higher incidence in Asia than the West. They are related to infectious agents such a Helicobacter pylori or inflammatory conditions such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis and hence chronic antigen stimulation resulting in B-cell proliferation and subsequent transformation to B-cell lymphoma represents a putative pathogenic mechanism in MZL. Targeting the B-cell receptor pathway with ibrutinib, a Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is thus a rational treatment strategy for this lymphoma where no standard treatment options exist. The aims of this study are to evaluate the clinical efficacy of ibrutinib in patients with relapsed or refractory MZL in a phase II open-label, multi-centre, clinical trial. Patients will receive ibrutinib at 560mg daily until disease progression, unacceptable toxicities or patient or investigator decision to end therapy. Computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography (PET)/CT scans will be performed at baseline and after every 8 weeks. The primary end point is overall response rate (ORR) and secondary endpoints are progression-free survival, overall survival, frequency and severity of adverse events encountered on study. Simon’s 2 stage minimax design will be used to determine the number of patients recruited on study. Twelve patients will be enrolled in the first stage of the study. If there are at least 3 responders, a total of 21 patients will be enrolled. The treatment will be declared ineffective if there are less than 8 responders in total. This design has a 90% power to detect an ORR of 50% at a 5% significance level.

title: AN OPEN-LABEL, SINGLE-ARM PHASE 2 CLINICAL TRIAL OF REGORAFENIB IN PATIENTS WITH MULTIPLY RECURRENT EPITHELIAL OVARIAN CANCER
abs: Regorafenib is an oral multikinase inhibitor that blocks the activity of kinases involved in angiogenesis (VEGFR 1,2,3 and TEK), oncogenesis (KIT, RET, RAF1 and BRAF) and tumour growth (PDGFR and FGFR). Pre-clinical research data from patient derived xenografts at the National Cancer Centre Singapore indicates that Regorafenib has a high level of activity in Endometriod, Clear cell and other subtypes of ovarian cancer. Our data is also consistent with Bayer's internal data showing a extremely high level of activity in 5/6 of their ovarian PDX cancer cell lines. Whilst Regorafenib has been FDA approved for the treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer who have failed prior bevacizumab, its role in the management of ovarian cancer remains to be defined. In this prospective single arm, open-label, phase II clinical study, 34 patients with multiply recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer who progress after 2 initial lines of platinum based chemotherapy will be evaluated for Regorafenib safety and efficacy. This study aims to valid our earlier pre-clinical findings, bringing pre-clinical knowledge back to the clinic, to comple the cycle of research initiated by tissue donation from more than 50 NCCS and KKWCH patients. Primary Objective•Investigator assessed progression free survival (RECIST and/or GCIG Ca125 progression criteria)Secondary Objective•Tumour response rate (RECIST and/or GCIG Ca125 response)•Overall survival (in bevacizumab and non-bevacizumab exposed patients)•Safety and tolerability•Health related quality of life•Biomarker analysis (circulating cell free plasma DNA)

title: AR-V7 Splice Variant in Asian Patients with Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer (CRPC)
abs: Abiraterone and Enzalutamide are two novel agents for the treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) that target the androgen pathway. Nevertheless, 20-40% of CRPC patients does not respond to these therapies or develop resistance to them after initial response. One of the postulated mechanisms for this resistance is the development/presence of androgen receptor splice variant-7 (AR-V7), a truncated form of the androgen receptor (AR) that lacks the ligand-binding domain, which is the target of these agents. A study has shown that detection of AR-V7 in circulating tumor cells (CTC) from advanced CRPC patients is associated with resistance to the new hormonal agents. In a more recent report, it was reported that taxanes may be more efficacious than AR-directed agents in AR-V7-positive men. Another study showed that patients treated with taxane chemotherapy may actually have a reversion of their AR-V7 status, hence potentially enabling them to derive benefits from the hormonal agents subsequently. Whilst these results were interesting and potentially practice changing, it was done on small population of Caucasian patients and has not been replicated elsewhere.Thus, we are proposing a multinational, multicentre project to study the incidence of the AR-V7 in Asian population and how different treatments impact the patient outcomes. We aim to recruit 101 patients with CRPC from 5 countries over a 1-year period. Blood and tissue specimens will be collected at two timepoints (pretreatment, at disease progression) for extraction of CTC and analysis of AR-V7. Our primary endpoint is to determine the proportion of ARV-7 positive patients at baseline. Secondary objectives include determining PSA response rate, survival outcomes and the incidence of AR-V7 at the time of progression.With better understanding of the mechanism of resistance and response to androgen-directed therapies, we hope to improve treatment outcomes for these patients.

title: A phase II single arm trial to assess the efficacy of ASLAN001 plus capecitabine in previously irradiated, progressing central nervous system (CNS) metastases for HER2 positive breast cancer patients.
abs: Brain metastasis in breast cancer (BMBC) has very poor prognosis. The focus for this group of patients is on palliation as well as therapeutics that offer meaningful clinical benefits. A few phase II studies have demonstrated the activities of either lapatinib alone or in combination with capecitabine for treatment of brain metastases after radiosurgery and/or WBRT. Nancy Lin et al showed CNS responses of around 5-20% with lapatinib single agent or lapatinib with capecitabine. While the combination showed activity, it was associated with significant grade 3-4 toxicities. Newer agents should be researched for this exclusive group of patients. This provides the basis for this phase II trial which also uses small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor ASLAN001 (a potent, specific, adenosine triphosphate competitive inhibitor of the tyrosine kinases of the cell surface receptors human epidermal growth factor receptor HER-1, HER-2, and HER-4) in combination with capecitabine for evaluation of CNS response rate in previously irradiated, progressing CNS metastases.This is a single arm, single center, phase 2 study. A total of 29 eligible HER2 positive breast cancer patients with irradiated, progressing brain metastasis will be enrolled to receive ASLAN001 400 mg orally BID with capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 orally BID for days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle. Treatment will continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The secondary objectives include evaluation of the clinical benefit of ASLAN001 in combination with capecitabine in systemic disease (outside CNS), and evaluation of the safety and tolerability of ASLAN001 in combination with capecitabine. Baseline brain imaging using either magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be performed; non-brain imaging with a CT will also be performed in the same settings. Radiological imaging to assess disease status will be performed at baseline and every 2 cycles until disease progression.

title: The Alzheimer’s disease THErapy with NEuroaid (ATHENE) Study : Assessing the Safety and Efficacy of Neuroaid II (MLC901) in patients with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease stable on Cholinesterase inhibitors or Memantine: A Randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial
abs: Neuroaid (MLC-601) is a possible modulator of amyloid precursor protein (APP). In a preclinical study; MLC601 has shown increase in levels of sAPP? and significant decrease in full length Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP) in human neuroblastoma cell line. MLC901 (Neuroaid-II) is a simplified from of MLC601, having comparable effect to MLC601. MLC 601 was tested in mild to moderate Alzheimer’s Disease(AD) patients, unable to tolerate or failed benefit from Rivastigmine. It was well tolerated and showed promising effects on cognitive function during 18 months of treatment. In another study, MLC601 efficacy and safety was tested against the standard CHEIs (Donepezil, Rivastigmine, Gallantamine).It showed promising safety profile and its efficacy was comparable to standard CHEIs. We aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Neuroaid II (MLC901) as an add-on therapy to standard CHEIs/Memantine in mild to moderate AD patients. Our hypothesis is to prove that Neuroaid-II is safe and effective drug for mild to moderate AD and Neuroaid-II may slow disease progression in AD. Patients will be randomly assigned to Neuroaid II or Placebo arm(1:1). Neuroaid-II is available as 0.4 mg capsules; dose is 2 capsules three times daily, matching placebo capsules will be used. title: A Multicentre Phase II randomised trial of DURVALUMAB versus physician’s choice chemotherapy in recurrent ovarian clear cell adenocarcinomas (MOCCA)
abs: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma (OCCC) is one of the main histologic subtypes of EOC. It has a significantly higher prevalence rate in the Asian population and approaches 25% of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). Women diagnosed with OCCC tend to be younger and more likely to be diagnosed with earlier stage disease (Stage I-II. When adjusted for stage, the 5 year disease specific survival of patients with advanced stage OCCC is much worse than the more common high-grade serous ovarian cancers. Retrospective studies of response rates in recurrent OCCC have been disappointing with <10% response rates to further lines of chemotherapy observed in these women. Studies also observed a median PFS of ~11 weeks and median overall survival ~40 weeks. There is increasing evidence to support the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors in EOC with response rates in the recurrent setting ranging from 11% - 23% and disease control rate of around 35% - 55% from early phase trials. Given the limited benefit observed from cytotoxic chemotherapy, there is now great interest in the development of other therapies for the treatment of OCCC.In collaboration with Korea and Australia, we plan to undergo a multicenter, Phase 2 study in patients with recurrent OCCC to determine if DURVALUMAB improves progression free survival compared to physician’s choice chemotherapy. Patients will be randomized 2:1 to receive either DURVALUMAB every four weeks or physician’s choice chemotherapy. This will be the first signal seeking study to evaluate the efficacy of the immune checkpoint inhibitor DURVALUMAB, in patients with recurrent OCCC lead by National University Hospital in collaboration with leaders in the ovarian cancer field from Australia and Korea. This is a rare tumour but nevertheless important particularly in Asia. It has been largely neglected but there are potentially active targeted therapies now available which need to be investigated.

title: Phase 0 trial of 18F-3-Fluoro-5-[(pyridin-3-yl)ethynyl] benzonitrile ([18F] FPEB), a PET imaging tracer for quantifying the cerebral distribution of Metabotropic Glutamate 5 receptors(mGluR5): To study radiochemical safety, biodistribution, tracer kinetics and radiation dosimetry in the Asian population.
abs: BACKGROUND Glutamate is a major excitatory neurotransmitter found to be implicated in several neurodegenerative disorders. Signalling of glutamate is mediated by G protein-coupled metabotropic receptors (mGluRs) that are predominantly expressed in the brain. The binding of glutamate to mGluR activates intracellular messenger systems and thus regulates neuronal excitability.There are eight subtypes of mGluR (mGluR1 to mGluR8). In this study, we focus on mGluR5. mGluR5 is linked with neurological disorders such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s disease and multiple sclerosis. [18F] FPEB is a Position Emission Tomography (PET) tracer which is highly selective for mGluR5. In preclinical and clinical studies, they show a regional uptake pattern consistent with known distribution of mGluR5 in the brain. AIMS In an Asian population, (1) evaluate the safety of [18F]FPEB positron emitting radiotracer administered intravenously, for potential use as a PET tracer for mGluR5, and (2) assess the ability of [18F] FPEB (radiotracer) to image and quantify mGluR5 in the brain regions by PET imaging. METHODOLOGY The study will consist of two parts. The first cohort will receive a single dose of [18F] FPEB. A whole body scan, with venous sampling will be performed to calculate radiation exposure. The second cohort of patients will receive two separate doses of [18F]-FPEB. Dynamic PET brain and arterial blood samples will be performed to analyze pharmacokinetics of [18F]-FPEB and validate its utility for quantifying mGluR5 in brain. Test-retest reliability of the method will be performed by repeating the PET scan on the same subjects at a different time points.SIGNIFICANCE Quantification of mGluR5 binding in vivo could help to elucidate the role of glutamate in physiological and pathological conditions. No potential benefit is expected. The potential risks will be radiation exposure to the subjects, which will be kept to a minimum by selection of as low dose as possible.

title: An Investigator Sponsored Phase I Study of the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Escalating Doses of combination treatment of AZD5363 + Olaparib + DURVALUMAB (Arm A) and Olaparib + Cediranib + DURVALUMAB (Arm B) in Patients with Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumor Malignancies.
abs: As targeted therapeutics continue to emerge, we are faced with new dilemmas from patient selection to its appropriate use in our treatment paradigm and management of ensuing toxicities and ultimately overcoming resistance that will undoubtedly follow. Despite some efficacy observed in pre-clinical and early phase studies, there has been lack of durable responses to monotherapy targeted therapeutics and early development of secondary resistance mechanisms, providing the rationale for safe and efficacious combination strategies. Pre-clinical studies have demonstrated synergistic anti-tumour activity in certain sporadic cancers when these targeted therapeutics are used in combination settings. We plan to undergo a single centre dose escalation, Phase 1 study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of combination treatment AZD5363 + Olaparib + DURVALUMAB (Arm A) and combination treatment Cediranib + Olaparib + DURVALUMAB (Arm B) and to determine the RP2D in patients with solid tumour malignancies. Both arms will be carried out in parallel. The combination treatment in both these arms without DURVALUMAB has been shown to safe, tolerable with manageable toxicities and efficacious. The study will include up to 40 patients (20 patients in each arm) using a modified 3 + 3 design. This is the first phase 1 clinical trial using a triple combination therapy for patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumour malignancies incorporating important targeted agents that will be utilised in the treatment paradigm of most patients with solid tumour malignancies as molecular and genetic markers become more commonly used in clinical practice.

title: Epigenomic Profiling of Altered Chromatin States in Gastrointestinal Cancer
abs: Epigenetic alterations are fundamental hallmarks of cancer genomes, profoundly influencing patterns of gene expression and chromosomal instability in tumors. Clinically, cancer-associated epigenetic changes have also been associated with patient prognosis, treatment response, and drug resistance. While promoter DNA methylation has been extensively studied, our current appreciation of chromatin and histone modifications in different cancer types, and the specific cis-acting regulatory elements (CAREs) bookmarked by these alterations (such as enhancers and promoters), remains nascent. Previous work by our group and others has highlighted an important role for epigenetics in gastric cancer (GC), the 3rd highest cause of global cancer mortality. Here, we hypothesize that CAREs deregulated in GC (G-CAREs) are likely to underpin the ability of GCs to initiate and maintain aberrant transcriptional programs, ultimately driving various aspects of malignancy. We thus propose to a) apply recently developed Nano-ChIPseq (Nano-scale Chromatin ImmunoPrecipation and Sequencing) methodologies to identify genome-wide patterns of G-CARE activity in primary GCs, b) Integrate G-CARE chromatin states with transcriptomics, chromatin-conformation measurements, and enhancer assays to dissect G-CARE cis-regulatory interaction landscapes and to elucidate the contribution of G-CAREs to altered GC gene expression, c) study connections between G-CARE activity and GC genetic and structural variation revealed through whole-genome sequencing data, and d) identify trans-acting factors and epigenetic-directed therapies important in initiating and maintaining G-CARE activity. The proposed work, which builds upon an already successful preexisting translational GC research infrastructure (Singapore Gastric Cancer Consortium) will yield insights into the spectrum of epigenomic configurations, transcriptional states, and genetic variants contributing to GC development, particularly in non-protein coding genomic regions which occupy 99% of the human genome. Our results will have translational impact by revealing potential biomarkers linked to GC initiation and progression, and may highlight new therapeutic approaches for GC via targeting tissue-specific G-CAREs necessary for maintaining GC cell survival. (299 words)

title: Multiparametric imaging for the differentiation between radiation necrosis and tumor recurrence using PET/MRI.
abs: Differentiating radiation necrosis from recurrent brain tumors is currently one of the most clinically challenging problems in care and management of glioblastoma patients. Both radiation necrosis and recurrent tumor exhibit similar morphological appearance on standard MRI making non-invasive diagnosis extremely challenging for clinicians, with surgical intervention being the only course for obtaining a definitive ground truth. Strong evidence suggests that phenotypic differences are obvious and hence cues from multiparametric imaging may distinguish between the two pathologies. One challenge is that these differences, if they exist, might be too subtle to distinguish by one modality alone. Each of the tumor characteristics is best identified by a specific imaging protocol and while one feature may not be really evident, a combination of multiple features acquired simultaneously may help to effectively differentiate the two with greater sensitivity and accuracy. For this we propose to use combined PET/MRI to explore the utility of tumor descriptors in identifying the MRI protocol or protocols that best distinguishes necrosis and recurrence across the cohort of patients. For this purpose, thirty patients who have undergone chemoradiation after surgical resection of brain tumor will undergo three consecutive scans at 0,6, and 12 months after surgery to evaluate imaging parameters as noninvasive prognostic markers for severity and progression of disease. Advanced imaging such as structural, perfusion, diffusion, and metabolic information will be assessed to provide for a broader spectrum of markers that will provide more accuracy in the distinction between the two tissues. We hypothesize that conventional MR and PET findings in combination may favor tumor recurrence or radiation necrosis on serial scanning. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study applying PET/MRI to study necrosis vs recurrence and to extract as much data as possible to better estimate the need for these additional markers.

title: Exploring the CNS Toxicity of Dexamethasone in the Treatment of Paediatric ALL: A Multi-faceted fMRI/MRS Study including Innovative Use of Fitbit Trackers in Children
abs: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is the most common childhood cancer, with cure rates approaching 90%. Dexamethasone is a steroid which is the cornerstone of ALL therapy, however it causes significant side effects such as mood changes and disturbed sleep -adding significantly to the family's stress of managing a child with cancer and can even put a child at risk of suicide. Little is known about how and why Dexamethasone causes all these side effects. Our study aims to use resting state functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging(MRI) and spectroscopy as a non-invasive way to discover the parts of the brain which are affected and changes in neurotransmitters caused by Dexamethasone, in relation to neuropsychiatric tests and the use of Fitbit for sleep tracking. We will recruit 100 children with ALL who are treated on the same protocol from 2 institutions over 24months. This will consist of 3 main time points, before, during and after completion of specific blocks of Dexamethasone. At each time point, children aged 4 to 16 will complete an MRI scan as well as neuropsychiatric testing. A study pilot involving 3 children with ALL aged 4 to 10 has been successfully implemented. A healthy control arm involving 20 adult subjects who voluntarily received 12mg of oral Dexamethasone for 5 days was also completed. Preliminary analysis revealed significant decrease in total brain volume and specifically the hippocampus, cerebellum and grey matter at drug peak -all of which were reversed on wash out scans. Functional MRI revealed significant decrease in functional connectivity in the frontal cortex and specifically between the cerebellum, hippocampus and thalamus. In addition, spectroscopy showed significant decrease in the GABA concentrations in the hippocampus from baseline to peak scan with reversal at washout. We hypothesize that similar changes and more will be seen in same study in children.

title: Harnessing the therapeutic capabilities of adipose derived stem cells for flap reconstruction
abs: Large soft tissue defects resulting from trauma and surgical ablation are a reconstructive challenge for the plastic surgeon. Flap reconstruction is an important option of treatment and reliable blood supply is a major consideration. Adipose derived stem cells (ADSC) have been shown to demonstrate angiogenic potential amongst other benefits in wound healing. However, mainstream utilization has yet to be realized in clinical practice.The main aim of this study is to evaluate the use of adipose derived stem cells in the enhancement of flap reconstruction for better flap survival and earlier flap division for staged reconstruction in a rodent model.The investigators hypothesize that the paracrine activity of ADSC can promote angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis in flap reconstruction resulting in better and earlier establishment of robust blood perfusion and, thus, flap survival. In the longer-term, a well-established intra-, through- and peri-flap lymphatic circulation may result in lesser flap edema.In this study, the investigators will be utilizing established rodent model of flap surgery with modifications; namely, the McFarlane’s dorsal skin flap model and the pedicled groin flap model. Flap survival will be quantified based on necrosis and epidermiolysis, and perfusion will be visualization using fluorescence technique. Biochemical analyses will evaluate the levels of signalling and growth factors and histology will be used to analyze capillary density and lymphatic vessels. Stromal vascular fraction and ADSCs will be isolated from rodent and human adipose tissue for characterization before transplantation.This study will demonstrate important preclinical information of ADSC use in flap reconstruction and facilitate the planned clinical trials in our department. Successful use of ADSCs or stromal vascular fraction will allow for better flap survival and/or earlier flap division in staged procedure; resulting in shorter hospital stay, lower rates of wound infection and lower overall healthcare cost.
