title: Implementation of a screening and early intervention program for breast cancer related lymphedema
abs: Lymphedema is a common problem experienced by many with breast cancer. It is characterised by swelling of the arm, and can cause pain, restricted mobility and recurrent cellulitis. Most often, it occurs after axillary clearance, but can also occur after sentinel node biopsy, axilla irradiation and from extensive nodal disease. Early intervention can halt progression to chronic irreversible lymphedema. We hypothesise that screening at risk patients will increase the detection of lymphedema at the subclinical and early mild stages, which are most amenable to currently available treatments. In this study, we aim to evaluate bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) as a screening modality. BIA can detect lymphedema early, even before arm swelling is appreciable. We will first determine an optimal cut-off threshold: 50 women with lymphedema will serve as reference, and compared with 50 healthy women and 180 women at risk of developing lymphedema. The 180 ‘at risk’ women will continue to be followed up during the study period. At each visit, BIA, limb girth (assessed by sequential circumferential tape measurements), body mass index will be measured. Standard demographic and clinical data, subjective self-reported symptoms and quality of life scores will be collected. Attending clinicians will also be surveyed on their assessment of lymphedema. We will determine how many cases of lymphedema are detected by screening. We aim to develop a grading to stratify lymphedema severity, using objective, clinical and subjective parameters. This will allow us to develop protocols that will enable any member of the breast team to initiate general treatment measures without having to wait for a formal physiotherapy review. In doing so, the lymphedema is not allowed to worsen before specialised physiotherapy treatments are started. We believe that screening and early intervention can reduce the incidence of chronic lymphedema and will improve survivors’ quality of life.
kw: early intervention; lymphedema; breast cancer

title: Inequalities in Socioeconomic Status and Executive Functions: Do Bilingualism and Language Stimulation Matter?
abs: Children of low socioeconomic status (SES) perform more poorly compared to their more advantaged counterparts on cognitive tests. “Executive functions” (EF) have been consistently shown to be more sensitive to SES than other components of cognition. Recent studies have suggested plausible mediating processes that link SES with EF; however, little is known about whether certain early experiences, like bilingualism and language stimulation, alleviate SES-related disparities in EF. AimsTo examine 1) the contributions of family SES to child EF and 2) whether the cognitive advantage associated with bilingualism and language stimulation extends to children challenged by a disadvantaged background. Hypotheses1)Lower SES is associated with poorer EF except for bilingual children2)Language stimulation mediates that relationship between family SES and child EF MethodsThe sample consists of ~600 children enrolled in the GUSTO (Growing Up in Singapore Toward healthy Outcomes) cohort. Demographics on SES, parental stress, early literacy activities, and family language background have been collected. We will examine the children’s EF profiles from age 4.5 to 6 using the Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF) and the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB). A linear regression model will examine the independent effects of three SES indices on child EF, after controlling for child (e.g. cognitive ability, age, gender) and family factors (e.g. parental stress, psychopathology). Multicollinearity of SES variables will be explored. Multiple regression models will determine the indirect effect of language stimulation and moderating effect of bilingualism on the relationship of SES and EF. Structural equation models will provide a structural analysis and examine latent constructs of SES and EF using multiple observed variables. SignificanceA better understanding of factors that promote early development of EF will advance interventions aimed at reducing social health disparities.
kw: Executive function, socioeconomic status, bilingualism, cognitive stimulation

title: Randomized Control Trial Comparing Proposed Algorithm and Current Best Practice in the Evaluation of Suspected Appendicitis.
abs: Although the use of computed tomography (CT) has reduced negative appendectomy rates, its radiation risk remains a concern. Indiscriminate CT utilization subjects patients to unnecessary radiation and contributes to increased healthcare costs. The Alvarado Score (AS) is a clinical scoring system that assesses the likelihood of acute appendicitis based on patient history, physical examination findings and blood investigations. Based on analysis of a prospective database of 500 consecutive patients admitted to the Department of General Surgery for suspected appendicitis, we compared the diagnostic performance measures for CT scan and the AS and identified ranges where patients were unlikely to benefit from CT evaluation. We thus propose an algorithm for the management of acute appendicitis using the AS to guide CT utilization (Figure 2). We hypothesize that this algorithm will reduce the proportion of CT utilization, significantly, from that of current best practice without compromising negative appendectomies in patients with suspected appendicitis. We propose a validation of our algorithm in the form of a phase 2 randomized control trial comparing the proposed algorithm compared to current best practice.Patients with suspected appendicitis recruited into the study from Singapore General Hospital will be randomized into 2 treatment arms:-i) Intervention Arm – Management as per proposed algorithmii) Control Arm – Current best practice (based on the individual discretion of the attending surgeon)Primary outcome of interest is percentage of CT scans in each arm.Secondary outcomes include the percentage of missed diagnosis, negative appendectomies, overall length and cost of stay. If the proposed algorithm is validated and found to be of value, it can potentially be implemented nationwide as a standard protocol for the evaluation of suspected appendicitis. This may reduce unwarranted CT scans and health care costs as well as the burden of radiation induced complications in the future.
kw: acute appendicitis, computed tomography, algorithm, alvarado score

title: A study of generic preference-based measures of health-related quality of life in patients with mental illness
abs: There has been a shift in mental health services from an emphasis on treatment focused on reducing symptoms based on a narrow notion of health and disease, to a more holistic approach which takes into consideration both well-being and functioning. With the significant increase in the use of generic preference-based measures in economic evaluation of mental health services, there is growing interest to assess the psychometric properties of these measures in patients with mental illnesses. The current study will compare the psychometric performance of three commonly used generic preference-based measures [EuroQol-5 Dimension (EQ-5D), Short Form Health Survey-6 Dimension (SF-6D) and Health Utilities Index Mark 3 (HUI3)] in patients with depression and schizophrenia spectrum disorders, their performance against disease-specific preference measures, to examine responsiveness over time and health related-quality of life status as well as health utilities of patients with these mental disorders. A cross-sectional study will be conducted among outpatients at the Institute of Mental Health. Data on three generic preference-based measures, disease-specific preference measures, socio-demographic characteristics, clinical history and service utilization will be collected. Findings from this study will provide evidence to clinicians and researchers about the best choice of generic preference-based measures that can be used to assess health-related quality of life of patients with mental illness in an Asian patient population. This measure also will allow comparisons of burden of disease and quality adjusted life years not only across health conditions, but also across treatments and programmes of care in Singapore in future.
kw: Health-related Quality of Life, EQ-5D, HUI3, SF-6D, Depression, Schizophrenia

title: Derivation and Validation of a Predictive Model using Machine Learning for Patients at Risk of Readmission in Singapore
abs: Readmission to hospital soon after discharge is considered a marker of poor quality of medical care. The reasons behind readmission are many and can range from unresolved medical issues, poor transition of care to unanticipated new problems. Patients with frequent admission consume a large amount of resources, and in a healthcare system operating at high occupancy, cause bed shortage. A systemic study of the reasons and risk factors for multiple admissions is essential for us to reduce admission and improve our healthcare system in terms of resource allocation and productivity. A model to predict patients at risk of readmission will help healthcare providers to allocate appropriate resources to improve the health of these patients. Several countries have developed predictive models for readmission, e.g. PARR-30 by the UK National Health System. However these models are not applicable to Singapore due to the differences in healthcare system. Moreover, most prediction models perform poorly (in terms of C-statistics etc). Therefore there is a need to develop an accurate prediction model for the local population. The aim of this study is to develop a predictive model using advanced machine learning techniques for readmission of patients admitted to a tertiary hospital in Singapore. The hypothesis is a model developed based on the variables which can predict patient’s risk of admission, within 30 days after discharge. Having a local model that predicts patients at risk of readmission can better prepare healthcare provider to look into the complex care needs of these patients and prevent their admission. Furthermore, there can be better allocation of resources for the group of patients at high risk of readmission and in the long term keep healthcare cost affordable.
kw: Predictive Model, Readmission, Machine Learning

title: Clinical, mechanical and histological characterization of trabecular meshwork in ocular hypertensive primates - Exploring mechanical strain in glaucoma
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. In Singapore, 3% of the Singaporean population above 40 years is afflicted with the condition. The pathogenesis of glaucoma includes an altered trabecular meshwork (TM) resistance to aqueous outflow and optic nerve damage.We have access to a unique group of naturally occurring ocular hypertensive (OHT) primates in our animal facility. Studying the natural clinical course of these primates in comparison to normal monkeys including intraocular pressure measurement, in-vivo TM imaging, outflow facility measurement and retinal/optic nerve imaging will provide us insights into the pathogenesis of glaucoma in these primates.This project aims to study 1. The natural clinical course of OHT in primates and the changes that occur in TM and optic nerve.2. We also aim to compute TM biomechanics through ex-vivo and in-vivo experiments to provide better understanding of this tissue in glaucoma pathogenesis. 3. Histological assessment of the TM tissue will be performed to correlate with clinical findings.Scleral and optic nerve head biomechanics have been studied previously using experimental and computational tools and were found to be useful in understanding some of the glaucoma related pathogenesis. Similar tools can be used to characterize the biomechanical properties of the TM. Ex-vivo experiments can be performed using human/primate cadaver TM tissue while in-vivo experiments can be performed using high resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT). Clinical characterization of these OHT primates will make it feasible to utilize them in future clinical intervention studies including pharmacological or gene therapy trials. We believe that comprehensive characterization of this primate group is a very valuable and unique resource for improving our understanding of this major blinding disease.
kw: Glaucoma, Trabecular meshwork, Biomechanics, Non-human primates, Anterior segment imaging, Outflow facility

title: Host inflammatory responses driving immunopathology in human central nervous system tuberculosis
abs: Central nervous system tuberculosis (CNS-TB) is the most virulent form of tuberculosis. Brain inflammation and tissue destruction can be very extensive despite a paucity of mycobacteria. However, the mechanism resulting in this immune-mediated pathology is not defined. Matrix metalloproteinase (MMPs) and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have an emerging role in TB immunopathology. Hypothesis: We hypothesise that MMPs and NETs have a key role in CNS-TB pathology and contribute to tissue destruction.The specific aims are:1.Investigate expression of MMPs, and their specific tissue inhibitors TIMPs in patients with CNS-TB2.Determine the diagnostic and prognostic values of MMPs and NETs3.Investigate the role of MMPs and NETs in the host pathology in an animal model of CNS-TBMethodologyPatients with TB, viral and bacterial meningitis and febrile seizures were recruited from Singapore and Malaysia. Clinical data, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and sera will be collected and neuroimaging will be performed. MMPs, TIMPs and cellular adhesion molecules will be analysed by Luminex Array and ELISA. Functional activity of MMPs will be analysed by quantitative fluorescent assay. The concentrations of MMPs, cellular adhesion molecules and NETs in CNS-TB will be compared with other infectious and non-infectious CNS diseases to determine if these host immune markers can aid in the diagnosis and in prognosticating the severity of CNS-TB. NET formation will be investigated using fluorescent assays, confocal microscopy and ELISA. A murine mouse model of CNS-TB would be used to investigate the mechanism of tissue destruction caused by MMPs and NETs. This study is crucial in identifying key human host factors driving immunopathology in CNS-TB. Determining the role of MMPs and NETs would aid in the identification of potential adjunctive therapeutic agents in the treatment of CNS-TB.
kw: Tuberculosis, immunopathology, blood-brain barrier, central nervous system

title: Musculoskeletal Bio-Imaging Comprehensive Program [A Themed Approach] – Developing a Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Program as an Intervention to improve Disease Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs Adherence in rheumatoid arthritis: A randomized controlled trial.
abs: BackgroundMedication non-adherence is a widespread issue in RA (adherence rate frequently reported to be <70%) which needs to be urgently addressed as it can lead to suboptimal therapy with poor disease outcomes. The subsequent need for more aggressive therapy and treatment of disease related complications can translate into increased healthcare utilization and costs. To improve medication adherence, we propose a Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Program (MUSP) intervention to improve disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) adherence. The MUSP synergises (1) the patients’ direct visualization of their joint inflammation and erosions real-time and (2) a Rheumatologist’s simultaneous reinforcement of the need for medication adherence. By doing so, we hope to improve patient’s understanding of their joint disease and motivate them to adhere to their medications. MethodologyWe propose to conduct a 6 month randomized trial at SGH rheumatology unit. RA subjects on DMARDs with a low adherence score (<6) on the locally validated 8-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8) will be randomized (1:1 ratio) to receive either (a) the MUSP intervention or (b) no MUSP (controls) while on follow-up with their attending Rheumatologist.Aim(s)To determine if MUSP is effective in changing medication-taking behavior so as to improve DMARD adherence in RA patients. Medication-taking behavior measures such as (1) the MMAS-8 and (2) proportion of days covered (PDC) using pharmacy dispense records will be utilized at specified time-intervals. We hypothesize that the proportion of patients with a low MMAS-8 score at 1 month will be significantly smaller in the MUSP group when compared to the non-MUSP group.SignificanceImproving treatment adherence is critical as it can improve treatment outcomes in RA. This research addresses an area of unmet clinical need, specifically, non-adherence to RA drug treatment. It is a part of a Comprehensive Program utilizing musculoskeletal bio-imaging to improve RA patient care
kw: ultrasound, adherence , rheumatoid arthritis

title: The role of monocytes in the pathogenesis of Parkinson’s disease
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) gene is the most important cause of familial and sporadic Parkinson’s disease (PD), a common neurological disorder. Genomewide association studies have found an association between LRRK2 and Crohn's disease, an autoimmune disease, as well as with PD, suggesting that these two diseases share common pathways. Our unpublished data indicate that LRRK2 is most abundantly expressed in human monocytes, followed by B cells while expression in T cells is low. Phenotypic study on Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) show that monocyte population doubled in PD patients than healthy control with an increase in a subset of dendritic cells that express CD1c in PD patients, which potentially play an important role in T cell polarization.Hypothesis: We hypothesize that; 1. Monocytes play an important role in the pathogenesis of PD, 2. The PD LRRK2 risk variants modulate monocytes activity and could in turn influence the polarization of T cells, 3. Lrrk2 modulate Wnt signaling pathway in monocytes.Objectives: Utilizing a case control methodology, we will investigate the role of monocyte function including T cell polarization in the pathogenesis of sporadic and familial PD.Methods: Peripheral blood from PD patients (LRRK2 risk variant carriers and non-carriers) and healthy controls will be collected. A bio-bank with cryopreserved PBMCs and plasma will be created and high throughput screening will be carried out. We will characterize monocytes with flow cytometry and CyTOF and then evaluate the role of LRRK2 variants in monocyte functions and signaling pathways with cell culture, flow cytometry, Luminex, and microarray. The monocyte-T cell interaction will also be investigated with cell culture and flow cytometry.Conclusions: Our study will provide new pathophysiologic clues on the link between monocytes and PD pathogenesis, and these will facilitate novel therapeutic approaches in modulating the immune system in PD.
kw: Parkinson's disease, LRRK2, genetic variants, immunotherapy, immunity

title: Using glycosaminoglycan enriched demineralized bone matrix in regeneration of periodontal tissues
abs: One of the two major causes of tooth loss is periodontal (gum) disease, which is an inflammatory disease causing progressive breakdown of the tissues surrounding teeth. The periodontal defect resulting from the disease leads to further anatomical challenge of maintaining local oral hygiene, thus starting a vicious circle of tissue damage. This disease is highly prevalent, with one out of two adults expected to experience the severe form of periodontal disease, known as periodontitis. Periodontitis may be associated with other chronic diseases, including diabetes and heart disease. Current standard of care focuses on mechanical debridement of the infected tissues to arrest the progression of the tissue destruction. Unfortunately the current techniques do not regenerate the defect and lost tissues. An emerging treatment option involves application of demineralized bone matrix (DBM) that has growth factors and cytokines into the defect area after the debridement procedure. Being a bioactive product, DBM is considered superior in promoting hard tissue restoration. However its efficacy is reliant on the quantity and quality of the growth factors present in the DBM preparation. These important parameters are also dependent on the age and health status of the donors, as well as the method used to prepare and administer the DBM. This proposal seeks to engineer a sugar (glycosaminoglycan) that can augment and sustain the activity of pro-healing growth factors present in DBM with a view to provide dentists with a novel mouldable supplement for the treatment of periodontal damage. This will translate into reduced rate of tooth loss, improve oral function and overall quality of life of patients.
kw: Periodontitis, Heparan sulphate, Regeneration, Glycosaminoglycan, Demineralized bone matrix

title: In vivo efficacy study of ASLAN001 and ASLAN002 in the gastric cancer PDX model: GC22-0808
abs: GC is the fifth most common malignancy worldwide, with an estimated 950,000 new cases in 2012; approximately two thirds of cases occur in men. Mortality statistics are even more striking, with more than 720,000 deaths due to GC estimated to occur each year, making it the third most common cause of cancer-related death. Surgical resection is the first choice of treatment for early-stage GC; however, many cases are locally advanced or metastatic at the time of diagnosis and are thus unresectable. Although a number of cytotoxic agents have been found effective in this indication, treatment options for patients whose diseases progress on chemotherapy are very limited. Several critical molecular signaling pathways such as hepatocyte growth factor receptor (c-met), vascular endothelial growth factor (VFGF)/VEGF receptor, ErbB receptors, Raf/MEK/ERK, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways are aberrant in GC. A considerable crosstalk and redundancy in signaling pathways are also observed in GC. Hence targeting single molecule or signaling pathway may have a limited efficacy. To be effective in GC therapies, new agents and novel therapeutic strategies must target various key signaling pathways. In this proposal we propose to evaluate the efficacy of ASLAN001 (a small molecule pan-HER inhibitor) and ASLAN002 (a small molecule cMET/RON inhibitor) in preclinical models of GC. In addition, combination of ASLAN001 and ASLAN002 and ASLAN001 and ramucirumab are also tested. Understanding the mechanisms of action of these therapeutic agents and methods of combining these drugs may help to increase their efficacy, reduce toxicity, and improve overall survival and quality of life in patients with GC.
kw: gastric cancer, targeted agents, combination studies

title: Analytical validation of ClearCell FX for clinical application in personalized medicine.
abs: In the last 5 years, the concept of capturing circulating tumor cells (CTC) has become a reality. They have been characterized and enumerated by different platforms. We have together with Clearbridge Biomedics initiated the ClearCell FX platform in the CTC CORE at SGH Pathology. In order to achieve full clinical use, several other validation steps are required. The hypothesis is that CTCs isolated using the ClearCell FX platform are as relevant clinically as data derived from repeat tumor biopsies. We thus propose the following collaboration with specific aims:Specific Aim 1: To determine the specificity of the ClearCell FX system to capture CTCs in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), patient subject samples analyzed with the above methods will have their EGFR mutation allele frequencies derived from CTCs compared against paired tumor. This will further consolidate implementation of the ClearCell FX for clinical use.Specific Aim 2: To evaluate the feasibility of performing Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) on the CTCs isolated from the ClearCell FX platform, patient subject samples will be enriched using the CTC ClearCell FX platform, and picked using proprietary technology developed locally. Targeted resequencing for somatic mutations using established local NGS platforms will be performed on paired tumor biopsies and CTC. NGS on the CTCs will help to unravel the heterogenous landscape of CTCs compared to the paired tumor.
kw: Circulating Tumor Cells; Single Cell Sequencing; Analytical Validation

title: A Phase I/II, multicenter, open-label study of EGFRmut-TKI EGF816, administered orally in adult patients with EGFRmut solid malignancies
abs: Despite the progress and efficacy of epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR TKIs), a definitive improvement in overall survival has not been demonstrated and there is still a need for better treatment options for patients with EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Novel third-generation EGFR therapies, which can target not only the primary activating mutations (e.g., L858R and ex19del) but also the acquired/resistant “gatekeeper” T790M mutation –while sparing WT EGFR inhibition and thus avoiding toxicity, are therefore urgently needed.EGF816 is a targeted covalent irreversible EGFR inhibitor that selectively inhibits activating and acquired resistance mutants. Based on preclinical data for EGF816 and the known clinical activity of other third-generation EGFR TKIs, EGF816 is expected to exhibit significant antitumour activity in NSCLC patients harbouring the activating EGFR mutations and/or the T790M mutation; while sparing WT EGFR. This Phase I/II, multi-centre, open-label study aims to examine the effect of single-agent EGF816 in adult patients with locally advanced (stage IIIB) or metastatic (stage IV) NSCLC. The purpose of the Phase I part (dose-escalation) is to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) or recommended phase II dose (RP2D) and to evaluate the preliminary antitumour activity of EGF816 in patients with documented EGFR T790M mutation.Phase II part of this study seeks to evaluate the efficacy and safety of EGF816 in patients whose tumours harbour specific EGFR mutations. It will consist of six parallel groups as defined by the specific EGFR mutations and the number of prior lines of systemic antineoplastic therapies, including prior EGFR TKIs. Oral EGFR816 will be administered once daily on a continuous schedule until patient experiences unacceptable toxicity, progressive disease and/or treatment is discontinued at the discretion of the investigator, withdrawal of consent or due to any other reasons. A treatment cycle is defined as 28 days.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of a novel virus-like particle pandemic influenza A (H1N1) 2009 vaccine
abs: There is an urgent need for new tools in our armamentarium to fight pandemics and seasonal influenza epidemics. Currently available influenza vaccines are egg- or mammalian cell-based, and associated with limited yield, time-consuming production that hinders rapid scale-up, and provides protection only against viruses that are antigenically closely matched to the vaccine strains. Recombinant virus-like particles (VLPs) open up new avenues for the development of influenza vaccines. A consortium of public institutions in Singapore has developed a novel VLP influenza vaccine, gH1-Qbeta based on a platform from Cytos (Schlieren, Switzerland). This is the first VLP influenza vaccine that is produced entirely in bacteria, is highly stable, non-infectious, cannot replicate and easily scalable. Unlike conventional vaccines, it induces a potent T cell response and demonstrates strong cross protection against drifted strains. A Phase 1 human trial conducted in Singapore confirmed good safety and immunogenicity. Conducting an efficacy trial would now be the next step towards bringing this vaccine forward.An increasing number of experts recommend that human challenge studies should be an integral step in the vaccine development pathway. These studies allow efficacy data to be generated quickly and help in identifying relevant immune correlates, thus avoiding unnecessary and costly large-scale trials.The significance of this trial is five-fold: (1) evaluation of efficacy of a locally developed VLP vaccine for the prevention of influenza, (2) evaluation of an array of immunological and gene expression profiles as markers for disease progression in an Asian population, (3) characterization in unparalleled detail of the immune response to influenza infection under controlled conditions, (4) establishment of controlled human infection studies expertise in Singapore for commercialization and (5) formation of an interdisciplinary group of researchers from different institutions in Singapore and overseas for bench- to bedside translational research in vaccinology.

title: Engineering of a Scalable Photonics Platform for Quantum Enabled Technologies
inst: IMRE - Institute of Materials Research and Engineering
abs: Quantum information networks are at the forefront of practical applications of quantum technology. Deployment of these networks allows the scale-up and acceleration of processing along with distribution of quantum information. Quantum networks employ stationary quantum systems as nodes which process and store quantum information. The nodes are interconnected by optical links, which transfer quantum information from one node to another. Two of the biggest challenges for large-scale quantum networks are: (1) Efficient connection between stationary nodes and their optical links and (2) A scalable and fabrication-friendly platform, which accommodates both stationary nodes and their optical links. In this project we will push practical implementation of quantum networks by using integrated photonic technologies. We will encode quantum information in spin states of atomic defects in nano-diamonds and use them as stationary nodes. Nano-diamonds will be interconnected via optical waveguides made of low-loss Silicon Nitride. Optically-resonant nano-structures will enhance the coupling of photons emitted from the nano-diamonds into waveguides. Photons will be sent to different nodes to create quantum entanglement between them. For readout of quantum information we will develop on-chip single photon sensitive photodetectors. This platform will allow execution of quantum networking protocols and quantum logic on-chip. The concepts, developed for quantum information can be applied for applications in magnetometry at room temperature. The interaction of external magnetic fields with spin of atomic defects in nano-diamonds modifies their energy spectrum, and opens an opportunity of using the developed platform for sensing applications. Wave-guiding photonic structures will be used to improve the sensitivity of this technique. The readout of the sensor response will be implemented by scanning energy levels of nano-diamond using a microwave antenna and on-chip photodetectors. The technology will lead to the development of a new family of highly sensitive electro-magnetic field sensors, which are compact and bio-compatible.
kw: Quantum Information;Photonics;Quantum optics;Semiconductor device physics;Diamond;Metrology

title: Development of Solvent Resistant Nanofiltration Membranes for Sustainable Pharmaceutical and Petrochemical Manufacture
abs: Pharmaceutical and petrochemical syntheses are often taken place in organic solvents through multiple steps of reactions. Thus, multi-step separations and purifications must be conducted in order to facilitate the reactions and to concentrate small molecular weight products from these organic solvents. GlaxoSmithKline has estimated that 85% of the total chemicals used in pharmaceutical manufacture consist of solvents, while their recovery rates are typically at only 50–80%.The majority of waste is sent to on-site incineration because of the high energy consumption of conventional methods such as distillation. However, with stricter environmental legislation and increasing prices of organic solvents, solvent recovery is essential and becomes a competitive alternative to incineration. The organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) process that not only recovers and reuses the organic solvents, but also purifies and concentrates the high value pharmaceutical and petrochemical products. Exxon Mobil and W R Grace have employed OSN membranes to dewax motor oil. They reported a 20% reduction in energy consumption when comparing with traditional separation methods. Therefore, this project aims to develop novel solvent resistant nanofiltration hollow fiber membranes possessing (1) high stability in organic solvents used in pharmaceutical and petrochemical processes; (2) nano-scale pores with size in the range of 0.5-2 nm and a molecular weight cut-off ranging from 300 to 1000 Da to separate high value added products from organic solvents; (3) environmental benign membrane fabrication process by replacing conventional toxic solvents with ionic liquids. A comprehensive program integrating fundamental materials science, molecular modeling and membrane technologies has been proposed and a multidisciplinary team has been assembled in order to develop various innovative purification, separation, and process technologies. We plan to commercialize these advanced technologies in Singapore. It is envisioned that the results of this program will place Singapore to be the global hub for sustainable pharmaceutical and petrochemical manufacture.
kw: Organic solvent recovery;Membrane technologies;Hollow fibers;Purification and separation;Solvent reuse;Liquid separation

title: “QSYNC”: Theory and Experiments of Quantum Synchronisation in Trapped Ions and Nano-mechanical Resonators
abs: Classical non-linear and damped systems can converge to constant steady states, they can be chaotic, or they can asymptotically approach self-sustained oscillations. Typical examples of these limit-cycles are e.g. the cardiac rhythm, the motion of the engine of a car, the swing of a driven pendulum (as in a mechanical clock). In all cases the steady state is periodic and one can associate to it a frequency and a phase. If we have two independent systems with slightly different frequencies they will oscillate autonomously without any correlations between the two. However, even very weak coupling between the two systems can force the oscillations to happen with the same frequency and a constant phase difference. For quantum systems, however, the same approach cannot be straightforwardly extended. Quantum states are defined by wave functions (or density operators) and their time evolution cannot be described with classical phase space trajectories. Even though the first steps towards a theory of quantum synchronization have been taken, there is still a lot to do. It seems likely that quantum correlations play an important role in the ability of coupled quantum systems to lock their dynamics. Understanding this connection will be at the core of this project, nicknamed 'QSync'. The first task of QSync will be to develop a rigorous and quantitative definition of synchronization for quantum systems. This will run in parallel with the fabrication of experimental devices such as coupled ion traps and nano-mechanical resonators (e.g. nanoscale cantilevers) that will test and inform the theory. A highly novel ultrahigh precision molecular acoustic sensor, or Single-Molecule Phonon Sensor (SMPS), will be developed as part of this work with a view to patenting. The device designs will be optimised with the help of numerical modelling.
kw: trapped ions;nano-mechanical resonators;quantum correlations;open quantum systems;quantum optics;optical microcavities

title: Novel and Automated Detection of Primary Angle-Closure Mechanism using Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography
abs: Primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) is a major cause of blindness inthe world. We have previously identified 4 distinct mechanisms of angleclosure which can be effectively treated by different modalities such aslaser peripheral iridotomy (LPI) and iridoplasty. The key toindividualization of therapy is accurate identification of specific angleclosure mechanism which can be challenging. There is also lack of dataon the prevalence of different angle closure mechanisms and theprogression of angle closure over time after successful primary lasertreatment.Our primary objective is to develop a novel fully-automated approach toidentify angle closure mechanisms based on response to laser treatment.We hypothesize that pre- and post-laser anterior segment parametersmeasured quantitatively from anterior segment optical coherencetomography (AS-OCT) can accurately determine the mechanism(s) inangle closure eyes. We aim to conduct an observational pre- andpost-treatment prospective study which includes 584 eyes with primaryangle closure suspect (PACS). Eyes with good response to LPI areassumed to have pupil block, eyes which responded to LPI and laseriridoplasty are assumed to have plateau iris or thick peripheral iris rolland eyes with poor response to both lasers are attributed to increasedlens vault. We have previously shown that morphological AC parameterscan be extracted from AS-OCT images using WND-CHARM algorithmfollowed by feature selection algorithm and machine learning classifiers.Our retrospective pilot study of 74 PACS eyes using the prototypesoftware showed sensitivity and specificity of 90.2% and 89.2%respectively in identifying the correct mechanism but a prospective studywith a larger sample size is required to validate this software.Our study addresses a major unmet need of PACG and is an importantstep towards more effective individualized therapy. It provides insightsinto the mechanisms of angle closure and the long-term response tolaser treatment.
kw: Primary angle closure, Anterior segment optical coherence tomography, glaucoma, pupil block, laser peripheral iridotomy, laser iridoplasty

title: Detection of occult paroxysmal atrial fibrillation following ischemic stroke in a multi-ethnic Asian population and elucidating their significance in relation to recurrent stroke outcomes
abs: Detecting paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) in patients with ischemic strokes presenting in sinus rhythm is challenging because these PAF episodes are often short, occur randomly, and are frequently asymptomatic. Limited data are available on the incidence of undiagnosed PAF among Asian stroke patients. Our preliminary data reveal a high incidence of undiagnosed occult PAF (16%) among stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients in Singapore. These patients were older and have higher levels of pro-brain natriuretic peptide, high-sensitivity troponin T and platelet aggregation defect in the cyclooxygenase-1 pathway. The significance of brief bursts of PAF in relation to recurrent stroke risk is not known. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the incidence of occult PAF and their relationship with recurrent stroke outcomes in a multiethnic Asian cohort of patients with ischemic stroke and TIA. Our secondary objectives are to investigate biomarker and echocardiographic predictors to improve the detection of AF in stroke/TIA patients. We hypothesize that occult PAF is under-diagnosed in Asian stroke/TIA patients and that the risk of recurrent stroke is higher in patients with a greater burden of AF especially when PAF are detected closer to stroke onset. Our secondary hypothesis is that neuroimaging patterns, vascular biomarkers and echocardiogram features can predict AF detection and stroke recurrence.This study, which transects across several multidisciplinary platforms in stroke neurology, digital health and translational medicine, aims to deliver key data on the burden of undiagnosed PAF and unlock the causes of stroke among Asians. Data derived from this study will provide critical insights on the biology of AF and stroke, and guide targeted screening of high-risk stroke patients for undiagnosed PAF.
kw: stroke, atrial fibrillation, remote monitoring, biomarkers, device, detection

title: Arousal Detection and Training for Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD)
abs: Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD) is the third most common mental health disorder, and has the highest lifetime prevalence rate (12.1%) among anxiety disorders. With one of the earliest ages of onset among psychological disorders, SAD leads to hefty direct healthcare costs and underestimated indirect costs on occupational productivity. Yet it remains severely undertreated, as socially anxious individuals may avoid seeking help due to fear of social interactions. Hence, empirically-validated interventions to improve the treatment rates and outcomes of SAD are urgently required. In 2010, our team developed a novel EEG-based Brain Computer Interface system that has shown success in training attention in ADHD children and global cognitive functioning in elderly. We now aim to develop a novel intervention for SAD that integrates psychoeducation, virtual reality exposure therapy and biofeedback, using EEG and pulse rate. This integration makes our system the first of its kind. During training, participants will learn to regulate their arousal while delivering speeches to virtual audiences. Training is personalized, graduated and automated, as the intensity level of exposure (determined by factors such as audience size and facial expressions) will be controlled by participants’ arousal. By training socially anxious individuals to reduce their arousal in contextually relevant settings using objective, real-time biofeedback, we believe that they can gain greater confidence and mastery over their arousal in anxiety-inducing real-life situations. If shown to be effective, our “personalized medicine” device can be used in the safety of one’s home to reach out to more SAD sufferers and motivate them to seek further treatment. It can also be used by therapists as a cost-effective complement to psychotherapy in the treatment of patients. We believe that this biofeedback-based system has great potential to be patented as a new made-in-Singapore intellectual property and be marketed globally.
kw: social anxiety, biofeedback, virtual reality exposure therapy, arousal control, EEG, non-invasive

title: Combination Antibiotic Therapy for Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Infection (CAMERA2)
abs: Introduction/Clinical SignificanceMethicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is the most prevalent antibiotic resistant human pathogen. MRSA bacteraemia has a mortality of 20-30%, exceeding that of methicillin sensitive S. aureus (MSSA) primarily due to the shortcomings of vancomycin, the standard therapy for MRSA bacteraemia. Although MRSA is by definition resistant to beta-lactam (?-lactam) antibiotics, recent in-vitro and animal studies, and preliminary clinical data, all suggest an unexpected but consistent benefit of combination therapy with vancomycin and a ‘anti-staphylococcal’ ß-lactam antibiotic.Specific AimsWe aim to determine whether combination antibiotic treatment (standard therapy plus 7 days of an intravenous (IV) anti-staphylococcal ß-lactam antibiotic) leads to a superior complication-free survival 90 days after randomisation compared with standard therapy (vancomycin or daptomycin) and if results for in vitro synergy testing correlate with clinical outcomes in adults patients with MRSA bacteraemia.HypothesisThe primary hypothesis is addition of ?-lactam to standard therapy will lead to synergistic bacterial killing and hence faster clearance of bacteria from the blood stream and other infected foci, and thereby reduce the risk of disseminated infection and death. We also hypothesise that there is correlation between in-vitro synergy and clinical effectiveness of antibiotic combinations.MethodologyThe trial will be conducted as a multicentre, assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial. There will be 220 patients per arm, with subjects on the intervention arm receiving either vancomycin or daptomycin and an extra standard-dose of ?-lactam antibiotic while patients on the standard therapy arm receiving either vancomycin or daptomycin.ImportanceMRSA bacteraemia is associated with high mortality, especially in resource-limited settings and where infection control practices are suboptimal. Since anti-staphylococcal ?-lactam antibiotics are already widely used, safe and cheap, if combination therapy is found to be superior, clinical practice locally and globally may change.
kw: combination, antibiotic, methicillin, resistant, MRSA

title: The Asia Primary Tube versus Trab (TVT) Study
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Raised intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main risk factor for development of glaucoma and progression of disease.The glaucoma disease burden is more pronounced in Asia, where almost two-thirds of the world’s population lives. For glaucoma sufferers in Asia, logistic and economic factors often result in late presentation with advanced disease. Many will not be able to comply with a regime of protracted medications. Therefore definitive treatment such as glaucoma surgery is often performed as surgery produces greater IOP reductions compared with lasers/medications. However sub-optimal IOP reduction occurs in the long term as a consequence of scarring. Due to ethnic differences, scarring after glaucoma surgery is known to be more aggressive in Asians.Trabeculectomy augmented with mitomycin-C (MMC) is the current standard for glaucoma surgery. However as this surgery carries a risk of significant complications, there is need to consider alternative surgical approaches. Glaucoma drainage implants have shown success in controlling IOP in eyes with secondary glaucoma and previously failed trabeculectomy. In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, we intend to study which surgical approach is most effective and safe for glaucoma patients in Asia. Using a standardized protocol as was used in the US Tube versus Trab study, this trial will compare the efficacy and safety of Ahmed Glaucoma Implants (AGI) against trabeculectomy/MMC over 5 years in 300 patients with uncontrolled glaucoma who have not had previous glaucoma surgery. This study will elucidate the most appropriate surgery for management of glaucoma in Asians and provide valuable data on glaucoma in Asia.SERI will be the coordinating centre for the trial with SCRI the trial the data management/analysis site. This CTG application is for funding for 60 patients in Singapore who will be recruited from SNEC/NUH/ TTSH, as well as SCRI costs.
kw: Glaucoma, Surgery, Ahmed Tube Implant, Trabeculectomy

title: Taking PI3K Inhibition to the Clinic in Haematological Malignancies: Rational Combinations and Patient Selection
abs: Research Project Title: Taking PI3K inhibition to the clinic in haematological malignancies : Rational combinations and patient selectionThe Phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway regulating cell survival and proliferation is a prime therapeutic target in haematological malignancies, but optimal deployment of therapies targeting this pathway requires an understanding of disease heterogeneity and of synergy with other anti-cancer agents. The overall objective of this proposal is to translate the preclinical observations from the UCL laboratory on multiple myeloma (MM) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) into clinical trials.Specific Aims : 1. To develop and validate biomarkers in a phase 1 study of PIK3 blockade with proteasome inhibition in MM2. To design a phase 1 study of Akt inhibition in combination with a PIM kinase inhibitor in AML, including the design of biomarker studies3. To work with pharma partners to secure compounds and funding for the AML study, undertake protocol development including statistical powering, and regulatory submissions.The MM study protocol is finalized and funding secured. Ethical approval will be obtained and study recruitment will commence in Q2 2015. Work on this project will involve carrying out the biomarker assays on tumour cells (genetic sub-type, pathway activation and pharmacodynamic proof of mechanism), and data analysis. For AML (Aims 2, 3), the work will involve engaging with pharma partners to identify suitable compounds (Akt and PIM inhibitors), further laboratory work to confirm their activity, and designing a phase 1 study to test the combination in the clinic. Laboratory work will be carried out in the Cancer Institute, while Clinical trial work will be conducted in UCLH NIHR/Wellcome Clinical Research Facility (CRF), which is equipped with state of art facilities for early phase clinical trials.
kw: Early Phase Clinical Trial

title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Colchicine for Symptom and Inflammation Modification in Knee Osteoarthritis
abs: Despite the high prevalence and global impact of knee osteoarthritis (KOA), current treatments are limited to analgesic and when it fails, surgical knee replacement We recently demonstrated significant involvement of uric acid and activation of the innate immune response in OA pathology and progression. The involvement of uric acid suggests that traditional gout therapy may be beneficial for OA. Our goal therefore is to assess colchicine, an existing commercially available agent for gout, for a new therapeutic indication–OA. We propose a randomized clinical trial (RCT) of 16 weeks’ therapy with standard daily dose oral colchicine or placebo for KOA. We hypothesize that colchicine will block inflammasome mediated inflammation, thereby improve the signs and symptoms of KOA, and reduce synovial fluid, serum and urine inflammatory and biochemical joint degradation biomarkers. If successful this study could contribute significantly to improvements in quality of life for the approximately 75.8 million of the world's population with KOA.The RCT with a target sample size of 120 subjects is funded by the Duke/Duke-NUS collaborative grant and currently in recruitment phase. Up to October 2014, 70 subjects were recruited and 50 subjects have completed protocol.This research fellowship training application will support a two-month research visit of the applicant (Dr. Leung) to Duke University, Durham, USA for training in biomarker analyses. Dr Leung will analyze samples generated from the RCT, which is an essential and integral part of this research to elucidate the mechanism of action of colchicine in KOA. The applicant is expected to learn what is necessary to conduct basic biomarkers measurement and to be able set up a small laboratory back in her home institute. It will establish cutting edge clinical research procedures for arthritis studies in Singapore that will open the door to future research and economic opportunities.

title: Perovskite Optoelectronics: Multidimensional Perovskites for High Performance Solution-Processed Light-Emitting Devices
abs: Solution-processed technologies promise possibilities of light-emitting devices comprising ultrathin flexible LED sources on paper and plastic enabled by large-area manufacturing techniques that make lighting, displays and optical diagnostics ultra-cost-effective. However, the formation of high quality electronic materials at low temperatures is a challenge due to defects associated with the deposition processes as well as structural disorder associated with the low temperatures (eg. organics, colloidal quantum dots). Charge transport in these materials is fundamentally limited since electrons have to hop between molecules/quantum dots. The conventional assumption that high quality crystalline materials cannot be formed at low temperatures seems to be disrupted by the rise of organic-inorganic halide perovskites. In photovoltaics, these materials have already achieved performance comparable to high temperature processed Si by forming crystalline defect free films at benign temperatures. This project aims to develop high performance light emission and lasing devices based on custom-designed multidimensional perovskites and optimal interfaces to ensure high quantum yield, brightness, stability and color quality. In contrast to the currently explored CH3NH3PbX3 halides, the project will focus on designing and synthesizing 2D, mixed perovskites with cations that allow for tunable exciton binding energy, improved charge transport through hydrogen/covalent bonding, better electronic overlap, fluorophore incorporation and improved stability through strategies such as topochemical polymerization. By employing thin films and nanostructured perovskites, light emitting diodes and light emitting transistors with performance exceeding state-of-the-art will be pursued by tackling the challenges of high balanced electrical injection, light extraction and ionic transport. Optically and electrically driven lasing will be pursued through polariton-based emission from 2D perovskites and free-carrier driven emission from nanostructured perovskites with the gate electric field induced high carrier concentrations required for electrical lasing. The project also aims to bridge the lab to fab transition through selected demonstrators- large area lighting, pixel arrays, electrically controllable lasing.

title: The cost-effectiveness study of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis patient in Singapore
abs: Aortic stenosis is one of the most common valvular heart diseases affecting elderly. While the standard treatment for severe aortic stenosis is surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) one third of patients are not suitable candidates for surgery. Patients who do not undertake surgery will be at high risk for mortality and need multiple hospital admission for symptomatic heart failure. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) presents a new alternative which has proven to be effective in reducing hospitalization rates and mortality. In Europe and North America, this approach has been accepted as alternative to the standard surgical treatment. However due to its high treatment cost only few patients have received this treatment locally. We will conduct the cost effectiveness study of this new treatment approach in the local settings. We hypothesize that TAVI is a cost effective treatment for patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Effectiveness will be assessed in terms of quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) combining both survival and quality of life. A two-phase economic model will be used to assess the cost-effectiveness of four treatment options: TF (transfemoral)-TAVI vs. MM (medical management) for inoperable patients, and TF or TA (transapical)-TAVI vs. SAVR for high risk operable patients. The model is composed of two correlated parts: a decision tree for the short-term phase (i.e. the 1st to the 30th day following the treatment), and a Markov model for the long-term phase (i.e. the 31st day to death). Model parameters will be estimated using clinical effectiveness from two randomized controlled trials and local quality of life and costs data. The impact of uncertainty around the model’s parameters on the cost-effectiveness results will be assessed using scenario and sensitivity analyses. This study has the potential of changing the local health policy and decision making in clinical practice for severe aortic stenosis treatment.
kw: severe aortic stenosis trancatheter cost effectiveness

title: Mapping and unravelling the peritoneal fluid lipid landscape in infertile women with endometriosis
abs: Infertility is a hallmark of endometriosis, and also one important tell-tale sign of endometriosis. Endometriosis, characterized by ectopic endometrial implants commonly in the peritoneum, affects up to 10% of women of reproductive age, with half of infertile women being afflicted. Poor ovarian quality in endometriotic women is associated with the chronic exposure to a toxic peritoneal microenvironment. However, prediction of developmentally incompetent oocytes in a toxic environment is challenging given a lack of non-invasive biomarkers and inadequate understanding of the pathophysiology. Hence, there is an urgent need to develop biomarkers predictive of the dysfunctional peritoneal environment found in endometriosis-associated infertility (EAI), and also to study the underlying pathobiology. Here, we aim to (I.a.) map peritoneal sphingolipids and oxylipins in women with severe endometriosis and infertility. Peritoneal fluid (PF) is directly in contact with endometriotic lesions where most lesions reside and also surrounds the ovaries, making this biofluid highly reflective of the pathological state of the ovarian microenvironment. Preliminary studies using high-throughput quantitative mass spectrometry revealed an altered sphingolipidome and eicosanoidome, of which four PF sphingolipids with significantly high odds ratio were found in infertile women with severe endometriosis after accounting for other infertility diagnoses. We plan to test these putative biomarkers in a prospective validation cohort of cases versus controls, and (I.b.) correlate the sphingolipids and oxylipins in the sera of the same patients in a paired analysis format with the objective of developing non-invasive biomarkers of assessing a defective peritoneal microenvironment. Lastly, (II) in an exploratory aim, to gain mechanistic understanding, we will functionally test the role of specific sphingolipids and/or oxylipins in obtunding oocyte development and fertilisation potential.This proposal, if successful, will allow the development of rationally-designed biomarkers that predicts a toxic peritoneal environment for identifying EAI non-invasively, allowing appropriate prognostication and/or developing strategies to address EAI.

title: Multimorbidity in primary care and its association with Depression, Anxiety and Quality of Life (MDAQ)
abs: This paper aims to observe the routine doctor-patient consultation process for a follow-up visit of chronic diseases. It serves as a direct observation and interpretive analysis of the two-way dyadic communication that transpires in a typical chronic care consultation. This will involve an ethnographic description of the consultation process to capture what elements of the patient-centred care using the patient-centred care measurement instruments.5 The study also aims to depict a patient’s full journey from preparation at their homes to see a doctor to leaving the polyclinic after meeting the doctor. This will give a good description of the enabling and hindering factors that affect the coping strategy of a person who suffers from multimorbidity in the perspective of the patient’s personal and social context.
kw: Multimorbidity, Depression, Anxiety, Quality of Life

title: Development of a new generation of bionic neural interface using in vivo modulation of axonal growth for voluntary control of an electromechanical prosthesis
abs: Seamless integration of mechatronic prostheses to the human nervous system is the final goal for all prosthetic research. The key hurdle lies in the development of a stable, long lasting interface between the human nerve and a synthetic electrode.The current state of the art designs of such electrodes result only in short term functionality due to the biological and mechanical incompatibility between the electrode material and the nerve. Extra-neural electrodes have limited signal selectivity with loss of contact and tendency for displacement due to peripheral nerve movement, whereas intra-neural electrodes may cause direct nerve trauma and fibrosis over time.In our recent experiments, we have developed a novel interface and successfully demonstrated the feasibility in the rodent model. The interface is based on the stimulation of fibroblastic proliferation concomitant with axonal growth, resulting in mechanically stable and an electrophysiologically active interface.In this proposal, we aim to demonstrate the feasibility of this interface in the non-human primate model as the penultimate step to human translation. Non-human primates are used in this proposal, as they also capable of dexterous movements with their hands. We will use the data from the non-human primate experiments to obtain regulatory approval for human translation.
kw: nerve, interface, prosthesis, bionic, paralysis,biocompatible

title: Nano-magnetized Three-dimensional Bioprinting Strategies to generate Saliva-secreting Epithelial Tissue Transplants from Human Embryonic Stem Cells to restore Salivary Gland Function after Radiation Therapy in Head and Neck Cancers
abs: Head and neck cancers (HNC) are on the top 10 most prevalent cancers in Singapore. Radiotherapy is the standard treatment; nevertheless it causes irreversible salivary gland (SG) hypofunction in more than 60% of patients. Irreversible radiation damage preferentially occurs in SG secretory epithelial cells, resulting in a near-complete loss of saliva, rampant caries, mucosal infections and difficulty swallowing; which greatly impair patients’ oral-systemic health. Current prevention and treatment approaches (e.g. gland-sparing intensity-modulated radiation therapy, saliva stimulatory agonists) are largely ineffective. Tissue engineering approaches offer a potentially safe clinical solution for the regeneration of SG tissue and recovery of function. Recent approaches used adult stem/progenitor cells, which are unreliable heterogeneous populations with lack of cell scalability, thus providing limited functional outcomes (e.g. restricted saliva flow). High numbers of stem cells with a reliable potential for differentiation like human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) are therefore needed for clinical applications to generate epithelial progenitors and create bio-functional saliva-secreting epithelia.Under an autologous paradigm, patients’ hESCs can be expanded, differentiated and assembled into de novo three-dimensional (3D) saliva-secreting epithelial-like tissue (SET) transplants mimicking native cellular environments; furthermore, these 3D structures may be promptly assembled by nano-magnetic and bioprinting techniques, which can generate bio-functional high-cell content SET for the site of radiation damage.Herein, I propose the development of hESC differentiation strategies using 3D magnetic bioprinting techniques to create SET transplants for in vivo restoration of SG function. The central hypothesis is that magnetized bioprinted 3D saliva-secreting epithelial-like tissue (SET) transplants derived from hESC can restore in vivo SG function after radiation damage. To test this hypothesis, I propose two Specific Aims:1. Develop an in vitro, human-derived, bio-functional, magnetized, bio-printed 3D SET from epithelial-like differentiated hESC cultures. 2. Evaluate the biocompatibility and salivary function of irradiated mouse SGs after in vivo transplantation of SET.
kw: Salivary gland regeneration, saliva-secreting acinar epithelial cells, human embryonic stem cell, radiotherapy-induced xerostomia, head and neck cancers
