title: Treatment to Reduce Vascular Calcification in Hemodialysis Patients using Vitamin K (TReVasC-HDK)
abs: Specific AimsTo evaluate the prevalence and progression of vascular calcification in a cohort of maintenance hemodialysis patients. It also aim to evaluate the efficacy of vitamin K 2 supplementation in reducing the progression of vascular calcification. Hypotheses1. Significant vascular calcification in hemodialysis population may be related to sub-clinical vitamin K deficiency, which is prevalent in hemodialysis patients because of the typical dietary restriction. 2. Vitamin K deficiency will result in the failure of the matrix GLA protein (MGP) to undergo carboxylation. MGP is a natural local inhibitor of vascular calcification and the lack of functional (carboxylated) MGP may contribute to increase vascular calcification.3. Vitamin K supplement should therefore correct this anomaly and decrease the rate of vascular calcification in this population of patients on long-term maintenance hemodialysis.Methodology and ApproachThis will be a single-center randomized, prospective and open-label interventional clinical trial of end stage renal failure patients on hemodialysis. All suitable patients who have consented will undergo a first (baseline) MSCT. Patients with a minimum score of 30 will be eligible for randomization to either the control arm (standard care) and active treatment arm (standard care plus vitamin K2 supplementation). Biomarker for vitamin K deficiency; dp-uc MGP will be drawn at baseline. At the end of the 18 months, the patients will undergo a second MSCT for CAC score. The absolute difference in CAC score at 18-month between control and intervention arms will be compared. Clinical SignificanceThis study will allow us to test the efficacy of using oral vitamin K supplementation to reduce vascular calcification. Successful retardation of CAC (and/or aortic valve calcification) will be a huge step forward in supporting a larger and longer-term trial aim at reducing death and CV endpoints in this high-risk population using a relatively cheap and safe vitamin supplementation strategy.
kw: Vascular calcification; Vitamin K; dephosphorylated- undercarboxylated MGP; Menaquinone-7; Hemodialysis

title: Evaluation of flow dynamics in diabetic retinopathy mouse model using fluorescein labelled leukocytes and ICG-loaded erythrocyte ghost cells.
abs: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is an important microvascular complication of diabetes which can potentially lead to blindness in the working age population. Alterations in the blood flow can lead to visual loss in patients with DR, however, the specific mechanism is still unclear with contradictory reports of decreased or increased blood flow. Currently, it is uncertain if early visual deficits in diabetic retinopathy are caused by vascular compromise or other non-vascular factors. Using computer based retinal vascular image analysis, retinal vascular calibers has been objectively and reliably quantified. Variations in retinal vascular caliber are associated with DR. Along with retinal vascular caliber changes, blood components such as leukocytes, erythrocytes and platelets are thought to be involved in the control of circulatory processes by numerous mechanisms. Qualitative and quantitative assessment of the leukocytes and erythrocytes dynamics in the retinal and choroidal circulation can provide us additional insight into the disease mechanism in DR. Using the Ins2Akita (Akita) mouse, a well established genetic model of DR, we will evaluate the flow dynamics of labelled cells, in both the retinal and choroidal circulation and correlate it with visual function using electroretinogram and imaging tools like retinal vascular geometric markers and retinal flowmeter to establish a composite model affecting the microcirculation in DR. The proposed study will investigate the changes in retinal and choroidal blood flow after onset of hyperglycemia using a DR mouse model and ascertain if this alteration in blood flow are associated with visual field deficits and retinal vascular caliber changes.The immediate significance of this mechanistic study is the development of a microvascular model for DR and identifying new insights into disease pathogenesis. The wider long-term significance is the potential to predict disease progression and developing a model to study treatment response to new therapeutic agents for vasoproliferative disorders including DR.
kw: Erythrostasis, leukostasis, diabetic retinopathy, flow dynamics, retinal and choroidal circulation, fluorescein labelled red blood cells

title: Characterization of Candidate Genes Associated with Unexplained Developmental Delay or Regression
abs: Developmental delay (DD) is an abnormality of cognition, learning and adaptive behaviour and is one of the most common human disease (3% of any population). It is recognized to be one of the most common reasons for referral in paediatric clinical practice. Despite this, the ability to reach an underlying etiological diagnosis is difficult as the causes of DD are myriad. This is a significant problem as many patients undergo extensive and sometimes repetitive investigations that drain healthcare and financial resources rapidly. The evaluation of DD can be complex and onerous. Clinically, distinctions are made between syndromic and non-syndromic DD, which imply that syndromic DD is due to chromosomal anomalies and non-syndromic DD is due to single gene abnormalities. In reality, single gene abnormalities may cause dysmorphism and occasionally, chromosomal rearrangement problems may not. Therefore the evaluation of such patients requires stepwise evaluation for both the chromosomal rearrangements and single gene abnormalities. Whole exome sequencing is a powerful new technology that selectively focuses on protein-coding regions of the genome, retrieving information of over 21,000 protein-coding genes, sequencing a very small fraction of the whole genome (~1%). With this, there is an increased achievement of genetic diagnoses from only 5 – 15% to about 50% of cases. We plan to harness both chromosomal microarray analysis and whole exome sequencing (next generation sequencing) technology:1. To identify novel candidate genes associated with DD or regression in 25 families with phenotypically distinct features?2. To correlate the identified mutations in genes with varying clinical phenotypes, including severity onset and other systemic involvement. This would contribute towards new understanding of the molecular pathogenesis, genetic heterogeneity of DD or regression. We would also explore the change of parental quality of life and psychosocial impact, both before and after the diagnosis has been determined.
kw: developmental delay, developmental regression, whole exome sequencing, chromosome microarray analysis, intellectual disability

title: Defining T lymphocyte signatures associated with protection from severe Dengue virus infection
abs: Dengue is the most significant mosquito-borne viral disease afflicting human populations and causes a spectrum of clinical symptoms that include fever, muscle and joint pain, maculopapular skin rash and hemorrhagic manifestations. Dengue virus (DENV) is estimated to cause up to 390 million infections per year, of which 100 million cases are symptomatic. There is currently no specific therapy or vaccine available for DENV. Dengue infection elicits a broad antigen-specific T lymphocyte response that has been implicated in protection from severe disease, but the precise role of these cells is still poorly understood. In particular, the association of certain HLA class I molecules with decreased susceptibility to severe dengue disease provides further evidence that the CD8+T cell component of the immune response may play a key role in the outcome of dengue infection. The aim of this study is to identify the phenotypic and functional signatures of human dengue-specific CD8+T cells restricted in “protective” versus “non-protective” HLA alleles by using Cytometry time of flight (CyTOF), a novel technology that combines mass spectrometry with flow cytometry. CyTOF allows to investigate many more parameters than previously possible to give a deep assessment of the cellular diversity of virus-specific CD8+T cells. We hypothesize that dengue-specific CD8+T cells restricted to protective versus non-protective HLA types will differ profoundly in terms of their magnitude, differentiation status, capability to proliferate, produce anti-viral effector cytokines and home to distinct anatomical sites. In addition, we aim to compare T cell immunity elicited in patients during natural dengue infection with that of individuals receiving a recombinant, live, attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccine. We hypothesize that the partial protective efficacy of the most advanced phase 2b clinical trial vaccine may be in part explained by its inability to elicit an adequate virus-specific T lymphocyte response.
kw: Infectious disease, Immune response, dengue virus, vaccine, T lymphocytes

title: Role of TP53 mutations in epigenetic aberrations of cell proliferation gene regulatory elements
abs: Somatic mutations in the TP53 gene are the most common genetic aberrations found in human cancers. Most of these mutations affect the DNA binding domain and lead to the production of an altered protein that cannot bind effectively to DNA. In our collaborator’s previous studies, TP53 was identified as a partner of the methyltransferase DNMT1. However, the epigenetics consequences led by TP53 mutations and the direct effects on gene regulation are still unclear. Our preliminary meta-analysis of published genomic and epigenetic sequencing datasets derived from gastric cancer patients suggests an interesting association between TP53 somatic mutations and hypomethylation of 7,000 CpG sites located predominantly in the vicinity of AP1 binding sites. Gene based studies have shown on one hand, the association between TP53 expression and promoter methylation of genes like survivin, and on the other hand, the association between TP53 expression and AP1 binding loss such as within the TFF2 promoter. Based on these observations, we hypothesise that TP53 silences numerous genes by recruiting DNMT1 and causing methylation of gene regulatory elements, predominantly at AP1 binding sites. TP53 mutations may consequently abolish this recruitment. In this proposal, we aim to elucidate a novel aspect of the TP53 pathway and characterise genes silenced by the TP53-DNMT1 complex in various tissue types using published sequencing datasets comprised of 3000 patients among 12 cancers. Functional validations will be made on TP53 KO/KIN cell lines. With a team which combines multidisciplinary expertises such as statistics, bioinformatics, genomics, molecular biology and drug treatment, we believe our study will yield important new understanding concerning functions of TP53, particularly in the orchestration of silencing genes critical to tumorigenesis and cancer cell proliferation via epigenetic events. These discoveries will identify previously uncharacterized consequences of TP53 alterations observed in cancers and potentially highlight novel therapeutic strategies.
kw: TP53 pathway, Transcription factors, Cancer epigenetic, Cell proliferation, Genes regulation, DNA methylation

title: Development of an effective xeno-free and chemically defined culture system to expand keratinocytes for therapeutic use in burns and chronic wounds
abs: The current treatment of severe burns involves the use of split-thickness skin autografts for wound closure. However, such indication remains a challenge where there are insufficient donor sites. Cultured epithelial autograft (CEA) is one technology developed to address this problem. CEA culture involves the isolation and expansion of skin keratinocytes (SKs) in the presence of murine feeder cells and bovine serum for optimal growth while maintaining stem cell population. Although no adverse events have been reported in clinical practice for more than 30 years, this procedure is restricted to major burns and large wounds in critically-ill patients primarily due to the use of such animal products. It is now technically possible to culture cells, such as human pluripotent stem cells in chemically defined and xeno-free environments on specific biologically relevant matrix molecules. This was achieved by using isoforms of basement membrane laminins that are present in stem cell niches in-vivo. In the body, there are at least 16 different laminin isoforms that are important for cell adhesion, differentiation and phenotype stability. In the proposed study, we will explore the potential to develop a protocol for culturing of human SKs on SK-specific laminins in a defined and xeno-free environment. The SKs will be evaluated in terms of long-term growth, clonal expansion, colony-forming efficiency, cell migration, stem cell phenotype and genetic stability. If the procedure yields high quality SKs, the cells can be cultured under GMP conditions and tested for efficacy on patients.The development of an effective and safe culture system for skin epithelial cells under animal-free and defined conditions can not only address the stringent regulatory requirements for therapeutic use, but will open avenues in the advanced wound care market, estimated at US $5 billion. This would include the management of chronic diabetic wounds, seen rising in developed countries.
kw: Skin keratinocyte culture; Basement membrane; Laminin; Xeno-free; Chemically defined; Burns and chronic wounds

title: Investigation of the role of the cellular ATPase ABCE1 in paramyxovirus replication and identification of small molecule drugs that interfere with ABCE1-paramyxovirus interactions.
abs: Paramyxoviruses are a family of non-segmented, single-stranded RNA viruses that includes major human pathogens such as measles virus (MeV), mumps virus (MuV) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). While some of the most successful vaccines have been developed against paramyxoviruses, such as the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine, which confers life-long protection, no antiviral drugs are currently available. Effective therapeutic options are required for the treatment of infection with well-known paramyxoviruses, as well as for preparedness for outbreaks of newly emerging viruses from this rapidly expanding family. As intracellular parasites, viruses rely on host-cell functions for most aspects of their replication cycle. To uncover common cellular host factors essential for the paramyxovirus life cycle, genome-scale RNA interference (RNAi) screens were performed on MeV, MuV and RSV, identifying 32 candidate host factor genes common to all three viruses. The ATPase ATP-binding cassette protein E1 (ABCE1), a known inhibitor of the classical RNase L antiviral pathway, was identified as a cellular factor. We hypothesize that ABCE1 is crucial for paramyxovirus replication, and acts in an RNase L-dependent mechanism. To identify candidate drugs with broad anti-paramyxovirus activity, we will take advantage of an autophagy-based high throughput drug screening assay, as activation of RNase L is a known autophagy inducer. We expect that this study will provide insights into the role of ABCE1 in the paramyxovirus life cycle, and yield starting points for the development of novel antiviral or immune response-enhancing therapeutic strategies.
kw: paramyxovirus, siRNA screen, ABCE1, infectious disease, virus/host interaction

title: Deciphering the Function and Regulation of miR-574-5p in APP-mediated Adult Neurogenesis
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disease seen at the National Neuroscience Institute (NNI), Singapore. Amyloid precursor protein (APP) is a key molecule involved in the pathogenesis of AD. Although this protein is expressed throughout the developing and adult brain, the roles of APP in neural stem cell function are not well established. We recently demonstrated that ablation of APP enhances the neurogenesis in the developing cerebral cortex by targeting miR-574-5p-Sox12 complex. However, little is known about the effect of miR-574-5p contributes to APP-mediated neurogenesis in the adult mice. Our preliminary in situ hybridization (ISH) result showed the localization of miR-574-5p in the dentate gyrus (DG) of adult mouse hippocampus. Furthermore, we detected a higher intensity of miR-574-5p signal in APP KO brains compared with WT brain, which further indicates the APP represses the miR-574-5p level in the adult mouse.Hypothesis: We hypothesize that miR-574-5p is an important down-stream effector of APP that regulates multiple phases of adult neurogenesis, and detailed analysis of miR-574-5p regulatory pathway will identify novel mechanisms that underlying APP-mediated adult neurogenesis. Aims: We will dissect the function and regulation by which miR-574-5p and Sox12 affect adult neurogenesis, and elucidate miR-574-5p-Sox12 whose modulation would rescue phenotype defect of APP.Methodology: Using gain-and loss-of-function in adult neural stem cells in vitro and retroviral delivery in the adult mouse hippocampal via stereotaxic surgery in vivo, we will determine miR-574-5p-mediated neural proliferation and differentiation. Subsequently, the rescue experiment will define the miR-574-5p and Sox12 contribute to APP-mediated neural stem cell fate in vivo.Clinical significance: We believe that our findings will identify a novel function of miR-574-5p as a key regulator in adult neurogenesis. It provides the mechanism by which APP regulates the neurogenesis through miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional regulation, thus links abnormal neurogenesis with the pathogenesis of AD.
kw: APP, microRNA, Neurogenesis, Neural stem cells, Neural proliferation, Neural differentiation

title: The impact of sequence evolution in the dengue non-coding RNA on mosquito transmission
abs: Dengue is a debilitating and sometimes fatal illness endemic to Singapore and the rest of Southeast Asia that is vectored by Aedes mosquitoes. Epidemic potential of dengue viruses is partly determined by transmission efficiency, which results from the interaction between vector and virus genetics. Working with clinical virus isolates characterized as endemic and epidemic dominant foreign lineages, we previously determined that sequence variation in the non-coding subgenomic flaviviral RNA (sfRNA) is specific for each lineage and that the dominant lineage sfRNA inhibits the interferon innate immune response in human cells, thus affecting the production of infectious particles and underlying the epidemic potential. To bridge the knowledge gap in the dengue virus lifecycle, this proposal aims to characterize the impact of sfRNA on transmission efficiency in the main dengue vector. First, we will determine infectivity in whole mosquitoes for the endemic and dominant foreign isolates by implementing oral blood meal infection and quantifying infectivity in terms of virus genome (gRNA), infectious particles and ratio of sfRNA/gRNA. Further experiments will determine the incubation period between infectious blood meal and presence of dengue virus in midguts and salivary glands. Second, we will functionally characterize the impact of sfRNA on virus production using RNA-affinity chromatography coupled with quantitative mass spectrometry to identify proteins bound to sfRNA from endemic and dominant foreign viruses and an RNAi-based cell assay with reporter-replicon possessing different sfRNA sequences to determine the function of the sfRNA-bound proteins and immune genes. Targets of interest will be validated in whole mosquitoes using RNAi and blood meal infection. By transferring the cutting-edge tools to mosquito biology study, this transdisciplinary proposal will improve our understanding of the impact of sfRNA on transmission and identify new targets to design alternative control strategies aiming at blocking mosquito transmission of dengue virus.
kw: dengue; mosquito; vector competence; non-coding RNA; innate immunity

title: Elucidating the molecular mechanism of NCAPG in contributing to early recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the sixth most common cancer and the second leading cause of cancer related deaths worldwide. Surgical resection is the only curative treatment modality which consistently offers survival advantage to HCC patients. Unfortunately, recurrence occurs in more than two-thirds of these patients despite initial curative intent and converts the situation to a dismal prognosis. The variations in prognosis following surgery differ substantially and such large variation is mostly unexplained. Various surrogate clinicopathologic features such as lymphovascular invasion, capsular invasion, satellite lesions, and tumour foci are often used but give varying degree of reliability. To understand the molecular mechanisms leading to early HCC recurrence, we performed whole genome expression microarrays to profile transcriptome changes between matched normal non-tumors, early recurrent HCC tumors (?2 years) and non-recurrent HCC tumors (>2 years). We identified Non-SMC Condensin I Complex subunit G (NCAPG) to be significantly over-expressed in early recurrent HCC tumors (FC>4, FDR<0.05). NCAPG is a subunit of the condensin complex which is responsible for the condensation and stabilization of chromosomes during mitosis and meiosis. High NCAPG levels is significantly associated with poorer recurrence-free survival in HCC patients (p<0.001). Moreover, NCAPG as a single predictor can identify early recurrent HCC at >70% accuracy. In this proposed study, we aim to elucidate the NACPG-linked molecular mechanism in contributing to the early recurrence of HCC. Additionally, potential novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers associated with the NCAPG-mediated gene networks will be identified and characterized. The ability to stratify HCC patients who may at high risk of developing early recurrent disease with clearly defined molecular and cellular network to enable targeted therapeutic strategies is currently an unmet clinical need for HCC. The understanding of NCAPG mediated HCC early recurrence and its biomarker potential would be extremely useful for the clinical management of HCC patients.
kw: Hepatocellular carcinoma, early recurrence, predictive marker, NCAPG

title: Reactivating NK cells in treating refractory head and neck cancer
abs: Immune escape of cancer cells is increasingly recognized in patients with solid tumors and lymphomas, worsening the risk of relapse. Natural killer (NK) cells are cytotoxic cells of our innate immunity that are critical in controlling intracellular viral infections and cancer. They have been successfully used to treat hematological cancers with good safety profiles.Nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) is ideal for cancer immunotherapy as it expresses Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) antigens and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Although NPC is chemo- and radio-sensitive, survivors suffer severe life-long morbidities of dry mouth and wooden neck. In addition, 20% of patients with NPC suffer loco-regional or distant relapses and have limited therapeutic options as further radiotherapy causes radionecrosis. We propose a Phase I (n=9) lead in to Phase II study (n=22 patients) based on expanded autologous NK cells using our K562-mb15-41BBL system, with cetuximab, an EGFR-targeting monoclonal antibody. We hypothesize that NK cells expanded using our K562-mb15-41BBL system is highly cytotoxic to NPC cells and that this is enhanced by cetuximab through antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity as supported by our pilot in vitro studies. The aims of this study are two-fold. First, we will determine the feasibility, safety, and effectiveness of expanded autologous NK cell therapy with cetuximab in patients with EGFR-positive refractory NPC in a Phase I /II model. Second, we will characterize the immune changes in paired tumor biopsies before and after treatment. This is a multi-disciplinary collaboration. My mentor, Professor Dario Campana, has developed several protocols using expanded NK cells in leukemia and solid tumors. The strategy of reactivating autologous NK cells to treat virally-associated cancer should open up new avenues for treating other cancer subtypes.
kw: Nasopharyngeal Cancer, Immunotherapy, Natural Killer Cells

title: JAK-STAT Signaling in the Murine Hair Cycle
abs: Mammalian skin is composed of functionally and anatomically distinct compartments such as the hair follicle (HF), sweat glands, and interfollicular epidermis (IFE). Each compartment has been shown to be independently maintained by populations of stem cells, which are able to replenish neighboring compartments during wound healing. AIMS The aims of this project are to understand the responses of stem cells in the IFE and HF during chronic basal cell depletion.HYPOTHESES We hypothesize that there are keratinocyte-specific mechanisms of responding to cell loss, resulting in proliferation of IFE cells, and recruitment of HF stem cells. We postulate that stem cell compartments are maintained by cell-cell interactions, and this is disrupted during cell depletion.METHODOLOGY We have generated a mouse model of basal cell depletion using inducible diphtheria toxin in the basal epidermis. Our preliminary data suggests that unlike previous models that perturb epidermal homeostasis, our model has a minimal inflammatory component. This allows us to isolate and study the keratinocyte-specific responses to chronic cell loss. The skin of experimental mice exhibits hyperproliferation and stem cell exhaustion of the IFE and HFs over time, suggesting that it recapitulates some aspects of a chronic wound, without the inflammation.APPROACH In order to examine the IFE hyperproliferative response, we will examine the role of Wnt signaling in the maintenance of basal stem cells of the IFE. To study the response of the HF bulge stem cells, we will perform lineage tracing and gene expression profiling of bulge stem cells. Using a multi-color Confetti reporter, we will attempt to delineate the compartment boundaries within the hairy skin of mice, and observe their responses to basal cell ablation. Understanding these aspects of stem cell biology will inform us on novel and specific therapies for regenerative medicine, in particular wound healing and the construction of bio-engineered skin constructs.
kw: Epidermis, Stem Cells, Niche, Regenerative Medicine, Wound Healing

title: Biological Subtypes of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abs: Cancer-initiating cells (CICs) are a subpopulation of tumor cells that have increased ability for tumor formation in vivo. They have a unique ability to self-renew, as well as differentiate into phenotypically diverse (non-CIC) cancer cells. In head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), CD44 has been the best characterized marker. However, CD44+ cells are still very heterogenous, with CICs accounting for a minor fraction of the CD44+ population. CD271, a neurotrophin receptor of the tumor necrosis receptor superfamily, has recently been identified to be a novel marker of CICs in HNSCC. Studies at the Stanford University School of Medicine demonstrated that the CD44+CD271+ subpopulation had the greatest tumor-initiating capacity. Incubation with recombinant NGF resulted in enhanced Erk phosphorylation, providing evidence for CD271 functional activity (privileged, unpublished data).The aim of the research project is to evaluate the potential of CD271 as a therapeutic target in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.Hypotheses:1.CD271+CD44+ cells will have lower reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels compared to CD271-CD44+ cells in HNSCC.2.Inhibition of CD271 will be associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and will sensitize the cells to cisplatin and radiation therapy.3.The systemic inhibition of CD271 will result in significant tumor reduction in mice.Methodology:1.Primary human HNSCC cells will be sorted by FACS into CD271+CD44+ and CD271-CD44+ cells, oxidative stress assay performed, and intracellular ROS levels determined.2.Human HNSCC xenograft tumors will be transduced with lentiviral constructs expressing either CD271 shRNA or a scrambled control. The transduced cells will be injected into Rag2-/- gamma-c-/- immunodeficient mice, and subsequent oxidative stress assays performed. Colonogenic assays will be performed on human HNSCC cell lines and xenografts treated with cisplatin/radiation and anti-CD271 (blocking) antibody.3.HNSCC xenograft tumors will be expanded in Rag2-/- gamma-c-/- mice. Cohorts of mice will be treated with intraperitoneal injections of a monoclonal blocking antibody against CD271. In an ongoing collaboration between Dr. Sunwoo and Dr. Irving Weissman*, a novel high-affinity CD271 small molecule antagonist will also be developed and similarly investigated.*Irving Weissman. title: Cardiovascular structure and function in mildly overweight Asian Subjects of Mixed ethnicity following Early versus delayed lifeStyle intervention – a randomized controlled study (CASMES)
abs: Studies demonstrated that cardiovascular structure and function change in the morbid obese. Such changes could also be present in mildly overweight Asian subjects, whose body mass index (BMI) is 23-27.5 kg/m2. However, the changes may be subtle to be identified using conventional techniques. To detect and measure these, we now have newer, more sensitive echocardiographic techniques and blood assays. Our main purpose is to assess the effects of 6-months of lifestyle intervention (LSI) consisting of diet and exercise encouragement program. Specifically, we aim to:i) compare the effects pre- and post-LSI;ii) compare effects of immediate LSI with a delayed weight lost group;iii) determine sustainability of the cardiovascular improvement post-LSI;ii) correlate novel cardiac and circulating cellular parameters at baseline and post-weight loss.We hypothesize that the LSI will result in improvement in circulating endothelial progenitor cellular markers and subclinical cardiac dysfunction associated with fat loss.We will randomize 100 mildly overweight subjects. Group A will go through LSI immediately whilst Group B at 24 weeks from randomization. Using echocardiography and new parameters that can detect subclinical dysfunction, we will assess the heart. Furthermore, we will perform assays on circulating vascular progenitor cells (EPC) and microparticles as surrogates for vascular health. Investigations will be performed at 0, 24 and 48 weeks.This study allows a more complete understanding on how subclinical cardiac dysfunction and circulating cellular derangements in the mild overweight may be affected by weight loss. This may be used to develop novel markers in predicting cardiac prognosis and new therapeutics, which is lacking for obesity-related cardiomyopathy.By demonstrating that simple lifestyle changes may improve cardiovascular function, we aim for overweight reduction. Reducing obesity, which has reached global epidemic proportions and is associated with many comorbidities, will result in healthcare improvement in the population.

title: A Phase Ib/IIa single-centre, double blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, parallel-group dose ranging trial in adult participants with uncomplicated dengue fever in Singapore
abs: Dengue infection results in nearly 500,000 patient hospitalizations and approximately 100 million symptomatic human infections annually; in Singapore, over 22,000 cases were reported in 2013. As there is no medication approved for treatment of the dengue virus, there is an unmet medical need necessitating development of new treatments. There is early stage scientific evidence to suggest that celgosivir and modipafant may be of clinical benefit to dengue fever patients. Celgosivir is an antiviral that works by inhibiting enzymes that are essential for replication and spread of the virus throughout the body. Modipafant is intended to reduce the likelihood of severe dengue fever symptoms such as haemorrhagic shock. The aims of the study are to evaluate the efficacy and safety of celgosivir and modipafant, and to assess the amount and metabolism of each drug in the blood after patients have been dosed. We propose to conduct a two part clinical study in dengue patients; Part 1 will evaluate the effect of celgosivir and modipafant treatments in dengue patients when administered separately, versus a placebo. Part 1 is designed to give an early indication of whether the two drugs at the dose strength and frequency used are safe and effective. Patients will be randomly assigned to one of 4 treatment groups and remain in the investigational medicine unit for 5 days to be treated. Data from Part 1 will be evaluated and used to guide the number of patients and treatment to use in Part 2. In Part 2, the best treatment from Part 1 will be selected, and the efficacy and safety in patients with dengue fever versus placebo will be confirmed.

title: Evaluation of susceptibility-enhanced contrast-optimized (SECO) T1-weighted images with Bowsher-prior for Quantitative PET Brain Imaging
abs: The aim of this proposal is to evaluate the use of susceptibility-enhanced contrast-optimized (SECO) T1-weighted images as the brain anatomical images in Quantitative PET Brain Imaging. The hypotheses is segmentation of small structures in SECO T1WI images will be superior to 3D T1WI images, thus with that, the quantification of PET isotope tracer registered in SECO T1WI image will be better defined.Methodology: The study subject must have both PET and MRI Brain within a short period. The ideal situation is the data collected from MRI-PET scanner, which the registration errors are negligible.A special set 3D volumetric gradient T1WI image is collected. Both real and imaginary components of the 3D gradient data will be captured at the time of scanning. SECO T1WI images will be produced by using SWI post-processing in Matlab. And 3D T1WI images are the magnitude images of the same data set. Auto segmentation of the brain region for both images will done using FSL. The resulted images are registered with PET images in Bowsher-prior. The signal of PET for each component of the brain is quantified in both SECO T1WI images and 3D T1WI images. The statistical p value will be calculated to see whether the result in SECO T1WI images is significant different to that in 3D T1WI images.Approach of this research: The interest to quantify PET radiotracer uptake is the differentiation of small or narrow tissues. In routine practice, which is using 3D T1-weighted images, abnormal brain tissue tend to have more susceptibility contrast than the normal tissue due to the small calcification, tissue necrosis and minor hemorrhage. As SECO T1WI images can produce both T1-weighted and susceptibility-enhanced image contrast in the same data, thus the segmentation of small structures in SECO T1WI images will be superior to 3D T1WI images.
kw: DKU Medical Physics program

title: The Role of Hope and Emotion Regulation on Daily Stress and Well-Being
abs: Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often require long-term care and management of co-morbid issues, such as regulating repetitive behaviors, self-injury or aggression. Caregivers of individuals with ASD face significant stress and negative outcomes such as lower life satisfaction, and physical and mental health compared to caregivers of typically-developing (TD) individuals. Nevertheless, caregivers of individuals with ASD have also been found to exhibit resilience which is defined as adaptive coping with positive outcomes despite adversity. Resilience is shown when traits within the individual influence the perception of chronic stress, resulting in positive outcomes. Studies have identified hope and self-efficacy as traits that may influence parents’ perception of chronic stress and in turn affect their life satisfaction. The study aims to understand the effects of hope, self-efficacy, chronic stress on levels of life satisfaction in Singapore caregivers with ASD children compared to caregivers of TD individuals. It is hypothesized that:1.Caregivers of ASD individuals are more vulnerable compared to caregivers of TD individuals and they experienced greater levels of chronic stress and lower life satisfaction. 2.Resilience traits such as Trait hope and self-efficacy are protective factors against chronic stress. It is expected that caregivers of individuals with ASD with higher levels of trait hope and self-efficacy will report lower levels of chronic stress and in turn, higher life satisfaction, indicating resilience despite chronic stress experience. Caregivers of ASD and TD individuals complete questionnaires measuring their trait hope, self-efficacy, chronic stress levels and life satisfaction. Within-group analysis is performed using correlation and regression analyses. Between-group comparisons are performed using independent samples t-test.
kw: resilience, chronic stress, life satisfaction, caregivers, autism spectrum disorders

title: Cell Based Therapies in Lung Cancer
abs: Lung cancer is common and lethal, locally and globally. Clinical outcome is typically dismal and new therapies are urgently needed. Immunotherapy is an emerging therapeutic strategy in oncology but has not been explored thoroughly in lung cancer. Natural killer (NK) cells can distinguish neoplastic and normal cells; they can exert direct cytotoxicity against different tumor types and their anti-cancer potential is being tested in clinical trials. The laboratory of Prof. D. Campana at the National University of Singapore has developed unique methods to activate, expand and modify NK cells to increase their anti-tumor capacity. These technologies have been adapted to large-scale conditions that currently support ongoing early phase clinical trials. Our overall objective is to develop novel NK cell based immunotherapies for the most common subtype of lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) by pursuing the following specific aims:1)To test the cytotoxicity of activated, expanded NK cells against NSCLC cell lines in vitro 2)To test the cytotoxicity of activated, expanded NK cells against NSCLC cell lines in murine models3)To determine whether NK cell cytotoxicity can be enhanced by small molecules, chemotherapy, and monoclonal antibodiesThe proposed bench work will be done under the direct supervision and mentorship of Prof. D. Campana and in collaboration with investigators in NCCS and in A*STAR. Promising combinations will be developed further in the setting of Phase I clinical trials in patients with advanced cancer.

title: Fiber Medical Devices for Diagnosis of Coronary Artery Disease
abs: Coronary artery disease (CAD), and its clinical manifestation, acute myocardial infarction (AMI), is the leading cause of death in Singapore and worldwide. Although current imaging technologies have greatly improved the diagnostic accuracy and patient care, our ability to understand, diagnose, and management of CAD has been hindered by lack of an imaging tool to obtain microscopic pathological information in vivo. The objectives of the entire programme include: 1) development clinically viable, next generation, fiber-optic imaging technologies capable of obtain subcellular resolution images of coronary arteries; 2) development a dual-functional intracoronary fiber-catheter combining the next generation fiber-optic imaging probe and a fiber pressure sensor; and 3) validate the feasibility and safety of the proposed fiber medical devices for diagnosis of coronary artery diseases in animal models. Specifically, we will design, develop, and validate two completely novel optical imaging technologies, we term nanometer resolution optical coherence tomography (nano-OCT) and intravascular multiphoton endomicroscopy (MPE) respectively, and a multifunctional intracoronary catheter which enables simultaneous intracoronary imaging and Fractional Flow Reserve (FFR) measurement. Combining nano-OCT and MPE enables simultaneous morphological and molecular contrast imaging. Both imaging technologies will achieve a spatial resolution of 200-1000 nm, which is more than two order of magnitude higher than the highest resolution intracoronary imaging modality (Intracoronary OCT). With the unprecedented resolution, cardiologists will be able to visualize, for the first time, sub-micron details of coronary atherosclerosis in vivo which was only available with histology of autopsy tissue. Ability of combining intracoronary imaging and FFR will provide cardiologists with both structural and functional pathological information of the disease. The development of the next generation optical diagnostic technologies may dramatically change the clinical practice and improve patient care. It will be the first time that the high-resolution histological information is acquired from human subjects, which will help to increase the diagnostic accuracy, reduce the burden of patients and the load of clinicians. The results of this programme will be a platform to develop imaging technologies for cancer detection, and biomedical applications, such as pulmonary airway diseases, eye diseases and skin diseases, where visualization of sub-cellular morphology in vivo is critical.

title: Cyber-Security and Network Resilience in Complex Networks
abs: Complex engineered networks are ubiquitous – Online social networks enabled by mobile computing, smart grids, heterogeneous wireless networks and others. The network entities can communicate, and information data are collected and processed collaboratively over networks. Thus, the complex network is a network of networks with many unique characteristics that requires fundamental understanding of the interactions and inter-dependencies. The interconnection complexities and the system dynamics rapidly outstrip our ability to unravel them. These networks could mash together introducing or accelerating black swan events: catastrophic cascading failures due to cybersecurity attacks and malicious information spreading. Cybersecurity provides a compelling context in which network resilience can be quantitatively studied. An action triggered by one complex network entity, e.g., failure due to attack, could lead to a cascade of other state changes and widespread messages being exchanged over the network. Understanding this embedded interaction and cascading effect is important to guarantee security, reliability and network resilience in a network. Detection and identification of such cascading sources in the complex networks allows timely quarantine of the security breach. For example, law enforcement agencies can identify computer hackers who use malicious code to cause widespread power blackout or identify online malicious rumor sources. The broad objective of this project is to create mathematical theories, algorithms and network cybersecurity protocols to speedily uncover the origins of cascading sources. The novelty in our research is to utilize novel links between statistical inference, probability theory and graph convexity to design optimal detection and to analyze the tradeoff between reliability, security and speed of detection. Cybersecurity protocols will be developed to both improve the diagnosability of complex networks when attackers strike as well as to enhance network resilience of complex networks by identifying risks before attackers do. This has long-term impacts that are aligned to the national interests of Singapore.
kw: Cybersecurity;Big Data Analytics;Complex Networks;Network Resilience;Graph Algorithms;Statistical Inference

title: Phase III Multi-Centre Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial of Selective Internal Radiation Therapy versus Sorafenib in Locally Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abs: BackgroundApproximately 25% of HCC may benefit from potentially curative ablative therapies such as surgical resection or radio-frequency ablation. For the rest, options are limited and the prognosis is poor. Sorafenib, a systemic therapy confers improvement in survival that is important for patients with extra-hepatic (metastatic) HCC because there is no other proven efficacious therapy. In the group of patients with locally advanced HCC however, the benefits of sorafenib over efficacious loco-regional ablative therapy Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (SIRT) is unclear.HypothesisSelective-internal radiation therapy (SIRT) confers better overall survival compared to sorafenib therapy in the treatment of locally advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma.AimsTo conduct a phase III multi-center open-label randomized controlled trial that compares the efficacy of SIRT versus sorafenib in the management of locally advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.MethodologyThis investigator-initiated multi-centre study will enroll 360 patients in a phase III trial under the auspices of the Asia-Pacific Hepatocellular Carcinoma Trials Group. Patients with locallyadvanced HCC who satisfy the study eligibility criteria, will be randomized to receive either:• A single administration of SIRT (SIR-Spheres®) targeted at HCC in the liver by the transarterial route.• Oral Sorafenib therapy at a dose of 400 mg b.i.d until disease progression, no further response, complete regression or unacceptable toxicity.Exclusion criteria include previous systemic therapy or trans-arterial delivered therapy, metastatic disease or complete occlusion of the main portal vein.Overall Survival (OS) is the primary endpoint and will be assessed according to intention-to-treat. Secondary endpoints are tumour response rate, time to tumour progression, progressionfree survival, Qol and down-staging to receive potentially curative therapy.Clinical SignificanceDefinitive data comparing these 2 therapies will determine clinical practice in the large group of patients with locally advanced HCC and improve outcomes for such patients.
kw: hepatocellular carcinoma, Yttrium-90, SIR-Spheres, Selective Internal Radiation Therapy, phase III, Sorafenib

title: Influence of severity of myopic maculopathy on efficacy of aflibercept treatment in eyes with choroidal neovascularization (mCNV) secondary to pathologic myopia
abs: An important complication of pathologic myopia is choroidal neovascularization (CNV). In particular, myopic CNV is a frequent cause of vision impairment in patients aged less than 50 years. The efficacy of intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy, intravitreal aflibercept, provided sustained and improvements in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over the entire observation period of 48 weeks. The mean number of injections received was 2.9 up to week 24, and a further mean 1.3 from week 24 to week 48. The response of aflibercept treatment in eyes with different levels of severity of myopic maculopathy is not known.Our hypothesis is that eyes with more severe baseline myopic maculopathy have more refractory CNV, have poorer response, will require more treatment episodes and will have more recurrence episodes. Our primary aim is to study the influence of myopic maculopathy grade as a prognostic factor for outcome of mCNV treated with Aflibercept. We will utilize the colour fundus photos of randomized eyes in the MYRROR study to grade the baseline severity of myopic maculopathy according to a classification system that reflects the severity of the disease.Our analysis will study the association between myopic maculopathy grading and visual outcome, cumulative injection number, and recurrence episodes. Our statistical analysis will take into account other known risk factors. In addition, we will also grade the myopic maculopathy severity at week 48 and by comparing to baseline grading, determine progression rate of myopic maculopathy and risk factors for progression in treated/untreated eyes. Progression of myopic maculopathy may be an independent risk factor for late visual loss, independent of mCNV.This will be the first study to study the utility of this new classification system in a clinical trial. We anticipate many other future studies in myopia will adopt this classification system and comparisons will be made with the current study

title: KIDs-In View (Keeping Infectious Diseases In View): A sentinel surveillance system for respiratory infections in Singapore childcare centres
abs: Respiratory infections are a major cause of disease burden worldwide. Young children are a particularly vulnerable group: studies in high-income countries indicate that children aged <5 years experienced approximately 1 episode of influenza-like illness (ILI) per year; 10%-20% of these are caused by influenza virus. Household transmission studies have shown that secondary attack rates are considerably higher in children compared with adults, while serological evidence points to a substantial under-ascertainment of influenza infections in children; approximately 10 times more infections due to pandemic H1N1 occurred in the UK in children <3 years old than were apparent through clinical surveillance. Current ILI surveillance systems in Singapore are based primarily on hospitalisations and polyclinic visits, but cannot monitor transmission in the wider community and are not specific to young children. Childcare centres provide a unique opportunity to do this and Singapore, with its extensive network of childcare centres, provides an ideal opportunit to establish a novel sentinel surveillance network for early childhood infections. This study aims to improve understanding of the burden and epidemiology or respiratory infections in young children, through a sentinel surveillance network in child care centres. Through this sentinel network, we will quantify the incidence and aetiology of acute paediatric respiratory illnesses in a community setting. The study will provide timely, highly-detailed information on the epidemiology and microbiology of respiratory illnesses circulating in children in the community in Singapore, by combining routine respiratory syndromic surveillance in childcare centres, parent-led active reporting of children’s respiratory symptoms, state-of-the-art molecular diagnostics, and social media data streams. Data from the network will be extensively validated against external data sources, including paediatric hospital admissions, polyclinic visits and data from social media data streams relating to respiratory illnesses.

title: The Role of Risk Factors in Influencing Inpatient Utilization and Costs: Evidence from linked Singapore Chinese Cohort Data
abs: Background: To accommodate its aging population, Singapore is expanding health insurance coverage while trying to keep health care costs under control. This proposed research aims to inform these policy efforts through investigating elderly’s inpatient costs in their aging years and at the end-of-life, and evaluating effects of cost-controlling features of the MediShield program. Specifically, we propose: Aim 1: To characterize hospital admission frequency and its associated costs among older adults (age 65 and above) with select risk factors (smoking, drinking, excess weight) and chronic conditions (e.g. diabetes). We hypothesize that admission frequency and inpatient costs are greater for those with risk factors and/or chronic conditions. Aim 2: To characterize inpatient costs, admission frequency, and length of stay in the final 12-18 months before death as a function of risk factors and/or chronic conditions. We hypothesize that people with risk factors and/or chronic conditions have higher end-of-life costs. Aim 3: To study the association between Medishield’s age cut-off and deductibles and inpatient care utilization. We hypothesize that older adults will have greater inpatient utilization when they have exceeded (or nearly attained) their deductible or are near age cut-off. Methods: Data from the Singapore Chinese Cohort Study merged with billing data from the Singapore General Hospital. Outcomes of interest are number of hospital admissions, length of stay, and total inpatient costs. Regression models will be fitted to examine the relationship between risk factors and inpatient costs and to examine the association between MediShield age cut-off and deductible and inpatient care utilization. Significance: The proposed study informs current government efforts to revamp the MediShield program and is useful for forecasting expected inpatient expenditures in the future at the per capita and aggregate levels.

title: Evaluation of Treatment Strategies in Prevention of Stroke and Coronary Heart Disease among Type 2 Diabetic Patients using Markov Decision Process
abs: ContextDiabetes is one of most common chronic diseases in many countries including Singapore. Without good management of blood pressure and cholesterol level for diabetic patients, the risk of developing stroke and coronary heart disease (CHD) could be very high. This could substantially contribute to high mortality and morbidity in a population. Aims1.To determine the optimal decisions on medication initiation timing and sequence for managing blood pressure and cholesterol in prevention of stroke and CHD events among type 2 diabetic patients over the course of their lifetime;2.To evaluate the cost and effectiveness of current protocol for controlling blood pressure and cholesterol in Singapore as compared with the no control baseline. MethodologyWe will develop a Markov decision process model to determine the optimal decisions on medication initiation timing and sequence. The objective is to maximise total expected quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) and minimise cost of treatment and medication. Major risk factors, blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol, will be addressed using HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein factors in the model. Singapore Coronary Risk Score and the United Kingdom Prospective Diabetic Study risk model, which will be calibrated to local diabetic population, will be applied to predict the risks of events. Sensitivity analysis will be used for addressing the variance in decision. Alignment analysis will be applied for model validation. The cost and effectiveness of current protocol for controlling blood pressure and cholesterol in Singapore will be compared with the no control baseline. Effectiveness will be measured by QALYs and cost will include direct and indirect cost from both patient and societal perspectives. Importance to Science or MedicineThe proposed model will facilitate evidence-based clinical decision making process, and help clinicians to make better and comprehensive treatment decisions for type 2 diabetic patients in terms of cost and QALYs.
kw: Type 2 Diabetes, Stroke, Coronary Heart Disease, Prevention, Markov Decision Process

title: Development of a self management E Health tool for atrial fibrillation through a user-centred approach.
abs: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a growing disease burden on Singapore due to its aging population. Integrated care clinics have been demonstrated in such patients to reduce morbidity and mortality. However, the benefits of patient self management and empowerment have not been utilized in these programmes because the E-health tools for this are not available. We hypothesis that we can improve upon the integrated care clinic model for AF patients by empowering and educating patients through self management and education E health tools. Our aim in this study is to develop an innovative patient self management and education E-health tool and to demonstrate its efficacy and safety in Singaporean patients. In Phase 1, in collaboration with international expert centres, a mixed methods approach of semi-structured interviews and focus groups of patients and healthcare providers in Singapore will define the structure and content of the patient education and self management programme. This will help us to develop and refine the design of a Self management and Education Tool for AF patients (SETAF) which will used by ambulatory patients in their home setting to facilitate self care. This E-health tool will then be piloted in Phase 2 with 60 AF patients to determine patient acceptance and usability over 4 months and to further refine the SETAF. Patient knowledge of AF will be assessed before and after the 4 month E-health intervention to assess for any improvements in the patient’s understanding and attitudes towards AF. Their usage and acceptance of the SETAF will also be studies using surveys and structured interviews. This study will demonstrate the efficacy and utility of a self management E-health tool in chronic AF patients. Furthermore, it will serve as a model for integrated care services for other chronic medical conditions such as heart failure or diabetes in Singapore.
kw: Atrial fibrillation, Chronic care, E health, self management

title: Using an Incentive Design with Fixed and Dynamic Target Number of Steps for a Family-based Walking Program
abs: Childhood obesity is one of the major challenges in developed countries, including Singapore. One of the main reasons behind growing childhood obesity is low levels of physical activity, and children may be patterning their levels of inactivity after their parents. Physical activity interventions that target children and parents could have a significant public health impact. Incentives for meeting activity goals can be effective in promoting sustained levels of physical activity. However, further research is needed to identify optimal incentive strategies. We propose to extend current research by testing two types of incentive strategies for a family-based walking program, where all participating family members need to meet their activity goals in order to receive rewards. Specifically, this study proposes to test the effects of a 6-month family-based walking program where families are randomized into one of two incentive schemes. Study aims and hypotheses are as follows:Aim 1: To test the effects of a scalable family-based incentive program with potential for high reach among Singaporean families. We hypothesize that the average number of steps taken by children will be higher when incentives are offered than when they are not.Aim 2: To compare the effectiveness of two types of incentive strategies (fixed threshold versus a dynamic threshold based on peer effects). We hypothesize that the average number of steps taken by children will be higher when incentives are based on a dynamic threshold than when they are based on a fixed threshold. If found effective at 6 months, the program with the optimal incentive design can be scaled up to test the long-term effectiveness.
kw: Obesity, family health, randomized controlled trial, peer effects, behaviour change, physical activity

title: Sleep Study-Guided Multidisciplinary Therapy for Patients Presenting with Acute Coronary Syndrome
abs: The aim of this randomized, open-label clinical trial is to determine the impact of Sleep Study-Guided Multidisciplinary Therapy (SGMT, i.e. continuous positive airway pressure and behavioral therapy) for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in the sub-acute phase of acute coronary syndrome on cardiovascular outcomes. We hypothesize that SGMT will result in a lower (1) plasma NT-pro BNP level, (2) 10-year risk of cardiovascular mortality based on the European SCORE algorithm, and (3) cardiovascular event rate, when compared with Standard Therapy. OSA is an emerging cardiac risk factor and prognostic marker. We have reported that OSA is a prevalent and independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome. In this clinical trial, a continuation of my research and publication trajectory, 180 patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome will be randomly assigned to SGMT (n=90) or Standard Therapy (n=90) groups. Both groups will receive guideline-mandated treatment for acute coronary syndrome. Those assigned to SGMT will undergo a sleep study. Those found to have OSA will attend the SGMT clinic run by a multidisciplinary team. Advice on continuous positive airway pressure and behavioral therapy (weight loss, exercise, positional therapy, abstinence of alcohol and sleeping pills) will be given. The primary endpoint is plasma NT-pro BNP concentration at 6-month follow-up. The secondary endpoint is 10-year risk of cardiovascular mortality based on the European SCORE algorithm which includes age, sex, smoking status, systolic blood pressure, and serum total cholesterol or total/HDL-cholesterol ratio. Adverse cardiovascular events at 3-year follow-up will be determined. In our aging population with an increasing prevalence of obesity, OSA will potentially become an increasingly important contributor to cardiovascular disease. Leveraging the collective expertise of a team of cardiologists and sleep physicians, our work will benefit society by advancing our understanding of the cardiovascular benefits of screening for and treating OSA.
kw: Acute coronary syndrome; sleep apnea; biomarkers; cardiovascular risk; secondary prevention; treatment

title: The Role of Thyroid Status in Regulating Brown Adipose Tissue Activity, White Adipose Tissue Partitioning and Resting Energy Expenditure (TRIBUTE).
abs: Specific Aims and Hypotheses: A new method to assess brown adipose tissue (BAT) volume and activity will be developed using infrared (IR)-based and MR imaging and validated against 18-FDG-PET. This new imaging method will be utilized in determining the effect of thyroid status on BAT, white adipose tissue partitioning, body composition, insulin resistance and metabolic rate. Finally, the metabolic-related phenotyping will be utilized to validate a new algorithm for titrating anti-thyroid drug therapy in hyperthyroidism patients.Methodology and Approach:We will first recruit euthyroid healthy volunteers (n=30) to develop and validate infrared (IR) and MR imaging for brown adipose tissue (BAT) quantification against the present 18-FDG-PET gold standard. Capsinoids will be used to induce thermogenesis through stimulation of BAT. The optimized protocol of MRI and IR imaging will then be utilized in a randomized, double-blind, fixed sequence clinical study of hyperthyroid patients (n=30) treated with anti-thyroid drugs, and their therapy guided either by standard treatment, or by hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis set-point targeted therapy. Subjects will be evaluated at baseline and re-evaluated at stable biochemical euthyroidism by assessing BAT volume and activation, white adipose tissue (WAT) partitioning, basal metabolic rate and selected biomarkers. Importance to Science or Medicine:This research will offer insights into the nature of BAT functionality and WAT partitioning according to thyroid status and physiologic state. This work will establish IR thermography, MRI and calorimetry for BAT assessment, which will facilitate future metabolic research addressing obesity and diabetes. These studies may lead to a new approach for guiding anti-thyroid therapy in hyperthyroidism.Clinical Significance:Developing a new method for BAT imaging that eliminates ionizing radiation will be an important addition to BAT research. Establishing a precise novel technique of titrating thyroid medication that optimizes BAT, energy metabolism, WAT partitioning, and body weight is an important public health priority.
kw: Brown adipose tissue, White adipose tissue, Infrared thermography, Thyroid hormone, Metabolic rate, Whole body calorimetry

title: Developing Experimental Therapeutics and Understanding Mechanisms of Drug Resistance in Asian Breast Cancers
abs: Systemic treatment remains the cornerstone for breast cancer therapy, but intra-patient tumor heterogeneity and tumor evolution following drug treatment are major challenges to effective therapy. Funded by the NMRC Senior Clinician Scientist Award over the last five years, we have developed an internationally recognized breast cancer program comprising of a clinical trial program to test novel treatment strategies along with a breast tissue biobank and pharmacogenetic DNA bank for discovery of tumor and host predictive biomarkers of treatment response and toxicity. In parallel, we have established a translational laboratory to analyze drug pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects, and a pilot study to enrich circulating tumor cells (CTCs) with culture to increase their detection limit. In the next five years, we will expand the program by: (1) continuing to design and execute clinical trials in the refractory/metastatic, neoadjuvant, or window-of-opportunity settings, focusing on optimizing combination strategies between novel biological agents and the backbone chemotherapy or endocrine therapy of breast cancer. In addition, we will evaluate immunotherapy in breast cancer using a patented technology to expand and activate autologous natural killer cells to enhance antibody-directed cell cytotoxicity mediated by therapeutic monoclonal antibodies such as trastuzumab; (2) expand our collection of resistant tumors post-systemic therapy for deep molecular characterization and to generate patient-derived cell lines for in vitro drug sensitivity studies to understand mechanisms of resistance and uncover potential therapeutic targets to inform the selection of drugs in clinical trials; and (3) develop a reliable liquid biopsy protocol for ex vivo drug sensitivity testing using enriched CTCs and test its utility in guiding therapy and tracking progress in the clinic. This breast cancer experimental therapeutics program will address the challenges of tumor heterogeneity, tumor evolution and drug resistance, with the ultimate goal of applying the findings in routine clinical practice and improving patient outcome.
kw: Breast cancer, Drug resistance, Developmental therapeutics, Circulating tumor cells, Predictive biomarkers, Clinical trials

title: A Study of Cow’s Milk Allergic (CMA) Children Aiming to Identify Mechanisms of Tolerance Induction in Asian Children (CMA Tolerance Cohort)
abs: Cow's milk allergy (CMA) is one of the most common food allergies affecting 0.3 - 3.5% infants and young children. In CMA, immediate type hypersensitivity reactions such as anaphylaxis are IgE mediated whereas the delayed type hypersensitivity reactions are indicative of a T cell response. The development of optimum prevention and treatment strategies involving oral tolerance have been precluded by insufficient knowledge of the T cell responses against the CMA protein. The major objective of this study is to identify peptides from CMA protein that potentiate tolerance induction. 25 infants and children with CMA and 25 age matched healthy controls without CMA will be inducted into this study based on positive/negative Skin Prick test (SPT). T cell epitopes of the CMA protein will be elucidated using overlapping peptides spanning the entire protein. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from CMA subjects and healthy controls will be stimulated with peptides characterised as T cell epitopes. This is to identify those peptides that favour tolerance induction presumably in healthy controls or inflammation in CMA subjects. PBMC from CMA subjects and healthy controls will then be stimulated with the identified peptide(s) for 5 days. Following this CD4+ T cells will be sorted using a FACS Aria III cell sorter. RNA will be isolated from these peptide specific CD4+ T cells and analysed using the nCounter Human Immunology panel on NanoString gene expression analysis system. The idea is to identify specific gene signature associated with peptide specific tolerance induction or inflammation. The knowledge gained from the above study will support the development of treatments and prevention strategies for CMA.
kw: cow's milk allergy, tolerance induction

title: Targeting Fibrosis in Systemic Sclerosis
abs: Background:Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a prototypic multi-systemic fibrotic disease due to excessive collagen production. Ten-year survival is 66%. Therapies are ineffective partly due to our incomplete understanding of the mechanisms of fibrosis and inadequate subsetting of this heterogeneous disease to allow targeted treatment. Traditional subsetting into limited (LcSSc) and diffuse cutaneous (DcSSc) SSc has limitations in the early diagnosis and prognostication of SSc. Identification of a collagen synthesis gene signature will enhance molecular subsetting of SSc. Our overarching hypothesis is that there exist several unidentified genes regulating collagen synthesis, whose dysregulation play key roles in fibrosis underlying SSc. We specifically aim to 1)Discover novel genes/pathways regulating elevated collagen synthesis in SSc dermal fibroblast by human genome-wide ribonucleic acid interference-(RNAi)-screening; 2)Determine whether genes regulating collagen synthesis are dysregulated in SSc dermal fibroblasts of different SSc clinical subsets, through targeted gene expression profiling.Methodology:Our target-driven approach will enable us to discover even moderate changes in gene expression, which would otherwise be missed by conventional microarray techniques due to high background noise. 1)We will perform RNAi-screening using immortalized dermal fibroblasts from three DcSSc patients. A system-level view of genes and signaling pathways regulating collagen synthesis will be generated using bioinformatics analysis. Our pilot-proof-of-principle RNAi-screen on immortalized dermal fibroblast from a DcSSc patient demonstrates the feasibility of this approach, and has identified 22 regulators of collagen synthesis. 2)We will determine using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction whether the newly discovered regulatory genes/pathways are differentially expressed in SSc dermal fibroblasts from patients with (a)very early SSc (n=5); (b)LcSSc (n=10); (c)DcSSc (n=10), with disease onset <3 years compared with healthy subjects (n=10).Significance:This study has the potential to discover novel genes regulating collagen synthesis and to identify collagen synthesis gene signatures to molecularly subset SSc, which will lead to earlier diagnosis and targeted treatment for SSc.
kw: Systemic sclerosis, Collagen, Autoimmunity, Fibrosis, RNAi screen

title: A population-level study of vaccine attitude, acceptance, and uptake in Singapore
abs: Influenza and dengue are two communicable diseases that have substantial burdens on the public health and economic ecosystems of Singapore. However, both these national concerns are at different points of the vaccination continuum. While the readily available seasonal influenza vaccine has witnessed poor uptake rates, media reports suggest that the dengue vaccine may be licensed and available in 2015/16, spurring popular debate about its documented efficacy and potential use. Across these events, the public health system and policymaking community is confronted with the twin challenges of improving low influenza vaccine coverage on the one hand, and managing the limited scientific evidence and public perception data critical in the process to evaluate the new dengue vaccine on the other. This proposal is an attempt to bolster the national response to these twin challenges by conducting the first national study of the informational, structural and psychological dynamics that currently influence influenza vaccine uptake, and might affect future public response to the dengue vaccine. This study will be conducted in 3 phases. In Phase 1, we will synthesize scientific evidence on informational, structural and psychosocial determinants of vaccine-related behaviors. This will be done through a systematic review. In Phase 2, we will use focus group discussions to engage key at-risk groups to generate evidence on Singapore-centric vaccine-related issues and concerns. In Phase 3, we will draw upon findings from Phases 1 & 2 to conduct the first population-level quantitative assessment of vaccine-related ISP issues and concerns among the general public in Singapore. Our study will provide specific, detailed, and actionable recommendations that can be used to, a) design demographically-targeted, community-specific vaccine education interventions, b) introduce policy-level initiatives that can address barriers and strengthen facilitators to vaccination, and c) pre-empt public questioning and ambivalence about vaccines through a comprehensive national vaccine communication strategy.
kw: vaccine, vaccination, knowledge, attitude, belief, behavior

title: Modeling for the cost-effectiveness of new dengue control methods in Singapore
abs: In Singapore, the annual economic costs and disease burden of dengue are substantial. They have been estimated to be between US$85-115 million and 9-14 DALYs per 100,000 habitants. The year 2013 marked Singapore’s worst dengue epidemic where the number of cases was 1.5 times that of the previous major dengue epidemic in 2005.New vaccines and the development of sterile insect technique (SIT)-based interventions namely Release of Insects with Dominant Lethality (RIDL) and release of mosquitoes infected with the Wolbachia bacterium often promise to reduce the burden of dengue in Singapore substantially. To date, it is not known whether such new interventions are cost-effective for the case of Singapore and how they should be implemented.In this project we aim to: (i) evaluate whether the new vaccines are cost-effective for Singapore, under what price and age-structured vaccination strategy; (ii) evaluate whether RIDL and Wolbachia-infected mosquito release as SIT and Wolbachia-infected to replace existing dengue vectors is cost-effective; and (iii) evaluate combinations of vaccination and vector control programs to see whether there are potential synergies between them.To answer these questions we will divide the project in two Phases. In Phase 1 we will develop and parameterize a vector-host epidemic model for Singapore that will incorporate interventions of the vector and the host considering the four dengue serotypes and different levels of dengue severity in multiple age groups. In Phase 2 the model will be expnaded with economic modules to consider intervention costs and avoided direct and indirect economic impacts. The model will then be used to asses cost-effectiveness of the different control interventions.
kw: Cost-effectiveness, dengue, vaccine, RIDL, vector-control

title: Intrinsic mechanisms critical for reactivation of neural stem cells
abs: The switch between neural stem cell quiescence vs. proliferation is a central but poorly-understood issue in stem cell biology. Similar to mammalian neural stem cells, Drosophila larval neural stem cells, neuroblasts, transit from a quiescent to reactivated state in response to intrinsic and extrinsic stimuli. The presence of nutrition triggers insulin production by glial cells, activating the insulin/PI3K pathway in underlying neural stem cells and stimulating their growth and proliferation. Prospero (Pros), a differentiation factor, is able to induce neuroblasts into a quiescent state through its transient expression in neuroblasts. However, intrinsic cures that allow cell cycle re-entry of quiescent neural stem cells are unknown. We reason that a subset of cell cycle regulators is an important component of intrinsic cues for reactivation of neural stem cells. Our unpublished data suggest that a unique group of mitotic regulators, termed spindle matrix proteins, are required for reactivation of neural stem cells. Our overall objective is to identify critical intrinsic cues that control nutrient-dependent reactivation of Drosophila neural stem cells. Our central hypothesis is that spindle matrix proteins mediate reactivation of neural stem cells intrinsically. The goal of this application will be achieved by three specific aims: 1). To determine the function of spindle matrix proteins during reactivation of neural stem cells; 2). To determine the functional link between spindle matrix proteins, Insulin pathway and Prospero during reactivation; 3). To analyze spindle matrix-dependent and independent transcriptome in neural stem cells. This work is highly innovative because it will identify important intrinsic mechanisms of neural stem cell reactivation. This work is significant because identification of intrinsic cues for neural stem cell reactivation will create new knowledge on neural stem cell behavior, ultimately providing strong basis for stem cell-based therapy for preventing/treating neurodegenerative diseases.
kw: Drosophila, neural stem cells, reactivation, quiescence, cell cycle

title: Characterization of the antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties of Q203, a promising clinical candidate for the treatment of multi-drug resistant tuberculosis
abs: Tuberculosis remains a devastative disease that result in 1.3 million deaths every year. Despite progress in public health management, the epidemic of drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a serious issue worldwide. New drug candidates are urgently needed. We recently developed the small-molecule Q203 as a promising drug candidate for the treatment of tuberculosis. Q203 kill M. tuberculosis by inhibiting the respiratory bc1-aa3-type cytochrome c oxidase complex. The mode of action of Q203 appears complex and deserves to be thoroughly investigated in order to fully exploit its therapeutic potential. We showed that in contrast to its exceptional bactericidal activity in vivo, Q203 is barely bacteriostatic in vitro, with a clear dependence on the carbon source present in the culture medium. Furthermore, in addition to its direct bactericidal activity, Q203 uniquely inhibits the formation of granuloma in vivo. This anti-inflammatory property is interesting since the granuloma offers a micro-environment exploited by mycobacteria to persist, therefore suggesting that Q203 may reducing the
