title: Nanofluidics with Two-dimensional Materials
abs: With the increased demand and dwindling supply of the fresh water, more efficient technologies for water desalinization and filtering are needed. Nanofluidics of 2D materials (2Dmat) attracted lots of research and industry attention last year, driven by its potentially superior performance in water desalinization, pervaporation water treatment, and for molecular sieving. 2D materials (for example, graphene, graphene oxide, boron-nitride, dichalcogenides, etc) consist of a monoatomic, freestanding sheets material – they could be layered or interconnected into thicker membranes, or perforated with sub-nanometre scaled pores. Here we propose to develop and implement a new, superior type of filtration membranes, based on 2Dmats. We have previously shown that pristine, atomically thin graphene membrane is completely impermeable to water and ions, but if perforated with sub-nanometre pores exhibits ion-specific permeability due to size exclusion. In the direction parallel to graphene’s basal plane, water flows with very little frictions, even in sub-nanometre constrictions between graphene-oxide sheets. This combination of tuneable ion-specific permeability and frictionless water flow makes graphene-based membranes potentially disruptive technology for water desalinization and filtering, and molecular sieving. We will employ team’s world-renown expertise in 2Dmat nanofluidics, nanofabrication, material science, atomically-resolved electron imaging, and predictive theory to develop in-depth understanding of parameters governing water-2Dmat interactions. This will allow us to rationally tailor chemical and structural properties of 2Dmat membrane to achieve desired water/ion permeation properties. The final goal is to set technological targets, secure intellectual property and demonstrate prototype membrane devices that will outperform traditional polymeric membranes in water desalinization, or have some other unique advantage. The commercially viable device will be developed subsequently with industrial partners.
kw: 2D materials;graphene;nanofluidics;desalinization;nanopores;ion selective membrane

title: Large volume intraoperative peritoneal lavage as a simple intervention to improve the survival of gastric cancer patients - an international multi-center randomized controlled trial
abs: Gastric cancer is the second most common cause of cancer death in the world, and is particularly prevalent in Asia. It frequently recurs after treatment, with the peritoneum as one of the commonest sites of recurrence. Peritoneal recurrence is not only fatal, but also brings significant morbidity to patients. Currently, there is no treatment for peritoneal recurrence. Hence, prevention is a key strategy. There is a suggestion that extensive intraoperative peritoneal lavage (EIPL) with large volume of physiological saline reduces the risk of implantation of free cancer cells on the peritoneum, prevents peritoneal recurrence and improves survival after surgery for gastric cancer. EIPL is a very simple and safe procedure with minimal cost. Our aim is to test the efficacy of this procedure by conducting a large international multi-centre randomized-controlled trial. Our hypothesis is EIPL can improve the survival of gastric cancer patients after surgery with curative intent. The estimated sample size is 600 patients, with locally advanced gastric cancer (T3, T4a/b, M0, AJCC 7th edition) who are undergoing curative surgery. They will be randomized into 2 groups after surgery: 10 litres of physiological saline peritoneal lavage before wound closure, or no lavage. All patients will be followed-up according to a standard protocol. Our endpoints are overall survival, disease-free survival and risk of peritoneal recurrence in three years. We believe that this study will be the first study to confirm the role of extensive peritoneal lavage on gastric cancer. It may change the clinical practice of cancer surgery in general and potentially brings significant benefits to our patients with minimal morbidity. (256 words)
kw: peritoneal lavage, gastric cancer, peritoneal recurrence, gastrectomy, survival

title: The Glaucoma Initial Treatment Study: Comparing the Effectiveness of Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty with Topical Medication. A Multi-Centre, Prospective and Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. With ageing population, glaucoma morbidity will raise; causing increased healthcare costs for a condition in which visual loss is irreversible. From population-based studies, the prevalence of glaucoma was found to be 3.2% in Chinese Singaporeans with glaucoma the leading cause of blindness. Medications, in forms of topical eye drops, are used worldwide as the first line treatment to lower intraocular pressure (IOP) in glaucoma patients. However, topical medications are associated with numerous side effects, poor adherence and high long-term costs. Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT), also effective at lowering IOP, is a relatively new technique that appears to be more beneficial in patient-centred quality of life outcomes. SLT has recently been proposed as a viable alternative to medications as the first line therapy for glaucoma. Although a number of smaller studies indicate that SLT and topical prostaglandins are equally effective at lowering IOP, these were generally underpowered and did not consider the impact of these two treatment modalities from patient-centred and health economic perspectives. Thus, whether SLT should be recommended more widely as the first line treatment for glaucoma, saving healthcare systems millions of dollars each year, remains unclear. We therefore propose a multi-centre prospective randomized trial, which will determine the optimum first line therapy for people with primary open angle glaucoma. This study will: evaluate treatment outcomes with respect to patient quality of life (QoL); provide detailed economics effectiveness analysis; and compare the clinical effectiveness with respect to degree of IOP lowering and rates of treatment failure over 2 years.Overall 400 patients will be recruited from Australia, Malaysia and Singapore. The trial in Australia is already funded by NHMRC Australia. This CTG application is to fund 120 subjects who will be recruited and followed up in Singapore from 3 hospitals.
kw: Glaucoma, Selective laser trabeculoplasty, multi-centre prospective randomized trial, quality of life (QoL), optimum first line therapy

title: Biophysically-derived Pro-Angiogeneic (BPA) Mesenchymal Stromal Cells (MSCs) for the Enhancement of Hematopoietic Recovery after Umbilical Cord Blood Transplantation
abs: Umbilical cord blood (UCB) is a good alternative source of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) for transplantation to treat various bone marrow (BM) related cancers and functional failures. However, the advantages of a lowered incidence of donor-cell induced graft–versus-host-disease (GvHD) and the ability to facilitate histocompatibility mismatched transplants appears to be offset by delayed hematopoietic recovery after transplantation with consequent increased transplant related mortality compared to fully matched BM transplants. Part of this delay is related to poor homing of cord blood HSCs to chemotherapy damaged BM tissues, which becomes devoid of functional “HSC niches” that are essential for HSC maintenance and development into mature blood cells.Together with researchers from the Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology, we have developed a label-free means for large-scale isolation of a BM mesenchymal stromal cell (MSCs) subpopulation called “biophysically-derived pro-angiogeneic (BPA)-MSCs”. BPA-MSCs possess potent regenerative properties and secrete molecules which accelerated both the recovery of radiation induced BM injuries and post-HSC-transplant hematopoiesis in immunodeficient mice. We propose a standard early phase II clinical trial design to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BPA-MSCs administered together with donor UCB in the setting of a conventional dual UCB transplant (UCBT). Fifteen patients will be recruited from the Singapore General Hospital and National University Hospital who are eligible for standard UCBT based on adequate cell dose and histocompatibility. The study will span over three years with primary endpoints being neutrophil and platelet engraftment times. Secondary endpoints will evaluate safety, which is defined by the incidence of GvHD, organ toxicity, relapse (to ensure that MSCs do not contribute to tumor recurrence), overall and disease-free survival. Tertiary endpoints will examine the kinetics and profile of immune reconstitution. This will be the first such clinical study using these BPA-MSCs, especially in a transplant setting.

title: Characterizing and Elucidating Pathways of Cardiac Aging in an Asian population
abs: The rapidly aging population of Singapore has several implications for public health. Successful aging is key if older people are to remain independent. Cardiovascular function is central to overall functioning. However, cardiac aging attributable to chronological aging consists of a variety of complex changes in cardiac structure and function, which in turn have not been comprehensively characterized by advanced cardiac imaging in an Asian population. We aim to characterize the myriad of complex changes that occur as part of cardiac aging, and to elucidate pathways underlying cardiac aging, using biomarkers consisting of adiponectin, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin and brain natriuretic peptide.We will characterize cardiac aging by comparing cardiac structure and function between a group of elderly Chinese adults aged ?70 years who are lifetime non-smokers, without previously diagnosed cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, hypertension (Old Healthy Group), and a group of young Chinese adults, aged 21-40 years (Young Healthy Group). The Old Healthy group will be identified from the ongoing Singapore Chinese Health Study (SCHS) (respondents of Follow-up Study III). The Young Healthy group will be identified from healthy volunteers. To further establish findings in the hearts of the Old Healthy as part of aging and not related to age-related risk factors, we will compare the hearts of Old Healthy with a group of Non-healthy elderly from the cohort with hypertension or diabetes mellitus but without cardiovascular disease.All participants will be studied using state-of-the-art quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography and arterial tonometry. Baseline and change in biomarkers will be analysed from archived blood (1999-2004) and fresh blood (2014-2015) while longitudinal information from midlife consisting of anthropometric, diet and lifestyle data will be used as supporting variables.This study will advance fundamental understanding of the characteristics and pathways of cardiac aging in Chinese adults required for retardation of cardiac aging.
kw: cardiac aging, cardiac imaging, cardiac function, elderly

title: Response of the myocardium to hypertrophic conditions in the adult population
abs: Calcific aortic stenosis and hypertensive heart disease are leading causes of adult heart failure. In response to the increased afterload, myocardial hypertrophy is initially compensatory to maintain cardiac function. Due to progressive myocyte death and myocardial fibrosis, ventricular decompensation and heart failure ultimately occur. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) techniques and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I are novel markers of myocardial fibrosis. Therefore, they hold potential of identifying patients at risk of heart failure. We hypothesize myocardial fibrosis is associated with impaired ventricular function recovery after valve replacement in patients with small aortic valve area low transvalvular gradient (small-area low-gradient) aortic stenosis and impaired systolic ejection fraction; and it is associated with increased left ventricular mass and reduced cardiac performance in patients with essential hypertension. The specific study aims are to:(1) Establish reference ranges of cardiac morphology in an Asian populationCurrent CMR reference ranges were developed in Caucasian populations. We will establish reference ranges of cardiac morphology in 240 healthy adults using 3T CMR, in order to develop new paradigms for assessing myocardial disease in Singapore. (2) Validate markers of myocardial fibrosis in predicting functional recovery after aortic valve replacementContemporary approach of dobutamine stress echocardiography is limited in predicting myocardial function recovery after valve replacement in patients with small-area low-gradient aortic stenosis and impaired ejection fraction. In 50 patients with small-area low-gradient aortic stenosis and impaired ejection fraction, we will investigate novel imaging and circulating markers of fibrosis in predicting myocardial function recovery after valve replacement.(3) Assess determinants associated with myocardial fibrosis in patients with essential hypertensionThe significance of myocardial fibrosis in hypertensive heart disease is currently not well characterized, underscoring a critical knowledge gap. We will determine the association of left ventricular mass, measures of cardiac performance and peripheral blood pressure with myocardial fibrosis in 500 patients with essential hypertension.
kw: cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging; aortic stenosis; hypertensive heart disease; left ventricular hypertrophy; myocardial fibrosis

title: Keloids: Therapy with drug-free solid and steroid-laden hyaluronic acid dissolving Microneedles
abs: Keloids are a prevalent dermatosis in which excessive production of collagen results in exuberant and disfiguring masses. Existing treatments have limited efficacy and/or a high recurrent rate. Recently, we discovered that the proliferation of cultured keloid fibroblasts was prohibited by the physical presence of drug-free microneedles. Consistent findings were further demonstrated in our rabbit hypertrophic scar model and clinical observations in our patients. We investigated the role of gap junctions in this process and found the expression of Connexin 43 to be reduced in keloid fibroblasts subjected to microneedles. We hereby propose using drug-free solid microneedles in a continuously applied manner to be a potentially effective, safe and cost-effective treatment option amenable to self-administration by patients. Concurrently, we had investigated the use of drug-containing hyaluronic acid (HA) dissolving microneedles in laboratory in vitro/vivo studies and found these to have good mechanical strength, rapid dissolution profile and stable storage. They also had pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties comparable to the traditional subcutaneous injection form of a diabetic drug. We hereby propose the use of steroid-containing HA microneedles for the treatment of keloids, which circumvents many problems of conventional steroid injections. This project aims to develop new alternative and adjunctive treatments for a condition with a huge unmet clinical need. Its specific aims are:1.To conduct a randomized intra-individually -controlled clinical trial to determine the clinical efficacy of self-administered continually-applied drug-free microneedles and once-a-day steroid-laden hyaluronic acid dissolving microneedles in the treatment of keloids.2.To study the mechanism of the physical anti-proliferative effect of microneedles on keloid fibroblasts.This project comprises the collaborative efforts between dermatologists, engineers and the industry. In the clinical trial, subjects with three keloids between 1-2cm in diameter will be randomized to different treatments: (i) one-time intralesional corticosteroid injection; (ii) continuous microneedle application for four weeks; (iii) once-a-day self-adminstration of triamcinolone-laden hyaluronic acid dissolving microneedles for four weeks. At baseline and after 4 weeks, assessments comprise of: (i) Keloid volumes using a 3-dimensional camera and silicon mould resin; (ii) Vancouver Scar Scale by a blinded dermatologist; (iii) patient self-assessment of pain and itch. In the laboratory studies, the changes in cell-cell communication leading to inhibition of keloid fibroblast proliferation will be investigated.
kw: scar, hypertrophic, needles, steroid, triamcinolone

title: The role of the BIM deletion polymorphism in type 1 diabetes
abs: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a lifelong condition with significant risk of serious complications despite the use of insulin replacement therapy. Pathologically, T1D is initiated by environmental factors triggering an autoimmune response against insulin-producing beta-cells in the endocrine pancreas. In addition, significant heterogeneity in the presentation and natural history of patients with T1D suggests that some individuals harbour beta-cells that can survive the autoimmune attack better and for longer periods. Because beta-cell death is critically dependent on the expression of the pro-apoptotic BCL2 family member, BIM, we postulated that functional polymorphic variants in the BIM gene might alter beta-cell apoptosis, and contribute to the T1D heterogeneity, including age at presentation. Accordingly, we have begun to investigate the contribution of a novel East Asian-specific BIM deletion polymorphism to age of presentation in patients with T1D. Because the BIM deletion polymorphism results in the expression of non-functional BIM splice isoforms, we hypothesize that the polymorphism will delay the onset of T1D by impairing the apoptotic response to cytokine-mediated beta-cell death. Our preliminary data indicate that individuals who harbour the BIM deletion polymorphism experience a striking five-year delay in T1D presentation compared to those without (p=0.06). In this project, we will pursue the following Specific Aims: (1) confirm if the presence of the BIM deletion polymorphism delays the age at presentation of T1D in East Asian patients; and (2) determine if the BIM deletion polymorphism confers protection from cytokine-induced cell death in human beta-cells. The completion of this project will increase our understanding of the mechanisms involved in beta-cell death, and explain in part the heterogeneity of disease presentation in T1D. Finally, because it is therapeutically possible to alter BIM expression to favour non-functional isoforms, our work may also set the stage for interventions which alter the natural history of T1D.
kw: BIM; polymorphism; type 1 diabetes; pancreatic beta-cells; apoptosis; cytokines; heterogeneity

title: Management of Hypertension and multiple risk factors to Enhance Cardiovascular Health- A Cluster Randomized Trial in Singapore Polyclinics
abs: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of disability and death in Singapore. Uncontrolled hypertension confers the highest attributable risk of CVD. About one in four adults suffer from hypertension in Singapore, 50% of them have uncontrolled blood pressure (BP). We propose a cluster randomized trial in eight polyclinics in Singapore, 4 deliver a structured multi-component intervention and 4 deliver usual care. 1000 adults with uncontrolled hypertension will be followed for two years for change in systolic BP as the primary outcome and change in serum LDL cholesterol as a secondary outcome with the following aims: •Specific Aim 1: To determine the effectiveness of a structured multi-component structured primary care program comprised of 1) algorithm-driven antihypertensive treatment for all patients using fixed-dose combination (FDC) and lipid lowering for high risk patients, 2) subsidy on FDC antihypertensive medication; 3) motivational conversation for high risk patients; and 4) telephone based follow-ups of all patients by a team of physician supervised nurse practitioners and nurses in the polyclinics in Singapore•Specific Aim 2: To quantify the source of payment and costs for the multi-component intervention and perform an incremental cost effectiveness analysis in terms of cost per projected quality adjusted life year (QALY) saved from the societal, payer, and participant perspectives relative to usual care.•Specific Aims 3: To determine the impact of the above-mentioned program on adherence to anti-hypertensive and lipid-lowering medications. Hypotheses: In polyclinics in Singapore,•The structured, multi-component primary care program is better than usual care for improving systolic BP among patients with uncontrolled hypertension.•The structured multi-component program is cost effective relative to usual care in terms of cost per QALY saved from the societal and payer perspectives.If proven effective, the information will be valuable in informing the policy-makers to upscale strategies for enhancing management of hypertension in Singapore, and other countries with similar healthcare infrastructure.

title: Continuation of ATX in glaucoma – ATX inhibitor study in Dutch belted rabbits
abs: Primary open-angle glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness in the United States and is commonly associated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). The increased IOP is caused by diminished aqueous humor (AH) drainage through the trabecular pathway. The molecular basis for increased resistance to AH outflow through the trabecular pathway is not fully understood and explored. There have been some recent observations suggested that Autotaxin-lysophosphatidic acid (ATX-LPA) axis might be a potential therapeutic target for lowering IOP in glaucoma patients. Autotaxin (ATX) is a secreted enzyme that is present in key tissues/fluids modulating IOP namely aqueous humor (AH), trabecular meshwork (TM) cells, and the ciliary body. Based on the results of the ongoing rabbit study with the ATX dual inhibitors, we are proposing a continuation of this study with the existing 48 rabbits to further profiling of the ‘duals’ require similar efforts as ATX program.

title: Portable wireless microfluidic device for real time healthy monitoring
abs: What is the ideal dose to a patient in real time? How can we prevent the urgent clinical situations for the patients who are identified as high risk groups of stroke or cardiovascular diseases? To solve these challenges, it is essential to measure the biomarkers in vivo. In the last decade, significant advancements in wireless chips capable of providing an opportunity to conduct patients and medical doctors regardless the long distance, which opened the possibility of remote real time body condition monitoring for intensive health care. However, current wireless chips are not available for long time usage for intensive health monitoring. Moreover, most biosensors were not applicable for real time assay. Indeed, at present, real-time molecular monitoring is available for only a handful of analytes that produce readily measureable signals from analyte-specific reactions, such as glucose through glucose oxidase activity, which were not sufficient for health care monitoring. In this project, we propose a portable microfluidic system integrated with an advanced low power wireless chip for remote real time multiple biomarker detections (such as micro-RNA, thrombin and dose concentration). The biomolecule concentrations are assayed in vivo through flowing blood plasma to a micro-channel with aptamer sensors. Meanwhile, the signals are immediately sent through a wireless network to a medical centre for diagnosis. Once the biomarkers' (or dose) concentration is detected to be low/high, the clinical treatments can be performed on time for personalized medicine.

title: Data generation and construction of an integrated database on pre-clinical models
abs: The primary tumour mouse xenograft programme of Huynh Hung at the National Cancer Centre Singapore (NCCS) has been extremely successful in facilitating drug development and attracting pharmaceutical investment to Singapore. This programme has established more than 100 primary tumour xenografts from Asian cancers, which have been used to test the efficacy of an extensive range of novel agents. The Centre for Translational Research and Diagnostics (CTRAD) led by Richie Soong at the National University of Singapore (NUS) is a recognized centre of excellence for biomarker development and molecular diagnostics in Asia, and has likewise attracted significant academic and industry investment to Singapore. CTRAD incorporates the National University Health System (NUHS) Tissue Repository (TR), the Translational Interface (TI) translational research laboratory, and the College of American Pathologist (CAP)-accredited Diagnostic Molecular Oncology Centre (DMOC) and Molecular Diagnosis Centre (MDC). Together, these units provide CTRAD with capabilities and expertise in biosample resources, digital pathology, medical genomics, medical bioinformatics, molecular therapeutics and molecular diagnostics. These two programmes have been in close collaboration for more than 6 years through studies with Bayer Healthcare. These collaborations have led to the launch of 3 first-in-world clinical trials in Singapore, with many others in development. This proposal seeks to capitalize further on the programmes and their close working relationships through executing deep molecular profiling of tumours in the primary tumour xenograft programme. A database will be generated for the management and intuitive query of the generated data. The establishment of this database is anticipated to provide advanced knowledge of each model, enabling better selection of models and enhance drug development. The integration and analysis of the multiple levels of clinical, molecular and drug efficacy information is also expected to be a rich resource for novel insights into cancer biology and pharmacology.

title: Data generation and construction of an integrated database on pre-clinical models
abs: Advances in HCC, ovarian cancer and gastric cancer treatment face several challenges apart from identification of active agents. One challenge is the prediction of activity of an active agent in these cancers. The establishment of predictive biomarkers is fraught with difficulties in interpretation and reproducibility of clinical studies contributed by the unrecognized heterogeneity that exist even within a histological subtype. Current animal models in pre-clinical oncological studies often fail to predict the clinical efficacy of new/novel anticancer agents, largely due to their inability to reflect disease heterogeneity and complexity. Xenograft models are usually established using human cancer cell lines maintained in culture for years and do not recapitulate the biological/ histological characteristics of the tumor of origin. Response in cell line-derived xenografts may therefore not coincide with what is observed in clinical situations as they do not reflect the biological heterogeneity observed clinically hence weakening their predictive value. A potential solution to these challenges is the use of patient tumor-derived cancer xenograft (PDX) model. The development of a sufficiently large bank of such PDX models to reflect the heterogeneity of actual clinical situation can help in developing predictive biomarkers of response to novel agents and allowing mechanistic studies of drug action thereby deriving predictive biomarkers before the clinical phase of investigation. Over the last 10 years, NCCS has created a unique collection of human xenograft models (160 PDX) that enables the evaluation of the effectiveness of new cancer drugs in a range of human cancers including HCC, gastric and ovarian cancers, which are prevalent in the Asian region. This’ project is to characterize cancer models at NCCS/NUS which BAYER will use in the future for profiling studies. Molecular data will be generated and integrated into a database which the 3 partners will jointly access.

title: In vivo efficacy study of BET-inhibitor (BET-BAY 002) in HCC PDX models
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer death worldwide often presenting in the advanced stage when cure is not possible. As such, there is an urgent need for more efficacious systemic therapy. c-Myc is a master regulator of cell proliferation and metabolism and is central to the pathogenesis of HCC, by the coordinated upregulation of a transcriptional program influencing metabolic adaptation, cell division, and survival. Over-expression of c-Myc induced HCC, whereas inhibition of c-Myc expression resulted in the differentiation of tumor cells c-Myc transcription is positively regulated by members of the bromodomains and extraterminal (BET) domain family of proteins. This study aims to determine the in vivo antitumor activity of BET-BAY 002, a small-molecule compound with high potency against BET proteins, in preclinical models of HCC.

title: Investigating the interactions between Type 2 diabetes and neurodegeneration
abs: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and neurodegeneration (ND) rank 1st and 3rd in disease burden in Singapore. From an economic perspective, combined societal cost of ND conditions like Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease in Singapore was SGD1.4 billion in 2009 (39% of the healthcare budget). Both T2D and ND are increasingly prevalent, which will cause societal cost to escalate. Epidemiology suggests that these increasing trends do not occur in isolation, as T2D patients are predisposed towards ND. A common set of molecular processes is implicated in both classes of diseases; these processes are conserved between humans and model organisms, such as Drosophila, the fruitfly. I have produced novel evidence that a T2D-like condition predisposes flies toward ND, thus demonstrating that the interaction between the two diseases is also conserved in flies. Using a combination of electrophysiology, cell biology and genetics, I will systematically investigate in flies: (1) the early warning signs or biomarkers preceding ND in this T2D-like condition, (2) interactions of the insulin signaling pathway with ND, and (3) susceptibility genes influencing the T2D-ND interaction across the genome. Given the conserved nature of insulin signaling and ND, I expect that investigations of T2D-associated ND in humans will benefit from parallel studies in flies. By elucidating the role of insulin signaling in ND, our studies in flies will greatly facilitate current efforts to improve insulin-based therapies targeted at the human brain to treat ND. In addition, we will identify key susceptibility genes from candidates that will be found in ongoing human genome-wide association studies of T2D-associated ND, and help design a medical device for identifying T2D patients that are genetically susceptible to ND.

title: MicroRNA and competing endogenous RNA crosstalk: Post-transcriptional regulatory networks in cancer pathogenesis and therapeutics
abs: My research will focus on the post-transcriptional control of MYC in human cancers. MYC is a critical proto-oncogene which is frequently activated in multiple human cancers. In addition to changes at the genomic level, aberrant changes in the post-transcriptional regulation of MYC may also contribute to cancer initiation and progression. MicroRNAs and RNA binding proteins (RBPs) are two important classes of post-transcriptional regulators which play key roles in multiple biological processes and have been linked to cancer development. Although several studies have shed some light on microRNA- and RBP-dependent MYC regulation, a comprehensive analysis of microRNA and RBP regulation of the full-length MYC transcript has not been performed and the potential crosstalk between these two mechanisms of post-transcriptional regulation has not been studied. I have previously demonstrated that in addition to conventional 3’UTR targeting, functional microRNA binding can occur in coding regions of target genes. I have also shown that transcripts can co-regulate each other by sequestering shared microRNAs, thus acting as competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs). To date, nothing is known about transcripts which regulate MYC via ceRNA crosstalk. Additionally, competition for RBPs may represent another post-transcriptional regulatory dimension that is both distinct from and intricately intertwined with ceRNA interactions. To elucidate novel post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms of MYC, I thus propose the following Specific Aims: (1) To examine novel miRNA regulation of the full-length MYC transcript; (2) To characterize the MYC ceRNA network; (3) To explore the potential interplay between RNA:RNA and RNA:protein interactions in post-transcriptional regulation of MYC. Accomplishing these aims will lead to important insights into the regulation of this important proto-oncogene. It also has broader implications for our understanding of cancer biology and post-transcriptional gene regulation, and may facilitate the discovery of novel oncogenes and tumor suppressors, in turn providing potential targets for diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

title: Integrated strategies to target the vulnerabilities of cancer stem cells
abs: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are key drivers of malignancy and chemotherapy resistance, thus, underlying the problem of clinical relapse. Chemotherapy disrupts tumor growth by inhibiting rapidly proliferating bulk tumor cells but selects for the outgrowth of CSCs. The effective treatment of cancer will need to address how one can selectively eradicate CSCs, in addition to eliminating bulk non-CSCs. My overarching objective is to define the new paradigms in CSC biology which can lead to the development of novel strategies that target CSCs. Building on my expertise in CSCs, I have defined a set of biological processes distinctly adopted by CSCs; these include the activation of autophagy, altered lipid metabolic pathways, and their ability to undergo differentiation. Using breast cancer as a model, my research focuses on connecting these new paradigms to the hallmarks of CSCs: (i) How does autophagy promote CSC tolerance to environmental stress? (ii) How does the reprogramming of lipid metabolic pathways contribute to CSC therapy resistance? (iii) Can we exploit the ability of CSCs to differentiate as a synthetic lethal trait? Gaining insights into the emerging facets of CSCs will uncover novel therapeutic modalities that can eradicate CSCs and improve disease outcome. Because currently available cell line models do not accurately represent human primary tumors, I will generate and incorporate patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models that more closely recapitulate the cellular heterogeneity within human tumors for assessing the outcome of cancer therapies. In the long-term, I plan to extend my research focus towards other types of carcinomas that include those arising from the prostate, gastrointestinal tissues and pancreas, which have been found to be driven by CSCs.

title: Micro-fabricated Electron/Ion Sources
abs: The goal of this project is to use make electron/ion sources that can be made by Integrated Circuit (IC) technology. The method will be based upon fabricating ring-cathode geometries, as opposed to the point cathode geometry used in conventional electron/gun designs. Micro-fabrication will first involve defining and growing Carbon Nanotube (CNT) nano-thin ring electron emitters. A method of cancelling -off-axis geometrical aberrations, invented by the lead PI, will be used to form the focused electron beam column. An array of such electron guns will then be fabricated and tested, and form the first step towards making and testing a parallel array of focused electron beams. Multi-beam columns of this kind have applications for parallel SEM inspection and parallel array Electron Beam Lithography. The project will then go on to use the ring CNT electron gun concept for designing and testing a high brightness micro-chip nano-aperture electron impact ion source, for applications such as multi-species focused ion beams (FIBs) and micro-chip mass spectrometers. The electron impact source will use a ring CNT emitter column for generating electrons,focusing a high current electron beam into the centre of a micro-ionization chamber.

title: Optofluidic Nano-cytometer for Virus Purification, Sorting and Quantification as an Assistive Toolkit for Virus Diagnosis
abs: Medical experts are calling for an effective and efficient engineering toolkit that is similar to the flow cytometers to sort out viral particles from other biological objects in body fluid sample, and quantify the number. The development of such engineering toolkit for virus manipulation will be a big breakthrough to help out in virus disease diagnosis. Current clinical and research techniques for virus purification and enrichment include mechanical filters, absorption/elution-based positively-charged filters, ultra-centrifugation, electrophoresis and laser tweezers. However, problems such as low recovery rate of 20-50%, clogging, tedious operation, risk of accidental lab exposure, low throughput and not adaptable and tunable for different functionalities exist. More importantly, since these techniques only filter nanoparticles from microparticles, they cannot discriminate related families of viruses and other organelles of similar size, and hence are limited in specificity. To address these challenges, we exploit the potential of optofluidics, which centered on the marriage of fluidics and optics, to control liquid flow streams and guide light in a microchannel so that viral particles can be sorted with ease in a closed environment. Combining a unique collection of recent breakthrough and discoveries in surface treatment for anti-fouling and signal processing systems for object characterization and tracking, in this program, we propose an optofluidic nano-cytometer as the ultimate engineering toolkits for clinicians and virologists to effectively and efficiently manipulate nanoparticles and viruses with the functionalities of (1) 1-to-many manipulation in a safe and closed environment, (2) trapping, sorting and patterning viruses in a single platform so that adaptability is not an issue, and (3) automatic characterization and counting via signal processing that gives highly accurate quantification.

title: Automated Isolation of Fetal Cells from Maternal Blood and Clinical Application Using High-Throughput Massively Parrallel Sequencing for Non-Invasive Prenatal Diagnosis
abs: Non-invasive prenatal diagnosis (NIPD) using fetal cells derived from cellular fractions of maternal blood is the Holy Grail of all prenatal diagnostic procedures. More now that cell-free fetal DNA within maternal blood plasma fractions have shown that fetal aneuploidy screening is possible with high specificity (NIPS, non-invasive prenatal screening). NIPS can only screen, and cannot be diagnostic.Diagnostic methods for fetal aneuploidy and monogenic disorders remain invasive, and associated with a clinically-significant risk of miscarriage. Fetal cells derived from maternal blood would eliminate this ?1% iatrogenic risk of fetal loss. If fetal nucleated red blood cells (FNRBCs) and trophoblast cells could be reliably enriched and amplified from within maternal blood, it would be a richer and purer source of fetal DNA for detecting a wide range of chromosomal and genetic disorders.We have shown previously that epsilon-globin is the ideal marker for FNRBCs enriched from maternal blood, and have developed a novel protocol that consistently enriches epsilon-globin-positive FNRBCs from fresh maternal blood samples. These cells have been shown to be suitable for whole genome amplification (WGA), PCR and array CGH. Recently, for the first time, we were able to detect chromosomal abnormalities from single FNRBCs isolated from villi tissues, using next-generation, massive parallel sequencing (MPS). This project is proposed as a logical extension of our earlier work to bring our sorting and genomics analysis techniques towards clinical utility. We hypothesize here that (1) we can enrich sufficient CD147+ FNRBCs and trophoblast cells from maternal blood; (2) that we can develop an unbiased fetal cells isolation methodology that isolates fetal cells based on their physical size; (3) that we can automate our novel fetal cell isolation process to aid large-scale clinical studies and clinical applicability; and (4) that we can establish a standard WGA-MPS method for fetal molecular karyotyping for NIPD.

title: Diagnostics of Immunodeficency Diseases in Adults
abs: Between individuals, the basis for the varied susceptibility and immune response to pathogens causing infections is not fully understood. It is attributed to variations or specific defects in the host immune innate response. Conventionally, the identification of defects in the immune signaling pathways has been tedious but this process has been revolutionalized with the advent of Next Generation Sequencing technology. We aim to harness this technology and acquire the capability to perform whole exome sequencing to investigate from the bedside-to-the bench-and back: patients with unusual presentations of infections e.g. atypical fungal and mycobacteria infections – with the intention of elucidating novel immune defects in patients. In addition functional validation studies of immune pathways implicating candidate genes identified through whole exome sequencing will be a requisite. To date, such a one-stop expertise and capability by the bedside is not available in Singapore.
kw: Next Generation Sequencing, Personalised Medicine

title: An ethnic-specific standard for small-for-gestational-age as a predictor of adverse neonatal outcomes in Singapore
abs: The objectives of this study are first; to explore the effect of induction of labour (IOL) on caesarean delivery (CD) in a large Asian cohort. In particular, we will examine CD rates following elective (non-medically indicated) IOL. The third objective is to prioritise areas of further research that can reduce CD rates. We hypothesise that (1) elective IOL may not protect against CD in Asian women, contrary to the large observational studies published from Caucasian populations, and may even increase the risk when performed at 40 weeks gestation and beyond; and (2) in women of Indian ethnicity, IOL may actually increase the risk of CD. The Department of O&G at NUS; Department of Epidemiology, NUS School of Public Health and Singapore MOH, are currently working together to construct a Collaborative Perinatal Surveillance and Research Project. Based on an estimated birth rate of 40,000/year in Singapore, we hope to obtain a large sample size of around 200,000 over the past five years. Upon successful establishment of this partnership, we will work closely with members from each institution who have various expertise (clinicians, biostatisticians, computing technicians, health economists), to extract, analyse and interpret the data. We propose that the analysis mimics an intention-to-treat analysis of a randomised trial comparing elective IOL to expectant management. We will apply logistic regression to examine the relationship between elective IOL and CD at each gestational week, and also adjust for important covariates such as ethnicity, parity, age and other socio-demographic indicators such as marital status and payment class. We intend to apply an interaction term in the regression model to test if there is an effect modification by ethnicity on elective IOL. If the interaction term analysis reveals a possible significant relationship, we will further develop our analysis by examining the various ethnicities as a subgroup.

title: Understanding how RUNX inactivation leads to loss of genomic integrity during carcinogenesis
abs: Cancer cells harbour hundreds of mutations and chromosomal aberrations. Whereas normal cells possess DNA repair checkpoints and surveillance pathways to maintain genomic integrity, it is unclear how cancer cells evade such mechanisms. We hypothesize that tumor suppressors like RUNX3, inactivated at the early stages of cancer constitute an important line of defence to guard genomic integrity. Specifically, I will be investigating how RUNX proteins guard genomic integrity and implications to cancer therapy.In the first part of this study, we seek to understand how RUNX proteins regulate DNA double-strand break repair. One of our notable findings is that in the absence of RUNX3, DNA repair is impaired because of defective histone H2AX phosphorylation, particularly in cells undergoing epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). However, how exactly EMT cross-talks with DNA repair is a largely unexplored area. Here, I will investigate how the ‘mesenchymal state’ of a cell compares against an ’epithelial state’ in the context of DNA repair. After EMT induction, cells will be assessed for sensitivity to DNA damaging agents, including known chemotherapeutic drugs, and the underlying mechanisms will be studied.The second part of this study is designed to explore the clinical relevance of RUNX involvement in DNA repair for human cancer. Since most cytotoxic chemotherapeutic compounds are DNA damaging agents, and RUNX3 is frequently inactivated in human cancer, we will study if RUNX3 loss can be converted into a therapeutic gain. Non-small cell lung cancer cell lines (NSCLC) will be used to knockdown RUNX3 and drug sensitivity will be compared. RUNX3- NSCLC cells will be also treated with a panel of DNA repair inhibitors to identify novel strategies to kill cancer cells based on RUNX3 status.In conclusion, this study will generate insights on how cancer cells disrupt genome maintenance during tumor evolution and provide newer ways of therapeutic targeting.
kw: DNA repair, genomic instability, EMT, RUNX, cancer

title: Understanding ethnic differences in insulin resistance and obesity dependent/independent pathways leading to insulin resistance by studying substrates involved in insulin signaling in human myoblasts
abs: Insulin resistance (IR) is a key feature or type 2 diabetes (T2D). Upon insulin binding, the insulin receptor engages the canonical phosphoinositide-3 kinase (PI3K)/Akt and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathways. An unbiased approach to define the insulin signaling network in 3T3L1 adipocytes identified 1798 insulin regulated phosphoproteins, of which only 50% are blocked by PI3K/mTOR inhibitors. However, muscle (rather than adipose tissue) is responsible for 75-80% of insulin stimulated glucose uptake. Furthermore, 3T3L1 cells are murine in origin. We aim to use phosphoproteomics to identify the phosphorylated substrates which show altered levels after insulin stimulation in human primary myoblasts, which we believe that is more relevant to human IR. We have previously demonstrated that lean South Asians exhibit more IR than lean Chinese. In a similar way, we have shown that overweight Chinese exhibit greater IR than lean Chinese. These findings are recapitulated in primary myoblast cultures from these individuals. We believe that comparison of the insulin regulated phosphoproteome in primary myoblast cultures from these groups of individuals represents a unique experimental model with which to identify obesity dependent and obesity independent pathways leading to IR. Finally, we hypothesize that differences in the levels of phosphoproteins in these different groups of myoblasts may result from differential expression of insulin signaling proteins in these samples. Therefore, we will also compare the expression (using RNAseq) of the proteins showing differential phosphorylation between groups. All these findings will be validated in muscle biopsies taken from humans before and during a hyperinsulinemic, euglycemic clamp. These findings may identify novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of diabetes which work by reducing IR, and also explain a widely studied clinical phenomenon (increased IR in South Asians compared to other ethnic groups).

title: Randomized Controlled Trial of an Incentive-based Physical Activity Program targeting both Children and Adults (FIT-FAM)
abs: There is overwhelming evidence that sustained physical activity reduces the risk of many common diseases. Yet, data reveals low levels of physical activity among working age adults and their children in Singapore. One strategy that has been successfully employed to influence behaviors of parents is to use their children as an intermediary. This strategy has a successful track record in public health, where children have helped their parents quit smoking and wear seatbelts. In this study we propose to test whether children can promote increased physical activity of a working parent at the same time that they increase their own activity level. This proposal is an extension of a prior study where we showed that modest financial incentives can increase physical activity levels among children. We now propose to conduct a follow-on trial where the reward is tied not only to the child’s own steps, but to that of their parents. Rewards will be based on step activity measured through a state-of-the-art wireless step counter. Just as children were motivated to increase their own activity levels in efforts to achieve the incentive, we hypothesize that they will also be effective advocates for increasing the activity levels of their parents. Specifically, we propose to conduct a 12 month two-arm RCT to evaluate the efficacy of the family based incentive scheme on working parents physical activity. We hypothesize that parents in the family-based incentive arm (FBI) will show a greater number of weekly moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA) bouts at 12 months compared to parents in the child based incentive (CBI) arm, as measured by accelerometery. Secondary Aims test the effects of the intervention on parent’s and child’s activity levels throughout the intervention period, on health outcomes and health-related quality of life.

title: Improving diabetes and health outcomes: enhancing health literacy in patients with diabetes and diabetic retinopathy
abs: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of vision loss and blindness in Singapore. Vision impairment from DR is associated with increased mortality, heart disease, kidney disorders, and poorer vision-related quality of life. The onset and progression of DR can be prevented and controlled in most cases if diabetes control is optimally self-managed. However, successful disease management is affected by patients’ levels of “health literacy” (HL). HL is the degree to which individuals have the capacity to obtain, process, and understand the basic health information and services needed to make appropriate health decisions and manage their conditions. Currently, only generic HL screening tools are available. To address this significant knowledge gap, PI Lamoureux and this group has undertaken extensive pilot research. In addition to pilot testing a novel 21-item Diabetic Retinopathy Health Literacy Scale in Australia, his findings have led to the hypothesis that improving DR-specific HL may improve clinical diabetes outcomes in these patients. However, a complete understanding of DR-specific HL and its impact on diabetes control is not known as no psychometrical and culturally valid tool is available in Singapore. In this study we aim therefore to develop and validate a socially and culturally valid DR-specific HL instrument to assess the magnitude, impact, and risk factors of DR-specific HL in patients in Singapore across the three main ethnic groups. We specifically propose to use classical and modern psychometric methodologies, to validate the tool, understand the impact of suboptimal DR-specific HL on clinical diabetes, ocular and health-related QoL endpoints, and identify determinants of suboptimal DR-specific HL. This study will be the first to provide evidence-based data to quantify the level of poor DR-specific HL, investigate its impact, and importantly, inform the design of appropriate interventions/programs to improve patients’ understanding and management of diabetic eye diseases in Singapore.
kw: Diabetes, Diabetic retinopathy, Health literacy, Diabetes control, Self-management, diabetes management

title: Colonoscopy Quality and Safety in Public Hospitals in Singapore (Extension) The “Track & Train” Program
abs: The “Colonoscopy Quality and Safety in Public Hospitals in Singapore” study aimed to evaluate the quality and safety of colonoscopy as a Colorectal Cancer (CRC) screening modality nationally. The first phase of the grant saw the development of an electronic system which automatically collects data on the completeness, adequacy, effectiveness, safety and appropriateness of the procedure in the restructured hospitals.Thus far, we have shown:a)The rate of adenoma (the precursor lesion to CRC) detection is dependent upon the time taken to survey the colon (withdrawal time).b)The previous metric used to assess bowel preparation was inadequate.c)The novel automated system developed for withdrawal time is both accurate and objective, and described a threshold time to achieve optimal adenoma detection.The data has been presented at gold-standard Healthcare Quality and Gastroenterology conferences, and has garnered a MOH Healthcare Quality Merit Award.ObjectivesBased on our findings from the initial study, this second phase of seeks to implement changes to the colonoscopy process, to improve adenoma and colorectal cancer detection by targeting the endoscopist/operator. Methods This study will be based on a three-pronged approach:First, the automated system will be expanded to generate individual scorecards for endoscopists at regular intervals. This will allow them to monitor their adenoma detection rates, completeness of colonoscopy (caecal intubation rates) and averaged withdrawal time. The indication for colonoscopy (appropriateness of the procedure) and complication rates will also be tracked. This will be benchmarked against their peers and international standards, and give the physician an indication of how he/she is performing. Second, these indices will be trended and presented periodically for self-assessment, with the aim of helping endoscopists identify areas that need improvement. Finally, we aim to design and test a remedial learning system to help individual endoscopists improve their colonoscopy practice and technique.Significance and benefits to health-care deliveryThe ultimate aim is a standardized system, where CRC screening and adenoma detection is optimized and complications minimized through an automated indices tracking and quality control system.

title: Developing a combinatorial approach involving stimulation of lipogenesis and autophagy to counter lipotoxicity in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH).
abs: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the leading cause of chronicliver disease worldwide. The spectrum of NAFLD ranges from hepaticsteatosis to fibrosis with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) as the mostworrisome form of the disease. Although early manifestations of NAFLDmay represent benign accumulation of liver fat alone, NASH is marked bylipotoxicity that promote the activation of intracellular stress kinases,inflammation, and apoptosis that ultimately can lead to hepatitis and liverfailure. Inhibiting fat deposition in liver has been advocated as the beststrategy to treat or reverse NAFLD, however, several recent studies inrodent models suggest that fat storage in lipid droplets may be aprotective mechanism in advanced stages of NAFLD, and can delay ordiminish the progression of NASH by decreasing lipotoxicity. Thiscounter-intuitive concept is supported by clinical studies of advancedNASH in humans, which clearly reveal an inverse relationship betweenthe expression of lipogenic genes (hence, lipid accumulation) withhepatic damage. In our preliminary hepatic cell culture studies, weobserved a similar protective effect of increased lipogenesis againstlipotoxicity induced by saturated fats. Surprisingly, we discovered that“autophagy”, which is known to decrease fat deposition in hepatocytes, isalso essential for lipogenesis and survival via the pro-lipogenic Liver XReceptor (LXR) in a lipotoxic environment. We thus hypothesize that acombinatorial increase in autophagy and lipogenesis could be a usefultherapeutic approach against the lipotoxicity associated with NASH.Using cell culture and animal models of NASH, we will first investigatethe effects of hepatic lipogenesis and autophagy on lipotoxicity and thenuse genetic/pharmacological interventions to test our hypothesis. Webelieve that the results obtained from this study will shed light on thecomplexity of NASH and provide novel targeted therapies for itstreatment.

title: Understanding chromatin interactions of adiponectin related genetic locus and their functional consequences for novel strategies in diabetes management
abs: Adiponectin plays central roles in driving obesity-linked diseases. Therapeutic strategies targeted to the adiponectin pathway could therefore be useful for the prevention and treatment of diabetes and/or cardiovascular disease. We recently identified a novel inter-genic locus that was positively associated with plasma adiponectin levels in East Asians. Neighboring genes whose expression might be novel determinants of serum adiponectin are ~300kb or further away. Hence, the mechanisms by which this non-coding region affect adiponectin pathway are unknown. There are suggestions that such disease associated variants lie on functional enhancers that can regulate gene expression through long distance enhancer-promoter interactions. Without prior knowledge of the chromatin interactions mediated by enhancers at positions where the variants cluster, an accurate prediction of the influence on genes and pathways will be difficult. Thus, we will chart the topological changes in chromatin interaction landscape at the locus to understand specific influence of the locus and its variants on transcripts within its chromatin network and their relationship with associated quantitative traits. In addition, we will test the hypothesis that the locus exerts the associated phenotype by the modulation of active enhancers, at the chromatin level (via modification of chromatin interaction landscape) and at the transcript level (via enhancer RNA). A better understanding of the mechanisms governing the association between this novel locus can identify a new pathway that can be targeted to increase adiponectin and improve dyslipidemia and obesity simultaneously. Such therapies will have significant advantages over currently available therapies for type 2 diabetes that target glucose levels alone.
kw: Adiponectin, enhancer, diabetes, chromatin interactions, GWAS, fat biology

title: A 'miR' boost at the synapse
abs: MicroRNA (miRNAs) are short non-coding RNAs with broad impacts on gene expression. They are increasingly implicated in brain disorders where synaptic function is lost. However, the impact of miRNAs on the synaptic transcriptome remains largely unknown. We thus investigated the effect of miRNAs on all known genes that make up the mammalian presynapse and control synaptic transmission. Our findings revealed that a majority of the ~200 presynaptic genes are altered by a global loss of miRNAs, indicating that miRNAs are important regulators of the presynaptic transcriptome. As we recently reported a role for the disease-associated miR-27b in presynaptic assembly, we focused on the impact of this miRNA on the presynaptic transcriptome. Surprisingly, we found that miR-27b upregulates a majority of presynaptic genes, including synaptotagmin1, a critical component of the neurotransmitter release machinery. Furthermore, we observed that miR-27b also promotes neurotransmitter release. As miRNAs generally downregulate gene expression, we hypothesize that miR-27b drives synaptic transmission by downregulating a repressor of presynaptic genes. We aim to determine if synaptotagmin1 (SYT1) mediates the regulation of synaptic transmission by miR-27b and elucidate the mechanism underlying miR-27b-mediated upregulation of presynaptic genes. For the second aim, we will define the regulatory regions of presynaptic genes that confer upregulation by miR-27b and identify the repressor targeted by miR-27b. The objective of this proposal is to investigate how miR-27b regulates presynaptic function and provide insight into a novel mechanism underlying miRNA-mediated regulation of the presynaptic transcriptome. The proposed research will also further our understanding of how microRNAs function in our brain and may contribute to development of miRNA-based therapy for brain diseases.
kw: microRNA, presynaptic function, synaptic transmission, neurotransmitter release, miR-27b

title: Osteoinductive PEGylated-fibrinogen hydrogel matrix for bone healing after median sternotomy
abs: Open-heart surgery is predominantly performed through a median sternotomy. This procedure provides access to all mediastinal structures and is quick and easy to perform. Despite its advantages, potential sternotomy complications exist, and the method constitutes significant morbidity and mortality. These complications include deep wound dehiscence, instability, nonunion of the sternum and bone or mediastinal infection. The goal of this project is to propose the use of a novel hemostatic and regenerative scaffold consisting of antibiotic and bonemorphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) containing PEGylated fibrinogen hydrogel in conjunction with traditional wire sternal closure. The project will compare the degree of bone healing and regeneration between the use of antibiotic-BMP-2 containing PEGylated fibrinogen hydrogel and bone wax, which is a commonly used hemostatic agent in local hospitals. We hypothesized that augmenting sternal closure with antibiotics and BMP-2 enriched hydrogel will enhance bone healing, regeneration and bone resistance to infection that in turn may accelerate functionalrecovery from cardiac operations and prevent major sternal complications. Midline sternotomy will be performed in rabbit models to evaluate the efficacy of antibiotic-BMP2-loaded PEGylated fibrinogen hydrogel on sternal bone healing. Sternal healing will be assessed by X-ray, histology, peripheral quantitative computerized tomography and mechanical strength testing at 6 weeks post-treatment. The results of this study will set the stage for systematic optimization of PEGylated-fibrinogen hydrogel to accelerate healing and manage contaminated wound sites not only in sternal bone defect but also in bone defect involved in orthopedic surgery, neurosurgery as well as oral and maxillofacial surgery, thus expanding the pool of patients that can benefit from this novel therapeutic treatment.
