title: Singapore YouNg Dementia Cohort Study (SYNC): Clinical, Pathophysiological and Economic Cost Characterization
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Young onset dementia (YOD), defined as onset of dementia before age 65years represents an important component of cognitive disorders. Study of patients with YOD will allow research into pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases as YOD has a strong genetic basis and often represents pure pathology compared to dementia in the elderly wherein genetic predisposition is rare and pathology often mixed in nature. A systematic study of YOD in multiethnic Singapore will be able to identify unique pathophysiological processes among Asians which may be generalized to the entire population of the South Asia due to the close genetic make-up of this population. In this study, we aim to characterize the clinical, cognitive, genetic, neuroimaging and cerebrospinal fluid features of YOD among Asians. The collaboration with the University of California, San Francisco will allow direct comparison between Asian and Caucasian YOD. We will also perform advanced neuroimaging with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and functional MRI (fMRI) that will allow us to better understand the anatomical-functional connectivity patterns involved in YOD. As our previous work has demonstrated a high burden of small vessel cerebrovascular disease (svCVD) among Asians, the DTI and fMRI studies will allow us to elucidate the impact of svCVD on Amyloid and Tau pathology. As we also aim to perform DTI, fMRI and microRNA studies on asymptomatic mutation carriers from offsprings and siblings of patients with familial YOD, we will be able to study the utility of combination biomarkers (Genetic, DTI, fMRI, microRNA) in the prediction of YOD among genetically predisposed individuals. Along with clinical and biomarker studies, we will also collect health economic data from our patients and caregivers. This would be crucial in understanding the cost differences between YOD and late onset dementia and will allow health planners in projecting long-term resource requirements for dementia in general.

title: Ultra-precision Dimensional Metrology using Femtosecond Laser Frequency Combs
abs: The broad objective of the proposed research is to advance the ultrafast photonics technology for ultra-precision dimensional metrology. Precision is a common aspect that governs most of strategically important industries related to Information Technology (IT), Bio-Technology (BT), Nano-Technology (NT) and Space Technology (ST) which occupy a large portion of Singapore’s GDP. In response to ever-growing demands on precision, various light sources have been used to attain sub-wavelength precision in diverse fields of manufacturing and measurement by means of photons. The precision-directed laser photonics will continue to advance to the direction of ultra-precision to achieve better resolutions, larger functional ranges, higher throughputs, and improved stability. However, the light sources available today are limited in the wavelength bandwidth, photon energy, spatial coherence, temporal coherence, and peak power, which consequently hinder breakthroughs toward the realm of ultra-precision. This research is to investigate the novel technological possibilities of ultrafast femtosecond lasers with the aim of establishing the new foundation for ultra-precision dimensional metrology that will enable nano/micro manufacturing over extensive ranges as demanded in the next generation of nano-science as well as bio-technologies, and space technology in the near future.

title: Quantum manipulation of hybrid solid state system
abs: The broad objective of the proposed research is to develop quantum manipulation techniques based on hybrid solid state system, and further study their applications in quantum computation, quantum communication and quantum sensing, which are revolutionarily more powerful and efficient than their classical counterparts. Although various candidate systems have been proposed to implement quantum information processing, no single individual system can meet all the requirements for a large-scale quantum computation. Compared to a single system, a hybrid quantum system can combine the advantages of different sub-systems, and thus holds great promise for the future scalable quantum technologies. Especially, compared to atoms and photons, solid-state implementation of quantum system is promising for a scalable architecture, just like that the invention of the classical transistor leads to the integration circuits in the conventional computer processors. This project will study quantum manipulation of hybrid solid state systems, and try to make breakthroughs in quantum manipulation techniques based on silicon carbide (SiC) defect electron spins, nuclear spins, natural atoms and photons. The key contents we want to study include: (1) On-chip hybrid quantum network with electrons, nuclear spins, and wave-guided photons; (2) The interface between semiconductor quantum dot and natural atomic systems; (3) Quantum interface between SiC defect electron spins and optomechanical resonators. The research lies in the intersection of quantum physics, information theory, engineering technology and material science. The result of the proposal will not only provide powerful research techniques for studying fundamental quantum physics, but also lead to the future practical quantum technology.

title: Mechanisms of epigenetic reprogramming and its implications in complex human diseases
inst: IMCB - Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology
abs: The objective of this proposal is to understand the fine prints of epigenetic reprogramming, their dynamics and complexity during development and their relevance to human health and disease. Epigenetic gene regulation is with increasing incidence identified as cause for developmental deficiencies, syndromes and cancers. The epigenome is most vulnerable during the pre-implantation period of embryogenesis, where extensive epigenetic reprogramming prepares the embryonic genome for the developmental tasks ahead. Consequently, disruptions during this process can have detrimental effects and a number of syndromes caused by epimutations at e.g. imprinted gene regions are described in humans. In addition, a large proportion of unexplained complex syndromes, tumors, molar pregnancies, premature pregnancy terminations and both male and female infertility might be caused by epimutations occurring in or affecting the early embryo. However, the complexity of epigenetic defects (epimutations), often having pleiotropic, genome-wide consequences frequently obscure disease relevant targets and pathways. The mechanisms acting during epigenetic reprogramming and ensuring the faithful removal of a subset of epigenetic marks and the maintenance of others are poorly understood. I have recently uncovered a protein, TRIM28, to be essential for proper embryonic epigenetic reprogramming. TRIM28 mediates the interaction of epigenetic modifier enzymes with transcription factors of the KRAB-ZFP family, to instate or maintain localized epigenetic states. The KRAB-ZFP family comprises over 400 members, over 30 of which are expressed throughout early preimplantation embryogenesis. Based on my work and current knowledge, I suggest that each KRAB-ZFP protein mediates targeting of TRIM28 and the epigenetic modifier enzymes to specific genomic loci during epigenetic reprogramming. I propose to decipher this complex network, its players and targets using combinatorial approaches of conventional genetic and biochemical methods with novel single-cell epigenomics. My work will give substantial insights into the mechanisms of epigenetic reprogramming and its implication in complex human diseases and syndromes.

title: Transcriptome analysis to gain a better insight in the pathogenesis of dengue virus and assessing serotype-specific differences.
abs: Dengue is the most prevalent mosquito-borne viral infection worldwide and recent reports suggest that the global diseases burden is much higher than previous estimates by the WHO. There are no approved antiviral therapies or safe vaccines available at present to treat or prevent dengue disease. Therefore there is an urgent need for clinical development of safe and efficacious antivirals. We propose to use a combination of genomic and proteomic analysis and interactome studies to build a profile of the dynamic changes in the level of regulatory proteins in DENV infected cells and compare the differences between the serotyps. This analysis will identify molecular pathways that can be assessed for their relevance to pan-DENV protein function, replication and changes in host cell function. Initially we will focus our investigations on the UPR, an essential cellular response which is known to be induced in DENV infection, both in vivo and in vitro. The strength of this proposal is that preliminary data is available in the PIs laboratory to support and they bring to the table important tools and valuable DENV research experience to address the contribution of the viral genome to disease severity, using both model systems and clinical isolates. We anticipate that the studies will generate results that can be readily translated to benefit patients as the knowledge may be useful for the development of intervention strategies or diagnostics that are currently not available, but urgently required. The specific aims of this project are:1.Elucidate the growth characteristics of DENV 1-4 clinical isolates (3/serotype) and test against a panel of DENV inhibitors. 2. Analyse the transcriptome of the three genotypes of DENV2 and selected DENV 1,3 & 4. to identify differentially regulated genes. 3.Validate selected human genes which have the potential to be broad acting pan-flaviviral targets.

title: Validation of a Novel Micro-fluid Cytokine Analysis Platform for aqueous and vitreous humour in normal and eyes with Diabetic Retinopathy
abs: To validate the use of a novel micro-fluid cytokine analysis system (Ayoxxa System, Ayoxxa Biosystems, Köln, Germany) for the measurements of angiogenic cytokine concentrations from minute quanitites of aqueous and vitreous samples of normal and eyes with diabetic retinopathy. The secondary aim of this study is to derive a protocol for handling and sampling of vitreous samples for cytokine analysis.Hypothesis: The Ayoxxa System is comparable to other methods of cytokine analysis systems such as the Bioplex System and standard ELISA immunoassay systems.Methodology: Samples from aqueous and vitreous humour obtained during either 1) routine cataract surgery and/or vitrectomy for non-diabetic retinopathy/systemic diabetic patients and 2) cataract surgery/or vitrectomy for diabetic retinopathy without vitreous hemorrhage are compared between the Ayoxxa System and BioPlex system (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc., Hercules, CA) and standard ELISA immunoassay. Assessment of agreement between each test as well as spike and recovery and linearity-of-dilution experiments will be performed for validation of the Ayoxxa system.Conclusion: With the validation the Ayoxxa System, micro quantities of aqueous and vitreous humour can be used to detect cytokine concentrations which can impact the diagnosis, monitoring and treatment of angiogenic retinal diseases.

title: Efficacy of bispecific crossmab antibodies in model of laser induced CNV in NHP
abs: Age related macular degeneration (AMD) is a chronic, progressive and degenerative eye disease affecting the macula of the eye, where our sharpest central vision occurs. It has become the major cause of blindness in the elderly, in both developed and developing countries. There are two forms of AMD: wet (neovascular or exudative) and dry. Wet AMD causes the highest percentage of central vision loss secondary to disease. This neovascular form involves formation of new blood vessels under the retina, known as choroidal neovascularization (CNV). Indeed, the clinical development of anti-VEGF therapies represent a major advance in the treatment of wet AMD. Although patient quality of life has been improved significantly, repeated intraocular anti-VEGF injections are required to preserve a patient's vision and also resistance to existing anti-VEGF therapies does occur. Therefore, further advances in this field are necessary including finding alternative target to overcome resistance and developing/validating new agents intend to enhance efficacy. Our recent preclinical data in rats have shown that simultaneous inhibition of Ang2 and VEGF show superiority compared to anti-VEGF monotherapy in CNV. Based on the results of the ongoing laser-induced CNV model in rats, we are proposing a translational proof of concept study of the selected compounds in non-human primates since NHP model is better predictive of human response.

title: A prospective study on the safety and efficacy of the Automated Wearable Artificial Kidney Peritoneal Dialysis (AWAK PD) in the treatment of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients (Phase 01)
abs: Current work on wearable artificial kidneys is mostly based on hemodialysis or hemofiltration, either of which requires blood flow through an extracorporeal circulation. This calls for anticoagulation and stringent monitoring and is encumbered with possible immunologic and non-immunologic complications secondary to blood–artificial membrane interactions. A peritoneal-based automated wearable artificial kidney (AWAK PD) requires no blood exchange. By continuous regeneration and reuse of spent peritoneal dialysate in perpetuity via sorbent technology, the need for purchasing fresh dialysate is also eliminated.AWAK PD works by draining uremic-toxin-laden peritoneal dialysate from the subject, removing contained toxins using sorbents, and returning the regenerated dialysate back to the subject. An integrated infusion system reconstitutes the calcium and magnesium concentrations to the desired levels and adds glucose to compensate for the dilution and absorption of glucose by the subject. The continuous recirculation of dialysate provides the patient a continuous TPD treatment with up to 42L of fresh dialysate per day. This high turn-over rate produces steady conditions for dialysis and fluid removal throughout the treatment and yields a physiological dialysate, which is well equilibrated with the patient.This single-centre pilot study adopts a prospective single-arm study design. It aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of AWAK PD in the treatment of ESRD subjects requiring dialysis. It is hypothesized that AWAK PD is safe and equally efficient or better than conventional CAPD. The study is divided into two phases. For Phase 01, 15 subjects will be enrolled. The

title: Impact of hearing loss on significant other and intervention through hearing aids
abs: Research Project Title: Impact of hearing loss on significant others and intervention through hearing aidsAbstract:Objective:Hearing loss is one of the most disabling conditions among elderly. It has negative impact on not only on one’s health and wellbeing, but also affect quality of life of their significant others. Negative impact of hearing loss on significant others of hearing impaired individual is also known a third party disability. We sought to i) determine third party disability in significant others of people with hearing loss, ii) determine effect of hearing aid in reducing third party hearing disability in significant others.Study Design:Prospective pre and post studyStudy population:Elderly who are diagnosed with hearing loss and their significant othersMethodology: This study will be incorporated into a community based mobile hearing clinic project in Singapore. In the mobile hearing clinic, elderly will be fitted with hearing aid and receive aural rehabilitation services that mimic the routine care of audiology clinic in tertiary hospital. We will study the effect of hearing aid and aural rehabilitation in reducing the self-perceived hearing handicap in people with hearing loss and third party disability in significant others using the Hearing Handicap Inventory for the Elderly (HHIE) and Significant Other Scale for Hearing Disability (SOS-HEAR) questionnaire. Outcome measurement will be performed at pre hearing aid fitting, 3 months and 6 months post hearing aid fitting. Statistical Analysis:ANOVA test will be used to compare the difference of SOS-HEAR score among pre hearing aid fitting, 3 months and 6 months post hearing aid fitting.Key words:Hearing loss, hearing aid, third party disability, elderly, significant others

title: Home is where I would like to be: A multi-method study aiming to increase the number of
abs: This project aims to answer the question of how to increase the number of home deaths among those who wish to die at home and, in doing so, to strengthen existing evidence on the impact of community-based approaches implemented in actual healthcare settings in Singapore and abroad. The 3-year project will explore multiple perspectives ranging from patients to health policymakers using a variety of methodologies. The outcomes of this project will be used to for informing health policy in the planning of end-of-life care in rapidly ageing societies. Currently, it is not well understood what are the levers that can support respecting and honouring the wish for home death. Quantitative and qualitative methodologies will be used. Qualitative methodologies include expert opinion elicitation methods and semi-structured interviews or focus groups. A systematic review of published literature will also be conducted to identify, appraise, select and synthesize high quality research evidence on the effectiveness of different mechanisms used for the financing, organisation and delivery of end-of-life care. Quantitative methodologies include the exploration of different statistical methods to address study attrition due to death and illness in the analysis of economic burden to clarify the uncertainty in literature regarding the statistical method to be used to address the challenge of censored data. A modeling exercise will be conducted to map out the end-of-life care system in Singapore. A synthesis of the data gathered using the aforementioned methodologies will be conducted and will be used in model to simulate the cost and volume impact on providers at various levels of care depending on the model of end-of-life care explored.

title: Analysing the immune contexture of primary and corresponding metastasis from Gastric cancer patients
abs: In order to aid the development of novel anti-cancer therapeutic tools and improve treatment outcomes, one must comprehensively understand the nature of tumor immune infiltration both with respect to the types of immune cells present, their number, their synergistic or opposing effects with the tumor cells and their qualitative characteristics as correlate to invasion, disease progression and prognosis. In a series of seminal publications, Galon et al. have demonstrated that the measurement of the immune infiltrating population density and their functional capacity at tumor sites may be considered a prognostic and possibly predictive biomarker that can complement conventional TNM staging and may allow predicting response to therapy. The collaboration aims to leverage on the expertise of NUHS and pRED to gain a better understanding of gastric cancer tumor microenvironment. It seeks to explore the immune contexture of clinically annotated GC samples utilizing advanced IHC methods generated by Roche. It is expected that the quantity and quality of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes identified by capturing nests of infiltrates will aid the development of gastric cancer vaccine program being considered for collaboration with Singapore.

title: Using multimodal brain imaging to identify the brain substrate underlying language dependent IBS symptom reporting between Chinese & Caucasians and between two Chinese populations, speaking Mandarin and English.
abs: Using multimodal brain imaging to identify the brain substrate underlying language dependent IBS symptom reporting between Chinese & Caucasians and between two Chinese populations, speaking Mandarin and English.BackgroundIn the absence of generally agreed upon biomarkers, functional GI disorders such as IBS and FD and related subgroups are currently defined and classified by symptom criteria which were originally developed in English and translated into other Western languages. In Asia there are major language and cultural differences that could have significant impact on the validity of the current Rome classification system. In this proposal, we aim to test the general hypothesis that while FGID symptoms are generated by neurobiological mechanisms shared by Asian and Western patients, the verbal expression of these central representations of abdominal discomfort and the cultural responses to these symptoms show significant culture and language dependent differencesAims & Hypothesis1)Chinese IBS subjects, regardless of primary language will show similar brain signatures as Caucasian IBS subjects.2)Verbal expression of symptoms differs between Mandarin speaking Chinese and English speaking Chinese3)Non verbal symptom assessment scale will show better correlation than verbal expression MethodsWe will use advanced brain imaging techniques to characterize brain signatures in two Chinese populations residing in different cultural contexts and speaking different languages, and compare them to brain signatures from an existing brain image database of age and sex matched Caucasian subjects.Methods from the emerging field of neuroanthropology, which provides concrete methodological recommendations for correlating neuroscience findings with personal narratives, will be used to relate our findings in Aims A and B. By studying 60 Chinese female IBS subjects (30 speaking Mandarin, 30 speaking English as primary language)ImpactIt is expected that the proposed studies will confirm the universality of biological mechanisms involved in the generation of FGID symptoms, but that the language and culture specific differences in symptom expression will require modification of current symptom-based classification.

title: Phase I study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of ASLAN001 in combination with Oxaliplatin and Capecitabine
abs: The HER family of tyrosine kinase receptors (HER1-4) are frequently dysregulated in tumours. This is associated with tumour proliferation, survival, invasion and resistance to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and may portend a worse prognosis. Targeting the HER receptors is now the standard of care for molecularly selected gastric, breast and lung cancers.ASLAN001 (previously ARRY-33543) is a potent balanced tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) of HER-1, 2 and 4. Compared to the dual EGFR and HER2 TKIs afatinib and lapatinib, ASLAN001 exhibits reversible inhibition and greater potency for EGFR and/or HER2 in cell lines. In rodent xenograft models, ASLAN001 has single agent activity and is additive or synergistic when combined with chemotherapy agents. Phase I studies of ASLAN001 alone and combined with chemotherapy have also shown good tolerability. Capecitabine and oxaliplatin (CAPOX) is used in gastric, colorectal cancers and pancreaticobiliary cancers. Targeting EGFR or HER2 in these cancers have been shown to improve efficacy compared to chemotherapy alone. We therefore hypothesize that addition of ASLAN001 may increase the effectiveness of CAPOX in EGFR and/or HER2-dysregulated tumours. We propose a Phase I, open-label, dose escalation study of ASLAN001 in combination with CAPOX, in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. The primary objective is to determine the maximal tolerated dose of ASLAN001 in combination with CAPOX using a modified 3+3 dose-escalation design in 12-18 patients. This will help select the dose for a randomised Phase II study in metastatic EGFR/HER2 dysregulated gastric cancer and evaluation in other solid tumours. The secondary objective is to evaluate the efficacy and the pharmacokinetics of ASLAN001 for this combination. Exploratory objectives are to determine the biological effective doses through pharmacodynamic effects in blood and tumour biopsies, as well as to evaluate for predictive biomarkers. Furthermore, potential resistance mechanisms in HER2 or EGFR dysregulated tumours will be examined.

title: Evaluation of the use of a non-invasive 3D ultrasound Clarity system in real-time tracking of the target volume in prostate RapidArc therapy
abs: Aims/HypothesesUse of pre-treatment Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) images does not provide real-time information on the position of the prostate during treatment. This study aims to evaluate the capability of a 3D ultrasound Clarity® system in providing real-time information of the prostate movement during the treatment delivery. This would provide a basis to review the adequacy of the planning margins employed through the continuous real-time tracking of the prostate throughout the course of the treatment. The study hypothesize that the prescribed planning margin is not sufficient to account for the target motion. Methodology/Approach of the research proposalA total of 40 unselected consecutive patients would be recruited prospectively. The approach of this proposal uses a non-invasive 3D ultrasound imaging technique for soft tissue visualization (i.e prostate). Eligible participants would be required to be position in a semi-lithotomy position to allow transperineal ultrasound scan to take place during the treatment. Consequently, the patient would be required to remain in this position from CT to treatment stage. Clinical target volume (CTV) would be delineated on the Clarity® system to allow analysis of the centroid displacement with reference to the planning target volume (PTV) from the planning CT. Threshold on the Clarity® system would be user-defined based on the planning margin used. If the CTV exceeds the threshold of the PTV boundaries, this would signify that the target volume has deviated from the intended position. In the event of gross tumour motion, the radiation oncologist would be promptly informed to consider the need to review the given planning margin.
kw: Real-time tumour tracking, imaging, 3D Clarity system, Prostate radiotherapy

title: Novel Metabolomics Markers for Characterization and Early Detection of Malignancy in Pancreatic Cysts
abs: Background:Pancreatic cysts can transform into pancreatic cancer. They have better survival than ductal pancreatic cancer as they are detected earlier and provide opportunity for early resection. Currently cyst characterization based on imaging and fluid analysis is inaccurate as 40% of cysts undergoing surgery are benign. New technology like metabolomics may help differentiate malignant from benign pancreatic cysts. It may also help detect malignant change in premalignant cysts. Pilot data on 16 cyst fluid samples (4 malignant, 4 premalignant and 8 benign) identified 4 unknown metabolites present in high amounts in the malignant cyst but absent or significantly lower in the benign cysts. Premalignant samples showed much lower amounts of these metabolites possibly implying that it could be a potential biomarker for a malignant transformation in process.Aim:1.To confirm whether selected differentially expressed metabolites found in our pilot study are present exclusively or are significantly more in a larger sample of malignant cysts.2.To quantitatively assess whether these metabolites can predict when premalignant cyst transform into cancer.Methods:Prospective study of 100 patients undergoing endoscopic ultrasound fine needle aspiration or surgery will have their cyst fluid sent for metabolomics using LC-MS with identification of key differential metabolites using statistical tools. Levels of metabolites will be correlated to clinical diagnosis based on surgical histology or supportive imaging and standard fluidic analysis.Significance:Studied metabolites are expected to be present exclusively or significantly higher amounts in malignant cysts and with increasing amounts in premalignant cyst. Future studies can then be done to determine on need for surgery or timing of surgery based on the presence and quantity of this metabolite in the pancreatic cyst. If successful, this study can potentially lead to a new generation of novel markers for cancer risk stratification and guiding of therapy for pancreatic cysts.
kw: pancreatic cysts, pancreatic cancer, metabolomics

title: Defining circulating microRNA biomarkers for the early diagnosis and prognosis of sepsis
abs: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. However, current clinical and laboratory indicators for early diagnosis of sepsis are limited and non-specific. Presently available biomarkers are detected late in the inflammatory process when considerable damage to organs has already occurred. This contributes to delayed recognition and initiation of timely clinical interventions that could prevent severe organ damage and death. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional master regulators of the human genome linked to immune responses in various diseases. Emerging evidence suggests circulating miRNAs to be valuable diagnostic biomarkers. We postulate that the development of panels of miRNAs as sepsis-specific biomarkers will be a promising strategy for the early and accurate diagnosis of sepsis before its overt clinical manifestation. The objectives are to:1.derive and validate a panel of miRNAs that are consistently differentially expressed in the plasma of patients with and without sepsis2.investigate the prognostic and predictive values of the panel of miRNAs to guide treatment 3.investigate the roles of these differentially-expressed circulating miRNAs in immune modulation during sepsisThe methodology involves sampling of blood from controls and subjects in the sepsis continuum at their earliest presentation in the emergency department longitudinally to hospitalisation. We will develop panels of miRNAs that are specific to early and late stages of sepsis, and correlate clinical, biochemical and microbiological outcomes with these miRNAs. Our

title: Discovery of Biomarkers for Intrinsic Radiation Sensitivity in Asian Patients with Late Normal Tissue Toxicities following Radiotherapy
abs: Radiotherapy features prominently in the primary treatment of human cancers. In most tumour types, a positive dose-response relationship is demonstrated for local control. Nonetheless, the onset of permanent late normal tissue adverse effects following radiotherapy limits the ability to intensify radiotherapy doses. It is estimated that 20% of patients develop radiation-induced chronic toxicities over their lifetimes. Although algorithms for late adverse events based on clinical variables are becoming available, biomarkers of tissue radiosensitivity are desperately needed in order to improve outcomes further. The proposed work is intended to investigate if biomarkers of radiation exposure predict for late toxicities in patients with cancer of the nasopharynx and prostate. Cellular responses such as DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair, induction of apoptosis, and chromosomal radiosensitivity measured in ex vivo irradiated blood lymphocytes of radiotherapy patients have been tested in clinical studies as predictive markers of late toxicities following radiation exposure. Specifically in breast, head and neck, and prostate radiotherapy patients, these markers have demonstrated good levels of association between cellular and clinical phenotypes. In these studies, impaired DSB repair and apoptosis induction correlated with clinical radiosensitivity. Despite the successes of small case-control studies reporting positive associations between cellular and clinical phenotypes, a common argument against the clinical implementation of these cell-based assays relates to the lack of large-scale prospective validation. Hence, an integral component of this project involves correlating the above mentioned cellular parameters with late normal tissue outcomes in nasopharyngeal carcinoma and prostate cancer patients, who are currently being prospectively monitored in two clinical trials. The biomarkers will be tested in ex vivo irradiated blood lymphocytes of these individuals. The hypothesis under test is surrogates of cellular radiation sensitivity predict for individual risk of late normal tissue adverse effects following head and neck and pelvic radiotherapy.

title: Prospective trial to investigate the burden of anti-platelet resistance in ischemic stroke patients and correlation with one year stroke outcomes incorporating a novel Multiplate aggregation assay
abs: Stroke patients are at high risk of developing further vascular events. Despite compelling preclinical and clinical data linking anti-platelet resistance and poor outcomes, few studies have linked the laboratory documentation of antiplatelet resistance and long-term clinical events in stroke patients. Previous studies were limited by a small sample size, lack of serial determination using accurate platelet assays and correlation with the clinical consequences of antiplatelet resistance among Asians.We hypothesize that markers of platelet reactivity are elevated in patients following stroke onset and that changes in these markers following antiplatelet therapy predict recurrent vascular events. The specific aims of the study are to investigate the relationships between the biochemical assessment of platelet reactivity using the Multiplate aggregation assay (Roche) and one-year recurrent vascular events in ischemic stroke patients. In a preliminary study, we have demonstrated the feasibility of performing these measurements in our stroke patients and made early observations on the extent of antiplatelet resistance in stroke patients using this biochemical platform. This proposal, which incorporates a rigorous study design and the Multiplate aggregation assay, will be the first study to prospectively evaluate the association between platelet reactivity in ischemic stroke patients and long-term outcome determined a year following stroke onset in an Asian population. Results from this study will allow us to better understand stroke diversity, identify differences between patients, identify the best drug targets, improve the quality and efficiency of the design of clinical studies and aid in the development of biomarkers and diagnostic tests.
kw: Stroke, antiplatelet, platelet resistance, vascular events

title: Genomic, Functional and Therapeutic Studies of Chromatin Enzymes in Asian Cancer
abs: For the renewal of my STaR award, will focus on 2 interrelated areas: Genomics of Asian Cancer and Chromatin Biology. We have been productive in our cancer genomics studies in the last 4 years (66 papers with 2 in Nature, 3 Nature Genetics, 1 Cancer Discovery, 1 Science Translational Medicine). One common finding that emerges from our genomic profiling is the frequent mutation of chromatin enzymes in different cancer types.Hypothesis: Chromatin enzymes play an important role in tumorigenesis by regulating gene expression of key tumorigenic pathways and altering epi-genomic environment. Epigenetic drugs may provide novel cancer treatment or synergistic effects to standard cancer therapy. Specific Aims:1) To generate high-quality genomic and epigenomic data by high-throughput profiling. 2) To analyze and correlate clinic-pathological data including drug response. 3) To establish an integrated program to study the roles of chromatin enzymes in tumorigenesis: a) knock-down, overexpression and synthetic lethality studies of the targeted CE and resultant biochemical and phenotypic changes; b) Chip-sequencing and RNA-sequencing to identify CE-regulated genes; c) confirmation of the biological effects of CE-regulated genes in cancer; d) structural studies of the targeted CE and e) testing and mechanism studies of novel CE drugs. High-throughput approaches including whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, chip-sequencing, methylation and histone mark profiling will be performed on both tumor samples and cell lines. RNAi and synthetic lethality screening using the shRNA or CRISPER technology will be performed. Protein cloning by Escherichia Coli and crystallography followed by X-ray diffraction studies will be employed to study functional domains of CE. Finally, we will collaborate with pharmaceuticals/biotechs on testing novel CE drugs and studying their related mechanisms. Our studies will shed light on the roles of CE in cancer, translate discoveries into clinical applications, and find effective CE drugs for Asian cancers as a single or combined therapy.
kw: Cancer genomics, chromatin enzymes, Asian cancer

title: FAP PET Radiotracer for Imaging of Liver Fibrosis
abs: Fibrosis is an important pathophysiological process seen in many diseases including liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, atherosclerosis, Crohn’s disease, cancer and renal failure. There is a need to image fibrosis and to use imaging as a biomarker to assess disease status and efficacy of therapy. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) has been developed by Roche as a potential agent with specificity for collagen type I fibres and gelatin. Labeled with PET tracers, FAP has the potential to serve as a imaging biomarker. Autotaxins have been shown to be active in liver fibrosis. The industry partner has a potential drug candidate that acts as an autotaxin inhibitor. FAP could potentially serve as a companion imaging biomarker for the drug candidate. The project aims to prepare a small library and optimize a FAP inhibitor tracer for PET imaging and to determine the efficiency of binding to a thioacetamide (TAA) mouse model of liver fibrosis. ATX inhibitor/ murine liver fibrosis model will be used to demonstrate sensitivity of the radiotracer to drug treatment. In vivo PET imaging in TAA mice as proof of concept experiment with FAP radiotracer as an imaging biomarker of fibrosis which can potentially serve as a companion biomarker for the ATX inhibitor drug candidate.

title: Relationship of haptoglobin phenotype to vascular changes and response to Vitamin E supplementation in patients with Diabetes Mellitus Type 2: The EVAS trial
abs: Specific Aims:The phenotype haptoglobin 2-2 (Hp 2-2) is associated with higher oxidative stress, inflammation, LDL peroxidation and higher cardiovascular risk in patients with diabetes. We aim to determine whether Hp 2-2 phenotype is associated with surrogate markers of cardiovascular risk, inflammation, lipids and lipoprotein profile, oxidative stress, and endothelial cell (EC) apoptosis (in vitro study) in patients with diabetes in our population and whether vitamin E supplementation mitigates this risk.Methods:Screening Phase:We will recruit 300 patients with diabetes mellitus type 2 (100 Chinese, 100 Malays and 100 Indians) and assess their Hp phenotype, surrogate markers of cardiovascular risk, inflammation, vascular biomarkers and lipids phenotype.In vitro Study: Serum from 20 patients with Hp 2-2 phenotype and 20 patients with non Hp 2-2 phenotype will be studied in vitro using a haemodynamic lab-on-chip system to determine whether there is a difference in EC apoptosis between the two groups. Subsequently, we will add vitamin E at varying concentrations, to each serum sample and measure EC apoptosis to evaluate improvements by vitamin E concentrations both within and between the Hp 2-2 phenotype and non Hp 2-2 phenotype patient samples.Randomisation Phase:200 patients will be recruited to a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT), stratified by Hp 2-2 phenotype status (100 Hp 2-2 and 100 non-Hp 2-2), and randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either vitamin E 400 IU supplementation daily for 6 months or a placebo group. The trial will determine whether vitamin E improves the aforementioned surrogate markers in the Hp phenotype strata.Importance of proposed research to science and medicine:This study allows us to understand the possible mechanism of cardiovascular risk in patients with Hp 2-2 phenotype and to see whether vitamin E supplementation reduces this risk in a pharmacogenomic targeted manner.

title: MRI-TRUS fusion biopsy and cell cycle proliferation signature assessment: A novel approach to active surveillance in prostate cancer
abs: Prostate Cancer is the most incident cancer in the US and the 3rd most incident cancer in Singapore males. The widespread availability of PSA screening has resulted in a stage migration with majority of cancers being detected at an early stage and a large proportion of these are indolent cancers. While it is recognized that most low-risk cancers are indolent, a proportion of intermediate risk, and all high risk cancers are likely to be aggressive and will cause significant morbidity and mortality. The risk stratification system today (serum PSA level, biopsy Gleason score and clinical stage) is heavily dependent on systematic, non-targeted prostate biopsies, hampered by sampling error and pathologic inter-reader variability. We aim to improve prostate cancer risk stratification with imaging, imaging guided biopsy, and genetic profiling of men with low- and intermediate-risk prostate cancer. We hypothesize that this comprehensive approach to will identify men at high risk (more than 10% difference) of active surveillance failure within 1 year. Men with low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer will be subjected to a confirmatory MRI-fusion biopsy and 3D transperineal mapping biopsy of the prostate and all tissues will be sent for genetic testing of cell cycle proliferation (CCP) markers. These will be used to stratify men to groups at low (estimated 5%) or high (estimated >15%) risk of active surveillance failure by the end of 1 year. Planned recruitment is 280 men with PSA testing at 6 months and repeat biopsy at 1 year. The role of MRI fusion biopsy and CCP markers will be evaluated against traditional metrics in a multivariate model.The study of this novel approach to active surveillance of men with prostate cancer will help to identify men who may be managed conservatively, and identify early on, men who would benefit from radical intervention.

title: Customizable circulating tumor nucleic acid assays to monitor disease burden, detect known drug resistance mutations and identify novel drug resistance mutations in patients with metastatic gastrointestinal cancers.
abs: Treatment monitoring is constantly required in metastatic cancers to enable treatment decisions based on each patient's evolving clinical course. In Clinical practice, tumor markers are routinely used as an adjunct to CT scans as non-invasive tests to monitor patients. 30% of metastatic Colorectal Cancer (mCRC) do not express tumor markers and there are no tumor markers in metastatic Gastrointestinal Tumors (mGIST). Beyond treatment monitoring, there is no routinely available clinical test to pinpoint the mechanisms of drug resistance and inform choice of subsequent therapy. Cancers constantly release cell-free nucleic acids into the blood. We hypothesize that genetic alterations can be qualitatively and quantitatively assayed from serial plasma samples to characterize the dynamic evolution of disease biology with time and treatment in each patient. We propose to develop clinically implementable circulating tumor nucleic acid (ctNAs) assays to monitor disease burden, detect emergence of known drug resistant mutations and identify novel drug resistance mutations in patients with tumor marker-negative mCRC and mGIST. We have developed expertise in (1) targeted high depth next generation sequencing of tumor tissues, (2) multiplex amplicon-sequencing to genotype and measure ctNAs, with a lower limit of detection of variant allele-frequency of 0.2% across 20 amplicons using 10ng of cfDNA and (3) plasma exome sequencing from 20ng of cfDNA. To monitor patients, we will identify somatic mutations in each patient's tumor specimen and measure the abundance of these mutations in each patient’s serial plasma samples. We will determine the sensitivity and negative predictive value of serial ctNAs in monitoring for worsening disease. We will also determine if known acquired drug resistance mutations are detectable in patients with worsening disease and evaluate the temporal dynamics of these mutations in serial samples. Amongst patients with unexplained drug resistance, we will perform plasma exome sequencing to identify novel mechanisms of drug resistance.

title: Evaluation of the synergistic cytotoxicity of busulphan, melphalan, gemcitabine, SAHA and decitabine in lymphoma cell lines.
abs: Aim: To evaluate the synergistic cytotoxicity of busulphan, melphalan, gemcitabine, SAHA and decitabine in lymphoma cell lines. Hypothesis: Combining nucleoside analogues, DNA alkylators, histone deacetylase inhibitors and hypomethylating agents would synergistically enhance the cytotoxic effect in lymphoma and therefore would be more efficacious as a preconditioning regime prior to haematologic stem cell transplant. Methodology: J45 (T-lymphoma) and Daudi (B-lymphoma) cells will be cultured and exposed to cytotoxic agents at different combinations of the drugs, and at varying concentrations. The cytotoxic effect would be determined by the MTT and Annexin V assays. Mechanisms of cell death will be assessed by Western blot analysis; cleavage of poly ADP ribose polymerase-1 and caspase 3, status of histone modifications and leakage of pro-apoptotic proteins from mitochondria will be determined. Changes in the mitochondrial membrane potential will be assessed by flow cytometry. Global DNA methylation will be assessed using immunofluorescence staining with anti-5-methylcytidine antibody.

title: Adaptive Radiotherapy Planning for Local-Regionally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma - A Dosimetric Comparison amongst Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy, RapidArc, Helical Tomotherapy and Intensity-Modulated Proton Therapy
abs: Due to the complex anatomy of the nasopharyngeal region, the demand for high doses to the target volume and the sparing of nearby critical neural structures are especially crucial for advanced NPC treatment. Highly conformal radiotherapy techniques like Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy, Volume Modulation Arc Therapy, and Helical Tomotherapy are available for clinical treatment at National Cancer Center Singapore (NCCS), and the new Proton facility expected to be ready by year 2018, multiple radiotherapy options will be available to treat NPC patients at NCCS. Many studies have shown that patient’s anatomy can expect numerous changes throughout course of treatment, and these changes are expected more on local-regionally advanced NPC patients going through concurrent chemo-RT with radical treatment dose. Generally, both primary and nodal volume will reduce, and patients usually lose weight. Organs at risk (OARs) might be displaced into the treatment volume creating unintentional and unnecessary toxicities. Thus, adaptive radiotherapy (ART) is recommended. However, there is no standard strategy for ART with different radiotherapy techniques yet. 5 patients will be selected for this study, 3 sets of CT simulation images will be obtained at pre-RT, weeks 3 and 5 during radiotherapy. Patients will receive standard clinical radiotherapy with weekly Cone-Beam CT as prescribed by Radiation Oncologist. IMRT, RA, HT and IMPT will be planned on each set of CT simulation data with treatment planning system for computer-based dosimetric study. A total of 100 plans will be evaluated on tumor, OARs anatomy and dose change. Optimum time interval for adaptive planning of 4 different planning techniques on local-regionally advanced NPC will be determined. Finally, an adaptive strategy for advanced NPC radiotherapy treatment at NCC will be proposed after the study. The optimum planning techniques for advanced NPC in terms of planning and treatment efficiency and cost effectiveness at NCCS will be evaluated.

title: Space Based Quantum Key Distribution
abs: In this proposal, we will demonstrate several key pieces of technology necessary for a cost-effective space-based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) network that can span the globe. We will develop the apparatus for operating ultra-bright entangled photon sources in space and the corresponding communication protocols enabling efficient QKD to take place in the space environment. With satellite-based sources we may imagine scenarios where entangled photon-pairs are beamed from Low Earth Orbit to ground, enabling distant ground receivers to share quantum correlations for QKD. Satellite-to-satellite QKD is also possible. We will use our expertise in building entangled photon systems to build a compact and ultra-bright source of photon-pairs based on Spontaneous Parametric Downconversion. We aim for these next-generation sources to be space-qualified and to have sufficient brightness for satellite-to-satellite or satellite-to-ground communication. Brightness will be boosted by incorporating collection optics while minimizing form-factor changes to an existing design. Fundamental physics research also benefits directly from the proposed program. Satellite-based entangled photon sources can enable very long range tests of the distance limit of entanglement (e.g. using two widely separated satellites). Another research objective is to uncover any sources of noise affecting the viability of space-based entangled photon correlations. One key plank of our proposal is the development of theoretical tools to evaluate this likelihood, and to check if there is a need to update existing QKD protocols. A number of other technological objectives are expected to have spill-over effects for Earth-based applications. We aim to demonstrate a compact source that is ready for deployment on commercial optical fiber networks. We also anticipate that the improved single photon technology (sources and detectors) can carry over to a number of low-light applications.

title: Further Studies on Celgosivir: Combinations and Mechanism of Action Studies
abs: Dengue is the most prevalent mosquito-borne viral infection worldwide and recent reports suggest that the global diseases burden is much higher than previous estimates by the World Health Organization. There are no approved antiviral therapies or safe vaccines available at present to treat or prevent dengue disease. Therefore there is an urgent need for clinical development of safe and efficacious antivirals. This collaborative research with 60 degrees Pharmaceutical PLC will evaluate Celgosivir and Modipafant in a preclinical setting to determine if a combination of the two drugs will be a viable therapeutic against dengue diseases. Celgosivir or Bu-Cast is a 6-O butanoyl prodrug of castanospermine, a naturally occurring iminosugar derived from the seeds of Castanospermum australe. It exerts antiviral activity by inhibiting the ER-resident alpha-glucosidase I enzyme which together with alpha-glucosidase II is required for the trimming of three terminal glucose residues attached to N-glycans of newly syntheiszed glycoproteins including viral glycoproteins E, prM and NS1 that are essential for virus life cycle. Modipafant is a platelet activating factor receptor (PAFR) antagonist. PAFR plays an important physiological role in endothelial cell permeability and platelet aggregation. PAFR (-/-) knockout mice exposed to dengue 2 exhibited reduced hemoconcentration, thrombocytopenia, and pain relative to infected wild-type mice, suggesting that PAFR has an important role in mediation of the severe manifestations of dengue. In this project we will:1.Investigate prophylactic efficacy of celgosivir in mice.2.Investigate efficacy of delayed celgosivir dosing over three days BID. 3.Identify an effective dose of celgosivir administered via a six hourly regimen.4.Investigate the efficacy of a combination of celgosivir with modipafant, for various dosing regimens.5.Perform phamacokinetic modeling for drug combinations.6.Conduct proteomic and transcriptomic studies to pin-point the mechanism of action of the combination therapy.

title: Study of Wnt-inhibitors and Sorafenib in three HCC PDX models
abs: Hepatocellular cancer (HCC) is the fifth most common malignancy worldwide with 660,000 deaths annually. HCC is highly dependent on angiogenesis for growth and metastasis. Recently, sorafenib has been shown to produce a 3-month gain in survival of patients with advanced HCC. Because of the improvement of sorafenib is marginal and many patients eventually turn out to be refractory to this therapy, new agents and novel therapeutic strategies are urgently needed to prolong life expectancy of patients with advanced HCC. In this proposal we propose to evaluate the efficacy of WNT inhibitors (BAY 6167, BAY 6071) and sorafenib in preclinical models of HCC. Understanding the mechanisms of action of Wnt inhibitors and methods of combining these drugs with sorafenib may help to increase the efficacy, reduce toxicity, and improve overall survival of patients with HCC.

title: Evaluating PI3K-AKT Oncogenic Activity in Non-Hodgkin's Lymphomas. A collaboration between Bayer and the National Cancer Centre Singapore (NCCS)
abs: The phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT pathway regulates cell growth, proliferation, and metabolism and is one of the most deregulated signaling pathways in human cancers. Genetic aberrations in this pathway, such as activating mutations in the catalytic subunit of PI3K, deletion of the PTEN gene (encoding the phosphatase and tensin homolog), or genomic amplifications of upstream receptor tyrosine kinases, are identified in a wide range of human cancers. Given the central role of the PI3K-AKT pathway as an oncogenic driver of tumorigenesis, small molecules targeting this pathway are under active development as anti-cancer therapeutics. Indeed, a host of these kinase inhibitors that target key pathway components such as PI3K and AKT are at various stages of clinical trials. Although targeting the PI3K-AKT pathway remain a promising anticancer strategy, PI3K-targeted inhibitors in clinical development are likely to be limited due to the presence of multiple feedback loops and/or cross-talk with alternative oncogenic signaling pathways. Therefore, preclinical evaluation of PI3K-AKT pathway and its associated oncogenic pathways is necessary to identify underlying mechanisms of tumor formation that may be exploited therapeutically. Non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas (NHLs) are a heterogenous group of lymphoproliferative malignancies with differing patterns of behavior and responses to treatment. The two most common types of NHL are diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and Follicular lymphoma (FL), which account for approximately 50-75% of newly diagnosed lymphoid neoplasms in the world. Thus a better understanding of the biology of DLBCL and FL is needed for the development of potential therapeutic agents that target oncogenic signaling pathways. In this study, we propose to evaluate the role of PI3K-AKT pathway in Non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas. We will investigate the PI3K-AKT activity in both DLBCL and FL through different technologies. In future, we hope to be able to stratify NHL patients therapeutically based on the activity of PI3K-AKT pathway.

title: Translational PoC study of RO6897779 in NHP with ocular hypertension
abs: RO6897779 is a new compound that inhibits the Autotaxin-lysophosphatidic acid (ATX-LPA) axis. Autotaxin (ATX) is a secreted lysophospholipase D (LysoPLD) that is important for the generation of lysophosphatidic acid (LPA). This enzyme is present in key tissues/fluids modulating Intraocular Pressure (IOP) namely aqueous humor (AH), trabecular meshwork (TM) cells, and the ciliary body. These monkeys are well-characterised and are being used for testing the therapeutic efficacy of various pharmaceutical drugs. title: ATX in glaucoma – ATX inhibitor study in Dutch belted rabbits
abs: Primary open-angle glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness in the United States and is commonly associated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). The increased IOP is caused by diminished aqueous humor (AH) drainage through the trabecular pathway. The molecular basis for increased resistance to AH outflow through the trabecular pathway is not fully understood and explored. Autotaxin (ATX) is a secreted enzyme that is present in key tissues/fluids modulating IOP namely aqueous humor (AH), trabecular meshwork (TM) cells, and the ciliary body. There have been some recent observations suggested that Autotaxin-lysophosphatidic acid (ATX-LPA) axis might be a potential therapeutic target for lowering IOP in glaucoma patients (IYER, Plos One, 2012).Importantly, our previous study in 21 ocular hypertensive Dutch-Belted rabbits has successfully shown that ATX being a differentiated target for primary open angle glaucoma with a potential to act on top of standard of care. The current study will involve: Stage 1: Testing the efficacy of ATX inhibitor, RO6897779 in combination treatment of other therapeutic agents currently available for treating glaucoma and ocular hypertension including carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (Dorzolamid) and Prostaglandin (Latanoprost). Stage 2: As hyperemia is a common side effect of IOP-lowering drugs, this effect will also be closely monitored in the above treatment as well as in comparison with Rho kinase (ROCK)-inhibitor, either singly or in combination treatment. Stage 3: 6 additional compounds work by inhibiting the ATX pathway will also be screened.

title: Studies of the antitumor activity of CDK4/6 inhibitor, FGFR4 inhibitor and IGF1R inhibitor alone and in combination with other targeted agents in GIST and HCC models
abs: Hepatocellular cancer (HCC) is the fifth most common malignancy worldwide with 660,000 deaths annually. Apart from abnormal angiogenesis, several critical molecular signaling pathways such as Raf/MEK/ERK, Ang/Tie2, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, Wnt/?-catenin, JAK/Stat pathways and cell cycle regulators are aberrant in HCC. Their activation contributes to tumor development, progression and metastasis. A considerable crosstalk and redundancy in signaling pathways are also observed in HCC. To be effective in HCC therapies, new agents and novel therapeutic strategies must target various key signaling pathways and will likely be combined with cytotoxic drugs or growth factor receptor inhibitors or intracellular kinase inhibitors to effectively control advanced HCC. This multi-target approach can be accomplished by using either combinations of selective agents or agents that interfere with various targets. In this proposal we propose to evaluate the efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitor, FGFR4 inhibitor and IGF1R inhibitor as monotherapy as well as combination therapies for HCC treatment. Understanding the mechanisms of action of these therapeutic agents and methods of combining these drugs may help to increase their efficacy, reduce toxicity, and improve overall survival and quality of life in patients with HCC.

title: Next Generation Spin Torque Memories: From Fundamental Physics to Applications
abs: The mainstream research activities in the field of STT-MRAM is to use CoFeB as a magnetic storage material with a MgO barrier to form an magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) structure as it can provide the highest TMR with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA). However, current CoFeB-based STT-MRAM suffers from the low thermal stability, determined by the product of the thermal energy barrier and the volume of the storage layer, when it is scaled down to 50 nm. In addition, it is reported that CoFeB film has an increasing damping constant as its thickness decreases below 2 nm. An ideal material would provide high PMA to ensure a sufficient thermal energy barrier, low damping constant and structurally match with MgO barrier for high TMR ratio. The most promising candidates known so far are the Heusler alloys and MnGa. Therefore, in this project, we will focus on the investigation on STT-MRAM using Heusler alloys and MnGa. Another thrust to realize highly efficient STT-MRAM is to utilize spin orbit torques (SOT) in conjunction with the above Heusler alloys that have low damping and high PMA SOT in the form of interfacial Rashba field or spin Hall effect which can be incorporated to achieve efficient electrical manipulation of non-volatile magnetic memories like STT-MRAM. Unlike present method of STT-MRAM being pursued by industry, switching via the spin orbit coupling (SOC) method does not rely on injection of spin current in the nanopillar, and can thus be more efficient and less susceptible to spin depolarization at the interfaces and the spacer layer. The physics of the interplay between these two effects has not been elucidated. Understanding the underlying physics will pave the way for interfacial engineering as a means to improve the spin transfer efficiency in magnetic memories and reduce the required switching current density, thereby achieving higher energy efficiency. The SOC effect can be utilized together with the conventional STT effect in order to reduce the required switching current. Interfacial engineering may be also used to introduce strain into the system, so as to alter the magnetic properties and increase the TMR of the device and improve the read-out sensitivity of the device.

title: A Cutting-Edge Silicon Based Mid-IR Photonics Platform for Emerging Communication And Sensing Applications
abs: With continued steep growth in transmitted data volumes on all media, there is a widely-recognized and urgent need for more sophisticated photonics technologies in both the core and access networks to forestall a 'capacity crunch' in the medium term. Recently, large scale research projects have been initiated to investigate new glasses and optical fibres for transmission to 3 μm (MIR) with large improvement in performance. However, these existing programmes do not address corresponding realization of photonic devices at either end of the fibres, operating efficiently at the MIR wavelengths. This project will address these issues by developing efficient silicon photonic circuits for the MIR, to be utilized as transceivers and signal processing circuits in the optical domain. By combining the attractive properties of group IV materials with the advantages of III-V photonics in the MIR spectrum, it is envisioned that a cutting-edge MIR photonic integration technology for emerging communication and sensing applications can be realized. Hence, the motivation of this program is to push the research frontiers in group IV MIR photonics and their integration with III-V MIR sources and detectors which will allow us to open a new spectral window for communications and other applications. The four key focus areas in this program are: (1) Si/Ge materials and passive devices in the MIR, (2) high performance MIR modulators, (3) III-V on Si MIR lasers and detectors, (4) demonstration of MIR photonic circuits for communications and sensing using the components and modules developed in this program.

title: Monitoring seasonal/pandemic influenza vaccine effectiveness and early warning system for outbreaks or emerging infectious diseases amongst healthcare workers in a hospital setting via an integrated digital syndromic and diagnostic surveillance system (FluMobile)
abs: The project will aim to evaluate a novel way to monitor influenza vaccine effectiveness in a hospital setting via the integration of a novel mobile phone syndromic surveillance system with systematic consistent sampling. It will also explore the utility of such a novel integrated digital syndromic and laboratory testing surveillance system to strengthen real time monitoring for early outbreak warning of influenza or emerging infectious disease amongst healthcare workers. We hypothesize that influenza effectiveness data derived from a combination of mobile phone technology with syndromic surveillance and consistent subset sampling amongst healthcare workers will be comparable to published figures using current traditional surveillance system. We also hypothesize that such a surveillance system can improve capacity for detecting outbreaks or emerging infectious diseases in hospital settings by demonstrating early warning of influenza and other respiratory infectious diseases outbreaks.We will make available a syndromic surveillance system on a digital media platform which integrates the internet with a mobile phone application (App) to be used by healthcare workers. The easy to use App software will allow users to provide reports of non-specific syndromes such as influenza-like-illness on a weekly basis. We will incorporate a consistent sampling methodology for a subset of healthcare workers. Samples will be tested for influenza and various other common viruses using a respiratory multiplex. Blood will also be collected during acute and convalescent periods to further allow analysis of serological outcomes. Using influenza vaccination status data, we will derive vaccine effectiveness estimates in near real time. Through the collection of other variables, we will identify risk factors associated with influenza and various acute respiratory infections amongst healthcare workers. We will assess whether such a system could provide earlier warning of an influenza season by comparing the data from current laboratory and syndromic surveillance systems.

title: Epidemiology and transmission of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in the community in Singapore
abs: Since its emergence in the 1960s, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has become the most common multidrug-resistant organism in healthcare settings worldwide, with considerable resulting health and economic burden. In Singapore, around 8% of patients admitted to the major acute and tertiary care hospitals are colonized with MRSA, and this organism causes 2-3 bacteraemias per week in each of these facilities. Compared with MRSA non-infected patients, MRSA-infected patients have, on average, higher mortality, longer hospitalization, four-fold higher hospitalization costs, higher healthcare costs post-discharge and poorer quality of life scores. Infection control activities, including MRSA screening at admission and ward transfer, cohorting of MRSA-infected patients, and enhanced hand hygiene, have contributed to marked and sustained reductions in MRSA infection in the major hospitals. Further reductions in MRSA burden, however, will require extension of control activities to step-down care facilities, nursing homes and the community, all of which which represent a vast reservoir for MRSA transmission. The epidemiology of MRSA in the community following patient discharge, however, is poorly characterized, precluding understanding of the transmission dynamics of this pathogen and its circulation between hospitals and the community. We propose to address this knowledge gap by conducting a longitudinal study of MRSA-colonized discharged patients and their household contacts. The study will include a baseline survey of MRSA colonization prevalence and monthly, longitudinal sampling of index patients and their contacts, together with molecular typing of bacterial strains and collection of epidemiological risk factors. title: One Health, Zoonotic Diseases and Pandemic Planning: Creating a Bioethics Framework in Singapore
abs: One Health (OH) is a collaborative initiative to improve both the health of human and non-human animals as coexisting within a shared environment. Its calls for a paradigm shift in public health approaches, requiring wide-reaching policy revisions to encompass an innovative focus, as well as the inclusion of stakeholders from private and governmental sectors outside of traditional public health groups.OH has been used in understanding zoonotic diseases and prevention of emerging pandemics. In Singapore, due to efficient implementation of an evidence-based public health policy, the threat of an emerging zoonotic disease has largely been tamed, but as the global environment changes, so arise the need to review existing public health measures. Continued urbanization, climate change and international trade of agricultural products amplify the risk for transmission of vector borne pathogens and emphasize the importance of assuring biosafety in Singapore.In the proposed study, the first aim is to map current public health policy in Singapore with implications of the OH initiative. We propose conducting a Policy Delphi survey among a wide group of experts in Singapore, which allows us to review perspectives of diverse specialists with expertise in zoonotic disease management or interests in how such diseases are implicated, such as park and wildlife-resource managers, agencies involved in the transport, preparation and consumption of food, and environmental agents and planners. This will be followed up with semi-structured interviews with respondents to gain a deeper understanding of the factors involved in the propagation of zoonotic diseases and the possible preventive measures that could be taken to abate risks. The second aim is to assess the bioethical issues of the OH initiative in respect to pandemic strategies. Using our structured data, we will consider public health policies which are congruent with the OH approach.
kw: One Health; Public Health Policy; Bioethics; Pandemic Planning; Zoonotic Diseases; Policy Delphi

title: Epidemiological and evolutionary dynamics of respiratory viruses in Singapore
abs: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) cause significant morbidity and mortality especially among children, with the disease spectrum ranging from upper respiratory symptoms to lower respiratory diseases like bronchiolitis and pneumonia. The diversity of bacterial and viral agents in children is reasonably well known and the major contributors to disease burden are respiratory viruses. However, most of the work to describe the epidemiology of respiratory viruses has been in pediatric populations with little focus on adults apart from reports of the prevalence of respiratory viruses. As such, with the exception of influenza viruses and respiratory syncytial virus, the morbidity and mortality of respiratory infections among adults, is understudied in most countries. The prevalence, epidemiological trends and evolution of viral agents causing adult respiratory infection also remain largely unknown. In this study we will screen over 2,000 respiratory clinical specimens collected from adults presenting with acute febrile illness from 2007–2013 using quantitative PCR assays against 15 common respiratory viruses. Using associated clinical and epidemiological information we will characterize the epidemiology and severity of ARI in adults in Singapore. Positive specimens will also be sequenced and virus genetic data will be analyzed to determine the epidemiological and evolutionary dynamics of those viruses. The information generated in this study will provide a clearer understanding of the disease burden of respiratory viruses in adults and provide insights into their local and global circulation. This information will inform focus areas for future research and healthcare policy and to aid in responding to emerging epidemics and public health emergencies.The specific objectives of this project are:(1)Identification and sequencing of viral agents associated with acute febrile respiratory illness in adults(2)Study the epidemiology of viral agents identified in Aim 1(3)Characterization of the evolutionary dynamics of respiratory viruses from Singapore in a global setting

title: Uropathogens and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns in UTI diagnosed in primary care settings
abs: Urinary tract infection (UTI) is a frequent condition encountered in primary care. Most UTI occur in women and treatment of UTI is usually empirical without urine culture or antibiotic susceptibility testing to guide treatment. This approach has been chosen because the causative uropathogens and their antimicrobial susceptibility profiles are considered to be predictable. Accurate and updated information about prevalence of uropathogens and their antimicrobial susceptibility patterns is therefore important. However, there is strong and increasing evidence of antimicrobial resistance in community-acquired uropathogens. Limited data from local studies have shown significant resistance to contrimxazole and ciprofloxacin, two antibiotics commonly used for UTI treatment in primary care. While hospitals do capture antibiotic resistance patterns of organisms cultured in its laboratories, these patterns may overestimate resistance patterns for community-acquired infections.This study aims to describe the distribution of uropathogens and their antimicrobial susceptibilities amongst patients who have been diagnosed with UTI in primary care clinics in Singapore. The results will be directly applicable to our primary care doctors. Additionally, we will examine risk factors for antimicrobial resistance and determine the circulating resistance genotypes in community-acquired uropathogens, and establish antimicrobial prescribing patterns for urinary tract infections in primary care. This cross sectional studies will recruit 700 female patients who are diagnosed by their primary care physician to have UTI. Upon enrolment, the physician will fill out a data collection form that will obtain information on risk factors for antimicrobial resistance. The patient will be instructed to provide a clean-catch mid-stream urine sample for urine culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Additional genotypic screening will be performed using conventional PCR. Both descriptive and analytical statistics will be used to analyse the data.

title: The molecular basis for EV71 pathogenesis and epidemic potential
abs: EV71 is known to cause a spectrum of clinical syndromes that range from HFMD to CNS infections, most frequently in children under the age of four. Currently, there is neither vaccine nor specific antiviral treatment to ameliorate infection. Over the last 15 years several large epidemics of EV71 related diseases, especially brain stem encephalitis, have occurred in Asia that may be the result of viral evolution. Where these genomic changes occur and how they are mechanistically responsible for the severe disease phenotype is unknown. The lack of such understanding prevents an evidence-based approach to surveillance and disease prevention. In this proposal, we will utilize a unique collection of clinically relevant, low passage EV71 isolates from Singapore and the ongoing HFMD epidemic in Vietnam to characterize the mechanisms underlying pathogenesis and epidemic potential. To accomplish this goal, we will attempt to gain a comprehensive view of the transcriptional response to infection for EV71 strains isolated during epidemic or inter-epidemic periods. We will then assess the functional requirement of these differentially regulated genes for viral propagation. To identify the “phylogenetically informative” mutations with epidemic relevance, we will sequence the full genome of viruses in this collection. We will then assess the functional relevance of these mutations by characterizing the effect they have on viral growth and innate immune response kinetics. In order to dissect molecular mechanisms of pathogenesis, we will construct infectious clones that will allow us to interrogate the contribution of mutations on biological processes with an emphasis on innate immune pathways. The findings from this study should pave the way for much-needed, evidence-based, active genomic EV71 surveillance for disease prevention. Further, we envisage that this work will serve as a springboard for future studies that bridge the gulf between mechanistic molecular biology and epidemiological observations.
