title: Excitonics Science and Technology toward Revolutionary Semiconductor Lighting: Ultra-Efficiency Excitonic Energy Transfer for Next-Generation Lighting and Displays
abs: Today, the most commonly used SSL sources are based on phosphor integrated color conversion LEDs. The broad yellowish emission of yttrium aluminum garnet (YAG) phosphors along with blue LED (around 460 nm) yields white light generation with correlated color temperatures (CCTs) of 4000–8000 K, and color rendering indexes (CRIs) typically lower than 80, which is due to the missing of red component in the spectrum. Therefore, using phosphors, it is currently impossible to achieve high luminous efficacy of optical radiation (LER) >350 lm/Wopt and high CRI (>90) at warm CCT (<3500 K), all at the same time. In this project, we propose a new class of high-efficiency excitonically driven LEDs based on nonradiative energy transfer using quantum dots (QDs), taking two separate approaches in polymer platforms and inorganic platforms, in addition to using plasmon-exciton interactions in energy transfer for both. This project includes the study of highly efficient colloidal QD nanocrystals (with quantum efficiency of >80%) interfaced with conjugated polymers in organic LEDs, epitaxial quantum well nanowires in inorganic LEDs, and metal/dielectric hetero-nanoparticles as nanoluminophors in hybrid architectures for mediating and controlling the energy flow in the active LED device structures. In particular, we will work on the science of excitonics to understand, develop and demonstrate: (1) high-efficiency disordered QD LEDs employing QDs as exciton formation that are driven by nonraditive energy transfer in the polymer diode structure; (2) high-efficiency QDs integrated into quantum well nanowires in inorganic LED structure for high efficiency, high quality lighting (with consideration of scotopic/photopic enhancement); and (3) high-efficiency QDs that are assembled on metal/dielectric hetero-nanoparticles integrated in LEDs for strong plasmon-exciton interaction and polarization control. In this project, we will make excitonically driven QD LEDs that improve both visual acuity and color discrimination by achieving high LER of >350 lm/Wopt and high CRI >90.

title: Is it safe to transfuse Leucocyte Depletion Filter (LDF) processed Intra-Operative Cell Salvage (IOCS) blood, in spine tumour surgery?
abs: BackgroundIntra-operative blood loss is a significant complication of spinal tumour surgery. A patient undergoing surgery for metastatic spinal disorders(MSD) loses 1500mL of blood and requires an average of 3 units of packed cell transfusion. This blood loss is presently replenished by allogenic blood transfusion(ABT). ABT places an enormous burden on blood bank resources, and exposes patients to associated risks of infection, immunosuppression, tumour progression and other transfusion reactions. Intra-operative cell salvage(IOCS) is efficient in preserving intra-operative blood loss. It is avoided in tumour surgery because of the possibility of returning tumour cells to patients. Leucocyte depletion filter(LDF) can fully eliminate viable tumour cells from salvaged blood. However, there remains much reservation amongst spine surgeons about using cell salvage in spine tumour surgery.AimsTo investigate if LDF processed IOCS blood is safe to be returned to patients undergoing spine tumour surgery.HypothesisIOCS blood filtered by LDF does not contain viable tumour cells.MethodPatients with MSD requiring spine surgery will be recruited. Blood will be obtained at 5 different stages as follows: venous blood before skin incision, venous blood at maximum tumour manipulation, salvaged blood from the reservoir, salvaged blood after IOCS processing and salvaged blood after IOCS processing and LDF filtration. 3 separate samples will be taken at each stage making fifteen samples per patient. Tumour cells from each sample will be detected using a panel of three monoclonal anti-cytokeratin antibody stains and examined using light microscopy. Viability will be confirmed by detecting nucleated malignant cells and a tryphan blue exclusion test.Clinical significanceCell salvage can then be safely applied in spine tumour surgery and may be extended to other oncological surgeries, as a viable alternative to ABT. This will reduce the burden on blood banks and minimize patient exposure to the deleterious effects of ABT.

title: CHInese Medicine Neuroaid Efficacy on Stroke recovery (CHIMES) Study
abs: Although thrombolysis, aspirin, and stroke-unit care are of proven efficacy in acute stroke treatment, there remains need for treatments that would further improve outcome.Danqi Piantang Jiaonang (DJ) is a Traditional Chinese Medicine used for over 10 years in Chinese stroke patients. Evidence of its efficacy and safety have been investigated by randomized positive-controlled trials, conducted to Chinese Medicine standards. This investigator-initiated, randomized placebo-controlled trial aims to test DJ's efficacy in acute ischemic stroke using established stroke trial methodology.1100 ischemic stroke patients of intermediate stroke severity presenting within 72 hours will be randomized to receive DJ or matched placebo, in addition to usual stroke care. The primary outcome measure is the modified Rankin Score distribution at 3 months. Secondary outcome measures include the NIHSS, MMSE and Barthel scales.Sixteen sites in Singapore, Philippines, Thailand, Sri Lanka and Hong Kong are participating with further sites planned in India, Malaysia and France. As of 30th October 2010, 665 patients have been randomized, 362 from Singapore. At a conservative monthly recruitment rate of 20 the trial will complete recruitment in August 2012, follow up in December 2012, database lock in March 2013 and the results presented in May 2013.This study is a unique collaboration of major stroke trials centers in Singapore, important regional stroke centres and the Singapore Clinical Research Institute. The study also has the support of international stroke leaders who are contributing their expertise to study management. The NMRC’s continued support is vital for the successful completion of this landmark trial which has reached over 60% of its target recruitment.The trial is important for translational medicine in Singapore through (i) setting new standards for systematic evaluation of Asian Traditional Medicine for integration into standard medicine practice (ii) potentially establishing a novel therapeutic approach for improving recovery after stroke.

title: Enabling the Next Wave of Ultra Low Power Nano-systems: Heterogenous Integration of Low Power Electronics with High Performance Photonics
abs: This flagship program aims to develop a set of novel heterogeneous semiconductor wafer processes targeted at the ultimate implementation of 22nm node CMOS technology for advanced functional diversification with ultra low power requirement. In future CMOS technology, reduction in supply voltage and power consumption can be achieved without compromising speed performance if FETs employ a III-V compound semiconductor (III-V) channel with extremely high carrier mobility. It is anticipated that being semiconductors with extremely high carrier mobilities, III-V and Ge are the strongest candidates for implementation into future high speed N-MOS and P-MOS device technology, respectively. Furthermore, the problem of intra-chip signal propagation delay and thermal issues can be alleviated using optical interconnect technology based on III-V direct bandgap materials. Since these semiconductors have large lattice mismatch compared to Si, a new heterogeneous wafer platform is required to enable high performance device implementation. In this flagship program, the key bottlenecks in MOSFETs with III-V and Ge channels will be solved through innovations in MOSFET device technology, such as strained source/drain region, advanced surface passivation techniques and unprecedented FET structures such as FinFETs and nanowire FETs. Moreover, the use of Ge-terminated Si-based substrates will enable the electronic substrate module that contains the III-V and Ge MOSFETs to be developed concurrently with the optical interconnect epitaxy-stack technology. The MOSFET and optical interconnect modules will be fused together through a selection of graded buffer technologies with the option to use low temperature oxide fusion bonding and substrate exfoliation processes. The prime novelty of this flagship program lies in the strategic implementation and integration of the MOSFET substrate module and optical interconnect epitaxy-stack substrate module that offers great potential for intellectual property generation. Our research methodology will also take into account critical considerations in thermal budget and cross contamination during the new technology insertion phase. Furthermore, our novel modular solutions have cutting-edge industry-compatible implementation strategies, i.e. concurrent development cycle and parallel manufacturing capability for individual modules, which offer unprecedented flexibility in device and process design.

title: Modulation of thyroid hormone action by SIRT1 histone deacetylase activity
abs: Thyroid hormones (THs) (T3, T4) are essential for normal metabolism and cellular function throughout life. Thyroid hormone receptors (TRs) belong to a superfamily of nuclear hormone receptors that act as ligand-regulatable transcription factors that bind to enhancer sequences of target gene promoters and recruit transcription complexes which covalently modify specific histone sites. Currently, little is known about the specific histone modifications that determine transcriptional regulation by thyroid hormone receptors (TRs). Additionally little is known about whether chromatin modifications of target genes are affected by aging or metabolic conditions. SIRT1 is a histone deacetylase which is a key regulator of aging, glucose homeostasis, and energy metabolism. Recently, we found that SIRT1 is recruited to TH-regulated target gene promoters and alters their transcriptional activities. These novel findings suggest that SIRT1 may modulate transcription by TH in metabolically active tissues such as the liver and during aging. We thus propose:1) To examine the effects SIRT1 on TH-mediated gene regulation in hepatocytes under different metabolic conditions.2) To examine role of SIRT1 in modulating TH-mediated hepatic gene regulation in vivo during aging, starvation, and obesity. Our studies will shed light on the molecular mechanisms and epigenetic changes that are modulated by SIRT1 in TH signaling. These also should provide information on how transcription by TRs may be co-regulated by SIRT1 during aging and different metabolic states. This, in turn, potentially could lead to novel therapeutic strategies such as activation or enhancing expression of SIRT1 in combination with hormone therapy to treat conditions associated with aging and metabolic disorders.

title: Functional Investigation of matrix metalloproteinase ADAMTS4 in atherosclerosis using knockout mice model
abs: Atherosclerosis, the formation of thickened and inflammatory arterial wall plaques as the result of a build-up of fatty materials such as cholesterol, causes serious cardiovascular diseases including myocardial infarction, stroke and peripheral occlusive vascular diseases. It results from complex interactions among multiple genetic and environmental factors. Advanced atherosclerotic lesions are laden with large amount of lipid-loaded macrophages accompanied with ectopic neovascularization and matrix degredation. Plaques that are prone to thrombotic rupture (vulnerable plaques) are particularly dangerous for acute myocardial infarction. Inflammation, matrix degradation and angiogenesis are thought to precipitate plaque rupture or erosion, causing arterial thrombosis and cardiovascular events. Despite major advances in our understanding of atherosclerosis, we still do not fully understand the biological factors that influence this disease. In particular, factors that regulate plaque vulnerability are poorly understood. Extracellular matrix remodeling by metalloproteinase is believed to play a major role in plaque destabilization, but the identities of matrix-degrading proteinases remain the subject of speculation. ADAMTS (a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motifs) is a family of secreted metalloproteinase with 19 members in human. Recently, ADAMTS4 is shown to be an inflammation- regulated proteinase highly upregulated in human and mouse atherosclerotic plaques. In patients with acute coronary syndrome, plasma ADAMTS4 was significantly increased. We therefore hypothesize that ADAMTS4 plays a pathogenic role in atherosclerosis and plaque destabilization. In this proposal, we aim to clarify the role of ADAMTS4 in atherosclerosis using Adamts4-/-ApoE-/- double knockout mice. ApoE-/- mice is a well characterized mouse atherosclerosis model which develop extensive atherosclerotic lesions similar to that of human. Atherosclerotic pathology including plaque vulnerability, severity, burden, as well as extent of inflammation, fibrosis and angiogenesis will be investigated. This work will expand our knowledge of atherosclerosis and plaque vulnerability and help in identifying novel drug target for this deadly disease.
kw: heart disease, ADAMTS4, atherosclerosis, vulnerable plaque, Matrix metalloproteinase

title: Regulation of Circadian Rhythms
abs: Circadian rhythms are endogenous 24-hour cycles that regulates fundamental physiological and behavioral functions. Daily fluctuations of wakefulness, stress hormones, metabolism, immune functions and the cell division cycle are all controlled by the molecular clocks that function throughout our bodies. Disruption of rhythms predisposes to cancer, and restoration of rhythms holds promise for cancer therapy. The clock is formed by a negative feedback loop of transcription, translation, and inhibition of transcription. Mutations in regulatory components of the clock can shorten or lengthen the timing of the rhythms and have significant physiological consequences. As one of the key components providing precise clock timing, PER2’s stability and localization is controlled by the protein kinase Casein Kinase 1 (CK1) and protein phosphatases. In this proposal, the role of phosphorylation in regulating PER2 function in the clock will be explored in detail. A comprehensive understanding of how reversible protein phosphorylation regulates circadian rhythms could provide new approaches to clinical manipulation of circadian rhythms, which may provide important benefits for human health.
kw: circadian rhythms, kinase, cancer, phosphorylation, phosphatase

title: Novel 2D Materials with Tailored Properties: Beyond Graphene
abs: Technological progress is determined, to a great extent, by the developments in material science. The most surprising breakthroughs are attained when a new type of material or new combination of old materials, with reduced dimensionality and functionality, is created. One of the old pillars of solid state physics is that the band structure of 3D materials is set by their geometry and chemistry. Although this concept is the force behind modern electronics and technology, it also has its limitations since it is very difficult to modify and manipulate because in order to generate a new functionality one has to create a new crystal. With the recent developments in 2D crystal growth (driven by the discovery of graphene in 2004) a new paradigm has been created. 2D crystals open a new venue for engineering of the electronic properties. We will set-up the first fully integrated growth facility for 2D crystal heterostructures. There will be several recipes for the preparation of the elementary blocks (various 2D crystals), their modification (by chemistry, mechanical means, etc) and subsequent combination to create materials with predefined properties. The large variety of starting blocks, modification methods and combination options guarantees not only a huge range of materials possible, but also their multi-functionality, which will be of crucial importance for future applications. We will use an integrated approach based on growth, characterization and theoretical modeling, that will make of Singapore a innovation hub for materials science for the 21st century.
kw: electronic properties;optical properties;structural properties;photovoltaics;composite materials;photonics

title: Molecular Epidemiology of HIV-1 in Singapore and Characterization of Unique Novel Recombinant Forms
abs: BackgroundThe annual incidence of new HIV-1 diagnoses in Singapore is rising. In parallel, the proportion of new diagnoses reporting men who have sex with men (MSM) and bisexual transmission risk has increased. An ongoing study has detected novel HIV-1 recombinant forms and a change in HIV-1 molecular epidemiology in Singapore. The novel HIV-1 recombinant forms were present mainly among MSMs and bisexuals. However, the current information is insufficient to establish the number and nature of these novel recombinants. AimsThe primary study aims are to:(1) confirm and characterize the novel recombinant forms and, (2) establish representative estimates of HIV-1 subtypes in Singapore in 2011 and 2012. The secondary aims are to: (1) determine baseline genotypes for treatment-naïve patients and, (2) determine trends in subtype prevalence in Singapore.Methods1. Phase 1 involves full genome sequencing of 19 patient samples identified from a current study as possible novel recombinants.2. Phase 2 targets the majority of newly diagnosed HIV-1 patients in Singapore for recruitment into a prospective genotyping study to establish reliable baseline estimates of the various subtypes. The 4 main Singapore HIV-1 care centers are included in this study. Demographic, transmission risk data and baseline laboratory results will be collected. Samples collected will be genotyped in 3 HIV-1 genomic regions using established methods. Clinical significance1. The resulting data will aid policy makers in targeting high-risk populations for prevention interventions and monitoring results. 2. Genotyping data generated will contribute to the knowledge of global subtype distributions and help in efforts to develop and test an HIV-1 vaccine.3. A current study has revealed inter-subtype differences in rates of HIV-1 clinical progression in Singapore. Baseline genotyping data will help provide information to further test this hypothesis

title: Uncovering the anticancer potential of phenylpropanoid sucrose esters
abs: The pharmacologically active phenylpropanoid sucrose esters isolated from various plants have been used as folk medicines for treatment of cancer, haemostatics, arthritis and articular pain. Extracts of Polygonum pennsylvanicum, containing Vanicosides, were found to inhibit protein kinase C. Vanicoside B displayed an IC50 of 31 µg/ml. Structurally related phenylpropanoids Lapathosides A-D isolated from Polygonum lapathifolium showed significant inhibitory effects on the Epstein-Barr virus early antigen activation.These compounds are contemplated to be valuable anti-tumor-promoters for cancer chemoprevention. The potential of these compounds has not been systematically explored to date although they have shown clear promise. Reasons include (i) laborious methods needed to extract and purify such compounds from their natural sources. (ii) lack of mechanistic insights into their activity (iii) no existing routes to describe their laboratory synthesis. (iv) variable structural candidates are needed to asses the structure activity relationships to develop more active structures.The bioactivity of majority of the reported phenylpropanoid esters (124 reported so far) has not been investigated although they have shown clear promise. Cancer is the leading cause of death in Singapore. This proposal focuses on uncovering the anticancer potential of phenylpropanoid esters and aims to examine their mechanistic activity. We aim to develop synthetic protocols that allow their effective synthesis in a concise and robust manner to obtain structural variations for screening. Preliminary studies on two phenylpropanoid we synthesized (compounds 9 and 10) using HeLa cells showed very good IC50 of 5.26 and 6.01 mM (48 h). The primary screening showed less cytotoxic activity against HUVEC cell lines by comparison with the standard anticancer drug camptothecin. Preliminary experiments further suggest that pre-treatment with phenylpropanoid esters for 6h can inhibit IL-6-induced STAT3 activation in HeLa cells, thereby indicating that potential anti-cancer effects of these compounds may be mediated through suppression of STAT3 signaling cascade.

title: Exploiting the relationship between parkin and DMT1 to generate a novel gene-environmental mouse model of Parkinsons disease
abs: Exposure to metals such as iron and manganese has consistently been implicated by epidemiological studies to be a significant risk factor for Parkinson’s disease (PD). Under normal circumstances, cellular iron and manganese uptake is regulated by the Divalent Metal Transporter 1 (DMT1). Accordingly, alterations in DMT1 levels may underlie the abnormal accumulation of metal ions and thereby disease pathogenesis. Indeed, DMT1 expression has recently been demonstrated to be significantly elevated in the substantia nigra of PD patients compared to age-matched controls. Interestingly, parkin, a ubiquitin ligase associated with recessive parkinsonism, has separately been demonstrated to promote the degradation of a specific isoform of DMT1. Consistent with this, we found that parkin over-expression affords considerable protection to cells treated with iron. Further, we found that iron overloading in turn enhances endogenous parkin expression, suggesting a reciprocal relationship. Similarly, the expression of parkin is markedly enhanced in transgenic mice over-expressing DMT1. Because parkin is known to function as a potent neuroprotectant, we believe that the observed phenomenon is a specific cellular response to guard against metal-induced neurotoxicity, which may explain why DMT1 mice fail to exhibit robust signs of parkinsonism. We therefore seek in this proposal to clarify our speculation. Given the proposed relationship between parkin and DMT1, it is also attractive to speculate that mice engineered to over-express DMT1, when ablated of endogenous parkin expression, have a good chance of recapitulating the phenotypic and pathologic features of PD. Notably, none of the genetic mouse PD models generated to date (including parkin mice) has turned out to be a good replica of the human condition. Our proposed study holds promise to create a much-needed representative PD mouse model, the success of which would not only enhance our understanding on PD pathogenesis but also facilitates PD drug discovery efforts.
kw: Neurodegeneration, Parkinson's disease, Parkin, Divalent Metal Transporter

title: The effectiveness of therapeutic play intervention on outcomes of children undergoing inpatient elective surgeries: a randomized control trial
abs: AimsTo examine the effects of therapeutic play on outcomes (state of anxiety and postoperative pain) of children undergoing inpatient elective surgery and to examine the effects of therapeutic play for children on their parents’ state of anxiety. Hypotheses(1) Children receiving preoperative therapeutic play intervention will report lower level of anxiety, exhibit fewer negative emotions during the induction of anesthesia and report less postoperative pain than those in the control group. (2) Children having higher level of pre-operative anxiety will report higher postoperative pain intensity.(3) The anxiety level of children and their parents will be positively related.(4) Parents who accompany their children to receive therapeutic play intervention will have less anxiety than those who do not.(5) Children and their parents will find the therapeutic play intervention beneficial in the preparation of children’s operation. MethodologyA randomized controlled, two-group pretest and repeated posttest, between subjects design will be used in this study. 6-14 years old children undergoing an elective surgery in a Singaporean hospital and their parents will participate in this study. Instruments that will be used to collect data include the State Anxiety Scale for Children or Chinese version of the State Anxiety Scale for Children, Children’s Emotional Manifestation Scale, State Anxiety Scale for Adults, Numeric Rating Scale and process evaluation interview guide. Data will be analysed using SPSS software and thematic analysis. Significance of the studyThis study will identify a clinically useful and potentially effective approach to prepare children for surgery by reducing preoperative anxiety of both children and their parents during the perioperative period. The reduction of anxiety would lead to reduction of postoperative pain, which eventually will improve the physical and psychological well being of children, quality of care to children and the satisfaction level of children and their parents.
kw: Therapeutic play, Anxiety, Children, Parents, Postoperative pain, Surgery

title: In silico design of trans-splicing RNA and amalgamation with other RNA technologies for genetic therapy
abs: RNA trans-splicing represents a technology which is suitable to repair defect gene expression on the level of the precursor messenger RNA (pre-mRNA) without the need of intervention with the genomic DNA. As opposed to cellular cis-splicing which occurs within one pre-mRNA transcript, trans-splicing describes splice reactions between two different pre-mRNAs. Trans-splicing may occur naturally, however for therapeutic purposes an artificial trans-splicing RNA (tsRNA) is created to target a deleterious cellular pre-mRNA. The trans-splice technology allows molecular-surgical repair of defect gene functions and, hence, trans-splicing has high therapeutic potential comparable with the RNAi technology. So far, studies in mice indicate relatively low trans-splicing activities which are considered suitable to alter only few disease phenotypes. One reason for low observed trans-splicing rates is based on the fact that intermolecular trans-splicing has to compete with intramolecular cis-splicing reactions. To improve the process, trans-splicing efficiencies have to be optimized and cis-splicing has to be actively suppressed. We hypothesize in silico design and synergies with other RNA technologies can push trans-splicing towards therapeutically relevant degrees of efficiency. In preliminary experiments we designed and tested a variety of modules required for the assembly of tsRNA. The aim of this project is to investigate the computational design of tsRNA and the amalgamation of RNA trans-splicing with other RNA technologies such as RNAi and mRNA design. Our specific aims are: (i) to investigate a novel design for improved trans-splicing activity; (ii) to design novel double-trans-splice constructs in order to expand the range of targetable defects; (iii) to foster RNA trans-splicing by other RNA technologies including RNAi; and (iv) to create trans-splicing-based vectors targeting cells infected with human papilloma virus type 16 and liver cancer cells. The design of trans-splicing-based vectors which accomplish therapeutically relevant efficiencies may lead to the development of novel therapies targeting various genetic disorders
kw: HPV-16, RNA in silico design, genetic therapy, trans-splicing,

title: The Role of Adipose Tissue Expandability in Maintaining Metabolic Homeostasis
abs: The prevalence of obesity, along with associated metabolic complications including type 2 diabetes mellitus (characterized by insulin resistance [IR]), dyslipidemia and cardiovascular disease is exponentially increasing worldwide. The precise mechanisms by which obesity results in metabolic disturbances remain unclear. When there is persistent positive caloric balance, the capacity to safely store fat may be vital. We hypothesize that the capacity for adipose tissue expansion is not infinite; once an individual’s limit is reached, lipid not stored in adipose tissue is deposited in other tissues (such as liver and muscle). This “adipose tissue expandability” ensures that an individual remains metabolically healthy when adipose tissue can safely accommodate caloric excess. Once exceeded, exhausted fat cells could promote insulin resistance. In other words, it’s not how fat you are, but what you do with it that counts. We aim to test this hypothesis by: (1) determining fat distribution and adipose tissue morphology; and (2) characterizing differences in biochemical pathways for lipid storage, in adipose tissue of overweight Chinese men who are IR versus insulin sensitive [IS]. We will screen 100 overweight Chinese men, and enroll individuals who are “insulin sensitive” (bottom 20% in HOMA index, n=20) and “insulin resistant” (top 20% in HOMA index, n=20). Fat distribution by MRI/ MRS, metabolic profiles (plasma lipids, adipokines) as well as subcutaneous gluteal adipose tissue biopsies will be obtained. If the adipose tissue expandability hypothesis holds true, we expect to see increased liver and muscle fat, and proportionally less subcutaneous adipose tissue, as well as differing adipose tissue characteristics in IR individuals when compared to IS individuals. These findings would improve our understanding of why some can gain weight without metabolic consequences, while others develop metabolic disease at low levels of obesity. Such insights can guide improved prevention and treatment strategies for obesity and metabolic diseases.
kw: Metabolic syndrome, Adipose tissue, Fat storage

title: Guillain-Barré syndrome in Singapore: Electrophysiological subtypes and immunopathological features
abs: Background Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a leading cause of acute limb weakness worldwide, can be divided into major subtypes, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP), acute motor axonal neuropathy (AMAN) and Fisher syndrome (FS). Despite effective therapies, it continues to be associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Project 1. GBS database and tissue repository To systematically collect and collate clinical and laboratory data, as well as blood and CSF from GBS patients at five public hospitals in Singapore. The material from the database will drive the studies described in the rest of the proposal. On its own, the database will help characterize various aspects of GBS in Singapore. Project 2. Prospecitve, serial nerve conduction studies We have shown that repeated nerve conduction studies are essential to distinguish AMAN from AIDP. We believe that prospective serial electrophysiology studies would help understand the time course of the changes seen in the GBS, and develop more rigorous criteria for the classification of GBS. We also believe that serial nerve conduction studies will help elucidate the neuropathology of FS patients, and those who develop limb and respiratory weakness. Project 3. Skin biopsy studies Post-mortem studies have demonstrated complement deposition on Schwann cells in AIDP and on motor axolemma in AMAN. In animal models of AMAN, disappearance of sodium channel clusters has been shown. We hope to replicate and extend these studies on myelinated fibers found in the dermis of skin biopsies obtained from patients with AIDP, AMAN and FS. Project 4. IgM/A intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment Preliminary data have shown that IgM/A-containing IVIG blocks complement activation more effectively than standard IVIG (IgG alone). We aim to clarify the action mechanism for developing new treatment. Importance to medicine Building on our previous success, we hope to further our understanding of the immunopathology of GBS and improve therapy.

title: To Investigate The Effectiveness Of Zinc Supplementation In Patients With Advanced Non Small Cell Lung Cancer Treated With Palliative Radiotherapy; Can Lipid Oxidation Products Be Used To Predict Which Patients Will Benefit?
abs: Hypothesis Radiotherapy (RT) is offered in patients with incurable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) for relief of local symptoms. 40-80% of patients will improve, however 40% will experience RT induced dysphagia for which there is no effective prophylaxis. Supplementation with zinc during RT may reduce the severity and frequency of dysphagia. Zinc is reported to be effective in reducing RT mucositis and dermatitis without compromising outcome in head and neck cancer patients. Its role during RT for NSCLC is unknown. Radiation damage occurs by the formation of free radicals from water, which can attack lipids and DNA, causing oxidative damage. As Lipid oxidation products (LOPs) and products of DNA damage (8OHdG), have been established as markers of oxidative damage, measuring these products will allow us to evaluate the impact of zinc on RT for NSCLC. No established biomarkers exist which predict for treatment success during RT. If found to correlate with response and toxicity, LOPs and 8OHdG could be used as predictive tools for RT outcome. Aims A) Determine the effectiveness of zinc supplementation during RT. B) Develop an understanding of the mechanism by which zinc achieves its therapeutic effect and its relation to variations in levels of LOPs and 8OhdG. C) Determine if variations in levels of these markers can predict for toxicity and response to RT. Methods Patients (n=214) with NSCLC planned for palliative RT (36Gy in 12 Fractions) will be recruited. Zinc gluconate 50mg or placebo will be administered three times a day, from day 1 of RT until 4 weeks post treatment. Blood and urine samples for LOPs, liver and renal function and serum zinc levels will be obtained pre-RT, after 12Gy, 24Gy and 36Gy and at Week+2, Week+4 and Week+10 post RT and correlated with toxicity and CT thorax response at 10 weeks post RT.

title: The Role of IL-33 and ST2 in the Pathogenesis of Seronegative Spondyloarthritis
abs: The seronegative spondyloarthritides (SpA) are characterised by asymmetric and axial arthritis, enthesitis, ocular inflammation and HLA-B27 positivity. Collectively the population prevalence of SpA exceeds that of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and the course may be equally destructive and deforming. Patients not responding to conventional therapy with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and DMARDs require expensive anti-TNF or other biologics to control disease symptoms. A proportion of patients do not respond, and often relapse occurs soon after cessation of anti-TNF therapy. Studies show clear differences in the inflammatory milieu of the affected joints of SpA and RA, with greater vascularity, neutrophil and CD163+ macrophage counts in SpA. IL-33, a novel cytokine of the IL-1 family is highly expressed in human RA synovium and synovial fibroblasts. IL-33 amplifies the polarisation of M2 macrophages, and exacerbates autoantibody-induced arthritis; whereas experimental arthritis was attenuated by inhibition through either sST2 blockade or directly by neutralization with anti-IL-33 antibody. We propose to examine the role of the IL-33/ST2 axis in SpA by measuring levels of IL-33 and its soluble ligand sST2 in serum and synovial fluid, in correlation with activity of peripheral and axial arthritis, determining the expression of IL-33 and ST2 in SpA synovium in correlation with synovial histology, and the effect of IL-33 on synovial cultures from SpA patients. New and potentially important information will be obtained from determining the role of IL-33 and ST2 in these autoimmune diseases.
kw: Spondyloarthritis, Synovium, Cytokines

title: Advanced FO Membranes and Membrane Systems for Wastewater Treatment, Water Reuse and Seawater Desalination
abs: The forward osmosis (FO) process is an emerging membrane technology for water reuse and desalination. The osmotic pressure gradient between the feed and draw solution supplies a spontaneous driving force for water transport. The semi-permeable membrane that retains ions but allows water through is the heart of the FO process. Compared with traditional pressure-driven membrane processes, FO requires less energy expenditure to induce a net flow of water across the membrane and offers recognized advantages including a high rejection rate of contaminants, more reversible membrane fouling and a lower operational energy demand. Therefore, FO membranes have great potential to replace (i) ultra-filtration (UF) membranes currently used in membrane bioreactor (MBR) for wastewater and municipal water reuse, and (ii) reverse osmosis (RO) membranes for seawater desalination. The major challenges of the current FO technology are (i) ineffective membranes which are the hearts of osmotic MBR (OMBR) and desalination systems and (ii) lack of user friendly and economic draw solutes that can be recycled easily. Therefore, we will conduct fundamental research on novel FO membrane materials with superior semipermeable characteristics (i.e., high flux and salt retention), design highly hydrophilic draw solutes with characteristics of high osmotic pressure, easy recovery and low cost for desalination and OMBR, and study hollow fiber membrane bioreactors based on FO for the activated sludge process, and for treating high strength industrial wastewater. The successful development of FO membranes and draw solutes for water reuse and desalination will significantly revolutionize the water and desalination industries. The recycle of wastewater and municipal water, and the desalination of seawater can be made much more affordable and sustainable with reduced energy consumptions compared with the current hydraulic pressure driven processes.

title: Tracking hydro-climate variation in the tropical Indo-Pacific with highly resolved cave records
abs: Hydro-climate of the tropical Indo-Pacific is critical to the socio-economic health of the region. In a warming world, it is predicted that regions of high rainfall today will become wetter while dry lands will become drier. These predictions could be tested with past hydro-climate proxy data. However, the current lack of long and precisely dated paleoclimate records prohibits a full understanding of the regional climate variability. Cave carbonate deposits have been demonstrated to provide highly resolved records of climate variability with robust ages. Many caves are known from this region, and thus it is possible to develop the needed paleoclimate records. I propose to reconstruct continuous, well dated, high-resolution hydro-climate records covering the last ~100,000 years in the tropical Indo-Pacific, by using cave carbonates from southern Sulawesi, western Sumatra, and central Myanmar. The records will be absolutely dated by the high precision uranium-thorium method on a multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer. Multiple geochemical tracers, including both elemental (e.g., Mg/Ca and Sr/Ca) and isotopic (e.g., 18O/16O, 13C/12C, and 234U/238U) ratios, will be applied to establish the regional hydro-climate history. Cave sites are carefully selected to encompass areas that are under the influence of the Asian monsoon, but each site represents a distinctive aspect of the regional climate regime, including the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, the Indian Ocean Dipole and the monsoon. Therefore, comparisons among the records will reveal the interactions among these climatic phenomena through time. The records will also be compared with other regional and global datasets to investigate the forcing mechanisms in the regional climate system, the role of the tropics in global climate cycles, and the ultimate mechanisms responsible for the glacial-age abrupt climate change. Moreover, I will use the records, with ultra-high temporal resolution, to test the connection between climate and culture in this region.
kw: tropical Indo-Pacific;hydro-climate;speleothem;U-Th dating;glacial-interglacail;civilization

title: Implantable Ceramic-Based Porous Carriers Loaded with High-Yield Stem Cells for Bone Regeneration and Remodeling
abs: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have vast potential for treating several diseases, directing towards creating a more sustainable, outcome-orientated healthcare delivery system, thereby benefiting both the ageing and young population. Although advances have been made in defining conditions to promote MSC self-renewal and differentiation, a major barrier to the development of MSC-based therapies is the inability to expand these cells in abundance, usually in a scale of hundreds of millions within a single run, using the existing basic technique of culturing in plastic T75 flasks. For example, to obtain 500 million MSCs will require approximately 600 T75 flasks and 10 litres of cell medium, which is labour-intensive and costly. The process of repeated trypsinisation is also likely to lead to reduced intra-cellular signaling responsible for cellular survival, proliferation and differentiation. Furthermore, such exposure will present a risk of infection with other pathogens that could be transmitted to the patients when these MSCs are transplanted. Certainly, a carrier cell culture system which mimics the microenvironment in-vivo for cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, offers an effective alternative technique to obtain sufficient MSCs for transplantations. Existing available carriers in the market are made of polymers or glass-based matrices which are unsuitable for therapeutic implantations, such as in bone implant science.This proposal aims to (i) develop suitable novel apatite-based porous microbeads as cell carriers; (ii) establish the apatite-based porous microbeads as an efficient tool for obtaining high yield MSC isolation and expansion in culture; (iii) establish apatite-based porous microbeads as an efficient platform for driving directed differentiation of MSCs into osteogenesis in culture; and (iv) evaluate the efficacy of the MSC-loaded apatite-based porous microbeads to generate ectopic bone formation in-vivo. This porous microcarrier will not only facilitate MSC expansion and differentiation, but also serves as an implantable system to support bone tissue repair after implantation.
kw: Stem Cells, Apatites, Bone, Implant Science, Microcarriers

title: Monoclonal Antibody Targeting of Nuclear Autoantigens to Specific Antigen-presenting Cells: Investigation of Autoantibody Induction
abs: Traditional strategies in vaccine development, using killed or attenuated pathogens, led to numerous effective vaccines. However, for more invasive pathogens, these strategies are overwhelmed. Recombinant vaccines have held great promises but few succeed. A more recent, fast-growing strategy is the targeting of antigens to antigen-presenting cells (APCs), especially DCs.The core techniques in antigen targeting are to link antigens to monoclonal antibody (mAb) specific for APC surface receptors and then inject these conjugate into mice. A major challenge is the access to adequate APC-specific mAbs (1-10 mg level). A second challenge is the generation of viable mAb-antigen conjugates. In a recent sabbatical stint, the applicant has acquired well-tested 15 hybridoma cell lines including N418 (CD11c), F4/80 (macrophages), and ID3 (B cells). The applicant also co-developed an mAb-antigen conjugation protocol. Here we will evaluate this platform by linking mouse nuclear antigens to the three mAbs. The conjugates are injected to mice to evaluate which APC type instigates the antinuclear antigen autoantibody production.Antinuclear antibodies are proven pathogenic in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a major autoimmune disease, and are proven pathogenic because they deposit in connective tissue and cause tissue inflammation and injuries in multiple organs. As self-antigens, how they elicit the immune system and cause antinuclear autoantibodies is unknown. While this inevitable involves the breakdown of tolerance and defective APC functions, which APC is instigative is also unknown. With this question, we will isolate nuclear antigens (nucleosomes) and use mAbs to target these antigens to specific APCs so as to evaluate which APC type causes autoantibody production and/or SLE disease. With this project, we hope to develop a protocol for antigen targeting in vivo which can be applied to vaccine development and also to establish an SLE mouse model focusing specifically on tolerance breakdown at the autoantigen-APC interface.
kw: APC, vaccines, monoclonal antibody, autoimmunity, nuclear antigen, dendritic cell

title: Does polyphenol supplementation improve vascular function? A cross-over study incorporating markers of oxidative damage, endothelial and platelet function
abs: Despite results from population studies suggesting that adopting polyphenol-rich diets may protect against cardiovascular disease, the benefit of dietary polyphenols as part of a diet or as supplements is unclear.The aims of the study are:1. To examine if specific dietary polyphenols, such as quercetin, (-)-epicatechin and theaflavin, exert acute anti-platelet effects in young smokers by regulating activities and expressions of platelet cyclooxygenase-1 and P2Y12 receptors.2. To examine if specific dietary polyphenols, such as quercetin, (-)-epicatechin and theaflavin, acutely improve endothelial function in young smokers via modulation of endothelial nitric oxide synthase and cytochrome P450 activities and expressions.3. To examine if specific dietary polyphenols, such as quercetin, (-)-epicatechin and theaflavin, alleviate inflammation acutely in young smokers by regulating the activities and expressions of pro-inflammatory mediators, such as myeloperoxidase and leukotriene B4.We hypothesize that pure specific dietary polyphenols improve human vascular health. This is achieved by reducing the extent of vascular reactivity via modulation of inflammatory responses, anti-platelet effects and endothelial function. We propose a randomised controlled, cross-over, double-blinded trial in healthy individuals to examine the effects of acute exposure to specific dietary polyphenols in smokers. This study aims to elucidate the in vivo mechanisms of dietary flavonoids on vascular function and their cellular interactions. Results of such studies are pivotal to the evaluation of dietary polyphenols for cardiovascular protection.

title: Cell Death Index as a Novel, Rapid and Valuable Tool for Classification of Antimalarial Drug Action
abs: The devastation of malaria has been a major concern for decades, especially in poor countries. Despite the global concerted effort to eradicate malaria, the parasite’s evolving resistance against antimalarials has enabled the disease to persist and spread. As such, the development of novel antimalarials is imperative and even these must be used in combination so as to prevent or delay the onset of resistant strains. We suggest a new way of classifying antimalarials based on their mechanisms of action, instead of their structures, to facilitate combination therapy. Three parameters gathered from two programmed cell death (PCD) assays were evaluated for three groups of well-known antimalarials and used to generate drug cell death indexes (CDI). A multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) statistical analysis done on the drug indexes re-classified the antimalarials into sub-divisions of the current groups. The current proposal seeks to extend the list to include most currently used antimalarials and subsequently validated with two drug libraries. Future studies (as in an IRG proposal) will include the validation of this method in generating clinically relevant drug combinations for combination therapy.

title: Analysis of novel genes in microglia and their implications in neurodegenerative diseases
abs: Microglial cells respond to CNS diseases and injuries and remove the damaged cells by phagocytosis. Morphologically, microglial cells are classified into amoeboid and ramified. The ramified microglia become hypertrophic, attain an amoeboid shape, proliferate and migrate when activated by neurodegenerative stimuli. In general, the microglia have a neuroprotective function by secreting neurotrophic agents and eliminating debris including beta-amyloid via phagocytosis. Mounting evidence indicates that chronic activation of microglia causes neurotoxicity through the release of potentially cytotoxic molecules such as proinflammatory cytokines and reactive oxygen intermediates indicating that microglial cells play a significant role in the progression of the AD. It is hypothesized that morphological differences in amoeboid, ramified and pathologically activated microglia are functionally relevant and are regulated by a specific set of genes. To address this, we performed a microarray analysis and compared the transcription profiles of amoeboid with that of ramified microglia. The novel gene LRRGT (Genbank id AI228978) was found to be highly specific and highest expressed in the amoeboid microglia. Other set of genes regulating cell proliferation, differentiation and migration such as the Septins and Sox11 were also identified to be differentially expressed. Therefore, suppression of microglia-mediated inflammation by the study of novel genes may prove to be an important strategy in mitigating neurodegenerative diseases including AD
kw: neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, microglia, novel genes

title: An isoform specific role for Fyn tyrosine kinase (FynT) in reactive astrogliosis : Relevance to Alzheimer’s disease
abs: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia in old age. One of the hallmarks of AD is the accumulation of amyloid plaques in the brain. Astrocytes, being the most common cell type in the brain, provide essential supports for brain homeostasis including neuronal growth and synaptic development. Reactive astrogliosis, whereby astrocytes undergo molecular and morphological changes in response to disease-relevant stresses, seems to exert both beneficial and detrimental effects. Reactive astrogliosis surrounding amyloid plaques is a well-known pathological feature of AD. However, its role in AD progression remains virtually unexplored. In our preliminary study, we observed significant increase of FynT expression in AD as compared to control samples. FynT is one of the isoforms of Fyn tyrosine kinase which predominantly expressed in T lymphocytes. Most importantly, expression of FynT but not FynB, the isoform that found mainly in the brain, showed significant correlation with neuritic plaque, neurofibrillary tangle counts and cognitive impairment. Further analysis revealed that FynT expression was positively correlated with genes associated with cell morphology, cellular movement, extracellular matrix and reactive astrocytic markers; and negatively correlated with synaptic-associated genes. Furthermore, we showed that FynT was primarily expressed in the cells of astrocytic origin. In summary, we hypothesize that FynT may play an important role in the process of astrocyte reactivation. In this study, we would like to (1) determine FynT over-expression in AD is associated with astrocyte reactivation; (2) identify the role of FynT tyrosine kinase activity in reactive astrocytes, whether they have neuroprotective or neurodegenerative effect towards AD. Identification of the impact of FynT activity in the progression of AD is of clinical significance because FynT might serve as a potential target of therapeutic intervention for AD through modulating the status of reactive astrocytes.
kw: astrogliosis, Fyn tyrosine kinase, reactive astrocyte, Alzheimer disease, neuroinflammation

title: Investigation of the role of serum amyloid A in atherosclerosis through initiation of apoptosis
abs: Specific AimsAtherosclerosis is one of the major killers in developed countries and its prevalence is increasing in developing countries. Serum amyloid A (SAA) has been identified as a biomarker of atherosclerosis. Much attention is now on determining its role in atherosclerosis. In view that apoptosis in endothelial cells is an initial cause of atherosclerosis, we aim to:I. Determine if SAA induces apoptosis in vascular endothelial cellsII. Validate genes and proteins related to apoptosis which we previously identified through microarray gene expression studies to be regulated as a result of SAA exposure. III. a) Determine if SAA promotes oxidative stress through enhancing intracellular ROS levels b) Devise strategies to inhibit the effect of SAA on apoptosis.All three aims will generate novel findings as these have never been investigated.Hypothesis We hypothesize that SAA induces apoptosis in vascular endothelial cells by acting on genes and proteins involved in the apoptotic pathway. Apoptosis of these endothelial cells results in cell aggregation, endothelial dysfunction and subsequently, atherosclerosis. Methodology and ApproachHuman Coronary Artery Endothelial Cells and Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells will be treated with SAA at various concentrations (5-40ug/ml) for 24h and 48h with media as control. The proportion of viable cells will be compared between control and treated cells using MTT assay. Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling assay will be carried out to detect DNA fragmentation, which is an apoptotic characteristic. To elucidate the likely mechanisms through which SAA induces apoptosis, genes and proteins involved in apoptotic pathways will be measured using real-time-PCR, western blot and ELISA. Inhibitors of specific genes and proteins will be used to further confirm the results. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) induced by SAA will be measured and inhibited using antioxidants to determine if apoptosis is a consequential effect of ROS.
kw: apoptosis, Serum amyloid A, atherosclerosis

title: Exploration of Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Gamma (PPAR?) Agonist in Neurodegeneration Therapy – A Therapeutic Enigma
abs: Neurodegenerative disorders are a group of brain diseases characterized by selective and gradual loss of neurons, with the more common forms being Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Huntington’s disease (HD). Studies have shown that mitochondrial dysfunction is likely to be an essential common theme in these neurodegenerative disorders.It has also been revealed that PPARy coactivator 1a (PGC-1a) expression is downregulated in brain tissues of patients with AD, PD, and HD. Therapeutic effects of PPARy agonist have been observed in various animal models for neurodegenerative disorders. However, no evidence of efficacy of PPARy agonist was detected in any of the patient populations. We hypothesize that the discrepancy in efficacy of PPARy agonist in Alzheimer’s disease patients from preclinical findings was due to poor permeation of the drug through the blood brain barrier. In vivo brain penetration of orally administered PPARy agonist can be enhanced with co-administration of GF120918, a dual inhibitor for permeability-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) efflux transporters. Metabonomics analyses using gas chromatography time-of-flight mass spectrometry (GC/TOFMS) and high resolution magic angle spinning nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (HR-MAS NMR) can be used to uncover novel mechanistic pathway underlying the therapeutic benefits of PPARy agonist in neurodegenerative disorders.
kw: pharmacokinetics, PPAR gamma Agonist, Neurodegenerative disease, Blood brain barrier, Metabonomics

title: An assessment of gastric mucosal IL-22 expressing cells in intestinal metaplasia associated with Helicobacter pylori infection
abs: Infection with Helicobacter pylori (HP) elicits a chronic inflammatory response in the gastric mucosa, and also triggers a step-wise progression of pre-malignant mucosal changes that may result in gastric adenocarcinoma. The appearance of intestinal metaplasia (IM) may represent a critical stage of no return in this pathological cascade. However, not all HP patients develop IM or gastric adenocarcinoma, and we currently have no good way of identifying HP-infected individuals who are at increased risk of progression to IM and cancer. In our preliminary data for this proposal, we have made the novel observation that HP patients with IM express lower levels of gastric mucosal IL-22 than HP patients without IM. We hypothesise this is due to a reduction in the number of cells that express IL-22 in the gastric mucosa. This is significant because IL-22 has a role in epithelial regeneration and the maintainance of epithelial integrity. In this proposal, we aim to characterise the cellular sources of IL-22 in the gastric mucosa of HP-infected individuals, in order to determine whether specific subsets of IL-22-producing cells are reduced in patients with IM. To do this, we will obtain gastric biopsy specimens from a cohort of HP patients with IM, or without IM, and employ immunofluorescence microscopy and immunohistochemistry to identify and enumerate subsets of IL-22 expressing cells in these biopsy samples. We will also expand lamina propria mononuclear cells from biopsy samples and stimulate them with HP antigens to characterise the HP-specific IL-22 responses in these patients. By determining whether particular subsets of IL-22 producing cells are deficient in IM patients, we may be able to better understand the pathophysiology of HP-induced gastric cancer, and identify biomarkers that can be used to predict HP patients with increased risk of progression to IM and gastric cancer.
kw: Helicobacter pylori, Interleukin 22, Mucosal immunity, Immune regulation, Intestinal metaplasia

title: Investigating serum exosomes as a source of biomarkers to prospectively stratify pregnant women at risk for preterm birth, intra-uterine growth restriction and pre-eclampsia
abs: Preterm birth, intra-uterine growth retardation and pre-eclampsia account for ~70% of adverse pregnancy outcomes. Robust predictive biomarkers or a better understanding of their pathophysiology will prevent or enable early intervention to improve these outcomes. This proposal will explore the possibility of using serum exosomes to identify novel biomarkers for pre-term delivery, pre-eclampsia and intra-uterine growth retardation. The rationale is that as exosome composition is regulated by the pathophysiological state of cells, exosomes are likely to be enriched for disease-associated biomarkers. In this study, we propose using serum from the prospective cohort of 1000 women to be recruited for follow-up from the first trimester till delivery in the NMRC-funded NORA1 study. Second trimester serum of small patient sample groups within NORA-1 will be pooled into four groups that have: 1) pre-term birth, 2) pre-eclampsia, 3) intra-uterine growth retardation and 4) normal pregnancy. Exosomes will be purified from these pooled sera and analyzed for their RNA and protein profiles. The profiles from the first three groups will be compared to that from women who had normal pregnancy. Those RNAs or proteins that are unique to at least one of the first three groups will be selected as candidate diagnostic biomarkers or potential causative agents in the pathogenesis of these conditions. These candidate biomarkers will form the supporting preliminary data for larger studies to validate the biomarkers in the 1000 NORA-1 patient cohort and develop diagnostic assays to address a critical unmet clinical need. As these exosome-based biomarkers are likely to reflect the pathophysiological states of the patients, they could potentially be used in other studies to investigate the underlying molecular pathophysiology of these conditions.
kw: Bio-markers, Exosomes, Pre-eclampsia (PE), Intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR), Pre-term labour

title: Marrying microRNAs and microfluidics to spawn new insights in CNS axon regeneration.
abs: In the adult central nervous system (CNS), injured axons fail to regenerate, leading to devastating and permanent disabilities after spinal cord injury, strokes, or other CNS trauma. A large body of evidence indicates that CNS neurons progressively lose the capacity to regenerate as they mature. This age-dependent decline in regenerative growth has been associated with a developmental switch that occurs as axons reach their synaptic targets; axons must stop growing and the axonal growth cone has to differentiate into a presynaptic terminal. According to this model, global changes of gene expression that occur upon synaptogenesis lock CNS neurons in a fully-differentiated state and prevent reactivation of an axon growth program. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are short non-coding RNA molecules that function as posttranscriptional regulators of gene expression. miRNAs are highly expressed in the CNS and have been implicated in neurite outgrowth, dendritic spine morphogenesis and synaptic plasticity. Recent profiling studies show that miRNA expression patterns markedly vary during neuronal differentiation and aging, as well as in response to neuronal activity, suggesting that global miRNA-dependent changes in gene expression may contribute to the poor regeneration capacity of adult CNS neurons.Here, we propose to develop a novel microfluidics-based imaging assay to study the inhibitory role of synapse differentiation and neuronal activity on CNS axon regeneration. Using this assay, we will test the hypothesis that miRNAs regulate axon regeneration in differentiated CNS neurons. This project explores a novel experimental paradigm to identify genes relevant to CNS axon regeneration, with the ultimate aim of designing
