title: Diabetic Retinopathy: ARRESTING DIABETIC RETINOPATHY AND IMPROVING QUALITY OF LIFE - Identifying the factors influencing effective diabetic management and proposing a novel care model
abs: Diabetes mellitus is a major public health priority in Singapore affecting approximately one in twelve Singaporeans aged 18 to 69 years. This figure is likely to increase because of our ageing population and an increasing prevalence of risk factors, such as obesity and sedentary practices. Moreover, it is estimated that up to half of those affected are unaware they have the condition. One of the most severe complications of diabetes is diabetic retinopathy(DR). Recent data indicate that less than one in five Singaporeans with DR maintain a good diabetes control suggesting that access to health care and public health messages have a minimal impact on optimal diabetes management in this the community . This study plans to implement an evidenced-based approach to diabetes management in people with diabetes and DR . It proposes first to identify barriers and facilitators that differentiate patients with good and poor control. With these new data, the second aim of this novel project is to develop a new evidenced-based model of diabetes care with a patient-centred and personalized approach. Patients with diabetes will be recruited from the Singapore National Eye Centre. They will undergo a comprehensive ophthalmological examination to assess their severity of DR and blood investigations to assess their glycemic control. They will also undergo several interviewer-administered questionnaires to obtain data on dietary and lifestyle habits; self efficacy; disease education; and perception barriers to self care;, quality of life and health status; emotional well being; as well as confidence in performing diabetes self-care activities.The outcomes of this study are the identification of unique factors affecting diabetic control in people with DR and a novel diabetes care model to improve diabetes control; delay the progression and incidence of DR; and improve self efficacy and quality of life in Singaporeans living with diabetes.
kw: Self Care, Diabetes, Diabetic retinopathy, Patient education

title: Sclera Cross-linking in the Experimental Rabbit Eye Model
abs: Introduction: Myopia is an increasingly common affliction of urbanization and is characterised by enlarged ocular axial length. It is associated with chorioretinal pathologies, and incurs huge costs in management. Purpose: To examine the effect of subtenon glyceraldehyde injection on refractive status in rabbits.Setting: Singapore Eye Research InstituteMaterials and Methods: Previous published studies demonstrated a more than 1000% increase in the Young modulus of rabbit sclera treated with glyceraldehyde crosslinking.Background data on rabbit eye growth is available from SERI. Glyceraldehyde is biologically non-toxic, and causes glycation-induced chemical cross-linking. Singhealth Institutional Care and Use Committee application had been approved for this study. Our preliminary study on a rabbit eye injected with subtenon glyceraldehyde at 37 degrees celsius had shown a more than 6 times increase in sclera tensile strength.Four groups of eight rabbits will be treated with parabulbar (subtenon) injections of 0.10 mL 0.5 M glyceraldehyde dissolved in a solute or gel at four different meridians, at 4 time points (post-natal age of one month, 6 weeks, 2 months and 3 months). The rabbits will be treated unilaterally, with the untreated eye serving as control. Primary outcomes such as axial length measurements with A-scan ultrasound and refraction with a handheld autorefractor will be performed weekly, as well as secondary outcome of intraocular pressure with the Tonopen. Four animals in each group will be sacrificed 2 weeks post-treatment, and ocular tissues obtained for secondary outcome studies of stress-strain function, histology, biochemistry and toxicology. The remaining rabbits will be followed up for at least two months post-treatment. Four other rabbits will serve as controls, with one eye each treated with sham saline injections. Outcome measures will be compared between the treated and untreated eyes, and to controls and previous preliminary data. Results will be analysed with T-test for statistical significance.
kw: Cellular toxicity, Myopia progression, Sclera cross-linking, Axial length, Rabbit model, Glyceraldehyde

title: Novel Ocular Biometric Risk Factors in Primary Angle Closure
abs: Primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) is a leading cause of visual loss, particularly in Asian countries. The rate of blindness from PACG exceeds that from primary open-angle glaucoma, which is more common than in Western countries. The early detection and treatment of angle closure, before the onset of glaucomatous optic neuropathy, would lead to less visual morbidity and improved visual prognosis. However, existing modes of screening are inadequate, and current treatment strategies for PACG do not address all the mechanisms involved in angle closure. Studies have suggested that ocular biometric risk factors, may be key predisposing factors for PACG. The development of anterior-segment optical coherence tomography (ASOCT) has further allowed objective visualization of the angle structures. It remains unclear what ocular biometric risk factors and parameters are the major risk factors for angle closure.This study will investigate and quantify ocular biometric and anterior segment parameters in angle closure from ASOCT images, with the following Specific Aims:1) To identify novel ocular biometric risk factors and anterior segment parameters from ASOCT images between subjects with angle closure and normal population controls. 2) To quantify differences in anterior segment parameters between age groups and different races from ASOCT images with an aim to provide normative data in the general Asian population.To achieve these aims, we will analyze ASOCT scans from 570 subjects with angle closure. This includes 300 subjects recruited from glaucoma clinics in two tertiary institutions, and 270 subjects recruited from three population-based studies. We will compare ASOCT data with 2423 controls who have been obtained from the population-based studies. This study will identify a range of ocular biometric risk factors for angle closure, which can be used in the determination of optimal screening strategies for persons at risk of angle closure.
kw: Imaging, Angle closure, Glaucoma

title: Generation and validation of genetic mouse models for HCC with cirrhosis and mutant p53 -reliable preclinical therapeutic testing tools in vivo.
abs: Hepatocellularcarinoma (HCC) is a common human malignancy usually associated with underlying liver diseases such as cirrhosis. Systemic chemotherapy is generally ineffective. Although new targeted therapeutics improve the overall survival benefits of HCC patients, the increase is very marginal and response rate remains low, despite the promising and robust response was observed in initial pre-clinical xenograft models. Therefore, there is some degree of discrepancy in the results between current pre-clinical animal models and clinical trial in patients. It is noteworthy that most commonly used pre-clinical xenograft models for HCC completely ignore the involvement of the immune system, cirrhosis and important genetic aberrations such as p53 mutation. We therefore hypothesize that the lack of these major factors in the pre-clinical model is the cause of inaccurate evaluation of therapeutics efficacy. Hence, we propose to generate genetically modified (GM) mouse models in which de novo HCCs with different p53 genotypes are developed in livers with underlying cirrhotic lesion. Using this model, we will be able to investigate the functional significance of these major factors and their interactions in hepatocarcinogenesis. This model also allows us to validate the novel potential application of DCE MRI modality for accessing liver cirrhosis. Furthermore, we strongly believe that the GM mice, in which all the major factors (chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis and complete loss/mutation of p53) of HCC are present, will faithfully recapitulate a key feature in human HCC – treatment resistance. More importantly, these GM mice will be excellent tools for evaluating novel therapeutics in future and offer higher accuracy in evaluating efficacy. With a collaborative effort of clinicians, scientists, public research institutions and pharmaceutical industry, we will be able evaluate efficacy more accurately in pre-clinical studies with the use of GM mouse models, hence, increasing the success rate of clinical trials, ultimately bringing better therapy to HCC patients.
kw: Genetically modified mouse model, Cirrhosis, Diagnostic imaging, HCC, P53, Targeted therapy

title: Role of TRPM4 channel in cerebral blood vessels of ischemic stroke
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Stroke is common with a 3.65% prevalence rate in the Singapore population and an expected rising incidence with our ageing population. It is the leading cause of adult disability and 4th most common cause of mortality in Singapore. Ischemic stroke is the predominant stroke subtype affecting elder patients due to the occlusion of cerebral blood vessels. Acute treatment focuses on the vascular recanalization. However, reperfusion increases the risk of hemorrhage. Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 4 channel (TRPM4) was recently identified to be critical in vascular integrity. Hypoxia induced ATP depletion can activate the channel to flux in monovalants that potentially lead to oncotic cell death. TRPM4 is expressed at low level in vessels. De novo expression of TRPM4 was found in capillaries in spinal cord after traumatic injury and caused secondary hemorrhage. Hypotheses: TRPM4 could play a critical role in ischemic stroke. De novo expression of TRPM4 after stroke could damage vascular endothelium. Our preliminary data showed an upregulation of TRPM4 coupled with angiogenesis as early as 6 hours after stroke in a rat model. siRNA application tends to reduce the infarct. Furthermore, we detected an increase of TRPM4 mRNA in the blood of rats with stroke. To extend our study, we will investigate the expression of TRPM4 and its functional role in angiogenesis and vascular injury during ischemia reperfusion after ischemic stroke both in rats and TRPM4 mice. We will also establish the expression profile of TRPM4 in the blood of human stroke patients. Understanding the role of TRPM4 in vascular integrity after ischemic stroke is important as angiogenesis determines neurogenesis. De novo expression of TRPM4 provides a potential target for treating stroke. As a pilot study, we will generate polyclonal antibodies that can block TRPM4 specifically and use it to treat stroke animals.
kw: Ischemic stroke, Ischemia reperfusion, Ion channel, Angiogenesis, Biomarker, Calcium homeostasis

title: Tumor-Selective Transgene Expression for Glioma Therapy Mediated by Human iPS CellDerived Neural Stem Cells
abs: Owing to their migratory capacity and tumor tropism, neural stem cells (NSCs) have recently emerged as one of the most attractive cellular vehicles for targeted gene delivery into cancers, including highlyaggressive malignant glioblastoma multiforme. Recent progress in creating human inducible pluripotent stem (iPS) cells has provided a great opportunity of using the iPS cells as a reliable and accessible source to generate unlimited amounts of human NSCs. iPS cell-based approaches also help bypass the sensitive ethical issue surrounding the use of human embryonic stem cells. However,since NSCs can be chemoattracted to non-target regions especially after systemic administration, offtarget transgene expression is still a concern for the clinical application of NSC-mediated cancer gene therapy. To minimize this side effect, approaches that enable tumor site-selective transgene expression are desirable. This project attempts to develop a novel regulatory system that functionswithin human iPS cell-derived NSCs to achieve glioma-selective expression of transgenes. Designed based on the unique features of tumor microenvironment, two systems will be developed and tested for their ability in regulating transgene expression in NSC vehicles in an inducible manner in response to either tumor acidosis or tumor hypoxia. Off-target transgene expression will be further controlled byincorporation into the expression cassette of targeting sequences of microRNAs that express at high levels in non-target sites. Our studies on the specificity and efficacy of the two approaches will suggestthe feasibility of a novel therapeutic intervention for glioblastoma multiforme.
kw: Glioblastoma multiforme, Gene therapy, Neural stem cells, Human iPS cells, Tumor targeting

title: Investigation of the tumor suppressor functions of Sema5A and plexin-B3 in human gliomas
abs: Gliomas are the most common tumor in the central nervous system. Among them glioblastoma mutliforme is notorious for its high invasiveness and resistance to radiotherapy, leading to a high recurrence rate even after radical surgical resection and a short survival after initial diagnosis. Characterization of glioma at the molecular level revealed aberrant activation of the Ras/PI3K/Akt/ /Rac1 and the integrin/FAK/Rac1 pathways that contribute to heightened invasion and proliferation features. Recently, accumulating evidence points to the emerging role of axon guidance molecules such as semaphorins, neuropilins, and plexins in glioma progression. We have previously demonstrated the effects of Sema5A and plexin-B3 in inhibiting glioma cell migration and invasion by Rac1 inactivation via RhoGDIa. Our recent data show their involvement in the suppression of glioma cell proliferation. Since Sema4D and plexin-B1 have formerly been shown to negatively regulate the R-Ras and integrin pathways, we hypothesize that plexin-B3 may respond to Sema5A stimulation by toning down the R-Ras-related and/or integrin/FAK pathways, thereby suppressing cell adhesion, migration, and proliferation. In fact, we provide evidence that stimulation of human glioma cells with Sema5A causes a disruption of focal adhesions in a plexin-B3 dependent manner. This proposal aims to further elucidate the mechanisms of the tumor suppressor functions of Sema5A and pelxin-B3 by systematically assaying for the activation status of key intermediate signaling molecules in these candidate pathways. Backed by our recent observation of a significant reduction of Sema5A expression in high grade gliomas, which are highly infiltrative and resistant to radio-/chemotherapies, we proposed to substantiate the tumor suppressor hypothesis by evaluating the efficacy of exogenous Sema5A in counteracting infiltration and proliferation of glioma cells in in vivo model of brain tumors. Taken together, validation of the importance of Sema5A and plexin-B3 in glioma progression may render them as potential therapeutic targets.
kw: brain cancers, semaphorins, plexins, invasion, proliferation

title: Active targeting of tuberculosis via novel nanotherapeutics
abs: Tuberculosis (TB) is the second most deadly infectious disease and is a major challenge in public health. Although the incidence in Singapore has been relatively low, the number of cases is still higher than that for most western industrialized countries. Drug resistant TB is also now widespread and a threat to TB control programs in many countries. It is widely recognized that there is a need for the development of new and effective diagnostics, vaccines and antimycobacterial drugs. Our long term goal is thus to develop novel nanotherapeutics to meet this challenge. Our previous work has shown that cationic core/shell nanoparticles (micelles) self-assembled from amphiphilic peptides are an emerging class of novel antibiotics but challenges in peptide therapeutics such as hemolytic toxicity, instability and high cost are likely to impede their further development. To overcome this, we propose to develop novel cationic polycarbonate oligomers with structural prerequisites of these antimicrobial peptides and use them as nanoparticles for the targeted delivery of antimycobacterial drugs. We hypothesize that these polymeric nanoparticles can kill mycobacteria more effectively than conventional drugs by (i) having intrinsic antimycobacterial activity, and (ii) offloading antimycobacterial drugs strategically at TB infection reservoirs. Functional polycarbonate polymers will be synthesized via a metal-free ring-opening polymerization process and used as nanoparticles to deliver antimycobacterial drugs specifically to alveolar macrophages. We will also determine the in vitro and in vivo antimycobacterial activity of the nanotherapeutics. In the long term, our studies will show that better therapeutic effect can be achieved and drug resistance can be prevented with the use of cationic polycarbonate nanoparticles for the delivery of antimycobacterials. This will significantly improve patient compliance and adherence to TB drug regimens and may provide an alternative/adjunct therapeutic strategy to multidrug resistant TB.
kw: tuberculosis, nanoparticles, therapeutics, polycarbonates, alveolar macrophages, drug resistance

title: The effects of steroid therapy on satellite cells and fibro-adipocytes in Duchenne and Becker Muscular Dystrophy
abs: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) and Becker Muscular Dystrophy (BMD) are allelic disorders resulting from mutations of the dystrophin gene. Dystrophin protein is responsible for maintaining sarcolemma integrity of muscle cell and therefore loss of dystrophin function leads to sarcolemma ruptures and progressive muscle necrosis. In addition, fibrotic tissue accumulation and fatty infiltration is also reported in dystrophic muscle. To date no direct therapy is available to restore wild type dystrophin expression and contain muscle loss. In clinical practice however, steroids are known to enhance strength and to retard progression of muscle degeneration in DMD and BMD patients. The action of steroids on dystrophic muscle is unclear although it was recently demonstrated ultrastructurally that steroid therapy is associated with increased numbers of satellite cells in skeletal muscle. Satellite cells (SC) are quiescent muscle stem cells that are responsible for furnishing new muscle fibers during muscle regeneration and therefore, SC are credited with maintenance of the skeletal muscle mass. We hypothesize that this increase in SC number due to steroids treatment could be due to increased proliferation and self-renewal of SC, which will lead to increase muscle growth and regeneration in dystrophic muscle. The aims of the study therefore are (i) firstly to examine the systemic effects of steroid treatment on satellite cell behavior in explant culture systems (ii) secondly to identify the molecular mechanism through which steroids increase satellite cell numbers and (iii) finally identify the beneficial effects of steroids in alleviating the fibrosis and fatty infiltration in muscle during disease progression. The treatment of DMD/BMD requires a multipronged approach. Therefore a combination therapy that includes drugs, which will not only enhance satellite cells biology but also alleviate fibrotic tissue accumulation and fatty infiltration in muscle will certainly increase muscle strength and prolong life expectancy of dystrophic patients.
kw: Muscular dystrophy, Glucocorticoids, Steroids, Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, Becker muscular dystrophy, Satellite cells

title: The Role of Mast Cells in Dengue Virus Induced Vascular Leakage
abs: Dengue virus (DENV) is a human pathogen that is of growing global concern. The 4 serotypes of DENV affect relatively distinct areas of the tropics and account for greater than 50 million infections yearly worldwide. Individuals become infected through mosquito bites, and the resulting disease can vary greatly in severity. While primary infections of each serotype result in a quickly contained febrile illness, secondary infections, especially those with a heterologous serotype, are more likely to result in possibly fatal complications including Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF), Dengue Shock Syndrome, thrombocytopenia, and a range of other vascular changes collectively falling under the umbrella of “dengue vasculopathy”. The current paradigm of the DENV field is that “antibody enhanced infection” causes of vasculopathy, where increased uptake of virus by phagocytic cells allows enhanced viral replication and higher viral titers. Here, we propose that higher viral titers, alone, may not explain the pathological hemorrhagic sequelae of DHF and we have identified another cell type which binds antibodies, the mast cell (MC), as a potential mediator of DENV-induced vascular changes. Our provided preliminary data shows that MC sensitization with DENV-specific antibodies may contribute to the pathogenesis of DENV during secondary infections through the ability of these cells to detect DENV and to promote vascular permeability. We now aim to determine if MC sensitization can contribute to DHF in the absence of a specific memory response, as is clinically observed when a secondary DENV challenge is of a different serotype than the primary challenge. Additionally, we hope to limit vascular leakage in DENV-infected animals using the drug Cromolyn, a well known MC stabilizing drug. If effective, this would constitute a novel and potentially clinically relevant strategy for the treatment of individuals with vascular complications associated with severe DENV infection.
kw: vasculopathy, mast cell

title: The role of eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha phosphorylation in amyloid-beta induced dendritic spine loss
abs: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia in the elderly. Synapse loss induced by amyloid beta (Aß) is thought to be a primary contributor to cognitive decline in AD. However, underlying molecular basis of Aß mediated synapse loss is not clear. Recent findings indicate levels of the phosphorylated form of eukaryotic initiation factor-2 alpha (eIF2a) are elevated significantly in neurons exposed to Aß in the brain of animal models of AD and human AD patients. Because eIF2a phosphorylation suppresses efficacy of mRNA translation and de novo protein synthesis, we propose that the altered phosphorylation state of eIF2a evoked by Aß may underlie synapse loss and cognitive impairment in AD. We will investigate changes in signaling pathways involved in Aß mediated eIF2a phosphorylation in neurons. Next, using cultured hippocampal organotypic slices, an ideal system to study spine plasticity, we will examine whether the eIF2a phosphorylation is the central mechanism for Aß mediated dendritic synapse loss. Information gained from these studies will enable the design of novel therapeutic strategies to reduce Aß mediated synapse loss, providing a more effective management of AD.
kw: synaptic plasticity, eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha, amyloid-beta, GADD34, PP1, dendritic spine

title: Dissecting the Role of the Polypyrimidine Tract Binding Protein in Dengue VirusReplication: A Possible Target for Small Molecule Intervention
abs: Dengue virus (DENV is the etiologic agent of dengue diseases dengue fever, currently the mostprevalent arthropod-borne viral disease of humans, and dengue hemorrhagic fever. Despiteapproximately 3.6 billion people at risk, they are currently no commercially available vaccines oranti-viral drugs available to treat these dengue diseases. The lack of a viable interventionunderscores the need for a more complete understanding of the molecular mechanisms usedby DENV to infect human cells and propagate. The discovery and unraveling of the mechanismof host proteins interactions with the viral RNA genome, and their involvements in the viralreplication and life-cycle are clearly significant.The polypyrimidine tract-binding protein (PTB) is an RNA binding protein and is required forthe efficient proliferation of poliovirus, encephalomyocarditis virus and HCV. We have previouslyshown that PTB can bind to the DENV RNA genome during infection and that silencing itsexpression in human cells reduced the amount of infectious DENV produced. There are somesignificant issues yet to be addressed. Here, we propose to characterize the role PTB in DENVreplication with the following specific aims:(1) To characterize the molecular details of the PTB-DENV RNA interaction and thefunctional relevance of these interaction to DENV replication.(2) To ascertain the step in the viral life cycle that requires PTB. We will test the hypothesisthat PTB has a specific role in the viral RNA synthesis and not viral translation of the DENV,specifically that PTB is involved in the transcription of one of the two polarity viral RNA (positiveand negative viral RNA strand synthesis).At the conclusion of the two-year funding period we would have achieved a much betterunderstanding of mechanism of how PTB affects DENV in the virus lifecycle and form the basisfor rational small molecule-based intervention to DENV infections.
kw: Viral RNA synthesis, Host factors, PTB, Virus replication, Dengue

title: Glycemic and non-glycemic determinants of HbA1c, and the identification of novel markers of glycemia
abs: HbA1c is the most widely used method for assessing glycemic control. It has also been recently recommended as a diagnostic test for diabetes mellitus (DM). However, studies have suggested that a significant portion of intra-individual variation in HbA1c is attributable to non-glycemic factors. This study aims to evaluate the factors determining HbA1c levels in Chinese individuals, and to ascertain the relative roles of glycemic and non-glycemic factors in HbA1c determination. It is our hypothesis that glucose-independent factors may be particularly important in Chinese, as preliminary data from our studies suggests that fasting plasma glucose explains the lowest amount of Hba1c variance among our 3 local ethnic groups (Chinese, Malay and Indians). We are particularly interested in the HbA1c range of 5.0 to 7.5%, which brackets the currently recommended diagnostic threshold and therapeutic targets currently used worldwide. A secondary aim is to identify potential novel markers of glycemia that could be used as alternatives to HbA1c for the diagnosis and monitoring of DM. We will conduct a cross-sectional study involving 200 Chinese subjects with HbA1c 5.0-7.5%. Glucose profiles will be obtained using a using a continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS), together with measurements of HbA1c, red cell parameters and iron profiling. Determinants of HbA1c will be identified using multiple linear regression. We will identify novel glycated proteins using mass spectrometry immunoassay (MSIA), and compare the degree of correlation with glucose with that of HbA1c. Understanding glucose-independent factors is important in the interpretation of HbA1c values, especially in the context of deciding glycemic targets and thresholds for the diagnosis of DM. Given the limitations of HbA1c, a novel glycemic marker that is less influenced by non-glycemic factors may have widespread applicability in terms of diagnosis and monitoring of DM.

title: Feasibility study of polarimetry imaging for the diagnosis of gastric pathologies including pre-neoplasia and neoplasia
abs: We propose to perform a multi-spectral Mueller matrix polarimetry study on fresh gastric tissue slices to systematically investigate the relationship between measured polarization parameters and tissue biophysical properties at the different stages of histological cascade leading to neoplasia. We aim to investigate the relationship between tissue polarization parameters derived from polarimetry imaging and tissue biophysical properties for gastric pathologies including gastritis, gastric atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, low-grade dysplasia, high-grade dysplasia and cancer. Malignant moles were found to be less depolarizing than the surrounding tissue. High-speed polarity system for imaging oral precancer on hamster cheek pouches induced by DMBA showed that precancerous lesions depolarize less than healthy tissue. Depolarization power and diattenuation were sensitive parameters in discriminating normal cervical tissue and dysplasia. Analysis of polarimetric images of regular and malignant human tissues from the cervix, intestine, kidneys and breast showed the potential of polarimetry imaging for automated analysis of unstained tissue sections. While many biopsies will only contain mucosa in which nuclei size and density can be estimated, some biopsies may include submucosa and the distribution of collagen and elastin will be determined for these biopsies. In our proposed study, tissue specimen will be obtained from endoscopic tissue biopsies and surgical specimens post-resection. We aim to obtain endoscopic tissue biopsies from 250 patients. Oesophagogastroduodenoscopy will be performed and the gastric mucosa will be carefully inspected. Tissue biopsies will be obtained as per clinical indication. Tissue specimens will also be obtained from post-surgical resection gastric cancer specimens. We aim to obtain tissue from 20 post gastrectomy resection specimens. Immediately after resection, forcep biopsy specimens will be obtained from the macroscopic tumour. Each biopsy specimen will sliced into 2 portions. The smaller portion will be used for the polarimetry. The larger portion will be sent to the pathology laboratory for interpretation by a pathologist

title: Comparative transcription analysis to identify novel targets for malaria intervention.
abs: Despite extensive efforts to control the parasite, malaria remains one of the most important health burdens in the world. Genomic, transcriptomic as well as proteomic approaches are powerful tools to study the biology of the parasite and the availability of the genome sequences of now six different species of Plasmodium have significantly improved our understanding of parasite biology. Despite this our understanding of parasite induced pathology, mechanisms of immune evasion and adaptation, as well as mechanisms of drug resistance remains limited. Information to improve our understanding of any of these phenomena would be not only valuable in terms of understanding parasite biology but would also be useful for the management of clinical cases and the development of new diagnostic tools. The genomes of Plasmodium species code for approximately 5,000 to 6,000 genes. For about half of them there are no corresponding orthologues in any other organism making functional annotation difficult. The fact that these genes are either unique to the parasite or have diverged so much from their corresponding gene in other organisms makes them attractive drug targets. In the proposal we will use comparative transcriptomics to investigate transcriptional differences in parasites as they relate to disease severity, immune evasion and host adaptation as well as drug resistance. The transcriptional difference will provide important insights on the factors that regulate these processes in the parasite. In parallel we will utilize the transcriptome data to further improve the interaction network that we have generated. This improved network will further improve our ability to functionally annotate parasite unique genes. Finally unique genes predicted by the different approaches to play an important role in the parasite will be functionally characterized. Combining the transcriptional analysis with functional validation provides new insights into parasite biology as well as providing a list of unique drug targets.
kw: Malaria, Drug Targets, Transcriptome analysis, Plasmodium falciparum

title: Prospective Randomized Trial Comparing Drug Eluting Balloon Angioplasty (DEB) versus Conventional Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty Balloon (PTA) For The Treatment Of Hemodialysis Arterio-Venous Fistula (AVF) or Arterio-Venous Graft (AVG) stenoses
abs: Introduction:Neointimal hyperplasia is the main cause of hemodialysis access (arterio-venous fistula (AVF) or graft (AVG)) dysfunction and thrombosis. Although endovascular techniques like percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA), catheter directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy or bare metal stenting, may salvage the access, long term patency remains dismal due to recurrent stenosis from neointimal hyperplasia.Drug Eluting Balloons (DEB) is effective in inhibiting neointimal hyperplasia for treatment of coronary in-stent restenosis since 2006 and more recently in femoropopliteal arteries, reducing restenosis rates and prolonging patency.Aim:To determine efficacy of DEB in reducing restenosis rates and prolonging patency of AVFs/AVGs compared to PTA. Hypothesis:DEB is superior to PTA in reducing late luminal loss and restenosis rates, while prolonging primary and secondary patencies.Methodology:Prospective, randomized clinical trial with study population comprising of patients with dysfunctional AVFs/AVGs due to underlying stenoses. The patients will be randomized to receive either DEB or PTA.The 6-month late luminal loss will be primary end point. The secondary endpoints will be the restenosis rate, as well as primary and secondary patencies will also be determined.Major Clinical Significance:Hemodialysis access failures constitute significant morbidity and costs to patient and healthcare system. Maintaining access patency consumes significant resources and constitutes a significant portion of the work of vascular surgeons, nephrologists and interventional radiologists.Any strategy that reduces access failure or prolonging access lifespan will be beneficial. If DEB is proven to be superior to PTA, there will be a paradigm shift in the management of hemodialysis access failures from restenosis - similar to how DEB has changed practice in managing coronary artery in-stent restenosis.There are only a few multicentre trials focusing on the role of DEB in non-coronary applications. If this trial is successful, it will certainly put Singapore on world map for hemodialysis access intervention research.
kw: AVF stenosis, Conventional Balloon, Hemodialysis, AVG stenosis, Drug Eluting Balloon, Venous stenosis

title: Nano/Microparticle-based Intravesical Therapy for Bladder Cancer
abs: Bladder cancer is the costliest cancer to treat because about 70% of patients with superficial disease will develop tumor recurrence, thus requiring long-term follow-up and repeat interventions. BCG immunotherapy, the current standard treatment for preventing recurrence and progression in newly diagnosed bladder cancer, suffers from a number of limitations such as BCG intolerance and failure. Intravesical chemotherapy reduces the recurrence rate in the short-term but there is no evidence that it reduces the long-term incidence of recurrence or the risk of disease progression. One of the shortcomings associated with current intravesical chemotherapy is the short residence time of the drug in the bladder since much of it is lost upon the first voiding of urine. The proposed work aims to develop nano/microparticulate carriers which can deliver the drug/vaccine more effectively to the urothelium to eradicate the cancer cells. Firstly, non-cytotoxic mucoadhesive polymers will be synthesized for use in encapsulating and then releasing the drug/vaccine at the urothelium. Since chemotherapeutic drugs have a wide range of solubility, amphiphilic polymers will be designed and tailored to have different proportions of hydrophobic and hydrophilic blocks and/or neutral and charged blocks in order to optimize mucoadhesiveness and release profile of the drug. Secondly, nano/microparticles incorporating both drug/vaccine and magnetic seeds will be prepared. The latter will enable targeting and retention of the drug-containing nano/microparticles on the urothelium by means of an external magnetic field. Furthermore, since magnetic nano/microparticles can react to microwave energy used for thermotherapy, this type of nano/microparticles can also potentially offer the synergistic benefit of concurrent thermotherapy and chemotherapy. Thirdly, drug/vaccinecontaining nano/microparticles will be conjugated with a tumor-specific antibody to achieve effective targeting of the cancer cells. The effectiveness of the nano/microparticulate drug/vaccine carriers will be evaluated in vitro before testing in animal models is carried out.
kw: Bladder cancer, EGFR targeting, Nano/microparticulate carriers, Mucoadhesive, Drug/vaccine encapsulation, Thermotherapy

title: NOT ALL SMALL INFARCTS ARE LACUNAR STROKES - Uncovering the heterogeneous profiles and prognosis of small volume infarcts through study of clinical-radiological patterns and correlations in the hyperacute, subacute and chronic periods
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Small volume cerebral infarcts are heterogeneous in aetiology. We hypothesize that there are two distinct patterns: 1) true lacunes due to small, penetrating arterial disease; and 2) small infarcts due to thromboembolism involving large cerebral arteries or cardiac sources (non-lacunes). The prevalence, natural history and treatment response for “lacunar infarcts” have been described, but are possibly inaccurate as these studies included small infarcts not due to “true lacunes”. There are limited data on magnetic resonance (MR) imaging patterns and no published data on the effect of stroke treatments for small infarcts, which may vary based on aetiology.This study aims to profile and compare small volume infarcts which are true lacunes and non-lacunes, in terms of:1.patient characteristics, clinical presentation and natural history2.MRI characteristics and imaging natural history3.correlation between clinical and imaging profiles4.allelic distribution of the protein kinase C-eta (PRKCH) geneThis is a prospective observational study of consecutive acute ischemic stroke patients. We will screen patients with MR imaging within 48 hours of symptom onset. Inclusion criteria are clinical lacunar syndrome or baseline infarct volume <10mL. Patients will undergo serial MR imaging, clinical and functional assessment at day 1-2 and day 30. DNA will be isolated from blood from study participants to study allelic distribution of the PRKCH gene. The remaining DNA will be stored to study other candidate genes discovered in the future. This will be the first study of adequate size to study small infarcts with advanced imaging, thus providing evidence of their differing patterns. Differentiating small infarcts would guide aetiological determination and prognostication. This would also impact selection for future treatment trials as the potential benefit for some therapies may vary across aetiologies. Understanding the various patterns holds promise for specific, targeted treatment according to aetiological subtype.
kw: Lacunar Stroke, Small volume infarcts, Etiology, Reperfusion treatment, Prognosis, Natural History

title: Does relaxin-3 relax the brain? An investigation of the nucleus incertus and relaxin-3 as novel targets for the treatment of anxiety disorders
abs: The lifetime prevalence of anxiety disorders (ANX) is approximately 17% worldwide. In Singapore, about 10% of people are affected by some form of ANX. Ambiguity in the aetiology of ANX and the occurrence of various subtypes hamper the effectiveness of available treatments. Hence, the search for new treatments persists. The nucleus incertus (NI) may be a novel target for neuropsychopharmacological treatment of ANX. The NI, the chief neuronal source of relaxin-3 (RLN-3), projects to the putative neural correlates of anxiety including the median raphe nucleus (MRN), bed nucleus of stria terminalis (BNST), hippocampus and amygdala. All these brain regions express relaxin family peptide type-3 (RXFP3) receptor, the target for endogenous RLN-3. In addition, the NI richly expresses corticotrophin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1), Gamma aminobutyric acid type A (GABA) and 5hydroxytryptamine subtype 1A (5-HT) receptors, which are anxiolytic drug targets. Using a systems neurobiological approach we propose to test the hypothesis that the NI/RLN-3 plays a role in anxiety-related behaviours. A series of preclinical studies involving in vivo single unit, multiunit and evoked potential recordings will be conducted in rats to establish the functional role of the NI in anxiety-related pathways. The effect of anxiolytic drugs on the activity of NI neurones and the firing of NI neurones during anxiety-related behaviours will be studied. NI-lesioned rats will undergo behavioural assays of anxiety. Effects of NI stimulation and RLN-3 on the MRN, BNST and amygdala will be assessed by in vivo electrophysiology and effects of RLN-3 will be investigated in rat brain slice preparations. Optogenetic stimulation and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) will map the functional connections of the NI. This project will determine the role of the NI and RLN-3 in anxiety and will determine the validity of the NI and the RXFP3 receptor as a novel target for anxiolytic-drug action. 1AA

title: Regulation of innate and adaptive immune responses to H1N1 and H3N2 influenza viral infection by MAPK phosphatases
abs: Influenza viruses are among the most common respiratory pathogens, causing endemic infections and pandemics and remaining a serious cause of morbidity and mortality throughout the world (1),(2). Among the three types of influenza viruses, type A influenza virus is clinically the most important and the only type that causes pandemics. The abilities of influenza A viruses to mutate at a very high rate could lead to the emergence of a novel strain that resists to current antiviral substance and to which there is no immunity in humans, making vaccine strategies and pandemic planning difficult. To recover from influenza infection, effective immune responses must be induced after infection. Understanding the mechanisms that regulate host immune responses holds the promise to develop novel therapeutic intervention for influenza infection before unraveling the pathogenesis of the virus. Host innate and adaptive immune responses are regulated by signal transduction pathways. Among them, MAP kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways play essential roles in both innate and adaptive immune responses (3). The

title: CMV RETINITIS INTRAVITREAL GANCICLOVIR SINGAPORE STUDY
abs: Cytomegalovirus retinitis (CMVR) is the commonest opportunistic cause for ocular infection and vision loss in AIDS patients. While systemic treatment with anti-CMV agents is the standard-of-care in developed countries, high cost and inaccessibility remain prohibitive to many centres worldwide. Regular weekly intravitreous ganciclovir injections have proven to be an efficacious and cost-effective modality of treatment in such countries. A key gap in current clinical care is that there is no accepted standardised intravitreal treatment regime. A pilot study of 34 eyes over 2 years has demonstrated that weekly intravitreous therapy has minimal complications whilst achieving a long mean time-to-progression (496.7 days) in HAART-naïve patients. In small series’, fortnightly injections were shown clinically to maintain clinical remission. In this proposal, we will investigate the effect of reducing the dosage frequency of intravitreal treatment from weekly to fortnightly in HIV patients on HAART. We hypothesize that a reduced frequency of fortnightly maintenance intravitreal injections is as efficacious as the current weekly regime in HAART patients. This will be supported clinically and evidence from aqueous analysis. Patients who return for weekly injections have a high default rate (20-40%) due to inconvenience of time and discomfort. We will analyse the link between frequency of injections with the quality-of-life (QOL) of these patients. We hypothesize that the reduced regime will translate into better QOL and compliance.Our study will be the first worldwide to test these hypotheses in HIV patients. Definitive findings will translate into a gold-standard intravitreal treatment schedule with reduction of treatment-related complications and improvement of QOL. Aqueous cytokine and CMV DNA analysis will provide evidence on immunological processes of CMVR, monitor disease progression during treatment and prognostication. Possible identification of novel markers in CMVR may also lead to subsequent development of more targeted treatment strategies in management of CMVR.

title: Identifying Novel Genes Associated with Familial Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abs: Hypothesis: We hypothesize that there are additional genes associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), other than those within the HLA complex, and single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in genes identified from genome wide association and other studies, and that these gene(s) can be identified using next generation sequencing of families with a strong family history of NPC. Specific Aims:Aim 1: To sequence the exome of affected and unaffected members of an NPC family, using next generation sequencing (NGS). This family includes affected and unaffected twins.Aim 2: To validate the sequence variants detected by NGS, using conventional Sanger sequencing on the same samples and samples from an independent cohort of patients with sporadic or familial NPC (n=100).Novelty: To our knowledge, there have been no previous exome sequencing studies on NPC cancer families. In addition, we have a unique NPC family with three affected and five unaffected family members, including affected and unaffected twins. The strategy proposed here has the potential to uncover novel candidate genes associated with NPC susceptibility.Clinical Significance:Identification of novel genes associated with familial NPC may impact on the understanding of the aetiology of this complex disease, and may result in improved disease screening, monitoring of the disease, and enhance our understanding of the influence of these genes on disease progression in NPC cancer families. The strategy described in this grant proposal could also be utilized to identify genes involved in other hereditary cancer syndromes. In addition, future studies could potentially determine if mutations in the candidate genes correlate with the clinical presentation and biology of the cancer.

title: The role of non-adsorbing macromolecules in the increased adhesion of erythrocytes to endothelial cells in diabetes mellitus and beta thalassemia
abs: The adhesion of red blood cells (RBC) to endothelial cells (EC) is usually insignificant. However, abnormal RBC adhesion to EC has been observed in various clinical states such as beta-thalassemia or diabetes mellitus and the degree of this increased RBC-EC adhesiveness has been linked to the vascular complications associated with such diseases. Several plasma factors have been identified to be involved in the adhesion of pathological RBC to EC (e.g. fibrinogen) but the underlying mechanisms often remain obscure. In the past, it has been suggested that these plasma proteins act as ligands, cross-linking receptors on adjacent cells, but the identification of binding sites or receptors that could confirm this assumption are often missing. Recently, we identified an alternative pathway by demonstrating that non-adsorbing macromolecules can also have a marked impact on the adhesion of RBC to EC. This effect originates from the depletion of macromolecules from cell-cell interfaces thereby inducing macromolecular depletion interaction. The central hypothesis of the proposed project is that depletion interaction induced by non-adsorbing macromolecules is a determinant of the known increases of RBC adhesiveness in pathological conditions. In order to explore this hypothesis it is planned to investigate in vitro the impact of non-adsorbing macromolecules on the adhesion of RBC from patients with beta-thalassemia intermedia and diabetes mellitus. Our long-term goal is to get a better understanding of the pathology of such diseases. Such insight should eventually pave the way for the rationale development of new therapeutic agents to alleviate vascular complications and to new or improved diagnostic tools and hence improved patient care.

title: Insight from four-dimensional flow into the mechanism of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by combining cardiac magnetic resonance and computational fluid dynamics
abs: Background70% of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), a relatively common genetic disorder, have dynamic resting or inducible left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. While mitral-septal apposition has been observed, the mechanism of LVOT is not fully understood. AimsTo construct a 4-D heart-valve model from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and mathematically simulate intracardiac flow using advanced using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) techniques. Study and compare LVOT vortex formation in HCM patients with versus without obstruction. Methodology Cardiac MR images from HCM patients (10 each for obstruction and nonobstructive HCM) are segmented and transformed to generate time-resolved 3D mesh models. These meshes form the structure of patient-specific time-dependent ventricular geometry model in conjunction with valvular geometry (aortic and mitral valves) used for CFD simulation. CFD simulations are performed to evaluate the hemodynamics across LVOT, downstream and upstream of mitral-septal contact. Three-dimensional flow velocities, pressure gradients, and pressure differences across LVOT throughout systole are determined. Vorticity formation is determined and compared downstream of mitral-septal contact between obstructive and non-obstructive HCM. Clinical significanceCFD derived blood flow is able to provide detailed hemodynamic information that is unobtainable from cardiac imaging alone. Continuous 3-D velocity profiles, instantaneous LVOT pressure gradients, and vorticity downstream of mitral-septal contact can be determined. These can facilitate better understanding of obstruction in HCM, and research into ways to optimize and refine surgical treatment approaches.

title: Towards a better understanding of climate change and natural hazards in and around Southeast Asia through geodetic data combination
abs: The proposed research will use geodetic data to achieve a better understanding of natural hazards and climate change across the regions of South and Southeast Asia. Geodetic data sets measure signals from a wide range of geophysical processes that include, amongst others, changes in sea level, melting glaciers, changes in continental water storage, and tectonic and volcanic deformation. It can be difficult to separate these different signals in the data, which leads to uncertainty in our estimates of their implications for societal risk. Different geodetic data sets observe the Earth system with a range of different spatial and temporal resolutions, areas of coverage, uncertainties, and types of observable. This means that combination of the data sets can be used to separate the different signals. However, the differences also present challenges for data combination. The goal of the proposed research is thus to develop techniques for consistent combination of different geodetic data sets and models, taking these differences into account. In order to ensure that the work has direct relevance to societal risk assessment, emphasis will be placed on careful characterisation of uncertainties in the models and data. We will therefore investigate the use of a Bayesian (probabilistic) approach to data combination. Prior to data combination, data exploration techniques will be used to investigate temporal patterns, transients, and correlations in the data, in order to form hypotheses and models for the underlying processes. The project will use a broad suite of geodetic data sources, including Gravity and Climate Experiment (GRACE) satellite, tide gauge, Global Positioning System (GPS), Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), remote sensing and palaeogeodetic data.

title: FRONTIERS IN PHYSICAL AND LIFE SCIENCES: BIO-INSPIRED AND BIOMIMETIC MATERIALS
abs: Living organisms are true green chemist masters. They process tailored, functional, and structural materials across various length scales in (i) an aqueous environment, (ii) at ambient temperatures, and most importantly (iii) they use naturally-occurring compounds as building blocks. With the increasing necessity for more environmentally sustainable solutions, there are critical lessons to be learned by elucidating how nature synthesizes complex materials at a low energetic cost. Natural materials have also evolved to serve multifunctional roles, with often a unique set of properties not achieved in mad-made materials. This proposal seeks to contribute to the burgeoning field of biomimetic materials engineering, by expanding our understanding of the underlying principles of biological materials synthesis, structure, and chemistry, and to explore their translation into novel materials solutions, with particular emphasis on health-related and tissue engineering applications. The proposed work will use model systems that are biased towards marine invertebrates because of the relevance of their living environment to the human physiological milieu and of their accessibility. The research will rely strongly on a highly multi-disciplinary approach, which is recognized as a central strategy in order to make breakthrough discoveries in this field, Fig. 1. Efforts will be focused on creating a multidisciplinary team, in particular by hiring research personnel with distinct academic backgrounds, including molecular biologists, biophysicists, polymer chemists and computational materials scientists, who will help foster this vision. Three distinct but complementary aspects of bio-inspired materials will be pursued, including: (i) structure-property relationships from the macro- to the molecular scale, (ii) biochemistry and protein chemistry of biological materials and extra-cellular tissues, (iii) translation of fundamental biological processing and design principles into applied strategies for industrial and biomedical materials synthesis. I will initially focus my research on 4 types of model systems: (i) non-mineralized hard tissues with high abrasion resistance; (ii) bioelastomeric materials with shock-absorbing capability and selective permeability; (iii) hierarchical and complex mineralized tissues from mechanically active bio-tools; and (iv) underwater adhesives processed by complex coacervation for use as orthopedic glues. I will also maintain a keen eye toward the use of novel biological systems that might be added to our repertoire when they enhance or improve our current research direction.

title: Combating Infectious Diseases:Engineering Strategies for Molecular Virology
abs: Throughout history, infectious diseases have shaped population demographics, hindered economic potential, and most critically robbed far too many individuals of their lives. Despite advances in therapeutic drugs and tools, much work remains towards the eradication of infectious diseases. Our studies will focus on using engineering strategies to target the Hepatitis C virus (HCV), which affects over 170 million people worldwide and for which current therapeutic options are ineffective. Therefore, we seek: 1) to understand the role of conserved BAAP domains in HCV proteins; and 2) to engineer antiviral peptides that rupture lipid membrane-enveloped HCV particles. The HCV NS5A protein specifically binds the host cell phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) lipid via the BAAP domain structural motif found within its N-terminal amphipathic, alpha-helix (AH). To develop this structural motif—which is also found in other infectious diseases including Malaria, Dengue virus (DV) and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV)—into a drug target, we will investigate how the PI(4,5)P2:NS5A AH interaction affects the latter binding the critical host cell protein TBC1D20, determine the effect of BAAPP domain mutations on NS5A localization and HCV replication, and develop screens to identify candidate inhibitors of the PI(4,5)P2:NS5A AH interaction. Moreover, we will optimize the chemical sequence of a previously identified antiviral peptide by investigating its ability to lyse lipid vesicles that mimic lipid-enveloped virus particles, determining its virucidal effect on HCV particles, and measuring its potential to reduce HCV infectivity in vitro. To start translating this activity into a clinical application, we will then explore covalent stitching and stapling modifications that preserve the peptide’s properties while increasing its chemical stability. In the long term, the work achieved in this proposal will lay the groundwork for combating a wide range of infectious, viral diseases whose membrane-associated biologic activities make them amenable to our methods.

title: Adjunctive Vitamin D3 with Anti-Fungal Agents as Novel Drug Combinations for Enhanced Treatment of Invasive Fungal Infections
abs: In the context of the increasing numbers of immunocompromised patients seen in haematology, oncology, transplantation and intensive care units, mortality rates from invasive fungal infections (IFI) have remained high, approaching 50%. This dilemma is further confounded not only by the limited range of effective anti-fungal (specifically anti-mould) medications available, but also the exceedingly high costs of these drugs. We have found that vitamin D3 is a potent modulator of host immune response in both Candida and Aspergillus infections in-vitro. More importantly, the resultant immunodulatory effect of vitamin D3 is linked to a trend towards favourable clinical response in IFI patients. Our hypothesis is that vitamin D3 enhances host immune capability against invasive yeast and mould infections and augments microbicidal activity. By virtue of its favourable immunomodulatory profile, vitamin D3 may further ameliorate the toxic profiles associated with amphotericin B deoxycholate (AmBD), an older, but cheaper and proven anti-fungal agent.We will translate these findings from the bench for validation in in-vivo systems using immunocompetent and immunosuppressed mice models of invasive candidiasis and invasive aspergillosis. Infected mice will be treated with cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) alone and in combination with anti-fungals (AmBD, voriconazole, caspofungin and liposomal amphotericin B) at varying doses and dosing intervals. Primary outcome measures are survival, clearance of fungemia, fungal burden in tissues and histopathology. Secondary measures include circulating cytokine production, and differential expression of pattern recognition receptors on immune cells.Our pilot study in mice has shown that vitamin D3 with AmBD is a potentially viable combination therapy. This novel therapy with adjunct vitamin D3 aims to increase therapeutic efficacy and potentially reduce toxicity of anti-fungal treatment. The results will facilitate the eventual conduct of clinical studies with the goal of creating novel combination drug/treatment regimens that are efficacious and financially viable for patients especially in Asia.

title: Novel Anti-androgens of Botanical Origin as Multiple-Site Modulators of Androgen Receptor Signalling to Inhibit Prostate Cancer Development and Growth
abs: The development and clinical progression of prostate cancer is highly related to functions of the androgen receptor (AR). As such, AR is the most therapeutically relevant target for chemoprevention and therapy for prostate cancer. Prenylflavones are ubiquitous compounds found in fruits, vegetables and legumes. Epidemiological studies indicate that consumption of these compounds reduce the prevalence and incidence of prostate cancer. Our preliminary data indicated that the naturally occurring and non-toxic prenylflavones icaritin (ICT) and desmethyicaritin (DICT) inhibited the growth of prostate cancer cells. ICT/DICT are anti-androgens that bind AR to block coactivator recruitment and transcription. These represent a very rare class of phyto-anti-androgens of botanical origin. ICT/DICT also destabilized AR protein through direct binding to aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) and promoted AhR-mediated degradation of AR. Our working hypothesis is that prenylflavones like ICT/DICT are dual modulators of both AR and AhR. On one hand, these compounds serve as antagonists that inhibit AR activation; on the other hand, they activate AhR to promote proteasomal degradation of AR.To test our hypothesis, we will:#1: Investigate and define the mechanistic basis of action of ICT/DICT and selected compounds on androgen receptor (AR) and arylhydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signalling pathways and consequent anti-proliferative effects on human prostate cancer cells.#2: Validate the anti-proliferative effects and validate the mechanistic insights in animal models of prostate cancer growth (xenograft) and development (TRAMP).Achievement of these specific aims will likely result in new insights on how natural compounds like ICT/DICT impact both AR and AhR signalling pathways to inhibit prostate cancer cell development growth, and provide proof of principle for a new scientific paradigm for the next generation of multiple site anti-hormone agents for primary prevention and therapy for prostate cancer.

title: MICRORNA EXPRESSION SIGNATURES OF BREAST CANCER PATIENTS AND THEIR POTENTIAL AS DIAGNOSTIC AND PREDICTIVE TOOLS
abs: HYPOTHESISOur hypothesis is that circulating microRNA species are differentially expressed in the peripheral blood of breast cancer patients, as compared to healthy women. Expression profiles of circulating microRNA may be useful for developing blood-based diagnostic or prognostic tests for breast cancer screening. AIMS AND METHODOLOGY1.To analyze the microRNA profiles of serum microRNA from breast cancer patients (n=30) and healthy controls (n=30) using a microarray platform, in order to identify differentially expressed microRNAs. 2.To validate the cancer-associated microRNA signature on a further independent set of serum samples from patients with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) (n=25), and those with Stages 1, 2, 3 or 4 breast cancer (n=25 each; total n=100), using a real-time RT-PCR platform (eg. Taqman assays). CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCEThe high prevalence of breast cancer and the good prognosis for patients with early-stage disease have motivated an active search for diagnostic biomarkers for breast cancer screening. Although there is increasing evidence that microRNAs are linked to malignancy, very little is known about the status of circulating microRNAs in breast cancer. If this study succeeds in identifying discriminatory circulating microRNA signature(s) for breast cancer, these could potentially be used for disease screening for the early detection of breast cancer, prediction of disease recurrence, and/or monitoring of treatment response.NOVELTY ASPECTRecent investigations into the expression profiles of circulating microRNA in colorectal and prostate cancer patients have suggested that the measurement of plasma or serum derived microRNA may become a new approach for the blood-based early detection of human cancer. However, extensive profiling of microRNA from the blood of breast cancer patients and control cases has not been attempted so far. This study may lead to the identification of novel microRNA expression signatures which could potentially be developed as blood-based biomarkers for breast cancer screening.
kw: MicroRNA, Breast Cancer, Expression Signatures, Early Detection

title: A comprehensive evaluation of circulating tumour cells as a predictive marker of therapeutic response in renal cell carcinoma
abs: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the 7th most common cancer among males in the United States and its incidence is continuing to rise. In patients with high risk localized disease, relapse post nephrectomy is frequent, with hematogenous metastases as the major cause of mortality The role of circulating tumour cells (CTCs) in predicting disease activity is of growing clinical and biologic importance, particularly in correlation with therapeutic interventions. The technique is accessible, non-invasive, and may be repeated at biologically and clinically meaningful time intervals. The overall goal of our study is to evaluate CTCs as an early biomarker for predicting the success of therapeutic interventions in RCC by monitoring disease activity, from localized to metastatic RCC. We have developed a novel technology that sensitively and accurately isolates CTCs based on physical properties of size and deformability of CTCs. In the setting of localized disease, CTC counts may be a useful adjunct for clinical risk assessment, particularly since the advent of novel kinase inhibitors have made adjuvant therapy a possibility for investigation. We plan to monitor CTC counts in patients with localized RCC pre- and post-nephrectomy, until relapse or up to three years, to evaluate its value in early determination of outcomes. In metastatic RCC, CTC counts have yielded extremely promising prospects as an early predictor of the outcomes of multi-targeted kinase inhibition over and above conventional radiologic evaluation of response, supported by our preliminary data. We plan to confirm our findings in a larger series of patients with metastatic RCC. Our hypothesis is that CTCs are an excellent and early biomarker of outcomes following therapeutic intervention throughout the clinical course of RCC for urologists and medical oncologists. These findings would be of high and immediate clinical and pharmacoeconomic importance.
kw: Renal cell carcinoma, Circulating tumour cells, Nephrectomy, Sunitinib

title: Non- Invasive Evaluation of Chronic Allograft Nephropathy (CAN)/ Interstitial Fibrosis and Tubular Atrophy (IFTA) in Renal Transplants with Advanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging Techniques
abs: Prevention and early intervention in chronic allograft nephropathy (CAN) or interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA)remains long term unmet medical needs in renal transplantation to improve long-term outcomes of renal transplants (RT). Current gold standard, renal biopsy is subject to poor acceptance, complications, sampling errors and inter-observer variability. There is a need for safe, non-invasive, and accurate investigation for diagnosis of CAN/IFTA especially if repeated monitoring is needed. Non-invasive techniques like MRI are being explored as biomarkers of pathological processes. Diffusion weighted imaging (DWI), blood oxygen level dependent (BOLD), have been shown to be feasible in evaluation of RT but there are no large series to support their routine clinical utility. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) and MR Elastography (MRE) are new techniques that have not been explored yet. We propose a multiparametric evaluation of RT with MRI techniques (BOLD, DWI, ASL and MRE) to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of RTs for early detection of CAN/IFTA. Normal recent RT recipients (<8 weeks after transplantation from living donors) with normal function will form the normal group. Patients with RTs and biopsy proven CAN/IFTA will form the CAN/IFTA group. MRI protocol including all research sequences will be performed. The derived quantitative parameters -ADC, R2*, perfusion and stiffness will be compared between the groups and correlated with histological grades of CAN/IFTA. Statistical analysis will be performed for accuracy of techniques to identify early CAN/IFTA and differentiate among different grades of CAN/IFTA. Comparative analysis between different techniques will also be performed.MRI derived quantitative parameters such as stiffness values, ADC, R2* and perfusion may be useful as a non-invasive surrogate marker for CAN/IFTA, and therefore yield a non-invasive diagnosis of CAN/IFTA. The multi-parametric approach may also be useful for assessment of treatment response to intervention and in following up progression of the disease non-invasively.

title: Targeting and eradicating human hepatocellular carcinoma cells in vivo with bone marrow-derived human mesenchymal stem cells transduced with oncolytic measles virus.
abs: Human hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is among the most lethal and prevalent human cancers. In Singapore, it is ranked the fourth most common cancer in the males and the third cancer with the highest mortality. Although surgery still provide the best long-term survival for patients with early-stage HCC, there is no effective systemic therapy for patients with advanced HCC, and hence the outcome for these patients is dismal. Although recent preliminary studies suggested that sorafenib may be effective in treating HCC. The effectiveness of sorafenib for the systemic treatment of advanced HCC is still at its infancy stage and has not yet been well established. Additionally, the high costs of sorafenib will certainly be an added limitation. Hence, the clinical management of HCC is far from being satisfactory and studies aimed at more selective and effective therapeutic interventions of advanced HCC are much needed. Recently, human mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) are emerging as novel cell-based delivery agents to target tumor lesions. It has also been demonstrated that measles virus (MV) could induce tumor-specific cytopathic damages specifically in human tumor cells that expressed high level of the CD46 receptor and not normal cells that express low level of the CD46 receptor. In this proposal, we would like to investigate the strategy to employ live attenuated Edmonston vaccine strain of MV to transduce BM-hMSC which we then hypothesize would specific target CD46+ tumor cells. The fate and therapeutic efficacy following the introduction of MV alone and MV-transduced BM-hMSC to orthotopically implanted HCC xenografts in SCID mice will be compared and studied. Although the present study addresses specifically the therapeutic potentials of MV-transduced BM-hMSC on HCC, similar strategies could form the basis for developing stem cell-based viral therapies targeted for other human cancers expressing high level of the CD46 receptor.

title: Key Drivers of Tumor Growth in Nasal Polyposis
abs: Nasal polyposis (NP) occurs in nearly 1 percent of the population and is marked by recurrent, nonmalignant tumors. These tumors raise chronic burdens to affected individuals and the medical resources. Major gaps in our understanding of NP include the molecular triggers for their growth and strategies for effective, non-surgical therapies. This is a proposal to uncover key pathways involved in recurrent tumor growth and to generative new therapeutic approaches based on our molecular analysis of these tumors. In airway epithelium, basal cells are considered to have stem/progenitor cell activity, which can direct the differentiation of other epithelial cell types. This study is proposed to investigate the biological role of p63 and p73 in epithelial remodeling in NP using highly organized banks of tissues from 50 NP (before and after nasal/oral glucocorticosteroid (GC) treatment) and 50 control patients, and will involve an array of molecular and histochemical technologies. These studies will act as a backdrop to our progressing studies involving the cloning of stem cells of normal nasal turbinate cells and patient-matched stem cells from NP. We have made important progress in analyzing these cells as the transcriptome level and have shown that almost all genes are identical between the normal and disease stem cells. However, there is a small subset of genes that standout as up or down regulated between these two populations with high p-values. Our microarray analysis has highlighted the hyper-elevated expression of the chemokine Cxcl17 in NP stem cells. We hypothesize that this chemokine is playing a major role in driving tumor growth, and will generate monoclonal antibodies and RNAi strategies to test the significance of this factor for NP. We anticipate that these studies could uncover important directions for the therapeutic intervention of this highly common and difficult disease.
kw: Nasal polyposis, Mucosal inflammation, Epithelial remodeling and repairing, p63, p73, CXCL17

title: A randomized clinical trial comparing phacoemulsification and goniosynechialysis with phacoemulsification alone in the management of primary angle closure
abs: Primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) is a significant cause of global blindness. High intraocular pressure (IOP) has consistently been shown to be an important risk factor for glaucoma progression, and lowering of IOP has similarly been shown to reduce risk of progression. Subjects with primary angle closure (PAC) or PACG have, by definition, narrow drainage angles and this is thought to contribute to raised IOP. There is evidence that widening of the drainage angle results in lowered IOP. Initial management of PAC/PACG is to perform laser peripheral iridotomy, which can widen the drainage angle. The presence of peripheral anterior synaechiae (PAS) limits the extent that the drainage angle can open, which may in turn reduce the effectiveness of any angle opening procedure. Phacoemulsification + intraocular lens implantation (PEI) has consistently been shown to open the drainage angle and lower the IOP in subjects with PAC/PACG. The effect of PEI on PAS has only been examined in one study, which showed that PEI does significantly decrease the amount of PAS by approximately 25%. It has been proposed that if a greater proportion of PAS could be broken, this could result in greater IOP reduction. This is the theory behind goniosynechialysis (GSL) which is the mechanical breaking of PAS using a spatula or viscoelastic. Usually this is combined with PEI (PEI-GSL) and has been shown to result in significant decrease in IOP. There have been no comparative studies to determine which of these 2 treatment options is superior in terms of IOP control and safety in PAC/PACG subjects. We propose to conduct a multicentre randomized clinical trial of PEI versus PEI-GSL to help resolve this issue. The main outcome measure will be IOP control at 1 year, with secondary measures being complication rate, drainage angle depth change and amount of PAS.
kw: Phacoemulsification, Primary angle-closure, Glaucoma, Goniosynechialysis, Viscogonioplasty, Primary angle-closure glaucoma

title: Exploring biomarkers as risk factors for cardiovascular disease in paediatric chronic kidney disease
abs: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of death among young adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) since childhood. CVD starts in early CKD, manifesting as arteriopathy and cardiomyopathy. The primary objective of this retrospective and prospective longitidinal study is to define a predictive algorithm to allow for better risk stratification and prediction of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in paediatric patients with stages 1-5 CKD in Singapore. As the young patients do not develop cardiovascular ischaemic events, the main surrogate outcome markers will be left ventricular hypertrophy measured by left ventricular mass index (2D echocardiography); early diastolic LV dysfunction measured by early diastolic mitral annular velocity (pulsed-wave transmitral Doppler); preclinical atherosclerosis measured by carotid intima-media thickness and endothelial dysfunction measured by endothelium-dependent flow mediated dilatation (high resolution B-mode ultrasonography); arteriosclerosis measured by two-point pulsed wave velocity (applanation tonometry). Besides traditional cardiovascular risk factors, we will examine CKD-related risk factors including biochemical parameters, chronic inflammatory markers (highly-sensitive C-reactive protein, interleukin-6), oxidative stress markers (asymmetric dimethylarginine, homocysteine) and biomarkers related to CVD risk prognostication (N-terminal pro-brain-natriuretic peptide, highly-sensitive cardiac troponin T, ST2 and growth differentiation factor-15, and urine neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin). Patients with CKD stages 2-5 will be undergo yearly 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, arteriopathy scan and 2D echocardiography. Biomarkers will be determined prospectively at baseline and then at 4-6-monthly intervals. Biochemical parameters will be collected retrospectively and prospectively at minimum 3-monthly intervals. Whenever possible, retrospective data will be collected from CKD stage 2. Controls who are age- and sex-matched patients with stage 1 CKD will undergo single arteriopathy scans and biomarkers determination.This is the first such study in this region that collectively studies both traditional and relatively novel risk factors for CVD in young CKD patients. It aims to facilitate early aggressive intervention so as to prevent future CVD.
kw: Chronic kidney disease, Cardiovascular disease, Arteriopathy, Left ventricular hypertrophy, Children, Biomarkers

title: The genetic determinants of Age Related Macular Degeneration in Asian populations – a comparative genetic study between three major Asian ethnic groups [Chinese, Indians and Malays] in Singapore.
abs: This project will stem from results of GWAS (genome-wide association studies) which will stimulate further investigations into new theories of what may be influencing the onset of AMD in Singaporean Asians. For example, whether epistatic and/or gene-environment interactions may play a role especially if no genome-wide significant evidence for association to AMD is found and/or it is known that the disease is of polygenic inheritance. Furthermore, identification of shared segments between ethnicities may provide information about the evolutionary history of AMD, leading to the development of more efficient strategies to identify novel genetic variants.Outcomes of such analyses may lead to the possibility that DNA structural variants, such as insertions, deletions and copy number variants may be involved in the development of AMD as well as the possibility that complex biological networks are involved. By being able to compare results from three ethnicities living in the same country with relatively similar socioeconomic status and environmental exposures will help fully elucidate the physiological pathways in the development of AMD that are more specific to an Asian population, leading to new and better well-characterised developments in its preventive care in Singapore.
kw: Age-related macular degeneration, Genetics, Genome-wide association, Gene-gene/gene-environment interactions, Segmental sharing, Asia

title: The influence of Small vessel cerebrovascular lesions on cognition and tau
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder with significant impact on cognitive performance. Although dementia is typically thought to occur in the late stages of PD, recent literature including data from our institute suggests that cognitive impairment is present in about 31% of patients with early PD. Cerebrovascular disease (CVD) is prevalent in the elderly and among Asians, it has been demonstrated to predominantly involve small vessels. It is hypothesized that the coexistence of vascular and PD pathology will hasten the development of cognitive impairment among patients with idiopathic PD.
