title: Photoactivable gene silencing using upconverting fluorescent nanoparticles for treatment of Malignant melanoma
abs: Cancer still remains one of the most deadliest disease till date after all the research done to cure various cancers. Malignant melanoma is a type of skin cancer which kills thousands of people every year, worldwide. A majority of these cases have a mutation in the B-raf gene. The last decade has seen a revolution in the field of gene therapy and an interesting method known as photoactivable gene silencing is gaining prominence. The genes can be silenced by shining light on siRNA which are photocaged. It can induce gene silencing with a very high spatial and temporal resolution. Specific silencing of genes is necessary as the same gene is present in an unmutated form in normal cells and their function cannot be disturbed. This methodology has been tested only in in-vitro systems because an UV-light source is needed for activation and currently UV lamps are used for this purpose. For proceeding to in-vivo systems, a light source is required which can penetrate deep enough inside the tissues to cause photoactivation with low power to prevent photodamage. We propose a novel idea of conjugating photoactivable siRNA against B-raf with upconverting fluorescent nanoparticles (UCN), which can absorb higher penetrating near-infrared (NIR) light and produce light in the UV-Visible region. So, the genes can be silenced specifically by shining NIR light on the tumor which in turn activates the siRNA only in the tumor. The multifunctional property of the UCN can also be exploited for imaging the tumor since they have absolute photostability and negligible background autofluorescence. We propose to demonstrate the utility and versatility of UCN to act as a photoswitch to silence B-raf gene expression in cell lines as well as in animal models of melanoma enabling a highly specific and efficient therapy.
kw: Photoactivable, Gene, Fluorescent, Upconverting, Nanoparticle

title: Investigation of the therapeutic effects of soluble IL-18 decoy receptor in keloid scars
abs: Keloids and other abnormal scars such as hypertrophic scars are examples of dermal fibroproliferative disorders resulting from pathological wound healing. Tender and itchy keloids behave like neoplasms, growing beyond the boundaries of the original wound edges and continuing to enlarge if left untreated. These abnormal scars are not only extremely unsightly, but may also cause tissue and functional problems by compromising normal biomechanical properties of skin especially in the vicinity of joints where scar contracture may limit motion. Keloids and abnormal scars represent a worldwide biomedical burden with approximately two billion people at risk and a multi-million dollar market of unmet medical need. Although keloids and abnormal scars have distressed patients and stymied health professionals for centuries, treatment options for keloids and abnormal scars remain limited and unsatisfactory. This is because the molecular dysfunction contributing to keloid scar pathogenesis still remains largely unknown. Understanding the formation of keloid scars would set the groundwork for effective new therapies for the treatment of keloid scars.IL-18 is a novel proinflammatory cytokine of the IL-1 cytokine superfamily, and plays a crucial role in developmental biology, immune-related diseases, angiogenesis, solid tumour biology, inflammation, and fibrogenesis. However its role in normal tissue repair and its function in keloid and scar pathogenesis remain unclear. This project is designed to investigate in-vitro the potential therapeutic effects of soluble IL-18 decoy receptors in keloid scars. The data generated from this project may provide good evidence for novel therapeutic application of anti-IL-18 agents in the prevention and treatment of keloids and other pathological scars.
kw: Keloid, IL-18, Wound healing, Scar, Fibrosis, Skin

title: Elucidating Potential Lipid-Based Biomarkers in Schizophrenia
abs: Schizophrenia has a lifetime prevalence of about 1%. Frequently, it begins in adolescence and runs a chronic and disabling course. For the last 2 centuries, the diagnosis and management of this complex disorder was done without objective laboratory tools. Clinicians depended on observations to make a diagnosis and monitor therapeutic efficacy. This situation arose because of a lack of understanding in the exact pathogenesis of this disorder, and consequently, a lack of suitable biomarkers. Today, researchers believe that it is primarily a disorder of the brain with disruptions in cellular signaling. The brain is a lipid-rich organ and it seems plausible that membrane lipids are involved in the disease process. Research had shown that blood lipids could be used to identify patients with schizophrenia, raising questions of whether it is a whole body disorder, not just a brain disorder. We hypothesize that schizophrenia involves perturbations in cellular membranes. In this case-control study, we aim to identify differentially expressed lipids from red blood cell (RBC) membranes and their accompanying lipid metabolizing enzymes. We would obtain blood samples from 100 patients and 300 controls. Lipids will be extracted from the RBC membranes, and identification and quantification performed with tandem mass spectrometry via multiple reaction monitoring. A list of differentially expressed lipids will be obtained after correcting for multiple hypotheses testing with the false discovery rate set at 5%. Their accompanying lipid metabolizing enzymes will also be characterized. Bioinformatic tools such as principal component analysis will be used to reduce the multivariate data and support vector machine modeling to generate a predictive model.Results from this study will inform researchers on the species of lipids involved in schizophrenia and guide us in the subsequent research direction to further our understanding of this disorder with the aim of validating potentially clinically useful biomarkers.
kw: schizophrenia, biomarkers, lipidomics

title: Derivation of patient-specific dopaminergic neurons via induced Pluripotent Stem Cells for molecular dissection of Parkinson’s Disease
abs: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a debilitating neurodegenerative disorder caused by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. PD afflicts ~1% of the population above 60 years of age and as the world’s population ages rapidly, the incidence rate of PD is expected to rise in tandem. Despite intensive research, our knowledge of the molecular etiology of PD has remained sparse. Two major limitations that have impeded progress in our understanding of the disease are the absence of an accurate experimental model for PD and the lack of a homogenous source of diseased neurons for analysis. With the advent of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology, there now exists a powerful tool for addressing both limitations. Using this technology, it is now possible to derive PD patient-specific dopaminergic neurons for analysis. The etiology of PD is complex, arising from both inheritable genetic mutations as well as causes that do not show any clear underlying genetic component. In the former forms of PD, at least 6 gene loci have been implicated in the perpetuation of the disease, each manifesting a plethora of mutations. In this proposal, we outline an approach whereby homogenous dopaminergic (DA) neuronal populations can be derived from sporadic PD patients or patients harboring specific known PD-linked gene mutations by reprogramming their somatic cells into iPSCs and subsequently to differentiate the iPSCs into DA neurons. We postulate that by comparing the molecular signatures of DA neurons derived from PD patients and healthy individuals, we will be able to identify common themes of cellular perturbations that contribute to PD progression. This would be of great clinical significance, aiding in the design of strategies to delay or block the mechanisms that initiate disease progression. It will also provide insights into approaches for corrective therapy of the disease.
kw: Parkinson's Disease, neurodegeneration, IPSC, reprogramming, dopaminergic neuron, differentiation

title: Retinal Microvascular Changes in Optic Neuropathy Subtypes: Investigating Vascular Mechanisms Underlying Optic Nerve Disorders.
abs: The optic nerve is vulnerable to various insults that also affect the brain. Optic nerve disorders (collectively termed optic neuropathies) may be secondary to various insults such as ischemia, inflammation, extrinsic compression, trauma and toxins. Of these, ischemic optic neuropathy and optic neuritis are most frequently encountered. However, the exact pathogenic processes that underlie these potentially blinding conditions remain unclear at present.Retinal blood vessels share similar anatomic, physiologic and embryologic characteristics to cerebral vessels. Many retinal vascular conditions are associated with stroke, and studies have found that retinal signs, in particular hypertensive and diabetic retinopathy, may be markers of stroke risk and mortality. Thus, retinal microvascular imaging may be a relatively novel, non-invasive method of precisely quantifying subtle variations and abnormalities in the retinal microvasculature, and these changes may be markers of cerebrovascular, and perhaps even optic nerve disease.To date, there are no studies that explore the relationship between these retinal changes and optic neuropathies. This novel project aims to determine the relationship between a range of retinal microvascular changes (vessel diameters, tortuosity, branching angles, fractal dimensions) and 150 cases of ischemic and inflammatory optic neuropathies. We will also compare retinal changes between these optic neuropathy cases and 450 age-race-gender matched population controls from studies under the Singapore Epidemiology of Eye Disease (SEED) programme, in which retinal microvascular changes have been measured in about 10,000 persons of Chinese, Malays and Indian ethnicity. Lastly, we aim to determine if the severity of microvascular changes at onset is related to visual outcome at 6 months post-onset of optic neuropathy.Data from this study will provide important insights into the microvascular contribution to these two important types of optic neuropathy, and whether retinal vascular imaging analysis may be a useful tool for prognostication.
kw: optic nerve, retinal vascular changes, optic neuritis, anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

title: Sequence variations of genes in the estrogen pathway and perinatal depression
abs: Aims: Perinatal (antenatal and postnatal) depression is a common complication of childbearing, affecting 10 to 20% of mothers. We aim to screen for and identify cases of perinatal depression among women attending antenatal clinics and evaluate the association of variants in estrogen receptor and related genes with the disorder in our population.Hypothesis: Women are exposed to fluctuations in estrogen level during childbearing years, especially during pregnancy and following childbirth. For a subgroup of women with genetic predisposition rendering them more sensitive to such changes, pregnancy or childbirth can act as a trigger for the onset of perinatal depression. Variants of genes in the estrogen pathway are strong candidates for this genetic predisposition.Methodology: Women attending antenatal and postnatal clinics will be screened with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. DNA from 500 controls who are well throughout the antenatal and postpartum period and 250 cases meeting DSM IV criteria for depressive disorder will be genotyped for various genetic variants. The distribution of SNPs and haplotypes and non-genetic risk factors will be compared between cases and controls and within the case group. Results for different markers will also be combined and stratified for multi-loci analysis. The ESR-1 gene will also be resequenced for 50 cases. Significance of the project:As perinatal depression is known to contribute to inadequate self-care and poor compliance with prenatal care, early diagnosis and treatment interventions are critical for the health and well-being of both mother and infant. In the short term, identified genetic markers that increase vulnerability to puerperal triggering of depression can be an additional screening tool to identify at-risk expectant mothers for early management during a very critical period for mother, infant, and family. In the long run, it may lead to identification of new pathways or treatment targets for this common but under-studied disorder.
kw: pregnancy, gene polymorphism, postnatal, depression, antenatal, estrogen

title: New Biotechnology for Processing Metropolitan Organic Wastes into Value-Added Products
abs: To achieve the goal of converting metropolitan biomass wastes into value-added products in a country like Singapore, it requires an integrated research program involving innovative investigations on waste properties; culturing novel microbial consortia; characterizing and optimizing functional enzymes; integrating genomics and proteomics to design stable microbial consortia for bioprocessing; real-time monitoring of enzyme activities with the aid of novel biosensors; and separating biogas and biofuel into useful products by advanced membranes. The proposed research aims to culture and develop stable methane-generating cultures to treat multiple food wastes and to discover and characterize novel biofuel generating microbes that possess high yield and productivity. Novel cultures and their functional enzymes capable of hydrolyzing cellulose and hemicellulose at room temperature will be identified. The research team will develop DNA microarrays with the screened functional genes (e.g., various hydrolyzing genes, biofuel generating genes, etc) to characterize the microbial consortia. The array system can also be used for the rapid screening of key enzymes in any unknown microbial consortia. By understanding the systems through metagenomics, we will develop the necessary science and engineering framework to optimize and accelerate biomass destruction and bioenergy production. In the entire proposed bioconversion process, seawater will be used alone or in conjunction with freshwater in order to reduce the heavy reliance on freshwater in a water-scarce city. In order to fulfill the objectives of this proposal, a multidisciplinary team has been formed to conduct research to concentrate biogases via gas separation membranes and concentrate biofuels via pervaporation. Information gathered from the above research will pave the way for the efficient separation of the generated bio-products; thereby achieving a prototype for the systematic processing of metropolitan organic wastes in a highly urbanized city.
kw: biomass waste;bioenergy;microorganisms;biosensor;microarray;membrane separation

title: A photoactivation imaging approach to unravel the role of Disrupted in Schizophrenia 1 (DISC1) in axonal transport and neuronal polarization
abs: Schizophrenia is a devastating mental disorder which affects ~1% of the population worldwide. Althoughthe etiology of the disease remains largely unknown, several lines of evidence suggest thatSchizophrenia results from a series of subtle neuro-developmental defects. Disrupted in Schizophrenia1 (DISC1) was first identified as a gene disrupted in a large Scottish family affected with Schizophrenia,bipolar disorder and depression. Genetic linkage and association studies have since implicated DISC1as a probable general risk factor for Schizophrenia and other mental illnesses. Recent data indicate thatDISC1 regulates multiple facets of neuronal development; from the proliferation of neuronal precursorcells to neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth and integration of newly-born neurons in the adult brain.These studies point to a critical role of DISC1 in neurogenesis and neuronal morphogenesis throughcellular pathways and mechanisms that remain largely unexplored. Based on recently-identified DISC1partners, I postulate that DISC1 regulates membrane trafficking during neuronal development. I proposethat impaired and/or misregulated membrane transport resulting from reduced levels or diseaseassociatedmutants of DISC1 causes neuronal polarity and axon morphogenesis defects. To test myhypothesis, I have developed an imaging assay, based on GFP photoactivation, which allows me tomonitor and precisely quantify membrane transport in live, developing neurons. Using this assay, Iintend to show that DISC1 regulates polarized membrane trafficking towards the developing axon, aprocess which is key to the establishment and maintenance of neuronal polarity. Special emphasis willbe placed on determining the role of DISC1 in regulating Gsk3ß activity, an important regulator of axondevelopment recently implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders. I anticipate that this work will highlight anovel functional role of DISC1 in neuronal development, and may identify a new cellular pathway fortherapeutic intervention.
kw: DISC1, GSK3beta, schizophrenia, axon, membrane trafficking, polarity

title: Interleukin-1 Receptor Antagonist (IL-1ra): A Novel Therapeutic Approach for Corneal Inflammation
abs: The World Health Organization estimates that 314 million people are visually impaired worldwide and about 45 million of these are blind. Corneal inflammatory diseases are the second largest cause of blindness worldwide next only to cataract. It is caused by corneal injury, surgery or infection resulting in a wide variety of inflammatory eye diseases. Current strategies to suppress corneal inflammation and immune reactivity rely on drugs that have variable effectiveness and carry significant risk to the eye and the patient. Long-term use of corticosteroids can cause cataract and glaucoma, and cyclosporins can mediate nephrotoxicity. Globally, about 85% of all visual impairment and 75% of blindness can be prevented or cured. Corneal diseases are often characterized by a significant increase in the inflammatory cytokines like interleukin-1 (IL-1) released by the cornea epithelial cells. IL-1 is a pivotal mediator of the immune response to corneal injury. It binds to the IL-1 receptor and orchestrates the initial events in the wound healing mechanism, but if uncontrolled can result in corneal obliteration causing inflammatory diseases. Interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1ra), an endogenously synthesized inhibitor of IL-1, binds competitively to the same IL-1 receptor without any agonist activity. As a consequence, application of IL-1ra as a therapeutic drug has a significant appeal. In this study, we propose that naturally occurring IL-1ra can be exploited against the inflammatory milieu produced during corneal injury. The major goal of this project is to elucidate the mechanism of IL-1 driven inflammatory pathways in an injured cornea wound healing model, using IL-1 receptor antagonist deficient mice (IL-1rn-/-). The results derived from these experiments may provide a new paradigm to counteract the proinflammatory interleukins by IL-1ra, as a novel therapy to prevent corneal inflammation, without placing the patient at risk for toxicity or secondary infections.
kw: Cornea Diseases, Interleukin-1 receptor antagonist, Interleukin-1, Wound Healing, Inflammation, Cornea Injury

title: Identification and Evaluation of Novel Ribosomally-synthesized Antimicrobial Peptides (RAMPs) for Ocular Infections
abs: There are an estimated 225,000 contact lens users in Singapore and about 80% of the adult populations are affected by myopia. Contact lens-related microbial keratitis is common in tropical and subtropical countries. The pathogens readily form biofilms on the contact lens surface that can be refractory to treatment with current antibiotics, and subsequently lead to corneal infections. This may result in visual loss and subsequently the patients may require a corneal transplantation for visual rehabilitation. Ribosomally-synthesized antimicrobial peptides (RAMPs) are the natural antimicrobial agents of the host defense systems and have been combating the development of resistance by pathogens for over 100 million years. Thus, RAMPs are very attractive targets for drug development to treat conditions where traditional antibiotics are becoming less effective. The major goal of this proposal is to identify and characterize new RAMPs from economically viable natural resources and evaluate their role as antimicrobial agents in an infected contact lens and cornea model. Turtle eggs are laid in an environment where diverse populations of bacteria are found abundantly around the nesting sites. Eggshells are the natural physical barrier against microbial attack and physical environment. We hypothesize that RAMPs present in the eggshell may provide a protective secondary barrier against the invading microorganisms. Our aim is to identify and characterize various RAMPs present in the turtle eggshell, followed by analysis of their antimicrobial properties, hemolytic activity, and cytotoxicity. Promising RAMPs will be evaluated as potential antimicrobial agents in the treatment of microbial keratitis. This will be accomplished by infecting contact lenses/corneal epithelial cells with a clinically challenging pathogens and examine the role of RAMPs in preventing the formation of a biofilm. Evaluating the role of RAMPs from eggshells will lead to the development of novel compounds for the treatment of corneal infections.
kw: cornea, infections, microbial keratitis, antimicrobial peptides, structure-activity relationship, therapeutics

title: Development and evaluation of a novel, dual mode, wide-field, ocular digital imaging technology for evaluation of angle closure
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. In contrast to western countries, primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) is a major form of glaucoma in Asia, being responsible for the majority of bilateral blindness in Singapore, China and India. The main pathology in PACG is a closed anterior chamber angle, which is diagnosed clinically using gonioscopy, an instrument that uses a mirror system. However, this method is subjective and has poor to moderate agreement between clinicians, in spite of being low cost and simple to use. The search for an ideal tool which can objectively evaluate the anterior chamber angle to accurately diagnose the condition is still ongoing. Goniophotography, Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (ASOCT), Infrared gonioscopy and EyeCamTM are some of the instruments available; each of them having distinct advantages and disadvantages. Published literature and our own research done so far indicate that none of the available instruments can be used for a reliable and accurate diagnosis of angle closure disease, nor can they be utilized for population screening.We propose to develop and evaluate a novel, dual mode (infrared and visible light) wide-field digital imaging technology for ocular, especially angle imaging. The proposed instrument will utilize algorithms developed indigenously by NTU which enables imaging of curved surfaces, wide-field coverage, dual mode (in dark and light conditions) and will be of high resolution. In this study, we will build a prototype of the instrument, and then refine it using rabbit eye experiments and subsequently test it on human subjects. This instrument is expected to reliably and objectively image the angle, and will improve on existing diagnostic technologies for angle closure disease, with potential commercial applications.
kw: Ocular imaging, Angle closure Glaucoma, Conioscopy, Wide-field digital imaging, Infra-red digital imaging

title: Colony forming liver regeneration mediated in an injectable cell-laden hydrogel based phase transfer cell culture system
abs: The objective of this research project is to develop an innovative tissue engineering system for cell therapy to restore liver functionalities with a novel micro-cavitary hydrogel (MCG)-based scaffolding technology and a novel phase transfer cell culture (PTCC) strategy. This enables self-formation of morphologically bona fide neo-tissue with liver functionalities in an injectable artificial grafts. The MCG system is constructed by creating cavities in a cell-encapsulating hydrogel bulk via a delayed melting of embedded gelatin microspheres. The encapsulated cell colonies adjacent to the gel/cavity interface proliferate, outgrow the hydrogel phase and sprout into cavities based on affinity selection. This phenomenon is known as PTCC where cells fill up the hollow spaces in the entire hydrogel, forming scaffold-free neo-tissue spheroids throughout the system contributing to full liver tissue regeneration. The approach established for MCG-PTCC system can be summarized into 6 steps: (i) fabrication of gelatin spheres through emulsion method with partial surface cross linking (ii) encapsulation of gelatin spheres and cells in hydrogel. (iii) dissolving delay of microspheres results in cavities in hydrogel bulk. (iv) the interface around inner surfaces of the cavities stimulates high proliferation of adjacent liver cells. (v) filling up of cavities by outgrowing cell colonies, forming “scaffold-free” tissue; (vi) with the extended culture time, tissue islets further expand, contributing to full tissue regeneration. The clinical significance of this project is to provide a simple method to achieve self-assembled tissue in an injectable hydrogel environment which is an alternative to whole liver transplantation for liver cirrhosis patients. Self assembly and injectability in our system reduced complexity during operation as compared to culturing spheroids by spin culture. Moreover, it could potentially solve the clinical problems in the cell-based therapies such as lack of long term viability and functionality of hepatocytes, elevating the current situation of severe shortage in liver donors.
kw: Regenerative medicine, Biomaterials, Liver, Hydrogel, Cell therapy, Tissue engineering

title: Underwater Infrastructure and Underwater City of the Future
abs: A new and sustainable approach for space creation is proposed in this project. Using this approach, land can be reclaimed without the use of a large amount of fill materials and the space below the land reclaimed can also be utilized at the same time for infrastructure or other development. Precast, super-scale cylindrical structures will be used like caverns to form the underwater space. This new approach integrates reclamation, superstructure and underground space utilization into one and is thus the most efficient and cost-effective method for space creation and utilization. The design and construction of the super large cylindrical structures poses many challenges to both theories and practice. New technologies and innovative solutions are required to make the idea a reality. It is proposed in this project to carry out an intensive inter-disciplinary study to address problems related to structural, geotechnical, hydrodynamic, risk analysis, and socio-technical aspects. From this study, a series of innovative methods, new materials, and new construction technologies will be developed to make the proposed approach technically feasible and cost-effective. The scopes of the study include (a) new construction materials and innovative cylindrical structural design; (b) Innovative soil treatment and foundation methods; and (c) hydrodynamic study and harvest of energy. The innovative methods to be developed include the use of green concrete and new reinforcement, new methods for the installation of cylindrical structures such as suction caissons without soil improvement, new methods to address issues on vortex shedding, wave trapping and movement of sand waves relevant to the founding of extra large structures on the seabed, and methods to harness wave energy.
kw: Sustainability development;Infrastructure and ultilities;Land reclamation;Underwater construction;Innovative construction technologies;Space creation

title: Sustainable Urban Waste Management for 2020
abs: The main objective of this proposal is to develop a research program that would pave the way for developing sustainable urban waste management solutions for 2020. Research outcomes are expected to bring long term environmental, economical and social benefits to Singapore and eventually the rest of the world. To achieve the main objective, the following three research subprograms are proposed: Subprogram A: Communities as renewable resource recovery centres Subprogram B: Wastewater treatment plants as urban eco power stations Subprogram C: Rapid land reclamation of closed dumping grounds The key benefits of the proposed program are multi-faceted; they include the following: • Reduction of water consumption (A) • Reduction of wastewater treatment cost (A) • Recovery of NEWenergy from black water and food waste (A) • Recovery of nutrients from yellow water and digested residues (A) • Recovery of energy and compost from commercial and institutional organic wastes (A) • Reclamation of NEWater from grey water , if needed (B) • Recovery of energy from co-digestion of sludge and industrial organic wastes (B) • Reclamation of NEWland of closed urban dumping grounds (C) • Recovery of energy and materials from landfill mining (C) • Recovery of quality soil from remediated landfill site (C) The benefits listed above are substantial and applicable not only to the public sector, but also private sector. Most importantly, they could help make future urban waste management more sustainable with a decentralised “waste to resources” solution as opposed to the current centralised treatment/disposal method that has been implemented for more than 5 to 6 decades. This is important especially now that resources are diminishing rapidly.
kw: closed dumping grounds;land reclamation;anaerobic digestion;sludge co-digestion;waste to energy;waste to materials

title: Self-Assembled Organic-Inorganic Nanostructures to Solve Longstanding Problems in Physics
abs: The last decades, a vast amount of progress has been made in the development of new organic-inorganic materials. Especially appealing are the concepts of self-assembly to direct and control the synthesis of new organic-inorganic hybrid structures. In addition, the self-assembly of nanoparticles of well-defined shapes and sizes have not been widely explored, nor their use in nanoelectronics. The mechanisms of charge transport across nanoscale objects are very different from their macroscale counter parts. Large area tunnel junctions of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have been problematic to study due to the lack of reliable fabrication techniques, and to discriminate artifact from real data. The proposed arrays of tunnel junctions allow statistically large numbers of devices to be measured, and to study the mechanisms of charge transport across SAMs (and other nanostructures). The properties of magnetic impurities in a metal form one of the most intensively studied problems in solid state physics. Kondo showed, theoretically, that multiple scattering of conduction electrons by a magnetic impurity yields a divergent contribution to the resistance. Despite a great research effort over the last decades, there is still a remaining controversial aspect of the Kondo ground state: the Kondo screening cloud and the role of its characteristic dimension, the Kondo length ξK. Thin conducting films with magnetic nanostructures on top of them, form a novel class of potential Kondo systems, which could possibly shine light on the nature of the Kondo cloud.
kw: nanotechnology;molecular electronics;Kondo-effect;self-assembly;nanoparticles;supramolecular chemistry

title: Modeling complex interactions in the genetics and genomics of common phenotypes and infectious diseases
abs: Complex interactions between different genomes and with the environment present a significant challenge in the analysis of large-scale genomic data. Understanding and utilizing these interactions is important for downstream functional and pharmacogenomics developments. Exposure to different environments exerts distinctive evolutionary pressures in the genomes of organisms, which leave genetic signatures of these adaptations. This feature is known as positive natural selection, and is responsible for pathogens developing resistance to drug treatments, and for complex traits in humans like skin pigmentation and the ability to digest lactose in adulthood. Identifying genetic signatures of positive selection can often lead to the discovery of the genetic pathways responsible for trait variations, which is important for downstream therapeutic and translational developments in controlling and altering these traits. Sophisticated mathematical algorithms are required to detect these genetic signals of adaption, and current strategies are only capable of detecting signals that are common in the community. These methods are unlikely to discover signals that are rarer, which are the likely scenarios for emerging adaptations (for example, drug resistance strains in influenza). I propose to develop a novel mathematical strategy for identifying adaptations that are very recent and thus comparatively rare. Genetic variants that emerged from recent genome-wide surveys in diseases are mostly surrogates of the causal variants, and fine-mapping aims to deconvolute these association signals to identify the functional polymorphisms. The presence of long stretches of correlation in the human genome has proven useful for identifying regions that are associated with the phenotype, but creates a major challenge in distilling biologically irrelevant markers that are in high or perfect linkage disequilibrium with the causal variants. I propose to establish a novel strategy for combining trans-population genomic information to narrow the candidates for the causal variant, which is the goal of genetic studies of diseases.
kw: Statistical genetics;host-pathogen interaction;genome-environment interaction;genome-genome interaction

title: Eliminating chronic myeloid leukaemia stem cells by targeting proten post-translational modification
abs: The resistance of leukaemia stem cells (LSC) to Bcr-Abl tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI), such asimatinib, poses a therapeutic challenge in the management of chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML). Onestrategy to overcome LSC resistance is by targeting both Bcr-Abl-dependent and -independentpathways. Ras and Rac GTPases play important roles in CML haematopoiesis and leukaemogenesisand are attractive Bcr-Abl-independent targets. The biological function of Ras and Rac GTPases isdependent, to a large extent, on prenylation, a post-translational modification process. Prenylation canbe inhibited by depleting isoprenoid substrates produced in the mevalonate pathway, in which HMGCoAreducatase is a rate-limiting enzyme. Prenylation can also be targeted by inhibiting catalyticenzymes, such as farnesyl transferase (FT), geranylgeranyl transferase or isoprenylcysteine carboxylmethyltransferase (Icmt). We propose that LSC can be eliminated by inhibiting Bcr-Abl together withinhibiting prenylation, either ‘upstream’ with an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (e.g. statins) or‘downstream’ with a novel Icmt inhibitor (e.g. cysmethynil). Statins and cysmethynil have pre-clinicalefficacy against various tumour subtypes. Inhibition of FT alone or in combination with Bcr-Abl TKIreduces the number of CML LSC. We have shown that cysmethynil or simvastatin augments Bcr-AblTKI-induced apoptosis in CML cell lines and primary CML CD34+ cells and that this is possiblymediated through impairment of Ras or Rac activity. Our proposed studies will investigate the effect ofcombining Icmt inhibiton with Bcr-Abl inhibition or HMG-CoA reductase inhibition with Bcr-Abl inhibitionon primary CML stem and progenitor cells. We will investigate the effect of combining prenylationinhibitors with Bcr-Abl TKI in a transgenic CML murine model. This model mimics human CML andallows us to study the effects on haemopoietic stem cell (HSC) and progenitor cell number,clonogenicity and HSC competitive repopulation ability. Finally, we will elucidate the mechanisms bywhich the inhibition of prenylation enhances Bcr-Abl inhibition-induced killing.

title: Toward Efficient Sunlight Harvesting
abs: It is extremely beneficial to learn from nature on many elegant designs of photosynthesis perfected by millennia of evolution. Using femtosecond laser and quantum information theory, we explore the energy transfer pathways and develop a unified framework for excitation transfer from pigments to reaction centers in photosynthetic systems. In addition, we also seek to discover guiding principles for the optimal design of molecular structures and artificial devices to best enhance the efficiency and robustness of light-harvesting. Knowledge gained from the project will facilitate discovery of alternative materials and nanostructures for higher performance-cost ratio and help design artificial light-harvesting devices with an emphasis on efficiency and robustness of coherent energy transfer in a disordered but correlated environment.

title: Phase III Multi-Centre Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial of Selective InternalRadiation Therapy versus Sorafenib in Locally Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma.AHCC protocol 06.
abs: BackgroundApproximately 25% of HCC may benefit from potentially curative ablative therapies such assurgical resection or radio-frequency ablation. For the rest, options are limited and theprognosis is poor. Sorafenib, a systemic therapy confers improvement in survival that isimportant for patients with extra-hepatic (metastatic) HCC because there is no other provenefficacious therapy. In the group of patients with locally advanced HCC however, the benefits ofsorafenib over efficacious loco-regional ablative therapy Selective Internal Radiation Therapy(SIRT) is unclear.HypothesisSelective-internal radiation therapy (SIRT) confers better overall survival compared to sorafenibtherapy in the treatment of locally advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma.AimsTo conduct a phase III multi-center open-label randomized controlled trial that compares theefficacy of SIRT versus sorafenib in the management of locally advanced hepatocellularcarcinoma.MethodologyThis investigator-initiated multi-centre study will enroll 360 patients in a phase III trial under theauspices of the Asia-Pacific Hepatocellular Carcinoma Trials Group. Patients with locallyadvanced HCC who satisfy the study eligibility criteria, will be randomized to receive either:• A single administration of SIRT (SIR-Spheres®) targeted at HCC in the liver by the transarterialroute.• Oral Sorafenib therapy at a dose of 400 mg b.i.d until disease progression, no furtherresponse, complete regression or unacceptable toxicity.Exclusion criteria include previous systemic therapy or trans-arterial delivered therapy,metastatic disease or complete occlusion of the main portal vein.Overall Survival (OS) is the primary endpoint and will be assessed according to intention-totreat.Secondary endpoints are tumour response rate, time to tumour progression, progressionfree survival, Qol and down-staging to receive potentially curative therapy.Clinical SignificanceDefinitive data comparing these 2 therapies will determine clinical practice in the large group ofpatients with locally advanced HCC and improve outcomes for such patients.

title: Geological records of coastal hazards in southeast Asia
abs: This project aims to investigate the recurrence interval of large storms and tsunami in the northern South China Sea using historical and geological records. The area is seiemically active, experiencing earthquakes and tsunami along with frequent typhoons (tropical cyclones) early reconnaissance indicates that the coastal geology of this region records the impacts of historical and prehistorical events. Thus this area provides a unique opportunity to study the coastal impacts of tsunami and storm events. This project will use proven techniques for investigating storm and tsunami deposits to investigate a region where the risk and recurrence interval of these events is poorly understood. The work is regionally important as more than 45 million people and infrastructure worth more than $500 billion are at risk in this region. The work is scientifically important beacuse earth scientists still struggle to distinguish between storms and tsunami in the geological record.

title: Tailoring electronic structure of graphene for nanoelectronic, photonic and phononic applications
abs: Graphene, a novel two-dimensional atomic crystals made of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb lattice, has attracted great attentions because of its extraordinary electrical and mechanical properties. However the fact that graphene is metallic even at the neutrality point has been a major obstacle for developing device applications based on graphene transistors. In this proposal, we propose to develop methodology to effectively tailor electronic structure of graphene through structural deformation like applying local strain and chemical decoration like introducing foreign functional groups. The strain effects on the decoration such as tuning energy barrier required by decoration and selectively decorating graphene along certain crystallography will be investigated. Secondly, the evolution of the electronic structure of graphene will be in-situ studied by the proposed integrated facrication/characterization system, mainly through optical approaches like in-situ IR and Raman spectroscopy.

title: Translational pipeline: Developing novel therapeutics for cancer treatment, including the role of histone deacetylase inhibitors
abs: Program 1Cancer arises from aberrant cellular signaling as a result of overexpression of cellular receptors,mutations of cellular proteins, or silencing of tumour suppressor proteins. Small molecules andmonoclonal antibodies have been developed to modulate crucial molecules involved with oncogenicsignaling with successful application in EGFR-mutant adenocarcinoma of the lung, bcr-abl in CML, c-kitin GIST, PARP inhibitors for BRCA mutated breast cancer. With rapid screening and lead optimization,new agents have been developed against a variety of targets, making it imperative to design clinicaltrials that aim to prove inhibition in molecularly characterized tumours, optimally combine drugs, andwith relevance to East Asia, to evaluate efficacy in Asian tumours. Our group has developed several ofthese drugs from first in human to phase II studies, and we are well positioned to lead this effort in Asiawith successful partnerships drug developers. This program will amalgamate a team to conductpreclinical and early phase studies on several small molecules.Program 2An emerging class of anticancer drugs, histone deacetylase inhibitors, has been shown to acetylatehistone proteins, thereby relaxing chromatin and inducing expression of genes. Other cellular proteinsare also acetylated, and collectively small molecule histone deacetylase inhibitors exert pleiotrophiceffects on aberrant oncogenic pathways to induce apoptosis and inhibition of cell proliferation. Despitedemonstrating significant activity in cell lines and approval of prototype hydroxamic class panHDACinhibitor vorinostat for treating peripheral T-cell lymphoma, as single agent therapy antitumour activityhas been modest in clinical trials. Our preliminary in vitro work demonstrates highly synergistic activitywith gemcitabine in cancer cell lines, and we are beginning to elucidate this mechanistically. We havefound that glucuronidation is the main disposition pathway for belinostat and will pursue studies todetermine the impact of polymorphisms on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of this groupof molecules.

title: Singapore Heart Failure Outcomes and Phenotypes
abs: Heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HF-PEF) is a major public health problem. While studies from Western populations suggest that the prevalence and outcomes for HF-PEF are similar to that of HF with low ejection fraction (HF-lowEF), results vary widely and virtually no data exists in Asian populations. The continued lack of proven therapies in HF-PEF underscores the existing knowledge gaps regarding key pathophysiologic characteristics of this syndrome.Specific Aims1.Determine the overall prevalence and inter-ethnic differences in prevalence of HF-PEF within the population presenting with decompensated HF. We hypothesize that HF-PEF accounts for 50% of presentations and differs by ethnicity due to ethnic-specific differences in underlying substrates (including hypertension and diabetes) for HF. 2.Determine the clinical outcome of HF-PEF compared to HF-lowEF. We hypothesize that HF-PEF patients have lower mortality and rehospitalisation rates compared to HF-lowEF patients.3.Obtain detailed phenotypic characterization of HF-PEF using state-of-the-art methods, compared to HF-lowEF and age-/sex-matched controls without HF. We hypothesize that important cardiovascular structural and functional differences exist between HF-PEF and HF-lowEF, which are discernible on careful phenotypic characterization by echocardiography, vascular assessment, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and neurohormonal measurements.4.Perform pilot trials in HF-PEF using novel natriuretic peptides. We hypothesize that specially designed peptides will have superior biological properties compared to native natriuretic peptides, offering unique therapeutic benefit in HF-PEF.We propose a large, prospective multi-centre longitudinal study of in-/out-patients with a primary diagnosis of HF and age-/sex-matched controls without HF from the general community. All will undergo clinical assessment, comprehensive bio-imaging, neurohormonal profiling and follow-up for all-cause mortality and rehospitalisation at 2 years.This research will provide important information regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology and outcomes of HF-PEF in multiethnic Singapore, leading to greater understanding of the HF burden in Asians and identification of potential therapeutic targets.

title: Elucidation of the Roles of CAAX Proteins That Mediate the Antitumor Efficacy of Cysmethynil, Novel Icmt Inhibitor
abs: Targeting of protein prenylation, a three-step posttranslational process critical for function of a group ofproteins termed CAAX proteins, has been a focus in cancer research ever since the Ras oncoproteinswere identified as recipients of this processing. The shift from the Ras-centric view to the understandingthat multiple CAAX proteins play important roles in cancer has stimulated efforts to target the enzymeisoprenylcysteine carboxylmethyltransferase (Icmt), as it catalyzes the final step common to all CAAXproteins. The validity of targeting Icmt was first provided by gene disruption studies whichdemonstrated that Icmt function is important in oncogenic transformation. Our recent studies with anovel small molecule inhibitor of Icmt, cysmethynil, demonstrated that pharmacologic inhibition of Icmtinduces growth arrest and death in cancer cells in culture, and also markedly reduces tumor burden inmouse xenograft models. Our data provided the first evidence that inhibition of Icmt in cancer cellsinduces a cellular process termed autophagy; this process has recently captured attention as apotential therapeutic strategy. We found that the high level of autophagy induced by Icmt inhibition canenhance cell death either directly or through apoptosis. To identify the CAAX proteins that mediate theinduction of autophagy in response to cysmethynil treatment, we performed a screen using siRNAtargeting of all CAAX proteins. The screen yielded several CAAX proteins as potential novel regulatorsof autophagy. We propose to elucidate the nature of the involvement of these CAAX proteins in thecontrol of autophagy and cysmethynil-induced cancer cell death, and to assess the functional impact ofthese selected CAAX proteins in the development and progression of human cancer. These studiesshould provide novel insight into the regulation of autophagy and its impact on cell death, and alsoprovide critical information on targeting Icmt as an effective anti-cancer strategy.

title: Individualizing doses and predicting drug-drug interactions for anti-cancer and anti-HIV medications metabolized by UDP-glucuronosyltransferases
abs: Phase 2 enzymes metabolize a number of key drugs such as irinotecan, a leading cancer drug, and some anti-HIV drugs. Their importance is growing as the proportion of newly licensed drugs that are metabolized by these enzymes (instead of phase 1 enzymes) increases.To individualize therapy for these drugs, it is important to measure enzyme activity. Clinical probes for phase 1 enzymes exist but probes for phase 2 enzymes are limited. An ideal probe would accurately predict concentrations of clinically important drugs yet be non-toxic and not interact with therapy.My overall aim is to develop raltegravir as a probe for the phase 2 enzyme UDP-glucurnosyltransferase (UGT) 1A1. Raltegravir is a non-toxic metabolically-inert anti-HIV drug metabolized predominantly by UGT1A1. I hypothesize that raltegravir glucuronidation will predict concentrations and toxicities of irinotecan, thus allowing individualization of irinotecan dosage. I also hypothesize that raltegravir glucuronidation can predict drug-drug interactions involving UGT1A1, and that it can be added to zidovudine to form a UGT probe cocktail.Specific Aim 1: To demonstrate that raltegravir glucuronidation is a more precise probe than UGT1A1 genotyping for predicting pharmacokinetics of the cancer chemotherapy drug irinotecan.Specific Aim 2: To demonstrate the lack of effect of zidovudine on raltegravir glucuronidation and so allow the use of both drugs together as a probe cocktail for UGT1A1 and UGT2B7.Specific Aim 3: To demonstrate that the formation of raltegravir glucuronide will increase after administration of the inducer rifampicin and decrease after administration of the inhibitor atazanavir, thus validating the use of raltegravir as a UGT1A1 probe.We plan two clinical studies: 1.A study in cancer patients correlating irinotecan pharmacokinetics with raltegravir and the phase 1 enzyme probe midazolam2.A drug-drug interaction study in healthy volunteers between the anti-HIV drugs raltegravir and zidovudine, atazanavir and rifampicin

title: Understanding the Role of Chemical Communication in Insect Social Behavior: Identifying New Pheromones, Neural Circuits, and Metabolic Pathways Using Novel Mass Spectrometry Methods
abs: Many animals communicate through pheromones, chemical signals that can mediate behaviors as diverse as dominance, aggression, and mating. Insects express these chemical messengers on their cuticular surface in the form of hydrocarbon-based lipid molecules. I have recently developed several mass spectrometry-based methods that enable these components to be identified directly and rapidly from the intact animals and from crude cuticular extracts. Importantly, these novel methods complement existing techniques by detecting new chemical classes of cuticular compounds that had not been found before. By combining structural characterization of these chemicals together with Drosophila genetic tools that target disruption of single genes or single neural circuits, it will be possible to define many of the cellular and biochemical pathways underlying pheromone perception and ultimately, behavior. Moreover, the same mass spectrometry methods and chemical and behavioral analysis can be applied to examine pheromones of the yellow fever mosquito. Characterization of pheromones and their role in chemical communication provides an opportunity for identifying the neural substrates underlying complex social behaviors. In addition, there is significant potential for developing methods to control populations of disease-bearing insects such as mosquitoes.
