title: Regulation of TRAP1 expression and the impact on breast cancer progression
abs: A novel oncogenic mechanism has been proposed whereby the function of tumour suppressor proteins are impaired not by inactivating mutations, but by the loss of their molecular chaperone. The tumour necrosis factor receptor associated protein 1 (TRAP1, also known as heat shock protein (HSP) 75kDa) is a chaperone of retinoblastoma (Rb) and accentuates Rb regulation of cell cycle progression. Breast tumours which downregulate TRAP1 were associated with poor prognosis. This study aims firstly to characterize the pattern of TRAP1 expression in normal breast tissue, primary breast tumours and nodal metastases to evaluate the role of TRAP1 in breast tumour progression. Secondly, we will focus on the role of VHL and p53 in the regulation of TRAP1 expression. Preliminary work has found TRAP1 expression to be positively modulated by VHL. There are no published reports on TRAP1 regulation, however, p53 is known to regulate HSP70 (which bears close homology to TRAP1) and VHL has been reported to stabilize and activate p53. This raises the possibility that VHL may regulate TRAP1 through a p53-dependent mechanism. TRAP1 mRNA and protein expression levels will be evaluated in p53-deficient cell lines prior to and following re-introduction of p53. Sequential and concomitant silencing of VHL and p53 will determine whether VHL and p53 act together or independently of each other. In vivo luciferase assays using a TRAP1-promoter construct will provide conclusive evidence of whether VHL and p53 regulate TRAP1 transcription. Finally, the clinical significance of this will be evaluated with immunohistochemistry and quantitative RNA analysis of clinical specimens. The role of TRAP1 in breast cancer progression represents a novel oncogenic mechanism that has not been described. Understanding how TRAP1 is regulated in tumours will allow not only for better prognostication, but also for the development of novel therapeutic targets.
kw: Breast Cancer, Tumour progression, p53

title: Identification and dissection of mechanistic action of anticancer multidrug resistance reversal agents from a natural product library
abs: The objective of this pilot study is to identify and dissect the biological mechanism of action of anticancer multidrug resistance (MDR) reversal (MDRR) agents in a natural product library. These putative MDRR agents subsequently have the potential to be developed into adjuncts to current cancer chemotherapy protocols.MDR is a major factor in the failure of many forms of cancer chemotherapy. Resistance to treatment has been correlated to the presence of P-glycoprotein (P-gp), a transporter protein in the plasma membrane that actively expels chemotherapy drugs from the cell interior. Hence there is a pressing need to develop novel therapeutics to overcome MDR.The aims of this pilot study are to:a.Identify putative MDRR agents from a natural product libraryb.Determine the mechanism of action of putative MDRR agentsc.Validate clinical therapeutic potential of putative MDRR agents in a MDR xenograft mouse modelPutative MDRR agents validated in this pilot study would ultimately be used to reverse MDR in human tumors expressing P-gp.
kw: cancer, resistance, natural product, multidrug, MDR, MDRR agent

title: Functional genetic of adrenomedullin receptor gene in diabetic nephropathy
abs: Background: This is an exploratory project that will guide us in planning future studies in the functional genetics of adrenomedullin receptor (ADMR). Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is strongly influenced by genetic determinants. Adrenomedullin (ADM) is an important vasoactive factor in the pathogenesis of DN. We reported that plasma ADM is elevated in DN. The clearance of ADM is receptor (i.e. ADMR) dependent. Therefore, ADMR is a candidate gene for DN. We made the novel observation that a common 5’ promoter haplotype (formed by 3 SNPs in perfect linkage disequilibrium [r’=1.0], -244 C>T, -120G>T & –32 C>T [rs2279373], estimated minor haplotype TTT frequency = 0.14) of ADMR gene conferred a reduced susceptibility to DN (OR 0.71 [95%CI 0.55-0.91], P=0.007). rs2279373 is a predicted binding site for transcription factor Sp1. We also observed that allele T was associated with elevated plasma ADM concentrations in a dominant fashion (0.950.63 nM vs. 0.710.35, P=0.038) suggesting that the variation could be functional.Hypothesis: ADMR promoter exhibits haplotype specific differential efficiency (i.e. TTT < CGC) of gene transcriptionAim & methods: Using Dual Luciferase reporter gene assay in Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cell (HUVEC):(1) To study the functional of ADMR 5’ promoter haplotype (i.e. CGC vs. TTT)(2) To study the functional contribution of each of the individual promoter SNP by specific length genetic construct (i.e. truncation assay).Significance:The current proposal is a natural extension of our extensive preliminary observation.1. Inform our subsequent decision to further probe the ADMR haplotype function e.g. by electrophoretic mobility shift analysis or RNA interference.2. Strengthen ADMR as a novel candidate gene and shed light on the pathogenic mechanism of DN.3. ADM & ADMR are attractive novel targets for pharmacological intervention4. Common SNP like rs2279373 will confer substantial population attributable risk.
kw: Functional genetic, Adrenomedullin receptor, Diabetic nephropathy

title: THE ISOLATION AND CRYOPRESERVATION OF MALE GERMLINE STEM CELLS (SPERMATOGONIAL STEM CELLS) USING THE MOUSE AS A MODEL FOR THEHUMAN
abs: Aim: To establish the cryobiological conditions for optimal recovery of purified spermatogonial stem cells(SSCs) after cryopreservation. The mouse will be used as a model since most of the current work hasbeen conducted on mice.Hypothesis: Any cell type has its own membrane characteristics which determine its response tocryoprotective agent and cooling rate such that the protocol must be separately devised. So far onlymixed testicular cell populations have been cryopreserved and recoveries have not been optimised.Methods: A germ cell population will be recovered from the experimentally cryptorchid testis, and thenenriched for SSCs using flow cytometric sorting and fluorescently labelled antibodies to potentially uniquecombinations of characteristics of the cell surface.The enriched SSC samples will be subject to systematic investigation of sensitivity to commoncryoprotective agents. Having established the cryoprotective agent of choice, the optimum packagingand cooling rate will be determined using a controlled rate freezer. This should provide an optimisedcryopreservation package. Additionally, vitrification of samples will be investigated since many cell typescan be preserved by vitrification which allows storage in liquid nitrogen without the stresses of ice crystalformation in the sample. Criteria of success will be cell viability and the ability to divide in culture andretain their characteristic surface markers. Optimally cryopreserved cells will be tested for their ability toestablish spermatogenesis in a mouse transplant model using busulphan-treated sterile SCID mice.The application of this work is in storing enriched SSC samples from individual cancer patients prior totheir chemo- or radiotherapy for use in restoring their fertility after recovery from disease. This project willcontribute the essential missing step to establish the optimum cryobiological conditions for purifiedsample of SSCs.
kw: Stem Cells, cryopreservation, spermatogonia, male germline

title: Combined chemotherapy of gefitinib and API-2 inhibits survival of glioma stem cells without affecting survival of differentiated glioma cells.
abs: Recent isolation and identification of brain tumour stem cells (BTSCs) suggest that tumourigenicity is due to a selected population of stem-like cells and not all cells in the brain tumour mass. Thus, strategies targeting BTSCs are critical for improvement of brain tumour therapies. In this study, our aims are:1.To target BTSCs with combined chemotherapy of gefitinib and API-2 (inhibitors of tyrosine kinase and Akt, respectively), and show that combined inhibition of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and Akt activation synergistically reduces survival of BTSCs, without affecting survival of differentiated glioma cells in vitro and in vivo. 2.To investigate the anti-proliferative mechanisms of combined gefitinib and API-2 in BTSCs, whether the reduced survival are due to significant inhibition of Akt activation, DNA synthesis and cell cycle progression.We will use BTSCs and differentiated glioma cells cultured from malignant glioma tissues, as well as commercial BTSCs (HuBCSC) to investigate the anti-tumour effects of combined gefitinib and API-2 (compared to single treatments) by colony formation, cell proliferation and cell cycle analyses. We will analyse CD133+ cell population, phosphorylation of Akt, Akt activities and BrdU incorporation following treatment with API-2 and/ or gefitinib in BTSCs and differentiated gliomas. In vivo, we will xenograft hind legs of nude mice with HuBCSC, BTSCs and differentiated glioma cells, followed by gefitinib and/or API-2 treatment. Tumour growth will be measured and immunohistochemical staining of phospho-Akt, total Akt and CD133 in tumour tissues will be analysed. This study will reveal targeting of BTSCs with combined API-2 and gefitinib, by enhanced inhibition of Akt and DNA synthesis that lead to greater anti-tumour responses in BTSCs than differentiated glioma cells. Targeting BTSCs with API-2 and gefitinib, with their potential clinical use, will easily be translated to patients benefits.
kw: Glioma stem cells, Akt, survival, EGFR, Gefitinib, API-2

title: A Proof-of-Concept Study to Investigate the Exercise Mimetic Effects of Resveratrol-Induced SIRT1 Activation on PGC1-Alpha Regulation and Insulin Sensitivity
abs: BackgroundResveratrol, a natural constituent of red wine, effectively activates SIRT1 in vivo, leading to the activation of the master regulator PGC1-a with increased peripheral glucose disposal. PGC1-a is involved in fibre-type transformation and mitochondrial biogenesis. T2DM patients have a lower proportion of PGC1-a expression, slow fibres and mitochondrial density. The downstream effects of SIRT1 activation suggest that resveratrol may act as an exercise mimetic. Animal models have shown that SIRT1 activation is associated with improved insulin sensitivity and survival advantage. HypothesisResveratrol-induced SIRT1 activation in skeletal muscles is associated with increased insulin sensitivity.AimsThe primary aim of this study is to demonstrate that resveratrol-induced SIRT1 activation in skeletal muscles is associated with improved insulin sensitivity in subjects with T2DM and obesity.The secondary aims of the study are to study the effects of resveratrol-induced SIRT activation on downstream signaling, energy expenditure, clinical and biochemical parameters.MethodologyThis is a proof-of-concept study with a 2-arm double-blind randomized placebo-controlled design. Subjects are randomized to receive either resveratrol or placebo for 3 months after a 2-week placebo run-in period. Descriptive data collection includes adipose tissue content and distribution, indirect calorimetry, pedometer readings, biochemical and hormonal studies. Skeletal muscle biopsy will be performed to study expression of SIRT1 protein and its downstream targets.Clinical SignificanceThis study will show for the first time in humans, whether resveratrol-induced SIRT1 activation leads to improved insulin sensitivity. The mechanistic science of this study is closely tied to the descriptive clinical outcome and the hypothesis to be studied is one that is important epidemiologically, testable, focused and based on previous research. The results of this study will increase the understanding of the mechanisms of exercise and caloric restriction in treating T2DM and potentially provides a new therapeutic target for the development of more potent SIRT1 activators.
kw: Diabetes, Type 2, Insulin, PGC1-alpha, Resveratrol, SIRT1

title: A proof-of-concept study using a novel microfluidics platform for HIV-1 viral load quantification.
abs: BACKGROUND:A decentralized point-of-care HIV-1 viral quantitation test for treatment monitoring is much-needed but unavailable. A lab-on-a-chip miniaturizing all functions of a conventional laboratory in performing real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RRT-PCR) is a potential solution. Our IBN collaborator recently published in Nature Medicine 2007 the first integrated system of this kind detecting another RNA virus, H5N1 avian influenza.AIMS:We aim to conduct a proof-of-concept trial to demonstrate the feasibility of a microfluidic platform for the quantification of HIV-1 viral load via duplex RRT-PCR with an internal control. There are 2 phases as detailed below. If successful, we will be the first group world-wide to establish such a HIV-1 test.HYPOTHESES:Our microfluidic platform using a disposable credit-card-sized chip can accurately quantify HIV-1 viral loads (linear regression R2>0.95 over a dynamic range of 104 to 107 RNA copies/ ml patient plasma). A viral load of 104 RNA copies/ mL patient plasma represents a biologic threshold below which CD4 counts remain stable and risk of clinical progression is low. METHODOLOGY:Phase 1:We aim to develop 3 areas before the proof-of-concept experiment (collaborators responsible in brackets):1. Hardware for multiple-channel detection and further miniaturization (J. Pipper, IBN)2. RRT-PCR protocol (M. Inoue, IMCB; O.T. Ng, TTSH)3. Sample source (O.T. Ng, TTSH; Y. S. Leo, TTSH)Phase 2:This phase involves 2 sequential experiments using the results from phase 1:1. Performing RRT-PCR using uninfected blood spiked with HIV-1 RNA.2. Performing RRT-PCR using blood from HIV-1 infected patients.CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE:This microfluidic platform can be further developed into a field-ready hand-held device for monitoring HIV-1 viral loads in resource-poor settings for:1. Improvement in treatment outcomes with early detection of treatment failure.2. Diagnosis of HIV-1 infection in infants.With further refinements, it could compete with conventional laboratory-based RRT-PCR.
kw: HIV-1, Microfluidics, Real Time RT PCR

title: iTRAQ-coupled 2D LC-MS/MS Analysis on Protein Profile in Asian Patients Receiving WarfarinTreatment and HepG2 Cells Incubated with S- and R-Warfarin: Potential in Biomarker Discovery forEffective Warfarin Dosing
abs: Recognizing specific protein changes in response to drug administration in humans has the potential for the development of personalized medicine. Such changes can be identified by pharmacoproteomics approach based on proteomic technologies. When combined with pharmacogenomics, pharmacoproteomics has an important role in the development of personalized medicines. While proteomic analysis can be of relevance to molecular diagnostics in personalized medicine, pharmacoproteomics can provide functional representation of patient-to-patient variation. It can also be helpful in matching a particular target-based therapy to a particular marker in a subgroup of patients, in addition to the profile of genetic polymorphism. Warfarin is a commonly prescribed oral anticoagulant in patients with prosthetic valve disease, venous thromboembolism and stroke. It is a racemic mixture of R- and S-enantiomers and undergoes stereoselective metabolism. The S-warfarin is believed to account for 60-70% of the overall anticoagulation response, with the R-enantiomer accounting for 30-40%. There are wide interindividual variations in therapeutic response to the clinically available racemic warfarin.Using iTRAQ-coupled proteomic LC-MS/MS analysis, we have demonstrated the feasibility of identifying specific proteins in patients receiving low or high dose of warfarin. In this proposal, we propose to consolidate our combined pharmacoproteomics and pharmacogenetics approach for better warfarin treatment. The specific aims in this proposal include: 1). Identify specific proteins in patients receiving low or high dose of warfarin; 2). Establish protein profile in HepG2 cells incubated with S- or R-warfarin.The specific serum proteins identified in this proposal should have the potential to be the prognostic biomarkers to facilitate rapid optimization of warfarin therapy for local Asian patients, while the cellular protein profile should shed new light on the differential anticoagulating efficiency of S- and R-warfarin.Our approach has the application potential for other target-based therapies and should provide valuable information for the development of personalized medicine.
kw: LC-MS/MS Proteomics, Warfarin, Biomarker in Asian Patients, Chiral Enantiomers

title: MicroRNAs and metabolic diseases
abs: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is a major health burden in Singapore. Common metabolic diseases like hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus and hypertension are contributory to this significant increase in morbidity and mortality. For diabetes mellitus, despite having reached epidemic proportions, pathogenetic mechanisms of disease and their resultant complications are not completely understood. The combined defects in insulin secretion and insulin function contribute to hyperglycemia. It is however not fully known how disease progression occurs, with persistent damage to islet cells from by hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and oxidative stress likely to play a major role. A better understanding at the molecular level of cell biology and the mechanisms of insulin secretion and insulin resistance may provide insight into pathogenesis of disease and possibly guide our future preventive strategies and even lead to the development of novel therapeutic targets. In this exploratory project we aim at studying the expression profile of non-coding small RNAs such as microRNAs (miRNAs) present in the blood samples of various patients in different stages of diabetes, hypercholesterolemia and/or hypertension. In our laboratory we have already established that miRNA profiling can be effectively carried out from patient’s blood sample as little as 0.5 ml. The miRNAs detected will be used in determining their target genes and our interpretations will be validated using mRNA expression studies from tissues extracted from our animal models on hyperlipidemia, hypercholesterolemia and diabetes mellitus. This will enable us to understand the mechanism of action (gene activation or silencing) of the specific microRNAs. We are confident that our exploratory study will enable us to make future IRG applications to elucidate the potential of targeting selected miRNAs and their genes as possible therapeutic options as has been successfully carried out for miR-122 expression in non-human primate (Elmen etal., 17 Apr 2008, Nature, 452: 896-900)

title: The use of an immunomodulatory protein as a mucosal adjuvant for sublingual immunotheraphy for allergic asthma
abs: Up to 30 % of the population in industrial countries are affected by allergic diseases such as rhinitis, conjunctivitis, atopic dermatitis or bronchial asthma. Current therapies for these allergic diseases are largely symptomatic and allergen-specific immunotherapy (SIT) is the only treatment capable of modifying the course of allergic disease. However the major setback of the current SIT treatments is the inconsistent efficacy, it is believed that the inclusion of an effective adjuvant in SIT is the key to overcome such problem. Sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) is a method of choice for pediatrics patients as it is a noninvasive procedure, and the WHO ARIA statement acknowledges that the use of SLIT in children with respiratory allergies is evidence based. The long term objective of this study is to develop a more effective adjuvanted SLIT for allergic diseases. The current paradigm of immune mechanisms for successful sublingual immunotherapy of allergic diseases is the induction of allergen-specific regulatory T cells that suppress the development of allergic reactions. We hypothesize that sublingual co-administration of allergens with an immunomodulatory protein, designated as Fve (a fungal immunomodulatroy protein isolated from the edible mushroom Flammulina velutipes), could act as an adjuvant by enhancing such regulatory T cell responses and hence improve the efficacy of sublingual immunotherapy. Indeed, our recent preliminary data showed that Fve could expand the number of human Foxp3+CD4+CD25+ T cells and induced cell proliferation of mouse CD4+CD25+ T cells in vitro. These data indicated that Fve may serve as an immunomodulator that can potentially enhance the induction of regulatory T cells. The specific aims are : (1). To examine the immune responses after sublingual administration of allergen alone or allergen together with the immunomodulatory Fve protein in a mouse asthma model – with focus on the generation of allergen-specific regulatory T cells (Tr); and (2). To examine its subsequent effects on allergic airway diseases. The anticipated results from this study will represent a breakout in SIT for allergy as the adjuvant effects of Fve can be exploited for as an universal adjuvant for other immunotherapeutic vaccines for allergy in general.
kw: sublingual immunotheraphy, allergic asthma, immunomodulaion, mucosal adjuvant

title: Evaluation of the anti-inflammatory effect of recombinant lactobacilli for the treatmentof atopic dermatitis
abs: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common pruritic and chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disease of globalimportance. Current treatment for AD is largely symptomatic, and therefore novel therapy with theprospect of more effective treatment of this chronic disease is much needed. Dust mite allergy plays amajor role in the pathogenesis of allergic diseases. Although specific-allergen immunotherapy (SIT) is aneffective therapeutic modality for respiratory allergies, its effectiveness in AD is still uncertain. The longterm objective of this proposed study is to develop an effective means of SIT via orally administeredallergen adjuvanted by probiotics for the treatment of AD. Probiotics, such as lactobacilli, have beenshown to have anti-inflammatory and beneficial effects in the prevention and treatment of eczema inhumans. These effects could be conferred by the immuno-regulatory properties of probiotics, which mayserve as a microbial adjuvant for induction and differentiation of T regulatory cells in an oral mucosalmicro-environment. Recent published studies support the notion that antigen delivery through the oralmucosa route is an effective way to induce antigen-specific regulatory T cells. Additionally, the majorityof the CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells bear the functional skin-homing receptor. We, thereforerationalize that oral administration of recombinant lactobacilli expressing allergen would be an effectiveway to induce allergen-specific T-regulatory cells resulting in effective suppression of cellular andneurogenic inflammation seen in atopic dermatitis. As preliminary work, we have produced lactobacilliexpressing recombinant Blo t 5, which when delivered orally could successfully inhibit the production ofBlo t 5-specific IgE in a mouse model for AD that has been established in our laboratory. The specificaim of this study is to evaluate the effects of different recombinant lactobacilli strains expressing a majordust mite allergen Blot 5 in the treatment of AD in a mouse model. The anticipated results generatedfrom this study will potentially pave the way to develop a new immunotherapeutic strategy for atopicdermatitis.
kw: Atopic dermatitis, Allergic inflammation, Immunotherapy, Recombinant probiotics, Neurogenic inflammation

title: Preclinical investigation of the impact of a small molecule isoprenylcysteine carboxylmethyltransferase (Icmt) inhibitor on tumor growth and metastasis in mouse models of cancer.
abs: Many key regulatory proteins involved in oncogenic signaling processes are modified at their C-terminus by a process termed prenylation. This processing involves addition of an isoprenoid lipid, a proteolytic step, and then carboxymethylation by an enzyme termed Icmt. Genetic and pharmacologic blockade of Icmt activity has profound consequences on oncogenic transformation. The focus of this application is on a potent and selective small molecule inhibitor of Icmt termed cysmethynil. The studies are designed to further advance the preclinical evaluation of cysmethynil as an anticancer agent. In Aim 1, we will investigate the in vivo efficacy of cysmethynil using xenograft mouse models. Cysmethynil treatment of cancer cells causes G1 arrest and triggers a cell-death pathway termed autophagy, and significantly impacts tumor growth in xenograft models. These studies will be extended to assessing the in vivo efficacy of cysmethynil on hepatocellular and gastric cancers. In Aim 2, we will investigate in vivo biomarkers correlating with cysmethynil dosing. In Aim 3, we will test the hypothesis that cysmethynil possesses antimetastatic as well as antiproliferative activities. The rationale for these studies is that impact of Icmt inhibition is not limited to Ras, but also extends to the Rho GTPase family that has been implicated in metastatic progression of particular cancers. We have preliminary data that cysmethynil treatment of certain cancer cells impact on cell adhesion and also invasion through Matrigel, two properties important in tumor metastasis. Hence, we will assess anti-metastatic efficacy of cysmethynil in experimental mouse models. In Aim 4, we will investigate the pharmacokinetics and ADME/Tox properties of cysmethynil. These studies will be done in collaboration with A/Professor Lee How Sung of NUS, with whom we have developed a LC/MS/MS method to measure cysmethynil and its metabolites in biological fluids. We will apply this methodology to the mouse models being developed.
kw: Prenylation, Metastasis, Carboxylmethylation

title: Retinal vasculature changes, large arterial stiffness and nocturnal blood pressure patterns: The associations and prognostic implications of three novel vascular risk factors in ischemic stroke patients.
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Stroke is a devastating and common disease. In the last decade, there has been little advancement in secondary prevention strategies for subsequent vascular events partly because stroke pathophysiology is poorly understood, particularly for patterns typical among Asians such as intracranial large artery disease. Retinal vasculature changes, arterial stiffening and nocturnal blood pressure patterns have recently been recognised as potential vascular risk factors for stroke development and stroke prognosis. The proposed research project is a new, prospective observational study of acute ischemic stroke patients. It aims to investigate the associations and prognostic implications of these novel risk factors (retinal vasculature changes, large artery stiffness and nocturnal blood pressure patterns). We hypothesize that retinal arterial narrowing/ venular widening, stiffening of large arteries and absence of normal nocturnal blood pressure dipping are correlated with each other, and with other stroke risk factors that are predominant in Asian stroke patients (e.g. metabolic syndrome, intracranial large artery disease). We further hypothesize that these novel risk factors will predict risk of subsequent vascular events. We will recruit 500 ischemic stroke patients in this study. Participants will have detailed clinical examinations. The retinal vasculature will be assessed from retinal photographs taken with a non-mydriatic digital camera. Arterial stiffness will be measured with carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and central pulse pressure using applanation tonometry methods. Ambulatory blood pressure will be monitored using the BPro system. We will ascertain the incidence of vascular events and mortality at 24 months from baseline via telephone contact and counter-checking with electronic hospital records. I and my collaborators and mentor have extensive experience in such studies and have successfully recruited Asian stroke patients in their studies, including assessment of retinal vasculature, arterial stiffness and blood pressure patterns. The collaborators include world-renown experts in retinal vasculature, arterial stiffness and blood pressure patterns. The proposed project will lead to better understanding of the pathophysiology of ischemic stroke, particularly the unique clinical patterns seen in Asians. The data obtained will provide evidence for the utility and prognostication of these vascular risk factors studied. They will also be the basis for future hypotheses generation for treatment trials.

title: Reorganized connection of the reuniens thalamic nucleus in mouse model of temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and a novel approach to long-term therapeutic effect on TLE after deletion of its neurons
abs: The existence of common connections between surviving neurons in the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex or amygdala and midline thalamus, in particular, reuniens thalamic nucleus (RE) in the mouse model of temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) in our preliminary study strongly suggests that RE may play some important roles in the occurrence of spontaneously recurrent seizures in TLE. We therefore propose that RE may act as a synchronizer in TLE. The main aims of the study are to (1) trace the reorganized connections between RE and multiple limbic sites such as the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex and amygdala in the mouse model of TLE and investigate its role in epileptogenesis; (2) localize the epileptogenic foci by inserting the electrical probes into the RE, subiculum of hippocampal formation, lateral entorhinal cortex and basal lateral amygdala by using EEG telemetry (sampling rates: 2000HZ) and video camera monitoring system; (3) evaluate long-term therapeutic effect by chemical deletion [local injection of ibotenic acid (0.5µg)] of neurons in RE using EEG telemetry and video camera monitoring system. This study will open a new area for better understanding of the mechanism of epileptogenesis, and for more effectively controlling TLE by surgical approach to destroy RE. Instead of a traditional way of study on limbic system, we try to prove that reuniens thalamic nucleus may act as a synchronizer in the thalamolimbic circuit to initiate and propagate the seizure in TLE. If it is true, we may provide evidence for designing new approach for treatment of TLE.

title: Corneal endothelium reconstruction with nano-structured thermo-sensitive polymeric substrate
abs: Damaged corneas due to corneal injuries and clinical disorders are one of the major causes of visual disabilities in the world as well as in Singapore. Because of the complications associated with allograft cornea transplantation, tissue-engineered substitutes would be desirable; however, no widely accepted substitute is currently available.The cornea is a highly organized tissue with distinct structures within each of the corneal epithelial, stromal and endothelial layers. The basement membranes in the cornea are condensed layers of extracellular matrix (ECM), consisting of an interwoven meshwork of fibers and pores of nanoscale dimensions. We hypothesize that nano-structured substrates can enhance cell-substratum interaction, and direct cell differentiation into cell types with appropriate cell functions for each layer. By combining technologies in nano-fabrication, thermo-sensitive polymers and cell-sheet engineering, we propose to reconstruct each of the corneal layers on thermo-sensitive substrates with uniquely designed nano-structures. While each layer can be transplanted individually for lamellar transplantation, a full-thickness cornea graft can also be generated using a layer-by-layer approach.In this exploratory proposal, we aim to verify our hypotheses by focusing on the endothelial layer. Nanopatterns will be fabricated on a thermo-sensitive chitosan and laminin-blended substrates by solvent casting to mimic the substratum topography of the Descemet’s membranes for the endothelium reconstruction.The effects of cell-nanotopography interaction on corneal endothelial cell behavior and cell-sheet formation will be investigated. In addition, endothelial cells from alternate sources, in particular venous endothelial cells and bone marrow derived stem cells, will also be investigated in this study. This proof-of-concept study can be applied to the other corneal layers to develop a layer-by-layer cornea reconstruction platform. Since layered structures are found in many native tissues, the integration of nanotechnology and temperature-sensitive polymer with a layer-by-layer approach can also be extended to other regenerative medicine applications.
kw: Cornea Tissue Engineering, Thermosensitive Polymer, Cornea Endothelium, Nanotopography, Nanofabrication, Cell-Substratum interaction

title: Nanoparticle-based detection technology for a cheap and rapid identification of specific gene mutations for clinical screening
abs: In this proposal, we aim to test a new strategy to identify and differentiate genetic mutations among possible mutation sites in a single assay using nanoparticle technology. This can lead to future development of fast and simple assays for diagnosis of genetic diseases such as thalassemia, G6PD deficiency, muscular dystrophy, cystic fibrosis, sickle cell anemia as well as certain cancers that are associated with common mutations in various genes. This proposed genetic detection strategy is both sensitive and specific, and can also be used to screen genetic variations including single nucleotide polymorphisms. Detection of these genetic variations have important clinical ramifications related to individual differences in drug metabolism and holding great promise in the design of personalized medicine. This is especially important for a country like Singapore, where various ethnic groups with diverse genetic background are collectively receiving very similar, if not the same, medical therapies, even though individuals have different requirements and responses to the therapies. The current genetic diagnostic tools are complicated, time consuming, and expensive. We thus propose a new nanoparticle-based detection assay to overcome the current shortfalls and improve the quality of the medical services. The proposed assay in this proof-of-principle proposal involves fabricating gold nanoparticles of different sizes, and conjugating single but different DNA probes to specific mutations. The presence of target mutations/genetic variations triggers two nanoparticles assembling together to form a dimer. The dimer can then be easily identified via gel electrophoresis. Since the size of nanoparticles control their electrophoretic mobility, and each size of nanoparticles is conjugated with different DNA probes, the position of the dimer can be used to differentiate the presence of different genetic mutations/variations. This assay requires simple instrumentation like gel electrophoresis, making it more affordable, and can benefit even other ASEAN communities whose healthcare systems have limited budget.
kw: Gold nanoparticles, SNP detection, Clinical diagnostics, Point mutations screening, Nanoparticle assembly, Personalized medicine

title: Profiling and Identification of PTEN interacting protein by quantitative Mass Spectrometry to find prognosis makers and therapeutic targets.
abs: Mutation of the PTEN (phosphatase and tensin homologue) tumor suppressor protein frequently occurs in a variety of human cancers. PTEN is a phosphatase that negatively regulates the phosphatidyl-inositol-3-kinase (PI3K) pathway, and regulates cell proliferation, apoptosis, and cell motility. At the plasma and intracellular membranes, PI3K generates PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 and PTEN degrades PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 into PtdIns(4,5)P2. Thus, a high percentage of human cancers exhibit hyperactive PI3K signaling with loss of PTEN expression. Interestingly, wild-type PTEN localizes to both the cytoplasm and the nucleus. Up to recently, we believed that suppression of PI3K activity in cytoplasm is necessary and sufficient to PTEN’s tumor suppressor function. In addition to the cytoplasmic function, recent findings revealed that nuclear PTEN is critical for tumor suppression. The loss of nuclear PTEN correlates with poor prognosis, indicating nuclear PTEN’s importance. However, some PTEN mutants from patients predominantly localize to the nucleus and possess lipid phosphatase activity, but fail to suppress transformation, indicating that these PTEN mutants lack tumor suppressor function in the nucleus. The aim of this proposal is to understand the regulatory mechanisms of PTEN function through identification of its interacting proteins. We will define the proteins that physically interact with PTEN using cytoplasmic and nuclear fraction from the cells expressing PTEN wild type and cancer-associated mutants. To this end, we will: 1) identify proteins interacting with wild-type PTEN as well as cancer-associated and nuclear-localizing PTEN mutants in subcellular fractions, 2) establish data profile of subfractionalted PTEN interacting protein by quantitative mass spectrometry. The ultimate goal is to decipher the mechanisms of PTEN-mediated tumor suppression and to use this information to develop useful prognosis makers and therapeutic targets.
kw: PTEN, Tumorigenesis, Therapeutic target, Tumor suppressor, Prognosis markers, Proteomics

title: Identification and characterization of hypoxia-regulatory microRNAs (HRMs) and their target mRNAs in human hepatocellular carcinoma cells
abs: Hypoxia is suggested to be associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a hypervascular tumor. Our preliminary data showed that expression of 977 and 1006 genes were up- and down-regulated, respectively, in at least two HCC cell lines under hypoxic conditions using Affymetrix Genechip analysis.The identification of genes that are specifically induced by hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) has dominated hypoxia research. However, the mechanisms of gene repression by hypoxia, as well as gene regulation through HIF-independent pathways are still poorly defined. In view of the discovery of microRNAs, a newclass of small non-coding RNAs that negatively regulates gene expression by targeting mRNA transcripts for degradation or translational suppression, we propose that altered expression of microRNAs may be indirectly involved in gene modulation under hypoxic conditions. This study therefore aim to determinethe role of microRNAs in modulating gene expression under hypoxic conditions in HCC cells. First, we will employ microarray-based expression profiling to identify microRNAs that are differentially expressed in HCC cells under hypoxic conditions. Real time RT-PCR based TaqMan microRNA assays will be performed to confirm the altered expression of these known and putative novel hypoxia-regulatorymicroRNAs (HRMs). Putative target mRNAs of these HRMs will be identified based on published prediction algorithms, and compared against the differentially expressed genes in hypoxia-treated HCC cells derived from our existing Affymetrix database. The cross reference with the existing Affymetrix database enable us to verify and expand target mRNAs of known HRMs, as well as suggest new targetmRNAs of novel HRMs. Functional validation will be performed by transfecting HCC cells with synthesized microRNAs or anti-sense microRNAs and monitoring the expression of target mRNAs. Our proposed work will allow us to gain a better understanding of the gene regulatory function of microRNAsunder hypoxia conditions during hepatocarcinogenesis.

title: Exploration of the role of NG2 cells in immunity of the central nervous system
abs: Chondroitin sulphate proteoglycan (NG2) is expressed in a high proportion of glial cells in the adult central nervoussystem (CNS). It has been found that NG2 cells have some direct connections with neurons, can sense alteration inneurons and their microenvironment, become active in response to some cytokine stimulations or under pathologicalconditions, and even generate action potentials. However, the exact function of NG2 cells is still unknown (Commentfrom Nature Neurosciences, March 2008) [49].In our preliminary study, we have observed that the NG2 cells could respond directly to axonal alteration at theearlier stage of neurodegeneration and at that time there was no obvious microglial or astrocytic reaction. But at laterstage of neurodegeneration, inflammatory responses including microglial activation and neuronal cell loss graduallybecome obvious. We have also observed that the sign of inhibition in NG2 cells after specific blockage of microglialcomplement receptor type 3 in our focal-injury-inflammation model. NG2 cells are therefore assumed to contributedirectly to the immunity of the CNS or indirectly to facilitate the function of brain immune cells during variousneuropathologies.Owing to current lack of knowledge about the function of NG2 cells, the main goal of this proposed project is toprimarily characterize NG2 cell functions in the following aspects of brain innate immunity:a). Cell products: Cytokines and chemokines are extracellular signaling-proteins necessary for cell-cellcommunications and their signaling plays important roles in both health and disease states. Cytokines andchemokines released from NG2 cells and expressions of cytokine- and chemokine-receptors in NG2 cells will beinvestigated.b). Expression of cell surface integrins: Integrins are receptors with important roles in mediating certain cell-celladhesion, making transmembrane connections to cytoskeleton, and activating many intracellular signaling pathways.As integrins and their ligands play key roles in immune responses, expression of integrins in NG2 cells will bestudied.c). Expression of complement receptors: The complement system plays important role in innate defence system andparticipates in various immunoregulatory processes. As very important complement regulatory proteins, theexpression of complement receptors will be investigated in the NG2 cells.d). Phagocytotic and pinocytotic functions of NG2 cells: As some NG2 cells sharing microglial/macrophage marker,the study of NG2 cell ability in phagocytosis and pinocytosis will reveal if NG2 cells possess the ability to captureantigens, which may imply the direct involvement of NG2 cells in the CNS innate immunity.This study would allow us to develop further IRG proposals to derive a deeper understanding of immunity in the CNSand utilize NG2 cellular immunity as an important adjuvant therapy for neuroinflammatory, neurooncological orneurodegenerative di

title: Multicellular Angiogenic Spheroids to Improve Engraftment of Stem Cells and Bioartificial Tissue for Myocardial Restoration
abs: Background and hypothesis:With the advent of tissue engineering functional bioartificial tissues can be manufactured to replace diseased native ones. Thus far a major obstacle has been the inability to maintain thick viable tissues both in vitro and in vivo, due to the lack of a functional vascular network within them.In order to incorporate angiogenic networks, some authors have explored the generation of vascularized multicellular micro- and macrotissues using gravity-enforced techniques. So far this tissue engineering method has been used in a scaffoldless setting, not aiming myocardial restoration. We hypothesize that 3-dimensional solid and liquid bioartificial tissues for myocardial restoration will have a superior viability, angiogenic and restorative potential when supplemented with 3-dimensional spheroids containing stem cells and endothelial cells. Hence, the implantable graft will contain its own angiogenic load.In this proposal, we plan to generate bioartificial tissues enriched with three-dimensional pre-vascularized spheroids which will promote angiogenesis and prevent adverse remodeling following implantation for myocardial restoration. Aims and Methodology:Our first aim is to generate three-dimensional spheroids of Cord Lining Mesechymal Stem Cells in vitro, coated with endothelial cells. In our second aim we intend to fabricate 3-dimensional bioartificial tissues containing such spheroids using a bioreactor and a nanoporous matrix. Our third aim is to generate a liquid collagenous compound for myocardial injection, containing the restorative spheroids. Finally, our fourth aim will be to implant the vacularized 3-dimensional bioartificial tissues through open heart surgery for the solid grafts, as well as endoscopically for the liquid compound containing three-dimensional vascularized spheroids into the area of injury.Significance:The proposed project with its novel concept may be of great value for stem cell- and tissue engineering-based treatment of heart disease. For the first time in Myocardial Restoration research viability support, structural support, and revascularization are addressed in the same setting.

title: Developing a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus-specific Health-Related Quality of Life Item Bank for use among Multi-Ethnic Asian Patients
abs: Background: Health-related Quality of Life (HRQoL) measures assess the impact of illnesses on the physical, mental, and social well-being of individuals and are increasingly used in clinical research and practice. Item banking (IB) and computerized adaptive testing (CAT) represent the future of HRQoL assessment, with their importance reflected by NIH’s funding of a major research program todevelop IB and CAT for several clinical areas. Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a multi-system autoimmune disease of a waxing and waning nature associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Hence, experts recommend that HRQoL be assessed in all SLE clinical trials. An SLEspecific IB, which allows short-form measures and CAT to be developed, would have several advantages over static measures that are currently employed, including improved precision and reduced respondent burden.Aims: 1. To identify HRQoL domains regarded as important by multi-ethnic Asian patients with SLE.2. To perform item calibration and tests of model fit.Methods: A general framework on HRQoL issues in SLE will be constructed via literature review.Using this framework, focus group discussions would be conducted among 90 English-speaking Chinese, Malay and Indian SLE patients. Subsequently, one-to-one interviews among 120 SLE patients will be conducted to calibrate the items and test model fit.Clinical /Academic Significance: SLE is a very important disease in Singapore as its clinical manifestations are more severe in Asians compared to Caucasians. To the best of our knowledge, this will be the first SLE-specific HRQoL IB worldwide. This study would lay the foundation for future larger studies to develop SLE and other disease-specific CAT to vastly improve HRQoL measurement, thus improving clinical care and reducing sample size requirements for clinical trials.Singapore is suited to take the lead in developing such an IB given the ready availability of SLE patients, and the strong background in HRQoL research of the study team.

title: Development of molecular Gleason grading of prostate cancer using DNA methylation signature
abs: Gleason grading is an established pathologic technique of ascertaining tumour differentiation and aggressiveness in prostate cancer1. However, the grading system, established in 1974 when most prostate cancers presented at an advanced stage, lacks precision in differentiating early stage prostate cancers. Hypermethylation-induced gene silencing is known to occur via different CpG loci at promoter sites in prostate cancer. Our working hypothesis is that there are unique global gene methylation signatures that are specific for different phases of prostate cancer development and different prostate cancer phenotypes and may thus differentiate cancers from non-cancers, and aggressive cancers from indolent ones. Our aims of this study are to profile the gene methylation patterns in prostate cancers of different Gleason grades, prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia and benign prostatic hyperplasia. Previous studies were able to analyse only a small number of genes due to lack of suitable experimental screening tools. We will use high-throughput DNA methylation assay techniques and combined bioinformatics and wet-lab approaches using quantitative methylation-specific PCR to identifyphenotype-specific gene methylation signatures and novel methylated genes. To assess the silencing effect of the promoter hypermethylation, gene expression profile will also be generated. Our findings will be applied in subsequent studies on a larger group of patients with clinical follow-up data to validate the utility of the methylation signature in outcome prognostication. This will also pave the way for its use in prediction of response to adjuvant chemotherapy for patients with advanced disease. Subsequent mechanistic studies would provide further insights into the epigenetic pathways for carcinogenesis and highlight potential therapeutic targets.

title: Role of mesenchymal stem cells in microenvironmental system of glioma tumor angiogenesis
abs: AimsTumor microenvironment plays a crucial role in cancer progression and metastasis. Tumor tropism of stem cells has been exploited for delivering therapeutic genes for anti-cancer therapy. However, the exact contribution of stem cells in tumor growth remains poorly defined. In our preliminary study, we found that the presence of human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in the glioma microenvironment significantly enhance the expression of angiogenic markers such as von Willebrand factor (vWF) in the intracranial glioma region. This phenomenon is accompanied with concomitant increase expression of interleukin 6 (IL6), which are absent in the glioma alone and those co-injected with normal human astrocytes. Furthermore, mice bearing co-culture of MSCs/glioma have a shorter survival in comparison to glioma co-cultured with normal human astrocytes. In the present study, the role of MSCs on glioma neoangiogenesis will be investigated. Specifically, we propose to (1) determine whether interaction between MSCs and glioma will increase the tumor microvasculature through the recruitment of endothelial progenitor cells (EPC), (2) to verify if interleukin 6 (IL6) plays a role in the recruitment of EPC.HypothesesCrosstalk between MSCs and glioma cells enhance tumor angiogenesis through the recruitment of endothelial progenitor cells into the tumor microenvironment. MethodologyThe co-culture of MSCs and glioma tumor section will be analyzed for expression and localization of various angiogenic markers. In vitro angiogenesis assay using fibrin gel matrix will be employed to assess the neovessels sprouting in MSCs/glioma tissue sections. In addition, EPC will be isolated from Tie2-GFP mice to determine whether EPC are recruited to the MSCs/glioma regions. Furthermore, to determine if IL6 plays a role in the recruitment of EPC, siRNA against IL6 will be designed and tested. Approach of the research proposal including its importance to science or medicine in particular clinical significanceThe prospect of using MSCs for tumor therapy is enormous. Our proposal aims to understand whether MSCs/glioma interaction signals predispose glioma to growth and invasion through the augmentation of angiogenesis. The results obtained from this project will advance our understanding of tumor biology, and the feasibly of using MSCs as carrier for cell/gene therapy, thus enable us to design better strategies for tumor targeted therapy.
kw: Mesenchymal stem cells, Tumor, Endothelial progenitor cells, angiogenesis

title: Molecular approach to validate the prognosis of clinically stable young stroke patients
abs: Stroke is a global problem with heterogenous aetiologies. While many traditional risk factors for strokehave been described for patients with cerebral ischemia, up to 40% of patients do not have anyknown risk factors, particularly in those below 40 years of age. Extensive basic research hasidentified important pathways involved in the pathogenesis of stroke, primarily excitotoxicity and ionimbalance, oxidative stress and cell death. Recent discovery of microRNAs has opened up a newopportunity to examine the molecular events that are taking place in stroke patients as well to predictand develop novel therapeutic agents against stroke. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small (19–23nucleotides) non-coding RNAs that control the expression of genes at transcriptional or translationallevel. Importantly, individual miRNA can regulate multiple genes in a given cell, either by targetingmRNA for degradation, inhibition of translation or activation of transcription. Their importance inregulating the overall transcriptome and proteome under physiological and pathophysiologicalconditions is therefore useful in the assessment of the outcome of stroke and its subsequentmanagement in the clinics. Blood is obtainable without any major invasive procedures and hasrecently been shown to contain most of the microRNAs that could indicate the physiological status ofan individual/brain (see Jeyaseelan et al 2008 and our preliminary studies). Hence in this study wepropose to carryout miRNA typing/profiling from blood samples obtained from different subtypes ofstroke in young (<50years old) stroke patients who are currently being monitored as outpatients. Aftercompleting this short term exploratory project we will also be in a position to apply for an IRG projecton the mechanism of actions of specific microRNAs and their possible use as biomarkers andtherapeutic targets as there are no effective drugs except tPA available currently for treating strokepatients.

title: Development of an Ablation and Division Device with blood- flow sensor feature.
abs: AimsTo develop a single laparoscopic liver resection device that combines technology of Radiofrequency Ablation (RFA), a tissue cutting mechanism and blood- flow sensor.HypothesisThe new device is as safe as traditional devices, and can reduce blood loss and duration of operation.MethodologyCombining expertise from National University of Singapore’s School of Engineering and National University Hospital’s Department of Surgery, the novel device will be developed. Tests will be done on porcine models to test the efficacy of the device compared with CUSA.Importance to medicineLiver resection remains the most effective mode for liver tumour treatment. However, bleeding is a significant problem. One solution to this problem is RFA- assisted laparoscopic liver resections. Studies have shown that this method result in lesser blood loss during operation [1]. In RFA- assisted laparoscopic liver resection, the liver parenchymal is first coagulated with RFA. The surgeon then cuts within the coagulated tissue to divide the liver. This alternating coagulation and cutting step is continued till the line of transaction is completed to finally divide the liver. The problem with this method is that the surgeon does not know for certain which parts of the liver are still vascular. To prevent cutting too deep resulting in bleeding, they might cut too little and waste time coagulating a coagulated part of the liver again. Thus, there is a need for a device that can coagulate and cut the liver simultaneously, and at the same time detect the presence of blood- flow to confirm avascularity. This eliminates the risk of bleeding due to cutting too deep, as well as time loss due to re- coagulation of coagulated areas.

title: Phase Coherent Charge and Spin Transport in Nanostrutcured Graphene and Ferromagnet Hybrid Devices
abs: Nanoscale electronics and spin-electronics offer great opportunities that reach far beyond the current state-of-the-art silicon-based CMOS device technology. At the frontiers of nano-electronics and nano-spintronics are quantum transport phenomena in low-dimensional systems. The exploration of the quantum realm is rapidly leading to non-conventional device concepts, which eventually will outperform devices that are based on semi-classical electronics. Recent advances in device fabrication based on nanostructured systems and novel material platforms have provided us with vast opportunities, which are not merely limited to overcoming the fundamental limits to device miniaturization; they offer far more. Reducing the dimensions and dimensionality of material system reveal new phenomena and thus, from an application point of view provide us with new operating principles and systems with strongly enhanced functionalities. Here I propose the exploration and merger of two recent key developments in mesoscopic physics relevant for nano-electronics and nano-spintronics. These are graphene, a recently discovered 2 dimensional (2D) crystal, and spin transfer torque, a novel way of manipulating nanomagnets.

title: Biodegradable Cardiovascular Implants
abs: This proposal is driven by genuine unmet medical needs as defined by leading practioners from Singapore and abroad. We have selected 3 specific devices to focus our research on: (a) Biodegradable Stents for localized delivery of drug, genes and peptides, (b) a Bidogradable Occluder for atrial septal defect/ patent foramen ovale; and (c) a Cardiac "Pouch" for repairing damaged cardiovascular tissue. Enabling these devices will be research into a new class of biodegradable materials, the elastomeric biomaterial, as well as surface functionalization of existing biodegradable polymers. Both the new biomaterial as well as the surface-functionalized biomaterial will be evaluated for cellular interactions. The mechanisms of smooth muscle cell and endothelial cell attachment and proliferation on these polymers will be studied in vitro and confirmed in vivo; this understanding will help select for optimum surface modification. In addition, drug/peptide/therapeutic gene release from these same polymers will be evaluated; subsequently, the effects of these released bioactives on cells in vitro and on animal tissue will be studied. Data thus generated may be iterated for optimal performance of prototypes. Arising out of this work, several (~12) patents are anticipated, based on prototype design, composition of matter (formulation) and application-specific. Successful animal trials can have two outcomes: one is to proceed to human trials (which are not part of this proposal) and the other is to spin the technology off into companies which will then proceed to human trials. Similar multi-disciplinary programmes (from concept to clinical) are underway in a few locations world-wide, but we believe this is the first of its kind in Singapore. The PI and co-PI have demonstrated a level of success in this type of endeavour, as evidenced by the formation of 4 start-up companies here, one of which has attracted US VC funding.

title: Towards Manufacturability of Carbon Nanotube-based Printed Electronics
abs: Printing enables electronics products to be made over large area, on flexible substrate and with low cost, all not feasible with Si microelectronics. Organic semiconducting polymers are the current dominant semiconductor materials used in printed electronics but have low mobility (about 1 cm2/Vs) and stability. Present and emerging demand for higher performance printed electronics has inspired a worldwide effort to develop alternative printable semiconductor. Semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (sem-SWNTs) can have carrier mobility far exceeding (up to 20,000 cm2/Vs) that of polymers. SWNTs are also easily printable and have excellent mechanical, chemical and thermal stabilities and unique optical properties. However, current SWNT-based field effect transistors (FETs) have poor reproducibility because current synthesis results in mixtures of semiconducting and metallic (met-) nanotubes. Network, rather than individual, SWNTs improves device reproducibility due to statistical averaging. However, current SWNT network (SWNTnet) devices typically have poor yield and either high mobilities but low on/off ratio or vice-versa. The main problems are contaminating met-SWNTs and random orientation of the electrically anisotropic nanotubes. The objective of this research programme is to develop printed aligned SWNTnet-FETs with high mobility (> 100 cm2/V), on/off ratio (> 10**5) and yield (>60%) and demonstrate their use in high-performance logic circuits and a prototype device. Firstly, we will synthesize SWNTs with controllable chirality, and thus electronic properties, through novel catalysis procedures. Secondly, we will further enrich/purify specific nanotube chiralities using our novel dispersants and chromatographic separation. Thirdly, we will apply our present state-of-the-art fluidic and printing techniques and develop some new methods, including rubber anisotropic pattern compression and magnetic patterning of aligned SWNTs, to reproducibly assemble the purified sem-SWNTs into highly aligned SWNTnet patterns (with channel length tunable from 100nm to micron scales). Fourthly, we shall demonstrate superior printed SWNTnet-based logic circuits and diodes and a proof-of-concept display driver circuit.

title: Genome-Wide RNAi screen identification for combinational therapy of brain tumors with inhibitors of PI3 and Receptor tyrosine kinases
abs: The median overall survival for high-grade glioma is still limited, such as 12-15 months for glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). The standard of care for GBM, which is a treatment of concomitant adjuvant radiotherapy and temozolomide, offer a survival advantage over older chemotherapies, but the improvement is modest. High percentage of GBM and some solid tumors shows robust Akt’s activation with loss of tumor suppressor PTEN or amplification/mutation of EGFR and receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), indicating the importance of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway in gliomagenesis. Thus, inhibitions of RTKs and the downstream PI3K signaling pathway have shown promising target pathway for anticancer therapies. However, efficacy of their inhibitors in GBM and other solid tumors has been very little. We hypothesized that multiple signaling pathways are co-activated with RTKs activation in these tumors and that the inputs drive and maintain downstream signaling, thereby limiting the efficacy of therapies targeting single RTKs and PI3K. Inhibition of multiple signaling pathways is able to enhance the efficiency of the anti-proliferating ability in comparison to single treatment of each inhibitor. Recently, the combining chemotherapies have significantly improved clinical outcomes for various solid tumors, but the impacts are limited in its usefulness for specific types of cancers even in advanced stages. Moreover, there is no systematic and mechanism-based ways to find the combination of drugs. With the development of RNAi library, systematic and cost-effective genome-wide loss of function screen can be performed with the rapid identification of novel drug targets. We will perform synthetic lethal screen by RNAi library under treatment of inhibitors of PI3K and RTKs with the aim of finding novel combinations for the chemotherapy of GBM. We will find therapeutic targets for the drug screen from this research. Our ultimate goal is to establish the novel combination of chemotherapy for brain tumor.

title: Conditional ligands for class I MHC products; application to epitope discovery for Dengue and respiratory syncytial virus-specific CD8+ T-cells.
abs: Infection with Dengue virus (DV) or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) produces a spectrum of clinical illnesses and presents with significant morbidity. Vaccine development for these viruses primarily concentrates on stimulating humoral immune responses. Complete and long-lasting coverage is a vaccine prerequisite, however, to prevent antibody-dependent enhancement and exacerbation of the disease. The inclusion of immunogenic epitopes that elicit cellular immune responses could provide an additional layer of protection to vaccines. Traditional epitope discovery tools frequently rely on expansion of antigen-specific T-cell populations and probe only the cytotoxic capability of these cultured T-cells. As an alternative, class I MHC tetramer technology allows direct phenotypic identification of CD8+ T-cell populations from infected patients, but the production of such tetramers remains an arduous affair. A novel peptide exchange strategy, which employs class I MHC products loaded with conditional ligands, provides a fast and straightforward method to obtain arrays of class I MHC tetramers of diverse specificity, and facilitates CD8+ T-cell epitope discovery. Because CD8+ T-cell recognition is MHC-restricted, class I HLA polymorphisms need to be taken into account. For HLA products associated with Asian ancestry, well-defined epitopes are scarce. Therefore, I shall prepare, by solid phase peptide synthesis, conditional ligands with which tetramers can be constructed for common Asian class I HLA variants. The functional integrity of these reagents, after peptide exchange, will be validated. Concurrently, epitope libraries covering the DV and RSV proteomes will be assembled, and possible epitopes will be ranked by likelihood of producing a CD8+ T-cell response, based on bioinformatic approaches. From these epitope libraries, arrays of class I HLA tetramers will be generated to screen for antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations in response to DV and RSV infection in Asian populations. Newly identified epitopes should be considered candidates for vaccine development.

title: Aqueous [2 + 2 + 2] Cyclotrimerization of Alkynes As a More Versatile Click Reaction
abs: The transition metal-catalyzed alkyne [2 + 2 + 2] cyclotrimerization reaction is an excellent transformation that generates a benzene derivative. Because aromatic rings are central to many biological, pharmaceutical, and polymer molecules, alkyne cyclotrimerization is an important methodology. However, the utilization of this reaction is rather limited to synthetic organic chemistry area. The goal of the proposed chemistry is to make the cyclotrimerization reaction as versatile as a “Click” reaction. The specific aims are to (1) identify versatile Co(I) catalysts which are soluble in both organic and aqueous media, (2) allow catalysis under mild conditions, and (3) apply these discoveries to the modification of surface to demonstrate powerful potential applications of the proposed catalyst system. For these purposes, poly(ethylene glycol) supported Cp ligand based Co(I) complexes are proposed as versatile homogeneous catalysts for aqueous and organic alkyne cyclotrimerization reactions. These catalysts will allow catalysis in both organic and aqueous media under mild conditions. The activity of the proposed Co(I) complexes will be screened in pure water, more challenging media of current cyclotrimerization. Once the active catalyst system is identified, further applications on surface modification or bioconjugation chemistry will be pursued to demonstrate the versatile utility of this reaction. The proposed research will enable the powerful alkyne-cyclotrimerization reaction – modular, wide in scope, high yielding, generating ideally no byproduct, and highly thermodynamically driven – to maximize their potential application toward biological applications and materials science beyond it’s major focus on synthetic organic chemistry.

title: Theory and Practice of Coding and Cryptography
abs: The programme consists of two major subprogrammes: Coding Theory and Cryptography, divided into 7 interwoven projects. The programme on coding focuses on the following: - Construction of new block codes with good parameters and their encoding/decoding, construction of optimal constant-weight and constant-composition codes, deletion/insertion-correcting codes, and new applications of block codes in computer-aided design of VLSI circuits, nanotechnology, etc. Tools from mathematics and computer science will be employed. New knowledge created could improve fundamental understanding in coding, have widespread implications in communications and DNA computing, as well as pioneer new applications of coding theory. - Development of direct and systematic approaches to construct good quantum error-correcting codes, investigation of asymptotic behaviour of quantum codes, and characterizations of quantum codes, exploiting tools from algebra, geometry, combinatorics, computer science, etc, and leveraging on the team's unique expertise in coding theory. Quantum error correction is essential for quantum information processing, which may have potential for revolutionary advances over classical paradigms. - Constructions of unitary space-time codes and wireless network codes, using sophisticated mathematical and optimization tools that have not been considered previously. Space-time codes are used for multiple-antenna wireless communication, which promises very high data rates, and hold promises in wireless networks. The programme on cryptography focuses on the following: - Theoretical lower bounds on computational complexity of breaking modern public key cryptosystems; (2) Develop lattice techniques in public key cryptography; (3) Design new coding-related public key cryptosystems; (4) Construct and evaluate pseudorandom number generators. The approach will combine number theory, algebra and discrete mathematics. - Development of practical and provably secure private key primitives, which are fast enough to offer much more trustable alternatives to heuristically secure designs, investigation into the designs criteria for private key primitives immune against attacks, and cryptanalysis of stream cipher primitives. This will be done through a combination of techniques from algebra, discrete mathematics, complexity theory and cryptanalysis. - Analysis of existing designated hash functions that have resisted attacks to date, and design of fast and provably secure hash functions based on intractable problems, through the application of sophisticated techniques from areas such as coding theory, lattices and combinatorics. It is generally believed that there is an urgent need to re-evaluate existing techniques and theories in hash functions, as well as to develop new secure ones. - Development of new theories, techniques and tools in applications of secure multiparty computation for a wide range of computation domains, and design of practical secure MPC protocols with

title: Biologically-inspired Design, Nano-fabrication and Nano-lubrication of MEMS, NEMS and Micro-mechanical Devices
abs: Tribological problems are abundant in MEMS (Micro-electromechanical systems) and NEMS (Nano-electromechanical systems) devices (MNDs), especially in those that operate at high-speeds and at intermittent start-stop conditions. Complete solutions have not been found but current technology is able to provide customized solutions for individual devices that operate in dry, controlled conditions, often at the expense of performance. To improve their reliability, effective generic solutions must be found to address problems such as wear and energy loss, arising from stiction and dry friction, and from high viscous drag in semi- and fully-immersed liquid environments. Nature provides numerous examples of mechanical and surface designs that are successful in solving the problems of stiction and friction imposed by the environment. These include super-hydrophobic lotus leaves, nano-textured insect cuticle and fish skin, self-lubricating human skin and articular cartilage. The ability to fully utilize these designs will empower us to solve a wide range of existing and possibly future tribological problems in any scale. Adapting biomimetic surfaces will facilitate a new generation of MNDs with characteristics and capabilities not demonstrated with existing tribological surfaces. This lies in the fact that biological surfaces are less rigid than conventional MND surfaces and they are self-lubricating. They also display unique microscopic features that function to actively change the surface properties depending on environmental conditions. Once set in place within the MND, the surface properties of existing MND surfaces cannot be modified freely. Thus, this proposed research aims to conduct systematic research to find ways of lubrication to enhance the wear durability and life-cycle of MNDs, by engineering biologically-inspired and other tribological surfaces for applications in these devices. Major work to be conducted in this programme will be the development of new techniques to mimic, engineer and study suitable biological surfaces, and the development of biomimetic-enabled MNDs.

title: Expression of immune signalling molecules by muscle fibres as predictors of disease expression, response to treatment and prognosis in inflammatory myoapathy
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: The idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs), which comprise of dermatomyositis, polymyositis and inclusion body myositis, are a heterogeneous group of acquired, immune mediated, skeletal muscle diseases. Although muscular weakness and inflammation are common features, each has distinct clinical and histological as well as pathogenetical characteristics. Various immune signaling molecules not normally expressed by muscle fibre, including the MHC antigens, co-stimulatory molecules, cytokine signaling molecules, chemokines and metalloproteinases, have all been reported to occur in IIM. While their expression has been implicated in pathogenetic mechanisms of IIM, their clinical significance has not been examined in depth.Our routine use of MHC class I antigen immunostaining of IIM muscle biopsy specimens in the clinical diagnostic laboratory have shown different staining patterns. We postulate that the differential expression of MHC Class 1 antigen and other immune signaling molecules mentioned above will have predictive value in terms of disease phenotype as well as response to treatment and prognosis. We plan to study 50 muscle biopsy specimens from patients who meet diagnostic criteria of IIM endorsed by the European Neuromuscular Centre. Muscle specimens will be cryosectioned and immunohistochemically stained with antibodies to a panel of immune signalling molecules to determine their expression by muscle fibres. This expression will then be correlated with clinical presentation, functional impairment, and use of immunosuppression and treatment outcome.This information obtained will not only be very useful to clinicians in managing IIM but may also provide insight into possible therapeutic targets.

title: Immunotherapy of Multiple Myeloma by CD137
abs: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a tumor of B cells and the second most frequent hematological malignancy. Epidemiological data show an increasing incidence and a decreasing age of onset. No cure exists for MM and treatments such as chemotherapy are intended to improve quality of life and to prolong life. However, the average life expectancy after MM diagnosis is only three to five years.CD137 and its ligand are members of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor and TNF superfamiles, respectively, and potent immunoregulatory proteins. CD137 costimulates B cells and enhances proliferation and immunoglobulin synthesis of healthy B cells. However, in MM cells CD137 has the opposite effect and inhibits proliferation and induces cell death. This selective inhibition and killing of MM cells by CD137 while sparing healthy cells may offer a unique opportunity for the therapy of MM.In this project we aim to: - confirm the inhibitory effects of CD137 on multiple myeloma cells on larger sample numbers and most importantly on malignant cells from MM patients. - characterize expression of CD137 and CD137 ligand in MM.- assess the therapeutic potential of CD137 for multiple myeloma in vitro and in vivo in murine MM models.
kw: Multiple Myeloma, Immunotherapy, CD137, apoptosis

title: Family-based genome-wide association study of early-onset myopia
abs: Specific aims: We propose to perform Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS) of 500 families with Chinese children with early onset myopia recruited in the population-based STARS study (STrabismus, Amblyopia and Refractive errors in preschool Singapore Chinese children) to determine associated genes for early-onset myopia. Hypothesis: Myopia develops at a very early age in Singapore Chinese children and the subsequent progression to high myopia may be associated with retinal and other potentially blinding ocular complications. Family-based association studies with GWAS analyses may facilitate the search for the gene for early-onset myopia in Singapore Chinese children. Methods: Saliva tissue samples will be collected for DNA extraction in 500 Chinese family units (at least a trio of 2 parents and 1 child) with at least 1 affected myopic child or sibling participating in the STARS study, an on-going population-based study with comprehensive ocular and refractive assessments of very young children. We expect 400 parent-offspring trios and 100 families of 4 or more and the families will be examined either one of two clinic sites or at the homes. GWAS single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping for each family unit using the Illumina Humanhap 550 BeadChip will be performed. The GWAS data will be analyzed using family-based association methods (e.g. Transmission Disequilibrium Test (TDT) and Pedigree Disequilibrium Test (PDT)) on both qualitative (myopia versus no myopia) and quantitative (spherical equivalent, axial length) traits. Both Bonferonni correction and False discovery rate will be applied to correct for multiple testing. Two intervals of interest and top 20 sporadic SNPs identified will be followed up by high density SNP association mapping using the Illumina GoldenGate 1536 SNP custom array, Taqman genotyping or direct sequencing. MDR-Phenomics models and Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) will be applied to our dataset to evaluate gene-environment interactions. Significance: The onset of myopia at a very young age poses a significant burden because of the high probability of developing pathologic myopia in adulthood. This proposed family-based GWAS will identify genes or genetic loci for early-onset myopia in a population with one of the highest rates of myopia in the world.

title: Asymmetric Catalytic [4+1] Cycloadditions between Dienes and Carbene Precursors
abs: The proposal will be divided into two parts. (1) Rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric [4+1] cycloadditions. Homoleptic and heteroleptic rhodium complexes of chiral guanidinates will be prepared and used as catalysts in the cyclization between stabilized diazo compounds and electron-neutral and electron–rich 1,3-dienes. The method will be applied to the synthesis of Abacavir and aristeromycin. (2) Nickel-catalyzed asymmetric [4+1] cycloadditions. A new type of chiral N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands will be synthesized with chiral centers fused on N-aryl groups. Their nickel complexes will be used to catalyze asymmetric cycloadditions of electron-neutral and electron–poor 1,3-dienes. Alkylcarbenes precursors will be specifically targeted as cyclization partners. For mechanistic investigations, the NHC-ligated nickellacarbene intermediates will be synthesized. The new catalytic reaction will provide a shortcut to the synthesis of nucleotide analogs, such as anti-HIV drugs abacavir and carbovir.
