Success in the research proposed should have far reaching ramifications as the specificity of the receptor can be readily changed by replacing the anti-CD19 portion with another directed against other tumor antigens.
kw: Leukemia and Lymphoma, Gene Delivery Methods, Cell Therapy, NK and CIK cells

title: A genetic epidemiological investigation of a novel variant in the Serum Amyloid A1 gene and its role in coronary artery disease
abs: BackgroundAtherosclerosis is now recognized as a chronic inflammatory disorder that leads to CAD. SAA is known to play a direct role in atherosclerosis although the underlying mechanism remains unclear. HypothesesWe hypothesize that:1.Besides the novel variant that we had identified in the SAA gene from our preliminary study, there are functionally important ones that are yet undiscovered and which are associated with CAD risk.2.Since SAA is intimately related to CAD, its allele frequencies would be significantly different between CAD cases and controls.3.The close interaction between SAA and HDL suggests that SAA polymorphisms are expected to influence circulating SAA and lipid levels.4.Some SAA polymorphisms confer functional effects.5.Based on our preliminary data, SAA affects cholesterol efflux in endothelial cells due to its suppressive effect on the ABCA1 transporter molecule.AimsTo1.Screen and genotype the Singaporean Chinese population for novel and known SAA polymorphisms.2.Determine differences in SAA allele frequencies between CAD cases and controls.3.Evaluate the impact of SAA polymorphisms on circulating SAA and lipid levels.4.Conduct in-vitro functional characterization of the polymorphisms to elucidate their working mechanisms. 5.Investigate mechanisms underlying the effects of in-vitro SAA exposure on endothelial lipid homeostasis, especially its effect on ABCA1.MethodologyAim 1 will be accomplished by DHPLC mutation screening and melt-curve technology for genotyping. Aims 2 and 3 can be fulfilled by statistical and genetic epidemiological analyses. Aims 4 and 5 will be investigated in vitro using commercial human endothelial cell lines.SignificanceDespite its important role in CAD, SAA is a relatively neglected acute-phase protein compared to C-reactive protein,. Thus, its genetic epidemiology and functional characterization are two fertile grounds for investigation and might lead to SAA being a potential drug target for treatment of CAD.Coronary artery disease: CADSerum amyloid A: SAAATP-binding cassette A1: ABCA1
kw: Serum amyloid A, Genetic polymorphisms, Coronary artery disease, Association study, Functional characterization, Singaporean Chinese

title: Can oxidative stress markers predict early ischemic stroke outcomes? A prospective study using oxidative stress biomarkers, perfusion-weighted imaging and clinical stroke severity scales
abs: As the lipid-rich environment of the brain is susceptible to free radical damage, we hypothesize that, compared to inflammatory markers, oxidative stress markers are better surrogates of the cerebral infarct/penumbra volumes, and stroke severity. We propose to assess the relationship between oxidative stress markers and cerebral infarct/penumbra volumes, and to determine the time-course of oxidative stress markers in relation to inflammatory and antioxidant markers in ischemic stroke. We had previously analysed the oxidative stress and inflammatory profiles in patients with middle cerebral artery infarction, and had observed a rise in products of lipid peroxidation namely F-2-isoprostanes, hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid and oxysterols (7-keto cholesterol, 7-b-hydroxycholesterol, 24-hydroxycholesterol and 27-hydroxycholesterol), 8-hydroxy-2-deoxyguanosine (product of DNA oxidation), and inflammatory markers interleukins 6 and 10, intercellular and vascular cell adhesion molecules and tumour necrosis factor-alpha, compared to study controls. Preliminary findings also indicate enhanced levels of the oxidized lipids measured onset of stroke and a trend of decrease throughout recovery period. F2-isoprostanes (r=0.55) and interleukins 6/10 (r=0.60 and 0.54 respectively) positively correlated with the expansion of infarct volumes (p-values, 0.04-0.20). Multivariate analysis (adjusted for age and gender) identified total F2-isoprostanes as a potential predictor of the expansion of infarct volumes (odds ratio 1.82, 95% confidence interval 0.92-2.56). Although promising, our findings were limited by a small sample size, lack of comparison with the ischemic-penumbra volumes and stroke severity/functional outcomes.This proposal is a synergy of expertise by top scientists, neurologists, neuroradiologists and neuroanatomy software developers in addressing a topic that is highly relevant to the ageing population in Singapore and internationally. This study has the potential to translate state-of-the-art research to the clinical setting by identifying patients who may potentially benefit from antioxidant therapy, assessing early response to treatment and accurately predict the extent of neuronal damage following ischemic stroke.
kw: Cerebral infarction, Biomarkers, Penumbra, Oxidative stress, Imaging, Stroke severity

title: The role of the DNA damage response in the regulation of the tumor-associated antigen 1 (CD155) expression.
abs: Some of the most effective cancer chemotherapies cause DNA damage and trigger the p53-dependent DNA damage response to induce apoptosis in a cell-autonomous manner. However, disruption of p53 function is very common in human cancers. The combination of chemotherapies with treatments that do not rely on p53 function might therefore be an effective strategy to treat cancer. Recently, we have shown that chemotherapeutic agents via the DNA damage response alert the immune system by inducing the expression of NKG2D ligands and other yet unidentified ligands in a p53-independent manner. Preliminary experiments suggest that the expression of tumor-associated antigen 1 (CD155) is upregulated in response to DNA damage. CD155 is a ligand for the activating receptor DNAM-1 and CD96, which are constitutively expressed on most immune cells. Our hypothesis is that the efficacy of cancer chemotherapies partially depends on the p53-independent induction of CD155 on tumor cells and the consequent increased sensitivity to NK cell and T cell lysis. Strategies to enhance CD155-mediated activation of the immune system after chemotherapy may hold great promise for the treatment of cancer. The experiments herein are designed 1) to identify the molecular mechanisms of the DNA damage response-mediated CD155 regulation 2) to assess the functional consequences of CD155 upregulation in response to DNA damage and 3) to study regulation of CD155 expression in vivo using an AML mouse model and AML patient samples. Through the knowledge gained from these studies we hope to optimize NK cell immunotherapy protocols currently undertaken at the National University Hospital (Singapore) and St. Jude Hospital (USA).
kw: Innate Immunity, Oncology, Natural Killer cells, Chemotherapy

title: Molecular mechanisms behind mitochondrial myopathies
abs: Mitochondrial disorders are mainly defined as the defects in the mitochondrial respiratory chain. These are complex disorders due to clinical heterogeneity because of the ubiquitous distribution of mitochondria in all organs and cells. Myopathy is a common feature in most of these disorders. Even though the role of impairment of respiratory chain in muscle degeneration is recognized the underlying mechanisms are not completely understood. One of the important abnormalities lies in defects of complex IV of the respiratory chain (cytochrome c oxidase). In the COX10 conditional KO mice, where the ancillary subunit 10 of cytochrome c oxidase enzyme is specifically deleted in the muscle, a progressive myopathy similar to human mitochondrial myopathy is observed. We hypothesize that the progressive muscle loss seen in mitochondrial myopathies is multi-factorial. Firstly, the dwindling muscle mass associated with COX deficiency could be due to increased catabolism or reduced anabolism or both of muscle proteins due to perturbations in growth factor signaling. Hence, we will first analyze the extent of protein breakdown and synthesis by determining the expression of molecules involved in these pathways. Secondly, we will also determine the signaling pathways for eg. Myostatin, which induces atrophy and IGF-1, which induces hypertrophy in muscle. Muscle atrophy is often associated with impairment of muscle stem cell (satellite cell) biology leading to poor regeneration of the muscle and thus poor prognosis. Therefore, as a second goal in this proposal, the numbers and the propensity of the muscle stem cells to get activated and proliferate to give rise to muscle precursor cells will be determined. Finally, a therapeutic approach using follistatin based therapies will be undertaken to improve myopathy in COX10 deficient mice. The outcomes of this proposal will help delineate the molecular mechanism behind mitochondrial myopathies for which there is no current effective treatment.
kw: Mitochondiral, Myopathy, COX10, follistatin, satellite cells

title: The NUH-MGH prospective study to explore the role of estrogen exposure in EGFR mutations in non-small cell lung cancer in women
abs: This multiethnic, two center study aims to determine the relationship between estrogen exposure, its signaling pathways, and the occurrence of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) mutations in female non small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Our hypothesis is that there is an inverse mechanistic relationship between estrogen exposure and the incidence of EGFR mutations. The reasons for this are as follow:1.EGFR mutations are more common (about three to four fold) in Asian women, and Asian women have lower (approximately three fold) estrogen levels compared to Caucasian women.2.Most cancers, including lung cancers, are diagnosed at post or peri-menopausal ages, and women of these ages, have lower estrogen levels than men of corresponding age.3.Bench evidence suggests an inverse relationship between ER (estrogen receptor) and EGFR. Assuming a switch of reliance to the EGFR pathway for tumor growth in patients with relatively lower than higher estrogen levels, this may explain for an increased incidence EGFR mutations in patients with lower estrogen levels. We intend to prospectively recruit 50 newly diagnosed, non-smoking, female NSCLC patients from NUH and MGH respectively. Genomic sequencing for EGFR mutations and IHC stains for EGFR, ER and PR will be done on the tumor tissue. Indices of estrogenicity, including estrogen level and parameters of estrogen exposure such as ultrasound uterine and ovarian thickness, bone mineral density (BMD) and vaginal cornification index would be examined. We anticipate to establish the relationship between estrogenicity and the incidence of EGFR mutations. This knowledge will enable a better molecular understanding of the pathogenesis of EGFR mutations, and impact therapeutic decisions about hormonal replacement therapy in women. Given that EGFR mutations makes biomarker-guided and patient-specific tailored therapy possible in NSCLC, the improved understanding of its pathogenesis is an important issue to address.
kw: Non small cell lung cancer, Female non-smokers, Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) mutations, Estrogen, Ethnic difference

title: Investigation of new lead compounds as Adenosine receptors antagonists and their potentialapplication in the treatment of Neurodegenerative Diseases
abs: The modulation of adenosine activity at specific membrane receptors (called A1, A2A, A2B andA3, respectively) continues to suggest promising therapeutic applications, since the activation orinhibition of these targets might be beneficial in certain central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Forexample, new focus has been devoted to the neuroprotective effects associated with adenosinereceptor activation during cerebral ischemia. On the other hand, it has been recently proposed thatantagonists of specific adenosine receptor subtypes may be used in the treatment of certainneurological disorders such as Parkinson’s disease and Alzheimer’s disease.In particular, the development of new ligands for such targets would be highly innovative,since there is no drug available in the market that acts at specific adenosine receptors; theseevidence suggest that a selective interaction with adenosine’s receptors could open numerouschallenges and opportunities for the research and future development for novel therapies. Our grouphas initiated preliminary studies on derivatives of 1,3,5-triazines with the aim to induce a suitablemodulation of these receptors with different degrees of affinity and selectivity. In this project we wouldlike to exploit a wider design of compounds in order to identify a new scaffold and potentiallyinnovative class of drugs. It is our intention to synthesize and pharmacologically analyze highlydiversified structures. The main advantage is that these derivatives represent interesting alternativesand simplified analogues of previous, more complex compounds that have been reported in literature.In addition, through the subsequent optimization of the substituents attached to our new compounds,we should be able to obtain valuable information about the structure–activity relationships and thechemical parameters required to optimize this drug-receptor interaction. Molecular modelinginvestigation may further rationalize the observed affinities between receptors and ligands, thuspaving the way for the design of more potent and selective anti-Parkinson derivatives.
kw: Molecular modeling, Central Nervous System, Selective Antagonists

title: Role of a phosphodiesterase inhibitor rolipram on increasing the translational efficiency in Alzheimer’s disease
abs: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a slowly progressive disease of the brain that is characterized by impairment of memory and eventually by disturbances in reasoning, planning, language, and perception. Evidence suggests that AD begins as a disorder of synaptic function, caused in part by increased levels of amyloid ß-peptide 1-42 (Aß42). It has been reported that brief treatment with the phosphodiesterase 4 inhibitor rolipram ameliorates deficits in both long-term potentiation (LTP) and contextual learning in the double-transgenic mice for amyloid precursor protein. Rolipram stabilizes synaptic circuitry via alterations in gene expression by activation of the cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA)/cAMP regulatory element-binding protein (CREB) signaling pathway that make the synapses more resistant to the insult inflicted by Aß (Vitolo et al., 2002c). Presently most of the studies regarding the rolipram on AD are based on enhancing the transcriptional ability of the neurons. In AD patients the memory deficits occurs due to degeneration of neurons involved in memory consolidation from some areas in limbic system involving hippocampus. Gene activation through phosphodiesterase inhibition is a global phenomenon that affects the healthy and degenerating neurons in brain as well. Why healthy neurons require unnecessary gene activation? Does coding of all information in a neuronal net work require gene activation? Our recent experimental evidence suggests that synaptic memory is formed and clustered in some dendritic compartments, thus excluding the role of gene activation for all form of memory consolidation (Sajikumar et al., 2007c). Our aim is to investigate how rolipram regulate the translational ability within neuronal compartments. Which specific translational mechanism is impaired in AD? How rolipram regulates the impaired translational capacity of neuronal compartments in AD? How rolipram mediated translational processes which enhance proteins like PKM zeta in dendritic compartments? (PKM zeta is an atypical PKC isotype which is critical for memory). What could be the effect of rolipram on different neurotransmitter systems like cholinergic, noradrenergic and dopaminergic systems to enhance synaptic transmission in AD? By investigating the role of rolipram on the late-associative properties of LTP and LTD such as synaptic tagging and cross-tagging with particular emphasis on local protein synthesis, we will address the above mentioned questions in detail.
kw: Alzheimer’s Disease, Long term potentiation, Synaptic tagging, Synaptic plasticity, Long term depression, Synaptic cross-tagging

title: Pathogenesis of steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome: Role of B cells in Rituximab-responsive patients
abs: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRsNS) is an important cause of end-stage renal failure in Singapore children. Most children with SRsNS have focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, and a smaller number have minimal change disease as the underlying histopathology. Studies examining the pathogenesis of SRsNS have traditionally focused on T-cells and related cytokines. In recent years, case reports have emerged regarding the induction of remission of SRsNS in patients who have failed therapy with steroids and second-line immunosuppressive agents, but were treated with rituximab (anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody). This suggested a possible role of B-cells in the pathogenesis of SRsNS, either directly or indirectly through B-T interactions. The specific aim of this project is to investigate the role of B-cells in the pathogenesis of SRsNS by examining B-T abnormalities in patients who are being treated with the current rituximab protocol. This will be accomplished by studying the following pre- and post-rituximab:1.T and B-lymphocyte subsets: CD25, CD45RA, CD45RO, CD95, CD278, CD143, CD152, CD154, HLA-DR, FasL on CD4+ and CD8+ cells, and CD80, CD86, CD25, CD69, HLA-DR on CD19+ cells;2.Profiling Th1, Th2 and T-regulatory cells by measuring intracellular cytokine production of IL-2 and IFN-g (Th1), IL-4, IL-13 and IL-10 (Th2), and determining Foxp3 expression on CD3+CD4+CD25+ cells (T-regulatory cells);3.Profiling of B-cells by measuring intracellular production of IL-10 and IL-12 and comparing this with normal and non-SRsNS patients;4.Plasma cytokine levels (Cytometric Bead Array); 5.Differentially expressed genes from purified B- and T-cells by global screening methods (oligonucleotide microarray) and subsequent validation using quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction.The above results may elucidate the pathway involved in the pathogenesis of SRsNS, thus allowing more targeted therapy to be designed. This may have potential implications on the reduction in the incidence of end-stage renal disease and associated co-morbidities in children with SRsNS.
kw: pathogenesis, steriod-resistant, B cells, nephrotic syndrome, rituximab

title: Combined Application of Biochemical Signals & Contact Guidance for Treatment of Spinal Cord Injuries
abs: Spinal cord injuries can lead to devastating effects in a patient such as paralysis. Unfortunately, currently available treatment results in sub-optimal tissue regeneration and functional recovery. The overall objective of this project is, thus, to develop a novel biomimetic fibrous scaffold endowed with biochemical and topographical signals to enhance axonal re-growth and to target growth inhibitory molecules in the central nervous system (CNS) for enhanced spinal cord regeneration. We hypothesize that the use of a single scaffold that is capable of a) the sustained delivery of a neurotrophic factor to enhance axonal re-growth together with biomolecules that antagonizes growth inhibitory compounds in the CNS and b) contact guidance will provide a favourable microenvironment to help better manipulate the fate of cells and improve tissue regeneration in spinal cord injuries. We propose to purse the following sepcific aims: 1) Synthesize and characterize biofunctional micro-/nano-fibrous scaffolds with incorporation of biochemical signals and controlled scaffold architecture for spinal cord tissue engineering applications; 2) Evaluate the potential of biofunctional micro-/nano-fibrous scaffolds for enhancing spinal cord regeneration. The innovation of this project stems from the introduction of a neural tissue engineering construct that combines biochemical cues to promote axonal regeneration and antagonize growth inhibtion; and simultaneously include topographical signals to guide axonal re-growth in spinal cord injuries. This project will help identify a potential platform for enhancing nerve regeneration in the CNS and broaden the application of biofunctional fibrous scaffolds to neural tissue engineering.
kw: Spinal cord injury, Controlled release, Nanofibrous scaffolds, Contact guidance, Neurotrophic factor, Chondroitinase ABC

title: Comparison of the genetic profile and protein expression between human tumor xenografts derived from hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cell lines and patient-derived surgical HCC explants, and between orthotopic and ectopic sites.
abs: Research into the pathogenesis, molecular signaling and treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has traditionally been conducted using established cell lines implanted as tumour xenografts onto ectopic regions of small immunodeficient animals. Although the use of cell lines in such ectopic models for in vivo human disease fills a necessary gap, obvious discordance in the biology and behavior of tumor cell lines and primary tumors exist. The poor predictive power of pre-clinical therapeutics studies of subsequent clinical trials has been attributed to such biological differences. While xenografts created using patient tumour explants and/or in orthotopc locations would be expected to have better correlation with clinical efficacy, such tumour models are technically difficult to create and there has been experimental data showing significant differences in the genetic profile and protein expression has been lacking.Until recently, it has been challenging to probe the larger realm of differences and similarities between tumor cell lines and primary tumors. To obtain a more global view of the gene and protein expression of cultured HCC cells versus primary tumors derived from HCC patients’ explants, we propose to build on our experience with creating both cell-line and patient explant derived orthotopic xenograft models to perform both microarray analysis and subsequently western blot analysis. Mice will be implanted with tumors derived from either established cell lines or patients’ explants. Both ectopic as well as orthotopic (intrahepatic) models will be used. We hypothesized that the differences and similarities between the two states would highlight the potential areas of correspondence as well as define some of the selection pressures that are inherent in cell culture. Such findings will provide an important scientific basis for better tumour xenograft models in HCC as well as other tumours and provide insight into potential targets for therapeutics.
kw: Human hepatocellular carcinoma, Orthotopic, Gene profile, Xenografts, Human Explants, Proteomics

title: An individual-based simulation model for heterosexually acquired sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and HIV in Singapore a novel framework for interpreting trends, investigating causes, and prioritizing interventions
abs: Background of studyThere has been a sharp rise in the incidence of acute sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in heterosexual youths in recent years, with incidence having tripled between 2002 and 2006. It is unclear what is driving this increase, and what implications this may have on future HIV incidence.Specific aimsThe study aims to use a modeling approach to investigate key drivers behind the increase in acute STIs amongst heterosexual youth in Singapore, explore the potential for HIV transmission in these at-risk populations, and estimate the potential impact of different interventions for reducing future STI and HIV incidence.MethodologyWe propose a stochastic individual-based simulation of STI transmission built in an open source programming language which models various categories of individuals – unmarried men and women with low and high sexual risk activity, married men and married women, male clients of sex workers, and sex workers. The model will also account for interaction between local men and sex workers abroad using published estimates of STI/HIV prevalence in the region. Published and unpublished studies from Singapore will be used to inform parameter estimates of sexual behavior, while disease specific parameters on infectious duration and transmission probabilities will be obtained from published literature. We will use data mining approaches as well as fit the model to local STI/HIV incidence to estimate network parameters. The calibrated model will then be used to project the potential course of the future heterosexual STI/HIV epidemic in Singapore, with and without interventions, with appropriate sensitivity analysis for uncertainty in parameter estimates.Clinical SignificanceThe study will provide policy makers with pertinent information for planning programs to prevent and control STIs and HIV in Singapore.
kw: HIV, simulation, sexually transmitted infections, mathematical modeling, surveillance, public health

title: Development of Inorganic/Polymer Nanohybrid Materials with High Refractive Index for Artificial Corneal Implants
abs: Myopia and other forms of cornea-related refractive errors represent the commonest cause of visual disability today, and Singapore has one of highest rates of myopia in the world. The aim of this proposed program is to develop a hydrogel polymer-based artificial cornea with an adjustable and high refractive index by incorporating nanosized high refractive inorganic fillers (such as TiO2 and ZnS) in a polythiourethane polymer. Hydrogels represent an important class of biomaterials for a variety of medical applications (including tissue engineering) because of their excellent biocompatibility and high permeability to oxygen, nutrients, and other water-soluble metabolites. Hydrogels are crosslinked hydrophilic polymers that incorporate large quantities of water and take on physical characteristics similar to soft tissue. We propose a hydrogel based methacrylate-terminated polythiourethane filled with ex situ precipitated nano-sized inorganic particle like TiO2 and ZnS. The water soluble polythiourethane shall be photocrosslinked in the presence of the inorganic particles to make the high refractive index hydrogel. Their including refractive index, transparency, hydrophilicity and mechanical strength will be controlled and optimized. These inorganic/polymer nanohybrid materials will be evaluated for corneal biocompatibility, safety and efficacy for in vitro studies.
kw: nanoinorganics, refractive index, artificial cornea

title: Toward A novel Antimicrobial Strategy: Exploiting Bacteriocin Regulatory Mechanisms to trigger bacterial suicide in Pseudomonas Aetuginosa
abs: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a human pathogen deadly to patients hospitalized with cancer, cystic fibrosis, andburn. The clinical importance of P. aeruginosa stems from the fact that the infection causes extremely high fatalityrates in those immunocompromised patients and it is resistant to commonly used antibiotics. Toward thedevelopment of novel antimicrobial strategies effective against P. aeruginosa, the proposed research aims toexploit the regulatory mechanisms of bacteriocin and immunity genes to trigger bacterial suicide. Bacteriocins areribosomally synthesized, highly potent antimicrobial peptides. Bacteriocin-producing bacteria require immunityproteins for self-protection because bacteriocins are lethal even to the producers. Therefore, the repression ofimmunity proteins during bacteriocin synthesis results in bacterial suicide. P. aeruginosa produces a range ofbacteriocins, named pyocins, and immunity proteins. Despite previous efforts to elucidate the pyocin systems,regulatory mechanisms controlling pyocins and immunity proteins remain obscure. Moreover, there has been noattempt to explore bacteriocin regulatory mechanisms as a bacterial suicidal module. In this proposed research,thus, the specific aims are to: (i) determine genome-wide genetic bases controlling the expression of pyocin genes,(ii) characterize the mechanisms of the regulation of immunity genes, and (iii) correlate the regulation of immunitygenes with the expression of target transcription factors. These aims will be achieved by employing an integratedapproach of genetic engineering and microbial genomics. Transcriptome profiling coupled with gene knockout,fusion vectors and regulatable promoter assays will be used to advance our understanding of pyocin regulatorymechanisms in P. aeruginosa. The outcome of this proposed research may provide insight into the design of noveltherapeutic molecules that activate bacterial suicide by modulating the expression of immunity genes.
kw: Bacteriocins, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Regulatory mechanisms, Pyocins, Antimicrobials, Transcription factors

title: Unified platform for Accelerated Functional Return of Grasping, Wrist and Forearm Control in Stroke Patients with EMG Actuated UE Orthosis.
abs: This research is of an (Electromyogram-Functional Electrical Stimulation) EMG-FES actuated (Upper Extremity)UE orthosis allowing stroke patients to achieve earlier functional return of their affected UEs. Our hypotheses is through the concept of “position for function”, utilizing EMG-FES system will accelerate the functional gain for stroke patients’ affected hands with a forearm based orthosis covering up to the fingers. The patient will achieve earlier and better results for UE rehabilitation over this period. Stroke was the 4th cause of death in Singapore in 2006. It is the leading cause of disability in individuals below 35 years old. Despite optimal medical treatment, 45% of stroke survivors are left permanently disabled. Loss of upper limb function is one of the most devastating types of disability. For patients with persistent (>1 month) upper extremity (UE) weakness post stroke, only 10% regain functional use. Many researchers of developing UE robotic trainers, eg. MIT-Manus, MIME and ARM Guide show promising results. The first robotic therapy study was conducted with MIT-Manus confirmed that robots was an effective tool to aid in rehabilitation of movement deficits by increasing the therapy delivered to acute stroke patients (Leonard, 2003). When developed successfully, therapists can use this as a modality for stroke UE training for functional gain in the patients’ performance in their Basic/Individual Activities for Daily Living (BADL)s or (IADL)s. The majority of stroke patients with fair cognitive functions can be trained to use this device for accelerated stroke rehabilitation. After the prototype device has been developed, this will be followed by 3 trial cases with given adequate training and practice in phase 1. With their feedback, the device will be refined and a proper pilot study will be conducted in phase 2. We will

title: Characterization and differentiation of cardiac stem/progenitor cells from adult heart
abs: Heart failure resulted from ischemic heart diseases is one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in the world. Cardiomyocytes have been traditionally regarded as terminally differentiated cells that adapt to increased work and compensate for disease exclusively through hypertrophy. More recently, compelling evidences have accumulated suggesting that the heart has regenerative potential. Investigators have identified populations of stem cells within the myocardium that are capable of differentiating into cardiac myocytes, endothelial cells and smooth muscle cells. The cardiac stem cells derived from heart tissue are clonogenesis. They are able to migrate to the infarcted myocardium and contribute to myogenesis and revascularization. The applicant is currently isolating c-Kit+ cardiac stem/progenitor cells from porcine left ventricle/atrium and is optimizing the isolation condition. In current study, the applicant will purify, characterize and differentiate c-kit+ porcine cardiac stem cells. The cardiac stem cells will be purified by Magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS). The cells will be characterized for other cell markers: CD31, CD34, CD144, KDR/flk-1 et al. The growth factor expression profile of cardiac stem cells will be investigated. c-Kit+ cardiac stem cell will be induced to differentiate into cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells. The study will be served as a guidance for isolation, purification and characterization of human resident c-Kit+ cardiac stem cells in adult heart, and serves as a bridge for future in vivo animal studies and clinical trials that use autologous resident c-Kit+ cardiac stem cells for cardiac repair and regeneration.
kw: Cardiac stem/progenitor cells, c-Kit (CD117), Cell differentiation

title: Synthesis of fused polycyclic derivatives and thioxo analogues of 1,3,5-triazine-2,4-dione as newinhibitors of thymidine phosphorylase for potential use in cancer chemotherapy.
abs: The strategy of designing inhibitors of essential metabolic enzymes has been adopted successfully indrug development for cancer chemotherapy and this strategy forms the basis for this proposedinvestigation. The enzyme thymidine phosphorylase (TPase) catalyzes the reversible phosphorolysisof thymidine to thymine and a-D-2-deoxyribose-1-phosphate. TPase is known to be over-expressed inmany different types of solid tumors and plays an important role in angiogenesis, tumor growth,invasion and metastasis. Therefore it is hypothesized that the inhibition of TPase may lead to areduction in neovacularization and consequently diminished in cancer cell growth. There are two mainobjectives to this project; the first is to adopt a structure based approach to design and synthesizeTPase inhibitors that contain the 1,3,5-triazine-2,4-dione scaffold. Structural modifications on thescaffold to generate fused polycyclic derivatives of 1,3,5-triazine-2,4-diones and their thioxobioisosteres will also be carried out. The proposed synthetic schemes will involve new approaches inannulation reactions to give fused ring systems. The second objective is to evaluate the newheterocyclic compounds for potential inhibitory action against the human TPase through the use of anin vitro enzyme assay. Heterocycles that exhibit good TPase inhibitory activity will be furtherevaluated for antiproliferative and apoptosis induction activities using the MTT assay and flowcytometric analysis respectively. A range of cancer cell lines including HT-29 (colon), SK-OV-3(ovary), A549 (lung) and MCF-7 (breast) will be employed in the bioactivity investigation. Today,chemotherapy is still an important option in the treatment of cancer. This study explores thedevelopment of a new class of antineoplastic agents that may exhibit multiple bioactivities such ascellular antiproliferative effect, anti-angiogenic action, tumor growth reduction and metastasisprevention. Therefore, the potential impact of this project is the provision of an alternative option incancer chemotherapy that may translate into better clinical outcomes.
kw: thymidine phosphorylase, antiproliferative activity, 1,3,5-triazine-2,4-dione

title: Effects of Dynamic Tension and Growth Factor on Degenerated Human Annulus Fibrosus and Nucleus Pulposus Cells in Vitro
abs: Low back pain is a plague in modern society and a major source of disability and cost. It is the most common health problem for economically productive individuals between the age of 20 and 50 years. An annual average of 297 million restricted days and 87 million disability days worldwide are attributable to low back pain.Increasing evidence showed extracelluar micromechanical stimuli or several of the growth factors could modulate the biological response of the intervertebral disc (IVD) cells and play a critical role in determining the fate of individual IVD cells. However, the response of the IVD cells to the combination of dynamic tension and growth factor has never been studied. It has never been shown if degenerated IVD cells can be recovered under certain mechanical and biological conditions synergistically. This proposal focuses on the hypothesis that a combination of dynamic tension and growth factor will be able to reverse the biosynthesis of proteoglycan and collagen to a pre-compressed level, thus verifying that it is possible to make the degenerated IVD cells regenerate better than application of dynamic tension only. In this study, the model of degenerated human IVD cells will first be established by applying compression on the annulus and fibrosus cells. Subsequently, the degenerated cells will be loaded with combination of dynamic tension and growth factor (BMP-7). The combined effects of tension and growth factor (BMP-7) on the degenerated cells will be analyzed by the amount of biosynthesis of proteoglycan and collagen.The knowledge on the regenerative mechanism of IVD cells will shed light on the solution to IVD degeneration in clinical settings. This finding may help to translate into a new regime of prevention and treatment of low back pain.
kw: Dynamic Tension, Degenerated, Annulus Fibrous and Nucleus Pulposus Cells, Growth Factor, Human, In Vitro

title: Using dynamic contrast enhanced CT perfusion (CTP) to predict and measure response to radiation therapy for cerebral metastases.
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Introduction Patients with more than 3 cerebral metastases from a systemic malignancy are generally managed with radiation therapy (RT) alone for palliation. Although RT may prolong the median survival, most patients will eventually progress either in the brain or systemically. To date there is no conclusive method to predict which patients will respond to RT and whose survival will be improved. As more aggressive and costly systemic treatments are being utilized for the management of metastatic disease post whole brain radiotherapy (WBRT), it is increasing important to identify early indicators of intracranial response or progression that are sufficiently predictive to aid in determining which patients may potentially benefit from such an approach.One possible method to determine early response would be to study tumor and brain tissue perfusion using dynamic contrast enhanced CT perfusion (CTP). Microcirculation parameters of intracranial tumors such as cerebral blood flow (CBF), volume (CBV), time to peak (TTP) and permeability (PS) can be determined. Although preliminary work has suggested that low tumour perfusion may predict poor control in head and neck cancer and gliomas, there have been no previous studies characterizing tumour perfusion and permeability following WBRT in cerebral metastasis.Our group has developed the mathematical models to calculate these biomarkers and apply them to study cerebral metastasis using CTP. Aim A)determine markers of tumor microcirculation that predict intracranial response to WBRT B)characterize tumour perfusion and brain surface permeability following WBRT. Method40 patients with cerebral metastases from lung cancer planned for standard whole brain radiation therapy will be longitudinally studied using CTP at 4 different time points: pre-RT, end-RT, Week+6 post RT and Week +16 post RT. The microcirculatory parameters will be measured at each time point and correlated to the tumor response during the study and clinical outcome at long-term follow up. SignificanceIf this study confirms our hypothesis, these in vivo, non invasive biomarkers of tumor vascularity obtained using CTP can be used to predict response to WBRT. We will also better understand the effect of WBRT on CBF, CBV and surface permeability. Furthermore, such surrogate imaging end points may potentially select patients with hypoxic metastases for enhanced therapy such as a radiosensitiser or stereotactic radiosurgery boost, and CTP may be useful in clinical trials assessing novel and individually tailored cancer treatments.
kw: Cerebral, Metastasis, CT scan, Perfusion, Radiation

title: PHASE I/II STUDY OF SIR-SPHERES PLUS SORAFENIB (CHEMO-RADIOTHERAPY) AS FIRST LINE TREATMENT IN PATIENTS WITH NON-RESECTABLE PRIMARY HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA - A MULTI-CENTER TRIAL
abs: Most HCC (80%) are found in Asia. When diagnosed, only about 30% of patients areamendable to potentially curative therapies (surgical resection, transplantation, percutaneous ablation) The prognosis in the rest is grave with median survival of less than 3 months in the Asia-Pacific. The hepatogenesis of HCC is complex and conventional chemotherapy has little efficacy. The first positive systemic therapy phase III (SHARP) trial was only reported in July 2007. Sorafenib (Bayer), an oral molecular pathway targeted drug targets the raf/mek/erk pathwayand increased survival by 3 months in Child A inoperable HCC (7.9 vs. 10.7 months) although it demonstrated no significant tumour regression. Time to tumour progression was also significantly improved (12.3 vs. 24 weeks).While the liver is radio-sensitive, external beam radiation causes significant radio-toxicity. To overcome this, selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT) was developed to deliver a radiation source directly to liver cancer via the arterial route. SIR-sphere (Sirtex) is radioactive yttrium on a 35 micro-meter diameter resin carrier and is an established therapy in colorectal metastasis. SIR-sphere has been reported to cause significantly tumour regression in HCC. We hypothesize that the combination of an ablative therapy (SIRT) with a proven systemic therapy will confer added survival benefit to patients and propose a phase I/ II trial combiningSIR-sphere with Sorafenib. This investigator-initiated multi-center trial (data center inSingapore) will be carried out by an established collaborative group, the Asia-PacificHepatocellular Carcinoma (AHCC) Trials Group. SIR-sphere therapy will be administered at a central location in Singapore and patients will be administered Sorafenib at their native trial centers. Both Bayer and Sirtex are collaborating in this trial by sponsoring their therapeutics respectively. The primary objectives of this trial are (1) Toxicity and safety (2) tumour response, with a view to a subsequent phase III trial.
kw: hepatocellualr carcinoma, selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT), Sir-Sphere, phase I/II trial, molecular targetted therapy, Sorafenib

title: Substance P as an inflammatory mediator in acute pancreatitis and associated lung injury: mechanismof action and implications
abs: We have previously shown the presence of substance P in the pancreas and of its receptors (the NK1receptors) on pancreatic acinar cells in mice. On induction of pancreatitis, there is an up-regulation ofpancreatic substance P levels and of NK1 receptor expression. Moreover, knockout mice deficient ineither the gene for substance P (the preprotachykinin-A gene) or for NK1 receptors are protectedagainst acute pancreatitis and the associated lung injury. Moreover, treatment with CP-96,345, anNK1 receptor antagonist, protects mice against acute pancreatitis and associated lung injury. Theprincipal aim of this project is to investigate the pro-inflammatory role of substance P and neurogenicinflammation in acute pancreatitis and associated lung injury. A differential regulation of inflammationby substance P in the pancreas and lungs will be investigated. We propose to use two experimentalmodels in the mouse (caerulein hyperstimulation and choline deficient ethionine supplemented - CDEdiet). In order to investigate the signaling pathways involved in the action of substance P, studies willbe performed in isolated pancreatic acinar cells and in leukocytes in vitro. Two different andcomplementary approaches, i.e., gene deletion and pharmacological intervention, will be used toinvestigate the importance of substance P in the regulation of inflammation in the pancreas and lungs.The effect of substance P on leukocyte recruitment in the pancreas and lungs will be investigated.Furthermore, signalling pathways (such as NF-kB, MAP kinases, protein kinase C) that contribute tothe effects of substance P on leukocytes and isolated pancreatic acinar cells will be investigated. It ishoped that the results from this project will help us understand the role of the neurogenicinflammatory mediators in MODS associated not only with acute pancreatitis, but also with otherconditions and provide a rational basis for developing anti-neuroinflammatory mediator therapy.
kw: Neurogenic inflammation, Substance P, Leukocytes, Acute Pancreatitis, NF-kappaB, Adhesion Molecules

title: Serial vasopressin and copeptin levels in chidren with sepsis and septic shock
abs: The paediatric vasomotor response to sepsis is significantly different to that of adults. Vasopressin is a potent vasoconstrictor with an important regulatory role in the vasomotor response to sepsis. Serial values of vasopressin in septic shock in children do not follow the same pattern as in adults. The reasons for this have not been previously investigated. The aims of this study are to describe the serial levels of vasopressin and its precursor, copeptin, in children with sepsis and septic shock, and to test the hypothesis that copeptin levels correlate with vasopressin levels in paediatric septic shock. Intravenous vasopressin via infusion has become accepted treatment in paediatric septic shock unresponsive to other therapies, on the basis of adult and animal studies, without adequate data regarding the optimal timing, dose, and cessation.A prospective single center study will be conducted. The control group will consist of healthy infants and children. Eligible children with sepsis and septic shock will be recruited after informed consent is obtained. Admission levels of vasopressin and copeptin will be collected. Patients with septic shock will have their vasopressin and copeptin levels monitored serially. Statistical analysis will be performed to look for possible significant differences in the admission levels between the various subsets. The serial copeptin levels will also be described in children with septic shock. The results of this preliminary study will help in delineating the differences in vasopressin and copeptin levels for children with sepsis and septic shock. It will also confirm the correlation between vasopressin and copeptin levels in paediatric septic shock, as a preliminary step in establishing if the differences are the result of production, metabolism or receptor regulation issues. Thus, further studies to look into the vasomotor response in paedatric sepsis with respect to the timing and optimal dosing of vasopressin can be conducted.
kw: Septic Shock, Paediatrics, Copeptin, Vasopressin

title: Investigations into the role of immune activation and colonic inflammation in patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome - A pilot study
abs: Irritable bowel syndrome is one of the commonest problems seen in the Gastroenterology clinic. Studies in Caucasian populations have shown that an increased intestinal mucosal inflammatory infiltrate and an altered plasma cytokine milieu may play a role in the pathophysiology of IBS. We propose that IBS is caused by an increased mucosal inflammatory cell infiltrate with enhanced leukocyte cytokine release causing a disordered mucosal cytokine milieu. We aim to demonstrate and phenotypically describe the increased inflammatory infiltrate and demonstrate that this is associated with an altered intestinal mucosal and plasma cytokine milieu in IBS patients. This pilot study will recruit 60 IBS patients and 20 normal controls. Peripheral blood and colonic mucosa will be obtained. The number and distribution of activated lymphocytes and macrophages, and regulatory lymphocytes and suppressive myeloid cells will be investigated using FACS and immunohistochemistry. The levels of proinflammatory cytokines and regulatory cytokines will be measured in the serum and the mucosa of patients and normal donors.This project will be the first attempt to demonstrate a correlation between the inflammatory cell infiltrate in IBS patients with the mucosal cytokine milieu. A positive finding could result in a paradigm change in the way IBS is viewed and treated. It would be the scientific basis for trials looking for a correlation between gut immunity visceral hypersensitivity and gut dysmotility. It would also form the basis for trials investigating the role of anti inflammatory treatments in IBS patients.
kw: Irritable bowel syndrome, Cytokine, Lymphocyte

title: The Role of SPARC Expression on Conjunctival Wound Healing.
abs: SPARC expression is accepted to having a major role in the events of wound repair. Although evidence of the importance of SPARC is mounting in the development of tumourogenesis and dermal wound healing, the significance of SPARC activity in conjunctival tissue repair processes is currently not known. The following hypotheses of the study are1. SPARC expression is involved in the cellular events of conjunctival wound healing2. Inhibition of SPARC expression leads to a reduction in scar tissue formation following glaucoma filtration surgery and improves surgical outcome. This study aims to determine the effect of SPARC on human Tenon’s fibroblast wound healing functions (ie migration, proliferation, cell-matrix interaction, and collagen production) using established techniques including collagen I lattices and scratch wound model to investigate biological functions. Functional analyses will be performed with standard investigative tools on gene and protein expression (RT-PCR, western blot, ELISA). The effect of SPARC inhibition will be investigated on post-operative wound healing events on an established animal model of aggressive conjunctival scarring, which is also a well-accepted model of experimental glaucoma.The clinical significance of SPARC in post-operative conjunctival scarring will be explored and evaluated in this proposed study. It is anticipated that the project will be the first to describe the role SPARC expression plays in conjunctival wound healing, and in doing so provide further insight and understanding into the complex mechanisms of tissue repair in the eye.The project focuses on conjunctival wound healing, but it has great implications on wound healing modulation in all forms of ocular surgery. Examples include following refractive surgery with modulation of corneal wound healing from lasik (up and down-regulation of specific inflammatory mediators), development of posterior capsule opacification and capsule fibrosis and scarring post cataract surgery, and after vitreoretinal surgery such as in the development of posterior vitreoretinopathy (PVR).
kw: SPARC, Wound healing, Glaucoma surgery, Fibroblast

title: Characterization of Side Population and Isolation of Novel Cancer Stem Cell markers in Renal Cell Carcinoma
abs: Specific aims: To isolate and characterize cancer stem cell (CSC)-enriched Side Population and explore the molecular mechanisms of CSC involvement in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) progression and metastasis. Hypotheses: The abundance of CSC-enriched side population (SP) from 14 RCC cell lines may correlate to tumorigenesis and metastasis of RCC. Establish the characteristics of SP in RCC cell lines and establish the gene expression profiling of SP and non-SP to identify novel CSC markers and molecular pathways involved in CSC survival.Methodology: The SP of 14 RCC cell lines will be determined using protocol described by Goodell, M., et al. (1996), with some modifications. The abundance of SP will be correlated with the tumorigenic and metastatic potential of these RCC cell lines in vivo. The SP in RCC cell lines will be characterized using soft agar assay, in vivo tumorigenesis assay, cell migration and invasion assay, viability and cell proliferation assay. To identify CSC-specific markers, gene expression profile for SP and non-SP will be performed using microarray analysis. RNA will be extracted from these two groups of cells and the differentially expressed genes will be compared across the 14 RCC cell lines. Further characterization of the identified markers will be performed which include transcripts expression, protein expression by immunostaining and tumorigenic potential by animal work. Clinical Significance: The low 5-years survival rate of stage IV RCC and the high rate of cancer relapse after traditional cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy have been hypothesized to be attributed to the presence of CSC. CSC was suggested to be involved in the progression and metastasis of cancers. Currently, these hypotheses are rigorously tested and the mechanisms are largely unknown. The search of CSC-specific markers and characterization of CSC may shed some light to its roles in cancer progression and metastasis. Results from this study may led to development of new prognostic biomarkers for RCC and also revolutionized the way we treat this cancer in years to come.
kw: cancer stem cells, renal cell carcinoma, side population, metastasis, gene expression profiling, prognostic marker

title: Quorum-Based Technology: Developing N-Acyl Homoserine Lactonases as Therapeutic Biomolecules.
abs: The proposal focuses on developing N-acyl homoserine lactonases (AHLs) for use in the biomedical industry. Quorum-sensing is an integral part of microbial interaction, and is responsible for virulence or pathogenecity of disease-causing bacteria. Quorum-quenching mechanisms have been evolved by microbes to prevent colonization by other microbial populations. Many of these “quenchers” are enzymes like AHLs that are secreted into the environment to degrade the quorum molecules of competing microbial species, effectively disrupting the quorum-sensing pathways of these “foreign” populations. We will develop anti-virulence “antimicrobials” by specifically targeting the quorum-sensing pathways of pathogenic microbes. Due to the anti-virulence nature of the mode of disruption, this strategy does not present the selective pressure that always results in the development of resistance in microbes.These enzymes are refractory to prokaryotic recombinant expression due to insolubility. Hence, we will use directed evolution methods to evolve properties that are currently lacking in these enzymes for use in the biomedical industry; properties include increased solubility for recombinant expression in heterologous expression systems and increased thermal and pH stability. We will also obtain X-ray crystal structures of these evolved AHLs to facilitate future work in developing these biomolecules as therapeutic agents. We are ultimately interested in tailoring specificity within these AHLs to target specific human diseases, and developing broad-range specificity (promiscuity) providing treatment against a broad-spectrum of diseases caused by bacterial pathogens. This project will lead to the development of a new class of therapeutic biomolecules against infectious diseases that are caused by bacterial pathogens prevalent in Singapore; we envision this work will also result in the development of biomaterials that can be used to disrupt biofilm formation, finding use in numerous clinical settings such as in replacement surgeries to prevent opportunistic infections due to prosthetic implants.
kw: Quorum-Based Technology, Therapeutic Biomolecues, Protein Solubility, N-Acyl Homoserine Lactonases, Directed Evolution, Structure-Function Relationships

title: Novel Retinal Geometric Parameters as Biomarkers of Cardio-Metabolic and Retinal Diseases and Mortality: A Multi-Ethnic Population-Based Study
abs: Cardio-metabolic diseases (diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia) are the major causes of mortality, and retinal diseases (age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and diabetic retinopathy) the leading causes of blindness worldwide. The retinal vasculature provides a unique window for non-invasive visualization of the human circulation in vivo. Digital retinal photography and new imaging technology have enabled more precise documentation of subtle and early retinal microvascular changes, such as retinal arteriolar narrowing, and isolated retinopathy lesions. These changes in the retinal vasculature have now been shown to predict the development of both subclinical and clinical cardiovascular, metabolic, renal and retinal diseases in large population studies. However, previous studies have primarily focused on retinal vascular caliber, which represent only one of the many aspects of the retinal vascular geometry, and do not fully capture all the information regarding abnormalities of the retinal vasculature. The full potential of retinal image-analysis in relation to prediction of cardio-metabolic and retinal diseases therefore remains undetermined. This proposal describes a population-based study of 8,000+ persons from the three major racial/ethnic groups in Asia (Chinese, Indians and Malays), evaluating the relationship of novel geometric parameters of the retinal vasculature with cardio-metabolic and retinal diseases, and 5-year mortality outcomes. This will include the measurement of a range of previously unexplored retinal changes (e.g., fractal dimension, vascular tortuosity, branching angle) using newly developed computer software, and the diseases/outcomes analyzed will include diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, metabolic syndrome, chronic kidney disease, early and late AMD, diabetic and non-diabetic retinopathy and 5-year all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The proposal will use and capitalizes on the comprehensive data of high-quality digital retinal images, risk factors and disease outcomes already collected from two population-based cohorts, the Singapore Malay Eye Study (SiMES), and Singapore Prospective Study Program (SP2). Novel geometric parameters of the retinal vasculature will be measured and characterized from retinal photographs collected from the combined study population.The significance of this study is the development of novel retinal vascular imaging as a potential risk prediction tool for important cardiovascular and retinal diseases in Asia and worldwide.
kw: Retinal vessels, Retinopathy, Cardiovascular diseases, Retinal diseases, Diabetes, Risk prediction

title: CYP2D6 Pharmacogenetics and Its Influence on Tamoxifen Pharmacokinetics and Clinical Outcome in Asian Metastatic Breast Cancer Patients
abs: BackgroundIt is a well known fact that understanding interindividual pharmacokinetic variability is a major goal of clinical pharmacology. The interpatient variability to treatment outcome in breast cancer patients receiving tamoxifen therapy is high and the reasons for this disparity in treatment outcome are poorly understood.Recent findings suggest that interpatient variability in exposure levels to active metabolites of tamoxifen such as 4-hydroxy-tamoxifen and endoxifen may be responsible for the differences in therapeutic outcome. The formation of 4-hydroxy-tamoxifen and endoxifen is mediated by CYP2D6 enzyme and understanding the factors that influence CYP2D6 catalytic activity in breast cancer patients receiving tamoxifen therapy would be useful in predicting response. The CYP2D6 gene is highly polymorphic and patients homozygous for alleles associated with the poor metaboliser phenotype such as CYP2D6*4/*4 in Caucasians and CYP2D6*5/*5 and CYP2D6*10/*10 in Koreans and Japanese patients were associated with decreased levels of endoxifen and poor therapeutic outcome and survival. Such data is lacking in our local multiethnic population.Objectives and AimsThe objective of this study proposal is to investigate the influence of functional polymorphic alleles in the CYP2D6 gene (CYP2D6*5 and CYP2D6*10) on the pharmacokinetics of tamoxifen and clinical outcome in metastatic Asian breast cancer patients (Chinese, Malay and Indian patients). The aims of the study are as follows:1.To characterize the population distribution of CYP2D6 polymorphisms (CYP2D6*5 and CYP2D6*10) in healthy Chinese, Malay and Indian subjects.2.To study the pharmacokinetics of tamoxifen, N desmethytamoxifen (ND-TAM,) 4-hydroxy-tamoxifen (4-OH-TAM) and endoxifen in Asian metastatic breast cancer patients.3.To investigate the impact of common CYP2D6 polymorphisms in Chinese, Malay and Indian patients (CYP2D6*5 and CYP2D6*10) and CYP3A5*3 on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of tamoxifen and its active metabolites.4.To assess the influence of common CYP2D6 polymorphisms (CYP2D6*5 and CYP2D6*10) and CYP3A5*3 on clinical outcome in Asian breast cancer patients receiving tamoxifen.
kw: Tamoxifen, CYP2D6, Pharmacogenetics, Asian cancer patients

title: Understanding molecular mechanisms of post-transcriptional control in neuronal differentiation: a link between microRNAs, alternative pre-mRNA splicing and mRNA quality control
abs: Post-transcriptional gene regulation affords a rapid mechanism for changes in the cellular proteome and is widely used during nervous system (NS) development. Among the best-studied examples of post-transcriptional control are the regulation of alternative pre-mRNA splicing and the repression of protein synthesis by microRNAs (miRNAs). As a result of my postdoctoral studies, I have identified a link between these two pathways by showing that the NS-specific miRNA miR-124 downregulates the expression of polypyrimidine tract binding protein (PTBP1), a global repressor of alternative splicing. PTBP1 affects alternative splicing patterns of a number of pre-mRNAs. Among the targets of PTBP1 is a critical cassette exon in the pre-mRNA of PTBP2, an NS-enriched PTBP1 homolog. When this exon is skipped, PTBP2 mRNA is subject to nonsense-mediated decay (NMD). During neuronal differentiation, miR-124 expression is upregulated leading to a decrease in PTBP1 levels and a dramatic increase in PTBP2 levels. Here, I propose a systematic study of this newly identified miRNA/alternative splicing interface. I will characterize molecular mechanisms regulating expression and post-transcriptional modification of miR-124. I will also study an NMD-independent pathway whereby PTBP1 downregulates the abundance of PTBP2 and possibly several other pre-mRNAs by inducing intron retention and, as a result, restricting the nuclear export of the incompletely spliced mRNAs. To identify components of this novel pathway, I will carry out two genetic screens: a forward genetic screen in fission yeast (Schizosaccharomyces pombe) and an originally developed miRNA-based screen in mammalian cells. The proposed research should provide important insights into the post-transcriptional mechanisms regulating neuronal differentiation, generate novel technologies and resources, and possibly contribute to developing new therapies for neurodegenerative diseases and cancer.
kw: miRNA pathway;alternative pre-mRNA splicing;mRNA nuclear retention;regulation of gene expression;protein purification;genetic screens

title: Overcoming Resistance to Targeted Therapies in Blast Phase Chronic Myelogenous Leukaemia
abs: The goal of this research is to define the mechanisms by which the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), a central regulator of mRNA translation, contributes to the pathogenesis of blast phase (BP) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). We have recently determined that cap-dependent translation is critical to Bcr-Abl-mediated transformation, and that Bcr-Abl activity recruits a unique subset of mRNAs to actively translating polysomes. These results suggest that mTOR is critical to the pathogenesis of BP CML. Accordingly, we have begun to treat patients with imatinib (IM)-resistant BP CML, with the mTOR inhibitor, CCI-779, and have observed promising responses. Together, these observations lead us to hypothesize that mTOR contributes to BP CML by dysregulating cap-dependent translation. mTOR controls cell growth and proliferation in response to growth factors and the availability of nutrients. Several mediators of growth factor signaling to mTOR have been described, and include pathways known to be active in BP CML, such as Ras, PI3K, and Wnt/GSK-3. Both ribosomal protein S6 (rpS6) and eIF4E function are regulated by mTOR, and in turn control translation of genes involved in growth and survival. We thus propose a model in which mTOR integrates signals from several pathways which are active in BP CML, and contributes to leukemia via the translation of specific mRNAs. We will explore the pathways that activate mTOR in BP CML, as well as critical effectors of mTOR signaling. We will use a combination of biochemical and genetic approaches to pursue three specific aims. Aim 1: Determine if the GSK-3/mTOR axis is important BP CML. Aim 2: Determine if rpS6 phosphorylation regulates polysome assembly. Aim 3: Determine if eIF4E overexpression mediates imatinib-resistance in BP CML. These studies will increase our understanding of the pathogenesis of cancers fueled by dysregulated translation, and suggest novel therapeutic strategies.

title: Using Novel Unbiased Forward Genetic Screen and Comparative Genomics in Mice to Model Progression and Transformation of Multiple Myeloma
abs: Events mediating transformation of monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), a pre-malignant condition, to multiple myeloma (MM), an incurable B-cell malignancy, is unknown. As all the recurrent disease defining genetic abnormalities are already present at the pre-malignant MGUS stage at similar frequency to MM, we hypothesize that yet unknown cooperating genetic abnormalities must mediate transformation. The main objective of this study is therefore to identify the cooperating genetic defects using unbiased methods suitable for cancer gene discovery in the main genetic subtypes of MM. To achieve this we intend to use a transposon-mediated forward mutagenesis screen in mice with the appropriate genetic background simulating the initial genetic events in MM. These mice have already been generated and are phenotypically normal and hence ideal for identifying cooperating gene mutations. The sleeping beauty transposon has been engineer to â€˜hopâ€™ around and randomly integrate into the mammalian genome. The integration sites can be identified using tags left behind by the transposon. The genes mutated recurrently by transposon integration in mice that develop tumors can then be analyzed statistically to identify putative cooperating mutations. This result will then be integrated with global human gene expression and copy number data generated by gene expression profiling and array-comparative genomic hybridization. This cross species comparison and platform integration strategy will enable us to identify and characterize high priority early genetic events in multiple myeloma. The results of the research will have significant impact on not only the understanding of myeloma biology, but also identification of early therapeutic targets and generation of useful mouse models of myeloma.

title: Investigating genetic factors in Essential Tremor
inst: National Neuroscience Institute of Singapore Pte Ltd
abs: Background: Essential tremor (ET), with a prevalence of 4 to 39 cases per 1000, is an age related neurodegenerative disorder with significant impact on quality of life for sufferers. The vast majority of ET patients have a positive family history. The causative genes for ET have yet to be identified. Studies suggest that that a number of genes may be involved. The ETM2 locus was previously associated with a select group of familial ET patients in Singapore. Objective: Our primary objective aims to identify common ET genetic susceptibility variants In a genetic association study using a case control methodology, and to perform genome wide screening for linkage of candidate regions in ET families in Singapore. Methods: In a nationwide effort, we will build a national gene-bank and database for patients with ET. We will perform genomewide screening for linkage and further fine mapping of candidate regions, haplotype analysis and sequencing of positional candidate genes in a large cohort of Singaporean ET families with the aim of determining linked chromosomal regions and genes responsible for genetic susceptibility to ET. Separately, we will conduct haplotype analysis of candidate genes and whole genome wide analysis in a large cohort of ET probands and unrelated healthy controls. The whole-genome association analysis will be pursued using Illuminaâ€™s Human450S DNA Analysis BeadChip. Genotyping will be carried out using the Sequenom platform. In addition, we will determine phenotype-genotype correlation and gene-environmental interaction in ET through a detailed questionnaire interview of patients for exposure to environmental agent exposure. We will also evaluate functions of causative genes and genetic variants in cell based models. Conclusions: Our findings will facilitate both in-vivo studies in transgenic animal models and in-vitro studies in cell-based models upon identification of functional gene variants, potentially leading to development of therapeutic targets.

title: A MULTI-CENTRE, MULTI-FACETED THERAPEUTIC STUDY INCORPORATING WHOLE GENOME ASSOCIATION AND CANDIDATE PATHWAY STUDIES FOR PHARMACOVIGILANCE AND TOXICOGENOMICS IN CHILDHOOD ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKAEMIA: MALAYSIA-SINGAPORE ALL 2008 STUDY
abs: Childhood ALL is the most common childhood cancer. Although it has excellent outcome (~80% cure), treatment toxicity and relapse remain as important barriers for further improvement in therapy. Aims. We aim to define biomarkers for treatment response and toxicity using genome-wide association and candidate gene/pathway approaches to further optimise the differences in host genetic makeup to eventually customise the optimal therapy for each child. This study will be the first major study in a predominantly Asain population. Method: Using an Internet-enabled real-time patient management system for the doctors to order chemotherapy and drugs coupled with our tissue bank, we are able to create a comprehensive phenotype-genotype database for the study. We propose to use the Illumina platform in a 2-staged approach and compare with the SNP study in healthy myopia children in Singapore by AProf Saw (funded by BMRC). There is an estimated 1000 patients who will be enrolled in this whole-genome association study: 600 new patients are projected to be enrolled in this Ma-Spore ALL 2008 study over 5 years and the 400 from the current Ma-Spore ALL 2003 study. Importance This study will provide an exceedingly valuable database for basic, translational and clinical researchers in Singapore and beyond. It will be a major step towards truly personalising medical treatment for children with cancer. Its role in defining biomarkers for host infection susceptibility is especially valuable for the regional developing countries where majority of the adverse events (40-80%) are due to infective deaths.

title: Accurate phenotyping of angle closure glaucoma
abs: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. With ageing of the population, glaucoma morbidity will rise, causing increased health care costs and economic burden for a condition in which visual loss, once established, cannot be reversed. In contrast to western countries, primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) is a major form of glaucoma in Asia, being responsible for the majority of bilateral blindness in Singapore, China and India.In a recent population based survey in Singapore, the prevalence of glaucoma was 3.2% in Chinese people, glaucoma was the leading cause of blindness, with PACG the most visually destructive form of the disease. The emergence of new imaging technology such as ultrasound biomicroscopy and anterior segment OCT has contributed greatly to identifying and understanding the mechanisms and pathways critical to the PACG disease process. Although most studies on PACG to date have assumed that PACG is predominantly pupil block related, recent data have highlighted the importance of non pupil block mechanisms such as plateau iris. Other studies have opened new questions about the significance of uveal effusion as a contributory factor in PACG. These findings highlight the fact that PACG is not a homogenous disease. We cannot assume that the management of PACG should be the same regardless of mechanism and it is likely that responses to therapies will vary according to the predominant mechanism involved. To establish a DNA resource for the study of the genetic influences of PACG, the need to carefully document the phenotype of each patient is paramount because of the clinical heterogeneity and likely genetic heterogeneity of the disorder. In this study, we propose to maximize the utility of such a resource by initiating a careful series of investigations to allow the identification of specific sub-types of the disorder as well as responses to therapy.

title: Dissecting transcriptional networks controlling cell-type specific responses to salt stress in the root of Arabidopsis
abs: Organs are composed of cells with distinct identities designed to interpret stimuli in specialized ways and coordinately fulfill complex functions. To understand how cells perform these specialized functions, I propose to study the mechanisms by which cell identity controls transcriptional responses to a model stimulus of great agricultural importance, salt stress. I have recently utilized Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS) in conjunction with cell-type specific GFP-marker lines to generate a high-resolution map of the transcriptional changes that occur in the root of Arabidopsis in response to salt stress. These data provide the first ever genome scale view of the role that cell identity plays in guiding transcriptional changes in a multicellular organism under stress. I will use this unique resource to determine the regulatory mechanisms controlling cell type specific transcriptional responses with the ultimate goal of constructing transcriptional networks that model these responses. A network-level understanding of the response of roots to salt stress will facilitate the generation of salinity resistant plants using more sophisticated approaches than previously available.

title: Mechanism for Simvastatin-induced Colorectal Cancer Cell Death: By Selectively Impairing Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK Signaling to BIM/BAX.
abs: Statins are widely prescribed as lipid-lowering agents in the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. They are increasingly associated with potential chemopreventive effects with respect to cancer. A recent case-control study reported a 47% relative reduction in the risk of colorectal cancer associated with statin use after adjustment for other known risk factors. There is evidence of an inhibitory effect of statins on colorectal carcinogenesis from in vitro studies, animal experiments, and observational and epidemiological reports in humans. Although statins seem promising as chemopreventive agents, it is still too early to recommend their use against colorectal cancer outside the context of clinical trials. Because the absolute risk reduction is likely low, further investigation of the overall benefits of statins in preventing colorectal cancer is warranted. The objectives of this study are to examine the effects of statins on colon cancer cells and to determine their mechanism of action. Preliminary results demonstrate a positive association between high Ras activity and sensitivity to simvastatin in HCT116, possibly by inhibiting Raf/MEK/ERK signaling leading to accumulation of dephosphorylated BIM. In the present study, we will first 1) confirm the effect of simvastatin on HCT116 cells. Because our preliminary results support the statin sensitivity to high Ras activity, we will 2) investigate if Ras status plays a role in simvastatin-induced apoptosis in colon cancer. To further elucidate into intracellular pathways by which statins mediate its antitumor activity we will determine if 3) the effect of simvastatin is mediated through Raf/MEK/ERK pathway to BIM activity. Tumor suppressor, p53, has been shown to upregulate expression of BIM. We will then explore 4) if the inhibitory effect of simvastatin in HCT116 is p53-dependent. There is increasing evidence that chemotherapeutic drugs can work via acceleration of intracellular H2O2. Here, will 5) determine if H2O2 initiates signal for simvastatin-induced apoptosis via Raf/MEK/ERK pathway. The key to further improvement of prevention and therapeutic strategies for colorectal neoplasms is probably not to search for the Holy Grail: one ideal anticancer agent. Rather, it is defining new intracellular pathways that will ultimately result in killing neoplastic cells.

title: Treatment of severed central nervous system by controlled release of therapeutic proteins encapsulated in biocompatible microspheres
abs: Despite the fact that adult mammalian CNS neurons still retain certain degree of regenerative capacity, very limited functional recovery is observed after spinal cord injury due to various unfavorable factors. The expose of a number of neurite outgrowth inhibitory proteins from degrading myelin and evolving glial scar is believed to present a non-permissive milieu for regenerating axons. In addition, Wallerian degeneration is not only restricted to severed axons and oligodendrocytes at the site of injury but also their undamaged counterparts in the vicinity. This leads to an ongoing process of cell death during which apoptosis plays a significant role. Interestingly, accumulating evidence from various lines of research appears to converge to a common denominator that regulates these processes. Recent findings suggest that major myelin inhibitors, like MAG, Nogo-66, and OMgp share the same receptor complex comprising NgR (Nogo-receptor) and LINGO, coupled with either p75 neurotrophic receptor (p75NTR) or a TNF receptor TROY, which in turn signals through RhoA-mediated pathways and leads to subsequent growth cone collapse. Similarly, Sema4D upregulated in injured myelin interacts with plexin-B1 and activates the RhoA pathway. The inhibition of axonal growth by CSPGs in glial scar may also involve RhoA. Further, p75NTR and RhoA activation has been implicated in apoptotic neuronal and glial cell death during Wallerian degeneration in injured spinal cord. Given the seemingly central role of RhoA in signaling these counter-regeneration events, we propose to repress RhoA activation with C3 transferase. By harnessing the TAT-mediated cell transduction and the biopolymer encapsulation technologies, we successfully developed a microsphere-based controlled release system of cell permeable C3. The feasibility of this therapeutic agent in promoting axonal regeneration and functional recovery after spinal injury in rat will be assessed in this proposal.
